verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst

verdict.shared_subject: Uitsluitend geautomatiseerde individuele besluitvorming die rechtsgevolgen heeft of de betrokkene anderszins in aanmerkelijke mate treft
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision B formuleert voor de betrokkene een recht om niet aan zo’n besluit te worden onderworpen, terwijl provision A ervan uitgaat dat zulke besluitvorming plaatsvindt en de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke passende beschermingsmaatregelen moet treffen. Dat kan oppervlakkig lijken op een toestemming om een door B verboden besluit toch te nemen, mits maatregelen worden getroffen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A ziet volgens de meegeleverde context op een uitzondering op het verbod van artikel 22, eerste lid, en vereist daarbij passende maatregelen; provision B zelf bevat eveneens uitzonderingen wanneer passende maatregelen zijn voorzien. De bepalingen kunnen dus samen worden nageleefd: B geldt als uitgangspunt, terwijl A de beschermingsvoorwaarden voor een toepasselijke uitzondering concretiseert, zonder dat A zelfstandig een besluit toestaat buiten de voorwaarden van B.
verdict.missing_reference: De specifieke uitzondering op artikel 22, eerste lid, waarop provision A steunt — met name of de nationale wettelijke verplichting of taak van algemeen belang daadwerkelijk onder artikel 22, lid 2, valt en welke passende maatregelen de toepasselijke bepaling voorschrijft — is nodig om te beslissen of het concrete geautomatiseerde besluit rechtmatig van het verbod kan worden uitgezonderd.
verdict.decisive_exception: Artikel 22, lid 2, onder b, van Verordening (EU) 2016/679, voor zover de nationale bepaling die het besluit toestaat ook passende maatregelen ter bescherming van de rechten en vrijheden en gerechtvaardigde belangen van de betrokkene bevat.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij de geautomatiseerde individuele besluitvorming, bedoeld in het eerste lid, treft de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke passende maatregelen die strekken tot bescherming van de rechten en vrijheden en gerechtvaardigde belangen van de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De betrokkene heeft het recht niet te worden onderworpen aan een uitsluitend op geautomatiseerde verwerking, waaronder profilering, gebaseerd besluit waaraan voor hem rechtsgevolgen zijn verbonden of dat hem anderszins in aanmerkelijke mate treft.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions impose reporting duties, so an entity that is both a financial entity and an AI-model provider might face two separate immediate-notification regimes. However, neither provision requires reporting the same event to the same recipient, and the texts do not establish incompatible content or deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns financial entities reporting serious ICT-related incidents to a competent authority, while provision B concerns providers notifying the Commission when a general-purpose AI model meets a specified condition. An actor subject to both can comply with both duties by making the respective reports to the respective recipients; the duties are cumulative rather than contradictory.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns when a provider need not notify affected data subjects after a personal-data breach if the data are rendered unintelligible through appropriate technical measures. Provision B requires the governing body of a financial entity to establish and oversee ICT-risk-management arrangements, including policies protecting data confidentiality, but it does not prescribe a notification duty or prohibit reliance on A’s exception.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A financial entity can comply with B’s governance and confidentiality obligations while also applying A’s notification exception where the competent data-protection authority considers the protective measures appropriate. B’s requirements can support the technical and organisational measures relevant to A without conflicting with the notification rule.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet vereist indien de aanbieder naar het oordeel van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens gepaste technische beschermingsmaatregelen heeft genomen waardoor de persoonsgegevens die het betreft, versleuteld of anderszins onbegrijpelijk zijn voor een ieder die geen recht heeft op toegang tot die gegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het leidinggevend orgaan van een financiële entiteit bepaalt alle regelingen met betrekking tot het in artikel 6, lid 1, bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer, keurt deze goed, houdt toezicht op de uitvoering ervan en is ervoor verantwoordelijk.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions concern different regulatory acts and impose duties on different actors: provision A concerns a lead overseer compelling a critical third-party ICT provider to comply with measures, while provision B concerns notifying authorities notifying conformity-assessment bodies. Nothing in the texts makes compliance with one duty affect compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both obligations can plainly be performed simultaneously because they regulate different conduct by different institutional actors. A lead overseer may impose a coercive fine after non-compliance, while a notifying authority may notify conformity-assessment bodies through the Commission’s electronic system; neither requires or prohibits the conduct required by the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanmeldende autoriteiten melden elke in lid 1 bedoeld conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstantie aan bij de Commissie en de andere lidstaten door middel van het door de Commissie ontwikkelde en beheerde elektronische aanmeldingssysteem.

verdict.shared_subject: Providing information and documentation to public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require an organisation to transfer or provide information to a public authority, so an entity that is both an erkende dienst under Provision A and an aangemelde instantie under Provision B may have overlapping disclosure duties. However, the texts do not impose incompatible timing, content, confidentiality, or retention requirements; Provision A concerns withdrawal or transfer of recognition, while Provision B concerns documentation made available on request for supervisory activities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily be performed together: the entity can transfer the information necessary for its recognised activities to Onze Minister and separately make all relevant documentation available to the notifying authority on request. They concern different authorities, triggers, and potentially different categories of information, and neither provision forbids compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De erkende dienst waarvan de erkenning wordt ingetrokken of overgedragen draagt er zorg voor dat alle door hem opgeslagen informatie en gegevens die noodzakelijk was voor de uitvoering van de activiteiten waarvoor hij was erkend, worden overgedragen aan Onze Minister.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties stellen alle relevante documentatie, waaronder de documentatie van de aanbieder, ter beschikking van de in artikel 28 bedoelde aanmeldende autoriteit, en verstrekken die aan haar op verzoek, teneinde haar in staat te stellen haar beoordelings-, aanwijzings-, kennisgevings- en monitoringsactiviteiten te verrichten, en de in deze afdeling beschreven beoordeling te vergemakkelijken.

verdict.shared_subject: AI-systemen die vóór de genoemde datum in de handel zijn gebracht of in gebruik zijn gesteld en onder beide categorieën vallen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen regelen de overgang naar naleving van dezelfde verordening, maar hanteren voor bepaalde reeds bestaande systemen verschillende uiterste data: 2 augustus 2030 voor hoog-risico-AI-systemen die door overheidsinstanties worden gebruikt en 31 december 2030 voor AI-systemen die componenten zijn van bepaalde grootschalige IT-systemen. Als één systeem onder beide omschrijvingen valt, kan onduidelijk zijn welke uiterste datum geldt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen hebben verschillende toepassingsvoorwaarden en kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: naleving uiterlijk op 2 augustus 2030 voldoet ook aan de latere datum van 31 december 2030. De teksten schrijven nergens voor dat naleving pas op de latere datum mag plaatsvinden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In ieder geval ondernemen de aanbieders en gebruiksverantwoordelijken van AI-systemen met een hoog risico die bedoeld zijn om door overheidsinstanties te worden gebruikt, de nodige stappen om uiterlijk op 2 augustus 2030 aan de eisen en verplichtingen van deze verordening te voldoen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: AI-systemen die componenten zijn van de bij de in bijlage X vermelde rechtshandelingen opgezette grootschalige IT-systemen die vóór 2 augustus 2027 in de handel zijn gebracht of in gebruik zijn gesteld, uiterlijk op 31 december 2030 in overeenstemming met deze verordening gebracht.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires certain public bodies, recognised holders and issuers to provide the Minister with data and information needed to prevent or end infringements concerning secure electronic access. Provision B restricts high-risk AI providers’ processing of special-category personal data and, in particular, prohibits transmitting or otherwise making that data available to other parties; if the requested information included such data, the duties could point in opposite directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish that the actors, data, or purposes overlap: A concerns specified entities and information needed by the Minister, while B concerns providers of high-risk AI systems and exceptional processing for bias detection or correction. Even if an entity were subject to both, A can be satisfied by providing non-sensitive information or information lawfully shareable under B’s conditions; B’s text does not categorically prohibit every disclosure required by A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: de bijzondere categorieën persoonsgegevens worden niet verzonden, doorgegeven of anderszins geraadpleegd door andere partijen;

verdict.shared_subject: Information obtained by a data protection officer from a data subject’s complaint or request, where an AI Act authority requests information
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The GDPR-related provision requires the data protection officer to keep information obtained through a complaint or data-subject request confidential, while Article 112 requires the AI Board, Member States and national competent authorities to provide the Commission with information without delay upon request. If the requested information includes such confidential complaint information, disclosure could appear to violate the secrecy duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different actors: Article 39 binds the data protection officer, whereas Article 112 binds the AI Board, Member States and national competent authorities. Article 112 also does not expressly require disclosure of information protected by the data protection officer’s secrecy obligation, so both duties can ordinarily be complied with without conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: is verplicht tot geheimhouding van hetgeen hem op grond van een klacht of een verzoek van betrokkene is bekend geworden, tenzij de betrokkene in bekendmaking toestemt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken de AI-board, de lidstaten en nationale bevoegde autoriteiten onverwijld informatie aan de Commissie op haar verzoek.

verdict.shared_subject: Electronic access services and possible processing or transfer of personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: An erkende ontsluitende dienst must disclose all recognised business and organisational means and related electronic authorisation statements, while GDPR Article 44 prohibits transferring personal data to a third country or international organisation unless the Chapter V conditions are met. If carrying out the disclosure necessarily involved such a transfer, the disclosure duty could appear to require conduct that Article 44 conditionally prohibits.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 13 concerns making recognised means, authorisation statements and designated attributes available for access to electronic services; it does not require transfer to a third country or international organisation. Article 44 can therefore be satisfied by performing the Article 13 duty without such a transfer, or by ensuring that any transfer meets the Chapter V conditions.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een erkende ontsluitende dienst ontsluit alle erkende bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddelen, alle door erkende machtigingsdiensten afgegeven elektronische verklaringen waaruit blijkt dat een natuurlijke persoon, onderneming of rechtspersoon gemachtigd is namens de onderneming of rechtspersoon, bedoeld in artikel 15, eerste lid, op te treden bij de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening en alle op grond van artikel 12 aangewezen attributen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Persoonsgegevens die worden verwerkt of die zijn bestemd om na doorgifte aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie te worden verwerkt, mogen slechts worden doorgegeven indien, onverminderd de overige bepalingen van deze verordening, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker aan de in dit hoofdstuk neergelegde voorwaarden hebben voldaan; dit geldt ook voor verdere doorgiften van persoonsgegevens vanuit het derde land of een internationale organisatie aan een ander derde land of een andere internationale organisatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Confidential information obtained by authorities and its disclosure or handling
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits providing information covered by professional secrecy to any other person or authority, while Provision B requires notifying authorities to ensure that information obtained under Article 78 is treated confidentially. If Article 78 information must be shared with another person or authority to fulfil the notification authority’s duties, A could appear to prohibit the required disclosure.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B requires confidentiality, which is consistent with Provision A’s prohibition on disclosure of professional-secrecy information. Provision A also expressly permits disclosure where required by Union or national law, and nothing in Provision B requires disclosure or otherwise conflicts with that prohibition.
verdict.evidence_span_a: wordt aan geen enkele andere persoon of autoriteit verstrekt, tenzij op grond van Unierechtelijke of nationaalrechtelijke bepalingen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: waarborgen dat de door hen verkregen informatie overeenkomstig artikel 78 vertrouwelijk wordt behandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Wederzijdse bijstand tussen bevoegde/toezichthoudende autoriteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 61 AVG formuleert een beperkte afwijzingsregeling: een verzoek mag slechts worden afgewezen wegens onbevoegdheid of strijd met toepasselijk recht. Artikel 37 NIS2 verplicht bijstand, maar noemt daarnaast disproportionaliteit en wezenlijke belangen van nationale veiligheid, openbare veiligheid of defensie als afwijzingsgronden; bij een gemotiveerd NIS2-verzoek kan daardoor onduidelijk lijken of die extra gronden ook onder artikel 61 toelaatbaar zijn.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen kunnen naast elkaar gelden voor verschillende wettelijke regimes en bevoegde autoriteiten: artikel 61 ziet op bijstand onder de AVG, terwijl artikel 37 ziet op NIS2-toezicht bij entiteiten die in meerdere lidstaten actief zijn. Bovendien kan een NIS2-verzoek dat niet proportioneel is of nationale veiligheidsbelangen raakt, onder artikel 61 mogelijk worden afgewezen omdat het in strijd is met toepasselijk recht dat op de ontvangende autoriteit van toepassing is.
verdict.missing_reference: De specifieke samenloop- of voorrangsregel die bepaalt of artikel 37 NIS2 de afwijzingsgronden van artikel 61 AVG aanvult of beperkt wanneer dezelfde autoriteit en hetzelfde verzoek onder beide regimes vallen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: wijst dit verzoek slechts af indien:
verdict.evidence_span_b: mag dat verzoek niet weigeren, tenzij wordt vastgesteld dat zij niet bevoegd is om de gevraagde bijstand te verlenen, dat de gevraagde bijstand niet in verhouding staat tot de toezichthoudende taken van de bevoegde autoriteit, of dat het verzoek betrekking heeft op informatie of activiteiten inhoudt die, indien ze openbaar zouden worden gemaakt of zouden worden uitgevoerd, in strijd zouden zijn met de wezenlijke belangen van zijn nationale veiligheid, de openbare veiligheid of de defensie van die lidstaat.

verdict.shared_subject: Access to confidential information or AI-model source code by a public authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A excludes confidential data from the Wet open overheid, subject only to the stated environmental-information exception, while provision B says the Commission may request access to a general-purpose AI model, including its source code. If the requested source code is confidential data and the request is treated as an open-government access request, A could appear to block access that B permits.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A governs the applicability of the Wet open overheid to confidential data, whereas provision B concerns the Commission’s investigative competence to request access to an AI model through appropriate technical means. The texts do not establish that the Commission’s request is made under the Wet open overheid, that source code is confidential data under A, or that A limits access under the AI Act.
verdict.missing_reference: The specific legal basis and access regime governing a Commission request under Article 92—especially whether it overrides or is independent of the Wet open overheid exclusion in Article 66, and whether the requested source code qualifies as “vertrouwelijke gegevens”—is not shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De Wet open overheid is niet van toepassing op vertrouwelijke gegevens als bedoeld in het eerste lid, behalve voor zover die gegevens milieu-informatie inhouden als bedoeld in artikel 19.1a van de Wet milieubeheer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: kan de Commissie verzoeken om toegang tot het betrokken AI-model voor algemene doeleinden via API’s of andere passende technische middelen en instrumenten, waaronder de broncode.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/data protection obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A extends unspecified requirements in Article 11.7a(1)(a) and (b) to certain storage or access situations, while Provision B requires financial entities to use ICT technologies and processes meeting extensive security, availability, integrity, confidentiality, and data-management objectives. If A's extended requirements imposed a different or incompatible treatment of stored or accessed information, compliance could potentially pull in another direction from B's required protections.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different duties: A extends requirements concerning information stored on, or accessed through, an end device, whereas B requires financial entities to deploy suitable ICT security and risk-management measures. Nothing in the shown text requires conduct that B forbids or forbids conduct that B requires; the security measures in B could generally coexist with compliance under A.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0009950 art. 11.7a, first paragraph, under a and b, because Provision A expressly incorporates those requirements but their content is not shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in het eerste lid, onder a en b, genoemde vereisten zijn ook van toepassing
verdict.evidence_span_b: maken financiële entiteiten gebruik van ICT-technologieën en -processen die geschikt zijn overeenkomstig artikel 4

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI providers that transfer personal data to a third country or international organisation in response to a competent authority’s request.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 requires a high-risk AI provider to provide all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate conformity, potentially including personal data, to a competent authority in an official EU language. Article 44 prohibits transferring personal data to a third country or international organisation unless the GDPR Chapter V conditions have been satisfied, so a request from an authority outside the EU could require disclosure that cannot lawfully be made without an applicable transfer mechanism.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 21 does not itself require disclosure to a third-country authority or override other applicable law; it requires provision only on a reasoned request from a competent authority. Article 44 expressly permits transfers when its Chapter V conditions are met, so a provider can comply with both by supplying the requested information through a lawful transfer mechanism or by providing non-personal information.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider established in the EU operates a high-risk AI system and receives a reasoned request from a competent authority in a non-EU country for conformity documentation containing identifiable personal data. Article 21 points toward providing the requested documentation, while Article 44 prevents sending that personal data to the authority unless the GDPR Chapter V transfer conditions are satisfied.
verdict.decisive_exception: An applicable GDPR Chapter V transfer mechanism or other condition permitting the transfer to the third-country authority, such as an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards; Article 21 does not establish that exception.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Persoonsgegevens die worden verwerkt of die zijn bestemd om na doorgifte aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie te worden verwerkt, mogen slechts worden doorgegeven indien, onverminderd de overige bepalingen van deze verordening, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker aan de in dit hoofdstuk neergelegde voorwaarden hebben voldaan
verdict.evidence_span_b: Op een met redenen omkleed verzoek van een bevoegde autoriteit, verstrekken aanbieders van AI-systemen met een hoog risico die autoriteit alle informatie en documentatie die noodzakelijk is om de overeenstemming van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico met de eisen van afdeling 2 aan te tonen

verdict.shared_subject: Access to and handling of information by public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information obtained or supplied in the exercise of public functions. A possible tension is that Article 19 requires the Minister to disclose information about breaches to several recipients when necessary for their tasks or services, while Article 77 requires information or documentation obtained by specified fundamental-rights authorities to be processed under Article 78 confidentiality obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different information flows: Article 19 governs the Minister’s necessary provision of breach-related information, whereas Article 77 governs how designated authorities process documentation they obtain under Article 77(1). Disclosure under Article 19 can therefore be followed by confidential processing under Article 78, and nothing in the shown texts forbids the disclosure or makes the duties incompatible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister verstrekt gegevens en inlichtingen aan bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, aan de ingevolge artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houder van een erkenning of aan een ingevolge artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgever of dienst over de inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening voor zover dit noodzakelijk is voor een goede uitoefening van hun taken of te verlenen diensten in het kader van deze wet.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Informatie of documentatie die op grond van dit artikel door de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde overheidsinstanties of -organen wordt verkregen, wordt verwerkt overeenkomstig de in artikel 78 beschreven vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Verplichtingen rond hoog-risico-AI-systemen in de AI-waardeketen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen betrekking hebben op hetzelfde hoog-risico-AI-systeem nadat een wijziging of nieuwe ingebruikname heeft plaatsgevonden. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat de oorspronkelijke aanbieder bij een wijziging informatie en technische toegang moet verstrekken, terwijl de gebruiksverantwoordelijke tegelijk een grondrechteneffectbeoordeling moet actualiseren, wat praktische coördinatie en mogelijk tegenstrijdige verantwoordelijkheidsopvattingen oplevert.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen echter verplichtingen op aan verschillende actoren en regelen verschillende onderwerpen: artikel 25 verplicht de oorspronkelijke aanbieder tot samenwerking en bijstand, terwijl artikel 27 de gebruiksverantwoordelijke verplicht een effectbeoordeling te verrichten of te actualiseren. De samenwerking en informatieverstrekking uit artikel 25 kunnen juist helpen om aan artikel 27 te voldoen; geen van beide bepalingen verbiedt naleving van de andere.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Die oorspronkelijke aanbieder werkt nauw samen met nieuwe aanbieders, stelt de nodige informatie beschikbaar en verstrekt de redelijkerwijs verwachte technische toegang en andere bijstand die nodig zijn om te voldoen aan de verplichtingen van deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de gebruiksverantwoordelijke tijdens het gebruik van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico ziet dat een van de in lid 1 vermelde elementen is gewijzigd of niet langer actueel is, neemt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de nodige maatregelen om de informatie te actualiseren.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory authorities and critical third-party ICT-service-provider inspections
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes professional secrecy on supervisory-authority members and staff for confidential information learned in their duties, while provision B requires the lead overseer to notify a critical ICT provider of the consequences of resisting an inspection. One might argue that communicating inspection-related information could disclose confidential information protected by A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B requires only notification of the consequences of resistance, not disclosure of confidential information. The notification can be framed and delivered consistently with the professional-secrecy duty in A, so both provisions can be obeyed without any stated incompatibility.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Ten aanzien van de vertrouwelijke informatie die hun bij de uitvoering van hun taken of de uitoefening van hun bevoegdheden ter kennis is gekomen, geldt voor het lid of de leden en de personeelsleden van elke toezichthoudende autoriteit zowel tijdens hun ambtstermijn als daarna het beroepsgeheim
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de lead overseer de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten in kennis van de gevolgen van dit verzet

verdict.shared_subject: Notification to data subjects after a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the provider to notify the affected person immediately when the breach is likely to have adverse consequences for privacy. Provision B states that notification is not required when, for example, appropriate protective measures made the data unintelligible, potentially allowing non-notification in a case that still has likely adverse privacy consequences under A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be read as operating with different thresholds and exceptions: A concerns likely adverse consequences for privacy, while B's exceptions concern protective measures, remediation of high risk, or disproportionate effort. The supplied context for A expressly contains an encryption-based exception, and B's exception for unintelligible data is materially similar, so the rules may be jointly satisfied where that exception applies.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider suffers a breach involving encrypted personal data that is nevertheless assessed as likely to have adverse consequences for the affected person's privacy. A appears to require immediate notification, while B may dispense with notification under Article 34(3)(a); deciding whether the provider must notify requires determining whether the applicable A-side encryption exception applies and how it interacts with the GDPR exception.
verdict.missing_reference: The full text and legal applicability of BWBR0009950 art. 11.3a, particularly the provision corresponding to the supplied context's lid 5 and any rule resolving its relationship with GDPR Article 34(3), are needed to decide whether the encryption exception displaces the notification duty in A.
verdict.decisive_exception: The exception for appropriate technical protective measures making the personal data unintelligible to unauthorised persons, including encryption (A's lid 5 and GDPR Article 34(3)(a)).
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde mededeling aan de betrokkene is niet vereist wanneer een van de volgende voorwaarden is vervuld:

verdict.shared_subject: Incident notification involving personal data and high-risk AI systems that are safety components or devices covered by Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A creates an exception to notifying affected individuals about a personal-data breach when the data are appropriately encrypted or otherwise unintelligible to unauthorised persons. Provision B requires serious incidents involving specified high-risk AI systems to be reported to the designated national competent authority, so an incident could appear exempt from one notification route while still requiring the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different recipients and are triggered by different conditions: A concerns notifying the person whose personal data are affected, while B concerns reporting serious incidents to a national competent authority. Nothing in either text prohibits complying with both duties, and A's exception does not remove B's authority-reporting obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet vereist indien de aanbieder naar het oordeel van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens gepaste technische beschermingsmaatregelen heeft genomen waardoor de persoonsgegevens die het betreft, versleuteld of anderszins onbegrijpelijk zijn voor een ieder die geen recht heeft op toegang tot die gegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: Governance duties for partners of a Dutch general partnership and reporting significant incidents by essential or important entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply within the same regulatory setting, but Article 24 only extends the governance rules to each partner when the entity is a general partnership, while Article 25 imposes incident-reporting duties on the essential or important entity itself. One might argue that the provisions identify different duty-bearers, creating uncertainty about whether individual partners must also make the report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, complementary duties: Article 24 determines how governance rules apply to partners of a general partnership, whereas Article 25 requires the essential or important entity to report every significant incident. Nothing in Article 24 exempts, prohibits, or changes the reporting obligation in Article 25, and both can be complied with simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit een vennootschap onder firma is, is het bepaalde bij of krachtens het eerste tot en met zesde lid van overeenkomstige toepassing op iedere vennoot van die vennootschap onder firma.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and follow-up involving potentially criminal or serious incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern follow-up after an incident report, and a serious AI incident could also be suspected to be criminal. In that situation, the CSIRT gives guidance to the reporting entity about reporting to law-enforcement authorities, while the market-surveillance authority notifies specified national authorities or bodies; this could create overlapping notification channels, but neither text forbids the other or assigns incompatible content or deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors: provision A concerns CSIRT guidance to the reporting entity, whereas provision B concerns a market-surveillance authority notifying national authorities or bodies after receiving a serious-incident report. Both actions can occur cumulatively, and nothing in either text prevents the entity from following CSIRT guidance while the authority makes its separate notification.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Na ontvangst van een melding met betrekking tot een ernstig incident als bedoeld in artikel 3, punt 49), c), stelt de betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit de in artikel 77, lid 1, bedoelde nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen in kennis.

verdict.shared_subject: Bewaring van persoonsgegevens in archieven en voor toezichthoudende taken
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A disapplies certain GDPR rights for personal data in permanently preserved public-interest archives, which could make it possible to retain or use such data without those rights applying. Provision B, however, sets a maximum retention period of 15 years for the personal data referred to in Article 56(1), unless ongoing judicial proceedings require further retention; a permanently preserved archive could therefore appear to require retention beyond that limit.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different situations: A concerns personal data forming part of specified permanent archives, while B concerns personal data processed under Article 56(1) for the supervisory tasks of the ETAs and competent authorities. Nothing in A expressly authorises retention beyond B’s limit, and B’s 15-year rule can be complied with even if the GDPR rights listed in A do not apply.

verdict.shared_subject: Potentially an entity that is both subject to the obligations in BWBR0052872 art. 21 and an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst seeking recognition under BWBR0048156 art. 11
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits the competent Minister to exempt an essential or important entity from the obligations in article 21 when it operates in specified sensitive fields or exclusively serves a government body. If the same entity is also a service provider covered by provision B, the exemption could appear to remove obligations that might be relevant to the service's recognition requirements, creating a possible conflict if article 21 obligations overlap with the rules governing recognition.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns a discretionary exemption from obligations in article 21, while provision B requires recognition of an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst only when it satisfies rules established by or under a general administrative measure. The texts do not show that article 21 obligations are part of the recognition rules, that recognition requires compliance with article 21, or that an exemption under article 23 affects recognition; both provisions can therefore be obeyed independently.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister die het aangaat kan bij regeling of besluit, in overeenstemming met Onze Minister, een essentiële entiteit respectievelijk een belangrijke entiteit die activiteiten uitvoert op het gebied van nationale veiligheid, openbare veiligheid, defensie of rechtshandhaving of die uitsluitend diensten verleent aan een overheidsinstantie als bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, met betrekking tot die activiteiten of diensten ontheffen van de verplichtingen, bedoeld in artikel 21.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een ontsluitende dienst of een machtigingsdienst indien de dienst voldoet aan de met betrekking tot die dienst bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a public identification means or related facility in electronic communications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts the use of the public identification means and facility to access to electronic services by administrative bodies and designated organisations. Provision B requires public electronic communications network and service providers to preserve the confidentiality of communications and related data; using the identification means in communications could, on a particular implementation, create a confidentiality issue if it exposes or processes such data.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different subject matter: A regulates permitted use of a public identification means, while B imposes a confidentiality duty on providers of public electronic communications networks or services. A provider can comply with both by limiting use of the identification means as required and maintaining confidentiality; neither text requires disclosure or otherwise conflicts with confidentiality.

verdict.shared_subject: Governance and enforcement of essential entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A extends the rules in paragraphs 2–6 to natural persons who sit on the board on behalf of a legal person that is the board member of an essential entity. Provision B allows a natural person with management responsibilities at general-director or legal-representative level to be temporarily prohibited from exercising management functions, which could affect a person covered by A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A is only an applicability rule and does not itself require or permit a particular management act. Provision B is an enforcement power directed at an essential entity and expressly operates only until deficiencies are remedied, so the provisions can both apply without requiring incompatible conduct.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes a concrete maximum retention period—deletion within 12 months—while provision B contemplates that further rules may be made concerning the subject matter of its article. If those future rules were to prescribe a conflicting retention period, an apparent conflict could arise, but no such rule is shown.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not itself prescribe any retention period, permission, prohibition, or other operative requirement; it merely authorises further regulation by general administrative measure. Provision A therefore remains fully applicable, and the two provisions can presently be obeyed together.

verdict.shared_subject: Disclosure of information by regulated entities or authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires informing a data subject about appropriate safeguards when personal data are transferred to a third country or international organisation. Provision B requires notified bodies to provide relevant documentation, potentially containing personal data, to the notifying authority on request; disclosure to that authority could arguably involve a transfer to an international organisation or raise confidentiality concerns, but B does not prohibit or regulate the information that must be given to data subjects.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors and address different situations: A concerns a data subject’s access right following an international transfer, while B concerns a notified body’s cooperation with a national notifying authority. A notified body can provide the requested documentation and separately comply with A where its disclosure qualifies as a transfer covered by Article 46.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties stellen alle relevante documentatie, waaronder de documentatie van de aanbieder, ter beschikking van de in artikel 28 bedoelde aanmeldende autoriteit, en verstrekken die aan haar op verzoek

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a public identification means or related facility by organisations, and financial entities’ ICT continuity records
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts use of the public identification means and facility to access to electronic services provided by administrative bodies and designated organisations. Provision B requires financial entities to keep accessible registers of activities before and during ICT disruptions; if carrying out that register duty required using the public identification means for a non-covered system or service, A could prevent that method of compliance.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different conduct: A governs the permitted purpose and users of a public identification means, while B governs the content and accessibility of financial entities’ continuity and recovery records. A financial entity can comply with B by maintaining the registers through other systems or lawful access arrangements, and B does not require use of the identification means.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een publiek identificatiemiddel en de voorziening, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, onderdeel b, worden uitsluitend gebruikt voor de toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening door bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten houden gemakkelijk toegankelijke registers bij van hun activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen wanneer hun ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsplannen en ICT-respons- en herstelplannen worden geactiveerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Member States’ sanctioning rules and their notification to the Commission under the GDPR
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 83 provides a specific notification obligation for Member States that use the judicial-fine alternative where their legal system does not provide administrative fines. Article 84 separately requires Member States to establish and apply rules on other sanctions, including sanctions for infringements not subject to administrative fines under Article 83; one might argue that the two provisions could overlap in how a Member State classifies and notifies sanctions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different sanction categories: Article 83 concerns the procedural substitute for administrative fines in Member States whose legal systems lack them, while Article 84 concerns other sanctions, particularly infringements not subject to Article 83 administrative fines. Both impose compatible requirements that sanctions be effective, proportionate and dissuasive, and the related Article 84(2) context supplies the same 25 May 2018 notification deadline rather than a conflicting one.

verdict.shared_subject: An EU-established authorised representative for a high-risk AI provider in a third country who handles personal data and transfers it to a third country or international organisation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 22(b) requires the authorised representative to keep specified provider contact details and compliance documents available for ten years, and Article 22(c) requires supplying documentation, including logs, on a reasoned request. Article 44 permits transfers of personal data to a third country or international organisation only when the GDPR Chapter V conditions are met, so performing those Article 22 tasks may involve transfers that Article 44 independently restricts.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 22 does not itself require an international transfer of personal data; the representative can retain or provide the material in a manner compliant with Chapter V. Article 44 expressly operates alongside the GDPR’s other provisions, so the Article 22 duties and the transfer restrictions can both be satisfied by using an applicable Chapter V transfer mechanism or avoiding an impermissible transfer.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data, including special categories, by an AI-system provider or persons acting under its authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a processor and anyone acting under the controller’s or processor’s authority with access to personal data to process it only on the controller’s instructions, unless Union or Member State law requires the processing. Provision B exceptionally permits a provider of a high-risk AI system to process special-category personal data for bias detection and correction, which could appear to authorise processing beyond the controller’s instructions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B expressly makes its permission subject to the GDPR and other applicable data-protection law, while provision A permits processing where Union law requires it. The AI Act permission therefore does not displace the instruction-only rule: the provider can process the data on the controller’s instructions, or where another applicable legal rule requires it, while satisfying B’s additional safeguards.
verdict.decisive_exception: The apparent permission in provision B is expressly subject to Regulation (EU) 2016/679, including provision A; no conflict is established unless processing occurs without the controller’s instructions and without a separate Union- or Member-State-law obligation.

verdict.shared_subject: Cyber-crisis authority and market-surveillance authority handling serious incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern institutional handling of cyber or serious incidents, so one might initially suspect overlapping responsibilities or procedures. However, Provision A assigns the Minister general cyber-crisis-management tasks under the national plan, while Provision B requires the market-surveillance authority to take measures within seven days after receiving a high-risk AI serious-incident notification; neither text prohibits the other authority from acting or creates incompatible duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, simultaneously performable functions on different authorities: the Minister has the tasks assigned by the national cyber-crisis plan, and the market-surveillance authority must act within seven days and follow Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 procedures. The texts establish no conflicting deadline, prohibition, or exclusive allocation of competence.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister is de cybercrisisbeheerautoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 9, eerste lid, van de NIS2-richtlijn, en heeft in die hoedanigheid de taken die zijn opgenomen in het nationaal plan voor grootschalige cyberbeveiligingsincidenten en crisisrespons, genoemd in artikel 20.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen, en volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet.

verdict.shared_subject: Ministerial decisions concerning registration or designation of organisations/entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern ending a status by ministerial decision, so an organisation could potentially be affected by both regimes. However, Article 43 concerns a registration in the national register when the ground for registration has changed, lapsed, or is absent, while Article 2 concerns withdrawal of an organisation’s designation when it no longer provides specified electronic services; the texts do not make these decisions legally incompatible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be obeyed together because they regulate different legal statuses and different triggers. A registration may be changed, refused, or ended under Article 43, while a designation may be withdrawn under Article 2; neither provision requires maintaining the status that the other permits or requires ending.

Provision B concerns an exemption from the obligation to maintain a register of processing activities for certain organisations with fewer than 250 employees, so one might argue that a small organisation could have an incident-reporting duty while being exempt from the processing register duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different triggers: A regulates incident reporting by essential or important entities, while B limits when specified organisations must maintain a processing-activities register. Neither provision requires or forbids conduct addressed by the other, and exemption from the register obligation does not affect the incident-reporting duty.

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative fines for overlapping data-protection or AI-related infringements
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits the competent authority from imposing a fine under articles 80 and 87 for the same conduct once a GDPR fine has been imposed. Provision B authorizes the European Data Protection Supervisor to impose administrative fines on EU institutions, bodies, and agencies within the AI Act’s scope, potentially for conduct that could also constitute the same infringement addressed by the GDPR fine.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different authorities, addressees, and legal bases: A regulates a Dutch competent authority’s duplicate fine after a GDPR fine, while B concerns fines imposed by the European Data Protection Supervisor on EU institutions, bodies, and agencies. Nothing in B requires a second fine for the same conduct, and A does not purport to govern the EDPS’s competence under the AI Act.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De Europese Toezichthouder voor gegevensbescherming kan administratieve geldboeten opleggen aan instellingen, organen en instanties van de Unie die binnen het toepassingsgebied van deze verordening vallen.

verdict.shared_subject: Publication of information by public bodies
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits publication of a decision before ten working days have elapsed, subject to specified exceptions. Provision B contemplates rules requiring organs to publish a current statement on their website, which could theoretically require publication during that waiting period, but it does not say that the statement must contain or publish the decision covered by A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B concerns publication of a statement about the application of an appointed standard, whereas A concerns publication of a particular decision and expressly permits earlier publication in specified circumstances. The two duties can therefore be fulfilled together without any demonstrated conflict.

verdict.shared_subject: Substantieel gewijzigde AI-systemen met een hoog risico en de verantwoordelijkheden van de oorspronkelijke aanbieder
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 25 verplicht de oorspronkelijke aanbieder tot samenwerking, informatieverstrekking en technische toegang wanneer een andere actor door de omstandigheden van lid 1 aanbieder wordt. Artikel 43 verplicht vervolgens tot een nieuwe conformiteitsbeoordeling bij een substantiële wijziging; men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat de oorspronkelijke aanbieder daardoor moet meewerken aan een beoordeling voor een systeem waarvoor hij niet langer als aanbieder geldt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen verschillende, naast elkaar uitvoerbare verplichtingen op: artikel 25 regelt bijstand in de AI-waardeketen, terwijl artikel 43 de conformiteitsbeoordeling van het substantieel gewijzigde systeem regelt. Niets in artikel 43 verbiedt de samenwerking of bijstand van artikel 25, en niets in artikel 25 ontslaat een betrokken actor van de nieuwe beoordeling.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Die ursprüngliche aanbieder werkt nauw samen met nieuwe aanbieders, stelt de nodige informatie beschikbaar en verstrekt de redelijkerwijs verwachte technische toegang en andere bijstand die nodig is om te voldoen aan de verplichtingen van deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: AI-systemen met een hoog risico die reeds aan een conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure zijn onderworpen, ondergaan een nieuwe conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure telkens wanneer zij substantieel zijn gewijzigd

Provision B requires a digitally offered high-risk AI system's CE marking to be accessible through its interface or an accessible machine-readable code or other electronic means; an actor can comply with both without contradiction.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system and personal-data breach communications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern the same organisation using a high-risk AI system and processing personal data. However, Article 34 regulates whether affected data subjects must be notified of a personal-data breach, while Article 27 regulates a fundamental-rights impact assessment before and during use of a high-risk AI system; neither requires or forbids conduct addressed by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: An organisation can perform and update the required fundamental-rights impact assessment while also notifying data subjects of a breach, or relying on an Article 34 exception where its conditions are met. The provisions have different triggers, duties and subject matter, so compliance with one does not obstruct compliance with the other.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de gebruiksverantwoordelijke tijdens het gebruik van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico ziet dat een van de in lid 1 vermelde elementen is gewijzigd of niet langer actueel is, neemt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de nodige maatregelen om de informatie te actualiseren.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing special-category or criminal-offence personal data by a temporary commission or advisory body where the processing may rely on consent
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A creates an exception to the prohibition when obtaining explicit consent is impossible or disproportionately burdensome, provided the other safeguards are met. Provision B requires the controller to demonstrate consent whenever the processing is based on consent, so relying on A's exception could appear inconsistent with B if the processing is nevertheless characterized as consent-based.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not require or authorize processing on the basis of consent; it expressly addresses cases where obtaining explicit consent is impossible or disproportionately burdensome and imposes additional safeguards. verdict.missing_reference: The specific provision governing the AI evaluator's authority to request or receive health data, including any confidentiality, data-protection, or lawful-disclosure exception applicable to Article 92's requested information and access.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident and vulnerability reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns treating an earlier Wbni notification as an early warning of a significant incident and forwarding it to the competent authority. Provision B requires a designated CSIRT to coordinate vulnerability reports and protect the reporter’s anonymity, so tension might be alleged if the same report is both an incident notification and a vulnerability report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, sequentially compatible functions: A governs the transitional classification and forwarding of a specified prior notification, while B governs coordinated vulnerability disclosure by a CSIRT. Nothing in B forbids forwarding an incident notification, and nothing in A requires disclosure of the reporter’s identity or prevents CSIRT coordination and anonymity.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data for archiving in the public interest
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A excludes certain GDPR provisions, including Article 20, for personal data held permanently in qualifying archives. Provision B still states general GDPR processing principles, including purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, and security; this could suggest that permanent archival retention conflicts with storage limitation or that the Article 45 exception does not cover Article 5.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 45 expressly concerns only Articles 15, 16, 18(1)(a), and 20, not Article 5. Article 5(e) itself permits longer storage where data are processed solely for archiving in the public interest in accordance with Article 89(1), so qualifying permanent archives can retain data while complying with the applicable principles and safeguards.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use the concept of a representative or authorised party, so one might initially suspect that the duties could overlap where an AI provider also operates an erkende ontsluitende dienst. However, Provision A concerns the service's technical or access-related disclosure duties, while Provision B concerns enabling an AI provider's authorised representative to perform tasks under its mandate; neither text imposes an incompatible requirement.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different actors and functions: A requires an erkende ontsluitende dienst to disclose specified business and organisational means, electronic statements, and attributes, whereas B requires an AI provider to enable its authorised representative to perform mandated tasks. An actor potentially subject to both can comply with both duties simultaneously, and nothing in either provision forbids or limits the conduct required by the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Security measures and records of processing by public electronic communications providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A provider may be subject to A's obligation to adopt technical, operational and organisational security measures while B exempts a small organisation from the referenced record-keeping obligations. If the provider's security measures involve processing personal data, one might argue that A's security-governance duty points toward maintaining processing records while B may remove that GDPR record-keeping obligation for a qualifying small organisation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A requires security measures to manage risks to public electronic communications networks or services; B concerns whether certain enterprises must keep a register of processing activities. The provisions impose different duties and do not require or forbid incompatible conduct: a provider can implement A's measures without keeping the particular register covered by B, and B's exceptions preserve the obligation where its stated conditions apply.

No actor is required by one provision to do something that the other forbids or measures by a conflicting standard.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: An administrative body or designated organisation can provide the auditor’s statement required by Article 4 while the government separately submits an Article 5(6) general administrative order to both Houses and observes its four-week commencement procedure. The provisions impose distinct obligations with no incompatible deadline, content, actor duty, or legal effect.

verdict.shared_subject: Annual actions by public data-protection authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose annual obligations on data-protection authorities, so they are topically related. One requires the Dutch supervisory authority to prepare a draft budget before the relevant budget year, while the other requires the European Data Protection Supervisor to notify the Commission of fines and proceedings imposed or initiated under that article; if the same authority and reporting channel were involved, the duties would concern different annual outputs rather than mutually exclusive conduct.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different authorities: the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens must prepare an annual draft budget, whereas the European Data Protection Supervisor must notify the Commission about fines and proceedings. Nothing in either text prohibits or makes compliance with the other duty impossible.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk management, cybersecurity, incident handling and business continuity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose overlapping ICT-security and continuity duties, including incident handling, protection of systems, and backup/recovery measures. A possible tension is that the Dutch provision requires an all-hazards approach protecting both network and information systems and their physical environment, while the DORA provision supplies a separate simplified framework with differently formulated and potentially more specific requirements for certain small or exempt financial entities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied together: Provision B expressly requires its covered entities to maintain ICT-risk-management, monitoring, incident-handling, and continuity measures, while Provision A likewise requires risk analysis, incident handling, continuity, supply-chain security, and cryptography. Nothing in either text requires an entity to omit or violate the other provision’s measures; the more detailed or differently scoped requirements can operate cumulatively.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: An entity could comply with Provision A by promptly informing its service recipients of a significant incident and comply with Provision B by submitting its application to the competent notifying authority. verdict.shared_subject: Disclosure of health-related data or documentation by a high-risk AI provider to a competent authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes confidentiality on health data and permits disclosure only where the law requires it or where the controller’s task necessitates disclosure to persons otherwise authorised to process the data. Provision B requires a high-risk AI provider to provide a competent authority with all information and documentation necessary to demonstrate compliance, which could include health data and could therefore require disclosure to an authority not shown to be authorised under Provision A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed if the requested information and documentation do not contain health data, or if the competent authority is legally authorised to receive and process such data. Provision B requires disclosure only of information necessary for demonstrating compliance, while Provision A itself allows disclosure where the law requires it or where the recipient is authorised under the referenced provisions.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A healthcare provider that offers a high-risk AI diagnostic system holds patient health records used to demonstrate compliance with the AI Act. A competent authority makes a reasoned request for those records under Article 21, but the texts shown do not establish whether that authority is legally authorised to receive and process the health data under the applicable health-data rules.
verdict.missing_reference: The specific legal provision governing whether the requesting competent authority is authorised or legally required to receive and process the health data, including the referenced first, second, or third paragraphs and any applicable disclosure exception.

verdict.shared_subject: Communicating information about cyber or personal-data incidents to affected service recipients/data subjects
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to promptly tell potentially affected service recipients what measures they can take in response to a significant cyber threat, and, if necessary, to inform them of the threat itself. Provision B states that communication to a data subject is not required in specified circumstances, which could appear to permit withholding information where the same recipient is also a data subject.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different communications and triggers: A concerns significant cyber threats affecting recipients of an entity’s services, while B concerns notification of a personal-data breach to data subjects and expressly preserves alternative public or equivalent communication where disproportionate effort applies. A can therefore be complied with by giving threat-response information without necessarily making the GDPR breach notification described in B, and B does not prohibit A’s communication.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.

Provision A regulates conditioning access to a public-law body's information-society service on user consent; provision B regulates confidentiality duties of notified conformity-assessment bodies and their personnel.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different conduct: A concerns access to a service provided by or on behalf of a public-law legal person, while B concerns keeping information obtained during conformity-assessment activities confidential, subject to specified disclosures. Compliance with one does not require or prevent compliance with the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A extends certain electronic-communications requirements to information stored on, or accessed from, an end device even where the mechanism is not an electronic communications network. Provision B grants a data subject information about appropriate safeguards when personal data are transferred to a third country or international organisation; the texts do not identify any incompatible requirement or permission.

verdict.shared_subject: Samenwerking en wederzijdse bijstand tussen bevoegde autoriteiten bij grensoverschrijdende entiteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen zien op dezelfde grensoverschrijdende situaties en verplichten bevoegde autoriteiten tot samenwerking en bijstand. Een mogelijke spanning is dat artikel 60 spreekt over bijstand op een gemotiveerd verzoek, terwijl artikel 37 een uitgebreider stelsel voorschrijft, waaronder informatie-uitwisseling, raadpleging en bijstand die niet mag worden geweigerd behoudens specifieke uitzonderingen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen juist wederzijds ondersteunende verplichtingen op: artikel 60 verplicht de Nederlandse bevoegde autoriteit bijstand te verlenen, terwijl artikel 37 de inhoud, procedure en uitzonderingen van die wederzijdse bijstand nader uitwerkt. Artikel 60 kan daarom worden nageleefd door bijstand te verlenen overeenkomstig artikel 37; er is geen tegenstrijdig gebod of verbod.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een entiteit diensten verricht in meer dan één lidstaat, of indien zij diensten verricht in een of meer lidstaten en haar netwerk- en informatiesystemen zich in een of meer andere lidstaten bevinden, werken de bevoegde autoriteiten van de betrokken lidstaten met elkaar samen en verlenen ze elkaar indien nodig bijstand.

verdict.shared_subject: National competent authorities and information concerning significant incidents, cyber threats, and near-incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires CSIRTs or, where applicable, competent authorities to provide certain incident and threat information to authorities competent under Directive (EU) 2022/2557. Provision B requires national competent authorities, when performing their tasks, to comply with confidentiality obligations under Article 78; disclosure under A could therefore appear to conflict if the information is confidential under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different aspects of the authorities’ work: A requires specified information-sharing, while B requires confidentiality. Information can be shared with the designated competent authorities while still being handled confidentially, and the text shown does not establish that Article 78 prohibits the disclosure required by A.

verdict.shared_subject: Communicating personal-data breaches to the data subject
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A states categorically that the notification to the data subject includes specified information, which could suggest that such notification is always required. Provision B, however, expressly dispenses with that notification when one of its listed conditions is met, such as effective encryption or disproportionate effort.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A can be read as prescribing the contents of a notification when one is required, while provision B identifies circumstances in which no notification to the data subject is required. Thus, A's content requirements and B's exceptions can operate together without contradiction.
verdict.decisive_exception: The exceptions in Article 34(3), especially the conditions concerning effective protective measures, elimination of high risk, or disproportionate effort, determine when the data-subject notification is not required; the text supports treating Article 11.3a as applying when notification is made.

Provision B requires financial entities to maintain accessible registers during activated ICT continuity or response-and-recovery plans; the texts do not show that maintaining such registers requires conditioning service access on consent.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different rules on different apparent actors and conduct: A prohibits a public-law service provider from making access dependent on consent, while B requires financial entities to keep operational registers during ICT incidents. A financial entity can maintain those registers without making user access conditional on consent, so both rules can be obeyed.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De toegang van de gebruiker tot een dienst van de informatiemaatschappij die wordt geleverd door of namens een krachtens publiekrecht ingestelde rechtspersoon wordt niet afhankelijk gemaakt van het verlenen van toestemming als bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Information about incidents involving electronic services and personal-data breach notifications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires covered bodies and organisations to provide the Minister with data and information needed to prevent or end breaches of secure and reliable access to electronic services. Provision B removes the provider’s obligation to notify the affected person where appropriate technical measures make the personal data unintelligible to unauthorised persons; if the information sought under A includes such protected personal data, disclosure could appear to undermine B’s protective purpose.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different recipients and serve different functions: A concerns supplying information to the Minister for security measures, while B concerns notifying the affected data subject about a personal-data breach. A does not expressly require disclosure of intelligible personal data, and B does not prohibit supplying information to the Minister. The encryption exception in B may also mean that no notification duty arises, rather than that all disclosure is forbidden.

verdict.shared_subject: Protection of personal data against incidents involving network and information systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires security measures including policies and procedures concerning cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption, as part of protecting systems and their physical environment against incidents. Provision B provides that notification of a personal-data breach is not required when the provider has taken appropriate technical protective measures making the data encrypted or otherwise unintelligible to unauthorised persons; a broad reading could make A’s security measures relevant to avoiding B’s notification duty, while B’s exception may reduce the practical need to notify after an incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different rules: A is a preventive cybersecurity duty requiring specified measures, while B is an exception to a notification obligation triggered by a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy. Encryption adopted under A can satisfy B’s condition, and nothing in B forbids encryption or prevents compliance with A.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern sanctions imposed by public authorities for legal violations, so an entity could theoretically be subject to enforcement under both regimes. However, the provisions identify different authorities, different regulated conduct, and different sanctions; the texts do not make those sanctions mutually exclusive.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A authorizes a competent authority to impose a periodic penalty payment on an entity providing domain-name registration services for violations of specified articles. Provision B authorizes the Dutch Data Protection Authority to impose an administrative fine for violations of specified GDPR provisions. Both sanctions can coexist because nothing in either text prohibits the other authority or sanction.

verdict.shared_subject: Essential or important entities, including a commanditaire vennootschap and its managing partners
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions concern the same regulated entities and both impose obligations under the same Act. However, Article 24 concerns the application of governance rules to managing partners of a limited partnership, while Article 44 concerns prompt reporting of changes to register information; nothing in either text makes compliance with one prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A managing partner covered by Article 24 can comply with the applicable governance rules and also ensure that the entity reports any change in Article 44 information immediately or within two weeks. The provisions regulate different subject matters—governance and national-register updates—and can be satisfied simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit een commanditaire vennootschap is, is het bepaalde bij of krachtens het eerste tot en met zesde lid van overeenkomstige toepassing op de beherende vennoten van die commanditaire vennootschap.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De entiteiten, bedoeld in het eerste lid, melden Onze Minister onverwijld of in elk geval binnen twee weken na de datum van de wijziging, elke wijziging van de informatie die zij op grond van het eerste lid hebben verstrekt.

verdict.shared_subject: Acceptance and use of identification means for electronic services requiring substantial or high assurance authentication
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 6 requires access to be granted only when the identification means has at least the assurance level required for the service. Article 7 requires public authorities to accept, among other things, all EU-notified and approved schemes, without expressly stating in the excerpt that every such identification means meets the service’s required assurance level; therefore, a qualifying EU-notified means might have to be accepted even if it falls below the required level.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: Article 7 identifies the categories of means that must be accepted, while Article 6 requires that access be granted only where the means meets the required assurance level. The reference in Article 7 to EU-notified and approved schemes may in practice concern means satisfying the relevant assurance requirements, and Article 7(4) also shows that exceptions concern acceptance rules rather than an express relaxation of Article 6.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bestuursorgaan offers an electronic service requiring a high assurance level. A natural person presents an identification means belonging to an EU-notified and approved eIDAS scheme, but the means has only a substantial assurance level. Article 7 appears to require acceptance, while Article 6 permits access only with a high-level means; deciding whether this is a real conflict requires knowing whether the relevant EU-notified means is legally required to meet the service’s required level and how the acceptance rule is qualified.
verdict.missing_reference: The omitted legal provisions governing the assurance level and legal effect of identification means belonging to an EU-notified and approved eIDAS scheme—particularly whether Article 7(1)(c) is limited to means meeting the assurance level required for the service, and any applicable eIDAS or implementing provisions.
