verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data through high-risk remote biometric-identification AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 13 GDPR requires a controller collecting data from a person to provide transparency information, including the existence, logic, significance and expected consequences of automated decision-making. Article 26 AI Act regulates law-enforcement use of retrospective remote biometric identification and permits tightly limited use, documentation and reporting; in a practical police investigation, providing Article 13-style notice could potentially compromise the investigation. However, neither text shown imposes an express duty to withhold notice or an express prohibition on providing it.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties: GDPR Article 13 is an information duty toward a data subject where personal data are collected from that person, while AI Act Article 26 imposes authorisation, necessity, deletion, documentation and reporting duties on deployers of a particular high-risk AI system. Article 26 does not forbid the transparency information required by Article 13, and its operational safeguards can be fulfilled alongside any applicable GDPR information duties. Moreover, law-enforcement processing will often be governed by Directive (EU) 2016/680 rather than GDPR, so the two provisions may not apply to the same processing at all.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het bestaan van geautomatiseerde besluitvorming, met inbegrip van de in artikel 22, leden 1 en 4, bedoelde profilering, en, ten minste in die gevallen, nuttige informatie over de onderliggende logica, alsmede het belang en de verwachte gevolgen van die verwerking voor de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk gebruik wordt beperkt tot hetgeen strikt noodzakelijk is voor het onderzoek naar een specifiek strafbaar feit.

verdict.shared_subject: Delegated rulemaking powers concerning digital-identification-related matters and data provision/investigations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions delegate authority to make further rules, and rules adopted under them could conceivably both affect an organisation handling an electronic identification means and responding to a data-related investigation. However, neither quoted provision itself imposes a substantive obligation, prohibition, deadline, or benchmark on that organisation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 10 of BWBR0048156 requires ministerial rules about use of public identification means and specified facilities. Article 11.11 of BWBR0009950 merely permits an AMvB to set further rules about a separately referenced investigation, data provision, cooperation duty, and notification; the texts establish neither the same regulated activity nor incompatible delegated rules.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling worden regels gesteld met betrekking tot het gebruik van publieke identificatiemiddelen en de voorzieningen, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen nadere regels worden gesteld met betrekking tot: a. het onderzoek, bedoeld in het vierde lid; b. de gegevensverstrekking, bedoeld in het vierde lid; c. de medewerkingsverplichting, bedoeld in het vijfde lid; d. de kennisgeving van de verstrekking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het zesde lid.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A cloud provider, online marketplace, or other listed entity might also be a non-Netherlands-established dienstenverrichter using the central-loket mailbox. However, A only establishes the applicability of a separate statutory regime to listed entities, while B creates an exception to an identification-means acceptance duty for central-loket services; neither text requires conduct incompatible with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate distinct matters: A concerns the territorial application of rules to specified digital-service entities, whereas B excludes two central-loket situations from a duty to accept specified business and organisational identification means. An entity can fall within A's scope and use the B exception without any collision of duties.

verdict.shared_subject: Further processing of personal data, including potentially special-category personal data, for a purpose other than that for which it was obtained.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Where special-category data were processed on the basis of explicit consent for specified purposes, a controller's intended further use for another purpose may exceed that consent. Article 14 requires prior information about the new purpose, but providing that information does not itself obtain new explicit consent or establish another Article 9 exception.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different cumulative conditions rather than incompatible commands: Provision A states when the special-category-data prohibition does not apply, while Provision B requires advance transparency if a controller intends further processing for another purpose. A controller can rely on a valid Article 9 exception and also notify the data subject before the further processing.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voornemens is de persoonsgegevens verder te verwerken voor een ander doel dan dat waarvoor de persoonsgegevens zijn verkregen, verstrekt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke de betrokkene vóór die verdere verwerking informatie over dat andere doel

verdict.shared_subject: Information provision by a public authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information-sharing obligations on an authority, so an authority that is both a CSIRT and an AI notifying authority could potentially need to manage disclosures to different recipients. However, neither text imposes an incompatible confidentiality rule, deadline, or content requirement.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns a CSIRT forwarding information about reported cyber incidents, near-incidents, or cyber threats involving entities that are both essential and critical entities, to a critical-entities authority. Provision B concerns a notifying authority supplying the European Commission, on request, with information about the notification or continuing competence of a notified conformity-assessment body; these are distinct regulated subjects and triggers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het CSIRT verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een incident, bijna-incident of cyberdreiging
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanmeldende autoriteit verstrekt de Commissie op verzoek alle relevante informatie over de aanmelding of het op peil houden van de bekwaamheid van de betrokken aangemelde instantie.

verdict.shared_subject: Publicatie door overheidsorganen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Als een orgaan op grond van nadere regels een verklaring op zijn website moet publiceren, kan een zeer ruim geformuleerde publicatieplicht praktisch raken aan de vraag wanneer informatie over toezicht of naleving openbaar wordt. Artikel 21b beschermt echter specifiek de overtreder tegen vroege openbaarmaking van een beschikking, terwijl artikel 3 slechts een bevoegdheid schept om standaardenverklaringen en auditverklaringen voor organen voor te schrijven.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen betreffen verschillende documenten en adressaten: A beperkt de timing van openbaarmaking van een aan een overtreder bekendgemaakte beschikking; B staat toe dat bij AMvB regels worden gesteld over publicatie door organen van een actuele standaardenverklaring. B vereist zelf geen publicatie van handhavingsbeschikkingen en bevat bovendien slechts een regelgevende bevoegdheid.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De openbaarmaking van de beschikking geschiedt niet eerder dan nadat tien werkdagen zijn verstreken na de dag waarop de beschikking aan de overtreder bekend is gemaakt
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen nadere regels worden gesteld. Onder meer kan worden bepaald dat organen op hun website een actuele verklaring over de toepassing van de aangewezen standaard publiceren

verdict.shared_subject: Ministerial alteration or termination of a registration/recognition involving regulated entities or electronic-service providers.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the Minister to amend, refuse or terminate a national-register entry when its registration basis has changed, lapsed or is absent. If an entity that supplies a crucial electronic identification service loses the basis for registration, termination could undermine the continuity objective that Provision B permits the Minister to protect by requiring continued activities after withdrawal of recognition.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions govern different legal instruments and contexts: A concerns entries in the national register of essential/important entities under a regime whose competent authority is the health minister for medical-device manufacture, while B concerns withdrawal of an electronic-identification recognition by the interior minister. A changes a register entry; it neither prohibits the entity from operating nor prevents a separate continuity order under B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister wijzigt, weigert of beëindigt in overeenstemming met de bevoegde autoriteit die het aangaat een in het eerste lid bedoelde registratie, indien de grond voor registratie is gewijzigd, vervallen of ontbreekt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een erkenning kan op verzoek van de houder worden ingetrokken. Onze Minister kan bij dit besluit de houder verplichten zijn activiteiten voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.

verdict.shared_subject: Both provisions use the term "aanbieder", but in materially different regulatory contexts.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both impose an obligation following a request and could, at a high level, concern an entity described as an "aanbieder". One might speculate that investigations and disclosure obligations could create administrative burdens alongside AI-conformity documentation duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns a telecom provider's investigation of a subscriber's request for identifying information about a blocked nuisance or malicious caller. Provision B concerns an AI notified body's duty to provide conformity-assessment documentation to its notifying authority; it neither governs the telecom investigation nor requires incompatible disclosure or non-disclosure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder stelt naar aanleiding van het verzoek een onderzoek in, teneinde vast te stellen of tot verstrekking van de gegevens, bedoeld in het eerste lid, dient te worden overgegaan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties stellen alle relevante documentatie, waaronder de documentatie van de aanbieder, ter beschikking van de in artikel 28 bedoelde aanmeldende autoriteit, en verstrekken die aan haar op verzoek

verdict.shared_subject: Notification to data subjects and the supervisory authority after a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A states that notification to both the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens and the affected person must include specified information. Provision B says communication to the affected person is not required where, for example, effective protective measures were applied, subsequent measures remove the likely high risk, or individual communication would be disproportionate.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate together: A regulates the minimum content of a notification when one is made, while B supplies GDPR exceptions to the duty to notify the data subject. A does not expressly say that notification must be made regardless of statutory exceptions, and B does not relax the required content of a communication that is required or voluntarily made.
verdict.decisive_exception: GDPR Article 34(3)(a)-(c): the data-subject communication is not required if effective protection such as encryption was applied, subsequent measures eliminate the likely high risk, or individual communication would require disproportionate effort (with effective public communication instead).
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde mededeling aan de betrokkene is niet vereist wanneer een van de volgende voorwaarden is vervuld:

verdict.shared_subject: Enterprises/legal entities in digital-service regulation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern an enterprise: provision A extends certain governance obligations to every partner of a partnership that is an essential or important entity, while provision B concerns rules for recognised services enabling reliable electronic access for enterprises or legal persons. A partner could conceivably be involved in an entity using such electronic services.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: They regulate wholly different matters. A allocates the applicability of pre-existing governance rules within a vennootschap onder firma; B requires ministerial rules on how recognised services use a designated attribute for reliable electronic access. Neither provision prescribes conduct that contradicts, benchmarks, or conditions the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit een vennootschap onder firma is, is het bepaalde bij of krachtens het eerste tot en met zesde lid van overeenkomstige toepassing op iedere vennoot van die vennootschap onder firma.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een attribuut wordt aangewezen worden bij ministeriële regeling regels gesteld over de wijze waarop het aangewezen attribuut door de erkende diensten bij hun activiteiten moet worden betrokken, voor zover dat nodig is voor een betrouwbare toegang van ondernemingen of rechtspersonen tot elektronische dienstverlening.

verdict.shared_subject: Beveiliging/ICT-risico's bij een financiële entiteit die persoonsgegevens verwerkt
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Een financiële entiteit kan na een ICT-incident zowel moeten beoordelen of persoonsgegevens zijn geraakt als haar ICT-risico's opnieuw moeten identificeren. Artikel 34 AVG maakt onder voorwaarden echter bekendmaking aan betrokkenen overbodig, terwijl DORA voortdurende risico-identificatie verlangt; dit zou feitelijk kunnen betekenen dat een incident intern wordt onderzocht zonder individuele kennisgeving.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen regelen verschillende handelingen zonder tegengestelde uitkomst: artikel 34 AVG bepaalt uitsluitend wanneer mededeling aan betrokkenen niet vereist is na een datalek met hoog risico, terwijl artikel 8 DORA financiële entiteiten verplicht ICT-risico's en dreigingen doorlopend te identificeren en scenario's jaarlijks te evalueren. Interne risico-identificatie verhindert geen kennisgeving wanneer die onder de AVG nodig is, en de AVG-vrijstelling verhindert de DORA-risicobeoordeling niet.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 bedoelde mededeling aan de betrokkene is niet vereist wanneer een van de volgende voorwaarden is vervuld:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten identificeren permanent alle bronnen van ICT-risico

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/cyber-incident compliance involving regulated entities and critical third-party ICT service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A critical third-party ICT provider could also be an essential or important entity and, during an unresolved incident, may be subject both to an obligation to submit a progress report and to a daily coercive fine intended to compel compliance. The financial enforcement pressure could make the reporting and remediation situation practically burdensome, but neither text makes the required acts inconsistent.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A imposes an incident-reporting timetable on essential or important entities: a progress report if the incident continues, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Provision B instead limits the period for which a lead overseer may impose a daily coercive fine on a critical third-party ICT provider; it neither alters nor prohibits the reports required by A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 6 bedoelde dwangsom wordt dagelijks opgelegd tot aan de verplichtingen is voldaan, gedurende een termijn van ten hoogste zes maanden volgend op de kennisgeving van het besluit een dwangsom op te leggen aan de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Information provided to natural persons in relation to digital/AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern informing natural persons, and an AI provider may also be a GDPR controller. However, Article 34 concerns whether a data-breach notification is required after a high-risk personal-data breach, whereas Article 50 concerns upfront disclosure that a person is interacting with an AI system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern distinct events and information: Article 34(3) creates exceptions to notifying affected data subjects of a personal-data breach, while Article 50 requires a directly interactive AI system to disclose its AI nature unless that is already obvious. A provider can design its system to make the AI interaction apparent and, independently, rely on Article 34(3) only where the stated breach-notice conditions are met.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders zorgen ervoor dat AI-systemen die voor directe interactie met natuurlijke personen zijn bedoeld, zodanig worden ontworpen en ontwikkeld dat de betrokken natuurlijke personen worden geïnformeerd dat zij interageren met een AI-systeem

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative enforcement powers and administrative fines
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions empower a public authority to impose an administrative fine on an entity for statutory infringements. If one undertaking were subject to both regimes, overlapping enforcement could potentially expose it to different authorities and materially different maximum penalties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions confer enforcement competences under different statutes and for different enumerated underlying violations: A concerns domain-name-registration-service entities breaching specified provisions or an information-cooperation duty, while B concerns breaches of a long list of separate provisions. Neither provision requires conduct that the other prohibits, nor do their penalty ceilings create an operational duty for the regulated entity that cannot be jointly met.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor may be required by B to maintain a record of all categories of processing activities, including categories involving special-category data. If creating or maintaining that record itself involved processing identifiable special-category data, A's prohibition would require an applicable Article 9 exception.

verdict.shared_subject: Handling cybersecurity vulnerabilities/incidents, including the treatment of personal data connected with reports or incident response.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If a vulnerability report also reveals a personal-data breach, the designated CSIRT could need to preserve the reporter's anonymity under Provision B while a competent authority participating in the same handling must provide the Dutch Data Protection Authority with all necessary data, including personal data, under Provision A. If the reporter's identity were genuinely necessary to the joint breach handling, those duties could pull in opposite directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires exchange only of data that are necessary for handling a personal-data-breach incident; it does not specifically require disclosure of a vulnerability reporter's identity. verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A controller might treat measures recorded or updated in the AI Act fundamental-rights assessment as sufficient remediation after an AI-related data breach. verdict.shared_subject: Operational and organisational obligations of providers/organisations, including security-related measures and processing-record obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A public electronic-communications provider may be required by Provision A to implement technical, operational and organisational security measures, while GDPR Article 30 exempts some organisations with fewer than 250 employees from the Article 30 record-keeping obligations. One might argue that the national security regime's operational measures could include documentation that overlaps with GDPR-style records.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different duties: A requires communications-network/service providers to manage network or service security risks for national security and public-order purposes; B defines a limited exemption from GDPR processing-activity registers for smaller organisations. Article 30's exemption neither prohibits A's security measures nor relieves a provider from duties imposed under other legislation.

verdict.shared_subject: Ministerial recognition of an ontsluitende dienst (routing service) under BWBR0048156
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 11 uses mandatory language requiring the Minister to recognise an ontsluitende service once it complies with the applicable AMvB rules. Article 9 likewise uses mandatory language requiring refusal where there is a serious danger to cybersecurity, state security, criminal misuse, or the reliability and security of the Dutch electronic-services system; an ontsluitende service can fall within both provisions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be read as cumulative recognition conditions: compliance with the AMvB rules is necessary for recognition under article 11, while article 9 supplies an overriding negative ground requiring refusal despite such compliance. This harmonising reading is consistent with article 9's broad concern for the safety and reliability of the recognition regime, although article 11 does not expressly make its command subject to article 9.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A private ontsluitende dienst routes access between municipalities and recognised authentication providers. It satisfies every applicable AMvB rule governing ontsluitende diensten, so article 11 says the Minister must recognise it. However, an integrity assessment establishes a serious cybersecurity risk—for example, that its foreign-controlled infrastructure could enable compromise of access to public services—so article 9 says the Minister must refuse the recognition. On the wording shown, the Minister cannot both grant and refuse that recognition.

verdict.shared_subject: Exercise of GDPR Chapter III data-subject rights by minors or persons represented by a legal representative, including in journalistic, academic, artistic, or literary processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 43 broadly disapplies the Act for processing exclusively for journalistic, academic, artistic, or literary purposes. If Article 5's representation rules were among the disapplied provisions, a child or legally represented person's mechanism for exercising GDPR rights could be removed in those contexts.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 43 expressly excepts Article 5(1) and (2) from its disapplication: the Act is not applicable "met uitzondering van de artikelen 1, 2, 3, 4 en 5, eerste en tweede lid." Thus, rather than displacing the relevant Article 5 rules, the journalistic/expression exemption preserves them.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity notifications and the handling of information reported to national cybersecurity bodies.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A coordinator handling a voluntary vulnerability disclosure must guarantee the reporter's anonymity, while B requires a central contact point, on request, to forward received notifications to other Member States' central contact points. If the same report and its identifying information were treated as both a vulnerability report and a cross-border incident notification, onward transmission could risk exposing the reporter.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions govern different reporting streams and actors: A concerns voluntary reports of ICT vulnerabilities and the coordinator's protection of the reporter's anonymity; B concerns notifications received under Article 23(1), namely significant-incident reports, and transmission by a central contact point. B does not require disclosure of a vulnerability reporter's identity, and nothing shown establishes that A's voluntary reports are among B's notifications.

verdict.shared_subject: Electronic access to a ministerial national-register reporting mechanism
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If an essential or important entity had to use a public identification means to access the mechanism for submitting Article 44 information, Article 8 could limit that identification means to electronic services by public bodies or designated organisations. But the Minister receiving Article 44 information is a public body, so the use would ordinarily fall within Article 8's permitted purpose.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 44 requires specified entities to provide registration information to the Minister through a designated mechanism. Article 8 only restricts the purposes for which a public identification means and related facility may be used; it does not prohibit reporting information to a public authority, and electronic service provision by a public body is expressly within its permitted domain.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/data-security measures and incident handling by a financial entity that is also a provider subject to Dutch telecommunications privacy-breach rules
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A can remove the obligation to notify affected individuals after a personal-data breach where the data are rendered unintelligible, whereas Provision B requires governance arrangements and internal reporting channels concerning serious ICT incidents and their consequences. One might argue that an encryption-based decision not to notify individuals could reduce transparency about an incident that the financial entity's management must address.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different matters: A is a conditional exemption from notifying data subjects, while B requires the financial entity's management body to govern ICT risk, security, resilience, and internal information flows. A financial entity can rely on A's notification exemption while still documenting, escalating, assessing, responding to, and governing the incident fully under B.

However, neither text connects the designation decision to the third-country-transfer proceeding or to the no-remedy rule.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate wholly different matters. A concerns the unappealability of the Administrative Jurisdiction Division's decision to hold a request concerning infringements of the third-country-transfer regulation; B concerns ministerial power to designate certain electronic-service organisations for purposes of another statute.

verdict.shared_subject: Procedural publication/regulation rules in Dutch digital-law-related legislation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits ministerial rules specifying cases in which the Dutch Data Protection Authority's consultation duty for certain policy rules applies. Provision B requires publication in the Staatscourant of a decision to designate or withdraw a designation. If a ministerial rule under A addressed designation-related procedures, one might argue that its consultation framework could affect how such decisions are made.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts and actors: A concerns ministerial rulemaking about the AP's consultation duty before adopting certain policy rules, whereas B imposes a publication requirement for designation/withdrawal decisions. Nothing in A dispenses with, delays, or prohibits B's Staatscourant publication, and nothing in B restricts ministerial rules under A.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of public electronic identification means in connection with financial entities' ICT incident-response recordkeeping
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity that is also an "aangewezen organisatie" could use a public identification means to authenticate staff accessing incident registers. Article 8 limits that means to access to electronic services by public bodies and designated organisations, while Article 11 requires accessible incident-activity registers; if accessibility were interpreted as requiring broad access through that public means, the two could pull in different directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different matters: Article 8 restricts the purposes for which a public identification means may be used, whereas Article 11 requires financial entities to retain accessible records when specified ICT plans are activated. Article 11 neither requires use of a public identification means nor dictates any particular authentication method, so the registers can be made accessible through compliant internal access controls.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten houden gemakkelijk toegankelijke registers bij van hun activiteiten vóór en tijdens storingen wanneer hun ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsplannen en ICT-respons- en herstelplannen worden geactiveerd.

verdict.shared_subject: BWBR0048156 and the designation and publication of electronic-traffic standards
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern decisions under the same instrument, so one might initially ask whether the conditions for designating a standard must be reconciled with the publication requirement. However, Article 3 governs when a standard may be designated, while Article 17 governs how certain decisions are announced; neither requires or forbids conduct required by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 3 permits designation by general administrative order only if the listed necessity, procedural-accessibility, and free-or-reasonable-access conditions are met. Article 17 separately requires notification of specified decisions by publication in the Staatscourant; an authority can satisfy both requirements without contradiction.

The texts do not require either actor to disclose information that the other provision requires to remain anonymous.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose independent duties in different regulatory contexts and can be fully complied with simultaneously. The coordinator can follow up on a vulnerability report while preserving the reporter’s anonymity, and the notifying authority can separately inform the Commission and Member States of relevant changes to a notified body’s notification.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing personal data by a temporary committee or advisory body and informing the data subject
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns an exception to the prohibition on processing special-category and criminal-offence data, while provision B requires a controller collecting personal data to provide extensive information, including information about rights and automated decision-making. A committee relying on A may therefore have to process sensitive data while also complying with B's transparency duties, creating an apparent overlap but no incompatible command.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative requirements: A permits processing only when its stated conditions are met, while B requires information to be supplied when personal data are collected from the data subject. The committee can satisfy both by meeting A's safeguards and giving the information required by B; neither provision forbids the other's conduct or makes compliance with one substitute for compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data, including potentially special-category personal data, and the controller’s information duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts processing of special-category personal data unless one of the listed Article 9(2) exceptions applies. Provision B requires a controller that obtained personal data from another source to provide information about the processing, including the categories of data and legal basis; if the data are special-category data, complying with B may presuppose processing that A permits only under an applicable exception.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties: A determines when processing special-category data is lawful, while B governs transparency when personal data were not obtained from the data subject. A controller can comply with both by processing only where an Article 9(2) exception applies and then providing the Article 14 information, subject to Article 14’s own exceptions.

verdict.shared_subject: Public disclosure of legal or administrative consequences
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives a court broad competence to regulate all other consequences of suspending board members, which could theoretically include consequences affecting publicity or disclosure. Provision B, however, specifically requires a competent authority to publish information about administrative sanctions and later appeal outcomes, so a court-ordered consequence might appear to intersect with that publication duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns the court’s residual competence concerning the consequences of suspending board members, while Provision B imposes a publication duty on a competent authority concerning administrative sanctions. Neither provision says that a court’s regulation of suspension consequences may suppress, alter, or exempt the authority from the publication duty; both can therefore be complied with independently.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and subsequent handling by public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related notifications, and a high-risk AI provider could voluntarily submit an incident notification to a CSIRT while also being required to notify a market-surveillance authority. The CSIRT may prioritise mandatory notifications over voluntary ones, which might appear to create a risk of delayed handling compared with the seven-day action duty in Article 73.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 33 governs how a CSIRT processes voluntary cybersecurity reports and expressly makes them optional; Article 73 imposes a separate seven-day duty on a market-surveillance authority after receiving a serious-incident notification from a high-risk AI provider. The provisions concern different notifications, authorities, and duties, and nothing in Article 33 excuses or prevents the Article 73 notification or its seven-day response.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity information exchange and security measures for public electronic communications networks or services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the competent authorities, CSIRTs and central contact point to exchange information necessary for a NIS2 peer review. Provision B allows the Minister to impose security-related measures on providers of public electronic communications networks or services, so an information exchange could theoretically concern a provider or security matter also subject to such a measure.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable functions on different actors: A concerns inter-authority cooperation and information exchange for a peer review, while B concerns the Minister’s competence to impose measures on communications providers. Nothing in either text prohibits the exchange required by A or makes it incompatible with imposing measures under B.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory legal language, so one might initially suspect that the obligation to submit a confidential report could somehow require use of a telecommunications facility in a way that supplies incorrect information. But the texts regulate entirely different conduct: one concerns misleading a called user through network-number information, while the other concerns periodic reporting by the ESAs.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly be obeyed together. Article 11.10a prohibits using a network-number facility to provide false information to a called user; Article 44 requires the ESAs to submit a confidential international-cooperation report every five years. Compliance with the reporting obligation does not require any prohibited use of network-number information.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory obligations concerning regulated entities and authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a critical third-party ICT service provider to submit to on-site inspections ordered by the lead overseer. Provision B requires a notified body to ensure that subcontractors or subsidiaries meet Article 31 requirements and to notify the notifying authority; however, it does not prohibit or limit submission to inspections, and it addresses a different regulatory role.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors in different regulatory schemes: A concerns a critical ICT third-party provider and inspections by a lead overseer, while B concerns a notified conformity-assessment body and its subcontractors or subsidiaries. Even if an entity were subject to both regimes, it could comply with both by submitting to inspections and separately ensuring subcontractor compliance and notifying the authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten onderwerpt zich aan de inspecties ter plaatse die bij besluit van de lead overseer zijn gelast.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de aangemelde instantie specifieke taken in verband met de conformiteits-beoordeling door een onderaannemer of door een dochteronderneming laat uitvoeren, waarborgt zij dat de onderaannemer of dochteronderneming aan de eisen van artikel 31 voldoet, en brengt zij de aanmeldende autoriteit hiervan op de hoogte.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data, including special-category personal data, and the data subject’s right to restriction of processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits processing special-category personal data unless one of its listed exceptions applies. Provision B requires a controller to notify a data subject before lifting a restriction on processing, which presupposes that some processing may continue or resume. In a case where the restriction concerns special-category data and no Article 22 exception applies, B could appear to require conduct that A prohibits.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not itself authorise processing or require the controller to lift a restriction; it only requires prior notification if a restriction obtained under Article 18(1) is to be lifted. The controller can comply with both by maintaining the restriction or by lifting it only where processing is permitted under A or another applicable legal basis.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed for the compatibility classification: Article 18(2) does not override the prohibition in Article 22. If the restriction concerns special-category data and no exception permits processing, the controller must not resume processing; if it lawfully resumes processing, it must notify the data subject beforehand.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing biometric data through real-time remote biometric identification for law-enforcement purposes in public spaces
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits processing special-category personal data unless one of its listed Article 9(2) grounds applies. Provision B permits or requires a judicial or administrative authorisation for a narrowly defined use of real-time remote biometric identification, but the text shown does not establish that this authorisation is itself an Article 9(2) legal basis satisfying Provision A. Thus, the same use could be authorised under the AI Act yet remain prohibited under the special-category-data regime.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: an operator may use the biometric system only after satisfying the AI Act’s necessity, proportionality, authorisation, and other safeguards, and may additionally process biometric data only where an Article 9(2) exception applies. Provision B does not expressly override Provision A; indeed, the related text says Article 9 GDPR remains applicable to biometric-data processing for other purposes, so the AI authorisation need not displace the data-processing prohibition.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A law-enforcement authority seeks to use real-time facial recognition in a public square to locate a suspect in a qualifying serious offence, obtains the judicial authorisation required by Provision B, and satisfies B’s necessity and proportionality conditions, but the facts do not show that the suspect or other identified persons consented, that the data were made public, or that any other Article 9(2) ground listed in Provision A applies. The authority therefore has B authorisation while the biometric-data processing may still be prohibited by A.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the judicial or independent-administrative authorisation and the law-enforcement purpose under Provision B constitute, or are accompanied by, an applicable Article 9(2) exception to the prohibition on processing special-category biometric data under Provision A is not established by the texts shown.

verdict.shared_subject: Rules concerning the reliability and accuracy of services or data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use reliability-related language, and both contemplate rules being set by subordinate legislation. One could argue that reliability of an identification service or business/organisational means overlaps with reliability of data supplied under the communications regime.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns the competence to set rules for the operation, interoperability, security and reliability of recognised identification services or means. Provision B concerns the accuracy and reliability of data supplied under the separate electronic-communications emergency-number regime. They regulate different objects, actors and statutory contexts, and nothing in either text makes compliance with one substitute for compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De regels, bedoeld in het eerste tot en met derde lid, hebben betrekking op de werking, interoperabiliteit, beveiliging en betrouwbaarheid van de diensten of het bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel
verdict.evidence_span_b: regels gesteld met betrekking tot de nauwkeurigheid en betrouwbaarheid van de te verstrekken gegevens

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions mention a procedure handled by a public body, so one might initially suspect that the CSIRT’s processing of a voluntary cyber incident report could overlap with the supervisory authority’s prior-consultation procedure. However, neither text imposes an incompatible deadline, prohibition, or substantive requirement on the same actor or activity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns the CSIRT processing voluntary cybersecurity reports and permits it to prioritise mandatory reports. Provision B concerns a supervisory authority’s written advice and powers following a GDPR prior-consultation request; the two procedures can operate independently and nothing in either provision prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het CSIRT verwerkt de vrijwillige meldingen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, overeenkomstig de in artikel 36 omschreven procedure.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de toezichthoudende autoriteit van oordeel is dat de in lid 1 bedoelde voorgenomen verwerking inbreuk zou maken op deze verordening, met name wanneer de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke het risico onvoldoende heeft onderkend of beperkt, geeft de toezichthoudende autoriteit binnen een maximumtermijn van acht weken na de ontvangst van het verzoek om raadpleging schriftelijk advies aan de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en in voorkomend geval aan de verwerker, en mag zij al haar in artikel 58 bedoelde bevoegdheden uitoefenen.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing health data and conditioning access to a public-sector information-society service on user consent
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A regulates confidentiality when health data are processed under specified exceptions; provision B prohibits making access to a public-law entity’s information-society service dependent on consent under the referenced consent rule. A possible factual overlap exists if health data are stored on or accessed from a user’s device in connection with such a service, but neither text says that confidentiality duties require consent or that consent is needed for the health-data processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different conduct: A requires secrecy by persons processing health data, while B forbids conditioning service access on the user’s consent to device storage or access. An operator can comply with both by keeping qualifying health data confidential and not making service access conditional on that consent.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien toepassing wordt gegeven aan het eerste, tweede of derde lid, worden de gegevens alleen verwerkt door personen die uit hoofde van ambt, beroep of wettelijk voorschrift dan wel krachtens een overeenkomst tot geheimhouding zijn verplicht.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De toegang van de gebruiker tot een dienst van de informatiemaatschappij die wordt geleverd door of namens een krachtens publiekrecht ingestelde rechtspersoon wordt niet afhankelijk gemaakt van het verlenen van toestemming als bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory obligations concerning ICT or conformity-assessment entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations on regulated organisations, but they concern different conduct: Provision A requires financial entities to detect anomalous activities and test those mechanisms, while Provision B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit a notification application to the competent authority. No incompatible act, deadline, or substantive requirement appears.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A financial entity can maintain and test the detection mechanisms required by Article 10 while a conformity-assessment body submits its notification application under Article 29. The provisions address different actors and different obligations, so compliance with one does not prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten beschikken over mechanismen om overeenkomstig artikel 17 afwijkende activiteiten zo spoedig mogelijk te detecteren
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions both concern public-law institutions and legal procedures in a broad sense, so one might initially suspect that a mandatory standards regime could affect proceedings involving the Raad van State. However, neither provision regulates the same conduct or imposes an incompatible requirement.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns the availability of a legal remedy against the administrative-law division's decision to retain a request. Provision B concerns an administrative measure determining the scope, covered bodies, and commencement date of obligations to apply designated electronic-communication standards; compliance with that standards regime does not require or prohibit bringing a remedy against the decision described in A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Tegen het aanhouden van het verzoek door de Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak van de Raad van State, staat geen voorziening open.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij algemene maatregel van bestuur wordt bepaald: a. het functionele toepassingsbereik van een aangewezen standaard, b. de organen waarvoor de verplichting tot toepassing van een aangewezen standaard geldt, en c. de datum waarop de verplichting tot toepassing van een aangewezen standaard ingaat.

verdict.shared_subject: EU-regulated financial entities and cybersecurity/ICT-incident obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A can remove the NIS2 provisions, including supervision and enforcement, for entities covered by an equivalent sector-specific Union act. Provision B separately requires non-micro financial entities to provide aggregated annual ICT-incident cost estimates on request, so one might ask whether the sector-specific exclusion also displaces that reporting duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns the non-application of relevant NIS2 provisions where equivalent sector-specific requirements exist; it does not state that obligations under DORA, including Provision B, are displaced. Provision B is an independent DORA obligation, and the texts do not establish that its reporting requirement is a NIS2 obligation or that Article 4 overrides it.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien sectorspecifieke rechtshandelingen van de Unie voorschrijven dat essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten risicobeheersmaatregelen op het gebied van cyberbeveiliging moeten nemen of significante incidenten moeten melden, en indien deze eisen ten minste gelijkwaardig zijn aan de in deze richtlijn vastgestelde verplichtingen, zijn de relevante bepalingen van deze richtlijn, met inbegrip van de in hoofdstuk VII bedoelde toezichts- en handhavingsbepalingen, niet van toepassing op dergelijke entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Andere financiële entiteiten dan micro-ondernemingen verstrekken de bevoegde autoriteiten op hun verzoek een raming van de geaggregeerde jaarlijkse kosten en verliezen als gevolg van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten.

verdict.shared_subject: Journalistic, academic, artistic or literary processing of personal data and the data subject’s right to erasure
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A makes Articles 9 and 10 inapplicable where processing is necessary for a journalistic, academic, artistic or literary purpose. Provision B gives the data subject a right to erasure and obliges the controller to erase data in listed circumstances. Thus, a controller might argue that the purpose-based derogation permits retaining or processing data even when an Article 17 ground for erasure is present.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts shown do not establish that Provision A displaces Article 17: it expressly concerns only Articles 9 and 10, not Article 17. Moreover, Article 17(3)(a) expressly provides that the erasure right does not apply insofar as processing is necessary for exercising freedom of expression and information, which can cover journalistic and related expression interests; the provisions can therefore operate cumulatively, subject to that specific exception.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether Article 17(3)(a), and its application to the particular journalistic, academic, artistic or literary processing, removes the erasure obligation. The text shown supplies that exception for freedom of expression and information, but Provision A itself does not extend its derogation to Article 17.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De artikelen 9 en 10 van de verordening zijn niet van toepassing voor zover de verwerking van de in die artikelen bedoelde gegevens noodzakelijk is voor het journalistieke doel of de academische, artistieke of literaire uitdrukkingsvorm.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De betrokkene heeft het recht van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging wissing van hem betreffende persoonsgegevens te verkrijgen en de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke is verplicht persoonsgegevens zonder onredelijke vertraging te wissen wanneer een van de volgende gevallen van toepassing is:

verdict.shared_subject: Ministerial decisions concerning registrations or recognitions of entities or identification services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern a minister changing or ending an authorisation-like status. One might argue that ending a registration under provision A could undermine continuity of electronic services, while provision B permits withdrawal of an acknowledgement and continuation obligations to preserve continuity. However, the provisions address different statuses, ministers, and regulatory contexts, and neither requires or forbids the action governed by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires the competent minister to modify, refuse, or terminate a registration when its legal basis has changed, lapsed, or is absent. Provision B concerns withdrawal of an acknowledgement at the holder’s request and gives the Minister of the Interior discretion to require continued activity for a period when necessary to safeguard continuity; these duties and powers can operate independently and cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister wijzigt, weigert of beëindigt in overeenstemming met de bevoegde autoriteit die het aangaat een in het eerste lid bedoelde registratie, indien de grond voor registratie is gewijzigd, vervallen of ontbreekt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een erkenning kan op verzoek van de houder worden ingetrokken. Onze Minister kan bij dit besluit de houder verplichten zijn activiteiten voort te zetten gedurende een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode, voor zover dat nodig is om continuïteit van betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te borgen.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-system governance and operational resilience in regulated financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require ICT systems to be managed in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, but they apply to different regulated entities and impose entity-specific organisational or continuity requirements. The texts do not prescribe incompatible ICT standards, duties, deadlines, or permissions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A credit-rating agency can comply with Provision A by maintaining the specified administrative, control, risk-assessment, and ICT security arrangements, while a CCP or trade repository can comply with Provision B by maintaining the specified organisational, business-continuity, and ICT systems. The shared DORA reference coordinates the requirements rather than creating a conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een ratingbureau beschikt over een goede administratieve en boekhoudkundige organisatie, adequate interne controleprocedures, effectieve risicobeoordelingsprocedures en effectieve controle- en beveiligingsvoorzieningen voor het beheer van ICT-systemen in overeenstemming met Verordening (EU) 2022/2554
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een CTP beschikt over en werkt in het kader van een organisatiestructuur die de continuïteit en ordelijke werking bij het verrichten van haar diensten en activiteiten garandeert.

verdict.shared_subject: AI-based identification involving personal-data processing and human oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the controller to build safeguards into processing to comply with GDPR principles and protect data-subject rights, while provision B prohibits the user of certain high-risk AI systems from acting on system identification unless two qualified natural persons separately verify and confirm it. One might argue that A's technology-and-organisation safeguards could be implemented through the AI system itself, whereas B requires an additional human-verification step.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, compatible requirements on different aspects of the activity: A requires privacy-by-design measures for personal-data processing, and B requires a specific human-oversight procedure for high-risk identification systems. Compliance with A does not purport to replace B's separate verification requirement, so a controller/user can satisfy both by implementing A's safeguards and ensuring the required human checks before acting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: treft de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, zowel bij de bepaling van de verwerkingsmiddelen als bij de verwerking zelf, passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen
verdict.evidence_span_b: geen maatregelen worden getroffen of beslissingen worden genomen op basis van de identificatie door het systeem, tenzij deze identificatie door ten minste twee natuurlijke personen met de nodige bekwaamheid, opleiding en bevoegdheid apart zijn geverifieerd en bevestigd

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory consequences for entities handling personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A creates an exception to notifying affected persons where appropriate technical safeguards make the data unintelligible to unauthorised persons. Provision B requires administrative fines for important entities that infringe separate cybersecurity duties in Articles 21 or 23; one might argue that a protected breach under A should not attract sanctions, but B does not make its fines depend on whether notification under A was required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different matters: A concerns whether a provider must notify affected individuals after a personal-data breach, while B concerns fines for infringement of Articles 21 or 23. An entity can comply with both by applying A's notification exception where its conditions are met and avoiding, or accepting the consequences of, any separate Article 21 or 23 infringement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet vereist indien de aanbieder naar het oordeel van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens gepaste technische beschermingsmaatregelen heeft genomen waardoor de persoonsgegevens die het betreft, versleuteld of anderszins onbegrijpelijk zijn voor een ieder die geen recht heeft op toegang tot die gegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De lidstaten zorgen ervoor dat belangrijke entiteiten die inbreuk maken op artikel 21 of 23 overeenkomstig de leden 2 en 3 van dit artikel onderworpen worden aan administratieve geldboeten met een maximumbedrag van ten minste 7 000 000 EUR of ten minste 1,4 % van de totale wereldwijde jaaromzet in het voorgaande boekjaar van de onderneming waartoe de belangrijke entiteit behoort, afhankelijk van welk bedrag hoger is.

verdict.shared_subject: The duties of competent authorities when carrying out their statutory tasks, including information exchange and confidentiality.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities to exchange all necessary data, expressly including personal data. Provision B requires national competent authorities to comply with confidentiality obligations, so an exchange could appear problematic if the information is confidential or otherwise restricted.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be obeyed cumulatively: authorities may exchange necessary information under A while applying the confidentiality safeguards required by B, including limiting disclosure and protecting the information. Provision B does not prohibit information exchange, and A does not require disclosure contrary to applicable confidentiality rules.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteiten werken met elkaar samen voor de doeltreffende en doelmatige uitvoering van hun taken uit hoofde van deze wet en wisselen daartoe onderling alle daarvoor noodzakelijke gegevens uit, waaronder persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij de uitvoering van hun taken voldoen de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten aan de in artikel 78 vastgelegde vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data for journalistic, academic, artistic or literary purposes and processing for other purposes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A excludes most of its law from applying to processing exclusively for journalistic or academic, artistic or literary expression. Provision B prohibits using the relevant personal data for other purposes without the data subject’s explicit consent, so an expressive-purpose processor might appear exempt from A while still being restricted by B. However, the shown text does not establish that B’s data category or prohibition applies to the processing covered by A, nor that A overrides B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: A defines an exclusion from the scope of one statute, while B independently restricts subsequent or other-purpose processing of the data it covers. A processor can comply with both by limiting processing to the exclusive expressive purpose and, where B applies to another purpose, obtaining explicit consent or relying on the stated statutory exceptions.
verdict.decisive_exception: Not needed for the compatibility verdict. Although the contextual paragraph mentions exceptions for fraud investigation or processing required by law, the text shown does not establish that those exceptions create a conflict with Provision A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Deze wet, met uitzondering van de artikelen 1, 2, 3, 4 en 5, eerste en tweede lid, is niet van toepassing op de verwerking van persoonsgegevens voor uitsluitend journalistieke doeleinden en ten behoeve van uitsluitend academische, artistieke of literaire uitdrukkingsvormen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in het eerste lid bedoelde persoonsgegevens worden niet voor andere doeleinden verzameld of verwerkt, tenzij de betrokkene daarvoor zijn uitdrukkelijke toestemming heeft gegeven.

verdict.shared_subject: The scope of cybersecurity obligations for certain digital-service entities versus acceptance of identification means for cross-border electronic public services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern digital-service activity, but they regulate different matters. Provision A determines which entities fall within the cybersecurity law, while provision B creates an exception to an identification-acceptance duty for services provided through the central portal to service providers not established in the Netherlands.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose no incompatible commands: A is a jurisdictional/scope rule for DNS, cloud, marketplace and other listed providers, whereas B concerns Dutch administrative bodies and designated organisations accepting identification means in specified cross-border services. An entity can comply with both by applying the cybersecurity law where A makes it applicable and applying B's stated exception where relevant.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het bepaalde bij of krachtens deze wet met betrekking tot essentiële entiteiten en belangrijke entiteiten van toepassing op de volgende entiteiten
verdict.evidence_span_b: De plicht om uitsluitend de in het tweede lid bedoelde identificatiemiddelen en verklaringen te accepteren, is niet van toepassing ten aanzien van

verdict.shared_subject: An entity subject to the NIS2-register information duty that may also be a GDPR controller or processor
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires qualifying entities to provide specified information to the central contact point by a deadline. Provision B restricts transfers of personal data to third countries or international organisations unless the GDPR Chapter V conditions are met. If the information supplied under A includes personal data and is transferred to a recipient in a third country, A could require an act that B permits only subject to additional conditions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not require an international transfer, nor does it specify that the central contact point or ENISA is located in a third country. The information duty can therefore be fulfilled through a GDPR-compliant transfer, or by providing non-personal or appropriately protected information; A does not override B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De entiteiten, bedoeld in het eerste en tweede lid, verstrekken de informatie, bedoeld in het derde lid, uiterlijk op 17 januari 2025.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Persoonsgegevens die worden verwerkt of die zijn bestemd om na doorgifte aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie te worden verwerkt, mogen slechts worden doorgegeven indien, onverminderd de overige bepalingen van deze verordening, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker aan de in dit hoofdstuk neergelegde voorwaarden hebben voldaan;

verdict.shared_subject: Processing sensitive personal data in automated individual decision-making by a commission or advisory body
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits a commission or advisory body to process special-category and criminal-offence data when its stated safeguards and conditions are met. Provision B requires, in the specified Article 22(2)(a) or (c) cases, measures including human intervention, an opportunity to state one's views, and a right to challenge an automated individual decision; an automated decision using A-authorised sensitive data could therefore raise a question whether A's safeguards are sufficient for B's individual guarantees.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative requirements rather than incompatible commands: A concerns the legal conditions for processing sensitive or criminal-offence data, while B concerns safeguards for affected persons in certain automated decisions. A commission can satisfy A and additionally provide the human intervention, hearing, and challenge rights required by B; nothing in A exempts it from B or makes those measures impossible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het verbod om bijzondere categorieën van persoonsgegevens en persoonsgegevens van strafrechtelijke aard te verwerken door een commissie of adviescollege als bedoeld in het eerste lid niet van toepassing indien:
verdict.evidence_span_b: waaronder ten minste het recht op menselijke tussenkomst van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, het recht om zijn standpunt kenbaar te maken en het recht om het besluit aan te vechten.

verdict.shared_subject: Security and protection of electronic services involving personal-data transfers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: An organisation subject to both provisions may need to secure access to electronic services under A while also ensuring that any transfer of personal data to a third country satisfies all GDPR Chapter V conditions under B. If the security rules made under A required a transfer that B prohibited, or if they treated security as sufficient for transfer compliance, the duties could pull in different directions, but neither proposition appears in the text shown.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A imposes a general security and reliability obligation concerning access to electronic services, while B independently restricts international transfers of personal data unless Chapter V conditions are met. The organisation can comply with both by implementing secure access and refraining from, or lawfully structuring, transfers that do not satisfy B; A does not authorise or require any transfer.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties voldoen aan bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur te stellen regels met betrekking tot de werking, betrouwbaarheid en beveiliging van de toegang tot elektronische diensten op verschillende betrouwbaarheidsniveaus.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Persoonsgegevens die worden verwerkt of die zijn bestemd om na doorgifte aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie te worden verwerkt, mogen slechts worden doorgegeven indien, onverminderd de overige bepalingen van deze verordening, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker aan de in dit hoofdstuk neergelegde voorwaarden hebben voldaan;

verdict.shared_subject: Entities or providers subject to separate governance and continuity obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern an organisation involved in regulated infrastructure, but they impose different obligations on different subjects: provision A extends certain governance rules to each partner of a general partnership, while provision B authorises the Minister to impose a technical or organisational continuity measure on a provider whose continuity plan is inadequate. Nothing in either text makes compliance with one impossible or substitutes one obligation for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A can be satisfied by applying the referenced governance rules to each partner, while B can be satisfied by the provider adopting any measure imposed within the specified period. The obligations have different triggers, addressees and subject matter, and can readily be complied with cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit een vennootschap onder firma is, is het bepaalde bij of krachtens het eerste tot en met zesde lid van overeenkomstige toepassing op iedere vennoot van die vennootschap onder firma.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien het continuïteitsplan naar het oordeel van Onze Minister onvoldoende bijdraagt aan de in het eerste lid bedoelde continuïteit, kan Onze Minister een aanbieder als bedoeld in het eerste lid de verplichting opleggen om binnen een bepaalde termijn een technische of organisatorische maatregel te treffen met het oog op de in het eerste lid bedoelde continuïteit.

verdict.shared_subject: National competent authorities handling personal-data-breach incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities to exchange all necessary data, expressly including personal data, when cooperating with the Dutch data-protection authority. Provision B requires national competent authorities to comply with confidentiality obligations under Article 78, so one might argue that disclosure required by A could conflict with confidentiality under B if Article 78 prohibits that disclosure.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties in different contexts that can be performed cumulatively: authorities can exchange the necessary personal data required by A while observing the confidentiality obligations imposed by B, including any safeguards or limits in Article 78. Nothing in the text shown says that Article 78 forbids the cooperation or data exchange required by A.
verdict.missing_reference: The content of Article 78 would be needed to assess any specific confidentiality restriction, but the provisions shown do not establish a conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: wisselen in het kader van die samenwerking alle daarvoor noodzakelijke gegevens uit, waaronder persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: voldoen de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten aan de in artikel 78 vastgelegde vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Verplichtingen van een financiële entiteit inzake persoonsgegevens en ICT-incidentrapportage
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Een kleine financiële entiteit kan onder art. 30 GDPR vrijgesteld zijn van het register van verwerkingsactiviteiten, terwijl art. 19 DORA haar toch verplicht incidentrapportages op te stellen die mogelijk informatie over persoonsgegevens bevatten. Dat kan praktisch spanning geven als de rapportage-informatie niet elders is gedocumenteerd, maar art. 19 verbiedt het register niet en art. 30 maakt de rapportageplicht niet onmogelijk.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen regelen verschillende verplichtingen: art. 30 gaat over het bijhouden van een register van verwerkingsactiviteiten en bevat een vrijstelling onder voorwaarden; art. 19 gaat over het melden van ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten door financiële entiteiten. Een entiteit kan de DORA-rapportageplicht naleven zonder dat zij daarom een GDPR-register moet bijhouden, en kan beide verplichtingen cumulatief naleven wanneer art. 30 wel van toepassing is.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde verplichtingen zijn niet van toepassing op ondernemingen of organisaties die minder dan 250 personen in dienst hebben, tenzij het waarschijnlijk is dat de verwerking die zij verrichten een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkenen, de verwerking niet incidenteel is, of de verwerking bijzondere categorieën van gegevens, als bedoeld in artikel 9, lid 1, of persoonsgegevens in verband met strafrechtelijke veroordelingen en strafbare feiten als bedoeld in artikel 10 betreft.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Record-keeping by a provider of a public electronic communications service that is also subject to the GDPR.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 11.3a requires such a provider to maintain an overview of all personal-data breaches. Article 30(5) exempts small enterprises from the referenced register obligations unless specified conditions apply, which could appear to remove a GDPR record-keeping obligation for a small provider.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different record-keeping duties: Article 11.3a concerns an overview of personal-data breaches, while Article 30 concerns a register of processing activities under paragraphs 1 and 2. The GDPR exemption therefore does not prohibit or displace the separate statutory breach-overview duty, and a provider can comply with both where Article 30 applies.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst houdt een overzicht bij van alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in de leden 1 en 2 bedoelde verplichtingen zijn niet van toepassing op ondernemingen of organisaties die minder dan 250 personen in dienst hebben, tenzij het waarschijnlijk is dat de verwerking die zij verrichten een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkenen, de verwerking niet incidenteel is, of de verwerking bijzondere categorieën van gegevens, als bedoeld in artikel 9, lid 1, of persoonsgegevens in verband met strafrechtelijke veroordelingen en strafbare feiten als bedoeld in artikel 10 betreft.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and disclosure of personal data, including data revealing religious or philosophical beliefs
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits providing the relevant personal data to third parties without the data subject’s consent. Provision B requires inclusion of a subscriber’s personal data in publicly available directories or directory-service databases when the subscriber has consented, which could involve disclosure to third parties. If the directory operator and the relevant data fall within A, the directory obligation might appear to require the disclosure that A restricts.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions make consent central: A permits disclosure where the person concerned has consented, while B requires the subscriber’s consent and limits inclusion to the data specified by that subscriber. B therefore can be complied with without violating A, provided the subscriber’s consent is the relevant consent and the data are not disclosed beyond that scope; the texts do not establish that B overrides A or concerns special-category belief data.

verdict.shared_subject: Personal-data processing and communications to data subjects
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A makes a breach notification unnecessary when the provider has taken appropriate technical protective measures, while Provision B requires the controller to provide specified information and communications to the data subject in an accessible form. If the communication under Article 34 were treated as the breach notification covered by A, A could appear to remove a communication that B requires.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns an exception to a specific breach-notification duty under the referenced provision, triggered by effective encryption or equivalent protection. Provision B imposes general transparency and data-subject-rights communication duties, and nothing in its text says that those duties are displaced by A; both can therefore be complied with by omitting only the notification that A exempts while providing the other required communications.

verdict.shared_subject: Allocation of enforcement and competent-authority powers under two Dutch digital-law instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern public authorities and regulated entities in overlapping digital or infrastructure sectors, so an entity could potentially encounter both the authority designated under Provision A and ACM enforcement under Provision B. One might therefore suspect overlapping or competing competence, especially where an entity falls within a sector listed in Provision A and also violates a provision enforced by ACM under Provision B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A designates the competent authority for entities in specified sectors; it does not prohibit other legislation from assigning enforcement powers to another authority. Provision B separately gives ACM power to impose administrative sanctions for enumerated provisions, with the supplied context assigning certain personal-data matters to the Dutch Data Protection Authority; nothing in either text says that these powers are exclusive, mutually incompatible, or that one authority must refrain from acting when the other is designated.
