verdict.shared_subject: Enforcement powers for violations by entities providing domain-name registration services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions authorize an administrative enforcement measure for violations, so the same conduct might attract both a coercive order and a fine. However, neither provision prohibits the other measure, and they concern different legal violations and competent authorities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A permits a competent authority to impose a periodic penalty payment for violations of specified domain-name provisions, while Provision B permits the Dutch Data Protection Authority to impose a fine for specified GDPR violations. An entity can comply with both underlying regimes, and the provisions can operate cumulatively without requiring incompatible conduct.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteit kan een entiteit die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verleent een last onder dwangsom opleggen in geval van overtreding van het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 42, 44, 47, 49 en 50.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De Autoriteit persoonsgegevens kan in geval van overtreding van het bepaalde in artikel 83, vierde, vijfde of zesde lid, van de verordening een bestuurlijke boete opleggen van ten hoogste de in deze leden genoemde bedragen.

verdict.shared_subject: Recognition of an ontsluitende dienst or machtigingsdienst and exemption from obligations under BWBR0052872
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions could appear related if the same organisation is both an essential or important entity under BWBR0052872 and a service provider seeking recognition under BWBR0048156. In that situation, an exemption from obligations under articles 25–30 might seem to remove requirements relevant to the recognition decision, while article 11 requires compliance with the applicable recognition rules.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 32 concerns a discretionary exemption from specified obligations under articles 25–30, for entities or activities within listed public-interest domains. Article 11 independently requires recognition when the service satisfies the rules applicable to that service; nothing in either text says that the exemption grants recognition, prevents recognition, or substitutes for the recognition requirements. The provisions can therefore be complied with cumulatively, and they may apply to different actors or activities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister die het aangaat kan bij regeling of besluit, in overeenstemming met Onze Minister, een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die activiteiten uitvoert op het gebied van nationale veiligheid, openbare veiligheid, defensie of rechtshandhaving of die uitsluitend diensten verleent aan een overheidsinstantie als bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid, met betrekking tot die activiteiten of diensten ontheffen van de verplichtingen, bedoeld in de artikelen 25 tot en met 30.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister erkent een ontsluitende dienst of een machtigingsdienst indien de dienst voldoet aan de met betrekking tot die dienst bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur gestelde regels.

verdict.shared_subject: Access and acceptance of identification means for electronic public services requiring a substantial or high assurance level
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires access to be granted only when the identification means meets at least the assurance level required for the service. B requires public authorities to accept all admitted identification means, plus the listed electronic declarations and EU-notified schemes, without expressly repeating A’s minimum-assurance condition; if one accepted means fell below the required level, B could appear to require acceptance where A requires refusal.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be read cumulatively: B identifies the categories that must be accepted, while A independently limits access to means meeting the service’s required assurance level. The listed means in B can therefore be accepted only insofar as they satisfy A, and B’s wording does not expressly deem acceptance sufficient to override the assurance requirement.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of special-category personal data by a CSIRT
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits and limits a CSIRT's processing of special-category data where necessary for specified statutory tasks. Provision B states that processing special-category data is prohibited unless one of its listed Article 9(2) exceptions applies; the text shown does not establish that necessity for CSIRT tasks under A is itself one of those exceptions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: a CSIRT may process such data only when necessary for its specified tasks under A and only when an exception under B applies. If the processing also has a qualifying basis such as explicit consent, vital interests, public disclosure, or legal claims, both provisions are satisfied.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A CSIRT processes health data incidentally obtained during a cyber-incident investigation because that processing is necessary for one of its Article 16 tasks under A, but the affected person has not consented, the data were not manifestly made public, no vital-interest or legal-claim situation applies, and none of B's other listed exceptions is established. The CSIRT is permitted to process the data under A's task-necessity condition but remains subject to B's prohibition unless an applicable Article 9(2) exception exists.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the necessity of processing for the CSIRT's Article 16 tasks under A qualifies as one of the Article 9(2) exceptions incorporated by B, or whether another listed exception in B applies. The provisions shown do not establish that legal basis.

verdict.shared_subject: Information-handling duties involving cybersecurity vulnerability reports and notified conformity-assessment bodies
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the coordinator to follow up vulnerability reports and safeguard the reporter’s anonymity, while Provision B requires a notifying authority to provide the Commission with all relevant information about a notified body on request. If a vulnerability report concerned information relevant to a notified body’s competence, disclosure to the Commission might appear to risk revealing the reporter’s identity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different subject matters: A concerns a coordinator handling voluntary vulnerability reports, whereas B concerns a notifying authority supplying information about a notified body’s competence. Nothing in B requires disclosure of a reporter’s identity, and the duties can be performed cumulatively by anonymising or otherwise protecting irrelevant personal information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De coördinator met het oog op een gecoördineerde bekendmaking van kwetsbaarheden geeft opvolging aan de melding door het verrichten van de taken, genoemd in artikel 17, tweede lid, en waarborgt de anonimiteit van de natuurlijke persoon of rechtspersoon die de kwetsbaarheid meldt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanmeldende autoriteit verstrekt de Commissie op verzoek alle relevante informatie over de aanmelding of het op peil houden van de bekwaamheid van de betrokken aangemelde instantie.

verdict.shared_subject: Access to public-sector information-society services and data-subject information rights
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern interactions between a user/data subject and a public-sector service, but they regulate different matters. One prohibits conditioning access on consent for terminal-equipment storage or access, while the other grants information about safeguards when personal data are transferred to a third country or international organisation; no concrete incompatibility follows.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A removes consent as a condition of access in a specified public-sector service context, whereas provision B requires notice of appropriate safeguards for an international transfer. A service provider can comply with both by not conditioning access on consent and, where a relevant transfer occurs, informing the data subject about the Article 46 safeguards.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De toegang van de gebruiker tot een dienst van de informatiemaatschappij die wordt geleverd door of namens een krachtens publiekrecht ingestelde rechtspersoon wordt niet afhankelijk gemaakt van het verlenen van toestemming als bedoeld in het eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer persoonsgegevens worden doorgegeven aan een derde land of een internationale organisatie, heeft de betrokkene het recht in kennis te worden gesteld van de passende waarborgen overeenkomstig artikel 46 inzake de doorgifte.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or forwarding serious/significant ICT and cybersecurity incidents to competent authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident notifications and the involvement of competent authorities, so an incident involving a financial-market entity might appear to fall under both reporting frameworks. However, provision A is a transitional deeming and forwarding rule for notifications under the Dutch Wbni, while provision B preserves an ESMA/host-state-authority responsibility for a central securities depository under specified cross-border conditions; neither text requires incompatible conduct.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be cumulatively satisfied: a qualifying pre-existing Wbni notification may be treated as an early warning and forwarded by the Dutch Minister, while the competent authority may separately transmit incident details to the relevant host-state authority under provision B. They concern different legal mechanisms, actors, triggers, and institutional responsibilities, with no conflicting deadline, content, or prohibition.

verdict.evidence_span_b: doet geen afbreuk aan de verantwoordelijkheid van de bevoegde autoriteit om de bijzonderheden van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident onverwijld aan de relevante autoriteit van de lidstaat van ontvangst door te geven

verdict.shared_subject: The administrator’s disclosure of numbers and data and exemptions under the same statutory scheme
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 11.10 restricts disclosures by the administrator to two specified purposes: emergency assistance or combating misuse of a public-services emergency number. Article 11.12 allows an exemption to be granted subject to limitations and conditions, which could appear to permit a disclosure outside those purposes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 11.12 merely establishes competence to grant an exemption and attach conditions; it does not state that an exemption overrides the substantive purposes in Article 11.10. The provisions can therefore operate cumulatively: any disclosure must remain within Article 11.10 unless an applicable exemption provision expressly creates an exception.
verdict.missing_reference: The provision governing the legal effect and scope of an exemption under Article 11.12 would be needed to determine whether it can override Article 11.10’s disclosure restriction.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the exemption is legally capable of authorising disclosures outside the two purposes listed in Article 11.10 is not established by the text shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Verstrekking van nummers en gegevens door de beheerder vindt slechts plaats met het oog op de hulpverlening in noodsituaties of de bestrijding van het misbruik van een alarmnummer voor publieke diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een ontheffing kan onder beperkingen worden verleend. Aan een ontheffing kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT incidents involving personal data and security measures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A removes the notification duty when personal data affected by a breach are encrypted or otherwise unintelligible to unauthorised persons. Provision B nevertheless requires financial entities to register all ICT-related incidents and significant cyberthreats and to document their underlying causes, so an incident covered by B may still require internal recording even when A removes external notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different matters: A concerns whether a provider must notify affected individuals after a personal-data breach, while B concerns a financial entity’s internal incident-management and recording processes. A financial entity can comply with both by recording the incident under B while relying on A only to avoid the notification required by the referenced provision.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De kennisgeving, bedoeld in het tweede lid, is niet vereist indien de aanbieder naar het oordeel van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens gepaste technische beschermingsmaatregelen heeft genomen waardoor de persoonsgegevens die het betreft, versleuteld of anderszins onbegrijpelijk zijn voor een ieder die geen recht heeft op toegang tot die gegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten registreren alle ICT-gerelateerde incidenten en significante cyberdreigingen.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern regulatory oversight in the digital sector, so an entity involved in ICT services and AI could encounter both regimes. However, Article 57 governs a competent authority’s notification to an oversight forum, while Article 31 governs procedures of notified bodies; neither imposes an incompatible duty on the same actor or regulates the same underlying obligation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different matters: Article 57 requires a competent authority to notify an oversight forum when exercising specified supervisory powers, whereas Article 31 requires notified bodies to maintain procedures that account for provider and AI-system characteristics. Both duties can be performed simultaneously without one preventing compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteit stelt het oversightforum dat is opgericht op grond van artikel 32, eerste lid, van de Verordening (EU) 2022/2554 in kennis wanneer zij haar toezichts- en handhavingsbevoegdheden uitoefent
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties beschikken over de nodige procedures voor de uitoefening van hun activiteiten, waarin voldoende rekening wordt gehouden met de omvang van een aanbieder, de sector waarin deze actief is, de structuur en de relatieve complexiteit van het betreffende AI-systeem.

verdict.shared_subject: Internal allocation of tasks within a committee or membership body
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require an internal allocation of tasks, but they address different bodies and decision-makers: Provision A requires the members to establish a division of tasks and involve extraordinary members as far as possible, while Provision B requires the Committee's rules of procedure to establish the division between the chair and vice-chairs. No incompatibility follows from performing both allocations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be satisfied cumulatively: the members can allocate tasks while involving extraordinary members, and the Committee can separately specify the chair's and vice-chairs' tasks in its rules of procedure. They concern different institutional arrangements and do not prescribe conflicting task assignments, deadlines, or contents.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De leden stellen een verdeling van taken vast en betrekken hierbij zoveel mogelijk de buitengewone leden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het Comité stelt in zijn reglement van orde de taakverdeling tussen de voorzitter en de vicevoorzitters vast.

verdict.shared_subject: The scope of obligations concerning electronic business and organisational identification means and services under BWBR0048156.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions carve out situations from rules concerning business and organisational means, so they could appear to overlap if a private-system party operating only at level 1 also provides services to a non-Dutch-established service provider through the central portal. However, the texts do not impose incompatible commands: Article 15 excludes specified central-portal activities from the acceptance duty, while Article 24 excludes a different category of parties from its transitional provision.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 15 concerns the duty to accept the means and declarations referred to in Article 15(2), with exceptions for specified central-portal access and services to non-Dutch-established service providers. Article 24 simply states that its transitional provision does not apply to parties conducting exclusively level-1 activities; both exclusions can operate simultaneously without requiring an actor to accept and refuse the same means.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Dit artikel is niet van toepassing op partijen die binnen het private stelsel, bedoeld in het eerste en tweede lid, uitsluitend activiteiten op het niveau 1 uitvoeren.

verdict.shared_subject: The handling and onward transmission of significant-incident reports by authorities and central contact points
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information derived from incident reports involving essential entities, and both contemplate onward communication to another authority or contact point. One could therefore initially suspect overlapping transmission channels or duties for the same report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires the competent authority to provide information about a reported significant incident to the authority under the Critical Entities Resilience Act. Provision B requires the central contact point, upon request, to forward reports received under Article 23(1) to central contact points in other Member States. These are different recipients, actors, and triggers, and both duties can be performed cumulatively without incompatible content, timing, or prohibition.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Op verzoek van het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit stuurt het centrale contactpunt de op grond van lid 1 ontvangen meldingen door naar de centrale contactpunten van de andere betrokken lidstaten.

verdict.shared_subject: Dutch electronic communications regulation, but the provisions address different subjects
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions appear in the same statutory chapter and concern regulatory control over communications services: Article 11.9 imposes detailed obligations concerning caller identification, while Article 11.12 allows conditions and restrictions to be attached to an exemption. One might argue that an exemption under Article 11.12 could alter how the Article 11.9 obligations apply.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 11.9 requires providers offering number identification to provide specified blocking and refusal options. Article 11.12 merely states that an exemption may be granted subject to limitations and conditions; it neither grants an exemption here nor says that an exemption overrides Article 11.9. The provisions can therefore operate cumulatively without any stated incompatibility.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Een ontheffing kan onder beperkingen worden verleend. Aan een ontheffing kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulation of electronic communications and related data handling
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes a concrete maximum retention period for personal data processed by the CSIRT. Provision B authorises further rules and requirements concerning measures imposed on providers, so later rules could potentially affect how providers handle communications-related systems or data. However, B does not itself require retention, prohibit deletion, or establish a conflicting period.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A requires the CSIRT to delete the specified personal data no later than 12 months after first processing, while B merely grants competence to adopt further rules concerning specified measures and requirements for public electronic-communications providers. The competence in B can be exercised consistently with A, and nothing in B displaces or contradicts A’s deletion duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De persoonsgegevens, bedoeld in artikel 64, tweede lid, die door het CSIRT worden verwerkt worden niet langer bewaard dan noodzakelijk is ter uitvoering van haar taken op grond van deze wet, doch uiterlijk binnen 12 maanden na de eerste verwerking verwijderd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen nadere regels worden gegeven met betrekking tot de in het eerste en derde lid bedoelde maatregelen en kunnen eisen worden gesteld aan aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken en openbare elektronische communicatiediensten.

verdict.shared_subject: The exercise of data-subject rights under Chapter III of the GDPR in journalistic, academic, artistic, or literary processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 43 excludes the Act from applying to exclusively journalistic, academic, artistic, or literary processing, while Article 5 regulates who exercises Chapter III data-subject rights, including through a legal representative. If Article 5 were applicable to such processing, it could require representative involvement; however, Article 43 expressly preserves Articles 1–5, so its exclusion does not remove Article 5.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions expressly operate together: Article 43's exception excludes the Act generally but expressly leaves Articles 1–5 applicable. verdict.shared_subject: Processing of special-category personal data by trust-service providers

Provision B, however, requires trust-service providers to process only data obtained from the data subject or with that person’s explicit consent, unless its separate exception applies.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be read cumulatively: even where A removes the prohibition under Article 9(2), B independently limits the source and necessity of personal data processed by trust-service providers. The apparent conflict depends on whether A’s exceptions, or B’s paragraph 3 exception, displace B’s source/consent requirement; that relationship is not established by the provisions shown.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider processes a person’s special-category personal data because the data were manifestly made public by that person, relying on provision A, but obtains the data from a public source rather than directly from the person and without the person’s explicit consent. A permits the processing prohibition not to apply, while B appears to forbid the provider from processing data unless obtained from the person or with explicit consent, and the shown text does not establish an exception covering this situation.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether provision A’s Article 9(2) exceptions, or another applicable legal provision, also overrides provision B’s independent requirement that the data be obtained from the data subject or with explicit consent; paragraph 3 of B mentions fraud detection and processing required by law, but does not expressly resolve the Article 9(2) cases in A.

verdict.shared_subject: Organisational record-keeping and information-gathering duties concerning personal data and cyber threats
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 30 can exempt a small organisation from the register-of-processing-activities obligations, while Article 13 requires a financial entity to maintain capabilities and personnel to collect vulnerability, cyber-threat and incident information. If that information-gathering involves personal data, one might argue that the DORA duty creates a record-keeping or processing burden despite the GDPR exemption. However, Article 13 does not require the Article 30 register, and Article 30 does not prohibit the collection or analysis required by Article 13.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different regulatory subjects and concern different objects: Article 30 defines when the GDPR register obligations apply, whereas Article 13 requires financial entities to have capabilities and personnel for cyber-threat and incident information. A financial entity can comply with Article 13 while also complying with Article 30, including by maintaining any required records only where the Article 30 conditions make them applicable.

Nothing in either text makes providing instructions a substitute for prior consultation or makes consultation incompatible with providing the instructions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations are cumulative and readily separable: the controller can consult the supervisory authority before processing, while the provider supplies the required instructions to the deployer. They concern different actors, triggers, and duties, and neither provision forbids or overrides the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits a committee or advisory body to process special-category and criminal-offence personal data when its conditions are met. verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to the same high-risk AI system, but they impose different compliance obligations: GDPR Article 35 requires the controller to conduct a data-protection impact assessment before processing, while the AI Act provision concerns the notified body's identification number on CE marking and related advertising. verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulatively satisfiable duties or powers: an entity can undergo the independent security control and provide its results to the Minister while also supplying relevant audit reports and other information to the lead overseer. verdict.shared_subject: Use of an identification means in electronic public services and AI-based identification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern an organisation using an identification system for a natural person. Provision A requires acceptance of an authorised identification means in specified electronic services, while Provision B prohibits the responsible deployer from taking measures or decisions based on the system's identification unless at least two natural persons separately verify and confirm it.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties rather than incompatible commands: the public body or designated organisation can accept the authorised identification means while ensuring that any resulting measure or decision is based on the identification only after the required human verification. They also have different triggers and scopes, since Article 7 applies only where the Ministerial regulation so provides and the required assurance level applies, whereas Article 14 applies to specified high-risk AI systems under Annex III, point 1(a).

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the Minister or designated authority to conduct analyses and technical research concerning specified threats and incidents, while excluding investigations into the persons or organisations responsible for them. Provision B allocates competence among data-protection supervisory authorities to handle complaints or infringements, potentially concerning the same incident or organisation, but it does not prohibit the technical research described in A.

The same incident can be technically analysed under A while a competent supervisory authority separately handles any GDPR matter under B.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A extends the application of governance rules to each partner of a general partnership when the essential or important entity has that legal form. verdict.shared_subject: Security and human oversight of AI-related personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to an operator using a high-risk AI system to identify persons while processing personal data. Article 32 requires risk-appropriate technical and organisational security measures, whereas Article 14 prohibits decisions based on the system's identification unless two qualified natural persons separately verify and confirm it; a security-oriented system design could therefore appear to support automated use without satisfying the separate human-verification safeguard.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties addressing different matters: Article 32 concerns confidentiality, integrity, availability, resilience, incident recovery, and testing of processing security, while Article 14 regulates human verification before decisions based on certain high-risk AI identifications. An operator can implement both, including secure systems and the required two-person verification, so neither text requires violating the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and deletion of special-category personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A permits processing of special-category personal data in specified circumstances, including where the data subject has given explicit consent. Provision B can require the controller to erase personal data after consent is withdrawn, potentially making continued processing permitted under A impossible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative rules rather than contradictory commands: A concerns whether processing special-category data is exempt from the prohibition, while B concerns when a data subject can require erasure. Article 17 itself expressly limits erasure where another legal basis remains, and the shown text does not establish that A's consent exception is the only basis or that it overrides Article 17.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 17(3), especially the exceptions for a legal processing obligation, public-interest tasks, public-health processing, archiving/research/statistics, and legal claims, may prevent erasure; additionally, Article 17(1)(b) applies only where consent is withdrawn and there is no other legal basis. The provisions shown do not establish that every processing operation permitted by Article 22 is exempt from erasure.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk processing and AI systems requiring a data protection impact assessment
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to a high-risk AI deployment involving personal-data processing. Article 36 requires prior consultation where the DPIA shows a high risk absent mitigation, while Article 26 requires the AI deployer to use Article 13 information to fulfil its DPIA obligation; one might argue that the AI-specific information duty and the GDPR consultation duty create overlapping compliance benchmarks or sequencing questions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, compatible duties rather than contradictory ones. Article 26 helps the deployer perform the DPIA, and Article 36 separately requires prior consultation if that DPIA identifies the specified residual risk; complying with Article 26 does not replace or negate Article 36.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity that is both a GDPR controller and an entity covered by NIS2 and an equivalent sector-specific EU act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a controller to notify the competent data-protection authority within 72 hours for a personal-data breach, while provision B removes NIS2 provisions, including supervision and enforcement, where an equivalent sector-specific EU act governs the entity's cybersecurity measures or significant-incident reporting. This could create an apparent overlap or uncertainty about whether the NIS2 incident-reporting regime applies, but B does not state that it displaces GDPR reporting duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B concerns the applicability of NIS2 provisions to covered entities and expressly preserves NIS2 provisions for entities not covered by the sector-specific act; it does not prohibit or exempt GDPR controllers from reporting personal-data breaches under provision A. An entity can therefore comply with both regimes where their respective triggers apply, with A addressing personal-data breaches and B allocating the applicable cybersecurity/incident regime.

verdict.shared_subject: Potential interception or monitoring by an operator providing authentication or access services over a public electronic communications network
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an erkende middelenuitgever, authenticatiedienst or machtigingsdienst to provide all cooperation necessary for reliable access to electronic services. If that cooperation required interception or monitoring of communications, Provision B would appear to prohibit such conduct by a provider of a public electronic communications network or service unless one of its listed exceptions applies.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different duties and may apply to different actors: A concerns recognised identity/access-service providers, while B concerns providers of public electronic communications networks or services. Even where one entity is subject to both, the cooperation required by A can be supplied without interception, or interception can occur under B's express exceptions, particularly where necessary for network or service integrity and security or required by law or court order.

verdict.shared_subject: Obligations of regulated service or assessment entities concerning cooperation and information handling
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires certain recognised service providers to give an authorised unlocking service all cooperation necessary for reliable access to electronic services, which could in some circumstances involve sharing information. Provision B requires notified bodies to keep information obtained during conformity-assessment activities confidential, except for legally required disclosure or disclosure to the notifying authorities; if the same entity and information fell within both provisions, cooperation under A might appear to require disclosure that B restricts.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different actors and functions: A concerns recognised issuers, authentication services and authorisation services cooperating with a recognised unlocking service, while B concerns notified bodies and confidentiality of information obtained during conformity-assessment activities. They can be complied with cumulatively because A requires only necessary cooperation, and B expressly permits disclosure where legally required; the texts do not establish that A requires disclosure of information covered by B or that the same actor is subject to both roles.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een erkende middelenuitgever, erkende authenticatiedienst en erkende machtigingsdienst verlenen aan een erkende ontsluitende dienst alle benodigde medewerking die voor een goede ontsluiting van een erkend bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel en een betrouwbare toegang tot de gewenste elektronische dienstverlening noodzakelijk is.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties beschikken over gedocumenteerde procedures die waarborgen dat hun personeel, comités, dochterondernemingen, onderaannemers, geassocieerde instanties of personeel van externe instanties overeenkomstig artikel 78 de informatie die zij tijdens conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten in hun bezit krijgen vertrouwelijk houden, behalve wanneer de openbaarmaking ervan wettelijk vereist is.

verdict.shared_subject: Publication of an administrative decision and judicial remedies
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern administrative decisions and legal consequences surrounding them, so they may appear related at a high level. One closes off a remedy against keeping a request pending, while the other requires publication of designation or withdrawal decisions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts and obligations: Provision A concerns the availability of a legal remedy against a specific procedural act by the Administrative Jurisdiction Division, whereas Provision B concerns publication of a decision designating or withdrawing an appointment. Compliance with the publication duty does not require, or affect, the availability of a remedy against keeping a request pending.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Van een besluit tot aanwijzing of intrekking wordt mededeling gedaan door plaatsing in de Staatscourant.

verdict.shared_subject: Personal-data breach notification and records of processing activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern organisations processing personal data, and Article 30 creates an exception from its register obligation for many organisations with fewer than 250 employees. One might argue that this exemption removes a compliance duty in circumstances where the breach-notification rule still applies, creating an apparent mismatch in obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties: A requires a provider to notify the affected person promptly after a qualifying personal-data breach, while B concerns whether certain small organisations must maintain a register of processing activities. The Article 30 exemption does not prohibit notification or excuse a breach-notification duty, so both rules can be complied with independently.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern obligations connected with ICT incidents or regulatory enforcement, so one might initially suspect that a critical ICT provider could face overlapping timing or compliance burdens. However, Provision A governs an essential or important entity's incident progress and final reports, while Provision B concerns a daily coercive fine imposed on a critical third-party ICT service provider after a supervisory decision; neither prescribes an incompatible reporting or compliance deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different obligations on differently defined actors and operate at different stages: A requires a progress report during an ongoing incident and a final report within one month after resolution, whereas B authorises continuation of a coercive fine for up to six months after notification until obligations are fulfilled. An actor subject to both could submit the reports required by A and separately comply with the obligation enforced under B.

verdict.shared_subject: BWBR0040940 and the legal treatment of decisions by the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A bars any legal remedy against the Administrative Jurisdiction Division’s decision to stay a request. Provision B requires the AP to publish a decision imposing an administrative sanction, unless the specified Woo provisions prevent publication; if the stayed matter involved such a sanction decision, publication and the stay could appear procedurally related, but the texts do not say that the stay prohibits publication or that publication is the subject of the barred remedy.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts: A concerns the availability of a legal remedy against a particular procedural decision by the Council of State’s Administrative Jurisdiction Division, while B concerns the AP’s publication of an administrative-sanction decision, subject to Woo exceptions. The AP can publish the sanction decision while no remedy is available against the stay decision, so both rules can be obeyed simultaneously.

verdict.shared_subject: Data governance and impact assessment for high-risk AI systems involving personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 35 requires a controller to conduct a data-protection impact assessment before processing likely to create a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms. Article 10 separately requires high-risk AI systems to apply extensive governance practices to training, validation and test datasets, including assessing bias and data suitability; these obligations may overlap but do not prescribe incompatible actions or benchmarks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A controller operating a high-risk AI system can perform the Article 35 assessment and also implement Article 10’s dataset-governance practices. The DPIA addresses risks to personal-data protection, while Article 10 governs the quality, provenance, suitability and bias-management of datasets; satisfying one does not purport to substitute for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: Governance obligations of entities and continuity measures for public electronic communications services and networks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may concern an entity involved in electronic communications, and both impose obligations connected with organisational or operational resilience. However, Provision A only extends governance rules to each partner of a general partnership, while Provision B requires specified communications providers and network providers to take measures ensuring service availability during calamities or force majeure; neither requires conduct incompatible with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A determines which partners are subject to the referenced governance rules when an essential or important entity is a general partnership. Provision B imposes continuity measures on providers of specified public communications services or networks. An entity or partner can comply with both by applying the governance rules and taking the required availability measures.

verdict.shared_subject: Delegated rule-making authority concerning digital identification and electronic communications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions merely authorize subordinate legislation, but they concern different subject matters: A concerns use of public identification means and related facilities, while B concerns further rules on consent/information requirements and exceptions for storing or accessing information on user equipment. No text requires the same conduct to be regulated incompatibly or makes one delegation exclusive.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The delegations can operate cumulatively and independently: ministerial regulations under A can govern use of public identification means, while an algemene maatregel van bestuur under B can elaborate the separate electronic-communications requirements and exceptions. Nothing in either provision forbids the other form of rule-making or creates conflicting duties for an actor.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij ministeriële regeling worden regels gesteld met betrekking tot het gebruik van publieke identificatiemiddelen en de voorzieningen, bedoeld in artikel 5, eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen in overeenstemming met Onze Minister van Veiligheid en Justitie nadere regels worden gegeven met betrekking tot de in het eerste lid, onder a en b, genoemde vereisten en de in het derde lid genoemde uitzonderingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Legal effects of an exemption and restriction of personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A allows an exemption to be granted subject to limitations and conditions, while provision B requires a controller to notify a data subject before lifting a processing restriction. If an exemption condition purported to lift such a restriction without prior notice, the two requirements might appear to pull in different directions. However, A does not address processing restrictions, data subjects, or notification, and it does not authorise ignoring other applicable duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different matters: A concerns the competent authority's power to attach limitations or conditions to an exemption, whereas B imposes a notification duty on a controller when a GDPR restriction obtained under Article 18(1) is lifted. An exemption can be granted or conditioned while the controller still gives the required prior notice, so both provisions can be complied with.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een ontheffing kan onder beperkingen worden verleend. Aan een ontheffing kunnen voorschriften worden verbonden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een betrokkene die overeenkomstig lid 1 een beperking van de verwerking heeft verkregen, wordt door de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke op de hoogte gebracht voordat de beperking van de verwerking wordt opgeheven.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory powers concerning entities providing digital or domain-related services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions empower a public authority to impose obligations on a service provider, so an entity might theoretically be subject to directions under both regimes. However, neither provision requires conduct that the other forbids, and their triggers, authorities, and subject matters are distinct.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A permits a competent authority to issue a binding direction to a domain-name-registration service provider to comply with specified statutory obligations. Provision B permits the Minister, in an approval-transfer decision, to modify approval conditions or require continuation of activities to preserve reliable access to electronic services; an entity can comply with both directions cumulatively.

verdict.shared_subject: Information and documentation relating to data processing and ICT security testing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information connected with an organisation’s activities, and a TLPT may involve personal data. However, Article 12 governs how a controller communicates specified GDPR information and rights-related communications to the data subject, while Article 26 governs a financial entity’s post-test submission of findings, remediation plans and compliance documentation to an authority. The texts impose no incompatible content, recipient, deadline or method.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with cumulatively: a controller can provide data subjects with concise, clear GDPR information under Article 12 while the financial entity separately supplies the authority with the TLPT summary and supporting documentation required by Article 26. Their recipients, purposes and triggers differ, and neither provision prohibits compliance with the other.

However, Article 44 concerns supplying registration information to the Minister, while Article 15 concerns what public bodies and designated organisations must accept when providing specified electronic services; the texts impose no incompatible act on the same actor in the same situation.

Article 44 does not require refusing or accepting any identification means, and Article 15 does not prohibit supplying national-register information.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident and emergency-related information handling
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern the recording or reporting of information connected with incidents or emergency response. One might argue that information supplied in an early warning could overlap with data that telecom or alarm-number administrators must record, creating parallel handling obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors for different purposes: provision A requires an entity to include specified information in an early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority, while provision B requires designated administrators to record supplied numbers and other specified data for emergency assistance or combating misuse. Nothing in either text forbids the other's reporting or recording, and the duties can be performed cumulatively.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De beheerders zijn verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voor deze vastlegging.

verdict.shared_subject: Aanwijzing en intrekking van de aanwijzing van organisaties als entiteit
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen betreffen een ministeriële aanwijzing, maar zij regelen verschillende beslissingen: A maakt aanwijzing van een instelling voor hoger onderwijs als belangrijke entiteit mogelijk, terwijl B intrekking koppelt aan het niet langer verlenen van bepaalde elektronische diensten. Op het eerste gezicht kan daardoor onduidelijk lijken of een aanwijzing onder A ook op grond van B kan worden ingetrokken.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen geen tegenstrijdige verplichtingen op en regelen niet noodzakelijk dezelfde aanwijzing of dezelfde wettelijke regeling. A is een bevoegdheidsgrond voor aanwijzing van een instelling voor hoger onderwijs; B is een afzonderlijke intrekkingsgrond voor een organisatie die bepaalde authenticatiediensten niet langer verleent. Bovendien bepaalt A zelf al dat de aanwijzing wordt ingetrokken wanneer de grond daarvoor vervalt, zodat beide regels naast elkaar kunnen bestaan.

verdict.evidence_span_b: kan de aanwijzing van een organisatie worden ingetrokken indien die organisatie niet langer elektronische diensten verleent waarvoor authenticatie op betrouwbaarheidsniveau substantieel of hoog vereist is

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and management of data or results by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A restricts providers from processing retained traffic and location data for other purposes unless the processing is permitted under Articles 11.5 and 11.5a and complies with those articles. Provision B requires financial entities to ensure that external testers manage TLPT results, including generating, storing, aggregating, reporting, communicating, or destroying them without risks to the entity; if TLPT results contain retained traffic or location data, the required result-management activities might appear to constitute processing for another purpose.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not require processing traffic or location data, and Provision A does not prohibit all processing of such data: it expressly permits processing authorised under Articles 11.5 and 11.5a. A financial entity can therefore structure TLPT testing so that no Article 13.2a-retained traffic or location data is used, or ensure that any such processing satisfies the stated exception and conditions.
verdict.missing_reference: Articles 11.5 and 11.5a of the Dutch Telecommunications Act, including whether TLPT testing and the relevant processing of retained traffic or location data are authorised under those provisions; also, the facts would need to establish that TLPT results actually contain data covered by Article 11.13.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the processing required or contemplated for TLPT-result management is permitted under Articles 11.5 and 11.5a and complies with those articles.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verkeers- en locatiegegevens die de aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of openbare elektronische communicatiediensten bewaren op grond van artikel 13.2a, tweede lid, worden door de aanbieders niet voor andere doelen verwerkt, tenzij het gegevens betreft waarvan de verwerking op grond van de artikelen 11.5 en 11.5a is toegestaan en de verwerking plaatsvindt met inachtneming van die artikelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten zorgen ervoor dat de contracten met externe testers een degelijk beheer van de resultaten van de TLPT opleggen en dat de gegevensverwerking daarvan, met inbegrip van het genereren, opslaan, aggregeren, ontwerpen, rapporteren, communiceren of vernietigen van resultaten, geen risico’s voor de financiële entiteit meebrengt.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and their processing or conformity assessment
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern a high-risk AI system, but they impose duties on different actors and regulate different activities. Article 35 requires the controller to conduct a data-protection impact assessment where processing is likely to create a high risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms, while Article 31 prevents a conformity-assessment body and its personnel from participating in the system’s design, development, marketing, or use; nothing in the texts makes compliance with one impossible alongside compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A controller can perform the required impact assessment, while an independent conformity-assessment body refrains from designing, developing, marketing, or using the AI system and from activities compromising its independence. The provisions therefore impose cumulative, actor-specific safeguards that can readily be satisfied together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstantie, haar hoogste leidinggevenden en het personeel dat de conformiteitsbeoordelingstaken verricht, zijn niet rechtstreeks of als vertegenwoordiger van de betrokken partijen betrokken bij het ontwerpen, ontwikkelen, verhandelen of gebruiken van de AI-systemen met een hoog risico.

verdict.shared_subject: De Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens en de wettelijke regels die daarop betrekking hebben
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen noemen de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, maar zij regelen verschillende onderwerpen: samenwerking en gegevensuitwisseling bij privacy-incidenten enerzijds en ontslag van leden op eigen verzoek anderzijds. Er is geen tekstuele aanwijzing dat de samenwerkingstaak het ontslagrecht beperkt of dat ontslag op eigen verzoek de gegevensuitwisseling verhindert.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 58 verplicht bevoegde autoriteiten tot samenwerking met de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens en tot uitwisseling van noodzakelijke gegevens bij incidenten. Artikel 7 regelt uitsluitend dat de voorzitter en leden op eigen verzoek door de minister worden ontslagen; beide regels kunnen volledig naast elkaar worden nageleefd.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteiten werken samen met de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens bij de behandeling van incidenten die leiden tot inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens en wisselen in het kader van die samenwerking alle daarvoor noodzakelijke gegevens uit, waaronder persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Op eigen verzoek worden de voorzitter, de andere leden en de buitengewone leden van de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens door Onze Minister ontslagen.

verdict.shared_subject: Organisational and cybersecurity requirements for entities involved in electronic services or notified-body functions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose organisational and security-related obligations, so an entity falling within both scopes might face two sets of requirements concerning security and operational processes. However, the provisions do not prescribe incompatible content, deadlines, or benchmarks; Article 4 delegates detailed rules to a future or separate general administrative measure, while Article 31 requires appropriate cybersecurity and other capabilities for notified bodies.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can be satisfied together: an entity can comply with the applicable electronic-service access-security rules under Article 4 and separately meet the organisational, quality-management, personnel, process, and appropriate-cybersecurity requirements under Article 31. The provisions also concern different regulatory functions and do not state that compliance with one substitutes for or prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties voldoen aan bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur te stellen regels met betrekking tot de werking, betrouwbaarheid en beveiliging van de toegang tot elektronische diensten op verschillende betrouwbaarheidsniveaus.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties voldoen aan de eisen inzake organisatie, kwaliteitsbeheer, personeel en processen die nodig zijn voor het vervullen van hun taken, alsook aan de passende cyberbeveiligingseisen.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing personal data, including special-category personal data, subject to data-minimisation and access-by-default requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits processing special-category personal data unless one of the listed Article 9(2) exceptions applies, while Provision B requires the controller to design processing so that only data necessary for each purpose are processed and, in principle, are not accessible without human intervention to an unlimited number of natural persons. A controller might therefore need to process or make special-category data accessible for a purpose covered by B, while A independently prohibits that processing unless an A-listed exception applies.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative requirements rather than contradictory commands: even where processing is permitted under one of A's exceptions, the controller must still minimise the data and restrict accessibility under B. Provision B does not itself require processing special-category data, and Provision A does not prohibit compliant minimisation or human-access controls.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A controller operates a system that processes employees' health data and makes those data available to an unlimited number of natural persons without human intervention for a specific purpose. The controller must determine both whether an Article 9(2) exception under A permits the health-data processing and whether the design complies with B's minimisation and accessibility requirements; B's obligation does not itself establish an exception to A's prohibition.
verdict.decisive_exception: The text does not establish that the purpose and design obligation in Provision B fall within any of Provision A's listed exceptions to the prohibition on processing special-category personal data, such as explicit consent, vital interests, publicly made data, or legal-claim necessity.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke treft passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen om ervoor te zorgen dat in beginsel alleen persoonsgegevens worden verwerkt die noodzakelijk zijn voor elk specifiek doel van de verwerking.

verdict.shared_subject: Public-sector entities and statutory duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: An entity covered by provision A might also be involved in the identification function described in provision B, and A permits exemption from information duties while B imposes a responsibility concerning a high-assurance identifier. If those duties concerned the same conduct, an exemption could appear to undermine the responsibility.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different subjects and concern different matters. Provision A gives the competent Minister a discretionary power to exempt specified entities from obligations under article 44; provision B assigns the Dienst Wegverkeer responsibility for placing a high-assurance public identifier on driving licences, and nothing in A exempts that responsibility or makes the two duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister die het aangaat kan bij regeling of besluit, in overeenstemming met Onze Minister, een essentiële entiteit, een belangrijke entiteit of entiteit die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verleent ontheffen van de verplichtingen, bedoeld in artikel 44
verdict.evidence_span_b: De Dienst Wegverkeer, bedoeld in artikel 4a van de Wegenverkeerswet 1994, draagt namens Onze Minister zorg voor het plaatsen van een publiek identificatiemiddel op betrouwbaarheidsniveau hoog op het rijbewijs.

verdict.shared_subject: The early-warning obligation for significant incidents and the NIS2 sectoral-law exclusion
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 26 requires an essential or important entity to give an early warning within 24 hours, while Article 4 says that NIS2 provisions are not applicable where an equivalent sector-specific Union act governs cybersecurity risk measures or significant-incident reporting. Thus, if a qualifying sector-specific act applies, the entity might otherwise be subject to Article 26 but be excluded from it under Article 4.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 4 is an applicability rule, not an incompatible reporting deadline: Article 26 applies unless a qualifying, equivalent sector-specific Union act displaces the relevant NIS2 provisions. If no such sector-specific act applies, Article 26 governs; if one does apply, its own reporting regime governs, avoiding simultaneous contradictory duties.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether a specific sector-specific Union act applies and satisfies Article 4's equivalence conditions determines whether Article 26 applies; the provisions shown establish that mechanism rather than creating mutually incompatible commands.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien sectorspecifieke rechtshandelingen van de Unie voorschrijven dat essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten risicobeheersmaatregelen op het gebied van cyberbeveiliging moeten nemen of significante incidenten moeten melden, en indien deze eisen ten minste gelijkwaardig zijn aan de in deze richtlijn vastgestelde verplichtingen, zijn de relevante bepalingen van deze richtlijn, met inbegrip van de in hoofdstuk VII bedoelde toezichts- en handhavingsbepalingen, niet van toepassing op dergelijke entiteiten.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing special-category personal data and the controller’s data-protection obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits processing special-category personal data unless one of the listed Article 9(2) exceptions applies. Provision B requires privacy-by-design measures for processing, which could include processing such data; that requirement might appear to support or necessitate processing that A restricts.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not itself authorise processing special-category data: it requires appropriate technical and organisational measures and compliance with the Regulation. A supplies exceptions to the prohibition, so a controller can comply with both by processing such data only where an applicable exception exists and designing the processing accordingly.
verdict.decisive_exception: Not applicable: Provision B contains no permission or requirement to process special-category data, and Provision A’s listed exceptions govern whether such processing is lawful.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Overeenkomstig artikel 9, tweede lid, onderdelen a, c, d, e en f, van de verordening is het verbod om bijzondere categorieën van persoonsgegevens te verwerken niet van toepassing, indien:
verdict.evidence_span_b: treft de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, zowel bij de bepaling van de verwerkingsmiddelen als bij de verwerking zelf, passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen, zoals pseudonimisering, die zijn opgesteld met als doel de gegevensbeschermingsbeginselen, zoals minimale gegevensverwerking, op een doeltreffende manier uit te voeren en de nodige waarborgen in de verwerking in te bouwen ter naleving van de voorschriften van deze verordening en ter bescherming van de rechten van de betrokkenen.

verdict.shared_subject: The handling and disclosure of confidential information or documentation by authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 55 prohibits supplying information covered by professional secrecy to any other person or authority, while Article 77 requires fundamental-rights authorities to process information or documentation obtained under that article according to Article 78 confidentiality obligations. If Article 77 requires access to information that Article 55 prohibits supplying, the provisions could appear to impose incompatible disclosure and confidentiality requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 77 does not itself require disclosure to a particular authority or override professional secrecy; it regulates how information lawfully obtained under Article 77 must subsequently be processed. Article 55 expressly permits disclosure where authorised by Union or national law, and Article 77's access power may constitute such a legal basis, with Article 78 then governing confidentiality. The provisions can therefore be complied with cumulatively.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether Article 77's access power is a Union-law provision authorising disclosure within the meaning of Article 55, and the precise confidentiality rules in Article 78, would matter in a concrete case; however, the texts shown do not establish an actual prohibition-versus-obligation conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onder het beroepsgeheim vallende informatie, waaronder de uitwisseling van informatie tussen de bevoegde autoriteiten uit hoofde van deze verordening en de overeenkomstig Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555 aangewezen of ingestelde bevoegde autoriteiten, wordt aan geen enkele andere persoon of autoriteit verstrekt, tenzij op grond van Unierechtelijke of nationaalrechtelijke bepalingen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Informatie of documentatie die op grond van dit artikel door de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde overheidsinstanties of -organen wordt verkregen, wordt verwerkt overeenkomstig de in artikel 78 beschreven vertrouwelijkheidsverplichtingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Information held by regulated entities and its disclosure to requesting parties or authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires domain-name registries and registration-service entities to answer a lawful, properly motivated access request immediately or within 72 hours. Provision B requires notified bodies and their personnel to keep information obtained during conformity-assessment activities confidential, except where disclosure is legally required; if a notified body were also the relevant domain-name service entity, a request could appear to require disclosure while the information might be covered by professional secrecy.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors and information contexts: A concerns domain-registration data held by registries or domain-registration service entities, while B concerns information obtained by notified bodies during conformity-assessment activities. Moreover, B expressly permits disclosure when legally required, so a legally valid access obligation under A would not necessarily conflict with B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De registers voor topleveldomeinnamen en de entiteiten die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verlenen beantwoorden een verzoek om toegang als bedoeld in het eerste lid onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur na ontvangst van het verzoek.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aangemelde instanties beschikken over gedocumenteerde procedures die waarborgen dat hun personeel, comités, dochterondernemingen, onderaannemers, geassocieerde instanties of personeel van externe instanties overeenkomstig artikel 78 de informatie die zij tijdens conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten in hun bezit krijgen vertrouwelijk houden, behalve wanneer de openbaarmaking ervan wettelijk vereist is.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system involving personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require the responsible actor to assess and manage risks affecting natural persons, but they impose different compliance frameworks: GDPR Article 24 requires ongoing, risk-based technical and organisational measures that ensure and demonstrate compliance, while Article 27 requires a fundamental-rights impact assessment for specified high-risk AI uses and updating when listed elements change. One might argue that completing the Article 27 assessment could be treated as sufficient for the Article 24 accountability duty, or that the two assessments use different risk scopes and therefore leave the applicable benchmark unclear.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, compatible duties rather than contradictory ones. Article 27 requires a particular fundamental-rights impact assessment for covered high-risk AI uses, while Article 24 independently requires appropriate and periodically updated measures to ensure and demonstrate GDPR compliance; nothing in Article 27 says that its assessment substitutes for, overrides, or satisfies Article 24.
verdict.evidence_span_a: treft de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen om te waarborgen en te kunnen aantonen dat de verwerking in overeenstemming met deze verordening wordt uitgevoerd. Die maatregelen worden geëvalueerd en indien nodig geactualiseerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de gebruiksverantwoordelijke tijdens het gebruik van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico ziet dat een van de in lid 1 vermelde elementen is gewijzigd of niet langer actueel is, neemt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de nodige maatregelen om de informatie te actualiseren.

verdict.shared_subject: Delegated rulemaking by general administrative measure (AMvB) concerning CSIRT requirements versus further rules under article 11a.3
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions authorize further rules by or pursuant to an AMvB, so a superficial reading might suggest overlapping delegated rulemaking powers. If article 11a.3 were read as governing the same CSIRT organization and subject matter, the two delegations could potentially produce overlapping or inconsistent implementing rules.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A specifically concerns the functional, financial, technical, and organizational requirements for an organization designated as a CSIRT. Provision B merely permits further rules concerning the matters already addressed in article 11a.3; it does not state that those rules govern CSIRTs or conflict with the requirements authorized by provision A. The provisions can therefore operate cumulatively within their respective subject matters.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen regels worden gesteld over de functionele, financiële, technische en organisatorische vereisten ten aanzien van de organisatie die bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur als CSIRT wordt aangewezen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur kunnen nadere regels worden gesteld ten aanzien van het bepaalde in dit artikel.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information or ICT-related activities, but they regulate different conduct: Provision A requires transfer of information to the Minister after withdrawal or transfer of an accreditation, while Provision B regulates how financial entities plan audits of ICT-service providers and the competence of auditors. Nothing in the texts makes the transferred information unavailable for, or incompatible with, the audits.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction. The accredited service can transfer the necessary information to the Minister, while a financial entity separately determines audit frequency and scope and ensures auditor competence when auditing an ICT-service provider.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De erkende dienst waarvan de erkenning wordt ingetrokken of overgedragen draagt er zorg voor dat alle door hem opgeslagen informatie en gegevens die noodzakelijk was voor de uitvoering van de activiteiten waarvoor hij was erkend, worden overgedragen aan Onze Minister.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij het uitoefenen van toegangs-, inspectie- en auditrechten ten aanzien van de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten bepalen financiële entiteiten op basis van een risicogebaseerde benadering vooraf de frequentie van de audits en inspecties alsook de te controleren gebieden, door algemeen aanvaarde auditnormen in acht te nemen in overeenstemming met de instructies van de toezichthouder inzake het gebruik en de integratie van deze auditnormen.

verdict.shared_subject: Cooperation and information exchange between the Dutch Data Protection Authority and financial-sector supervisors concerning personal-data processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 19 makes the authorities obliged to provide each other with data necessary for their tasks or legal obligations. Article 21a subjects cooperation and information exchange with DNB and other relevant supervisors to the procedure in Article 26 of the Payment Services Directive; if that external procedure imposed narrower conditions than Article 19, the duties could point in different directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: Article 19 supplies a general authority and obligation to exchange necessary data, while Article 21a specifies the applicable cooperation and information-exchange framework for the payment-services supervision described there. Nothing in the text shown expressly prohibits an exchange required by Article 19 or states that Article 21a overrides it.
verdict.missing_reference: Article 26 of the Payment Services Directive, including its conditions, limits and any confidentiality or refusal rules, is needed to determine whether the required exchange under Article 19 can always occur under Article 21a.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn bevoegd uit eigen beweging en desgevraagd verplicht aan elkaar de gegevens betreffende de verwerking van persoonsgegevens te verstrekken die noodzakelijk zijn voor de uitvoering van hun taak of om te kunnen voldoen aan een op hen rustende wettelijke verplichting
verdict.evidence_span_b: vindt de samenwerking en uitwisseling van informatie met De Nederlandsche Bank N.V. en andere relevante toezichthouders plaats overeenkomstig artikel 26 van de richtlijn betaaldiensten

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of special-category personal data and the possible appointment of a data protection officer
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A regulates when the prohibition on processing special-category personal data does not apply, while provision B permits or requires controllers and processors to appoint a data protection officer in certain cases. One might argue that appointing such an officer is a governance obligation connected with processing, whereas A limits the legality of the underlying processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of rules: A concerns legal exceptions to the prohibition on processing special-category data, while B concerns designation of a data protection officer. Appointment of a data protection officer neither authorises processing nor conflicts with any of A’s listed conditions; an organisation can comply with both by satisfying an applicable processing exception and appointing an officer where required.
