verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen richten zich op verschillende handhavers en primair verschillende normadressaten: artikel 58 betreft de Nederlandse bevoegde autoriteit en in artikel 58, lid 2, bedoelde essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten, terwijl artikel 100 ziet op instellingen, organen en instanties van de Unie en de EDPS. Bovendien verbiedt artikel 58 alleen een specifieke Nederlandse boete ná een AVG-boete voor dezelfde gedraging; het verbiedt de EDPS niet om een AI-verordeningboete op te leggen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: legt de bevoegde autoriteit geen bestuurlijke boete op op grond van de artikelen 80 en 87
verdict.evidence_span_b: De Europese Toezichthouder voor gegevensbescherming kan administratieve geldboeten opleggen aan instellingen, organen en instanties van de Unie die binnen het toepassingsgebied van deze verordening vallen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incidents or other relevant information by entities and competent authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information being reported to public authorities, and a serious AI incident could potentially also be information voluntarily reported under Provision A. The reporting channels and duties differ: Provision A concerns information supplied by a reporting entity to central contact points, while Provision B requires national competent authorities to notify the Commission immediately of every serious incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and are triggered differently. Provision A expressly concerns voluntary reporting by a reporting entity and says that such a report may not create additional obligations for that entity; Provision B imposes the notification duty on national competent authorities, so the texts can operate cumulatively without either actor being unable to comply.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onverminderd de voorkoming van, het onderzoek naar en de opsporing en de vervolging van strafbare feiten, mag vrijwillige melding er niet toe leiden dat de meldende entiteit bijkomende verplichtingen worden opgelegd waaraan zij niet onderworpen zou zijn geweest indien zij de melding niet had ingediend.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De nationale bevoegde autoriteiten stellen de Commissie onmiddellijk in kennis van elk ernstig incident, ongeacht of zij al dan niet maatregelen hebben getroffen

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related duties of entities subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to notify its service recipients without delay when a significant incident adversely affects service provision. Provision B, as the specified norm, requires financial entities to remain fully responsible for handling and consequences of reported ICT incidents; this could be read as imposing an additional incident-handling responsibility, but it does not require a separate filing or impose an incompatible deadline or recipient.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: A is an external notification duty to service recipients, while B preserves the financial entity's substantive responsibility after an incident has been reported under Article 19(1). B neither forbids notification to recipients nor creates a second reporting obligation that could conflict with A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onverminderd de ontvangen feedback van toezichthouders blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and follow-up communications under the two NIS2-related provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern the same significant incident, but they impose duties on different actors and in opposite directions: A requires the entity to submit a final report to its CSIRT and competent authority, while B requires the CSIRT or competent authority to respond to the reporting entity within 24 hours. If the provisions applied cumulatively to the same incident, they would involve separate communications, recipients and deadlines rather than one report satisfying the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are compatible because A governs an entity's later substantive final report, whereas B governs the authority's or CSIRT's prompt response to an early warning received from the entity. They do not require the same actor to make two reports, and the extracted recipients confirm that B's recipient is 'de meldende entiteit', not an additional reporting authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt onverwijld en zo mogelijk binnen 24 uur na ontvangst van de in lid 4, punt a) bedoelde vroegtijdige waarschuwing een antwoord aan de meldende entiteit

verdict.shared_subject: Institutional handling and communication of regulatory or cybersecurity matters
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a supervisory authority to adopt and communicate a final decision within one month after notification by the Committee. Provision B requires CSIRTs to disseminate warnings, notifications and announcements about cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents to entities, competent authorities and other relevant stakeholders, potentially in near real time. If the same underlying event involved both a GDPR dispute and a cyber incident, the duties would concern different actions and recipients rather than one filing replacing the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different functions: A governs a supervisory authority’s final decision in a GDPR dispute, while B governs CSIRT information dissemination concerning cybersecurity matters. Neither provision forbids or delays the other, and A is not a reporting duty to the recipients listed in B; the duties can therefore be performed cumulatively without conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt onverwijld en uiterlijk binnen één maand na de kennisgeving door het Comité een definitief besluit vast
verdict.evidence_span_b: het verstrekken van vroegtijdige waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen en het verspreiden van informatie onder betrokken essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten en aan de bevoegde autoriteiten en andere relevante belanghebbenden over cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten, in bijna-realtime indien mogelijk

verdict.shared_subject: Notification duties concerning different regulatory events and recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use a notification obligation, and a notified body’s relevant notification change could conceivably occur in a context where the competent authorities also learn of a personal-data breach. In that event, the same notifying authority or entity might face overlapping communications under two instruments, with different recipients and no stated coordination rule.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggering events and different obligated actors: A concerns competent authorities learning of a possible GDPR personal-data breach by an essential or important entity, while B concerns the notifying authority reporting relevant changes in a notified body’s notification. Nothing in the texts makes a notification change a personal-data breach or makes either communication substitute for the other; they can therefore be performed cumulatively when their independent triggers occur.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer de bevoegde autoriteiten er bij toezicht of handhaving kennis van krijgen dat de inbreuk door een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit op de in de artikelen 21 en 23 van deze richtlijn vastgestelde verplichtingen een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 4, punt 12, van Verordening (EU) 2016/679 kan inhouden, die op grond van artikel 33 van die verordening moet worden gemeld, stellen zij de bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteiten als bedoeld in de artikelen 55 en 56 van die verordening daarvan onverwijld in kennis.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanmeldende autoriteit stelt de Commissie en de andere lidstaten via het in artikel 30, lid 2, bedoelde elektronische aanmeldingssysteem in kennis van alle relevante wijzigingen in de aanmelding van een aangemelde instantie.

verdict.shared_subject: Information-sharing about significant incidents, incidents, near-incidents and cyber threats with cross-border or critical-entity implications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern onward information-sharing about reported cybersecurity events, and a single cross-border incident involving an entity designated as critical under Directive (EU) 2022/2557 could fall within both. However, the provisions assign the duties to different institutional actors and recipients: Article 39 requires the central contact point to notify other affected Member States' central contact points and ENISA, while Article 23 requires CSIRTs or competent authorities to provide information to the authorities competent under Directive (EU) 2022/2557.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are complementary rather than contradictory: Article 39 establishes EU cross-border notification by the central contact point, whereas Article 23 establishes information-sharing with authorities responsible under the critical-entities regime. Nothing requires one notification to replace the other, and the different recipients indicate that both can be made cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt het centrale contactpunt de centrale contactpunten van de andere getroffen lidstaten en Enisa onverwijld daarvan in kennis
verdict.evidence_span_b: De CSIRT’s of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteiten verstrekken de uit hoofde van Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2557 bevoegde autoriteiten informatie over significante incidenten

verdict.shared_subject: Potentially the same conformity-assessment body as an entity experiencing a significant incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a significant-incident report to the entity’s CSIRT or, where applicable, competent authority, while provision B requires a conformity-assessment body to submit an application to its notifying authority. If the same body is subject to both, the authorities and purposes differ, so one filing would not obviously discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggers and filings: A is triggered only by a significant incident affecting service provision, whereas B is an application for notification as a conformity-assessment body. Nothing in B requires an incident report, and nothing in A requires a notification application; therefore both duties can be performed independently without contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting on cyber/ICT incidents and crises
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose reporting duties concerning incident-related matters, but they require reports to different recipients and on different schedules: EU-CyCLONe reports regularly to the Cooperation Group, while the ESAs report annually through the Joint Committee. If the same underlying incident information is relevant to both, one report would not discharge the other because the recipients and reporting functions differ.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are imposed on different institutional actors and concern different reporting products: EU-CyCLONe reports on the management and trends of large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crises, whereas the ESAs provide an anonymised, aggregated annual report on serious ICT-related incidents based on information supplied by competent authorities. Each actor can perform its own duty without preventing the other from doing so.
verdict.evidence_span_a: EU-CyCLONe brengt regelmatig verslag uit aan de samenwerkingsgroep over het beheer van grootschalige cyberbeveiligingsincidenten en crises, alsook trends, waarbij met name aandacht wordt besteed aan de gevolgen ervan voor essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De ETA’s brengen jaarlijks via het Gemengd Comité een geanonimiseerd en geaggregeerd verslag uit over de ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, de details waarvan door de bevoegde autoriteiten overeenkomstig artikel 19, lid 6, worden verstrekt, met vermelding van ten minste het aantal ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, de aard ervan, de gevolgen ervan voor de werking van financiële entiteiten of cliënten, de genomen corrigerende maatregelen en de kosten.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents that may simultaneously qualify as cross-border significant incidents under BWBR0052872 and serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A single incident can trigger both regimes. Provision A requires the central contact point to notify the central contact points of other affected Member States and ENISA without delay, while provision B requires the market-surveillance authority to notify different national public authorities or bodies; neither text says that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different authorities and can be performed cumulatively without either authority violating the other rule. Provision B does not itself impose a second filing by the reporting entity, and the texts do not expressly establish that the same incident necessarily satisfies both definitions or that the authorities cannot coordinate their notifications.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk AI system reports an incident occurring in two EU Member States that qualifies both as a significant incident under BWBR0052872 and as a serious incident under Article 3(49)(c) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. The central contact point must notify the other affected Member States' central contact points and ENISA 'onverwijld', while the market-surveillance authority must notify the national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1). Those are separate recipient groups, so notification through one authority does not discharge the other authority's duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt het centrale contactpunt de centrale contactpunten van de andere getroffen lidstaten en Enisa onverwijld daarvan in kennis
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit de in artikel 77, lid 1, bedoelde nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen in kennis

verdict.shared_subject: Handling and communication of ICT/cyber incidents involving a financial entity and cross-border authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the central contact point to notify the central contact points of other affected Member States and ENISA without delay when the reported incident, near-incident or cyber threat concerns at least two Member States. Provision B requires the competent authority to acknowledge receipt of the financial entity’s first notification and reports, but it does not impose a reporting duty on the same actor or specify a separate recipient/deadline that would create a cumulative filing burden.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and at different stages: A concerns the central contact point’s onward cross-border notification, while B concerns the competent authority’s acknowledgement after receiving a financial entity’s notification. The texts can both be complied with, and B’s acknowledgement is not a second filing by the central contact point or financial entity to a different recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt het centrale contactpunt de centrale contactpunten van de andere getroffen lidstaten en Enisa onverwijld daarvan in kennis
verdict.evidence_span_b: bevestigt de bevoegde autoriteit na ontvangst van de in artikel 19, lid 4, bedoelde eerste kennisgeving en verslagen, de ontvangst ervan

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or notification duties under EU legislation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose communications duties, but they concern different triggering events, actors, recipients, timing, and content. Provision A concerns the Commission notifying the European Parliament and the Council immediately after adopting a delegated act; Provision B concerns the ESAs reporting annually through the Joint Committee on serious ICT-related incidents.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are readily cumulative because they are imposed on different actors for different events and serve different purposes. The Commission can notify the Parliament and Council under Article 92 while the ESAs separately submit their annual anonymised and aggregated incident report to the Joint Committee; neither duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zodra de Commissie een gedelegeerde handeling heeft vastgesteld, doet zij daarvan gelijktijdig kennisgeving aan het Europees Parlement en de Raad.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De ETA’s brengen jaarlijks via het Gemengd Comité een geanonimiseerd en geaggregeerd verslag uit over de ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents that may simultaneously qualify as a significant incident under BWBR0052872 and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying event could trigger both regimes for the same actor: Article 26 requires an early warning to the CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, while Article 73 requires a notification to the market-surveillance authorities, potentially on a different causal-link trigger and with a 15-day outer deadline. The filings are cumulative because the recipients and statutory reporting regimes differ; sending the Article 26 warning does not, on the text shown, notify the market-surveillance authority, and vice versa.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions concern incident reporting and can be complied with by making the required notifications promptly. The 24-hour deadline is stricter than Article 73's 15-day deadline, so if the same notification and recipient were involved, compliance with Article 26 could satisfy Article 73's timing requirement; however, the texts identify different recipients and do not establish that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer is both an essential or important entity and a provider of a high-risk AI system. It becomes aware of a cyber incident that compromises the AI system's integrity and is also a serious incident causally linked, or probably linked, to that AI system. Within 24 hours it must give an early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority under Article 26, while Article 73 requires a separate notification to the market-surveillance authorities in the Member States where the incident occurred, immediately once the causal link is established and in any event within 15 days. Filing the first warning with the CSIRT and competent authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the market-surveillance notification.
verdict.decisive_exception: No exception or equivalence rule is shown stating that the Article 26 warning to the CSIRT and competent authority is also a notification to the Article 73 market-surveillance authorities, or that one filing discharges the other. The Article 73 provisions supplied also include potentially different special deadlines—two days for a widespread breach or specified serious incident and ten days for death—which could further affect timing, but they do not eliminate the separate-recipient issue.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident or notification-related communications under two different EU/Dutch regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose communication-related obligations, but they concern different actors, triggers, recipients, and subject matter. Provision A concerns CSIRT guidance to a reporting entity about reporting a suspected criminal significant incident to law-enforcement authorities; Provision B concerns a notifying authority informing the Commission and other Member States of changes to a notified body's notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly be complied with simultaneously because they do not require the same actor to make two reports about the same event. A is triggered by suspicion that a significant incident is criminal and involves CSIRT guidance concerning law-enforcement reporting, while B is triggered by relevant changes in a notification and is addressed to the Commission and other Member States.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer wordt vermoed dat het significante incident van criminele aard is, geeft het CSIRT ook richtsnoeren aan de meldende entiteit voor het melden van het significante incident aan de rechtshandhavingsinstanties.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanmeldende autoriteit stelt de Commissie en de andere lidstaten via het in artikel 30, lid 2, bedoelde elektronische aanmeldingssysteem in kennis van alle relevante wijzigingen in de aanmelding van een aangemelde instantie.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incidents by an entity or provider that falls within both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident reported under Article 25 by an essential entity that is also a critical entity triggers a transfer of information to the authority designated under Article 8 of the Critical Entities Resilience Act. Separately, a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system triggers reporting to the market-surveillance authority, after which that authority must notify the Article 77(1) national bodies; the texts identify different reporting chains and do not say that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively without contradiction: the same underlying incident may be reported through both statutory channels, with each authority receiving the information required by its own regime. Article 73 itself places the notification duty on the market-surveillance authority after receiving a provider's report, whereas Article 40 places an information-transfer duty on the competent authority, so the provisions do not expressly require the same actor to make incompatible filings.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk medical-device AI system is an essential entity that is also a critical entity. An incident causes serious harm to a person's health, making it a 'serious incident' under the AI Act, and is also a 'significant incident' reported under Article 25. The provider must report the serious incident to the relevant market-surveillance authority, which must notify the Article 77(1) national bodies, while the Article 40 chain requires information about the significant incident to be provided to the authority referred to in Article 8 of the Critical Entities Resilience Act. These are separate statutory channels and recipients; neither provision states that one report substitutes for the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: No exception or substitution rule is shown. In particular, the texts do not establish that reporting to the market-surveillance authority or notification to the Article 77(1) bodies satisfies the separate Article 40 information duty, or that the Article 40 recipient is the same recipient as the Article 73 reporting authority or its notified bodies.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na ontvangst van een melding met betrekking tot een ernstig incident als bedoeld in artikel 3, punt 49), c), stelt de betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit de in artikel 77, lid 1, bedoelde nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen in kennis.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or personal-data incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report to both its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the Article 27 notification. B separately requires a controller, where the breach is likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms, to notify the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours; the recipients and reporting contents are not stated to be interchangeable.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be satisfied cumulatively: the entity can make the GDPR notification within 72 hours and later submit the NIS2 final report within one month. Nothing in either text says that one filing substitutes for the other, and the different recipients indicate separate duties rather than a single report governed by the stricter deadline.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer qualifying as an essential or important entity suffers a cyber incident that compromises personal data and is likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms. It must notify the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, while also submitting the Article 29 final report within one month to its CSIRT and the competent authority; notifying the supervisory authority does not, on the texts shown, discharge the two Article 29 filings or vice versa.
verdict.decisive_exception: The GDPR notification duty does not apply if it is not likely that the breach poses a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. The scenario assumes that this exception does not apply. No provision shown establishes that the Article 29 report to the CSIRT and competent authority may be combined with, or substituted by, the GDPR notification to the Article 55 supervisory authority.

verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Governance and communication concerning ICT or personal-data incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to the same financial entity when a personal-data breach is also a serious ICT-related incident. Provision A requires immediate notification to the affected person, while provision B requires the governing body to establish internal corporate reporting channels capable of obtaining information about serious ICT-related incidents and their consequences; these are different actions and recipients, so one does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct, cumulatively satisfiable duties rather than incompatible commands. A concerns notifying the affected individual of a qualifying personal-data breach, whereas B concerns an organisational governance mechanism for internal information flow; the entity can notify the person and maintain the required internal channels without contradiction.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations for ICT/cyber incidents affecting entities and their clients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29, while B requires a financial entity to notify its clients without delay when a serious ICT-related incident affects clients’ financial interests. If the same actor and event fall within both regimes, the duties could be cumulative because A’s recipient and deadline are not stated here, whereas B expressly requires prompt client notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied together: the actor can make the report required under Articles 26–29 and separately notify affected clients without delay. The texts do not show that A and B require different filings for the same event, because A’s recipient, timing, and reporting content are left to Articles 26–29, and B is expressly a client-notification duty rather than necessarily a regulatory incident report.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0052872 Articles 26–29, especially the provisions specifying the recipient, deadline, and content of the report required by Article 25; also the scope provisions determining whether the same financial entity is an essential or important entity under A and a financial entity under B.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incidents involving entities or high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires CSIRTs or competent authorities to provide information to the competent authorities under Directive (EU) 2022/2557 about significant incidents and related cyber threats or near-incidents reported by entities designated as critical entities. B concerns measures and notification procedures involving the market-surveillance authority for serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems. If the same event is both a significant incident for a critical entity and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, the regimes may require information to be sent through or to different authorities, with no shown rule that one communication discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not themselves impose two reporting duties on the same actor: A assigns an information-sharing duty to CSIRTs or competent authorities, while B requires the market-surveillance authority to act within seven days after receiving a notification and follow Regulation 2019/1020 procedures. The contextual paragraphs indicate that the entity's notification under A and the provider's notification under B may be separate obligations, but the exact recipient and timing of B's underlying notification are not stated in the provision shown.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing text is the provision governing the notification referred to in 32024R1689 art. 73(1), including who must notify, to which market-surveillance authority, and when; and, if needed, the applicable reporting provisions of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Without that text, it cannot be established that the same actor must make two separate filings to different recipients or on different clocks.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen, en volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet.

verdict.shared_subject: A potential cybersecurity incident involving a personal-data breach during the transitional treatment of an earlier Wbni notification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern the same underlying incident and require communication to authorities, but they identify different recipients: A requires the Minister to forward the notification to the competent authority, while B requires the competent authority to notify the supervisory authority in its own Member State. If these are independent duties, one communication would not necessarily discharge the other, creating a cumulative reporting chain.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose sequential or complementary communications rather than incompatible obligations: A concerns treating and forwarding an earlier Wbni notification, whereas B concerns the competent authority notifying the GDPR supervisory authority after learning of a potential personal-data breach. Nothing in either text forbids the other communication, and B may simply operate after A where the relevant conditions are met.
verdict.missing_reference: The full provisions governing the competent authority's notification under Article 35(1), the relationship between Article 95's transitional forwarding mechanism and Article 35, and whether the Article 95 recipient is the same authority that must act under Article 35(2) would be needed to establish two independent filings rather than a complementary chain.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires reporting a significant incident to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, with an early warning and subsequent reports. B separately requires financial entities to report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority under Article 46, so one incident may trigger filings under both regimes, potentially with different content and procedures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can submit the NIS2 reports to the CSIRT or competent authority and the DORA reports to the relevant competent authority. B also expressly contemplates that information may be provided to NIS2 authorities or CSIRTs, and nothing shown makes one filing legally impossible or states that the two reports must be separate filings for the same incident.
verdict.missing_reference: The deadlines and reporting procedure in DORA Article 20, referred to in Article 19(4), are not shown. Those provisions would be needed to determine whether the same incident triggers genuinely separate filings on different clocks or whether the DORA filing can satisfy the applicable NIS2 reporting duty.

verdict.shared_subject: Significant incidents or security breaches affecting network and information systems, including transitional notifications.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A concerns forwarding an existing notification to the competent national authority, while B requires the CSIRT, competent authority, or central contact point to notify other affected Member States and ENISA without delay. If the same incident triggers both provisions, the national-authority forwarding in A does not itself notify the other Member States or ENISA, so the duties appear cumulative and directed to different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate sequentially: the notification under A is treated as an early warning and may be forwarded by the Minister to the competent authority, after which the competent authority or another designated body can make the external notifications required by B. Nothing in either text expressly makes the two notifications mutually exclusive or impossible to perform together.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A pre-existing notification concerning a security breach with potentially significant effects on service continuity is covered by A and is therefore forwarded by the Minister to the competent authority. The same breach is also a significant incident affecting two or more Member States. The competent authority must then notify the other affected Member States and ENISA without delay under B; forwarding the notification to the national competent authority does not itself constitute those separate notifications, and A supplies no deadline or rule coordinating the two steps.

verdict.shared_subject: Institutional procedures involving supervisory or coordinating authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a supervisory authority to adopt and communicate a final decision after an EDPB notification, while provision B concerns a CSIRT facilitating interaction between a vulnerability reporter and a manufacturer or provider. One might argue that both involve authority-mediated communications and could create overlapping procedural burdens, but they concern different proceedings, actors, and subject matter.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different authorities in different contexts: A governs final decisions in GDPR dispute-resolution proceedings, whereas B governs CSIRT facilitation of vulnerability reporting. A has a one-month deadline and communications tied to a final decision; B requires facilitation where necessary and does not require a filing by the CSIRT to the recipients identified in A. They can therefore operate independently without either duty discharging or obstructing the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related information and reporting involving the central contact point, ENISA, competent authorities, CSIRTs, and financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information following ICT or cyber incidents, and Provision A requires a recurring submission to ENISA. One might argue that the same incident information could also be involved in the notification and reports received by the competent authority under Provision B, creating overlapping reporting processes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A expressly requires the central contact point to submit an anonymised, aggregated quarterly summary to ENISA. The selected norm in Provision B instead requires the competent authority to acknowledge receipt of an initial notification and reports from a financial entity; it does not impose a second filing by that entity or central contact point, nor does it specify a conflicting recipient or deadline. The duties therefore concern different actors and functions and can readily coexist.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT- or personal-data incidents and the resulting notification, evaluation, or reporting duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without unreasonable delay after learning of a personal-data breach, while B requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated when serious ICT-related incidents occur and requires a report to the competent authority if requested. For an entity subject to both, the same serious incident could therefore trigger an immediate notification to the controller and a separate framework-evaluation report to the competent authority, with different recipients and potentially different timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties rather than contradictory ones: A concerns a processor’s notification of a personal-data breach to the controller, whereas B concerns evaluation and possible reporting of an ICT-risk-management framework to the competent authority. Each can be performed independently, and B’s annual or incident-triggered evaluation does not purport to replace A’s prompt notification.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity acting as processor suffers a serious ICT incident that also constitutes a personal-data breach. It must inform the controller “zonder onredelijke vertraging” under A, while under B it must document and evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework because a serious ICT-related incident occurred and must provide the evaluation report to the competent authority if requested; notifying the controller does not discharge the separate report-to-authority duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: Information sharing about reported incidents, near-incidents and cyber threats by CSIRTs/central contact points
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 39 requires the central contact point, in specified cross-border cases, to notify the central contact points of other affected Member States and ENISA without delay. Article 30 separately contemplates that CSIRTs and, where applicable, competent authorities provide central contact points with information about voluntary notifications; the duties could involve different transmitting actors and recipients, and Article 30 does not state that the Article 39 notification discharges this information-sharing duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively without contradiction: Article 39 concerns onward notification by the central contact point to other affected Member States and ENISA, while Article 30 concerns information supplied by CSIRTs or competent authorities to central contact points concerning voluntary notifications. Article 30 also expressly protects the reporting entity from additional obligations merely because it made a voluntary report, so it does not impose a conflicting duty on that entity.

Provision B requires the management body of a financial entity to establish corporate-level reporting channels for information about ICT incidents and their consequences, so an incident could involve both reporting-related duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B requires only the establishment of internal information channels; it does not require a separate incident filing, recipient, or deadline. Provision A concerns an external progress/final report to the CSIRT and competent authority, and the duties can readily be performed cumulatively without either discharging or contradicting the other.

These are distinct notification duties addressed to different recipients, and neither text says that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different authorities and can be performed cumulatively without either authority violating the other's rule. Moreover, the shown text does not establish that the same event necessarily satisfies both triggers, so there is no inherent contradiction or impossible deadline.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk AI system supplied in the EU causes an incident that both constitutes a serious incident under Article 3(49)(c) and may constitute a GDPR personal-data breach. The competent authority notifies the supervisory authority established in its own Member State under A, while the market-surveillance authority notifies the national public authorities or bodies referred to in Article 77(1) under B; filing one notification does not discharge the separate duty to make the other notification.
verdict.decisive_exception: None apparent from the provisions shown. The decisive feature is that the duties identify different recipients; no exception or substitution rule is stated.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risicobeheer, significante ICT-incidenten en rapportage door regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires incident-specific warnings, incident reports and later reports to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B requires a separate report on the evaluation of the ICT risk-management framework to the competent authority when requested. For a financial entity that experiences a significant ICT incident and is also asked to provide the framework-evaluation report, the incident filings do not obviously discharge the separate evaluation-report duty because they concern different subject matter and may involve different information and timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties rather than incompatible ones: A concerns reporting a significant incident, whereas B concerns documenting and evaluating the ICT risk-management framework and supplying an evaluation report on request. The fact that both may be sent to the competent authority does not create a conflict, and A's incident deadlines do not purport to replace B's requested evaluation report.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting involving a significant/serious incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the CSIRT or competent authority to respond to the reporting entity after receiving an early warning, while B requires national competent authorities to notify the Commission immediately of every serious incident. For an incident that is both significant under A and serious under B, these are distinct communications to different recipients, on different clocks, so neither communication discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively without contradiction: the competent authority can send its response to the reporting entity and separately notify the Commission. Nothing in either text forbids the other communication or makes the duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A national competent authority receives an early warning from an entity about an AI-system incident that both qualifies as a significant incident under NIS2 and causes serious, irreversible disruption to critical infrastructure, making it a serious incident under the AI Act. The authority must provide the reporting entity with a response, if possible within 24 hours, under A, and must separately notify the Commission immediately under B; sending one communication does not satisfy the other because the recipients are different.

These duties concern different actors and recipients, however, and B does not require the reporting entity to make the notification itself.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties on different actors: A concerns CSIRT guidance to the reporting entity, while B concerns competent authorities notifying GDPR supervisory authorities. The texts therefore do not require one actor to make two incompatible or cumulative filings, and compliance with one duty is not presented as discharging the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a central contact point to notify other Member States’ central contact points and ENISA without delay when a reported incident, near-incident or cyber threat affects at least two Member States. Provision B imposes an organisational independence requirement on notifying authorities concerning decisions on notifying conformity-assessment bodies. They do not regulate the same event, duty, recipient, or subject matter, so no concrete conflict is apparent.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant incidents involving entities covered by both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity itself to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B requires CSIRTs or competent authorities to provide information to the authorities competent under Directive (EU) 2022/2557, but it does not expressly require the entity to make a second filing; this may instead be an onward-information duty for public authorities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and can operate cumulatively: the entity reports under A, after which the CSIRT or competent authority can transmit the relevant information under B. Nothing in B requires the entity to duplicate its report or sets a conflicting deadline.

verdict.shared_subject: The Commission’s notification of an adopted delegated act to the European Parliament and the Council
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties, and they appear in separate EU instruments. One might argue that each creates an independent legal obligation, potentially requiring two notifications under two legal bases. However, both specify the same event, the same recipients, and simultaneous notification, with no textual indication that separate filings or different content are required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are substantively identical: once the Commission adopts a delegated act, it must notify the European Parliament and the Council simultaneously. A single simultaneous notification to those same recipients can satisfy both duties; nothing in either text requires duplicate filings, separate procedures, or different deadlines. Article 97(3) concerns revocation of delegations and does not alter the notification duty shown.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting involving a network/information-system service and a serious AI-system incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying pre-existing Wbni notification is treated as an early warning under Article 26 and, for certain continuity-related security breaches, is forwarded by the Minister to the competent authority. Separately, Article 73 requires the market-surveillance authority to notify the Article 77(1) national authorities or bodies after receiving a serious-incident notification; if the same event triggers both regimes, the texts identify different institutional channels and do not say that one notification or forwarding step discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 95 does not impose a second filing by the operator: it provides transitional treatment for an already-made Wbni notification and a ministerial forwarding duty. Article 73 likewise describes a downstream notification by the market-surveillance authority, while the referenced Article 73(1) duty concerns high-risk-AI providers reporting serious incidents to market-surveillance authorities; these may be sequential, cumulative administrative communications rather than incompatible obligations.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Before Article 106 enters into force, a provider of a service covered by Wbni Article 10(1)(b) has made a Wbni notification about a network-and-information-systems security breach that may significantly affect service continuity. The same event is also a serious AI-system incident under Article 3(49), and the provider is a high-risk-AI provider. The Wbni notification is treated as an early warning and is forwarded by the Minister to the competent authority, while the provider must report the serious AI incident to the market-surveillance authority, which must then notify the Article 77(1) national authorities or bodies. Filing through the Wbni route does not, on the text shown, establish that the provider's AI incident report to the market-surveillance authority—or the latter authority's notification to the Article 77(1) bodies—is unnecessary.
verdict.missing_reference: The full provisions governing the provider's reporting duty under Article 73(1), the identity and powers of the Article 77(1) bodies, and any coordination or deemed-compliance rule between the Wbni and AI Act reporting regimes would be needed to determine whether one filing legally substitutes for another.
verdict.decisive_exception: No text shown states that the Wbni notification or the Minister's forwarding of it is deemed to satisfy the separate Article 73(1) serious-incident reporting duty, or that notification of the Article 77(1) bodies replaces reporting to the market-surveillance authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de melding ziet op een inbreuk op de beveiliging van netwerk- en informatiesystemen die aanzienlijke gevolgen kan hebben voor de continuïteit van de door de melder verleende dienst als bedoeld in artikel 10, eerste lid, onderdeel b, van de Wet beveiliging netwerk- en informatiesystemen, zendt Onze Minister de melding door aan de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na ontvangst van een melding met betrekking tot een ernstig incident als bedoeld in artikel 3, punt 49), c), stelt de betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit de in artikel 77, lid 1, bedoelde nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen in kennis.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification and reporting of significant incidents by entities providing services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same significant incident and both require action without delay. However, they require communications to different recipients: service recipients under A, and the CSIRT or competent authority under B; neither text says that the regulatory report substitutes for notifying service recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are readily cumulative: the entity can notify its service recipients and separately report the incident to the CSIRT or competent authority. The different recipients mean that the 24-hour regulatory report cannot discharge the customer-notification duty, but this does not make simultaneous compliance impossible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider, which is an essential or important entity, becomes aware of a significant incident affecting the provision of its trust services and adversely affecting service delivery. It must notify its service recipients immediately under A and separately submit the B report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours; notifying one recipient does not notify the other, and the provisions do not specify how the two reporting processes are coordinated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an electronic communications service provider where the same security breach is also a significant incident under NIS2.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, while provision B requires an early warning and incident reports to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. If one breach satisfies both triggers, the provider appears to owe separate reports to different recipients, on different procedural requirements; reporting to one does not textually discharge reporting to the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative reporting duties rather than contradictory commands: a provider can notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately and separately submit the NIS2 warning and reports. The different triggers also mean that B may not apply to every breach covered by A, and the texts do not expressly establish that the competent authority is different from the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A public electronic communications provider suffers a security breach that adversely affects personal-data protection and also has significant effects on the provision of its services. The provider must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens 'onverwijld' under A and give the NIS2 early warning to 'het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit' within 24 hours, followed by the incident report within 72 hours under B; filing with one recipient does not, on the text shown, replace the filing to the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the NIS2 'bevoegde autoriteit' is legally the same authority as the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, and whether national implementation provides a single-report or forwarding mechanism that discharges the separate A duty, is not established by the provisions shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related obligations involving personal-data breaches and serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A personal-data breach involving a high-risk AI system could also be a serious incident, so the same underlying event may trigger both provisions. However, Article 33 requires documentation but does not state a notification deadline or a separate filing to a specified recipient, while Article 73 requires a report within ten days; the shown text therefore does not establish two cumulative reports to different recipients or on different clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties: Article 33 requires documenting personal-data breaches so the supervisory authority can check compliance, whereas Article 73 requires timely reporting of a qualifying serious incident involving a high-risk AI system. An operator can document the breach and make the Article 73 report; nothing shown makes either duty discharge or contradict the other.
verdict.missing_reference: The full reporting language of GDPR Article 33(1), including its recipient and 72-hour notification deadline, and the recipient/reporting details in AI Act Article 73(1), would be needed to assess whether the same event requires two separate filings. The text shown for Article 33 is limited to documentation, and the text shown for Article 73 does not identify a recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting and documentation concerning ICT/cyber incidents and ICT-risk management
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose recurring information or documentation duties that may concern overlapping incident-related material. A central contact point must submit a quarterly summary to ENISA, while the ICT-risk-management framework must be documented and evaluated at least annually and a report supplied to the competent authority on request; for an entity subject to both, these appear to be separate obligations to different recipients, with no text saying that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different objects and triggers: A requires an anonymised, aggregated quarterly summary of reported incidents and cyberthreats, whereas B concerns documentation and evaluation of the risk-management framework, with a report only when the competent authority requests it. They can therefore be performed cumulatively without incompatible content or deadlines; the different recipients do not by themselves create a conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity subject to both regimes has reported a significant ICT incident and must, through its central contact point, include it in the next quarterly anonymised and aggregated summary sent to ENISA. Separately, after its annual evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework, it must provide the competent authority with the requested evaluation report. Sending the ENISA summary does not send the framework-evaluation report to the competent authority, so both filings may be required on different clocks and to different recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient elke drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over gemelde significante incidenten, incidenten, bijna-incidenten en cyberdreigingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, alsook wanneer zich ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten voordoen en na toezichtinstructies of -conclusies die voortvloeien uit relevante tests of auditprocessen op het gebied van digitale operationele weerbaarheid. Het wordt voortdurend verbeterd op basis van de lessen die uit de uitvoering en de monitoring naar voren komen. Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.

verdict.shared_subject: A serious incident involving a high-risk AI system that is also a personal-data breach, where the provider is also the GDPR controller.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same event can trigger two mandatory notifications by the same actor to different authorities: the GDPR notification goes to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours, while the AI Act notification goes to the market-surveillance authorities in the Member States where the incident occurred. Neither provision says that one notification substitutes for the other, so one filing cannot discharge both duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with by making the required notifications, and there is no incompatible command or prohibition. The AI Act provision shown does not state a deadline in paragraph 1 itself, but its related paragraphs indicate an additional timing regime rather than an exemption from the GDPR duty.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider offers a high-risk AI system in several Member States. A cyberattack causes unauthorised access to stored personal data and constitutes a serious incident causally linked to the AI system. The provider, acting as GDPR controller, must notify the competent data-protection supervisory authority within 72 hours, and must separately notify the market-surveillance authorities of each Member State where the incident occurred; notifying one authority does not notify the others or discharge the other legal duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: No exception or substitution rule is shown stating that an AI Act notification to market-surveillance authorities replaces the GDPR notification to the competent data-protection supervisory authority, or vice versa.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: A trust-service provider's significant incident and its ICT risk-management framework
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A trust-service provider may have to report a significant incident within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority under A, while B requires the ICT risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated at least annually and a report on that evaluation to be supplied to the competent authority on request. These are different duties with different triggers and contents, so an incident report does not obviously discharge the separate framework-evaluation report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with: the provider makes the incident report required by A and separately documents and evaluates its ICT risk-management framework under B, supplying the evaluation report if requested. B's annual or periodic framework duty is not an alternative deadline for, or prohibition on, A's incident reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd

verdict.shared_subject: Official handling of reported cyber/AI-related serious incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious cyber incident involving a high-risk AI system operated by a critical entity could enter both regimes: it may be reported under NIS2 and shared by the CSIRT/competent authority with the CER competent authority, while the AI market-surveillance authority must act after receiving an AI Act serious-incident notification. This creates coordination demands between authorities, but neither text makes one filing or response incompatible with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different steps on different institutional actors. A requires CSIRTs or NIS2 competent authorities to provide CER authorities with information reported by critical entities; B requires a market-surveillance authority to take appropriate measures within seven days after it receives an AI Act notification. Neither provision says that reporting under one regime discharges, prevents, delays, or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De CSIRT’s of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteiten verstrekken de uit hoofde van Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2557 bevoegde autoriteiten informatie over significante incidenten, en cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations following a cybersecurity incident that is also a personal-data breach.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A medical-device manufacturer can be both an essential/important entity under the Dutch regime and a GDPR controller. A single ransomware incident affecting personal data can require a GDPR notification to the data-protection supervisory authority within 72 hours, while also requiring a separate Dutch final/progress report to both its CSIRT and its competent authority on a different timetable.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations do not command incompatible conduct: the GDPR requires an early breach notification, whereas Article 29 requires a later final report (or progress report if the incident continues). Their content substantially overlaps, so an entity may reuse factual material and comply with both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A manufacturer of medical devices suffers ransomware that both compromises availability of its network systems and permits unauthorised access to patient/device-user personal data. As GDPR controller, it must notify "de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit" within "uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen." As an essential or important entity, after its Article 27 notification it must submit its Article 29 report to "haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit" "uiterlijk één maand na de melding." Notification to the GDPR authority does not constitute filing the required report with the CSIRT and Dutch competent authority, and the Dutch report does not discharge the GDPR notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Authority-to-authority information flows following incidents that may involve critical entities and AI systems.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A possible dual-reporting concern arises if the same Dutch public body were both the Article 40 competent authority and the AI Act market-surveillance authority, and one event were simultaneously a reported significant incident and an AI serious incident. It could then have to communicate with the critical-entities authority under A and with the Article 77(1) bodies under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose notification duties on differently defined authorities, after different triggering reports: A concerns a significant incident reported under Article 25 by an essential entity that is also a critical entity, whereas B concerns the market-surveillance authority after an AI serious-incident report. Neither text establishes that the notifying authorities are the same actor, that the incident categories coincide, or that either notification substitutes for or obstructs the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is
verdict.evidence_span_b: Na ontvangst van een melding met betrekking tot een ernstig incident als bedoeld in artikel 3, punt 49), c), stelt de betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit de in artikel 77, lid 1, bedoelde nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen in kennis.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification of serious/significant incidents to public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A cross-border incident involving a high-risk AI system could qualify both as a significant cybersecurity incident under A and as an ernstig incident under B. It may then generate notifications to different national/EU recipients, potentially creating parallel information flows about the same event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors at different points in separate notification chains: A binds the centrale contactpunt after notification by the CSIRT, whereas B binds the betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit after it receives an AI serious-incident report. Neither text makes one actor's notification substitute for, prevent, or contradict the other's notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt het centrale contactpunt de centrale contactpunten van de andere getroffen lidstaten en Enisa onverwijld daarvan in kennis.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit de in artikel 77, lid 1, bedoelde nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen in kennis.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident handling following an ICT/security incident that may also be a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor experiencing a personal-data breach must promptly inform its controller, while a serious ICT-related incident also triggers evaluation of the DORA ICT-risk-management framework and may lead to a report to the competent authority if requested. This can create parallel compliance work for a financial entity acting as processor, but B does not itself require an incident report to the authority on that event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative functions: A is an immediate processor-to-controller notification duty upon a personal-data breach; B is a governance obligation to evaluate and improve the ICT-risk framework after serious ICT incidents, with a report to the authority only if it requests one. Neither provision says that compliance with one replaces, prevents, or discharges compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, alsook wanneer zich ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten voordoen en na toezichtinstructies of -conclusies die voortvloeien uit relevante tests of auditprocessen op het gebied van digitale operationele weerbaarheid. Het wordt voortdurend verbeterd op basis van de lessen die uit de uitvoering en de monitoring naar voren komen. Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.

verdict.shared_subject: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity and experiences a serious/significant ICT or cybersecurity incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same event could qualify both as a BWBR0052872 “significant incident” and as a DORA “ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident.” B requires the entity to notify affected clients “onverwijld,” while A requires a notification “overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29”; if those incorporated articles require notification to a supervisory authority or CSIRT, the event may generate separate notifications to different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Nothing in either displayed text prohibits satisfying both duties. B is expressly a client-information duty, whereas A merely refers to further provisions for the mechanics of reporting; an entity can ordinarily make both a regulatory/CSIRT report and a client notification if both are required.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0052872 articles 26 through 29, especially the provisions identifying the recipient(s), deadlines, and content of the Article 25 significant-incident notification. Those provisions are necessary to determine whether A entails a separate filing and therefore a dual_reporting_tension.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: A significant incident affecting the provision of a trust service by an essential or important entity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: For a trust-service provider that is also an essential or important entity, the same significant incident can trigger two outward communications: notification of service recipients under A and notification to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours under B. They have different recipients, so reporting to the authority does not inform affected customers, and informing customers does not make the regulatory report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative but not contradictory: A requires prompt information to recipients where appropriate, while B requires a prompt regulatory notification with a 24-hour outer limit. The provider can make both communications, and Article 23(1) itself pairs the authority-reporting obligation with informing service recipients, confirming that these are complementary channels rather than alternative ones.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A qualified trust-service provider that is an essential entity suffers a ransomware incident disabling its certificate-validation service for several hours. The incident significantly affects provision of its trust services and may adversely affect relying parties. It must notify the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours under B, while, where appropriate, it must also promptly inform its service recipients under A. These are separate communications to “de ontvangers van haar diensten” and to “het CSIRT of ... de bevoegde autoriteit”; filing the 24-hour authority report does not discharge the recipient-information duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Authority handling and communication following an incident that may be both a NIS2 significant incident and an AI Act serious incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A national authority that is both the relevant NIS2 competent authority/CSIRT interface and an AI Act national competent authority may have to send two separate communications concerning the same underlying event: feedback to the reporting entity under A and notification to the Commission under B. The recipients differ, and B requires notification “onmiddellijk,” whereas A requires a response “onverwijld en zo mogelijk binnen 24 uur,” so sending either communication does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different immediate triggers and functions: A concerns a response after receipt of an entity's NIS2 early warning, while B concerns Commission notification of an AI-related serious incident. They can ordinarily be performed cumulatively, and not every significant NIS2 incident is an AI Act serious incident, nor vice versa.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A Dutch authority is designated both as the competent authority receiving NIS2 reports from a hospital operator and as an AI Act national competent authority.
