verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security, integrity, misuse, or serious incidents involving an electronic service or high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same event is both a security or integrity breach of the organisation’s own electronic public service and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, Provision A requires immediate notice to the Minister, while Provision B requires a separate incident notification by the provider or deployer within ten days. The texts identify different triggering conditions and do not state that notification under one instrument satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions may apply to different actors and incidents: A concerns a public body or designated organisation and its own electronic service, whereas B concerns a provider or deployer of a high-risk AI system and death-related serious incidents. Moreover, B’s recipient is not specified in the excerpt, so the text does not conclusively establish that two separate filings to different recipients are required.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation operates a high-risk AI system as part of its own electronic public service. A fatal incident is both a security or integrity breach of that service and a serious incident causally linked, or suspected to be linked, to the high-risk AI system. The organisation must notify Onze Minister “onverwijld” under A and must also make the Article 73 notification “onmiddellijk” once the causal link is established or suspected, and in any event within ten days of awareness; notification to Onze Minister under A does not, on the text shown, establish compliance with B’s separate AI-incident reporting duty.
verdict.missing_reference: The recipient and procedural details of the Article 73 notification, including whether it is made to the same authority as under Article 18 and whether one notification can legally satisfy both regimes.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether Article 73’s omitted provisions designate the same recipient and permit a single filing to satisfy both duties. If they do, the stricter or earlier filing could make the duties compatible; that is not established by the text shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 wordt bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting certain security breaches or serious incidents involving AI or electronic communications services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the provider of a public electronic communications service to notify the Dutch data-protection authority without delay when a qualifying security breach affects personal-data protection. B imposes an immediate, at latest two-day notification duty for a widespread breach or serious incident, and the referenced paragraph 1 identifies market-surveillance authorities as the recipients; the same event could therefore trigger two filings to different authorities on different legal bases.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be satisfied: the actor can notify the data-protection authority under A without delay and make the separate notification required by B within two days. Neither text says that one notification substitutes for the other, and the different subject-matter triggers and recipients support cumulative rather than mutually exclusive compliance.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An AI system supplied by a public electronic communications service provider suffers a security breach that affects personal data, causes a serious and irreversible disruption to critical infrastructure, and qualifies as a serious incident under Article 3(49)(b). The provider must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens 'onverwijld' under A and must also notify the market-surveillance authority under Article 73(1), with B requiring that notification 'onmiddellijk ... doch uiterlijk twee dagen' after awareness; filing with the data-protection authority does not discharge the separate market-surveillance notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens die zijn verwerkt in verband met de levering van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst in de Europese Unie.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 van dit artikel wordt bij een wijdverbreide inbreuk of een ernstig incident, zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 3, punt 49), b), de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Serious ICT/AI-related incidents affecting clients and potentially falling under both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity may have to inform its clients immediately under Provision A, while an AI provider or deployer must report the serious incident under Provision B within a separate statutory period. The duties concern different actions and, on the text shown, Provision B does not make a client notification satisfy the market-surveillance notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the financial entity can notify affected clients immediately under A and the relevant provider or deployer can separately notify the market-surveillance authorities under B. They do not impose incompatible content, deadlines, or prohibitions; their different recipients indicate separate duties rather than a conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity uses a high-risk AI system, and a serious ICT-related incident both materially affects the financial interests of its clients and qualifies as a serious incident involving that high-risk AI system. The financial entity must notify its potentially affected clients “onverwijld” under A, while the provider or, where applicable, the deployer must make the Article 73 notification to the market-surveillance authorities “uiterlijk 15 dagen” after becoming aware of the incident. Client notification does not itself constitute the separate market-surveillance notification, so both filings are required, potentially involving different actors and clocks.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting-burden relationship on the text shown. The relevant issue is that the duties have different recipients: clients under A and, through the referenced paragraph 1, market-surveillance authorities under B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting and aggregation of cybersecurity incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related reporting, but they require separate submissions by different actors to different recipients on different schedules. An entity must submit its detailed final report to its CSIRT and competent authority, while the central contact point must submit a separate anonymised, aggregated report to ENISA every three months; one filing cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively without requiring incompatible content or timing: the entity supplies detailed incident information to its CSIRT and competent authority, and the central contact point later aggregates relevant reported information for ENISA. The duties fall on different actors and serve different reporting functions, so compliance with both is possible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer that is an essential or important entity suffers a significant incident and submits the required detailed final report within one month to “haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.” The central contact point must then separately include anonymised and aggregated information about that incident in its report to ENISA “om de drie maanden”; the manufacturer’s filing does not satisfy the central contact point’s ENISA filing, and the ENISA report does not satisfy the manufacturer’s detailed report.
verdict.decisive_exception: None apparent from the texts shown. The decisive feature is that the duties are separate and addressed to different recipients: the entity reports to its CSIRT and competent authority, while the central contact point reports aggregated information to ENISA.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten die overeenkomstig lid 1 van dit artikel en overeenkomstig artikel 30 zijn gemeld.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related or serious incidents involving a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident handling or reporting, and a death linked to a high-risk AI system could also be an ICT-related incident. Provision B imposes an immediate, externally oriented notification deadline, while A requires a process to detect, manage and report ICT incidents, so the exact relationship could appear unclear.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not specify a recipient, filing, or deadline; it requires a financial entity to establish and implement an internal incident-management process. Provision B imposes a separate notification duty on an AI provider or deployer, with a ten-day maximum, and nothing in A says that its process or reporting duty substitutes for B's notification. The duties can therefore be performed cumulatively where both apply.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious cybersecurity/ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: An entity subject to both provisions may have to submit an end report under Article 29 to its CSIRT and competent authority, while also submitting the Article 19 notification and reports to the relevant competent authority under DORA. The recipients and reporting regimes are not identical, and Article 19 expressly preserves possible additional reporting to NIS2 authorities or CSIRTs, suggesting that one filing does not automatically discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can prepare the Article 19 reports using the required models and separately submit the Article 29 end report within one month after the Article 27 notification. Article 19 does not prohibit or replace the Article 29 filing, and the texts shown do not establish that the same report must be duplicated or that the deadlines are incompatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity suffers one serious ICT incident that qualifies under both regimes. It must submit the Article 19 first notification and subsequent reports to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46,” while Article 29 separately requires, no later than one month after the Article 27 notification, an end report to both “haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.” Filing the DORA report to the relevant financial-sector authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate Article 29 filing to the CSIRT and the NIS2 competent authority; the applicable Article 19 deadline is also not shown here.
verdict.missing_reference: The precise deadlines and content requirements in Article 19(4), Article 20(1)(a)(ii), and the provisions determining whether the Article 19 relevant competent authority is the same authority as Article 29’s competent authority. Those provisions could clarify coordination or equivalence, but the shown text already identifies distinct reporting duties and recipients.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether Article 19’s reporting model or a national coordination rule expressly treats the DORA filing as satisfying the Article 29 filing. The shown Article 19 text instead says that reporting to the relevant competent authority is without prejudice to possible additional reporting to authorities or CSIRTs designated under Directive (EU) 2022/2555.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident involving both network-and-information-system security and personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the essential or important entity to submit a final report to its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the Article 27 notification. B separately requires the provider to notify the affected person without delay where the personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect privacy; these are different communications to different recipients, so one cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties rather than contradictory ones: the entity can report the incident to the CSIRT and competent authority and also notify affected individuals. The one-month deadline in A does not prevent the immediate notification required by B, and B's individual notice does not replace A's institutional report.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer that is an essential or important entity suffers a cyberattack compromising stored personal data and likely adversely affecting the privacy of identified individuals. It must submit the Article 29 final report to its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the Article 27 notification, while also notifying each affected person without delay; notifying the individuals does not satisfy the two institutional reporting duties, and filing the institutional report does not satisfy the individual notices.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap from the text shown. The separate duties may be subject to B's contextual exceptions, including the encryption exception in Article 11.3a(5), but those do not turn the two communications into one filing; whether that exception applies in a particular case would require its factual conditions.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: A financial entity providing a public electronic communications service, where the same security breach also constitutes a serious ICT-related incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident may trigger two distinct mandatory notifications by the same entity: provision A requires immediate notice to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, while provision B requires reporting the serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority under Article 46. The recipients are different and neither provision says that one filing substitutes for the other, so compliance with one does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the entity can notify both authorities, using the information and forms required by each regime. Provision B also contemplates coordination with other authorities, but that does not expressly eliminate the separate duty in provision A.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that provides a public electronic communications service suffers a security breach affecting personal data, and the breach is also a serious ICT-related incident. It must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately under provision A and separately report the serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority under Article 46 under provision B; sending the Article 46 report does not, on the text shown, constitute the required notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap. The decisive point is that the provisions identify different recipients and contain no substitution rule. The exact scope of the Article 46 reporting duty and its deadlines are supplied by Article 19(4) and Article 20, but those details do not make the two recipients identical.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious/significant incident involving a high-risk AI system operated by an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A single incident could qualify both as a significant incident under Provision A and as a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system under Provision B. A then requires a filing to both the CSIRT and competent authority within 72 hours, while B imposes a separate deadline of no later than ten days; if B requires a distinct report under the AI Act, the A filing would not discharge it, creating cumulative reporting duties with different clocks and no stated coordination rule.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts shown do not identify a recipient for Provision B or expressly require a separate filing distinct from the report under Provision A. Provision B's ten-day outer deadline is looser than A's 72-hour deadline, so if both provisions concern the same report and recipient, compliance with A would satisfy B's timing requirement.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity operates a high-risk AI system, and one event both compromises the availability, integrity, or confidentiality of network or information systems and causes death plausibly linked to the AI system. The entity reports to its CSIRT and competent authority within 72 hours under A, but the shown text does not establish whether it must also submit a separate report under B, to whom, or in what form.
verdict.missing_reference: The omitted provisions of Article 73 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 that identify the reporting recipient and specify whether the Article 73 notification is a separate filing, together with any coordination or cross-reference rules between that notification and the NIS2-law report under Article 27.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether Article 73's notification is a distinct filing to a different recipient, rather than the same report whose ten-day deadline is already met by the 72-hour filing under Article 27.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant incidents and related cyber incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to notify its service recipients immediately, while provision B requires the central contact point to submit a quarterly summary to Enisa. These are different reporting duties with different actors, recipients, content, and timing, so an incident may generate both obligations without one filing satisfying the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: the entity promptly informs its service recipients, while the central contact point later aggregates and anonymises relevant reports for Enisa. Provision B expressly refers to incidents reported under Article 30, indicating that the two duties are designed to coexist rather than replace one another.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A significant incident adversely affects an essential entity’s services. The entity must notify its service recipients “onverwijld” under Article 30, while the central contact point must separately submit an anonymised, aggregated summary concerning that incident to Enisa “om de drie maanden”; notifying the recipients does not discharge the central contact point’s Enisa filing, and the quarterly summary does not satisfy the entity’s immediate notification duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten die overeenkomstig lid 1 van dit artikel en overeenkomstig artikel 30 zijn gemeld.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk management and incident-related obligations for an entity subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an incident notification to two recipients within a short, incident-triggered deadline. Provision B requires periodic documentation and evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework, and submission of an evaluation report to the competent authority on request; these could create additional compliance work, but B does not require a separate incident report or identify a different recipient or incompatible deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties: A concerns reporting a significant incident to the CSIRT and competent authority, while B concerns documenting and evaluating the risk-management framework and submitting an evaluation report to the competent authority when requested. The texts do not require the same filing to satisfy both duties, nor do they create conflicting deadlines or recipients; both can be complied with cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting/documentation of incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A continuing incident requires a progress report instead of the final report, followed by a final report within one month after resolution; the referenced context says those reports go to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority. B separately requires a high-risk AI provider to notify the market-surveillance authorities in the Member States where the serious incident occurred, on an immediate or short deadline. Thus, one incident could require both a post-incident report under A and a separate notification to different authorities under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed: the entity can make the Article 73 notification promptly and also submit the Article 29 progress/final reporting required for the incident. Nothing in either shown provision says that one filing substitutes for the other or prohibits the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider is both an essential or important entity under BWBR0052872 and the provider of a high-risk AI system under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. A serious AI-related incident occurs and remains ongoing when the Article 29 final-report deadline arrives. The provider must submit an Article 73 notification to the market-surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred, while submitting an Article 29 progress report instead of the final report and later a final report within one month after the incident is handled; the filings go to different recipients and operate on different clocks.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap on the texts shown. The key unresolved issue is whether any unshown procedural rule coordinates or consolidates the filings; neither provision states that the Article 73 notification discharges the Article 29 reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid. Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related/significant incident management and reporting by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes a concrete external-reporting duty, with a 72-hour backstop, to both a CSIRT and the competent authority. Provision B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process that includes reporting, so if that process entails a separate external report, one incident could trigger two regimes with potentially different recipients or deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B, as shown, is a system-level process duty and does not specify a reporting recipient, deadline, or separate filing. It can therefore be satisfied by designing the process to include the reporting required by A; the text does not establish that B requires an additional report or that its process duty conflicts with A.
verdict.missing_reference: A specific provision under Article 17 or elsewhere in Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 that defines the reporting obligation's recipient, deadline, and whether it requires a separate filing from the Article 27 notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and transaction-reporting systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns an incident-related progress report and a later final report, while Provision B requires data-reporting-service providers to maintain systems for checking transaction reports. If the same provider is also an essential or important entity experiencing an ongoing incident, the operational reporting-system duty and the incident-reporting duty could create overlapping compliance work, but the texts do not require two reports to different recipients or on different clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of duties on different or potentially overlapping actors: A governs what an essential or important entity must submit when an incident continues, whereas B requires providers of data-reporting services to operate detection and retransmission systems for transaction reports. Nothing in B requires an incident report, and nothing in A regulates the technical checking of transaction reports, so both duties can be satisfied independently.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident documentation and reporting by an organisation experiencing an incident that is both a GDPR personal-data breach and a significant incident affecting a trust service.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A trust-service provider must report a qualifying significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours, while the GDPR provision requires documentation of every personal-data breach. If the GDPR documentation duty were itself a filing obligation, the same event might appear to require both a GDPR filing and a NIS2 filing. However, the text shown does not impose such a filing duty in Article 33.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires internal documentation so that the supervisory authority can check compliance; it does not require sending that documentation or impose a deadline. Provision B separately requires a trust-service provider to report qualifying significant incidents to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours. The duties can therefore both be performed, and B's report does not purport to replace A's documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an incident that is both a significant incident under the NIS2 implementing legislation and a serious or widespread AI incident under the AI Act.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same event could trigger both duties, with Article 27 requiring a report to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority within 72 hours, while Article 73 requires the Article 73(1) report immediately and no later than two days. The duties appear to concern different reporting regimes and potentially different recipients, so making the faster report would not necessarily discharge the separate NIS2 filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions require prompt reporting, and the two-day deadline in Article 73 is stricter than Article 27’s 72-hour deadline. If Article 73’s report were to the same recipients and contained the information required by Article 27, one filing might satisfy both in practice; however, the shown Article 73 text refers to a report to market-surveillance authorities, whereas Article 27 expressly requires reporting to the CSIRT and competent authority.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer is both an important or essential entity under BWBR0052872 and a provider of a high-risk AI system. A serious AI-system malfunction causes serious harm to a person and also compromises the availability or integrity of services or data, making it a significant incident under Article 27 and a serious incident under Article 73. The manufacturer must report the event to its CSIRT and competent authority within 72 hours and separately report it to the market-surveillance authority immediately and no later than two days after awareness; filing with one set of authorities does not, on the text shown, discharge the other duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the Article 73 report is legally capable of serving as the Article 27 report, or whether the relevant authorities have coordinated procedures allowing one filing, is not established. The shown Article 73(1) identifies market-surveillance authorities, while Article 27 identifies the CSIRT and competent authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 van dit artikel wordt bij een wijdverbreide inbreuk of een ernstig incident, zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 3, punt 49), b), de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting by an organisation or public authority concerning an electronic-service security/integrity incident and, potentially, a high-risk AI fundamental-rights-impact assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same public body or designated organisation uses a high-risk AI system and a security or integrity breach also triggers the fundamental-rights assessment notification, it must notify two different recipients: Onze Minister and the market-surveillance authority. The notification to one authority does not, on the texts shown, discharge the separately addressed notification to the other, and the first duty has an immediate deadline while the second has no stated deadline here.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can apply to different events and actors: provision A concerns a breach or misuse involving the actor’s own electronic service, whereas provision B concerns the results of a completed fundamental-rights-impact assessment for a qualifying high-risk AI system. Even when both apply, each filing can be made independently, and nothing in the texts makes compliance with one impossible or expressly substitutes one notification for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A Dutch public authority operates a qualifying high-risk AI system and uses it through its own electronic service. A security breach of that electronic service occurs, and the authority has also completed the required fundamental-rights-impact assessment for the AI system. The authority must notify Onze Minister onverwijld about the breach and provide the required information, while separately notifying the market-surveillance authority of the assessment results and submitting the completed template; notifying one recipient does not, on the text shown, notify the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision B contains a possible exemption under Article 46(1), but the facts and the content of that exemption are not supplied. If it applies, the second notification may not be required; absent that exemption, the two different recipients indicate cumulative filings.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_subject: Data-related obligations of service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose operational obligations on providers handling data: A requires prompt notification of certain personal-data breaches, while B requires transaction-reporting-service providers to maintain systems for checking and retransmitting transaction reports. A provider might experience a breach affecting systems used for transaction reporting and need to perform both duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts and triggers. A concerns notifying the affected person without delay after a personal-data breach likely to harm privacy; B concerns system functionality for checking transaction reports for completeness and obvious errors and requesting retransmission. Nothing in B prevents or substitutes for the notification required by A, and B does not establish a separate reporting recipient or deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer
verdict.evidence_span_b: beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving a trust-service provider and a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A trust-service provider must report a significant incident affecting its trust services within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority. A high-risk-AI provider or deployer must report a fatal serious incident no later than ten days after awareness, so one event could trigger both regimes with different reporting duties and deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not clearly establish that the same actor, incident, and reporting subject matter are covered by both duties. Provision B does not state a recipient in the text shown, and its ten-day rule may concern a distinct AI serious-incident report rather than the NIS2 report; therefore the texts do not establish two cumulative filings or an actual incompatibility.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing content is the remainder of Article 73, especially the provision identifying the recipient and the required contents/procedure of the AI serious-incident report, together with the definitions or scope rules establishing whether a trust-service provider is also the relevant provider/deployer of the high-risk AI system and whether the same fatal event qualifies both as a significant incident under Article 23 and a serious incident under Article 73.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations for a financial entity that is also a deployer of a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious ICT-related incident may also arise from the use of a high-risk AI system, requiring the financial entity to report to the relevant competent authority under Provision A and to notify the market-surveillance authority of the fundamental-rights assessment results under Provision B. The recipients and reporting subjects differ, and nothing in the shown texts says that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggering events and different substantive information: Provision A concerns serious ICT-related incidents, while Provision B concerns the results of a fundamental-rights impact assessment before use of certain high-risk AI systems. On the text shown, an incident does not necessarily trigger the Article 27 notification, and Article 27 does not necessarily concern an ICT incident.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank uses a high-risk AI system in a covered public-service or Annex III context and suffers a serious ICT-related incident involving that system. The bank must report the incident to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46” under Provision A, while, having completed the required fundamental-rights impact assessment, it must notify “de markttoezichtautoriteit” of its results under Provision B; the shown provisions provide no rule that either filing discharges the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: The texts do not establish whether the Article 27 exemption “in het in artikel 46, lid 1, bedoelde geval” applies, nor whether any other provision treats the two notifications as a single filing. If that exemption applies to the scenario, the second duty would not arise.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious ICT/AI-related incident by a financial entity that is also a provider of a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident could trigger both duties, requiring the actor to report to the relevant competent authority under DORA and separately to the market-surveillance authorities under the AI Act. The recipients are different, and neither provision says that one notification satisfies the other, so the actor would face two cumulative reporting obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed by submitting the required incident information to each authority. They regulate different reporting regimes and do not impose incompatible content or deadlines; the fact that one incident requires multiple reports is not itself a conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that provides a high-risk AI system experiences one serious incident that qualifies both as a serious ICT-related incident and as a serious incident involving its high-risk AI system. It must report the incident to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46” under Provision A and separately to “de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden” under Provision B; filing with the first authority does not, on the texts shown, discharge the second duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: No exception or equivalence rule is shown stating that a DORA report to the relevant competent authority also counts as the AI Act notification to the market-surveillance authorities, or vice versa.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting/application duties under two EU regulations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory language and require an actor to submit information to a recipient: Provision A requires financial entities to notify their clients without delay after a qualifying serious ICT incident, while Provision B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application to a notifying authority. If one entity were subject to both regimes, these would be separate duties to different recipients, but they concern different triggering events and different substantive acts.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different actors and triggers: A concerns financial entities responding to serious ICT-related incidents affecting clients, whereas B concerns conformity-assessment bodies applying for notification. Nothing in either text forbids or displaces the other duty, and compliance with one does not purport to satisfy the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting/documentation after incidents involving entities or AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same incident is both an incident under BWBR0052872 and a serious incident under the AI Act, the provisions impose different timing structures: A requires a progress report while the incident continues and a final report within one month after resolution, whereas B requires an incident notification immediately and no later than 15 days after awareness (subject to the contextual exceptions). This could create overlapping reporting burdens and uncertainty about whether the reports are separate and how their deadlines interact.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish the same filing: A's referenced rule requires a final report to the entity's CSIRT and competent authority, while B's referenced rule requires notification to market-surveillance authorities. They concern different regimes, recipients, and reporting content, so the stricter 15-day deadline cannot discharge A's separate post-resolution report; both can be complied with cumulatively.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An AI system operated by an essential or important entity causes a serious incident that is also an incident reportable under BWBR0052872. The entity must notify the relevant market-surveillance authority immediately and within 15 days of awareness under B, while submitting a progress report if the incident is still ongoing when the final report would otherwise be due and then a final report within one month after the incident is resolved under A; filing the AI notification does not replace the separate report to the CSIRT and competent authority.
verdict.decisive_exception: The supplied text does not establish whether the two regimes contain a coordination rule, exemption, or deemed-substitution rule for overlapping incidents. The contextual provisions identify different recipients and, for B, special deadlines of two or ten days for specified incidents, but do not eliminate A's separate reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant or serious incidents involving network/information systems or high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose incident-reporting obligations that could apply to the same real-world event, but the shown text does not identify the recipient or deadline for the Dutch-law report, while the AI Act provision sets a separate deadline. If the same actor and incident fall within both regimes, two potentially distinct reporting duties could arise.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish that the same actor must make two separate filings to different recipients. Article 25 expressly makes its duty subject to Articles 26–29, whose reporting recipient and timing are not shown, and Article 73 likewise concerns a specific AI-Act reporting regime; the texts therefore do not establish cumulative reporting or an irreconcilable burden.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0052872 Articles 26–29, especially the provisions specifying the recipient, content, timing and procedure for the Article 25 report; also the full scope of Article 73(1) if needed to confirm the same actor and incident are covered.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Security incidents affecting an entity that is both an essential/important entity and a provider of a public electronic communications service
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident may trigger both duties: provision A requires the essential or important entity to report every significant incident under articles 26–29, while provision B requires the communications provider to notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately of a qualifying personal-data security breach. The strongest tension case is that these may be separate reports under different regimes, with A's recipient and timing left unspecified in the text shown and B expressly requiring immediate notification to the data-protection authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: the entity can report the significant incident under articles 26–29 and also notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately under article 11.3a. Nothing in either excerpt says that the B notification substitutes for the A report, and A does not identify a different recipient or deadline in the text shown.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An entity that is both an essential or important entity and a provider of a public electronic communications service suffers one security incident that is significant under article 25 and also has adverse consequences for the protection of personal data processed in connection with the communications service. It must report under article 25 and notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately under article 11.3a, but the excerpt does not show where or when the article 25 report must be made, so it cannot establish whether the duties are genuinely separate filings or whether one report could satisfy both regimes.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0052872 articles 26–29, especially their provisions identifying the recipient(s), deadline(s), and content or form of the significant-incident report; potentially also any coordination or single-notification rule between that regime and article 11.3a.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the report required by articles 26–29 is made to the same recipient and on a deadline/content basis that is satisfied by the immediate notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, or instead requires a separate report to another recipient. The shown text does not establish this.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens die zijn verwerkt in verband met de levering van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst in de Europese Unie.

verdict.shared_subject: Serious incidents occurring in the context of financial-entity ICT or high-risk AI testing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious ICT-related incident affecting clients' financial interests requires the financial entity to notify its clients immediately. B requires every serious incident identified during real-world testing to be reported to the national market-surveillance authority and also requires immediate risk mitigation or suspension/termination measures; the same incident could therefore trigger distinct notification/reporting duties and additional operational measures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different recipients and are independently satisfiable: A requires notice to affected clients, while B requires a report to the national market-surveillance authority. Nothing in either provision says that one notification substitutes for the other, and the duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also the provider or potential provider of a high-risk AI system discovers, during real-world testing, a serious ICT-related incident that has major adverse effects on systems supporting a critical function and affects clients' financial interests. It must notify the affected clients 'onverwijld' under A and separately report the serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority under B; notifying the clients does not report the incident to that authority, and B also requires immediate risk-mitigation measures or suspension of testing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related governance and reporting duties for ICT/AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by a serious incident and impose incident-related action. However, Provision A requires periodic and incident-based documentation/evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, while Provision B requires a specific incident notification within ten days after awareness in a death case; the texts do not say that either action substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different objects and are independently satisfiable: A concerns documenting and evaluating a risk-management framework and submitting an evaluation report on request, whereas B concerns notifying an incident after a causal link is established or suspected. A does not prescribe a filing deadline or recipient for the incident, and B does not dispense with A's framework documentation duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 wordt bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-incident governance and reporting by a financial entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to report a significant incident promptly to its CSIRT or, where applicable, competent authority. Provision B requires the management body to establish internal reporting channels for information about ICT-service-provider arrangements and serious ICT-related incidents, so an incident may need to be communicated both externally under A and internally through B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties rather than conflicting reporting obligations: A concerns an external statutory incident notification, while B concerns an internal governance channel enabling the management body to obtain information. The texts do not require the same filing to be made twice, nor do they impose incompatible recipients or deadlines.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over:

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of serious ICT/AI incidents by an entity that is both a financial entity subject to DORA and a provider or deployer of a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious incident could trigger both regimes: DORA requires the financial entity to report to the relevant competent authority, while the AI Act requires a provider or deployer to report to the market-surveillance authority. Those are distinct reporting duties to potentially different authorities, and the AI Act's two-day deadline does not itself discharge DORA's separately required filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply only when their respective actor and incident conditions overlap, and each filing can be made cumulatively. Article 19 also contemplates additional reporting to other authorities or CSIRTs, so the texts do not make the two duties mutually exclusive or impossible to perform together.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that provides a high-risk AI system suffers an incident causing serious health damage and qualifying as a serious ICT-related incident. It must report the incident to the relevant competent authority under DORA and, immediately and no later than two days after awareness, report it to the AI Act market-surveillance authority; filing with one authority does not, on the text shown, satisfy the other duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: The exact DORA reporting deadlines and any rule determining whether a DORA filing can also constitute the AI Act notification are not shown. Nothing in the quoted provisions establishes such a substitution; the AI Act's referenced recipient is the market-surveillance authority, whereas DORA's recipient is the relevant competent authority under Article 46.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 van dit artikel wordt bij een wijdverbreide inbreuk of een ernstig incident, zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 3, punt 49), b), de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity/operator where the same event may also be a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report to both its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the Article 27 notification. Provision B imposes a separate notification duty on the provider or deployer of a high-risk AI system, with a ten-day maximum in the specified death case; the texts do not identify the same recipients or state that either filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions may apply to different actors, incidents, and regulatory regimes, and B does not expressly require a filing to a different named authority in the text shown. If the same actor and event are not within both scopes, there is no overlap; even where they are, the provisions could be cumulative rather than mutually incompatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A manufacturer of medical devices that is an essential or important entity operates or deploys a high-risk AI system. A single incident both compromises the availability, integrity, or confidentiality of data or services and causes a person's death, with the manufacturer suspecting a causal link to the AI system. The manufacturer must submit A's final report to “haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” within one month after the Article 27 notification, while B requires the death-related notification immediately upon establishing or suspecting the causal link and no later than ten days after awareness. The two duties are separate on the text shown, and filing the detailed report under A does not establish that the B notification has been made or that it goes to the same recipients.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive uncertainty is whether another provision of the AI Act identifies the recipient and content of the Article 73 notification and whether any rule coordinates or substitutes that notification with the NIS2-style report under Article 29. The shown texts do not establish such coordination.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 wordt bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory submissions by entities subject to both ICT-risk-management and conformity-assessment rules
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a report to the competent authority when requested, while Provision B requires a separate application to the notifying authority in the entity’s Member State of establishment. If the same body is subject to both regimes, the submissions go to different authorities and serve different purposes, so one filing would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties: A concerns documenting and evaluating an ICT-risk-management framework and reporting its evaluation upon request, whereas B concerns applying for notification as a conformity-assessment body. They do not regulate the same filing, deadline, or substantive content, and the fact that both may involve an authority does not itself create a conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant or serious ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A expressly requires an early warning to both the entity’s CSIRT and its competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B separately requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority, using the Article 20 reporting process; the two provisions therefore could require distinct submissions, particularly where the CSIRT and the relevant competent authority are different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can send the Article 26 early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority and also submit the Article 19 notification to the relevant competent authority. Moreover, Article 19 expressly contemplates communication to CSIRTs under national implementation, and the text shown does not establish that the incidents, recipients, or reporting triggers necessarily differ in a way that makes the duties irreconcilable.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity experiences one incident qualifying both as a significant incident under Article 26 and as a serious ICT-related incident under Article 19. It must give an early warning “aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” “binnen 24 uur”, while separately reporting the serious incident “aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46”; sending the Article 26 warning to the CSIRT and national competent authority does not, on the text shown, clearly discharge the Article 19 filing to the relevant Article 46 authority, and Article 19’s deadline and filing requirements are governed separately by Article 20.
verdict.missing_reference: The full Article 19(4) and Article 20 deadlines and procedures, and the applicable national designation under Article 19(1) and (5), are needed to determine whether the same submission can formally satisfy both regimes or whether the recipients and clocks are definitively distinct.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT incidents and ICT-risk-management obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to make an incident warning to both its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B requires periodic and incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework, with an evaluation report submitted to the competent authority on request; this could create additional reporting or documentation work after a serious ICT incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties rather than conflicting duties: A is an urgent warning about a significant incident to two specified recipients, while B concerns documenting and evaluating the risk-management framework and submitting an evaluation report only when requested. Nothing in B makes the A warning unnecessary, and B does not specify a second mandatory filing triggered by the same incident to a different recipient or on a different deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd. Het wordt voortdurend verbeterd op basis van de lessen die uit de uitvoering en de monitoring naar voren komen. Een evaluatieverslag van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt op verzoek bij de bevoegde autoriteit ingediend.

verdict.shared_subject: Incidents occurring during real-world testing of a high-risk AI system that may also constitute a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without undue delay when it becomes aware of a personal-data breach, while B requires every serious incident during real-world testing to be reported to the national market-surveillance authority. If the same event is both a personal-data breach and a serious testing incident, the duties point to different recipients and require separate communications; notifying the controller does not notify the market-surveillance authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with independently: the processor informs the controller under A, and the provider or potential provider reports the serious incident to the market-surveillance authority under B. They concern different legal triggers and actors, and neither text says that one report substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A processor conducting real-world testing of a high-risk AI system discovers that a security failure has caused unauthorised access to personal data and also constitutes a serious incident during the testing. The processor must inform the controller without undue delay under A, while the provider or potential provider must report the serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority under B; the two separate recipients mean both communications are required.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Institutional obligations involving authorities under EU digital-law instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a trust-service provider to report a qualifying significant incident within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application for notification to the notifying authority; if the same organisation falls within both categories, these are different obligations concerning different events and recipients, but the texts do not make them competing duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different actors, triggers, purposes and procedures: A concerns incident reporting by a trust-service provider, while B concerns an application for notification by a conformity-assessment body. Each can be performed independently, and neither provision forbids or substitutes for compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an event that is both a GDPR personal-data breach and a serious or widespread AI incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A single event may trigger both duties, with GDPR requiring notification to the competent data-protection supervisory authority within 72 hours and the AI Act requiring notification to market-surveillance authorities within two days. The recipients and legal regimes differ, so timely notification to one authority does not discharge the separate duty to notify the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The deadlines are broadly equivalent—72 hours versus two days—and both notifications can be prepared from the same incident. There is no express contradiction in the required content or timing; an actor can make both filings within the applicable periods.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk AI system causes an unauthorised disclosure of users’ personal data, constituting both a GDPR “inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens” and a serious incident under Article 73. The provider or deployer must notify the GDPR competent supervisory authority within 72 hours, while the Article 73 duty requires an immediate notification, no later than two days, to the market-surveillance authorities; filing with the first authority does not constitute filing with the second.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap. The decisive point is that Article 33 names a data-protection supervisory authority, whereas Article 73(1), which paragraph 2 refers to, names the market-surveillance authorities. The supplied text does not establish that either filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk-management evaluation/documentation and serious-incident notification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to a serious ICT/AI incident and impose time-sensitive action. However, Provision A requires a report only to the competent authority when requested and otherwise concerns evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework, while Provision B concerns a separate serious-incident notification with a ten-day deadline and no recipient stated in the excerpt; the texts do not establish that these are the same filing or that one discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different triggers and apparent scopes: A requires documenting and evaluating an ICT-risk-management framework and reporting that evaluation upon request, whereas B requires notification of a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system upon death. Nothing in the shown text requires the A evaluation report to be filed on the B deadline or treats the two reports as substitutes.
verdict.missing_reference: The provision identifying the recipient and legal nature of the serious-incident notification under Article 73, and any provision specifying whether that notification is separate from or can satisfy the Article 6 evaluation report requested by the competent authority, are needed to determine whether two cumulative filings are required.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the affected essential or important entity offering a trust service to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours at the latest. B requires the central contact point to submit a separate quarterly summary to Enisa, so the same incident may generate both an entity-level report and a later central-contact-point filing to a different recipient.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and at different reporting stages: A concerns the entity's immediate incident notification, while B concerns the central contact point's aggregated and anonymised quarterly report. The entity's compliance with A does not itself perform B, but the texts do not establish that the entity is responsible for B or that the two duties conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
