verdict.evidence_span_b: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system at a financial-sector entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a death-related serious incident involving a high-risk AI system to be reported immediately once the causal link is established or suspected, and no later than ten days after awareness. B separately requires specified financial-sector entities to make the relevant ICT-incident notification also to the designated sectoral CSIRT; if the same event triggers both regimes, the AI-law report and the CSIRT notification appear to be cumulative filings, with different or at least not fully specified recipients and no rule that one discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions could operate cumulatively without contradiction: the entity can make the AI-law serious-incident report within ten days and additionally notify the designated CSIRT. B does not state a conflicting deadline or prohibit the report required by A, and the text shown does not establish the recipient of A, so it is possible that the filings are coordinated or that another provision makes them one notification.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank operates a high-risk AI system. A person dies in an incident, and the bank immediately suspects a causal connection with the AI system. The bank must make the Article 73 report no later than ten days after becoming aware of the incident, while Article 5 separately requires the bank to make the relevant ICT-incident notification also to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors. Sending the AI-law report does not, on the text shown, establish that the separate CSIRT notification has been made.
verdict.missing_reference: The recipient and procedural details of the Article 73 report, and the referenced Article 19 ICT-incident notification rules, would be needed to determine the exact filing mechanics and whether any cross-recognition rule exists.
verdict.decisive_exception: No text shown establishes that the Article 73 report and the Article 19/CSIRT notification are the same filing or that notifying the Article 73 recipient discharges the separate duty to notify the designated sectoral CSIRT.
verdict.evidence_span_a: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident
verdict.evidence_span_b: tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant/serious incident involving a qualifying high-risk AI system that is also operated by an essential or important entity providing a trust service.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an immediate or 24-hour report to two recipients, the entity's CSIRT and competent authority. B separately requires reporting serious incidents to the nationally designated competent authority in the Member State where the incident occurred; if that authority is not the same as A's competent authority, the actor must make an additional filing, and B supplies no deadline that can be shown to be discharged by A's filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions may concern different incident categories and authorities, and B's designated national competent authority could in a particular case be the same authority as A's competent authority. If the reports are legally treated as one filing to the same recipient, A's 24-hour deadline would be compatible with B's undetermined deadline. The texts shown, however, do not establish that identity or consolidation.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A Dutch medical-device manufacturer provides a trust service and is an essential or important entity. Its high-risk AI system is a safety component of a device covered by Regulation (EU) 2017/745, and one incident both significantly affects the trust service and qualifies as a serious incident under Article 73. The entity must report within 24 hours to its CSIRT and its competent authority under A, while B requires a report to the nationally designated authority in the Member State where the incident occurred; where that designated authority is not the same as A's competent authority, filing with A's recipients does not discharge the separate B filing.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the two competent authorities are legally the same and whether the regimes permit a single filing to satisfy both duties is not established by the provisions shown. If they are the same recipient and one filing is recognised under both regimes, the relationship would instead be compatible; B's lack of an extracted deadline also prevents a deadline conflict from being established.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant incident that also constitutes a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the entity to report the significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority, while B requires the controller to report the personal-data breach to the Article 55 supervisory authority. If the competent authorities are different, one report does not discharge the other, creating two cumulative filings on essentially the same 72-hour clock.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions can be complied with: the actor can make the NIS2 report to its CSIRT and competent authority and separately make the GDPR report to the Article 55 supervisory authority. The deadlines are broadly aligned, and neither provision forbids or makes unnecessary the other report.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer that is both an essential or important entity and a GDPR controller discovers that a cyberattack has compromised personal data and qualifies as a significant incident. Within 72 hours it must report the incident to its CSIRT and the defined competent authority under A, and separately report the personal-data breach to the Article 55 supervisory authority under B; filing with the CSIRT or the ministerial competent authority does not, on the text shown, constitute filing with the data-protection supervisory authority.
verdict.decisive_exception: The texts do not establish that the competent authority under A is the same body as the Article 55 supervisory authority under B, nor that one filing is legally recognised as satisfying the other. B also contains a risk exception ('unless it is not likely that the breach entails a risk'), but the scenario assumes that exception does not apply.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Documentation and reporting of incidents involving personal-data breaches by an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report instead of a final report while an incident continues, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Provision B requires a controller to document every personal-data breach so that the supervisory authority can verify compliance; if the same incident is covered by both regimes, the texts do not expressly say whether A's reports satisfy B's separate documentation duty or whether B's documentation must contain A's specified reports and recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties rather than incompatible ones: A concerns a progress/final incident report, while B concerns documentation of personal-data breaches for supervisory verification. Nothing in either text forbids maintaining the documentation required by B while submitting the reports required by A, and B specifies no conflicting deadline or content requirement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk-management evaluation and serious-incident reporting by a regulated financial entity operating a high-risk AI safety component
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious ICT-related incident triggers A's duty to evaluate the ICT-risk-management framework and provide an evaluation report to the competent authority if requested, while B requires the serious incident itself to be reported to the designated national competent authority in the Member State where it occurred. If the same entity and incident fall within both regimes, these are different obligations concerning different subject matter, and the recipient and timing relationship is not fully specified.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not clearly require two reports about the same event to different recipients on different clocks. A concerns documentation and evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework, with a report supplied only if the competent authority requests it; B concerns notification of specified serious incidents and identifies the national competent authority. The texts therefore can be complied with cumulatively, without either duty preventing compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, alsook wanneer zich ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten voordoen
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant incident by an essential or important entity to the CSIRT and competent authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions address the same significant-incident reporting event and impose reporting duties on the entity. A superficial reading of provision B's wording—reporting to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority—could suggest a different recipient structure from provision A's express requirement to report to both recipients, potentially creating uncertainty about whether two separate filings are required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions identify the same CSIRT/competent-authority reporting channel and impose materially compatible timing and information requirements: A requires reporting without delay or within 72 hours, while B requires reporting without delay and, in its referenced procedure, specifies the same 72-hour incident report. B also expressly provides that, where the entity reports to the competent authority, that authority forwards the report to the CSIRT, so the texts support one coordinated reporting duty rather than two cumulative filings by the entity.
verdict.decisive_exception: None apparent from the texts shown. The apparent 'or' in provision B is qualified by the forwarding rule, and the extracted B deadline of 'onverwijld' is not a separate incompatible clock; the referenced 72-hour procedure supplies the incident-report deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an incident that is both a significant incident affecting a trust service and a personal-data breach.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident can trigger two cumulative reporting duties for the same entity: provision A requires a report to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, while provision B requires a report to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours. The recipients differ, so the faster report to A's recipients does not discharge the separate GDPR report to B's supervisory authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both duties can be performed without contradiction: the entity can report within 24 hours to the CSIRT and competent authority and also report within 72 hours to the Article 55 supervisory authority. The different deadlines therefore do not create an impossible obligation, although they create cumulative reporting burdens.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider that is an essential or important entity discovers at 10:00 that a significant incident affecting its trust service has also caused unauthorised access to customers' personal data. It must report the incident by 10:00 the next day to its CSIRT and competent authority, and separately report the personal-data breach to the Article 55 supervisory authority by 10:00 three days later; filing with the first two recipients does not constitute filing with the latter recipient.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision B contains an exception where it is not likely that the personal-data breach poses a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. On the stated facts, the breach is assumed to pose such a risk, so that exception does not remove the second reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Incidenten bij elektronische dienstverlening en AI-systemen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Als hetzelfde incident zowel een beveiligings- of integriteitsinbreuk op de eigen elektronische dienst is als een ernstig AI-incident, verplicht A tot onverwijlde kennisgeving aan Onze Minister. B betreft echter de melding van een ernstig incident door een aanbieder of gebruiksverantwoordelijke; volgens de meegeleverde context gaat die melding aan de markttoezichtautoriteiten, zodat één melding niet noodzakelijk de andere ontvanger bereikt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: de betrokken actor kan onverwijld aan Onze Minister melden en daarnaast de AI-melding binnen de toepasselijke termijn doen. Er is geen tekstuele aanwijzing dat de ene melding de andere vervangt of dat de termijnen onderling onverenigbaar zijn.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een aangewezen organisatie gebruikt onder eigen verantwoordelijkheid een hoog-risico-AI-systeem in haar elektronische dienstverlening. Een cyberinbraak veroorzaakt zowel een beveiligingsinbreuk op die dienst als een ernstig incident dat aan het AI-systeem kan worden toegeschreven. De organisatie moet de inbreuk ‘onverwijld’ aan Onze Minister melden op grond van A en het ernstige incident bovendien melden aan de markttoezichtautoriteit ‘onmiddellijk’ na vaststelling van het oorzakelijk verband en uiterlijk 15 dagen na bewustwording op grond van B; de eerste melding aan Onze Minister vervangt de tweede melding aan de markttoezichtautoriteit niet.
verdict.decisive_exception: Geen uitzondering is nodig om de twee meldplichten naast elkaar toe te passen. De relevante context bij art. 73 lid 1 identificeert voor B de markttoezichtautoriteiten als ontvangers; A noemt Onze Minister als afzonderlijke ontvanger.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious AI incidents and ICT incidents by financial-sector entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system to be reported under the AI Act, while B requires certain financial-sector entities to make the referenced ICT-incident report also to the designated sectoral CSIRT. If the same event is both a serious AI incident and an ICT incident, the provisions point to separate reporting regimes and potentially separate recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts do not expressly establish that the same event triggers both duties, nor do they identify the recipient or complete procedure for A within the provision shown. B may simply add the CSIRT as an additional recipient for the ICT-incident report, while A concerns a different AI-Act report to market-surveillance authorities. The duties can therefore be cumulatively satisfied, but the shown text does not fully establish the overlap or the exact second filing.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing part of 32024R1689 art. 73, especially the provision identifying the recipient and procedure for the report under paragraph 1, together with the referenced article 19 ICT-incident reporting rule establishing its trigger, recipient(s), and deadline. Those provisions are needed to establish that one concrete event triggers both duties and requires two separate filings rather than one report with an additional recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving an electronic public service and a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same serious security or integrity incident could trigger both duties for the same organisation: A requires immediate notice to the Minister, while B requires a notice to the market-surveillance authorities in the Member States where the incident occurred. The recipients are different, so notifying one authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the other obligation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the organisation can promptly send the required information to the Minister and separately report the serious incident to the relevant market-surveillance authorities. They concern different reporting regimes and the texts do not impose incompatible content or deadlines.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation provides an electronic public service using a high-risk AI system. A serious security incident involving that system occurs in a Member State and also constitutes a breach of the security or integrity of the organisation’s electronic service. The organisation must notify Onze Minister immediately under A and report the serious incident to that Member State’s market-surveillance authority under B; filing with the Minister does not, on the text shown, satisfy the separate market-surveillance notification duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents that may also constitute personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: An incident affecting an essential or important entity may also be a personal-data breach for which the controller must notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours. The two provisions impose different reporting duties with different timing and, in the contextual material, different recipients: the NIS2-style final/progress report goes to the CSIRT and competent authority, while GDPR notification goes to the Article 55 supervisory authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can submit the GDPR notification within 72 hours and separately submit the progress or final report required by Article 29. Article 29 applies only to an incident still ongoing when the final report is due, whereas Article 33 applies only where the incident is a personal-data breach presenting a likely risk, so neither duty purports to replace the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A personal-data security incident affecting an essential entity is still ongoing one month after it was reported under the NIS2 regime and also presents a likely risk to individuals. The entity must notify the Article 55 competent data-protection supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, while, because the incident remains ongoing when the final report is due, it must submit a progress report to its CSIRT and competent authority instead of the final report; the GDPR notification does not discharge the separate CSIRT/competent-authority reporting duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: The GDPR duty does not apply if it is not likely that the breach poses a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons; the scenario assumes that this exception does not apply. The provisions shown also do not establish that notification to the Article 55 supervisory authority substitutes for the CSIRT and competent-authority report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid. Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit, tenzij het niet waarschijnlijk is dat de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity/provider where a cybersecurity incident also constitutes a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A covered entity must submit a progress report instead of a final report while an incident continues, and later submit the final report within one month after resolution. Separately, a provider must promptly notify each affected data subject where a personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect privacy; these are different communications with different recipients and content, so one does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with: the entity can provide the statutory incident report to the recipients specified in Article 29 and separately notify affected individuals without delay. Nothing in either text prohibits or substitutes for the other notification.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity suffers a continuing cyberattack that exposes customers’ personal data and is likely to adversely affect their privacy. While the attack continues, it must submit a progress report under Article 29, and it must also promptly notify each affected data subject under Article 11.3a; after the incident is resolved, it must submit the final report within one month. Notification to affected individuals does not replace the progress/final report, and the Article 29 report does not constitute individual notification.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 11.3a(5) may remove the individual-notification duty where appropriate technical protective measures made the data encrypted or otherwise unintelligible to unauthorised persons, but that exception is not established on the stated facts. Article 11.3a(4) may also permit the supervisory authority to require notification if the provider did not notify; neither provision makes the two reporting duties substitutes for one another.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A central contact point must submit a quarterly summary to ENISA, while a financial entity must report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority. For an incident covered by both regimes, these are different reporting duties directed to different recipients, and the DORA report does not itself appear to discharge the separate ENISA summary duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the relevant authority or central contact point can use information received under DORA when preparing the quarterly ENISA summary. Provision A is imposed on the central contact point, whereas provision B is imposed on the financial entity, so the texts do not establish that the financial entity itself must make both filings.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an entity whose significant incidents are reported under NIS2 suffers one serious ICT-related incident with significant effects on its services. It must report the incident to the relevant competent authority under DORA, while the NIS2 central contact point must separately submit its quarterly aggregated and anonymised report concerning incidents reported under NIS2 to ENISA; reporting to the competent authority does not itself constitute the central contact point’s ENISA filing.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive issue is whether the DORA reporting route, including onward transmission by the competent authority or central contact point, is legally deemed to replace or discharge the separate quarterly ENISA summary obligation. The texts shown do not establish such a substitution; they instead identify different duties and recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten die overeenkomstig lid 1 van dit artikel en overeenkomstig artikel 30 zijn gemeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity or operator subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an essential or important entity offering a trust service to report a significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. B imposes a separate deadline for reporting a serious incident involving death, but the excerpt does not identify a recipient; if the same event also qualifies under B, the actor may face two reporting regimes with different triggers and potentially different filing requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not clearly establish that the same actor, incident, and reporting obligation fall under both rules. A concerns a significant incident affecting provision of a trust service, while B concerns death linked to a high-risk AI system and does not state a recipient in the text shown. If both apply, the 24-hour deadline in A is earlier than B's ten-day deadline, but that alone does not prove that A's filing discharges B's separate duty.
verdict.missing_reference: The provision(s) implementing or specifying the reporting obligation and recipient under Article 73 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, including whether the Article 73 report must be made to a recipient different from the CSIRT and competent authority under Article 27 of BWBR0052872, and whether the same incident and actor can fall within both scopes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In afwijking van het eerste lid dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit als dat incident gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van haar vertrouwensdienst.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 wordt bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Documentation and reporting of security incidents that may also constitute personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within a specified period. Provision B requires the controller to document every personal-data breach, but it does not itself require a filing to a recipient or set a deadline, so the texts do not establish two cumulative reports with different recipients or clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily be performed together: an entity can make the Article 27 report while separately maintaining the Article 33 documentation. Article 33's documentation duty is not a second reporting obligation on the text shown, and nothing in either provision says that one duty substitutes for or conflicts with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security or integrity incidents by public-sector or designated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying entity must submit an end report to its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the initial notification, while B requires a bestuursorgaan or designated organisation to notify the Minister immediately and provide all necessary information. If the same actor and event fall within both provisions, the recipients differ and the texts do not say that B's immediate notification replaces A's later report, so both obligations may apply.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: the actor can notify the Minister immediately under B and later submit the more detailed report to its CSIRT and competent authority under A. Nothing in either text prohibits multiple notifications or makes the deadlines mutually exclusive.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated public organisation in the medical-device manufacturing sector suffers a security incident affecting the integrity of its electronic public service. It must notify Onze Minister onverwijld under B, while also submitting the detailed final report to its CSIRT and competent authority uiterlijk één maand after the Article 27 notification under A; notifying the Minister does not, on the texts shown, discharge the separate report to the CSIRT and competent authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both the Dutch Telecommunications Act and NIS2
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the provider to notify the Dutch data-protection authority of a qualifying security breach without delay. Provision B separately requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident affecting its trust services to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours; the texts identify different recipients and do not say that a NIS2 report discharges the data-protection notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the same incident can be reported promptly to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens and separately to the CSIRT or competent authority. There is no incompatible content or deadline; the apparent burden is an additional reporting obligation, not an inability to comply with both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider offering a public electronic communications service suffers one security breach that both adversely affects the protection of personal data processed for that communications service and significantly affects provision of its trust services. It must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens 'onverwijld' under A and separately report the significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours under B; filing with either recipient does not, on the text shown, discharge the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious cybersecurity/AI incident by an entity that is both subject to the NIS2-style reporting duty and an AI Act high-risk-system provider.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same serious event could qualify both as an incident requiring an end report to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority and as a serious incident requiring notification to the Member States’ market-surveillance authorities. Those are different recipients, and Article 29 requires a later, substantive final report while Article 73 requires a separate notification, so one filing does not textually discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can notify the market-surveillance authorities under Article 73 and separately submit the Article 29 final report to its CSIRT and competent authority within one month. Neither provision forbids the other filing or states that the reports must be identical or mutually exclusive.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A manufacturer of a high-risk medical AI system is an essential or important entity. A serious malfunction compromises the availability or integrity of data and services, making it an Article 29 incident, and the same event is also a serious incident under Article 73. The manufacturer must notify the market-surveillance authorities in the Member States where the incident occurred and, separately, submit an end report describing the incident, cause and mitigation measures to its CSIRT and competent authority no later than one month after the Article 27 notification; reporting to either recipient does not discharge the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Handling and reporting ICT-related incidents by financial entities that are also trust-service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes a concrete 24-hour reporting duty on a trust-service provider to the CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B makes a financial entity remain fully responsible for handling and consequences of incidents reported under Article 19(1), which could be read as adding a separate responsibility alongside the NIS2 reporting regime.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not impose a second reporting obligation, recipient, deadline, or incompatible handling rule; it merely preserves the financial entity’s responsibility after supervisory feedback. The two provisions can therefore be complied with cumulatively: the entity reports under A and remains responsible under B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security incident that may constitute both a personal-data breach and a serious ICT-related incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident can trigger both duties for a financial entity acting as processor: it must inform the controller without unreasonable delay under A and inform affected clients immediately under B. These are separate communications to different recipients, so notifying one does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can promptly notify the controller and clients, and the deadlines are not inherently incompatible. They concern different recipients and purposes rather than contradictory reporting requirements.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity processes clients’ personal data and suffers a major unauthorised disclosure affecting the systems supporting a critical function and the financial interests of clients. The entity must, without unreasonable delay, inform the controller under A and, as soon as it notices the incident, inform its clients without delay under B; making the client notification does not notify the controller, and making the controller notification does not notify the clients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident handling and responsibility by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to submit a final incident report to both its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the initial notification. Provision B states that financial entities remain fully responsible for handling and consequences of reported ICT incidents, which could be argued to preserve a separate responsibility alongside A’s reporting duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B imposes no separate reporting, documentation, recipient, or deadline requirement in the norm being compared; it merely preserves the financial entity’s substantive responsibility despite supervisory feedback. Provision A’s reporting obligation and B’s responsibility rule can therefore both be complied with without contradiction or cumulative dual filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onverminderd de ontvangen feedback van toezichthouders blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Incidenten en beveiligingsinbreuken bij elektronische dienstverlening
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen zien op rapportage over incidenten, maar leggen de verplichting aan verschillende actoren en voor verschillende rapportagedoeleinden op. Als een bestuursorgaan of aangewezen organisatie tevens een centrale contactpuntfunctie vervult, kan eenzelfde incident aanleiding geven tot onmiddellijke melding aan Onze Minister én tot een afzonderlijk, periodiek geaggregeerd verslag aan Enisa.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn rechtstreeks cumulatief verenigbaar: artikel 18 vereist een onmiddellijke, inhoudelijke melding door het bestuursorgaan of de aangewezen organisatie aan Onze Minister, terwijl artikel 23 het centrale contactpunt verplicht om elk kwartaal een samenvattend, geanonimiseerd en geaggregeerd verslag aan Enisa te sturen. De ene melding is niet bedoeld als vervanging van het andere verslag; bovendien richten de verplichtingen zich primair tot verschillende actoren.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een aangewezen organisatie die tevens het centrale contactpunt is, ontdekt een beveiligingsinbreuk in haar eigen elektronische dienstverlening. Zij moet die inbreuk onverwijld met alle benodigde informatie aan Onze Minister melden op grond van artikel 18, maar moet daarnaast in haar rol als centraal contactpunt de relevante gemelde incidentgegevens opnemen in het afzonderlijke samenvattende verslag dat om de drie maanden aan Enisa wordt ingediend. De ontvangers verschillen (Onze Minister en Enisa), en de onmiddellijke melding aan Onze Minister vervangt het periodieke verslag aan Enisa niet.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten die overeenkomstig lid 1 van dit artikel en overeenkomstig artikel 30 zijn gemeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related reporting and ICT-risk-management evaluation by entities potentially subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by a serious ICT incident and involve sending information or a report to a competent authority. The strongest tension case is that the incident may require an immediate/72-hour notification under A while also triggering B's evaluation and requested-report duty, potentially creating overlapping documentation and reporting burdens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are materially different and cumulative rather than conflicting: A requires an incident notification to both the CSIRT and competent authority, with specified incident information, whereas B requires documentation and evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework and submission of an evaluation report only if the competent authority requests it. Nothing in B says that its evaluation report replaces A's incident notification, and nothing in A prevents or excuses the framework evaluation required by B.
verdict.decisive_exception: B's report is conditional on a request by the competent authority, and the provisions shown do not establish that such a request must be made for every incident. Even if requested, it would be a separate framework-evaluation report, not an alternative incident notification; the duties can therefore both be performed.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit met:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations for an entity that is both subject to the Dutch cybersecurity incident-reporting regime and an AI Act fundamental-rights-impact-assessment notification duty
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying entity could face two separate notifications arising in a related operational context: an incident final report to its CSIRT and competent authority within one month, and a fundamental-rights-impact-assessment notification to the market-surveillance authority. The recipients differ, and nothing in either provision says that one filing substitutes for the other, so a single event or deployment could require both filings on potentially different or partly unspecified timelines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggers and contents: A concerns an incident and a detailed incident report, while B concerns completion of a fundamental-rights-impact assessment before use of certain high-risk AI systems. They can therefore be complied with cumulatively, and the texts do not establish that the same event triggers both duties or that their deadlines conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer qualifying as an essential or important entity uses a covered high-risk AI system in providing a public service. After an incident affecting the availability or integrity of data or services, it must submit the incident final report to its CSIRT and competent authority no later than one month after the Article 27(1) notification, while, having completed the fundamental-rights-impact assessment for the AI system, it must separately notify the market-surveillance authority and submit the Article 27(5) template. Filing the incident report with the CSIRT and competent authority does not, on the text shown, notify the different market-surveillance authority or discharge the AI Act notification.
verdict.decisive_exception: No provision shown states that the AI Act notification to the market-surveillance authority substitutes for the NIS2-style report to the CSIRT and competent authority, or vice versa. Article 27(4)'s possible exemption from the AI Act notification is referenced but not supplied; if applicable, it could remove the second filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations arising from potentially harmful AI-related personal-data incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same operator could face both duties after a personal-data breach occurring in the use of a qualifying high-risk AI system: A requires immediate notice to the affected person, while B requires notification of the fundamental-rights-impact assessment results to the market-surveillance authority. These are separate notifications to different recipients, and neither text says that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with because they concern different triggering matters and recipients: A concerns a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy, whereas B concerns completion of a fundamental-rights-impact assessment. The texts do not establish that every breach is connected to a required assessment under B, so the duties may simply apply cumulatively only when their independent conditions are met.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A public-service provider uses a qualifying high-risk AI system and has completed the required fundamental-rights-impact assessment. A security incident then breaches personal data and is likely to adversely affect an identified person's privacy. The provider must notify that person immediately under A and separately notify the market-surveillance authority of the assessment results under B; notifying one recipient does not notify the other, and B provides no deadline that resolves the coordination issue.
verdict.decisive_exception: The possible exemption under Article 46(1) may release the user from B's notification duty, but its applicability is not established in the text shown. That exception does not alter A's separate duty to notify the affected person.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations for certain AI-system users and financial-sector ICT incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties that could, in a sufficiently overlapping situation, concern the same underlying event or use of a system. However, they require notification to different recipients: the AI Act market-surveillance authority and the sectoral CSIRT, so notification to one would not obviously discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers and subject matters. Provision A concerns the results of a fundamental-rights impact assessment for specified high-risk AI systems, while Provision B concerns ICT-incident reporting by specified financial-sector entities, including a voluntary report under Article 19(2). Nothing in the texts states that an AI fundamental-rights assessment result is an ICT incident or that the two notifications are alternative filings.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an incident that may simultaneously be a GDPR personal-data breach and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying event could trigger both duties: the GDPR controller must notify the competent data-protection supervisory authority, while the AI Act provider or deployer must notify the market-surveillance authorities. The filings have different recipients and different clocks, so notifying one authority cannot, on the texts shown, discharge the other duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can make both notifications, and the 72-hour GDPR deadline is earlier than the ordinary 15-day AI Act deadline. If the event does not meet both instruments' independent triggers, only one notification is required; moreover, the shown AI Act paragraph does not itself state the recipient, which is supplied only by the related paragraph 1.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk AI system is also the GDPR controller for personal data processed by that system. A security incident causes unauthorised access to stored personal data and is also a serious incident causally linked to the high-risk AI system. The provider must notify the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours and separately notify the market-surveillance authority under the AI Act; filing the first notification does not, on the texts shown, notify the second recipient or satisfy the second regime's duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: The conclusion assumes the incident satisfies both instruments' independent thresholds. Under GDPR Article 33, there is no notification duty if it is unlikely that the breach poses a risk to natural persons' rights and freedoms. Under the AI Act, the relevant serious-incident scope and any special deadlines are in the related provisions, including Article 73(1), (3), and (4); those provisions do not establish that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incidents by an entity/provider subject to both NIS2 and the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A single incident involving a high-risk AI system could also be a significant incident affecting the provider’s network or information-system services. The NIS2 duty is directed to the CSIRT or competent authority, while the AI Act duty is directed to the market-surveillance authorities, so reporting to one recipient does not textually discharge the other duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can make both notifications, and neither provision forbids or makes compliance with the other impossible. They may also apply to different incidents because the NIS2 trigger is a significant incident affecting service provision, whereas Article 73 concerns serious incidents involving a high-risk AI system.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company provides a high-risk AI system and is also an essential or important NIS2 entity. A cyberattack compromises the AI system and causes a serious operational disruption to the company’s services, making the event both a NIS2 “significant incident” and an AI Act “serious incident.” The company must report it “bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit” under Article 23 and separately report it “bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden” under Article 73; the two filings have different recipients, and the text does not say that either filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or ICT incident by a financial entity that is also a GDPR controller
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident may simultaneously be a GDPR personal-data breach and a serious ICT-related incident. The same financial entity would then have to notify the Article 55 supervisory authority under Article 33 and separately report to the Article 46 relevant competent authority under DORA Article 19; the texts do not say that one filing discharges the other, and DORA requires incident-specific information and reports under its own models and timetable.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the entity can make both notifications, using the GDPR deadline of at most 72 hours where applicable and the DORA deadlines under Article 20. The provisions address different regimes and recipients, so neither requires withholding information from or refusing to notify the other authority.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank, acting as GDPR controller, suffers a ransomware attack that causes unauthorised access to customer personal data and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. It must notify the Article 55 supervisory authority without unreasonable delay and, if possible, within 72 hours of awareness, while also submitting DORA's first notification and subsequent reports to the relevant Article 46 competent authority using the Article 20 models and deadlines. Filing with one authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate duty to file with the other.
verdict.missing_reference: The exact DORA deadlines and procedural details in Article 20, and any provisions coordinating or exempting overlapping GDPR and DORA notifications, are not shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity/provider or deployer subject to both NIS2 and the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident under NIS2 must be reported without delay to the CSIRT or competent authority, while a serious AI incident under the AI Act must be reported immediately and no later than two days after awareness. If the same event satisfies both definitions, the provisions could appear to impose overlapping reporting duties with different statutory regimes and potentially different authorities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The shown AI Act provision does not create a separate recipient or filing: it states that the notification referred to in Article 73(1) must be made within the specified period, and Article 73(1) identifies the market-surveillance authorities. The NIS2 duty is separately addressed to the CSIRT or competent authority, so both reports can be made cumulatively; the two-day AI Act deadline does not discharge the NIS2 report, which is required without delay and includes information enabling assessment of cross-border effects.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk AI system operated by an essential or important NIS2 entity causes serious, irreversible harm to a person's health and also causes a serious operational disruption to the entity's services. The entity becomes aware immediately. It must report the AI serious incident to the relevant market-surveillance authority under Article 73(1), within the Article 73(2) deadline as modified by paragraph 3, and must separately report the NIS2 significant incident without delay to its CSIRT or competent authority, including information enabling assessment of cross-border effects. Reporting to one recipient does not, on the text shown, constitute reporting to the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the cumulative-reporting problem. The decisive point is that the AI Act's referenced recipient is the market-surveillance authority, whereas NIS2 requires reporting to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. If in a particular Member State the same body is both the market-surveillance authority and the NIS2 competent authority, the practical duplication may be reduced, but the texts shown do not establish that identity or that one filing legally discharges both duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 van dit artikel wordt bij een wijdverbreide inbreuk of een ernstig incident, zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 3, punt 49), b), de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT incident/risk-management documentation and reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires incident-related submissions to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, including a warning within 24 hours and an incident notification within 72 hours. Provision B requires the ICT risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated periodically and, on request, the evaluation report to be submitted to the competent authority; an operator might therefore face both incident filings and a separate framework-evaluation submission.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different triggers and subject matter: A concerns reporting a significant incident, while B concerns periodic documentation and evaluation of an ICT risk-management framework, with submission only on request. Nothing in B requires a second filing about the same incident or makes the framework report an alternative to, or incompatible with, A's incident reports.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ein evaluatieverslag van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt op verzoek bij de bevoegde autoriteit ingediend.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT incident reporting and ICT risk-management documentation by a financial entity that is also a trust-service provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a trust-service provider to report a qualifying significant incident within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B requires the ICT risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated periodically and after serious ICT-related incidents, with an evaluation report submitted on request to the competent authority; this could create an additional incident-related submission concerning the same event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties, not two reports of the same incident: A is an incident notification to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B concerns documentation and evaluation of the ICT risk-management framework and only requires submission of an evaluation report when requested. The texts therefore allow both duties to be performed cumulatively, and B does not establish a separate mandatory incident filing or incompatible deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious/significant incident involving a high-risk AI system by an entity subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident may trigger two cumulative reporting duties: Provision A requires an early warning to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, while Provision B requires a report to the market-surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred. The recipients are different, and neither text says that one filing satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the actor can send the early warning required by A and separately notify the market-surveillance authorities under B. Provision B’s shown text does not state a deadline in paragraph 1, so A’s 24-hour deadline cannot be treated as conflicting with or necessarily discharging B’s duty.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk medical AI system operated by an essential or important entity suffers a significant incident that is also a serious incident and occurs in multiple Member States. Within 24 hours, the entity must give an early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority under A, while it must also report the serious incident to the market-surveillance authorities of each Member State where the incident occurred under B; filing the A warning with the CSIRT and competent authority does not, on the texts shown, constitute the B report to the market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap. The decisive point is that the provisions identify different recipients; the texts shown do not establish that the competent authority or CSIRT in A is the same body as the market-surveillance authorities in B, nor that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT/AI-related incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to notify their clients without delay when a serious ICT-related incident affects clients’ financial interests. Provision B sets a separate reporting deadline for a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, but the excerpt does not identify a recipient; if B entails a filing to a different authority, the same incident could trigger two cumulative duties with different clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The shown text of B specifies only when a notification must be made, not that it must be made to a recipient different from A’s clients. The duties can therefore be satisfied cumulatively, and B’s ten-day maximum does not prevent A’s separate immediate client notification; no actual incompatible deadline or duplicate recipient is established in the excerpts.
verdict.missing_reference: The omitted portion of 32024R1689 art. 73, especially paragraph 1 and the provision identifying the recipient and content of the notification required under B. It is necessary to determine whether B requires a separate filing to a different recipient or merely overlaps with A’s client notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related notification/reporting by an AI-system provider or other covered provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions can apply to the same event but require communications to different recipients: A requires immediate notice to the affected person, while B requires an incident report to the market-surveillance authority under its referenced paragraph 1. The duties therefore appear cumulative rather than substitutable, with different triggers and deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: There is no contradiction in notifying the affected person immediately and separately reporting the serious incident to the market-surveillance authority within the applicable period. The provisions address different recipients and purposes, so one filing does not purport to replace the other, but both can readily be made.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk AI system suffers a personal-data breach that is likely to adversely affect an identifiable person's privacy and is also a serious incident causally linked to the AI system. The provider must notify the affected person 'onverwijld' under A and separately make the B report to the market-surveillance authority 'onmiddellijk' after establishing the causal link and in any event within 15 days after becoming aware of the serious incident; notifying the person does not constitute the report to the authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a personal-data/security breach by a provider of a public electronic communications service
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the provider to notify the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens immediately, while B requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority under Article 55, if the breach is likely to pose a risk, within 72 hours where possible. If those authorities or reporting regimes were different, the same breach could require two filings on different clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions can apply to the same breach and point to the Dutch data-protection supervisory authority: the Article 55 competent authority is, on these facts, plausibly the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens. A's immediate notification is stricter than B's 72-hour outer limit, so one timely notification could satisfy both if the same authority, event and required information are involved. The texts shown do not establish that B requires a separate filing to a different recipient.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A public electronic communications provider, acting as controller, suffers a security breach affecting personal data and likely posing a risk to individuals. It notifies the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens immediately under A, but it remains unresolved from the provisions shown whether that notification is the Article 33 notification to the Article 55 competent authority or whether B requires a separate filing, particularly because B's conditional risk threshold and recipient formulation are not fully linked to A.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing reference is the provision(s) establishing which authority is the Article 55 competent supervisory authority for this processing and whether a notification under BWBR0009950 art. 11.3a is legally treated as, or must be supplemented by, the Article 33 notification under Regulation 2016/679. The relevant national implementing/coordinating rules and any applicable GDPR provisions on competence or sector-specific notification procedures are needed.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the Article 55 competent supervisory authority is the same recipient as the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, and whether the two regimes permit one notification to discharge both duties. If they are the same and the notification contents suffice, the stricter immediate deadline is compatible; if they are distinct or require separate filings, this would be a dual-reporting tension.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant or security/integrity incidents by an actor potentially covered by both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can require reporting of the same incident, but to different recipients: Provision A requires notice to Onze Minister, while Provision B requires a trust-service provider to report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours. The stricter 24-hour deadline does not discharge the separate duty to notify Onze Minister, so two filings may be required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can notify Onze Minister immediately and separately report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours. Their different scopes and triggers also mean that many incidents will fall under only one provision, but that does not eliminate the overlap scenario.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider that is also an aangewezen organisatie suffers a security or integrity breach affecting the provision of its trust services. The provider must notify Onze Minister 'onverwijld' under Provision A and separately report the significant incident to 'het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit' within 24 hours under Provision B; filing with one recipient does not, on the texts shown, discharge the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must promptly inform the controller of a personal-data breach, while a qualifying essential or important entity must promptly report a significant incident to its CSIRT or competent authority. A single cyber incident could satisfy both triggers, requiring separate communications to different recipients; reporting to the CSIRT or authority would not inform the controller, and informing the controller would not satisfy the public-authority reporting duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively because they impose duties on different recipients and concern different triggering conditions: any personal-data breach for A, but only a significant incident affecting service provision for B. There is no requirement that one filing substitute for the other, so the obligations do not make compliance with both impossible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A cloud-service company that is both a GDPR processor and an essential or important entity suffers a ransomware incident that exposes personal data and seriously disrupts its service.
