verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the entity to notify its service recipients without delay, while B requires certain financial-sector entities to make an incident notification also to the designated sectoral CSIRT. For an incident affecting service provision, these are separate notifications to different recipients, and B's filing does not notify the service recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can both be performed without contradiction: the entity can notify its service recipients immediately and separately report the incident to the CSIRT. Nothing in either provision says that one notification substitutes for the other or prevents the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank experiences a significant ICT incident that adversely affects the services it provides to customers. It must notify its service recipients 'onverwijld' under A and also make the relevant notification to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors under B; sending the CSIRT notification does not discharge the separate duty to notify customers, and B states no deadline for the CSIRT filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/security incidents affecting financial entities that are providers of public electronic communications services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires immediate notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens of a qualifying security breach. Provision B requires financial entities to establish and implement a process to detect, manage and report ICT-related incidents, so the same incident may fall within both regimes; however, the shown text does not identify a recipient, deadline, or separate filing under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, compatible duties: A specifies an immediate notification to the data-protection authority for a particular personal-data-impacting security breach, while B requires an internal incident-management process for financial entities, including reporting procedures. Nothing in B shown here requires reporting to a different recipient or sets a conflicting deadline, and B's reporting process can incorporate compliance with A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Security or integrity incidents affecting network, information, or electronic-service systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29, while B separately requires a public authority or designated organisation to notify the Minister immediately of a security or integrity breach involving its own electronic service, including all necessary information. If the same organisation and event fall within both provisions, the texts do not show that one notification discharges the other; A’s recipient and timing are not stated in the excerpt, whereas B identifies the Minister and requires immediate notice.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions may impose cumulative reporting duties rather than incompatible ones: an event can be reported under A and also immediately to the Minister under B. No contradiction appears, and A’s cross-referenced Articles 26–29 might specify a recipient, timing, or coordination rule that makes the duties compatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation operates its own electronic public service and suffers a security breach that is also a significant incident. It must notify the Minister “onverwijld” under B and provide all necessary information, while separately reporting the significant incident under A “overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29”; notification to the Minister is not shown to satisfy that separate reporting obligation, and A’s recipient and deadline are not given here.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0052872 Articles 26–29, which may identify A’s recipient, deadline, or any coordination/single-notification rule.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/security governance and incident-related information duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a public electronic communications service provider to notify the Dutch data-protection authority without delay of a qualifying security breach. Provision B requires the governing body of a financial entity to establish internal reporting channels for information about ICT matters, including serious ICT-related incidents and their consequences; if the same entity and event fall within both regimes, the duties concern related incident information and could create overlapping organisational burdens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose materially different duties on different actors and at different levels. A is an external, event-triggered notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, whereas B is an internal governance duty to establish channels enabling the governing body to obtain information; B does not require a second filing, recipient, or deadline, and satisfying B does not purport to replace A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents and related events under NIS2 and the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A central contact point must submit a quarterly summary to ENISA, while the AI Act requires an immediate serious-incident notification by the provider or deployer. A serious incident could also be a significant incident reported under NIS2, creating potentially overlapping reporting burdens with different actors, recipients, content and timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not impose the same filing duty on the same actor: provision A concerns the central contact point's aggregated quarterly report, whereas provision B concerns the provider or deployer’s incident notification. The quarterly ENISA summary is not discharged by the provider’s notification, but the texts shown do not establish that one actor must make both filings or that the same incident necessarily falls within both regimes.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions needed to determine whether the same entity is both the NIS2 central contact point responsible for the ENISA summary and the AI provider or deployer responsible for the serious-incident notification, and whether the relevant AI incident is also a NIS2 significant incident. In particular, the full scope and actor provisions of both instruments are needed.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and serious ICT-related incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the provider to notify the affected person without delay when a personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect that person’s privacy. B separately requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority; the same incident could trigger both duties, with different recipients and potentially different procedures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are addressed to different recipients and serve complementary purposes: individual privacy notification under A and regulatory incident reporting under B. Filing with the competent authority cannot replace notifying the affected person, but both obligations can be performed cumulatively, so there is no incompatibility or unresolved conflict between them.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of an incident that is both a significant incident under NIS2 and a widespread breach or serious AI incident under the AI Act.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying event can trigger two reporting regimes for the same actor: NIS2 requires an early warning within 24 hours and an incident notification within 72 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority, while the AI Act requires the Article 73(1) notification immediately and no later than two days. The strongest tension case is that these may be separate filings under different regimes, with different substantive content and potentially different institutional recipients, so the AI Act deadline does not itself discharge the NIS2 duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not expressly state that the reports must be separate, and both concern reporting the same incident to public authorities. The two-day AI Act deadline is not incompatible with NIS2's 24-hour early warning or 72-hour incident notification; an operator could submit the required NIS2 reports on time and separately satisfy the AI Act notification.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk AI system is also a NIS2 essential or important entity. A single cyber incident both significantly affects the provider's services and causes serious, irreversible harm to a person's health, making it a 'significant incident' under NIS2 and a 'serious incident' under the AI Act. The provider must give NIS2 'bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit' an early warning within 24 hours and an incident notification within 72 hours, while Article 73(1) requires reporting to 'de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden' and Article 73(3) requires that notification no later than two days after awareness. Filing with the NIS2 recipient does not, on the text shown, establish compliance with the separate AI Act duty to notify the market-surveillance authorities; both filings may therefore be required, on different clocks and with different required information.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive unresolved point is whether another provision of the AI Act or national implementation treats a NIS2 report to the CSIRT or competent authority as also satisfying the Article 73(1) notification to the market-surveillance authorities, or otherwise coordinates the two filings. No such equivalence or single-report rule is shown. The AI Act's Article 73(1) recipient and the NIS2 recipients are different on the supplied text, so the stricter deadline alone cannot discharge both duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: a) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven, waarin, indien van toepassing, wordt aangegeven of het significante incident vermoedelijk door een onrechtmatige of kwaadwillige handeling is veroorzaakt, dan wel grensoverschrijdende gevolgen zou kunnen hebben; b) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 van dit artikel wordt bij een wijdverbreide inbreuk of een ernstig incident, zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 3, punt 49), b), de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security incident that is both a personal-data breach and a significant incident under NIS2
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident can trigger two cumulative reporting duties for the same entity: GDPR reporting to the competent data-protection supervisory authority, and NIS2 reporting to the entity’s CSIRT or competent authority. These are distinct regimes and recipients; reporting to one does not, on the text shown, discharge the other, and NIS2 additionally requires a 24-hour early warning and later reports.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both duties can be performed without contradiction, and their deadlines do not require incompatible conduct: the entity can notify the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours while also notifying the NIS2 CSIRT or competent authority without delay. NIS2’s forwarding mechanism may reduce duplication within the NIS2 chain, but it does not state that a NIS2 report substitutes for the GDPR notification.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A cloud-service provider that is both a GDPR controller and an essential or important NIS2 entity suffers one cyberattack that exposes customers’ personal data and causes a significant service disruption. It must report the personal-data breach to the GDPR competent supervisory authority within 72 hours and separately report the significant incident without delay—including the early warning within 24 hours—to its CSIRT or competent authority; filing with either recipient does not, on the provisions shown, satisfy the other duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: The text does not establish any exception or equivalence under which a NIS2 report to the CSIRT or competent authority is also a GDPR notification to the Article 55 supervisory authority, or vice versa. The NIS2 forwarding rule only concerns forwarding within the NIS2 reporting structure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incidents by entities/providers subject to both NIS2 and the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same serious incident could also be a NIS2 significant incident, requiring the entity to report to the CSIRT or competent authority, while the AI Act separately requires a high-risk AI provider to report serious incidents to the market-surveillance authorities. These are different recipients, and neither provision says that one filing satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can both be performed: the actor can submit the NIS2 warning and incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority and separately notify the relevant market-surveillance authorities under the AI Act. The provisions therefore do not impose incompatible content or deadlines; the apparent issue is cumulative reporting, not impossibility of compliance.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider offers a high-risk AI system through a network and information system. A cyberattack compromises the system and causes a significant disruption of the provider’s services, making the event both a NIS2 significant incident and an AI Act serious incident. The provider must give the NIS2 early warning and incident report “bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit” and must separately report the serious incident “bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden”; filing with one recipient does not, on the text shown, discharge the other duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: No exception or equivalence rule is shown stating that a report to the CSIRT or competent authority is forwarded to, or substitutes for, notification to the market-surveillance authorities. The NIS2 provision does mention forwarding by a competent authority to the CSIRT, but not forwarding to the AI Act market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten zorgen ervoor dat de betrokken entiteiten, voor de in lid 1 bedoelde melding, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit: a) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires each essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29. Provision B requires the central contact point to submit a separate quarterly summary to ENISA, so an incident may generate both an entity-level report and a central-contact-point report, with different actors and recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and operate at different reporting levels: the entity reports the incident, while the central contact point aggregates and anonymises information for ENISA. The texts therefore do not require the same actor to make two filings, and compliance with one duty does not purport to replace the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity that is both a trust-service provider and a provider of a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same incident is both a significant incident affecting the provision of trust services and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, A requires a report within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B requires a report to the market-surveillance authorities by the AI provider. These are different statutory reporting duties with different recipients and triggers, so the 24-hour filing under A does not itself discharge B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both duties can be satisfied cumulatively: the actor can submit the A report within 24 hours and the B report within 15 days. The different deadlines do not create an impossibility, and the provisions do not expressly say that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company provides trust services and offers a high-risk AI system. A cyber incident affects its trust services and is also a serious incident causally linked, or reasonably likely to be linked, to the AI system. The company must report the significant incident within 24 hours to “het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit” under A and separately report the serious incident to the market-surveillance authority under B, no later than 15 days after awareness; filing with the first recipient does not discharge the second duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In afwijking van de eerste alinea, punt b), meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant or serious ICT-related incident by an entity that is both a trust-service provider covered by A and a financial entity covered by B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the entity to report a qualifying incident to both its CSIRT and its competent authority within 24 hours at the latest. B separately requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority under Article 46, and the texts do not establish that A's filing to its CSIRT and competent authority is the same filing as B's report or that one recipient's filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The two provisions may concern different incident classifications and regulatory regimes, and B's relevant competent authority could in some circumstances be the same authority as A's competent authority. If the incident is not both significant under A and serious under B, or if the filings are coordinated through the same authority, there is no conflict; the duties can also be performed cumulatively.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company is both a trust-service provider and a financial entity. A single ICT incident affects its trust service and qualifies as significant under A and serious under B. The company must, under A, report it “aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” “onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur”, while under B it must separately report the serious incident “aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46”. Filing the A report with the CSIRT and A's competent authority does not, on the text shown, establish that the B report to the Article 46 relevant competent authority has also been made; thus the company faces two potentially cumulative reporting duties and an unresolved recipient/procedure question.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions governing whether the Article 46 relevant competent authority is identical to A's competent authority, and the detailed Article 20 deadlines and procedures incorporated by B, would be needed to determine whether the reports can be combined and whether the authorities are the same in this concrete case.
verdict.decisive_exception: The result would be compatible if the applicable national or EU rules expressly treat the A filing as satisfying B's report, or if the relevant competent authority under B is the same recipient and the filing contains all information and meets B's deadline. That equivalence is not established by the text shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT incidents affecting entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an early warning to two public recipients—the entity's CSIRT and competent authority—within 24 hours at the latest. B separately requires a financial entity, when a serious ICT-related incident affects clients' financial interests, to notify its clients without delay and explain mitigation measures; the same incident can trigger both duties, requiring distinct communications to different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different recipients and purposes rather than contradictory conduct: A is an early regulatory/CSIRT warning, while B is client notification. An entity can make both notifications, so neither deadline or content makes compliance with the other impossible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer that is also a financial entity suffers one serious ICT-related incident that compromises a service and causes adverse financial consequences for clients. It must give the early warning to “haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” “binnen 24 uur” under A, and separately notify “hun cliënten” “onverwijld” under B, including the measures taken to limit the incident's negative effects; notifying either public recipient does not notify the clients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Governance and reporting concerning ICT risks or incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the financial entity’s management body to establish enterprise-level reporting channels for information about ICT-service-provider arrangements, planned material changes, their effects, and serious ICT-related incidents. Provision B requires a provider or deployer to make a time-limited notification when a person dies and a causal link or suspected link to a high-risk AI system is established. If the same financial entity is also the relevant AI provider or deployer, the incident could fall within both provisions, but A does not specify an external filing or deadline while B imposes a notification deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of duties: A is an internal governance and information-channel duty, with no extracted recipient or deadline, whereas B is an incident-notification duty triggered by death and a high-risk AI-system link, with a ten-day maximum. Nothing in A says that its internal channels replace, prohibit, or alter the notification required by B; both can therefore be performed cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over:
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT security, integrity and governance of an organisation or financial entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern ICT security and organisational responsibility. One might argue that the governance and communication-channel duty in Provision B could overlap with the immediate notification duty in Provision A, creating uncertainty about whether the governance arrangements must themselves include a separate reporting process.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify Onze Minister immediately of a security or integrity breach or misuse of access. Provision B instead requires the governing body of a financial entity to establish internal, company-level channels enabling it to obtain information about ICT-service arrangements, planned changes, effects, incidents and measures; it names no external recipient and imposes no incident-reporting deadline. The duties can therefore be performed cumulatively without either discharging or contradicting the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_subject: Electronic-service security/integrity incidents and transaction-reporting controls
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern detection or handling of failures in digital services, so an organisation might initially appear to face overlapping compliance duties. However, Provision B requires providers of data-reporting services to maintain systems for checking transaction reports; it does not require reporting an incident to a recipient, while Provision A requires notification of specified incidents to the Minister.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties on different or potentially overlapping actors: A requires prompt notification of a security or integrity breach or misuse involving the actor’s own electronic service, whereas B requires data-reporting-service providers to operate transaction-report checking and retransmission-request systems. Compliance with B does not purport to replace A’s notification duty, and B contains no separate reporting obligation or recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related reporting and documentation by an entity that is also a GDPR controller
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to give an early warning to both its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours (or without delay). Provision B requires the controller to document personal-data breaches so that the supervisory authority can check compliance, but it does not expressly state a separate notification, recipient deadline, or filing procedure; therefore the texts do not establish two cumulative reports with different recipients or clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily be performed together: the entity can make the early warning required by A and separately maintain the GDPR breach documentation required by B. Nothing in B forbids the early warning, and A's warning does not purport to replace the documentation required by B; the absence of a B deadline or recipient for a filing means there is no demonstrated dual-reporting conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen. Die documentatie stelt de toezichthoudende autoriteit in staat de naleving van dit artikel te controleren.

verdict.shared_subject: Security breaches involving electronic services that may also be public electronic communications services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same security breach could trigger both duties for an actor that is both a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie and an aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst. The provisions require notice to different recipients—Onze Minister and the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens—so notifying one does not, on the text shown, discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be satisfied cumulatively: the actor can promptly send the required information to Onze Minister and separately notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens. The provisions also have different triggers and scopes, so many breaches will trigger only one duty; that does not itself create a conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An aangewezen organisatie that provides a openbare elektronische communicatiedienst suffers a security breach affecting personal data processed in connection with that service. Because the breach concerns the security or integrity of its own electronic service, it must notify Onze Minister onverwijld under A; because it has adverse consequences for personal-data protection, it must also notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld under B. Filing one notice does not, on the text shown, satisfy the separate duty to notify the other recipient.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the cumulative reporting burden on the text shown; the decisive feature is that the recipients differ and both duties say 'onverwijld'.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/security incidents and ICT-risk-management obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires immediate notification to the Minister of a security or integrity breach, while provision B requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated periodically and after serious ICT-related incidents, with an evaluation report submitted on request to the competent authority. If a serious incident triggers both, the duties involve different actions and potentially different authorities, so the A notification would not itself satisfy B's documentation/evaluation duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct, cumulative obligations rather than incompatible ones: A concerns prompt incident notification to the Minister, whereas B concerns periodic or incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework. Nothing in either text forbids performing both, and B's shown text does not itself require a separate filing on every incident—only submission of an evaluation report when requested.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious or ongoing incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report while an incident continues and later a final report within one month after resolution. B separately requires a qualifying high-risk AI system to report serious incidents to the designated national competent authority; if the same incident triggers both regimes, the texts do not say that either filing satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can submit the progress or final report required by A and also make the notification required by B. A's quoted provision does not itself specify the recipient of the final report, while B identifies its recipient, so the shown text does not conclusively establish two distinct filings or incompatible deadlines.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing portions of BWBR0052872 art. 29, especially lid 1 and the provisions governing the incident notification in article 27, are needed to establish A's recipient(s), whether the report is a separate filing from B's notification, and whether the same incident triggers both duties. The relevant AI Act provisions defining the reporting deadline and any coordination or duplication rule may also be needed.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and serious AI-system incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without unreasonable delay when it becomes aware of a personal-data breach, while B requires the notification referred to in Article 73(1) immediately and no later than two days after the provider or deployer becomes aware of a serious incident. If the same event is both a personal-data breach and a serious AI incident, the duties may involve different legally responsible actors, triggers and reporting channels, and B's notification is to market-surveillance authorities under the referenced paragraph.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish two filings by the same actor to different recipients: A expressly requires the processor to inform the controller, whereas B's recipient is supplied only by the contextual paragraph and is not stated in the compared norm itself. Moreover, A's duty is satisfied by informing the controller without unreasonable delay, and nothing in the shown text says that B's notification substitutes for or conflicts with that communication.
verdict.missing_reference: The full operative text of Article 73(1), including its recipient and the actors legally responsible for making that notification, is needed to determine whether the same actor must make a separate filing under B. The shown norm B merely refers to the notification in paragraph 1.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij een wijdverbreide inbreuk of een ernstig incident, zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 3, punt 49), b), de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Authorities and reporting/application duties under separate digital-law regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to send an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B separately requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application to a notifying authority, so if the same organisation is both an in-scope entity experiencing such an incident and a conformity-assessment body seeking notification, the duties involve different acts and potentially different authorities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not regulate the same underlying act or trigger. A concerns urgent incident reporting by an essential or important entity, whereas B concerns a conformity-assessment body's application for notification; each can be performed independently, and neither text prohibits or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Responsibility and reporting/handling of ICT or personal-data incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern the same incident, and Provision A imposes a concrete notification duty to a supervisory authority within 72 hours. Provision B states that a financial entity remains fully responsible for handling and consequences of incidents reported under Article 19(1), which could be read as imposing an additional incident-related responsibility alongside the GDPR notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not impose a second reporting duty: the selected norm concerns continuing responsibility for handling and consequences, not notification to a different recipient or on a different deadline. Provision A's notification obligation and Provision B's responsibility rule can therefore both be satisfied, and there is no evidence of two cumulative filings.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities or AI providers/users
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same event: an incident affecting a network or information system may also be a serious AI incident. Article 25 requires the essential or important entity to report every significant incident, while Article 73 requires a high-risk AI provider or user to report a serious incident to market-surveillance authorities within two days; the texts therefore suggest potentially cumulative duties, with different actors and no stated rule that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not expressly establish two filings for the same actor, recipient, or event. Article 25 delegates the reporting details to Articles 26–29, and Article 73's referenced paragraph 1 identifies the market-surveillance authority, so the missing details of Article 25 could reveal a common recipient, deadline, or coordination rule under which both duties can be satisfied without conflict.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0052872 Articles 26–29, especially the provisions specifying the recipient, deadline, and content of the Article 25 report; those provisions are needed to determine whether the same actor must make a separate filing to a different recipient or on a different clock.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 van dit artikel wordt bij een wijdverbreide inbreuk of een ernstig incident, zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 3, punt 49), b), de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Operational obligations concerning incidents and transaction-reporting systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to issue an early warning about a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B separately requires providers of data-reporting services to maintain systems capable of checking transaction reports; if a transaction-reporting service provider is also subject to A, the same incident might affect both duties, but B does not impose a reporting duty or deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of obligations on different actors and triggers: A concerns incident notification by essential or important entities, while B concerns the design and operation of detection systems by data-reporting-service providers. Even if one actor is subject to both, it can notify the specified recipients under A while maintaining the systems required by B; neither duty discharges or contradicts the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.

verdict.shared_subject: Management and reporting of ICT-related incidents that may involve personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a controller to notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours when a personal-data breach presents a likely risk. Provision B requires financial entities to establish and implement a process to detect, manage and report ICT-related incidents, so the same incident could fall within both provisions and appear to require both external notification and incident-process reporting.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not specify a recipient, deadline, or separate filing obligation; it requires an organisational incident-management process. That process can incorporate compliance with Provision A, including the 72-hour notification, so the texts do not establish two cumulative reports to different recipients or on different clocks.
verdict.decisive_exception: The text of Provision B does not establish that its requirement to 'melden' entails a separate filing to a different recipient or by a different deadline. Without that information, the dual-reporting test is not met.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an incident involving a high-risk AI system that is also a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same event could qualify both as a GDPR personal-data breach and as a serious incident involving a covered high-risk AI system. Article 33 requires notification to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours, while Article 73 requires notification to a nationally designated competent authority; the provisions do not say that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be cumulatively satisfied: the controller can notify the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours and separately notify the designated national competent authority under the AI Act. Article 73 states no deadline, so there is no incompatible timing requirement, and the different recipients indicate that the duties are not the same filing.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company operates a high-risk AI system that is itself a medical device covered by Regulations (EU) 2017/745 and 2017/746. A security failure causes unauthorised access to patients’ stored health data and also constitutes a serious incident under Article 3(49)(c). The company must report the personal-data breach within 72 hours to “de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit” and report the serious incident to “de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan”; filing with the first authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate duty to notify the second.
verdict.decisive_exception: The text shown does not establish any exception or equivalence rule providing that an Article 73 notification to the designated national competent authority also constitutes the Article 33 notification to the Article 55 supervisory authority, or vice versa. Whether the authorities might be the same in a particular Member State is not established here.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: en wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant/serious ICT incident by an entity potentially subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident may trigger both duties for the same entity: provision A requires a report to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours at the latest, while provision B requires notifying clients without delay. These are separate communications to different recipients, so making the regulatory report under A does not notify the clients under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with: the entity can promptly notify its clients while also filing the required report with its CSIRT and competent authority. They concern different recipients and do not prescribe incompatible content or deadlines.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that offers a trust service suffers one significant ICT incident that affects provision of that trust service and has major adverse effects on systems supporting critical or important financial functions, with consequences for clients' financial interests. The entity must report the incident “onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur” to “haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” under A, and must separately inform “hun cliënten” “zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt” under B; filing with the CSIRT and competent authority does not discharge the client notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken

verdict.shared_subject: Early warning of a significant incident by an essential or important entity to the CSIRT and/or competent authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an early-warning duty for a significant incident, but A expressly requires the entity to warn both its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, whereas B frames the warning as being to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. If the applicable national arrangements treat these as separate recipients, A could require two transmissions while B contemplates one reporting channel.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern the same early warning, the same 24-hour deadline, and the same institutional reporting channels. B's wording and the related rule that a competent authority forwards a report to the CSIRT support treating the duties as one harmonised reporting process, with the stricter or more explicit A requirement satisfied through the applicable channel rather than as an additional filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: a) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/data-breach governance and communication duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a processor to inform the controller without unreasonable delay after learning of a personal-data breach. Provision B requires the financial entity’s governing body to establish internal reporting channels for information about ICT matters, including serious ICT-related incidents and their consequences; a breach could therefore generate both an external-to-the-controller notification and an internal governance communication.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties on different actors and do not require incompatible conduct. A processor can notify the controller under A while the financial entity maintains and uses the internal reporting channels required by B; B specifies no separate incident filing, recipient, or deadline that would conflict with A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant incidents affecting the provision of a trust service by an essential or important entity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions address the same triggering incident and require reporting to a CSIRT and competent authority. A possible tension is that Provision A expressly requires a report to both recipients within 24 hours, while Provision B says the entity reports to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, potentially suggesting an alternative recipient and leaving uncertainty about whether two separate filings are required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B expressly provides that, when the entity reports to the competent authority, that authority forwards the report to the CSIRT. For a trust-service provider, Provision B's own referenced exception also sets a 24-hour deadline, so the A duty can be satisfied through the reporting route contemplated by B without requiring incompatible content, timing, or duplicate filings.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision B's rule that, where the entity reports to the competent authority, that authority forwards the report to the CSIRT, together with the trust-service-provider-specific 24-hour rule in the referenced paragraph 4, means the provisions can operate as one coordinated reporting procedure rather than two independently required filings.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de betrokken entiteiten een significant incident overeenkomstig de eerste alinea melden bij de bevoegde autoriteit, zorgt de lidstaat ervoor dat die bevoegde autoriteit de melding na ontvangst doorstuurt naar het CSIRT.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-incidenten die tevens inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens zijn bij financiële entiteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Een financiële entiteit kan voor hetzelfde incident zowel als verwerker de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging moeten informeren als onder DORA een ICT-incidentbeheerproces moeten hebben dat incidenten meldt. Dat kan op het eerste gezicht op cumulatieve meldingslasten wijzen, maar artikel 17 noemt hier geen afzonderlijke ontvanger, termijn of concrete melding die naast de AVG-melding moet worden gedaan.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 33 legt een concrete meldplicht op aan de verwerker jegens de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, terwijl artikel 17 slechts verplicht een intern beheerproces voor detectie, beheer en melding van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten in te richten. De getoonde teksten verplichten dus niet aantoonbaar tot twee afzonderlijke meldingen; het proces kan de AVG-melding omvatten en beide verplichtingen kunnen naast elkaar worden nageleefd.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents during real-world testing of a high-risk AI system by a trust-service provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same serious incident could also be a significant incident affecting the provision of the provider’s trust services. Provision A then requires a report within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority, while provision B separately requires reporting to the national market-surveillance authority; the recipients differ, and A does not state that reporting to either of its recipients discharges B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed: the provider can make A’s report within 24 hours and also report the incident to the national market-surveillance authority under B. The duties concern different regulatory regimes and do not require incompatible content or conduct, although they impose cumulative reporting burdens.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider tests a high-risk AI system under real-world conditions. During the test, a serious incident is identified that also has significant effects on the provision of the provider’s trust services. The provider must report under A within 24 hours to “het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit” and must separately report under B to “de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit”; filing with the first recipient does not, on the text shown, constitute filing with the second recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In afwijking van de eerste alinea, punt b), meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: A serious/significant incident involving a high-risk AI system being tested under real-world conditions by an essential or important entity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident could trigger both duties: A requires an immediate or, if impossible, 72-hour report to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, while B separately requires every serious incident during real-world testing to be reported to the national market-surveillance authority. The recipients are different, and neither provision says that one report substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can send the A report to its CSIRT and competent authority and also report the incident to the national market-surveillance authority under B. B has no stated deadline, so there is no incompatible timing requirement; the apparent issue is an additional reporting burden rather than an inability to obey both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity in the medical-device manufacturing sector tests a high-risk AI system under real-world conditions. A serious incident compromises data integrity and is also a significant incident under A. The entity must report it immediately or within 72 hours to “haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” under A, and separately report the serious incident to “de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit” under B; filing with the first recipients does not, on the texts shown, discharge the separate report to the market-surveillance authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant or serious incidents by entities operating covered AI or network-and-information systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A covered entity may have to notify its service recipients immediately under Provision A while also reporting the same serious incident to a designated national competent authority under Provision B. The recipients differ, and B does not say that notifying service recipients satisfies the authority-reporting duty, so the obligations appear cumulative rather than substitutable.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed by making two notifications: one to the entity’s service recipients and one to the designated national competent authority. Provision B applies only to a narrower category of high-risk AI systems that are devices or safety components, but that narrower scope does not remove the separate recipient-notification duty where Provision A also applies.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An important entity operates a high-risk AI system that is a safety component of a medical device covered by Regulation (EU) 2017/745. A serious incident occurs that is also a significant incident adversely affecting service provision. The entity must notify its service recipients without delay under Provision A and report the incident to the designated national competent authority in the Member State where it occurred under Provision B; notifying the recipients does not discharge the separate authority-reporting obligation, and Provision B supplies no deadline that resolves how the two duties are coordinated.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: en wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Documentation and reporting duties concerning regulated ICT/AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same operator and involve documenting or communicating regulatory information. However, provision A requires an evaluation report of the ICT-risk-management framework to be submitted on request to the competent authority, while provision B requires notification of a fundamental-rights-impact assessment to the market-surveillance authority; these are different documents, triggers, and recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are independently satisfiable and do not prescribe incompatible conduct. An operator can periodically document and evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework, submit that evaluation report when requested by the competent authority, and separately notify the market-surveillance authority of the AI impact-assessment results when Article 27 is triggered.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een evaluatieverslag van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt op verzoek bij de bevoegde autoriteit ingediend.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident involving an essential or important entity that also constitutes a personal-data breach with likely adverse privacy consequences
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same event can trigger two distinct notification duties for the same provider: an early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, and notice to the affected person without delay. These are separate communications to different recipients, so satisfying the institutional warning does not notify the individual, and satisfying the individual notice does not notify either authority or CSIRT.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties address different recipients and purposes and can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the entity can promptly notify the CSIRT and competent authority and separately notify the affected person. Nothing in either provision forbids or makes compliance with the other impossible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer classified as an essential or important entity discovers a cyberattack that compromises stored patient data and is likely to adversely affect the patients' privacy. It must give the early warning to “haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” “onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur,” and separately notify each affected person “onverwijld.” The two filings have different recipients and both must be made; one does not discharge the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk governance and incident reporting by entities potentially subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an incident notification to both the CSIRT and the competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B requires a report to the competent authority when requested concerning the evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework; if that request were triggered by the same serious incident, the entity might face an additional report with a different subject matter and no stated deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties, not duplicate filings for the same event: A concerns immediate notification of a significant incident affecting a trust service, while B concerns documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework and a report only if the competent authority requests it. The A notification does not purport to be the B evaluation report, but the texts also do not establish that a B request must arise from the same incident or that the reports cannot be combined; therefore there is no demonstrated dual-reporting conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant ICT incidents by a trust-service provider that is also a bank, trading venue, central securities depository, or central counterparty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a trust-service provider to report a qualifying significant incident within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B separately requires certain financial-sector entities to make the Article 19 report, including a voluntary report, also to the sectoral CSIRT designated under the Cybersecurity Act; if the same entity and incident fall under both regimes, the texts do not expressly say that A's report discharges B's additional reporting destination.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions may concern different entities, triggers, and reporting regimes: A concerns significant incidents affecting the provision of trust services, while B concerns reports under Article 19 by specified financial entities. Moreover, A's CSIRT recipient could potentially be the same sectoral CSIRT designated under B, and B states no separate deadline, so the texts do not clearly establish two distinct filings rather than one report sent to the appropriate CSIRT.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company is both a trust-service provider and a bank, and a significant cyber incident affects its trust services while also constituting an Article 19 ICT incident. It must report the incident under A within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority, and under B also to the designated sectoral CSIRT for banking and financial-market infrastructure; sending the A report to the competent authority does not, on the text shown, establish that the separate B duty to report also to that sectoral CSIRT has been discharged.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive unresolved point is whether the CSIRT or competent authority receiving the report under A is the same designated sectoral CSIRT under B, and whether the applicable Article 19 rules treat A's report as satisfying B's separate 'tevens bij' reporting duty. The provisions shown do not establish that equivalence or discharge.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In afwijking van de eerste alinea, punt b), meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related incident management and reporting by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a final report, or an interim progress report followed by a final report, after an incident, while provision B requires a financial entity to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process that includes reporting-related functions. If the process duty were read as requiring a separate incident-management record or report, the same incident could generate overlapping obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B, as shown, requires a management process, not a particular filing, recipient, or deadline. Provision A imposes a concrete final/progress-report duty on an essential or important entity, and the two duties can readily be performed cumulatively without either requiring conduct prohibited by the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT or personal-data security incidents by a financial entity acting as a processor
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without unreasonable delay when it becomes aware of a personal-data breach, while B requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority. If the same event satisfies both triggers, the entity may owe two separate communications to different recipients, and B does not state that reporting to the authority replaces A's notice to the controller.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and use different triggers: A applies to a processor and requires notice to the controller, whereas B applies to a financial entity and concerns serious ICT-related incidents reported to a competent authority. A financial entity can comply with both by notifying the controller and separately reporting the serious incident to the authority; neither duty prevents the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is processing personal data for a controller and suffers a security incident that both constitutes a personal-data breach and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. The entity must inform the controller 'zonder onredelijke vertraging' under A and also submit the first notification and reports to 'de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46' under B; notifying the controller does not constitute the required filing with that authority, and reporting to the authority does not constitute notice to the controller.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without unreasonable delay when it becomes aware of a personal-data breach, while B sets a separate deadline for the notification referred to in paragraph 1 after the provider or deployer becomes aware of a serious incident. If one event is both a personal-data breach and a serious AI incident, the duties may involve different triggering knowledge and timing requirements, and notification under one provision does not expressly discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the processor informs the controller under A, and the provider or deployer makes the paragraph-1 notification under B. They address different recipients and different legally defined events, so neither text establishes that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk AI system causes a security breach that unlawfully exposes personal data. The processor becomes aware of the personal-data breach and must inform the controller under A without unreasonable delay; separately, the provider or deployer must make the paragraph-1 serious-incident notification under B immediately after establishing the causal link and in any event no later than 15 days after becoming aware of the serious incident. Informing the controller does not, on the texts shown, constitute the paragraph-1 notification, whose recipient is supplied by the referenced paragraph 1 rather than by B itself.
verdict.missing_reference: The recipient and substantive trigger for B are in Article 73(1), which is referenced but not reproduced as part of provision B; the text shown therefore does not fully establish the second filing's recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents that may affect services and personal-data breaches
