verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident can simultaneously be a personal-data breach, requiring the entity to notify its service recipients immediately and the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours. These are separate notifications to different recipients, so satisfying the GDPR notification does not satisfy the recipient-notification duty, and vice versa.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed without contradiction: the entity can notify service recipients immediately where appropriate and separately notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours if the GDPR conditions are met. They concern different recipients and triggers, but those differences make the duties cumulative rather than incompatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity that is also the GDPR controller suffers a ransomware incident that compromises personal data and significantly adversely affects the services it provides. It must notify its service recipients 'onverwijld' under provision A and separately notify the competent supervisory authority, if the breach presents a likely risk, 'uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen' under provision B; neither notification discharges the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit, tenzij het niet waarschijnlijk is dat de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or submitting information to authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use a mandatory submission or notification duty and identify an authority as recipient. If the same entity were simultaneously a conformity-assessment body covered by A and a bank, trading platform, central securities depository, or central counterparty covered by B, it would have duties involving different authorities, potentially suggesting two separate filings.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggering acts and different regulated actors: A requires conformity-assessment bodies to apply for notification to their notifying authority, while B requires specified financial-sector entities to make an ICT-incident notification also to the designated sectoral CSIRT. Nothing in either text says that one filing substitutes for the other, but neither text establishes that the same event or submission triggers both duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious ICT-related incident involving a high-risk AI system used by a financial entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity may have to report the same incident under both regimes, potentially on different clocks: Article 19 requires reporting to the relevant competent authority, while Article 73 requires a death-related report within ten days. If Article 73 requires a separate filing to a recipient not identified in the excerpt, the two duties could be cumulative.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The shown Article 73 text does not identify a recipient or establish that its report is separate from the Article 19 report. Article 19 already requires the financial entity to report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, and its referenced procedure may govern the applicable timing and form. On the text shown, there is therefore no established second recipient or separate filing that would make the duties genuinely cumulative.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing part of 32024R1689 art. 73, especially lid 1 (which should identify who must receive the report and what information/form it requires), and any applicable provisions specifying whether the Article 73 report is separate from or can be combined with the Article 19 report. The Article 19 deadlines and procedures in art. 20 are also needed to compare clocks.
verdict.decisive_exception: Not established whether the Article 73 report is a separate filing, or whether reporting under Article 19 to the relevant competent authority satisfies Article 73. The excerpt supplies no B recipient, so dual_reporting_tension cannot be established from the shown text.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Significante of ernstige incidenten affecting services provided by an entity that may also be a provider of a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires immediate notice to the entity’s service recipients, while B requires a report to the market-surveillance authorities in the Member States where the incident occurred. If the same incident triggers both provisions, these are separate communications to different recipients; reporting to one does not notify the other, and the texts do not establish a single coordinated filing or priority rule.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can promptly inform its service recipients and separately report the serious incident to the relevant market-surveillance authorities. They impose different duties to different recipients rather than mutually incompatible duties, so there is no impossibility of simultaneous compliance.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk AI system is also an essential or important entity. A serious incident involving that AI system adversely affects the services it provides and occurs in a particular Member State. The provider must immediately inform its service recipients under A and separately report the incident to that Member State’s market-surveillance authority under B; notifying the recipients does not constitute a report to the authority, and reporting to the authority does not inform the recipients. The reporting clocks also differ in the supplied text: A requires notice “onverwijld”, while B’s related paragraph requires immediate reporting and, in specified cases, no later than two days after awareness.
verdict.decisive_exception: None apparent from the provisions shown. The key point is that the duties are cumulative and addressed to different recipients, not that one overrides the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of ICT/cyber incidents by financial-sector entities and subsequent reporting to ENISA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident reporting and can involve the same underlying incident information. However, Article 23 assigns the quarterly summary to the central contact point, while provision B requires the listed financial entities themselves to report to the sectoral CSIRT; if both duties are triggered, they involve different actors, recipients, and reporting functions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are readily cumulative rather than contradictory: the financial entities report incidents to the designated sectoral CSIRT, while the central contact point later submits an anonymised, aggregated summary to ENISA. Nothing in either text says that the entity's report to the CSIRT replaces the central contact point's separate ENISA summary.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten die overeenkomstig lid 1 van dit artikel en overeenkomstig artikel 30 zijn gemeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting by an actor that is both a trust-service provider subject to NIS2 and an AI-system deployer subject to the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident may trigger A's 24-hour report to "het CSIRT of ... de bevoegde autoriteit," while B requires notification of the fundamental-rights-impact assessment results to "de markttoezichtautoriteit." These are distinct statutory notifications to different recipients, and A's incident report does not, on the text shown, include or substitute for B's assessment-results notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different triggering events and information: A concerns significant incidents affecting the provision of trust services, whereas B concerns completion of a fundamental-rights-impact assessment before use of a high-risk AI system. An actor can make both notifications, and the text does not expressly make one filing impossible or state that the reports must concern the same event.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider uses a high-risk AI system in a covered public-service context and has completed the required fundamental-rights-impact assessment. A significant incident then affects its trust services. Within 24 hours it must report the incident to "het CSIRT of ... de bevoegde autoriteit" under A, while B requires notification of the assessment results to "de markttoezichtautoriteit". Filing the incident report with the CSIRT or competent authority does not, on the text shown, notify the market-surveillance authority or discharge the separate notification duty; both filings are therefore required if B's notification obligation has been triggered.
verdict.decisive_exception: The possible exemption in Article 46(1) of the AI Act could remove B's notification duty, but whether it applies is not established by the text shown. The provisions also do not establish whether the competent authority under A is the same body as the market-surveillance authority under B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In afwijking van de eerste alinea, punt b), meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and transaction-reporting services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to submit a final or progress report after an incident, while provision B requires providers of data-reporting services to operate systems that check transaction reports and request retransmission where needed. If the same organisation falls within both categories, the duties concern reporting-related processes and could impose additional operational obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different triggers and objects. A concerns a post-incident report by an essential or important entity to its CSIRT and competent authority; B concerns the technical detection and correction of omissions or obvious errors in transaction reports by providers of data-reporting services. B contains no reporting deadline or recipient and does not prohibit or replace A's incident-reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related obligations affecting data-reporting service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires essential or important entities to report significant incidents to a CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. Provision B requires data-reporting service providers to maintain systems capable of checking transaction reports; if a failure of those systems causes a significant incident, the provider may fall within A, but B itself imposes no separate reporting duty or recipient.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of obligations: A is an incident-reporting duty triggered only by a significant incident, while B is a preventive system-design and detection duty. A provider can maintain the systems required by B and, if a qualifying incident occurs, separately comply with A; nothing in B forbids or substitutes for A's reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident or misuse reporting by an organisation subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires notification to Onze Minister, while provision B requires a significant-incident warning and incident report to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, with additional reports potentially required. The texts do not say that notifying Onze Minister is a notification to the CSIRT or competent authority, nor that one filing discharges the other, so the same incident may require separate filings to different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the actor can promptly notify Onze Minister under A and separately submit the required warning and incident report under B. There is no incompatible command, and the provisions may apply to different incidents or actors depending on the statutory scope and the incident's significance.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation suffers a significant incident that compromises the integrity of its own electronic service and therefore is both an 'inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit' under A and a significant incident under B. It must notify Onze Minister immediately and also give the early warning and submit the incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority; notifying Onze Minister does not, on the texts shown, constitute either of those B filings. The filings therefore run to different recipients and include different reporting content and clocks.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether national implementation or another provision treats Onze Minister as the competent authority or provides that the notification under A is forwarded to, or substitutes for, the CSIRT/competent-authority filings required by B. That equivalence or substitution is not established in the provisions shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by a trust-service provider where a significant incident also constitutes a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect the data subject’s privacy.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident can trigger two mandatory notifications by the same provider to different recipients: the data subject must be informed without delay under A, while the CSIRT or competent authority must be notified within 24 hours under B. Neither notification is addressed to the other recipient, so filing one cannot discharge the other; the texts also provide no coordination rule for the two duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the provider can notify the affected person immediately and separately report the significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours. Nothing in either provision forbids making the other notification or makes the deadlines incompatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider discovers a significant cyber incident affecting its trust services that also involves personal data and is likely to have adverse consequences for the privacy of identifiable data subjects. The provider must notify each affected data subject “onverwijld” under A and separately notify “het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit” within 24 hours under B; the two filings have different recipients and both remain required.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or personal-data incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying significant incident and a personal-data breach could arise from the same event. The entity must notify its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, while a processor must separately inform the controller without unreasonable delay; the recipients differ, so one notification does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed: the relevant actor can send the early warning to the CSIRT and competent authority and separately inform the controller. The duties have different triggers and recipients, but that makes them cumulative rather than legally incompatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer acting as a processor suffers a ransomware incident that is both a significant incident under BWBR0052872 and a personal-data breach under the GDPR. It must give the early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours and separately inform the controller without unreasonable delay; notifying the CSIRT or competent authority does not notify the controller.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving a high-risk AI system that is a medical device or in-vitro diagnostic device
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: For an entity covered by both provisions, the same serious incident could require an end report to its CSIRT and competent authority under A, while B requires reporting the incident to the nationally designated competent authority in the Member State where it occurred. If those are different authorities, the actor must make separate reports, and B supplies no deadline that can be compared with A’s one-month deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions may concern different reporting regimes and triggers: A covers an incident as defined by the cybersecurity instrument after a prior Article 27 notification, whereas B limits AI serious-incident reporting to the incidents specified in Article 3(49)(c). If the competent authority under A is the same authority designated under B, or if the reports can be combined, the texts shown do not expressly prohibit a single submission from satisfying both duties.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer is an essential or important entity and operates a high-risk AI system that is a safety component. A cybersecurity incident affecting the system is also a serious incident under Article 3(49)(c), and it occurs in a Member State different from the authority to which the entity normally reports. The entity must submit A’s end report within one month to its CSIRT and its competent authority, and must also report under B to the nationally designated competent authority in the Member State where the incident occurred; filing with the CSIRT and A’s competent authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate B reporting duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the authorities and reporting submissions are legally treated as the same recipient and filing, and whether another provision coordinates or consolidates the two reporting duties, is not established by the excerpts. The extracted recipients indicate potentially separate recipients, but the texts do not expressly state that one report discharges the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT incidents by financial-sector entities to a CSIRT
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires reporting significant incidents to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. Provision B requires banks and specified financial-market entities to make the Article 19 report, including a voluntary report, also to the sector-designated CSIRT; this could suggest an additional filing to a specifically designated recipient.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts do not establish two separate reporting events or two different mandatory recipients. Provision B says the report is made “tevens bij” the designated sectoral CSIRT, which can be the CSIRT contemplated by A, while A itself permits reporting to the CSIRT or competent authority and does not impose a conflicting deadline or content requirement. The provisions can therefore be satisfied cumulatively without an unresolved conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or ICT incident by a financial-sector provider that is also an electronic-communications service provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying security breach under Provision A must be reported immediately to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, while Provision B requires the specified financial-sector entities to make the relevant report also to the designated sectoral CSIRT. The texts identify different recipients and do not say that reporting to one recipient discharges the other, so the same incident may require two separate filings.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed without contradiction: the actor can report the incident immediately to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens and also make the required report to the sectoral CSIRT. Provision B's use of “tevens” supports an additional reporting channel rather than a substitute or prohibition.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank that provides a public electronic communications service suffers a security breach affecting personal data processed in connection with that service, and the same event is also an ICT incident covered by the report referred to in Provision B. The bank must notify the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens “onverwijld” and also report the event to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors; filing with one recipient does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate duty to the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an organisation that is both a GDPR controller and a NIS2 covered entity, where the same event is both a personal-data breach and a significant incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same event can trigger two reporting duties by the same actor: GDPR reporting to the Article 55 supervisory authority and NIS2 reporting to the CSIRT or competent authority. These are distinct regimes with potentially different recipients and additional NIS2 filings, so a report under one regime does not, on the text shown, discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the actor can report the event to the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours and separately provide the NIS2 early warning and incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority. Where the NIS2 competent authority is also the relevant GDPR supervisory authority, the practical burden may overlap, but the provisions do not establish that the filings are legally identical or that one substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company covered by NIS2 suffers a cyberattack that both compromises personal data, creating a GDPR personal-data breach, and significantly affects the availability of its services, creating a NIS2 significant incident. The company must report the personal-data breach to “de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit” within 72 hours, while also giving a NIS2 early warning to “het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit” within 24 hours and submitting the NIS2 incident notification within 72 hours. Filing the GDPR report does not, on the text shown, establish compliance with the separate NIS2 warning and incident-reporting duties, particularly where the recipients differ.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive unresolved point is whether national implementation or another provision treats a report to the NIS2 competent authority or CSIRT as also satisfying the GDPR notification duty, or designates the same body and filing as serving both regimes. No such substitution or coordination rule appears in the provisions shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving a high-risk AI system that is a safety component or device covered by Regulations (EU) 2017/745 or 2017/746
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: For a qualifying incident, Provision A requires the bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify Onze Minister immediately, while Provision B requires the incident to be reported to a different national competent authority designated by the Member State where it occurred. The texts do not say that reporting to one recipient satisfies the other, so the same event may require two separate reports.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can both be performed: the operator can notify Onze Minister immediately under A and also report the incident to the designated national competent authority under B. Nothing in either provision prohibits the additional notification or makes the recipients mutually exclusive.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An aangewezen organisatie operating a high-risk AI system that is a safety component of a device covered by Regulation (EU) 2017/745 suffers a security breach that is also a serious incident under Article 3, point 49(c), of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. The organisation must notify Onze Minister immediately under A and separately report the incident to the national competent authority designated by the Member State where the incident occurred under B; notifying one authority does not, on the texts shown, discharge the duty to notify the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap. The decisive issue is that the provisions identify different recipients and contain no rule equating the two notifications or making one substitute for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related incident management and reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the central contact point to submit a quarterly summary to ENISA, while provision B requires financial entities to establish a process to report ICT-related incidents. If a financial entity is also within the scope of provision A, the underlying incidents may feed both an entity-level reporting process and a separate central-contact-point summary, potentially creating cumulative reporting obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and at different levels: provision B concerns a financial entity's internal incident-management process, whereas provision A concerns the central contact point's aggregated, anonymised quarterly report to ENISA. Provision A does not require the financial entity to make the ENISA filing, and provision B does not specify a conflicting recipient or deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting and evaluation of ICT/cyber-incident and risk-management information by potentially overlapping financial or digital-service entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same actor and incident-related information fall within both regimes, Provision A requires a quarterly anonymised, aggregated report to Enisa, while Provision B requires a report on the ICT-risk-management framework to the competent authority when requested. These are different reports to different recipients, and neither text says that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different subjects and concern different information: A is a central contact point's periodic aggregation of previously reported incidents, whereas B concerns documentation and evaluation of a financial entity's ICT-risk-management framework. They can therefore be performed cumulatively without contradiction; moreover, B's report is conditional on a request, so it may never be triggered.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is subject to both instruments, and a serious ICT incident is included in the incident information that the central contact point must aggregate. The central contact point must submit the quarterly anonymised and aggregated report to Enisa, while the financial entity must also provide its ICT-risk-management-framework evaluation report to the competent authority after that authority requests it. Filing the entity's evaluation report with the competent authority does not discharge the central contact point's separate quarterly filing with Enisa, and the two provisions provide no coordination rule for the two reports.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision B's reporting duty is conditional on a request by the competent authority; if no request is made, the second filing is not triggered. The dual-reporting conclusion therefore depends on the concrete scenario including such a request and on the actor being subject to both regimes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.

verdict.shared_subject: Significante incidenten met een nadelige invloed op de verlening van diensten door essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij hetzelfde significante incident verplicht A de entiteit haar dienstontvangers onverwijld te informeren, terwijl B daarnaast een melding bij het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit verlangt. Dat zijn verschillende ontvangers en afzonderlijke communicatiedoelen, zodat een melding aan de autoriteit de kennisgeving aan dienstontvangers niet vervangt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: B bevat zelf eveneens de verplichting om de ontvangers van diensten onverwijld te informeren, met vrijwel dezelfde formulering als A. Voor zover A en B op dezelfde entiteit en hetzelfde incident van toepassing zijn, kan één kennisgeving aan de ontvangers dus aan beide bepalingen voldoen; de autoriteitsmelding onder B is daarnaast een afzonderlijke verplichting, maar maakt A niet onmogelijk.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een essentiële entiteit krijgt kennis van een significant incident dat de verlening van haar diensten nadelig beïnvloedt. Zij moet onverwijld haar dienstontvangers informeren op grond van A én onverwijld hetzelfde incident melden bij haar CSIRT of bevoegde autoriteit op grond van B; een van deze twee mededelingen kan de andere niet vervangen omdat de ontvangers verschillen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4. In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and notification by entities affected by ICT incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a trust-service provider to report a qualifying significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B requires a financial entity to notify affected clients without delay when a serious ICT-related incident affects clients’ financial interests; if one entity were subject to both regimes and the same incident met both triggers, these would be separate communications to different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity reports to the CSIRT or competent authority under A and separately informs clients under B. Neither provision says that one notification substitutes for the other, and the actors and incident definitions differ, so the texts do not establish a conflict merely because both concern incidents.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also a trust-service provider suffers a significant incident affecting its trust services, and the incident is also a serious ICT-related incident affecting clients’ financial interests. It must report the incident to “het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit” within 24 hours under A and separately notify affected clients “onverwijld” under B; notifying one recipient does not discharge the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or personal-data breach by a public authority or designated organisation that is also a GDPR controller.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident can trigger both duties: provision A requires immediate notice to the Minister, while provision B requires notice to the competent supervisory authority, normally within 72 hours of awareness. These are different recipients, so notifying one does not textually discharge the separate duty to notify the other; the actor may therefore face two filings and two reporting regimes for one breach.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be satisfied cumulatively without contradiction: the actor can notify the Minister immediately and notify the supervisory authority within 72 hours. Provision B also excludes breaches unlikely to risk individuals’ rights and freedoms, so not every security incident covered by A triggers B.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation providing an electronic public service suffers a cyberattack that both compromises the security of its service and unlawfully exposes stored personal data, creating a likely risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms. It must notify “Onze Minister onverwijld” under A and separately notify “de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit” under B, with the latter due, if possible, within 72 hours of awareness; filing with one recipient does not notify the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision B’s exception applies if it is not likely that the personal-data breach poses a risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms. If that exception applies, only A is triggered. The texts do not establish any exception allowing notice to the Minister to substitute for notice to the supervisory authority when B applies.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit, tenzij het niet waarschijnlijk is dat de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens een risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations triggered by different events involving potentially overlapping digital systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same operator is both an electronic-communications provider experiencing a qualifying personal-data security breach and a user of a qualifying high-risk AI system that has completed the fundamental-rights impact assessment, the provisions require communications to different authorities: the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens and the market-surveillance authority. A notification to one authority would not, on the text shown, discharge the separate notification duty to the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with cumulatively because they concern different triggering events and different regulatory regimes: A concerns a security breach with adverse effects on personal-data protection, while B concerns completion of a fundamental-rights impact assessment for a high-risk AI system. Nothing in either provision prohibits making both notifications, and B even contemplates a possible exemption under Article 46(1).
verdict.concrete_scenario: A telecommunications provider uses a qualifying high-risk AI system and has completed the Article 27(1) fundamental-rights impact assessment. The provider then suffers a security breach affecting personal data processed in connection with its electronic-communications service, while the Article 27 assessment has also been completed. It must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens without delay under A and separately notify the market-surveillance authority of the assessment results under B; notifying one recipient does not, on the text shown, satisfy the other duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the Article 46(1) exemption applies to the operator's Article 27 notification duty is not established by the text shown. The two duties also have different triggers, so the dual-reporting scenario requires both triggers to be present.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/cyber incidents reported under the respective instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the central contact point to submit a quarterly summary to ENISA. Provision B, however, does not require the financial entity to make a separate report; it states that the entity remains fully responsible for handling and consequences of incidents already reported under Article 19(1), while the authority may provide feedback.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, sequential responsibilities on different actors: A concerns the central contact point’s aggregated reporting to ENISA, whereas B concerns the financial entity’s continuing responsibility after its own incident reports and the authority’s possible feedback. Nothing in B discharges, contradicts, or duplicates A’s quarterly summary duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten die overeenkomstig lid 1 van dit artikel en overeenkomstig artikel 30 zijn gemeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onverminderd de ontvangen feedback van toezichthouders blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving an AI system and a network/information-system incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a significant incident to be reported to the CSIRT or competent authority, including an early warning within 24 hours and an incident notification within 72 hours. B separately requires a provider or deployer to report a fatal serious incident involving a high-risk AI system within ten days, but it does not identify the recipient in the text shown; if B entails a separate recipient or filing, the same event could require cumulative reports under different regimes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish that B requires a separate filing to a different recipient: B only states a deadline and does not specify the recipient or reporting content. If the AI incident is also a significant incident under A and both duties are directed to the same authority or filing mechanism, A's earlier and more detailed reporting sequence could satisfy the later B deadline.
verdict.missing_reference: The omitted parts of 32024R1689 art. 73, especially the provision identifying the recipient, form and content of the report required by paragraph 3, are needed to determine whether B requires a separate filing. The scope provisions defining a 'serious incident' and 'high-risk AI system' may also be needed to establish that the same event falls under both regimes.
verdict.decisive_exception: If the missing AI Act provisions require reporting to the same recipient and the NIS2 reports contain the information required by B, the duties may be compatible; if they require a separate report to a different recipient, dual reporting may result.
verdict.evidence_span_a: bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit: a) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Client notification of incidents affecting personal data or clients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the provider to notify the person whose personal data are concerned without delay when a personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect that person's privacy. B separately requires a financial entity to notify its clients without delay when a serious ICT-related incident affects clients' financial interests; one incident could satisfy both triggers, while the provisions identify different notification subjects and different information.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can notify each affected data subject under A and its clients under B, with the same immediate timing. The texts do not state that either notice substitutes for the other, and the recipients may overlap where a client is also the affected data subject.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity suffers one serious ICT-related incident that compromises clients' personal data and is likely to adversely affect their privacy, while also affecting the clients' financial interests. The entity must, without delay, notify the affected persons under A and notify its clients under B, including the measures taken to limit negative effects; notifying one recipient group does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate duty to notify the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting certain incidents involving high-risk AI systems that are also personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same event, but they require notifications to different recipients: the affected person under A and the designated national competent authority under B. Thus, notifying one recipient does not satisfy the other, creating cumulative reporting duties; B also supplies no deadline, leaving an unresolved timing relationship with A's 'onverwijld' requirement.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are individually compatible because they serve different recipients and purposes: A protects affected individuals, while B reports qualifying serious incidents to a public authority. Nothing in either text prohibits making both notifications, and B may apply only to the narrower category of serious incidents involving specified high-risk AI systems.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk AI system that is itself, or contains a safety component of, a device covered by Regulation (EU) 2017/745 or 2017/746 suffers an incident that is both a serious incident under Article 73 and a personal-data breach likely to have adverse effects on an affected person's privacy. The provider must notify the affected person 'onverwijld' under A and separately report the incident to 'de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan' under B; filing with either recipient does not discharge the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan

verdict.shared_subject: Incident management and notification following an ICT or personal-data incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the provider to notify the affected person without delay when a personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect that person's privacy. Provision B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process for detecting, managing and reporting ICT-related incidents; if the same event is both a qualifying personal-data breach and an ICT-related incident, the entity may have to perform both individual notification and incident reporting, with different content and potentially different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties rather than contradictory commands: A is an immediate notification duty to the affected person, while B is a system-level process duty and does not specify a conflicting deadline or prohibit notification. Article 17 as shown does not itself establish a separate filing to a different recipient or a reporting deadline, so the text does not establish the dual-reporting conditions.
verdict.missing_reference: The specific DORA provisions governing which ICT-related incidents must be reported, to whom, and within what deadlines—particularly provisions outside Article 17—would be needed to determine whether a qualifying event requires a separate regulatory filing in addition to the notification under Article 11.3a.
verdict.decisive_exception: Not applicable: the shown provisions do not establish a permission/refusal conflict or a second concrete reporting filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden

verdict.shared_subject: Responsibility and handling of ICT-related or serious incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incidents involving regulated digital systems, and an incident could potentially fall within both regimes. However, Provision A imposes continuing responsibility for handling and consequences, while Provision B imposes a time-limited notification duty; the texts do not establish two reporting duties, different recipients, or incompatible deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not require a filing or specify a recipient or deadline; it merely preserves the financial entity’s full responsibility despite supervisory feedback. Provision B requires the relevant provider or user to report a serious incident to market-surveillance authorities within the stated period. These duties can plainly be performed together, and A does not discharge, override, or conflict with B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onverminderd de ontvangen feedback van toezichthouders blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Handling and responsibility for ICT-related incidents involving entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 72 hours. Provision B states that financial entities remain fully responsible for handling and consequences of ICT incidents reported under Article 19(1), which could be read as imposing an additional responsibility alongside the NIS2 reporting process.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B does not impose a second reporting duty, deadline, or recipient; it merely preserves the financial entity’s substantive responsibility after reporting under Article 19(1). Provision A’s reporting obligation and Provision B’s responsibility rule can therefore both be satisfied without contradiction or duplicate filings.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd

verdict.shared_subject: Operational obligations concerning data-reporting services and serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations on providers, and a provider of a data-reporting service could also operate a high-risk AI system involved in a fatal serious incident. In that situation, one might initially suspect overlapping incident-related compliance duties, especially because provision B imposes an immediate reporting deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires transaction-reporting systems to check submissions for completeness and apparent errors and request retransmission; it does not require reporting an incident, identify a recipient, or set a deadline. Provision B requires a serious-incident notification after a causal link involving a high-risk AI system is established or suspected, but the shown text does not make that notification the same filing as anything required by A. The duties therefore address different subjects and can be performed cumulatively without conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Niettegenstaande lid 2 wordt bij overlijden van een persoon de melding gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder of de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een oorzakelijk verband heeft vastgesteld, of zodra hij of zij dit vermoedt, tussen het AI-systeem met een hoog risico en het ernstige incident, doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires documentation and periodic evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, with an evaluation report submitted on request to the competent authority. Provision B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application for notification to the notifying authority; if the same entity were subject to both, these would concern different submissions, authorities, and triggers, so they would not discharge one another.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors and different subject matters: A concerns a financial entity’s ICT-risk-management framework and an evaluation report, while B concerns a conformity-assessment body’s application for notification. Nothing in either text makes the ICT-risk-management report an alternative to, or incompatible with, the notification application.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een evaluatieverslag van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt op verzoek bij de bevoegde autoriteit ingediend.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-incidenten involving personal-data breaches at a financial entity/provider subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same serious ICT-related incident involving a personal-data breach. Provision A requires immediate notification to the affected person, while provision B requires a report to the competent authority when it requests the evaluation report; these are different recipients and distinct duties, so one communication does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable obligations rather than contradictory ones: A protects affected individuals through prompt breach notification, while B concerns documenting and evaluating the ICT-risk-management framework and supplying an evaluation report to the competent authority on request. An actor can make the individual notification and separately maintain or provide the required framework report.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity suffers a serious ICT-related incident that is also a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect an individual's privacy. It must notify the affected person immediately under A, and, when the competent authority requests the evaluation report following the incident, provide that report under B; the two filings go to different recipients and have different triggers and timing, so neither filing replaces the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, alsook wanneer zich ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten voordoen en na toezichtinstructies of -conclusies die voortvloeien uit relevante tests of auditprocessen op het gebied van digitale operationele weerbaarheid. Het wordt voortdurend verbeterd op basis van de lessen die uit de uitvoering en de monitoring naar voren komen. Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT incidents and ICT-risk-management obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an entity to report each significant incident immediately to its CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated periodically and at serious ICT-related incidents, which could be read as requiring incident-related documentation in addition to A’s report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties rather than two reports for the same triggering event: A is an external incident notification to a CSIRT or competent authority, while B concerns internal documentation and evaluation of the risk-management framework, with an evaluation report submitted only on request. Nothing in B requires a separate filing to a different recipient on a separate clock, and complying with A does not purport to replace B’s internal evaluation duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Operators potentially subject to both data-reporting-service and high-risk AI incident rules
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires data-reporting-service providers to operate systems that check transaction reports and request retransmission where needed. Provision B requires a high-risk AI provider or user to report serious incidents within a specified period, so a single operator might have both an operational monitoring duty and an incident-reporting duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different triggers and subject matter: A concerns completeness and errors in transaction reports, while B concerns reporting serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems. Nothing in A requires or forbids incident reporting, and nothing in B discharges or conflicts with A's system-control obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related/significant-incident management and reporting by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes an actual incident-reporting duty, with a 24-hour backstop, on an essential or important entity offering a trust service. Provision B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident management process that includes reporting, so an entity could potentially fall within both regimes and face an additional reporting framework.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B, as shown, is a system-level process-design and implementation duty; it does not specify a separate report, recipient, triggering event, or deadline. It therefore does not establish a second filing that would be cumulative with A. An entity can implement a process that ensures compliance with A, while any additional reporting details would have to come from other provisions not shown.
verdict.missing_reference: The specific DORA provisions that define which ICT-related incidents financial entities must report, to whom, and within what deadline—particularly provisions beyond Article 17—would be needed to assess any separate reporting obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related reporting and information flows
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident information, and the extracted recipients and timing differ: the processor informs the controller without unreasonable delay, while the central contact point submits a summary to ENISA every three months. If the same organisation or incident chain engages both roles, these are separate communications with different recipients and clocks, so one filing cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors: A binds the processor and B binds the central contact point. Moreover, B concerns a periodic, anonymised and aggregated summary, whereas A is an immediate notification to the controller; each can be performed independently without the texts requiring incompatible content or conduct.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens over significante incidenten, incidenten, cyberdreigingen en bijna-incidenten die overeenkomstig lid 1 van dit artikel en overeenkomstig artikel 30 zijn gemeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant incidents by essential or important entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a progress report instead of the final report when the incident is still ongoing, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Provision B requires immediate reporting of a significant incident to the entity’s CSIRT or competent authority, potentially creating an additional reporting duty with a different trigger and timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different stages of the same incident-reporting process: B requires the initial significant-incident notification, while A governs the later final-report deadline when the incident remains ongoing. The texts do not require two different reports to different recipients on incompatible clocks; A’s report is expressly tied to the final report required after the initial notification, and both can be satisfied cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid. Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk management documentation/evaluation and serious-incident reporting during real-world testing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may concern a serious ICT-related incident involving an AI system tested in real-world conditions. Provision A requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated at such incidents, while Provision B requires the serious incident itself to be reported to the national market-surveillance authority; this could create additional incident-related compliance work.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different triggers and objects. A concerns periodic and incident-related documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, with an evaluation report submitted only on request to the competent authority; B concerns immediate risk mitigation and reporting of a serious incident during real-world testing to the national market-surveillance authority. Nothing in A requires a filing to that authority, and nothing in B treats its incident report as an evaluation report under A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident under NIS2 must be reported immediately to the entity’s CSIRT or, where applicable, competent authority, while DORA requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority. If the same financial entity and incident satisfy both triggers, the provisions could require separate reports under different regimes, with potentially different forms, content and procedural timelines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can report the incident to the DORA relevant competent authority and separately comply with the NIS2 CSIRT or competent-authority reporting route. DORA also expressly contemplates information being provided to NIS2-designated competent authorities or CSIRTs, but the texts shown do not establish that a DORA filing automatically discharges the NIS2 duty.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also an essential or important NIS2 entity and suffers one cyber incident that is both a NIS2 “significant incident” and a DORA “serious ICT-related incident.” It must report under NIS2 “onverwijld” to “zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit” and under DORA to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46”; filing with the DORA authority does not, on the text shown, itself constitute the NIS2 report to the CSIRT or establish that the two reporting procedures are interchangeable.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive unresolved point is whether national implementation or the DORA procedures provide that one filing, or transmission by the competent authority, legally satisfies the separate NIS2 reporting obligation. The provisions shown do not establish such a substitution; DORA merely says that Member States may require reports also to NIS2 authorities or CSIRTs.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related information and ICT-risk-management obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by a serious or significant ICT incident and impose action by the same regulated entity. However, they require different actions for different recipients: informing service recipients without delay under A, while providing an evaluation report to the competent authority when requested under B; one communication cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are readily cumulative rather than contradictory: the entity can promptly inform affected service recipients and separately document or evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework and provide the resulting report to the competent authority if requested. The annual or incident-triggered evaluation duty does not replace the immediate customer-information duty.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A significant ICT incident adversely affects an essential entity’s service and also constitutes a serious ICT-related incident for a financial entity subject to B. The entity must inform its service recipients “onverwijld” under A, while separately documenting and evaluating its ICT-risk-management framework and, if requested, sending the evaluation report to “de bevoegde autoriteit” under B; informing recipients does not satisfy the authority-reporting duty, and the authority report does not satisfy the recipient-notification duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the separate duties on the text shown; the key point is that the recipients and functions differ. B’s authority-reporting obligation is conditional on a request, so it is not necessarily triggered in every incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or serious incident involving a high-risk AI system and personal-data protection
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same provider and incident, but they require notifications to different authorities: the Dutch provision requires immediate notice to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, while Article 73 requires notice to the market-surveillance authorities. The text does not say that one notification substitutes for the other, so a qualifying incident appears to require two separate filings, potentially on different procedural timelines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different regulatory regimes and recipients, and each can be fulfilled independently without preventing compliance with the other. Article 73's context supplies timing rules for its own notification, while Article 11.3a requires prompt notification to the data-protection authority; there is no express contradiction between making both notifications.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider offers a high-risk AI system in the EU through a public electronic communications service. A security breach involving that system adversely affects the protection of personal data processed in connection with the service and also qualifies as a serious incident under Article 73. The provider must notify the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens 'onverwijld' under Article 11.3a and separately notify 'de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden' under Article 73; notifying one authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the duty to notify the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: No exception or substitution rule is shown stating that notification to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens satisfies the Article 73 notification duty, or vice versa.
