The Article 73 timing provisions govern its own filing and do not identify the data-protection authority as an alternative recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens die zijn verwerkt in verband met de levering van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst in de Europese Unie.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van in de Unie in de handel gebrachte AI-systemen met een hoog risico melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations arising from different events and addressed to different recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties, and a single operator could potentially be involved in both a personal-data breach and the use of a high-risk AI system requiring a fundamental-rights-impact assessment. However, the duties concern different triggering events and require notifications to different recipients, so one notification cannot discharge the other if both are triggered.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are readily cumulative: the processor informs the controller of a personal-data breach, while the deployer informs the market-surveillance authority of the assessment results. Neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other, and the texts do not establish that the same event triggers both duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_subject: Governance and reporting of ICT or data-security incidents by a financial entity that is also a GDPR controller
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the controller to notify the competent data-protection supervisory authority within 72 hours when a personal-data breach presents a risk. Provision B requires the management body to establish internal corporate reporting channels capable of obtaining information about serious ICT-related incidents and their consequences, so the same incident may trigger both an external GDPR notification and an internal governance-information process.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties rather than conflicting ones: A is an external notification duty of the controller to a specified supervisory authority, while B is an internal organisational duty of the management body to establish channels for obtaining information. Provision B specifies no separate filing, recipient, or deadline, and nothing indicates that its internal channels replace or duplicate the GDPR notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting and documenting personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires prompt notification to the affected person when the breach is likely to adversely affect that person's privacy. Provision B requires the controller to document every personal-data breach so that the supervisory authority can check compliance; these duties concern different actions and recipients, so a single notification to the affected person does not itself satisfy the documentation duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties rather than incompatible ones: the provider/controller can notify the affected person promptly and separately document the breach for supervisory review. Provision B does not specify a separate reporting deadline or require a filing to a different authority on the facts shown, so there is no demonstrated dual-reporting conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-gerelateerde/significante incidenten bij an entity that is both a trust-service provider and a financial entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a trust-service provider to report qualifying significant incidents within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B requires a financial entity to establish and implement an incident-management process to detect, manage and report ICT-related incidents, so the strongest tension case is that one incident might trigger both an external report under A and a separate reporting process under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B, as shown, does not specify a separate recipient, deadline, or filing, and merely requires a process for reporting ICT-related incidents. It can therefore be implemented so that the process makes the report required by A, or otherwise supports any reporting required under DORA; the texts do not establish two mandatory filings to different recipients or on different clocks.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In afwijking van de eerste alinea, punt b), meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security or personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A covered public body or designated organisation must notify the Minister immediately, while B requires a processor to notify the controller without unreasonable delay. A single incident may satisfy both triggers, and the recipients are different, so notifying one does not on the text shown notify the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with by making two prompt notifications when the same actor is subject to both regimes. There is no incompatible content or deadline: “onverwijld” and “zonder onredelijke vertraging” are individually satisfiable, although they run to different recipients.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation that acts as a GDPR processor suffers a security breach involving personal data in its own electronic service. It must notify “Onze Minister” onverwijld under A and separately inform “de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke” without unreasonable delay under B; notifying either recipient does not discharge the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant incident by an essential or important entity to the CSIRT or competent authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern the same significant incident and impose an early warning to the CSIRT and/or competent authority. A possible tension is that provision A says the entity gives the warning to both recipients, whereas provision B describes reporting to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, potentially suggesting different recipient routes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are compatible because they prescribe the same early-warning event, substantially the same recipients, and the same immediate/24-hour deadline. Provision B's rule that a competent authority forwards a report to the CSIRT means that reporting through the applicable authority can discharge the corresponding CSIRT-routing requirement; it does not create a second independent filing to a different recipient. Provision B also adds later incident, interim and final reports, but those are additional reporting stages rather than a conflict with A's early warning.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity that is both subject to BWBR0052872 art. 27 and an AI Act provider or deployer covered by art. 73.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions can apply to the same incident but impose different reporting regimes: A requires a report to both its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, while B concerns the notification referred to in paragraph 1 and sets a separate deadline of up to 15 days, with the paragraph 1 context identifying market-surveillance authorities. Thus, one report to A's recipients would not necessarily discharge B's separate notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts shown do not expressly state that the same incident must simultaneously qualify as both a significant incident affecting a trust service and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system. If both duties did apply, however, the earlier 24-hour deadline could allow the operator to report promptly and then satisfy the later AI-Act deadline, provided the recipients and required contents were appropriately covered.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company provides a trust service and operates a high-risk AI system. A single cyber incident significantly affects the trust service and is also a serious incident causally linked to the AI system. The company must report the incident to its CSIRT and competent authority under A within 24 hours, and separately make the paragraph 1 notification to the relevant market-surveillance authority under B; filing with A's recipients does not, on the text shown, discharge the notification to the market-surveillance authority.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive issue is whether the AI Act's paragraph 1 notification to the market-surveillance authorities is a separate filing from the report to the CSIRT and competent authority under A. The supplied paragraph 1 context supports separate recipients, but the full procedural text of paragraph 1 and any coordination rule are not reproduced.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-incident reporting and ICT-risk-management documentation by an entity subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a final incident report to be filed with both the CSIRT and the competent authority within one month after the Article 27 notification. Provision B requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated periodically and, on request, an evaluation report to be submitted to the competent authority; this could create an additional submission concerning the same incident-related risk-management response, with no stated rule that A’s final incident report satisfies B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different objects: A is an incident-specific report containing facts, causes, consequences and mitigation measures, while B concerns periodic documentation and evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework and only requires its evaluation report upon request. Nothing in B requires a separate incident filing on the same trigger, and A’s report is not stated to be an evaluation report of the framework, so both duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het wordt voortdurend verbeterd op basis van de lessen die uit de uitvoering en de monitoring naar voren komen. Een evaluatieverslag van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt op verzoek bij de bevoegde autoriteit ingediend.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/security incident governance and reporting by entities subject to both instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an early warning to both the CSIRT and the competent authority within 24 hours of knowledge of a significant incident. Provision B requires documentation and evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework when serious ICT-related incidents occur, and a report to the competent authority if requested; the same incident could therefore trigger an incident warning under A and a separate framework-evaluation report under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different triggers and content: A is an incident notification, while B concerns documenting and evaluating the risk-management framework and reporting that evaluation only upon request. Both can be performed cumulatively, and A's 24-hour warning does not purport to replace B's evaluation or requested report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, alsook wanneer zich ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten voordoen en na toezichtinstructies of -conclusies die voortvloeien uit relevante tests of auditprocessen op het gebied van digitale operationele weerbaarheid. Het wordt voortdurend verbeterd op basis van de lessen die uit de uitvoering en de monitoring naar voren komen. Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of significant/serious ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the entity to report a significant incident to both its CSIRT and its competent authority within 72 hours at the latest. B requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority, using the DORA reporting process and forms; if the same incident satisfies both triggers, the texts do not say that an A report to the CSIRT or A's 72-hour filing discharges B's separate report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can submit the NIS2 report to its CSIRT and competent authority and separately submit the DORA notification and subsequent reports to the relevant competent authority. B also contemplates possible transmission to CSIRTs, which may facilitate coordination, although it does not expressly make that transmission equivalent to the entity's own A filing.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity discovers one ICT incident that is both a 'significant incident' under A and a 'serious ICT-related incident' under B. It must report under A 'onverwijld of ... binnen 72 uur' to both 'haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit', while B requires a separate first notification and later reports to 'de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46', using the Article 20 models and within the Article 20 deadlines. Filing the A report with its CSIRT and A competent authority does not, on the text shown, establish that the B filing to the relevant financial-sector authority has been made or that the later B reports are unnecessary.
verdict.missing_reference: The precise B deadlines and reporting content are in Article 20, and the exact identity/relationship of the relevant authorities may depend on Article 46 and national implementation. Those provisions could clarify coordination, but the shown text does not state that one filing legally substitutes for the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: No shown provision establishes that the Article 19 report to the relevant competent authority is the same filing as the Article 27 report to the CSIRT and A competent authority, or that one recipient's receipt discharges the other reporting duty. Article 19(6)'s onward transmission by the authority to CSIRTs is not stated to replace the entity's own Article 27 filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit met:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns an incident-related progress report and later final report by an essential or important entity, while Provision B concerns a conformity-assessment body's application for notification. No actor, triggering event, recipient, or deadline is shared on the texts shown, so there is no concrete basis for a conflict or cumulative reporting burden.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct duties on differently defined actors and for different purposes: A governs incident reporting during an ongoing incident, whereas B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application to a notifying authority. An entity subject to both could comply with each independently; neither provision purports to replace or obstruct the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid. Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant or serious incident by an entity/provider potentially covered by both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident could simultaneously be a significant incident affecting a trust service and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system. Provision A requires a filing to the CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, while provision B requires a filing to the market-surveillance authorities; these are different recipients, so the A filing does not discharge B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions may apply to different activities and incident definitions, and the texts shown do not establish that the same provider, system, or incident falls within both scopes. If both do apply, however, the duties are cumulative rather than mutually exclusive: the provider can make both notifications.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company provides a trust service through a high-risk AI system. A single incident both has consequences for the provision of that trust service and qualifies as a serious incident involving the high-risk AI system. The company must notify its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours under A, and separately notify the market-surveillance authorities of the Member States where the incident occurred under B; notifying the first recipients does not notify the market-surveillance authorities.
verdict.decisive_exception: The texts do not establish whether the incident definitions and scope conditions overlap in this scenario, nor whether any other provision makes one notification substitute for the other. On the stated scenario, the decisive fact is that the recipients are different.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: melden ernstige incidenten bij de markttoezichtautoriteiten van de lidstaten waarin dat incident heeft plaatsgevonden

verdict.shared_subject: Serious ICT-related incidents occurring during real-world testing of a high-risk AI system by an actor subject to both instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious incident during real-world testing may trigger both duties: Article 6 requires a report on the evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework when the competent authority requests it, while Article 60 requires every serious incident found during testing to be reported to the national market-surveillance authority under Article 73. The recipients and triggers are not stated to be identical, so one report may not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can report the incident to the national market-surveillance authority and, if requested, provide the ICT-risk-management-framework evaluation report to the competent authority. Article 6 does not prohibit or replace the Article 60 report, and Article 60 does not state that its report substitutes for Article 6’s requested evaluation report.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity conducts real-world testing of a high-risk AI system and discovers a serious ICT-related incident during the test. It must report the incident to the national market-surveillance authority under Article 60, and, when the competent authority requests it under Article 6, separately provide the report on the evaluation of its ICT-risk-management framework; reporting to the market-surveillance authority does not, on the text shown, satisfy the request from the competent authority.
verdict.missing_reference: The exact identity of the competent authority under Article 6 and the detailed reporting requirements and deadline under Article 73 of the AI Act are not shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aan de bevoegde autoriteit wordt een verslag bezorgd over de evaluatie van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer indien zij daarom verzoekt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Final and progress reporting after a significant incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions address an incident that is still ongoing when the final report would otherwise be due. Provision A requires the essential or important entity to submit a progress report instead of the final report and then a final report within one month after resolution. Provision B likewise requires a progress report at that point and a final report within one month after the incident is handled, potentially creating overlapping reporting duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions prescribe materially the same sequence and timing for the ongoing-incident situation: a progress report when the final report is due, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Provision B's reporting duty is to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, while A's referenced final-report rule is to the entity's CSIRT and competent authority; the texts do not establish separate recipients or incompatible deadlines requiring duplicate filings.
verdict.decisive_exception: None; the apparent overlap concerns aligned cumulative reporting content and timing, not incompatible duties or established duplicate filings.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid. Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious/significant incidents during real-world testing of a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident affecting an entity’s services must be reported to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B requires every serious incident found during real-world testing to be reported to the national market-surveillance authority. If the same testing incident satisfies both thresholds, the provisions name different recipients and do not state that one filing substitutes for the other, suggesting two cumulative reports.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can report the incident to the CSIRT or competent authority under A and separately to the national market-surveillance authority under B. Their triggers and reporting regimes are not identical, but that difference does not itself make compliance impossible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider’s high-risk AI system is being tested under real-world conditions and suffers a serious incident that also has significant effects on the provider’s network-and-information-system services. The provider must report it under A to the CSIRT or competent authority and under B to the national market-surveillance authority; filing with either recipient does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate duty to notify the other, and A additionally requires an early warning within 24 hours while B requires immediate reporting.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is established in the provisions shown. In particular, no rule states that a report to the CSIRT or competent authority is forwarded to, or legally substitutes for, the report to the national market-surveillance authority. The exact scope of A’s 'significant incident' trigger and B’s 'serious incident' trigger may require their external definitions, but the concrete overlap scenario assumes both are met.
verdict.evidence_span_a: bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit: a) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing geven
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Digital-service providers and incident/reporting or detection obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes a concrete incident-reporting duty on an essential or important entity offering a trust service, with a 24-hour fallback deadline and two recipients. Provision B imposes a systems-and-process duty on providers of data-reporting services to check transaction reports and request retransmission; the different operational duties do not require incompatible conduct or duplicate filings.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: An entity can report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority while also maintaining systems that check transaction reports for completeness and errors. Provision B specifies no reporting event, recipient, deadline, or prohibition that would prevent compliance with Provision A; the provisions principally address different actors and duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations concerning an incident that may also constitute a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same incident is both an incident covered by Article 29 and a personal-data breach, the essential or important entity must submit the Article 29 progress/final report, while a processor must separately inform the controller without unreasonable delay. The duties concern different communications and potentially different timing: Article 29 requires a final report within one month after the incident is handled, whereas Article 33 requires prompt notification to the controller.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed: the actor can promptly inform the controller and later submit the required progress or final report. Article 29 does not prohibit the earlier GDPR notification, and Article 33 does not state that its notification replaces the report to the CSIRT or competent authority; the duties therefore appear cumulative rather than mutually incompatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company is both an essential or important entity and a processor. A cyberattack causes an incident that is also a personal-data breach. The company must inform the controller 'zonder onredelijke vertraging' under Article 33 and must also submit the Article 29 progress or final report concerning the incident, ultimately 'binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld'. Informing the controller does not discharge the separate Article 29 reporting duty, and the texts shown do not identify how the two reporting processes or clocks interact.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or submitting information to authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 72 hours. Provision B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application for notification to the notifying authority; if the same organisation falls within both categories, these are submissions to potentially different authorities, but they concern different triggers and purposes rather than the same event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct duties on different actors and on different triggers: A concerns incident reporting after a significant incident, while B concerns an application for notification by a conformity-assessment body. Nothing in either text says that one filing substitutes for the other, and an organisation can comply with both independently.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a qualifying ICT or personal-data incident by financial-sector entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying personal-data breach must be reported to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours of awareness, while B requires the listed financial-sector entities to make the Article 19 notification also to the designated sectoral CSIRT. The recipients are different, and nothing in the shown provisions says that notifying one recipient satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the same incident can be reported to both the Article 55 supervisory authority and the designated financial-sector CSIRT. B does not set a conflicting deadline, prohibit the GDPR notification, or make the CSIRT notification an alternative to it.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank, acting as controller, discovers a security incident that constitutes a personal-data breach and also triggers the Article 19 ICT-incident notification. It must notify the Article 55 competent supervisory authority within 72 hours and separately make the Article 19 notification to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors; the provisions shown provide no common recipient or rule coordinating the two filings or their timing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant incidents affecting the provision of trust services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A expressly requires a report to both the CSIRT and the competent authority, whereas the operative exception in provision B requires reporting to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. If “or” means the provider may choose only one recipient, the same incident could require two filings under A but only one under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose compatible 24-hour reporting duties on the same trust-service provider for the same type of significant incident. Provision B can be read as setting the NIS2 reporting route, while provision A independently requires notification to both listed recipients; the texts do not expressly say that B’s “or” discharges A’s additional recipient requirement, but the recipients are the same institutional bodies and the deadlines are identical.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider learns at 10:00 that a significant incident affects its trust service. Under A it must promptly file the incident with both its CSIRT and competent authority. Under B’s operative norm it must report the incident within 24 hours to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. If the provider reports only to the competent authority at 11:00, it complies with B’s stated alternative but not A; if it reports to both, the texts leave unresolved whether the second filing is required despite B’s “or.”
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive unresolved point is whether provision B’s phrase “bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit” establishes an exclusive alternative recipient and thereby discharges the separate duty in A to report to both recipients, or merely describes the NIS2 reporting channel without overriding A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security, integrity, misuse, or serious incidents involving electronic services or AI testing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify Onze Minister immediately of a security or integrity breach, or misuse of access, involving its own electronic service. B separately requires every serious incident identified during real-world testing to be reported to the national market-surveillance authority; if the same event satisfies both triggers, the recipients differ and one notification cannot obviously discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers and may apply to different actors and activities: A concerns an organisation's own electronic service, while B concerns serious incidents during real-world testing of a high-risk AI system. Even when both apply, each filing can be made independently, so the duties are cumulatively satisfiable rather than mutually incompatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An aangewezen organisatie conducts real-world testing of a high-risk AI system as a public electronic service. During the testing, the system suffers a serious security breach that is also an incident involving the integrity of the organisation's own electronic service. The organisation must notify Onze Minister onverwijld under A and report the serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority under B; notifying one recipient does not notify the other, and B also requires immediate risk-mitigation or suspension measures.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed for the reporting classification. The decisive facts are that the same incident can trigger both provisions and that the specified recipients differ. The texts do not establish that a report to one authority substitutes for a report to the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting certain AI or ICT incidents by financial-sector entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an immediate report, at the latest within two days after awareness, for a widespread infringement or serious incident. B requires specified financial-sector entities to make an additional report to the designated sectoral CSIRT, so the same incident could trigger both an AI serious-incident report and a CSIRT report to a different recipient.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The shown text of A does not identify the recipient because it incorporates the reporting duty from Article 73(1), while B expressly refers to reports under Article 19 and also mentions a voluntary report. The provisions may therefore concern different triggering regimes or filings, and the excerpts do not conclusively establish that one identical incident must be reported under both duties.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank operates a high-risk AI system and becomes aware of an incident that qualifies both as a serious incident under Article 73 and as an ICT incident reportable under Article 19. The bank must make the Article 73 report immediately and no later than two days after awareness, while also making the Article 19 report to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors; reporting to the market-surveillance authority under Article 73 does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate CSIRT filing.
verdict.missing_reference: The full text of Article 19 and Article 73(1), including the Article 73 recipient and the precise Article 19 trigger, would confirm the overlap and whether the Article 19 report is mandatory for the same incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents that may simultaneously constitute a GDPR personal-data breach and a significant incident affecting a trust service.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A controller must report a qualifying personal-data breach to the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours, while a trust-service provider must report a qualifying significant incident affecting its trust services within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority. If one incident satisfies both triggers, the provisions require separate reports to potentially different recipients, and the NIS2 report does not state that it discharges the GDPR notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both duties can be performed cumulatively: the provider can submit the NIS2 report within 24 hours and the GDPR report within 72 hours. If the competent authority is the same practical recipient, the filings might be coordinated, but the texts shown do not establish that one filing legally substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider discovers that a cyberattack has caused unauthorised access to stored personal data, creating a risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms, and the attack has significant consequences for the provider’s trust services. The provider must report the significant incident within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority under Article 23, while also reporting the personal-data breach within 72 hours to the Article 55 GDPR supervisory authority; filing the first report does not, on the texts shown, discharge the second duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the CSIRT or competent authority under Article 23 is legally the same recipient as the Article 55 GDPR supervisory authority, and whether a single coordinated filing is legally accepted as satisfying both notification regimes, is not established. The provisions instead describe distinct reporting duties and recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: In afwijking van de eerste alinea, punt b), meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_subject: Early warning/reporting of a significant incident by an entity to the CSIRT and competent authority
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a 24-hour early-warning duty for a significant incident, and both refer to reporting to a CSIRT or competent authority. A possible tension would arise if Article 26 required a separate warning to both recipients while Article 23 permitted reporting to only one recipient, creating uncertainty about whether one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions describe the same early-warning obligation, with the same trigger, deadline, and recipient framework. Article 26 expressly requires the entity to give the warning to its CSIRT and competent authority, while the selected paragraph of Article 23 requires a trust-service provider to report to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority; the texts do not establish two separate filings to different recipients or incompatible deadlines.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed on the text shown. The apparent difference between “and” in Article 26 and “or, if applicable” in Article 23 does not establish a conflicting duty for the same actor: Article 23’s selected norm applies specifically to a trust-service provider and its applicable reporting channel, whereas Article 26 concerns essential or important entities in the specified sector. Even if an entity were subject to both regimes, the 24-hour deadlines are compatible; the text does not require two distinct reports to different recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: In afwijking van de eerste alinea, punt b), meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting/documentation duties triggered by a personal-data breach and a high-risk AI fundamental-rights assessment
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying personal-data breach must be reported to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours, while completion of the AI assessment must be notified to the market-surveillance authority. If the same operator and incident/system fall within both provisions, the texts identify different recipients and do not say that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggering events and different substantive duties: GDPR reporting follows a personal-data breach, whereas Article 27 reporting follows completion of a fundamental-rights impact assessment for specified high-risk AI uses. An operator can make both notifications, and Article 27 contains its own possible exemption; nothing expressly makes the duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A public-service provider uses a covered high-risk AI system and is both its gebruiksverantwoordelijke and GDPR verwerkingsverantwoordelijke. Before deployment it completes the Article 27 assessment and must notify the markttoezichtautoriteit of the results, while a security incident involving the system causes a personal-data breach that must be reported within 72 hours to the competent toezichthoudende autoriteit. The provider must make two filings to different recipients; the GDPR filing does not, on the text shown, discharge the Article 27 notification, and Article 27 supplies no deadline that resolves how the two duties interact.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 27 itself states that, in the case referred to in Article 46(1), users may be exempt from the notification duty: “In het in artikel 46, lid 1, bedoelde geval kunnen gebruiksverantwoordelijken van de verplichting tot kennisgeving worden vrijgesteld.” Whether that exemption applies is not established here. It does not establish that the GDPR breach-reporting duty substitutes for the Article 27 notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in

verdict.shared_subject: Incident involving personal data and affecting the services of an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity, where applicable, to notify its service recipients without delay about significant incidents affecting service provision. Provision B requires the controller to document every personal-data breach, potentially covering the same event, so the entity may face an additional compliance burden concerning the same incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different objects: A requires notification to service recipients, while B requires documentation for the supervisory authority's compliance monitoring. They are cumulative rather than contradictory; documenting the breach does not replace notifying recipients, and notifying recipients does not replace the required documentation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen. Die documentatie stelt de toezichthoudende autoriteit in staat de naleving van dit artikel te controleren.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory obligations involving authorities, but not the same triggering event or filing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity offering a trust service to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B requires conformity-assessment bodies to submit an application for notification to the notifying authority; if the same organisation falls within both categories, it would have separate obligations to different authorities, but the provisions do not make the application a substitute for the incident report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts, actors, and triggers: A concerns incident reporting by an entity offering a trust service, while B concerns an application for notification by a conformity-assessment body. Nothing in either text requires the same event to be reported under both provisions, and the B obligation has no incident deadline that could conflict with A's 24-hour deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: A significant incident occurring during real-world testing of a high-risk AI system that adversely affects service provision
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident could trigger two distinct immediate communications by the same entity: A requires informing the recipients of its services, while B requires reporting every serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority. These are different recipients and B does not say that reporting to the authority substitutes for informing service recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can promptly inform affected service recipients and separately report the serious incident to the market-surveillance authority. They regulate different communications and do not impose incompatible content, timing, or recipient requirements.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk AI system is being tested under real-world conditions by an essential or important entity. A serious incident occurs that significantly adversely affects the provision of the entity’s services and therefore also qualifies as a significant incident under A. The entity must inform its service recipients 'onverwijld' and report the same serious incident to the 'nationale markttoezichtautoriteit' under B; filing with the authority does not inform the service recipients, and informing the recipients does not satisfy the authority-reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting/documentation duties of an entity or AI-system user
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report during an ongoing incident and a final report within one month after the incident is resolved. B requires a qualifying AI-system user to notify the market-surveillance authority of the fundamental-rights-impact assessment results, potentially creating two communications if the same actor and circumstances fall within both regimes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggering events and different subject matters: A concerns an incident and reporting to recipients identified in the referenced provision, while B concerns the results of a fundamental-rights-impact assessment for certain high-risk AI systems and notification to the market-surveillance authority. Neither provision prevents the other filing, and the texts do not establish that the same event triggers both duties or that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk governance and communication concerning incidents in a financial or other essential/important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity, where applicable, to inform its service recipients without delay about significant incidents affecting service provision. Provision B requires the governing body to establish internal corporate reporting channels for obtaining information about specified ICT matters, including at least serious ICT-related incidents and their consequences; this could appear to create overlapping incident-communication duties with different audiences.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different objects and recipients: A is an external notification duty to service recipients, while B is an internal governance duty to establish channels enabling the governing body to obtain information. B does not require a filing to an authority or otherwise prohibit or replace notification under A, so both duties can be performed cumulatively without conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over:

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by essential or important entities and subsequent aggregated reporting by the central contact point
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern reporting information about incidents, and a significant incident may ultimately be reflected in both an entity's final/progress report and the central contact point's periodic report to Enisa. However, the duties are imposed on different actors and serve different reporting functions: provision A requires the entity to report to its CSIRT and competent authority, while provision B requires the central contact point to submit an aggregated report to Enisa every three months.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with cumulatively. The entity submits its incident-specific progress or final report within the deadline in provision A, and the central contact point later incorporates anonymised and aggregated information about reported incidents into its separate periodic submission to Enisa under provision B; neither deadline or recipient discharges the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het centrale contactpunt dient om de drie maanden bij Enisa een samenvattend verslag in met geanonimiseerde en geaggregeerde gegevens

verdict.shared_subject: Incident involving personal data in a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same event, but they impose different communications: provision A requires notifying the affected person without delay, while provision B requires a serious-incident notification by a stated deadline. If provision B's notification is to a different recipient or is otherwise a separate filing, one notification would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts shown do not identify a recipient for provision B, and provision B may concern a regulatory serious-incident report rather than a notification to the affected person. The duties can therefore be performed cumulatively; moreover, A's immediate individual notification is not incompatible with B's ten-day deadline.
verdict.missing_reference: The provision or paragraph specifying the recipient and content of the serious-incident notification under Article 73 (particularly Article 73(1), and any applicable provisions identifying the competent authority) is needed to determine whether B requires a separate filing from A's notification to the affected person.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis
verdict.evidence_span_b: doch uiterlijk tien dagen na de datum waarop de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity that is both subject to the NIS2-style obligation and a provider processing personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident could simultaneously be a significant incident affecting a trust service and a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect individuals. Provision A requires a report to the CSIRT and competent authority, while provision B separately requires notice to each affected data subject; one communication cannot discharge both duties because the recipients differ.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties address different reporting functions and can be performed cumulatively: the entity can promptly notify the CSIRT and competent authority under A and separately notify affected individuals under B. There is no textual incompatibility between the deadlines or contents, and A's 24-hour deadline does not replace B's individual notification duty.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider suffers one cyberattack that both significantly disrupts its trust service and exposes customers' personal data, with likely adverse effects on their privacy. It must report the significant incident within 24 hours to its CSIRT and competent authority, while also notifying each affected data subject without delay; reporting to the authorities does not notify the individuals, and notifying the individuals does not satisfy the authority reports.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: Documentation/evaluation of ICT risk management and reporting concerning serious ICT incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be engaged by the same serious ICT-related incident: Provision A requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated, while Provision B requires a serious-incident notification within a specified period. An operator might therefore face two incident-related compliance actions with different content and timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are materially different and cumulative rather than conflicting. Provision A concerns documenting and evaluating the risk-management framework and supplying an evaluation report to the competent authority only if requested; Provision B concerns notifying market-surveillance authorities of serious incidents, with the relevant recipient and trigger supplied by paragraph 1. Performing the incident notification does not purport to replace the framework evaluation, and the framework evaluation does not purport to replace the incident notification.
verdict.missing_reference: The exact recipient and scope of Provision B are stated in Article 73(1), which is supplied as context; no additional provision is needed to conclude that the two shown duties are different. The text does not establish that the same actor must make two reports to different recipients for the same event.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt ten minste eenmaal per jaar, of periodiek in het geval van micro-ondernemingen, gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd, alsook wanneer zich ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten voordoen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Melding aan verschillende ontvangers van hetzelfde mogelijk overlappende ICT-incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Een financiële entiteit kan één incident hebben dat zowel een significant incident onder A als een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident met gevolgen voor cliënten onder B is. Dan vereist A onverwijlde melding aan het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B een afzonderlijke onverwijlde kennisgeving aan de cliënten vereist; de ene kennisgeving vervangt de andere niet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen zijn inhoudelijk cumulatief en kunnen zonder tegenstrijdigheid naast elkaar worden nageleefd: de entiteit meldt aan de bevoegde autoriteit of het CSIRT en informeert daarnaast haar cliënten. Er is geen onverenigbare termijn, verboden handeling of bepaling dat één melding de andere vervangt.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een financiële entiteit onder beide instrumenten ontdekt een cyberincident dat haar kritieke ICT-systemen ernstig treft, aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor haar dienstverlening en de financiële belangen van cliënten raakt. Zij moet onverwijld een melding doen aan haar CSIRT of bevoegde autoriteit én onverwijld haar cliënten informeren; een melding aan de eerste ontvanger voldoet niet aan de afzonderlijke kennisgevingsplicht jegens de cliënten.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving an AI system supplied as a public electronic communications service
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same security breach could adversely affect personal-data protection and also qualify as a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system. Provision A requires immediate notice to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, while provision B concerns a separate incident notification under Article 73, with an immediate trigger and a maximum period of 15 days; the contextual paragraph 1 identifies market-surveillance authorities as recipients, so one filing would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: the actor can notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately under A and make the Article 73 notification to the relevant market-surveillance authority under B. The texts do not say that either notification substitutes for the other, and the different regulatory purposes and recipients support treating them as separate duties rather than a single report with a stricter deadline.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An AI system with a high-risk classification is supplied as part of a public electronic communications service. A security breach in that service both adversely affects the protection of personal data processed for the service and constitutes a serious incident causally linked to the AI system. The provider must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately under A and separately notify the market-surveillance authority under Article 73; notifying the first authority does not satisfy the second duty, and Article 73's 15-day outer limit does not remove A's immediate-notification obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident detection and reporting involving regulated digital or AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires data-reporting-service providers to operate systems that detect omissions and apparent errors in transaction reports and request retransmission; it does not itself impose an incident-reporting duty. Provision B imposes a separate, time-limited serious-incident notification duty, but only for the actors and AI systems within Article 73's scope and for the defined incidents.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable obligations: A concerns automated completeness/error checking and retransmission requests for transaction reports, while B concerns notifying market-surveillance authorities of widespread breaches or serious incidents. Nothing in A forbids or replaces the notification required by B, and A contains no reporting recipient or deadline that could conflict with B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij een wijdverbreide inbreuk of een ernstig incident, zoals gedefinieerd in artikel 3, punt 49), b), de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde melding onmiddellijk gedaan, doch uiterlijk twee dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Operational obligations of regulated digital-service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a trust-service provider to report a qualifying significant incident within 24 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B requires data-reporting-service providers to operate systems capable of checking transaction reports, but it imposes no incident-reporting duty, recipient, or deadline; therefore it does not create a second filing that could conflict with A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties on potentially different categories of provider: A concerns reporting significant incidents affecting trust services, while B concerns the functionality of systems used by data-reporting-service providers. A provider subject to both can maintain the required detection systems and separately make the required incident report within 24 hours.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van datarapporteringsdiensten beschikken daarnaast over systemen die transactiemeldingen doeltreffend op volledigheid kunnen controleren, omissies en aperte fouten kunnen opsporen en om hernieuwde transmissie van die meldingen kunnen verzoeken.

verdict.shared_subject: Governance, ICT-risk management and incident-related information for entities potentially subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a trust-service provider to report a qualifying significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority within 24 hours. Provision B requires a financial entity's management body to establish internal corporate reporting channels for information about ICT-service-provider arrangements and serious ICT-related incidents, so one might argue that an incident must be both externally reported and internally channelled under different arrangements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties rather than conflicting reporting duties: A is an external incident-notification obligation for a trust-service provider, while B is an internal governance and information-channel duty imposed on the management body of a financial entity. Provision B specifies neither an external recipient nor a separate filing deadline, so A's report does not purport to replace or discharge B, and the two can readily be satisfied together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt een verlener van vertrouwensdiensten significante incidenten die gevolgen hebben voor de verlening van zijn vertrouwensdiensten onverwijld, en in elk geval binnen 24 uur nadat hij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident, bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_subject: Authorities' submissions by organisations that may be both a personal-data controller and a conformity-assessment body
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same organisation experiences a personal-data breach while it is also a conformity-assessment body, Article 33 requires a breach notification to the competent supervisory authority, while Article 29 requires an application for notification to the notifying authority. The recipients and triggering events differ, so one filing would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different triggers: Article 33 concerns a qualifying personal-data breach by a controller, whereas Article 29 concerns a conformity-assessment body's application for notification. Nothing in either text says that an Article 29 application is a breach notification or that the two duties substitute for one another; they can therefore be performed cumulatively when both conditions occur.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Conformiteitsbeoordelingsinstanties dienen een verzoek om aanmelding in bij de aanmeldende autoriteit van de lidstaat waar zij zijn gevestigd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems that are safety components or devices, where the operator is also a covered financial-sector entity under the cybersecurity regime.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires reporting the relevant serious incident to the designated national competent authority in the Member State where it occurred. B separately requires covered financial entities to make the Article 19 report, including the voluntary report, also to the designated sectoral CSIRT, so the same incident may require two filings to different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed without contradiction: the actor can report to the national competent authority under A and also to the sectoral CSIRT under B. Neither provision states that reporting to one recipient substitutes for reporting to the other, and no incompatible deadlines are specified.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk AI system used as a safety component in a medical device causes a serious incident in the Netherlands, and its operator is a bank covered by B. The operator must report the incident to “de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan” under A and also make the Article 19 report to “het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt” under B; filing with one recipient does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate duty to file with the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: None shown. The decisive point is that the provisions identify different recipients and do not establish that either filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: wordt het incident gemeld bij de nationale bevoegde autoriteit die daartoe is aangewezen door de lidstaten waar dat incident zich heeft voorgedaan
verdict.evidence_span_b: tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt

verdict.shared_subject: Notification of a security or personal-data breach by an organisation/provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident may require the same actor to notify the Minister and provide all necessary information, while B may require notification of the affected person. These are different recipients and the texts do not say that notifying one recipient satisfies the other, so both notifications may be required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily operate cumulatively: the actor can notify the Minister immediately under A and the affected person immediately under B. Neither provision forbids the other notification, and both use the same deadline, 'onverwijld'; the duties therefore do not impose incompatible obligations.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation providing an electronic public service suffers a personal-data breach that is also a breach of the security or integrity of its own electronic service and is likely to adversely affect the privacy of the affected person. It must notify Onze Minister 'onverwijld' under A and separately notify the affected person 'onverwijld' under B; notifying the Minister does not notify the affected person, and vice versa.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap from the texts shown. Provision B's exceptions in paragraphs 4 and 5 could affect whether B applies in a particular case, but they do not establish that notification to the Minister discharges notification to the affected person.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst
