verdict.shared_subject: De verplichting om een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling (DPIA) uit te voeren bij hoog-risicoverwerking of hoog-risico-AI.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 35 verplicht de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een DPIA uit te voeren wanneer de verwerking waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt. Artikel 26 verplicht de gebruiksverantwoordelijke van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem de op grond van artikel 13 verstrekte informatie te gebruiken om aan diezelfde DPIA-verplichting te voldoen; dit kan vragen oproepen over de verhouding tussen de AI-informatie en de bredere inhoudelijke eisen van artikel 35.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 26 verbiedt of vervangt artikel 35 niet, maar verwijst er juist uitdrukkelijk naar en schrijft slechts voor welke informatie bij het nakomen ervan moet worden gebruikt. De bepalingen kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: de gebruiksverantwoordelijke gebruikt artikel-13-informatie én voert een DPIA uit die aan artikel 35 voldoet.
verdict.evidence_span_a: voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: gebruiken gebruiksverantwoordelijken van AI-systemen met een hoog risico de informatie die op grond van artikel 13 van deze verordening wordt verstrekt om hun verplichting na te komen om een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling uit te voeren op grond van artikel 35 van Verordening (EU) 2016/679

verdict.shared_subject: Personal-data breaches and regulatory enforcement
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may concern an operator involved in a personal-data breach, but they regulate different things: Article 51 governs how authorities determine sanctions or corrective measures, while Article 11.3a governs the contents of a breach notification. There is no textual requirement in Article 51 that conflicts with, limits, or substitutes for the notification contents required by Article 11.3a.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly be complied with together: the operator can submit a notification containing the required breach information, while the competent authority separately considers intent, seriousness, responsibility, cooperation, and other factors when deciding any sanction or corrective measure. They address different actors, functions, and stages without incompatible duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteiten houden bij het bepalen van het type en de omvang van een op grond van artikel 50 te nemen administratieve strafmaatregel of corrigerende maatregel rekening met de vraag, in hoeverre de inbreuk opzettelijk is, dan wel het resultaat is van nalatigheid
verdict.evidence_span_b: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: A high-risk processing activity involving a high-risk AI system before it is placed on the market
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply before the relevant activity proceeds: the GDPR requires prior consultation with the supervisory authority where the DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while the AI Act requires the importer to verify conformity before placing a high-risk AI system on the market. The strongest possible tension is practical sequencing or delay, because consultation may need to occur before processing while import checks must occur before market placement, but neither text forbids satisfying both duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different actors, triggers, and actions: the GDPR duty is imposed on the controller and concerns prior consultation about high-risk processing, whereas the AI Act duty is imposed on the importer and concerns checking conformity documentation and procedures before placing a high-risk system on the market. An importer and controller can comply with both independently; neither provision says that one consultation, verification, or deadline substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Alvorens een AI-systeem met een hoog risico in de handel wordt gebracht, zorgen de importeurs ervoor dat het systeem in overeenstemming is met deze verordening door na te gaan of:

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and processing of personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same AI system: GDPR Article 35 requires a data-protection impact assessment before processing where the processing is likely to create a high risk, while Article 16(a) requires providers of high-risk AI systems to ensure compliance with Section 2. The strongest possible tension is that the two regimes use different high-risk triggers and impose different compliance duties, potentially leaving uncertainty about whether an AI system is in scope under both.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and independently satisfiable: a controller can conduct the required impact assessment before processing and an AI provider can ensure compliance with Section 2. Article 16 does not state that compliance with Section 2 replaces or overrides the GDPR assessment duty, and Article 35 does not prohibit or make compliance with Article 16 impossible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens.

Nothing in the texts makes the required cooperation mutually exclusive or sets incompatible limits, recipients, or deadlines.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incidents by financial-sector entities

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are independently satisfiable because they are triggered in different proceedings and require different documents to be provided to different recipients. Nothing in either provision prohibits or substitutes for compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Bewaring en verwijdering van persoonsgegevens/documentatie door een verwerker of importeur
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 28, onder g, verplicht de verwerker na afloop van de diensten bestaande kopieën te verwijderen, terwijl artikel 23 de importeur verplicht bepaalde documentatie tien jaar te bewaren. Als dezelfde actor in beide hoedanigheden optreedt en de gebruiksaanwijzing of EU-conformiteitsverklaring persoonsgegevens bevat, kan verwijdering botsen met de bewaarplicht.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen richten zich primair tot verschillende actoren en hebben verschillende objecten en triggers: artikel 28 ziet op persoonsgegevens na beëindiging van verwerkingsdiensten, terwijl artikel 23 ziet op documentatie die een importeur van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem moet bewaren. Bovendien bevat artikel 28 zelf een uitzondering wanneer opslag wettelijk verplicht is, zodat een toepasselijke bewaarplicht van artikel 23 de verwijderingsplicht niet noodzakelijk schendt; zonder vaststelling dat de te bewaren documenten persoonsgegevens zijn en dat de importeur tevens verwerker is, is er geen conflict.

De getoonde teksten stellen echter niet vast dat artikel 23 een dergelijke verplichting tot opslag van persoonsgegevens oplevert, noch dat de documenten persoonsgegevens bevatten.

A CSIRT can perform its monitoring duty while an ETA performs its reporting and warning duty, with no conflicting deadline, recipient, prohibition or benchmark stated.

If the same operator and event somehow fell within both provisions, the duties would concern different subject matters and recipients, suggesting cumulative obligations rather than one filing satisfying the other.

Nothing in either text makes compliance with one duty impossible or substitutes one notification for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of high-risk AI systems involving personal-data processing and human oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives a data subject an individual right to object to processing based on GDPR Article 6(1)(e) or (f), requiring the controller to stop unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Provision B requires high-risk-AI deployers to assign human oversight to qualified natural persons, but it does not itself address whether processing must stop after an objection; an apparent tension could arise if oversight is treated as requiring continued processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties on different aspects of conduct: Article 21 governs an individual objection and the controller’s resulting processing decision, while Article 26 governs the organisational assignment and qualification of human oversight. A deployer can assign compliant human oversight and still stop or restrict processing when Article 21 requires it; nothing in Provision B overrides or substitutes for the individual right.

verdict.shared_subject: Significante incidenten bij essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen betrekking hebben op hetzelfde incident, maar leggen ogenschijnlijk verschillende mededelingen op: A vereist onverwijlde kennisgeving aan de ontvangers van de diensten, terwijl B een eindverslag binnen één maand na afhandeling vereist. Als dit afzonderlijke verplichtingen zijn, kan een entiteit dus zowel onmiddellijk de dienstontvangers moeten informeren als later een eindverslag moeten indienen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen richten zich op verschillende handelingen en ontvangers: A betreft een onverwijlde kennisgeving aan dienstontvangers wanneer een significant incident hun dienstverlening nadelig kan beïnvloeden, terwijl B een voortgangs- of eindverslag aan een niet nader genoemde instantie betreft. Niets in de getoonde teksten bepaalt dat de kennisgeving uit A het verslag uit B vervangt, of dat beide dezelfde filing zijn; de verplichtingen kunnen daarom cumulatief en afzonderlijk worden nagekomen.
verdict.missing_reference: De tekst van artikel 29 die de ontvanger, het indieningsmoment van het oorspronkelijke eindverslag en de verhouding tot de kennisgeving onder artikel 23 bepaalt, ontbreekt. Die informatie zou nodig zijn om vast te stellen of B dezelfde melding aan dezelfde ontvanger betreft of een afzonderlijk verslag verlangt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents and the roles of competent authorities and the CSIRT
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern responses to cybersecurity incidents, but they impose duties on different actors and operate at different stages: the competent authority must consider prior infringements when taking enforcement measures, while the CSIRT may respond to incidents. Nothing in either text makes the CSIRT’s response incompatible with the authority’s enforcement assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are fully cumulative and directed to different institutional actors. The CSIRT can respond to an incident, while the competent authority separately considers relevant previous infringements when imposing or taking enforcement measures; neither duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: elke veroorzaakte materiële of immateriële schade, met inbegrip van elke financiële of economische schade, effecten op andere diensten en het aantal getroffen gebruikers
verdict.evidence_span_b: indien van toepassing, het reageren op incidenten en verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both NIS2 Article 23 and DORA Article 19
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same serious/significant ICT incident, but the extracted norms impose different communications: A requires a final incident report after the incident is handled, while B requires immediate notification of affected clients. If the same financial entity and incident fall within both regimes, the entity must make both communications, to different recipients and on different clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are individually satisfiable and address different recipients and purposes: A concerns a final report to the CSIRT or competent authority, whereas B concerns informing clients about the incident and mitigation measures. There is no contradiction, because making the client notification does not prevent or replace the later regulatory final report.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity experiences a significant ICT incident that is also a serious ICT-related incident affecting clients’ financial interests, and the incident continues for several days. The entity must submit the NIS2 final report to the CSIRT or competent authority no later than one month after handling the incident, while it must notify affected clients without delay under DORA; notifying the clients does not discharge the separate filing with the CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uiterlijk één maand na de indiening van het in punt b) bedoelde incidentmelding, een eindverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken

verdict.shared_subject: Bevoegde autoriteiten en hun handhavingsmaatregelen bij inbreuken
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen raken aan handhaving na een inbreuk: A verplicht autoriteiten rekening te houden met eerdere inbreuken, terwijl B hun de bevoegdheid geeft een inbreukmakende gedraging te laten staken en herhaling te voorkomen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat A een beoordelingsfactor voorschrijft waar B slechts een bevoegdheidsgrond voor een maatregel formuleert, maar dat levert geen onverenigbare norm op.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen regelen verschillende, cumulatief verenigbare aspecten van handhaving. A schrijft een factor voor die bij het nemen van bepaalde maatregelen moet worden meegewogen; B verleent bevoegdheid om een gedraging te doen staken en niet te herhalen, zonder te verbieden dat eerdere inbreuken worden meegewogen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: elke veroorzaakte materiële of immateriële schade, met inbegrip van elke financiële of economische schade, effecten op andere diensten en het aantal getroffen gebruikers
verdict.evidence_span_b: natuurlijke of rechtspersoon bij officieel besluit gelasten de gedraging die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening, te staken en deze gedraging niet te herhalen

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns exchanging and discussing incident information within the CSIRT network when requested by an affected member. Provision B concerns the deadline for making a notification about a proposed transaction, including a special deadline for a public bid involving a listed telecommunications party; the texts identify no common event, actor, recipient, or duty whose performance could conflict.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct obligations in different regulatory domains: A governs operational cybersecurity cooperation among CSIRTs, while B governs a transaction-related notification deadline. An actor could comply with both whenever it falls within both scopes, because exchanging incident information does not prevent making the required notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk dat mogelijkerwijs gevolgen ondervindt van een incident, het uitwisselen en bespreken van informatie over dat incident en de daarmee samenhangende cyberdreigingen, risico’s en kwetsbaarheden
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien het voornemen betrekking heeft op een openbaar bod op een beursgenoteerde telecommunicatiepartij wordt de melding gedaan uiterlijk gelijktijdig met de aankondiging van een openbaar bod

verdict.shared_subject: Pre-deployment documentation and assessment obligations for high-risk processing or AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose pre-deployment documentation obligations for activities involving high risk, but they require different substantive content: the GDPR assessment concerns risks to natural persons’ rights and freedoms and measures addressing those risks, while the AI Act documentation demonstrates conformity with that Act and contains Annex IV elements. An operator might therefore be uncertain whether one document can serve both purposes or whether the two benchmarks overlap.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative obligations with different triggers, addressees and purposes, not incompatible commands. A controller can perform the GDPR data-protection impact assessment before processing and separately prepare and update the AI Act technical documentation before placing the high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service; neither provision says that one document or assessment substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Pre-deployment documentation and assessment duties for high-risk processing or AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose pre-deployment documentation duties, but they require different documents for different purposes: a GDPR data-protection impact assessment concerns likely high risks to natural persons’ rights and freedoms, while the AI Act technical documentation demonstrates conformity with that Act and supplies information for conformity assessment. An operator may therefore need to prepare both, but the texts do not make one document substitute for the other or create incompatible requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can readily be satisfied together: the controller can conduct the GDPR impact assessment before processing and separately prepare and update the AI Act technical documentation before placing the high-risk AI system on the market or putting it into service. They address different subject matters, contents, and regulatory purposes, with no prohibition, incompatible deadline, or stated substitution rule.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory powers and information duties in EU digital-law instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern regulatory compliance activity, and a notified body might also be a critical ICT third-party provider in a factual scenario. However, provision A concerns the lead overseer’s competence to impose a coercive fine after non-compliance with specified measures, while provision B concerns a notified body’s conditional duty to inform the notifying authority on request; neither prescribes conduct incompatible with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of norms on different actors and address different conduct: A authorises a lead overseer to impose a coercive fine, whereas B requires notified bodies to provide information about conformity-assessment activities when requested. A notified body can provide the requested information and, if separately subject to A, comply with any measures or pay a fine; nothing in either text forbids the other duty or makes one discharge or override the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant incident and supplying information in an early warning
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to report every significant incident without delay to a CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. Provision B separately requires information to be supplied in the early warning, but the shown text does not identify a separate recipient, deadline, or filing distinct from the Article 23 report; therefore it is most naturally an additional-content requirement within the same reporting process, not a second filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be satisfied cumulatively: the entity can make the Article 23 report without delay and include the responsible reporting officer’s contact details in the early warning. Nothing in the shown provisions requires two reports to different recipients or establishes a second clock, and Article 23’s reference to an early warning supports treating B as part of the Article 23 reporting procedure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt de entiteit de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-incident management, root-cause analysis and incident reporting by financial or essential/important entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to register incidents and establish processes ensuring that underlying causes are identified, documented and removed. Provision B separately requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report containing the likely threat or root cause, but it does not expressly say that this report or its submission satisfies A's process and remediation duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary obligations rather than incompatible ones: A concerns ongoing internal incident-management and remediation processes, while B concerns the contents and timing of a final report. An entity subject to both can maintain the required processes, remediate causes, and submit one final report to both named recipients; no conflicting deadline, prohibition, or alternative recipient structure is shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, teneinde ervoor te zorgen dat onderliggende oorzaken worden opgespoord, gedocumenteerd en weggenomen om dergelijke incidenten te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:

verdict.shared_subject: Nationale cyberbeveiliging en respons op cyberincidenten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A obliges CSIRTs to monitor and analyse cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents at national level. Provision B assigns the Minister responsibility for establishing a national plan for large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crisis response; one might argue that both provisions concern national-level incident preparedness and response, potentially creating overlapping institutional responsibilities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, compatible functions on different actors: CSIRTs perform operational monitoring and analysis, while the Minister establishes a strategic national plan. Nothing in either text requires one actor to refrain from the other's activity, and the CSIRT monitoring duty does not conflict with the Minister's planning competence.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister stelt een nationaal plan voor grootschalige cyberbeveiligingsincidenten en crisisrespons als bedoeld in artikel 9, vierde lid, van de NIS2-richtlijn vast.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities/providers subject to both NIS2 and the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident under Article 23 must be reported without delay to the entity’s CSIRT or competent authority, while an AI Act serious incident must be reported to the market-surveillance authorities. If one incident satisfies both definitions, the same actor faces two reporting duties to different recipients, with Article 23 requiring immediate reporting and Article 73 setting a separate clock of immediately after establishing causation (and in any event within 15 days).
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can each be fulfilled without contradiction: the actor can report the incident promptly to the NIS2 recipient and separately to the AI Act market-surveillance authority. The provisions do not require mutually incompatible content or prohibit the other filing; the burden is cumulative rather than impossible to perform.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk AI system is also an essential or important entity under NIS2. A malfunction of the high-risk AI system causes a serious operational disruption and material losses, making it both a NIS2 “significant incident” and an AI Act “serious incident.” The provider must report it “onverwijld” to its CSIRT or competent authority under Article 23 and also report it to the market-surveillance authority under Article 73, immediately after establishing the causal link and at the latest within 15 days after becoming aware. Filing with the CSIRT or competent authority does not itself constitute the separate filing with the market-surveillance authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Samenwerking en deelname aan Europese cyberbeveiligingsnetwerken
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A verplicht CSIRT’s om deel te nemen aan het CSIRT-netwerk. Provision B verplicht EU-CyCLONe om met datzelfde netwerk samen te werken volgens overeengekomen procedurele regelingen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat de samenwerking of procedures extra verplichtingen voor CSIRT’s meebrengen, maar de getoonde teksten leggen geen onverenigbare verplichting op.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Deelname aan het CSIRT-netwerk door CSIRT’s en samenwerking van EU-CyCLONe met dat netwerk zijn wederzijds verenigbare institutionele rollen. Provision B verbiedt of beperkt de deelnameplicht uit Provision A niet en bepaalt evenmin dat CSIRT’s een andere, daarmee onverenigbare handeling moeten verrichten.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het deelnemen aan het CSIRT-netwerk
verdict.evidence_span_b: EU-CyCLONe werkt samen met het CSIRT-netwerk op basis van overeengekomen procedurele regelingen

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk processing/AI systems and their associated assessment obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose assessment-related obligations for potentially high-risk activities, but they operate at different levels: Article 35 requires the controller to conduct a data-protection impact assessment before processing where the processing likely creates a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms, while Article 43(3) concerns a manufacturer’s optional avoidance of third-party conformity assessment subject to applying specified standards. One might argue that the manufacturer’s standards-based route could be treated as sufficient in place of a separate impact assessment, but Article 43 does not say that.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, independently satisfiable requirements on different actors and with different triggers. A controller can perform the Article 35 impact assessment, while a manufacturer separately uses—or does not use—the Article 43(3) option and, if using it, applies the required harmonised standards or common specifications; neither text exempts or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: kan de fabrikant alleen van die mogelijkheid gebruikmaken als hij ook geharmoniseerde normen of in voorkomend geval gemeenschappelijke specificaties als bedoeld in artikel 41 heeft toegepast, voor alle in afdeling 2 van dit hoofdstuk beschreven voorschriften.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities/providers where an incident may qualify both as a NIS2 significant incident and as a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident under Provision A requires prompt notice to the entity’s service recipients, while Provision B requires a separate notification concerning a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system. If the same event satisfies both triggers, the texts point to different reporting objects and potentially different timing rules, so notifying service recipients under A would not obviously satisfy the market-surveillance notification required by B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can notify service recipients immediately under A and make the notification required by B within its applicable deadline. Provision A’s recipient is expressly the entity’s service recipients, whereas the contextual text for B identifies market-surveillance authorities, so neither duty appears to discharge the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk AI system is also an essential or important entity. A cyber incident significantly disrupts its services and adversely affects service recipients, while also constituting a serious incident involving the high-risk AI system. The provider must notify service recipients “onverwijld” under A and separately notify the market-surveillance authorities under B, with B’s notification due immediately once the causal link or reasonable likelihood is established and in any event within 15 days of awareness; filing the first notice does not make the second filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT-taken bij het reageren op incidenten en het verlenen van bijstand
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide provisions impose a duty on a CSIRT to respond to incidents and provide assistance, but they could appear to differ in wording: provision A refers to 'betrokken essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten', while provision B uses the same categories in the singular formulation. If those formulations had different scopes, an incident involving an entity outside one formulation could create uncertainty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The operative norms are substantively the same: both require, 'indien van toepassing', responding to incidents and providing assistance to affected essential and important entities. Provision B is a national formulation of the same CSIRT task and does not prohibit, limit, or set a conflicting benchmark for the duty in provision A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) het reageren op incidenten en verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten, indien van toepassing;
verdict.evidence_span_b: c. indien van toepassing, het reageren op incidenten en verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit;

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations of potentially overlapping actors
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a financial entity to submit an interim report to the relevant competent authority after its initial notification, within the Article 20 deadlines. Provision B requires a cable provider to notify the municipal mayor or authorised official before public-ground cable-maintenance works, with the authorised official informing the mayor as soon as possible; if the same actor and event somehow fall within both regimes, the filings have different triggers, recipients, and timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate fundamentally different events and actors: A concerns serious ICT-related incidents of financial entities, while B concerns advance notification of cable-maintenance works on public land. Nothing in either text says that one filing substitutes for the other, but ordinarily an actor can comply with both independently, and the texts do not establish a single triggering event covered by both duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a)
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester

verdict.shared_subject: Incident management and reporting by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to establish processes ensuring that incident root causes are identified, documented, and removed, while provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report after an incident is handled. One might argue that documenting root causes under A overlaps with, or could be treated as an alternative to, the report required by B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: A concerns internal incident-management processes and remediation of root causes, whereas B concerns submitting a final report, with a specified deadline, after the incident is resolved. A contains no reporting recipient or deadline and does not state that its documentation substitutes for B's final report; therefore both duties can be performed independently.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, teneinde ervoor te zorgen dat onderliggende oorzaken worden opgespoord, gedocumenteerd en weggenomen om dergelijke incidenten te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification/reporting by regulated entities or providers in connection with ICT or network-security incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose prompt notification duties after a security-related event, using different formulations: A requires notifying clients immediately when a serious ICT incident affects their financial interests, while B requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber as soon as possible when urgent action prevented prior notice. If the same event and recipients are covered, the provisions could appear to impose overlapping clocks and potentially different notification content.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggering events, actors, and notification subjects: A concerns financial entities notifying clients about a serious ICT-related incident and mitigation measures; B concerns a provider notifying the involved subscriber about a specific measure taken under another provision. Even if one event overlaps, the duties can be performed cumulatively, and the texts do not establish that the notifications are separate filings to different recipients or that one deadline conflicts with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer dit wegens de vereiste spoed niet voorafgaand aan het nemen van de maatregel mogelijk is, doet de aanbieder zo snel mogelijk melding van de maatregel.

verdict.shared_subject: Melding van significante cyberdreigingen of significante incidenten door financiële/essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij een entiteit die onder beide bepalingen valt, kan dezelfde gebeurtenis zowel vrijwillig aan een bevoegde autoriteit worden gemeld als onverwijld aan de ontvangers van haar diensten worden meegedeeld. De ontvangers zijn geen bevoegde autoriteit, zodat de ene mededeling de andere niet vervangt; bovendien is A vrijwillig, terwijl B in voorkomend geval verplicht is.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen geen tegenstrijdige inhoud, termijn of verbod op. A laat een financiële entiteit slechts toe om vrijwillig aan een bevoegde autoriteit te melden, terwijl B een afzonderlijke informatieplicht jegens dienstontvangers bevat; beide kunnen naast elkaar worden nageleefd, en A wordt bovendien alleen geactiveerd als de entiteit ervoor kiest te melden.
verdict.decisive_exception: Niet van toepassing. Omdat de melding onder A vrijwillig is, kan een entiteit die geen melding onder A doet volledig aan beide bepalingen voldoen door alleen de verplichte kennisgeving onder B te doen; als zij wel vrijwillig meldt, zijn het twee afzonderlijke, cumulatief uitvoerbare mededelingen aan verschillende ontvangers.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

However, the provisions assign these functions to different actors and do not make either communication substitute for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A obliges CSIRTs to provide early warnings, notifications and announcements to specified recipients about cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents. Provision B obliges the competent authority to acknowledge receipt of a financial entity’s notification or reports; these are distinct duties, performed by different actors, and both can be carried out cumulatively without contradiction.

verdict.shared_subject: Allocation of supervisory competence over compliance with specified statutory provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions allocate supervisory authority, and an activity might appear factually connected to obligations covered by both instruments. If the same conduct fell within both listed scopes, the provisions could raise a practical question about which authority supervises it.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions designate authorities for different legal instruments and expressly defined sets of provisions: Provision A concerns specified articles enforced by officials designated by the Minister in Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, while Provision B assigns ACM supervision over specified chapters and articles of the Data Act, subject to stated exceptions and qualifications. Nothing in the texts requires the same actor to obey incompatible commands or shows overlapping jurisdiction over the same provision; separate supervisory competences can operate cumulatively or independently.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities involved in a personal-data breach and entities covered by the incident-reporting regime
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose reporting duties concerning an incident, and the same incident could potentially trigger both. However, the shown texts do not establish that the same actor is subject to both duties, nor do they identify B's recipient or show that B concerns the same report as A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the processor can inform the controller without unreasonable delay under A, while the essential or important entity can submit a progress report and later a final report under B. Nothing in either text says that one filing substitutes for the other or prohibits the other.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions establishing whether the same actor is both the processor under Article 33 and an essential or important entity under Article 29, whether the same incident triggers both duties, and the recipient/content requirements for Article 29's progress and final reports. Those provisions are needed to determine whether two separate filings to different recipients are required.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of serious ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority, while provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report when the incident is still ongoing at the final-report deadline. If the same entity and incident fall under both regimes, the texts could be read as requiring reports under two instruments, with no stated rule coordinating the recipients or filing mechanics.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not clearly establish two separate, simultaneous filings. Provision A expressly concerns reporting to a competent authority, whereas provision B, as shown, only specifies the replacement of a final report by a progress report and does not identify a recipient or independently define the incident-reporting trigger. The progress report may therefore be part of the reporting sequence under the other regime or an additional cumulative requirement, but the shown text does not establish a dual-recipient or dual-clock conflict.
verdict.missing_reference: The provision identifying the recipient, timing, and relationship of the progress report under BWBR0052872 art. 29 (including the referenced first paragraph and any provisions specifying whether it must be filed separately from a DORA report) is needed to determine whether both filings are required. For provision A, the relevant deadlines are also set by 32022R2554 art. 20, which is referenced but not shown.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and associated data-protection/compliance procedures

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties on different actors and address different assessments: A concerns the controller’s processing and privacy risks, while B concerns completion of AI conformity-assessment procedures by the relevant market-surveillance framework. Nothing in B exempts the controller from A, and nothing in A prevents the conformity procedures from being completed promptly.

verdict.shared_subject: Processing of personal data by a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives a data subject an individual right to object to processing based on Article 6(1)(e) or (f), requiring the controller to stop unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Article 14 requires a high-risk AI system to be designed so that effective human oversight is possible, but that system-level design duty does not itself resolve or override an individual objection right.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties that can both be satisfied: a high-risk AI system can provide effective human oversight while its controller separately handles objections and stops processing unless the Article 21 exception applies. Article 14 neither requires continued processing nor deems human oversight sufficient to defeat the objection.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 21 itself contains the decisive exception: processing may continue only where the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds overriding the data subject’s interests, rights and freedoms, or grounds relating to legal claims.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke staakt de verwerking van de persoonsgegevens tenzij hij dwingende gerechtvaardigde gronden voor de verwerking aanvoert die zwaarder wegen dan de belangen, rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkene of die verband houden met de instelling, uitoefening of onderbouwing van een rechtsvordering.

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingsplichten van een aanbieder bij verschillende gebeurtenissen en maatregelen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen verplichten een aanbieder tot een melding en gebruiken mogelijk overlappende spoedtaal. Als dezelfde gebeurtenis zowel een ernstig AI-incident als aanleiding voor een maatregel tegen een abonnee is, kan de aanbieder bovendien met twee meldingsmomenten worden geconfronteerd.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zien op verschillende meldingen met verschillende triggers: art. 73 betreft een ernstig incident bij een hoog-risico-AI-systeem, terwijl art. 7.6a een melding aan de betrokken abonnee vereist vóór of zo snel mogelijk na een specifieke maatregel. De teksten tonen geen identieke triggering event, geen verschillende ontvangers die voor hetzelfde incident cumulatief moeten worden bediend, en geen inhoudelijke onverenigbaarheid; beide meldingen kunnen afzonderlijk worden gedaan.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen. Wanneer dit wegens de vereiste spoed niet voorafgaand aan het nemen van de maatregel mogelijk is, doet de aanbieder zo snel mogelijk melding van de maatregel.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of serious/significant ICT incidents by entities subject to both DORA and the Dutch NIS2 implementation law
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the financial entity to prepare the initial notification and reports for submission to the competent authority under Article 19(4), while Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a notification to both its CSIRT and competent authority. If the same entity and incident fall under both regimes, the texts do not expressly say that the DORA report to the competent authority also constitutes the separate CSIRT notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can prepare and submit the DORA report to the relevant competent authority and also submit the NIS2 notification to its CSIRT and competent authority. Provision A itself permits Member States to require additional provision of the reports to CSIRTs, which supports coexistence rather than an impossibility of compliance.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is simultaneously an essential or important entity and suffers an incident qualifying as both a DORA serious ICT-related incident and a NIS2 significant incident. It must prepare the DORA initial notification and reports for the relevant competent authority, while also filing the NIS2 notification “bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” within 72 hours; filing only with the DORA competent authority would not, on the text shown, establish that the separate CSIRT filing was made.

Nothing in either text forbids the other notification or states that one communication discharges the other.

Dat vermoeden wordt echter niet door de teksten geconcretiseerd: artikel 28 ziet op een verwerker die de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke bijstaat, terwijl artikel 16, onder f, het CSIRT betreft en bijstand aan andere CSIRT-netwerkleden regelt.

Artikel 28, lid 3, onder e, verplicht de verwerker, voor zover mogelijk, de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke te helpen bij verzoeken van betrokkenen; artikel 16, onder f, verplicht het CSIRT binnen zijn capaciteiten en bevoegdheden wederzijdse bijstand aan andere CSIRT-leden te verlenen. verdict.shared_subject: Essential or important entities’ communications concerning significant cyber incidents or threats
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same entity and subject matter, but they require communications to different recipients: provision A requires reporting a significant incident to the CSIRT or competent authority, while provision B requires informing potentially affected service recipients about measures and, if necessary, the significant cyber threat. verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different content and recipients and can readily be performed cumulatively: the entity can promptly report the incident to the CSIRT or competent authority and separately inform affected service recipients about protective measures or the threat. verdict.shared_subject: Human oversight of a high-risk AI system and an individual's right to object to certain personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives an individual an invokable right to object, requiring the controller to stop processing unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Article 14(a) requires the high-risk AI system to be supplied so that oversight personnel can understand its relevant capabilities and limitations, which could be viewed as supporting continued monitoring rather than stopping processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties that can readily be satisfied together: the operator can provide oversight personnel with the required understanding while also stopping processing when a valid objection is made, unless Article 21's overriding-grounds exception applies. Article 14(a) does not require continued processing, prohibit objections, or deem system-level understanding sufficient to satisfy the individual's right.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 21 itself contains the relevant exception: processing may continue where the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds that override the data subject's interests, rights and freedoms, or where processing is connected with legal claims. Article 14(a) does not alter or replace that exception.

verdict.shared_subject: Transparency about automated decision-making and human oversight of high-risk AI
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the controller to inform the data subject about the existence of automated decision-making and, at least in the specified cases, its underlying logic, significance, and expected consequences. Provision B requires the high-risk AI system to enable responsible natural persons to understand, monitor, interpret, and override its output; one might argue that these overlapping transparency and oversight expectations create uncertainty about whether information must be directed to the data subject or supplied through human overseers.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties on different objects and recipients: A is an information duty owed by the controller to the data subject, while B is a system-design duty enabling human oversight of high-risk AI. The controller can satisfy both by giving the data subject the information required by A and ensuring that responsible overseers can perform the actions required by B; neither provision says that compliance with one substitutes for or prevents compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity subject to both the GDPR and the Dutch cybersecurity reporting regime
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same personal-data incident can trigger two mandatory reports by the same entity: a GDPR notification to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours of awareness, and a separate final report to both its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the Article 27 notification. The recipients and reporting contents differ, so filing the GDPR notification does not discharge the separate CSIRT/final-report duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can both be performed without contradiction because they have different deadlines and can concern different information: the earlier GDPR notification can be followed by the later, more detailed final report. The texts do not impose incompatible content, timing, or recipient requirements; they instead require cumulative filings under different regimes.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity suffers an incident involving personal data and becomes aware of it on 1 June. Because the breach is likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms, it must notify the Article 55 supervisory authority by 4 June under Provision A. The same incident is also reportable under Article 27, so the entity must subsequently submit, by the applicable one-month deadline, a detailed final report to both its CSIRT and competent authority under Provision B. The first notification does not constitute the required final report to the CSIRT and does not contain all of the specified final-report information.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious incidents or personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A national competent authority must notify the Commission immediately of every serious incident, while the provider must include specified consequences and remedial measures in a notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority. If one event is both a serious incident and a personal-data breach, the regimes impose different reporting duties to different recipients, and the shown text does not say that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: the competent authority can notify the Commission immediately, while the provider separately notifies the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens with the required content. They concern different actors and do not prescribe incompatible content or deadlines.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider's serious incident causes a personal-data breach. The national competent authority must notify the Commission immediately, while the provider must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens and include the consequences for the personal data and the measures proposed or taken. Sending the provider's notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens does not discharge the authority's separate notification to the Commission.

verdict.shared_subject: Documenting and notifying personal-data breaches

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and directed to different functions, not contradictory: documenting every breach under A does not prevent or replace notifying the affected person under B, and notifying the person under B does not prevent or replace maintaining the documentation required by A. The provisions also do not require two reports to different authorities; B is a notification to the affected person, whereas A is documentation that enables supervisory review.

verdict.shared_subject: Significant incidents or cyberthreats involving entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident may adversely affect an entity’s service recipients, requiring immediate notification to those recipients under A, while the same event may be a significant cyberthreat voluntarily reported under B and then forwarded to the ECB. These are different communications to different recipients, and neither text says that one notification discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not impose two mandatory reports for the same event: A concerns an incident with significant effects on service provision and, where applicable, notification to service recipients, whereas B concerns a voluntary report of a significant cyberthreat. An entity can avoid B’s voluntary mechanism, and the texts do not establish that every event covered by A is also a cyberthreat reportable under B.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity subject to both regimes suffers a cyber incident that significantly affects its services and is therefore required under A to notify its service recipients immediately. The entity also voluntarily reports the significant cyberthreat under B, after which the report is forwarded to the ECB; notifying the service recipients does not notify the ECB, so both communications must be made and the two immediate-reporting channels are distinct.
verdict.decisive_exception: The main qualification is that B’s cyberthreat reporting is expressly voluntary and applies only when the financial entity considers the threat relevant to the financial system, service users or clients. Thus, the dual-reporting tension arises only if the entity elects to make that B report; it is not an unavoidable conflict for an entity that does not invoke the optional mechanism.

Provision A requires prior consultation where the DPIA shows high residual risk absent mitigation, while Provision B requires the provider to ensure compliance with Section 2; the texts do not state whether AI Act compliance or conformity assessment removes the GDPR consultation duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are imposed on different actors and are triggered by different conditions: A concerns the controller's proposed processing and a DPIA finding, whereas B concerns providers of high-risk AI systems and imposes several product-compliance duties. A provider/controller can comply with both by ensuring Section 2 compliance and consulting the supervisory authority whenever Article 36's condition is met.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the provider to notify the affected person without delay when a personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect that person's privacy. B separately requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29; if the same event qualifies under both regimes, the duties may involve different reporting obligations and potentially different recipients or procedures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be satisfied cumulatively: the actor can notify the affected person under A and report the significant incident under B. B does not state that reporting under its Articles 26–29 replaces or discharges A's individual notification duty, and the text shown does not establish that the same actor, recipient, or incident necessarily falls within both provisions.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0052872 Articles 26–29, which are needed to determine whether the significant-incident report under Article 25 has a different recipient and deadline, and whether it covers the same incident as the personal-data breach in Article 11.3a. The identity of the actor's status as an essential or important entity and the applicable incident definitions may also be decisive.

verdict.shared_subject: Providers of public telecommunications services and their cooperation with legally authorised state measures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose broad cooperation duties on telecommunications providers, and a single provider could receive a lawful interception or recording order while military authority is applying Article 31 of the War Act. The texts do not specify how to resolve competing instructions or whether compliance with one duty affects the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different legal triggers and can be performed cumulatively: Article 13.2 concerns cooperation with specified interception or recording orders, while Article 14.5 concerns cooperation with military-authority orders during application of Article 31. Nothing in either provision requires refusing or violating the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aanbieders van openbare telecommunicatiediensten zijn verplicht medewerking te verlenen aan de uitvoering van een bevel op grond van het Wetboek van Strafvordering of artikel 13:3a, eerste lid, onderdeel b, van de Wet verplichte geestelijke gezondheidszorg dan wel een toestemming op grond van de Wet op de inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten 2017 tot het aftappen of opnemen van door hen verzorgde telecommunicatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Voorafgaande raadpleging en technische documentatie voor systemen/verwerkingen met een hoog risico
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen vóór ingebruikname of verwerking verplichtingen opleggen rond een hoog-risicosituatie, maar zij verlangen verschillende handelingen: raadpleging van een toezichthoudende autoriteit enerzijds en technische documentatie voor bevoegde autoriteiten en aangemelde instanties anderzijds. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat één documentatie- of conformiteitsproces niet duidelijk maakt of ook de afzonderlijke voorafgaande raadpleging is verricht.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen cumulatieve, inhoudelijk verschillende verplichtingen op met verschillende triggers en functies. Artikel 36 vereist voorafgaande raadpleging wanneer een DPIA een niet-gemitigeerd hoog risico vaststelt; artikel 11 vereist technische documentatie voor een AI-systeem met hoog risico, zodat overeenstemming kan worden beoordeeld. Beide kunnen zonder tegenstrijdigheid worden nageleefd.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations, but they concern entirely different actions and subject matters: CSIRTs must perform cyber-risk and incident analysis, while a party must submit a notification concerning a proposed transaction or public bid. No actor is required by these texts to perform incompatible acts or to choose between them.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations can plainly be performed together: a CSIRT can conduct dynamic cyber-risk analysis, and the relevant party can make the required notification within the applicable deadline. They apply to different actors, triggers, and regulatory domains, which is ordinary coexistence rather than tension.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or documenting incidents involving an AI system and a significant incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same event is both a significant incident under Provision A and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system under Provision B, the operator may have to submit a progress report under A while separately notifying the provider, importer or distributor, and market-surveillance authorities under B. These are different actions and recipients, so neither filing obviously discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively without contradiction: Provision A requires a progress report only when the incident is still ongoing at the time of the final report, while Provision B requires immediate incident notifications to specified AI actors and authorities. Nothing in either text forbids the other communication or makes one a substitute for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A high-risk AI system operated by an entity covered by both regimes suffers an incident that is both a significant incident and a serious incident, and remains ongoing when the operator's final report under Provision A is due. The operator must submit the progress report under A and, separately, immediately notify the provider first and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities under B; the two duties have different content, recipients and timing.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern an incident-related final report, but Provision A requires financial entities to submit a final report to the relevant competent authority under the Article 20 deadlines, while Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report within one month after the incident is resolved. If the same entity and incident fall under both regimes, the provisions could appear to impose different final-report timing rules.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts do not establish two separate filings to different recipients: Provision B specifies when its final report must be submitted but does not identify a recipient, whereas Provision A identifies the relevant competent authority. Provision B also expressly substitutes a progress report for the final report while the incident continues, and then requires the final report after resolution; this can operate cumulatively with, or be satisfied alongside, Provision A rather than creating an irreconcilable conflict.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing provision is the rule establishing the recipient and deadline for the final report under BWBR0052872 art. 29, including whether that report must be filed separately from the Provision A report and whether its one-month deadline is intended to replace or coexist with the Article 20 deadline applicable under Provision A.

Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat eerdere inbreuken onder A moeten worden meegewogen bij handhaving, terwijl B een verantwoordelijkheid van een bevoegde autoriteit voorschrijft om incidentbijzonderheden door te geven, maar geen van beide normen verbiedt of beperkt de andere.

B verplicht een bevoegde autoriteit om onder specifieke grensoverschrijdende omstandigheden incidentbijzonderheden aan een relevante autoriteit door te geven; beide verplichtingen kunnen volledig naast elkaar worden nagekomen en betreffen verschillende handelingen.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns competent authorities taking measures to protect financial-system stability after assessing a serious ICT incident. Provision B concerns making a telecommunications-control notification by a deadline; the provisions regulate different actors, events, recipients, and subject matter, so no concrete incompatibility is apparent.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can plainly coexist: the relevant authorities may take necessary stability measures when appropriate, while a person intending to acquire control of a telecommunications undertaking submits the separate notification within the applicable deadline. Neither provision requires or prohibits conduct that would prevent compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: CE-markering op een AI-systeem met een hoog risico
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen verlangen dat de vereiste CE-markering aanwezig is voordat het systeem in de handel wordt gebracht. Er is echter geen inhoudelijke botsing: de aanbieder moet de markering aanbrengen, terwijl de importeur moet nagaan of zij is aangebracht.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen zijn complementair en rusten op verschillende actoren. De aanbieder brengt de markering aan; de importeur controleert vóór het in de handel brengen of die markering aanwezig is, zodat beide verplichtingen gelijktijdig kunnen worden nageleefd.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity guidance obligations under Directive 2022/2555
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose guidance-related obligations, so they are topically related. However, Article 23 concerns the CSIRT or competent authority responding to a reporting entity after a significant-incident warning, while Article 29 concerns ENISA supporting information-sharing arrangements through best practices and guidance; neither requires an actor to choose between incompatible actions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively by different institutional actors and serve different triggers and functions. Article 23 requires incident-response guidance in a specified circumstance, whereas Article 29 requires ENISA to provide guidance in support of information-sharing arrangements; performing one does not prevent performing the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer het CSIRT de in de lid 1 bedoelde melding niet als eerste heeft ontvangen, worden de richtsnoeren door de bevoegde autoriteit in samenwerking met het CSIRT verstrekt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Enisa ondersteunt de invoering van de in lid 2 bedoelde informatie-uitwisselingsregelingen op het gebied van cyberbeveiliging door beste praktijken uit te wisselen en richtsnoeren te verstekken.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or handling ICT/security incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related communications, and an incident involving a financial entity’s electronic service might appear to require communication under both regimes. However, provision A concerns confirmation and possible feedback after a notification under Article 19, while provision B requires the relevant administrative body or designated organisation to notify the Minister of specified incidents; the texts do not establish incompatible content, deadlines, or recipients for the same actor.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the competent authority can confirm receipt of the Article 19 notification, while the administrative body or designated organisation can separately notify the Minister and provide the required information. They apply to different actors and triggers as stated, and provision A expressly leaves the financial entity responsible for the reported incident rather than prohibiting any additional notification.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying security breach must be reported to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, while B requires a significant incident affecting a trust service to be reported to both the entity’s CSIRT and its competent authority. If the same event satisfies both triggers, the actor must make separate notifications to different recipients, and notification under one provision does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately under A and notify the CSIRT and competent authority immediately, or within 24 hours where immediate notification is impossible, under B. Nothing in either text forbids making the additional notification required by the other provision.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider that is an essential or important entity suffers a security breach affecting personal-data protection in connection with its public electronic communications service, and the breach also has consequences for provision of its trust service. It must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens under A and separately notify its CSIRT and competent authority under B; the recipients differ, so one filing cannot discharge both duties.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI or data-processing activities and the obligations of the responsible actors.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a controller to consult the supervisory authority before processing where the DPIA indicates an unmitigated high risk. Provision B requires an original AI provider to provide technical access and assistance needed to comply with the AI Regulation, particularly high-risk AI conformity-assessment obligations; in a high-risk AI deployment, these duties could create parallel regulatory steps, but neither text makes compliance with one impossible or substitutes one for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties on different actors and under different triggers: A concerns a GDPR controller and prior consultation about high-risk processing, while B concerns an original AI provider assisting new providers with AI-Regulation compliance. Providing assistance does not prevent prior consultation, and consulting the supervisory authority does not prevent providing the required assistance.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT-related incidents and submitting a final incident report
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same entity and incident, but they require reporting to different recipient sets: provision A requires reporting to the relevant competent authority under Article 46, while provision B requires a final report to both the entity's CSIRT and its competent authority within one month. A report to the competent authority under A does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate CSIRT filing required by B, and A's reporting duty has no stated deadline here.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different reporting stages and can be performed cumulatively: A concerns reporting a serious ICT-related incident, whereas B concerns a final report containing specified information after the Article 27 notification. The same incident can therefore be reported to the relevant authority under A and later documented in a final report to the CSIRT and competent authority under B.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity that is also a financial entity suffers one serious ICT-related incident. It must report the incident to the relevant competent authority under provision A and, no later than one month after the Article 27 notification, submit a separate final report to both its CSIRT and its competent authority under provision B; filing the A report with the competent authority does not itself make the required CSIRT filing.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen bij één gebeurtenis communicatieverplichtingen activeren, maar zij richten zich op verschillende ontvangers en gebruiken verschillende triggers. Dat kan een cumulatieve rapportage- of informatiebelasting opleveren, vooral wanneer een significante cyberdreiging voor dienstontvangers tegelijk een ernstig AI-incident vormt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or providing information to authorities under separate EU digital-law regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information-related obligations on entities that may operate in overlapping digital or financial compliance contexts. However, Provision A concerns outsourcing incident reporting while retaining responsibility, whereas Provision B concerns a notified body's response to a request from the notifying authority about conformity-assessment activities; the texts do not make these the same event, recipient, deadline, or duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly be complied with together: a financial entity may remain responsible for incident reporting even when outsourcing it, while a notified body must provide information about its conformity-assessment activities when requested. They address different actors, triggers, subject matter, and recipients, with no incompatible command or prohibition.
