verdict.shared_subject: Het indienen van voortgangs- of tussentijdse rapporten over hetzelfde ICT-incident door een financiële entiteit die onder beide regelingen valt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen tijdens één voortgaand incident een tussentijdse rapportage verlangen. Artikel 23 verplicht een voortgangsverslag wanneer het incident nog aan de gang is, terwijl artikel 19 een tussentijds verslag verlangt bij een ingrijpende statuswijziging of wijziging van de behandeling; de bepalingen noemen niet dezelfde ontvanger of dezelfde termijn, zodat één verslag niet zonder meer beide verplichtingen vervult.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: de entiteit kan één inhoudelijk verslag opstellen en dit, waar nodig, afzonderlijk indienen bij de in beide bepalingen bedoelde autoriteiten. Bovendien kan artikel 19 voor financiële entiteiten een eigen, nader vast te stellen rapportageprocedure bevatten, zodat de teksten op zichzelf geen onmogelijkheid om beide te vervullen aantonen.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een financiële entiteit die tevens een betrokken entiteit onder Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555 is, heeft een ernstig/significant ICT-incident dat na de eerste melding nog voortduurt en waarvan de behandeling ingrijpend wijzigt. Zij moet dan op grond van artikel 23 een voortgangsverslag indienen bij het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit, en op grond van artikel 19 een tussentijds verslag indienen bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit; de twee bepalingen voorzien niet in één gemeenschappelijke indiening, één ontvanger of één klok die de andere melding automatisch vervangt.
verdict.decisive_exception: De precieze termijnen en eventuele model- of coördinatieregels van artikel 20 van Verordening (EU) 2022/2554 zijn niet weergegeven. Die kunnen de praktische samenloop regelen, maar de getoonde teksten bepalen niet dat een melding bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit de afzonderlijke voortgangsrapportage onder artikel 23 vervangt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: e) indien het incident nog aan de gang is op het moment dat het in punt d) bedoelde eindverslag wordt ingediend, zorgen de lidstaten ervoor dat de betrokken entiteiten op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: b) een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie

verdict.shared_subject: Obligations of providers of public telecommunications networks to cooperate with legally authorised interception or military-authority orders
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose broad cooperation duties on providers of public telecommunications networks, and in an unusual situation a military-authority order could potentially demand conduct affecting telecommunications that is also subject to an interception order or authorisation. If the two commands required incompatible technical actions or treatment of the same communications, the provider would need further rules to determine which command prevails.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties triggered by different legal bases: A concerns cooperation with a criminal-procedure or intelligence-service interception order or authorisation, while B concerns application of Article 31 of the War Act and orders from the military authority. Nothing in either text requires disobedience to the other, and both duties can ordinarily be performed together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aanbieders van openbare telecommunicatienetwerken zijn verplicht medewerking te verlenen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij toepassing van artikel 31 van de Oorlogswet voor Nederland zijn aanbieders van openbare telecommunicatienetwerken, openbare telecommunicatiediensten en gebruikers van de frequentieruimte verplicht het militair gezag alle medewerking te verlenen

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both the GDPR and NIS2
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without unreasonable delay of any personal-data breach, while a covered essential or important entity must report each significant incident without delay to its CSIRT or competent authority. A single incident may satisfy both triggers, and the reports go to different recipients, so one filing does not textually discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers and addressees: Article 33 concerns a processor informing the controller of a personal-data breach, whereas Article 23 concerns an essential or important entity reporting a significant service-impacting incident to a CSIRT or competent authority. They can therefore be complied with cumulatively, without incompatible content or deadlines.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity acting as a processor suffers a cyberattack that both constitutes a personal-data breach and causes a significant disruption to its services. It must inform the controller 'zonder onredelijke vertraging' under Article 33 and separately report the significant incident 'onverwijld' to 'zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit' under Article 23; informing the controller does not make the CSIRT or competent-authority report, and vice versa.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory duties concerning enforcement of cybersecurity and serious-incident notification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern official handling of cybersecurity-related non-compliance or incidents. One might argue that considering the duration of an infringement under NIS2 and following the notification procedures under the AI Act could create overlapping procedural demands, particularly where the same incident is involved.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires competent authorities to consider the duration of an infringement when taking enforcement measures; it does not impose a notification, deadline, or incompatible procedural prohibition. Provision B requires the market-surveillance authority to take measures within seven days after receiving a notification and to follow Regulation 2019/1020 procedures. These are different duties, addressed to authorities in different procedural contexts, and can be performed cumulatively without contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) de duur van de inbreuk;
verdict.evidence_span_b: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen, en volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident notification by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to prepare and submit an initial notification and reports to a competent authority, while Provision B requires immediate notification to the entity’s service recipients. These are different recipients and distinct communications, so notifying the authority does not notify the service recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different audiences and can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the entity can report the serious ICT incident to the competent authority and, where applicable, immediately inform affected service recipients. Nothing in either provision forbids the other notification or makes one substitute for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity enforcement and CSIRT functions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities to take the offender’s intent or negligence into account when imposing enforcement measures. Provision B requires the CSIRT, where possible, to disseminate early warnings, notifications and announcements; in a concrete incident, that dissemination could expose or affect an entity whose culpability is still being assessed.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different functions: A governs how competent authorities determine enforcement measures, while B defines the CSIRT’s operational information-sharing task. Nothing in B prohibits dissemination based on intent or negligence, and nothing in A prevents the CSIRT from issuing warnings.
verdict.evidence_span_a: opzet of nalatigheid van de pleger van de inbreuk
verdict.evidence_span_b: het verstrekken van vroegtijdige waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen en het verspreiden van informatie

verdict.shared_subject: Periods set by public authorities in relation to agreements concerning telecommunications access or shared use
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern determining a period connected with agreements, so one might initially suspect overlapping authority over the duration of arrangements. However, Article 3.21 concerns the Minister setting the period within which frequency users must conclude a joint-use agreement, while Article 6a.4e concerns ACM determining how long certain access or co-investment agreements are declared binding; they regulate different decisions, actors, triggers, and subject matter.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly operate together: the Minister may set a deadline for users to conclude a frequency-sharing agreement, while ACM may separately determine the period during which qualifying access or co-investment arrangements are binding. Compliance with one does not prevent compliance with the other, and neither text makes one period override or substitute for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In de gevallen waarin samenwerking tussen gebruikers van frequentieruimte noodzakelijk is voor het kunnen gebruiken van de aan hen toegewezen frequentieruimte, sluiten de desbetreffende gebruikers binnen een door Onze Minister te bepalen periode na de toewijzing als bedoeld in artikel 3.5 of de verlening van de vergunning een overeenkomst betreffende de voorwaarden tot gezamenlijk gebruik van dat deel van de frequentieruimte.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De Autoriteit Consument en Markt bepaalt gedurende welke periode de afspraken bindend worden verklaard, waarbij de periode voor mede-investeringsafspraken als bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel b, ten minste 7 jaar is, en kan deze periode telkens verlengen.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related compliance involving entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers the lead overseer to impose a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider after non-compliance with specified measures and a minimum 30-day period. Provision B separately requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident, but it does not prohibit, delay, or otherwise regulate the imposition of that fine.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of rules on different actors and address different triggers: A concerns supervisory enforcement against a critical ICT third-party provider, while B concerns incident reporting by an essential or important entity. Both can be complied with independently, and nothing in the shown text makes reporting an incident incompatible with a coercive fine or makes one duty substitute for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Responsibility for ICT/significant incidents and related reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to submit a final report within one month after handling an ongoing significant incident. Provision B makes the financial entity remain fully responsible for handling and the consequences of ICT incidents reported under Article 19(1), so an entity might face continuing responsibility while also completing the separate final-report process.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties rather than incompatible ones: A concerns submitting a final report to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B preserves the financial entity’s substantive responsibility despite supervisory feedback. Nothing in B excuses or prohibits A’s report, and nothing in A transfers or limits the responsibility stated in B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: binnen één maand nadat zij het incident hebben afgehandeld, een eindverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd

verdict.shared_subject: Essential entities that are also critical entities and the handling of incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incidents involving an essential entity that is also a critical entity. One might argue that A requires the competent authority to consider the duration of an infringement when taking enforcement measures, while B requires the CSIRT to provide incident information to another competent authority, potentially creating overlapping institutional handling of the same event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors at different stages. A governs how a competent authority exercises enforcement discretion and assesses the duration of an infringement; B requires the CSIRT to transmit information about a reported incident, near-incident or cyber threat to the competent authority under the Critical Entities Resilience Act. Nothing in either provision prohibits or substitutes for compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de duur van de inbreuk
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een incident, bijna-incident of cyberdreiging

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related incident management and reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to document and remove underlying causes as part of incident follow-up, while provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report when an incident continues past the final-report deadline. If the same entity is subject to both, the reporting obligation in B could be viewed as an additional incident-follow-up burden alongside A’s documentation duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties rather than incompatible ones. A requires internal processes and documentation of underlying causes; B specifies which report must be submitted when an incident is ongoing and requires a final report after resolution. Nothing in A forbids either report, and A does not itself require a separate filing or identify a recipient or deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, teneinde ervoor te zorgen dat onderliggende oorzaken worden opgespoord, gedocumenteerd en weggenomen om dergelijke incidenten te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Financial or other regulated entities’ management of ICT and network-and-information-system risks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern ICT incidents and risk management, but they require different activities: Provision A requires analysing incident frequency, types, scale, evolution and patterns, while Provision B requires proportionately considering exposure, entity size, incident likelihood and severity, including societal and economic consequences. One might argue that the regimes impose different benchmarks for the same broader risk-management duty, leaving uncertainty about whether incident-pattern analysis is sufficient for the proportionality assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative and independently satisfiable duties, not incompatible benchmarks. An entity can analyse ICT incidents as required by A and also consider the broader proportionality factors required by B when selecting measures; neither provision says that compliance with one substitutes for or prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zij inventariseren de ontwikkeling van ICT-risico’s in de tijd, analyseren de frequentie, de types, de omvang en de evolutie van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen en de patronen daarvan
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten aanzien van de evenredigheid van de maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, houdt de entiteit naar behoren rekening met de mate waarin zij aan risico’s is blootgesteld, de omvang van de entiteit en de kans dat zich incidenten voordoen en de ernst ervan, met inbegrip van de maatschappelijke en economische gevolgen.

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingen en daaropvolgende wettelijke handelingen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen betreffen meldingen, maar zij regulate different actors and events: A requires a market-surveillance authority to act after receiving a serious-incident notification, while B requires a notifying party to submit a notification before implementing a proposed transaction. No actor is required by the shown text both to perform and not perform the same act, and the provisions do not establish incompatible deadlines for one filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively without conflict. A concerns measures by the market-surveillance authority within seven days after receipt of an AI serious-incident notification; B concerns the timing of a notification about a proposed transaction, including a special rule for a public offer involving a listed telecommunications party.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De melding in het eerste lid wordt gedaan uiterlijk acht weken voor de beoogde datum van uitvoering van dit voornemen.

verdict.shared_subject: Information and reporting duties of regulated entities or bodies
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information duties, and an entity subject to both might need to include different information in communications arising from regulated activities. However, Article 45 concerns notifying the notifying authority about circumstances affecting notification scope or conditions, while Article 26 concerns the content of an early warning about a significant incident, including whether it may have cross-border effects; the texts do not make these the same triggering event, recipient, or report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties address different subjects and triggers: Article 45 requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about circumstances affecting their designation, whereas Article 26 requires an entity, in an early warning, to state whether a significant incident may have cross-border effects. Each can be fulfilled independently, and neither provision forbids or substitutes for compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding
verdict.evidence_span_b: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident grensoverschrijdende gevolgen kan hebben

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting information about a significant or serious ICT incident by a financial entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose reporting-related obligations, and a single incident might be described as both a serious ICT-related incident and a significant incident. If Article 26 required a separate early warning to a different recipient or on a different clock, the entity could face cumulative reporting burdens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The shown Article 26 text only specifies information that must be provided in the early warning; it does not identify a separate recipient, deadline, or filing distinct from the reporting framework. Article 19 requires updated notifications after the initial notification, while Article 26 requires particular fields in an early warning, so the duties can be satisfied cumulatively in the same reporting process without contradiction.
verdict.missing_reference: The provision containing the first-lid obligation and procedural details for the early warning in Article 26 would be needed to determine whether it is a separate filing, its recipient, and its deadline. On the text shown, however, that missing information does not establish a tension.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie, in voorkomend geval gevolgd door geactualiseerde kennisgevingen telkens wanneer een relevante actualisering van de status beschikbaar is, alsmede op specifiek verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit;
verdict.evidence_span_b: c. verstrekt de entiteit de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations of regulated entities to public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties, but they concern different triggering events and different actors: A concerns circumstances affecting a notified body's notification scope or conditions and requires notice to the notifying authority, while B concerns a security breach with adverse personal-data-protection consequences and requires immediate notice to the Dutch data-protection authority. If one entity were subject to both regimes and one event independently satisfied both triggers, the texts would require separate notifications to different authorities; notice to one would not, on the text shown, discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with cumulatively because they address distinct triggers and recipients. A has no deadline, and B's immediate deadline does not purport to replace A's notification duty; moreover, the texts do not establish that the same actor or event must fall within both provisions.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A notified conformity-assessment body that is also the provider of a public electronic communications service suffers a security breach that adversely affects the protection of personal data processed in providing that service, and the breach also changes the conditions or scope of its notification. It must notify the notifying authority under A and, without delay, notify the Dutch data-protection authority under B; the two recipients are different, so filing with one does not discharge the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aangemelde instanties brengen de aanmeldende autoriteit op de hoogte van:
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related information sharing involving Dutch public bodies, designated organisations, or essential/important entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident information, so an incident affecting an entity in the Netherlands might appear to trigger overlapping notification or information-sharing duties. However, Provision A requires a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify the Minister about a breach or misuse involving its own electronic service, while Provision B requires the central contact point to notify the relevant CSIRT and competent authority when information received from another Member State shows effects on an essential or important entity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors, arise from different triggers, and have different recipients: A concerns the affected body's own electronic service and notification to the Minister; B concerns the central contact point's receipt of information from another Member State and notification to a CSIRT and competent authority. Even if the underlying incident overlaps, the duties can be performed cumulatively and neither text says that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Als uit gegevens die het centrale contactpunt heeft ontvangen van een centraal contactpunt van een andere lidstaat van de Europese Unie blijkt dat een daar gemeld incident, bijna-incident of cyberdreiging gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van de diensten van een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit in Nederland, stelt het centrale contactpunt het betrokken CSIRT en de betrokken bevoegde autoriteit daarvan op de hoogte.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity information and incident information concerning AI models
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern cybersecurity-related information, and Provision B requires certain information about serious incidents and corrective measures to be kept, documented, and reported. One might argue that sharing vulnerability or incident information under Provision A could overlap with the information-handling duty in Provision B, creating uncertainty about whether information should be exchanged voluntarily or reported through the AI Act channels.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A establishes a voluntary possibility for entities to exchange relevant cybersecurity information with one another, for specified cybersecurity purposes. Provision B imposes a separate duty on providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk to keep, document, and, where applicable, report relevant information about serious incidents and corrective measures to the AI Office and national authorities; voluntary exchange can occur in addition to, and without discharging, that reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op vrijwillige basis onderling relevante informatie over cyberbeveiliging kunnen uitwisselen
verdict.evidence_span_b: relevante informatie over ernstige incidenten en mogelijke corrigerende maatregelen bijhouden, documenteren en onverwijld rapporteren aan het AI-bureau en, in voorkomend geval, aan de nationale bevoegde autoriteiten

verdict.shared_subject: Feedback or guidance following an incident notification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern feedback after an incident notification, and both mention guidance. One might argue that the financial-sector authority's feedback under Provision A overlaps with the CSIRT's response and guidance under Provision B, potentially creating uncertainty about which body should provide operational advice.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and operate through different mechanisms: Provision A concerns what the competent authority may provide after receiving specified notifications, while Provision B requires the CSIRT to respond to a reporting entity after an early warning and provides guidance only on request. The duties can readily be performed cumulatively, and Provision A expressly preserves CSIRT input and measures rather than displacing it.
verdict.evidence_span_a: kan zij, waar mogelijk, tijdig relevante en evenredige feedback of richtsnoeren op hoog niveau aan de financiële entiteit verstrekken
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek van de entiteit, richtsnoeren of operationeel advies voor de uitvoering van mogelijke risicobeperkende maatregelen

verdict.shared_subject: Obligations of telecommunications or market-infrastructure entities to provide cooperation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose cooperation duties, so an entity potentially falling within both categories could face two statutory cooperation obligations. However, the provisions concern different underlying measures and do not prescribe incompatible conduct, deadlines, recipients, or limits.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires public telecommunications-network providers to cooperate with lawful interception or recording orders or authorisations. Provision B requires specified financial-market entities to cooperate with the Minister in implementing paragraph 1; both duties can be performed cumulatively, and nothing in either text forbids compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Aanbieders van openbare telecommunicatienetwerken zijn verplicht medewerking te verlenen aan de uitvoering van een bevel op grond van het Wetboek van Strafvordering of artikel 13:3a, eerste lid, onderdeel b, van de Wet verplichte geestelijke gezondheidszorg dan wel een toestemming op grond van de Wet op de inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten 2017 tot het aftappen of opnemen van telecommunicatie die over hun telecommunicatienetwerken wordt afgewikkeld.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een beursgenoteerde betrokken partij, een aangesloten instelling, centraal instituut, intermediair, instelling in het buitenland of buitenlandse instelling met een functie vergelijkbaar met die van het centraal instituut verleent medewerking aan de Minister bij de tenuitvoerlegging van het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations triggered by different events and addressed to different authorities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a controller to report a personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours where the stated risk condition is met. Provision B requires a cable operator to notify the municipal mayor or authorised official before public-ground cable-maintenance work, with the authorised official then informing the mayor; if a single activity involved both a qualifying data breach and such cable work, the duties would concern different events and recipients rather than one filing discharging the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers, regulated activities, and recipients: A concerns personal-data breaches by a controller, while B concerns cable-maintenance work in or on public grounds by an operator. Even in an unusual overlap, each duty can be performed independently, and B's notice is required before the works, not as an alternative to A's breach notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and prioritisation of regulatory communications concerning AI systems or incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A establishes a three-month period, shortened to thirty days for non-compliance with the prohibited AI practices, after which a provisional market-surveillance measure is deemed justified absent an objection. Provision B requires the CSIRT to process voluntary incident, near-incident and cyber-threat reports, while allowing it to prioritise mandatory reports; one might argue that the different procedures and priorities could create uncertainty about how a report relevant to both regimes is handled.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different institutional processes: A governs the legal effect and objection period for a provisional market-surveillance measure, whereas B governs the CSIRT's processing and prioritisation of voluntary reports. Nothing in A requires or forbids CSIRT processing, and nothing in B alters the three-month or thirty-day period or the market-surveillance authority's measure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien er binnen drie maanden na ontvangst van de in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving door een markttoezichtautoriteit van een lidstaat of door de Commissie geen bezwaar tegen een voorlopige maatregel van een markttoezichtautoriteit van een andere lidstaat is ingediend, wordt die maatregel geacht gerechtvaardigd te zijn.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verwerkt de vrijwillige meldingen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, overeenkomstig de in artikel 36 omschreven procedure.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security or personal-data breaches in public electronic communications services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern a breach and require prompt notification, but they direct the notifications to different actors: A requires the processor to inform the controller, while B requires the provider to inform the Dutch Data Protection Authority. If the same provider is also the processor and the breach falls within both provisions, the texts appear to require two separate notifications on different reporting lines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the processor can promptly notify the controller under A and the public electronic communications provider can simultaneously notify the supervisory authority under B. Nothing in either provision says that one notification substitutes for the other, so there is no impossibility of obeying both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company provides a public electronic communications service and acts as processor for a controller. It discovers a security breach affecting personal data processed in connection with that service, with adverse consequences for personal-data protection. The company must inform the controller 'zonder onredelijke vertraging' under A and separately inform the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens 'onverwijld' under B; notifying the controller does not notify the authority, and notifying the authority does not notify the controller.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens die zijn verwerkt in verband met de levering van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst in de Europese Unie.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity obligations for entities and providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose cybersecurity-related duties, but they apply to potentially different regulated actors and use different formulations. If a provider of a systemic-risk general-purpose AI model is also an essential or important entity, it must satisfy both the general risk-proportionate network-and-information-system measures under A and the AI-model-specific cybersecurity protection duty under B; the texts do not make the benchmarks identical.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can be satisfied together: A requires appropriate and proportionate measures for the security risks of the systems used by essential and important entities, while B requires an appropriate level of cybersecurity protection for the AI model and its physical infrastructure. Nothing in either provision requires conduct that the other forbids, and B's more specific model-focused duty can be implemented as part of A's broader risk-management measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: passende en evenredige technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen nemen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van de netwerk- en informatiesystemen die deze entiteiten voor hun werkzaamheden of voor het verlenen van hun diensten gebruiken, te beheren
verdict.evidence_span_b: zorgen voor een passend niveau van cyberbeveiligingsbescherming voor het AI-model voor algemene doeleinden met een systeemrisico en de fysieke infrastructuur van het model

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity-risk governance and security measures of essential and important entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the governing bodies to approve and oversee the entities’ cybersecurity-risk-management measures so that they comply with Article 21. Provision B separately requires the entity, when assessing proportionality, to account for exposure, size, incident likelihood and severity, including social and economic consequences; one might argue that governance approval and oversight could impose a different or insufficiently specified benchmark for those measures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are complementary: A assigns governing bodies an approval, oversight and accountability role, expressly tied to compliance with Article 21, while B specifies factors the entity must consider when determining the proportionality of its measures. Nothing in A permits ignoring B or substitutes governance approval for the entity’s substantive duty to consider those factors.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten de door deze entiteiten genomen maatregelen voor het beheer van cyberbeveiligingsrisico’s goedkeuren om te voldoen aan artikel 21, toezien op de uitvoering ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten aanzien van de evenredigheid van de maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, houdt de entiteit naar behoren rekening met de mate waarin zij aan risico’s is blootgesteld, de omvang van de entiteit en de kans dat zich incidenten voordoen en de ernst ervan, met inbegrip van de maatschappelijke en economische gevolgen.

verdict.shared_subject: Risk-based technical and organisational measures for protecting personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a risk-based duty on the controller, and Article 32 additionally imposes concrete security capabilities and testing requirements. One might argue that Article 25’s broader requirement to implement all data-protection principles and safeguards could demand measures beyond, or different from, Article 32’s security-focused benchmark, leaving uncertainty about when the Article 32 measures suffice.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address complementary aspects of the same compliance programme: Article 25 concerns privacy by design and default, including effective implementation of data-protection principles, while Article 32 concerns an appropriate level of security. The controller can satisfy both cumulatively by designing processing to protect data-protection principles and by implementing the specified risk-appropriate security measures; neither provision says that compliance with one substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: treft de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, zowel bij de bepaling van de verwerkingsmiddelen als bij de verwerking zelf, passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen
verdict.evidence_span_b: treffen de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en de verwerker passende technische en organisatorische maatregelen om een op het risico afgestemd beveiligingsniveau te waarborgen

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose incident-reporting duties concerning the same kind of significant incident and require a report containing substantially overlapping information. If Provision A's incidentmelding and Provision B's eindverslag were separate filings under different regimes, the entity would face cumulative reporting obligations on different deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The shown text does not establish that the two reports are separate filings: Provision A's 72-hour incidentmelding is followed by a final report due one month later, while Provision B expressly concerns an eindverslag due one month after the Article 27 notification and addressed to the entity's CSIRT and competent authority. The overlapping final-report content and matching one-month timing strongly support that Provision B specifies or implements the same final-report duty rather than creating a second incompatible obligation.
verdict.missing_reference: The relationship cannot be established with complete certainty without the referenced Article 27(1) notification and the national-law provisions showing whether BWBR0052872 Article 29 implements Article 23(4)(d) or creates an additional report. However, on the texts shown, this is not enough to classify the pair as dual_reporting_tension.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-continuïteit, weerbaarheid en beschikbaarheid bij bepaalde financiële entiteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen continuïteits- en weerbaarheidsverplichtingen op, maar art. 16 formuleert die voor bepaalde vrijgestelde of kleine entiteiten als een vereenvoudigd kader, terwijl art. 9 een algemener en mogelijk uitgebreider beleids- en uitvoeringsvereiste formuleert. Men zou daarom kunnen vragen of naleving van het vereenvoudigde kader volstaat tegenover de eisen van art. 9.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn cumulatief verenigbaar: art. 16 verplicht de betrokken entiteiten tot bedrijfscontinuïteitsplannen en respons- en herstelmaatregelen, terwijl art. 9 verlangt dat financiële entiteiten beveiligingsbeleid, procedures, protocollen en instrumenten ontwerpen, aanschaffen en uitvoeren om weerbaarheid, continuïteit en beschikbaarheid te waarborgen. Niets in de getoonde tekst bepaalt dat het vereenvoudigde kader van art. 16 art. 9 vervangt, beperkt of als gelijkwaardig wordt aangemerkt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de continuïteit van kritieke of belangrijke functies waarborgen door middel van bedrijfscontinuïteitsplannen en respons- en herstelmaatregelen, die ten minste back-up- en herstelmaatregelen omvatten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten zorgen voor het ontwerp, de aanbesteding en de uitvoering van ICT-beveiligingsbeleidslijnen, -procedures, -protocollen en -instrumenten die er op gericht zijn de weerbaarheid, continuïteit en beschikbaarheid van ICT-systemen, met name die welke kritieke of belangrijke functies ondersteunen, te waarborgen

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident monitoring and information sharing involving CSIRTs and critical entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related cybersecurity information. One might argue that CSIRT monitoring and analysis under Provision A could overlap with the information-transfer duty in Provision B, creating uncertainty about which body must communicate incident information.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different actions: Provision A requires CSIRTs to monitor and analyse threats, vulnerabilities and incidents, while Provision B requires a competent authority to provide information to another competent authority about a reported significant incident. The duties are cumulative and can readily be performed together; Provision A does not prohibit the transfer required by Provision B.
verdict.evidence_span_a:
De CSIRT’s hebben de volgende taken:

a) het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau
verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.

verdict.shared_subject: Voorafgaande risicobeoordeling en documentatie van AI-/gegevensverwerkingsactiviteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen op een AI-systeem betrekking hebben en verlangen een voorafgaande beoordeling of documentatie. De triggers en normadressaten verschillen echter: artikel 35 ziet op verwerkingen die waarschijnlijk een hoog risico voor natuurlijke personen opleveren, terwijl artikel 6 ziet op een aanbieder die meent dat een in bijlage III bedoeld AI-systeem géén hoog risico inhoudt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen cumulatieve, afzonderlijk uitvoerbare verplichtingen op aan mogelijk verschillende actoren en met verschillende triggers. Een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke kan de gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling uitvoeren, terwijl een aanbieder daarnaast zijn beoordeling van de AI-risicoclassificatie documenteert; geen van beide teksten verbiedt naleving van de andere verplichting of bepaalt dat de ene beoordeling de andere vervangt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een aanbieder die van mening is dat een in bijlage III bedoeld AI-systeem geen hoog risico inhoudt, documenteert zijn beoordeling voordat dat systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory obligations concerning enforcement and serious incidents involving AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern regulatory compliance, but they impose different kinds of duties: Article 83 requires supervisory authorities to make GDPR administrative fines effective, proportionate and dissuasive, while Article 60 requires a provider or potential provider to report each serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority. No text indicates that imposing effective fines conflicts with, excuses, or alters the reporting duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different actors and regulate different conduct. Article 83 governs how supervisory authorities determine administrative fines for GDPR infringements; Article 60 governs providers or potential providers testing high-risk AI systems and requires incident reporting. An authority can impose an effective, proportionate and dissuasive fine while a provider separately reports a serious incident, so both duties can be satisfied.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke toezichthoudende autoriteit zorgt ervoor dat de administratieve geldboeten die uit hoofde van dit artikel worden opgelegd voor de in de leden 4, 5 en 6 vermelde inbreuken op deze verordening in elke zaak doeltreffend, evenredig en afschrikkend zijn.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: The timing and conduct of an operator’s response after receiving a report, potentially involving modification of an AI system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits conducting an investigation that modifies the AI system in a way affecting later causal evaluation unless the competent authorities are notified beforehand. Provision B requires that a decision be taken immediately after receipt of a notification; if taking that decision necessarily required such a prohibited modification before authorities could be notified, the duties could pull in opposite directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts and appear to apply in different legal contexts: A concerns an AI provider’s investigation after a serious incident, while B concerns taking a decision immediately after receiving a notification. Provision A does not prohibit the decision required by B, and B does not require modifying an AI system without prior notice; both can therefore be complied with independently.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verricht geen onderzoek waarbij het AI-systeem wordt gewijzigd op een wijze die van invloed kan zijn op de latere evaluatie van de oorzaken van het incident, zonder de bevoegde autoriteiten daarvan vooraf in kennis te stellen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant cyber threats or ICT incidents by financial entities, particularly banks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns a voluntary report to the relevant competent authority, with onward transmission to other authorities potentially occurring. Provision B requires certain entities to make the Article 19 report also to the designated sectoral CSIRT, suggesting that the same report may require a second filing to a different recipient.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A's quoted norm is itself voluntary: an entity can avoid triggering it by not making a voluntary significant-cyber-threat report. Moreover, Provision B expressly says the report is made 'tevens' to the CSIRT, which supports a cumulative additional-recipient obligation rather than a rule forbidding or replacing the report under Provision A. The provisions therefore do not establish an irreconcilable conflict; at most, they impose separate reporting channels when the optional report is made.
verdict.decisive_exception: The voluntary nature of Provision A is decisive: an entity that does not elect to make the voluntary report faces no conflict. If it does report, Provision B can be complied with by also filing with the CSIRT; the texts shown do not establish incompatible deadlines or a rule that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an organisation subject to both the GDPR and the Dutch trust-services incident regime
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same incident, but they require reports to different recipients and on different clocks: GDPR reporting goes to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours, while the trust-services rule requires reporting to both the CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. A 24-hour report to the CSIRT and trust-services competent authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate GDPR duty to notify the Article 55 supervisory authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are individually satisfiable and may sometimes involve the same or overlapping authority in practice; an actor can report within 24 hours and make all required notifications. There is no contradiction requiring an actor simultaneously to report and not report, and the provisions do not expressly state that the reports must use different forms or contain incompatible information.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider that is an essential or important entity suffers a significant incident affecting provision of its trust service, and the same incident is also a personal-data breach likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms. The provider must report the significant incident 'onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur' to 'haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit', while separately reporting the personal-data breach 'uiterlijk 72 uur' after awareness to the Article 55 supervisory authority. Filing the 24-hour report with the CSIRT and trust-services competent authority does not, on the text shown, establish that the GDPR notification to the Article 55 authority has been made.
verdict.decisive_exception: The GDPR exception applies if it is not likely that the personal-data breach poses a risk to natural persons' rights and freedoms; the trust-services rule applies only where the incident affects provision of the trust service. In the stated scenario both triggers are met. The text shown does not establish that the trust-services competent authority is the same recipient as the Article 55 supervisory authority or that one filing legally substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Cooperation duties imposed on regulated institutions or recognised service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose cooperation duties, but they apply to different categories of actors and serve different operational contexts. No text shows that compliance with one duty would prevent or legally excuse compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: An actor covered by both provisions could provide the cooperation required by each, because the provisions do not prescribe incompatible conduct, deadlines, recipients, or limits. The duties can be performed cumulatively and concern different counterparties and purposes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een aangesloten instelling, centraal instituut, intermediair, instelling in het buitenland, bewaarder van een beleggingsinstelling of buitenlandse instelling met een functie vergelijkbaar met die van het centraal instituut verleent medewerking aan een beursgenoteerde telecommunicatiepartij bij het onderzoek.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een erkende middelenuitgever, erkende authenticatiedienst en erkende machtigingsdienst verlenen aan een erkende ontsluitende dienst alle benodigde medewerking die voor een goede ontsluiting van een erkend bedrijfs- en organisatiemiddel en een betrouwbare toegang tot de gewenste elektronische dienstverlening noodzakelijk is.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of serious/significant ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an incident report within 72 hours to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B requires financial entities to prepare and submit an initial notification and reports to the relevant competent authority under DORA’s procedures. If the same financial entity and incident fall within both regimes, the texts could require separate filings, potentially with different formats, content, procedures, and recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions require reporting an ICT incident to a competent authority or CSIRT, and B expressly allows Member States to require DORA reports also to NIS2-designated authorities or CSIRTs. The shown text does not establish that the filings are separate, that their recipients necessarily differ, or that B’s reporting deadlines are incompatible with A’s 72-hour deadline; the duties could therefore be cumulatively satisfied through a filing that meets both regimes.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing DORA provisions governing the deadlines and filing procedure—especially Article 20, first paragraph, point (a)(ii)—and the applicable national implementation/designation rules are needed to determine whether the DORA notification and NIS2 incident report are separate filings to different recipients or whether one filing can discharge both duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and associated processing/logging obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same project, but they impose different obligations on different actors and are triggered by different conditions. Article 36 requires a controller to consult the supervisory authority before processing where a DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while Article 16(e) requires a provider to retain Article 19 logs when it controls them; neither obligation prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations are cumulative and independently satisfiable: a controller can consult the supervisory authority before processing, and a provider can retain the required logs. The provisions concern different duties, triggers, and generally different regulated actors, with no incompatible command, deadline, or permission.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: bewaren de in artikel 19 bedoelde logs die automatisch door hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico zijn gegenereerd, wanneer zij hierover de controle hebben

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related notifications by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident may require the entity to notify its service recipients immediately, while B requires a separate interim report to the relevant competent authority after the initial notification. These are different communications to different recipients, and neither text says that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can both be performed cumulatively: the entity can notify service recipients immediately and submit the required interim report to the competent authority within the applicable DORA deadline. They concern different recipients and different reporting functions, so there is no incompatibility in obeying both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity suffers one incident that significantly affects the provision of its services and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. It must, where applicable, immediately notify its service recipients under A, and must also submit the interim report after its initial notification to the relevant competent authority under B; notifying the recipients does not constitute the separate report to the authority, and the texts provide no rule making one filing sufficient for the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the cumulative reporting burden on the texts shown; the decisive point is that A and B identify different recipients and separate communications. The optional wording in A ('In voorkomend geval') limits when A is triggered but does not eliminate the overlap in the stated scenario.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: b) een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie, in voorkomend geval gevolgd door geactualiseerde kennisgevingen telkens wanneer een relevante actualisering van de status beschikbaar is, alsmede op specifiek verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit;

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related/significant incidents affecting a financial or essential/important entity’s services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident consequences and communications, but provision A does not impose a separate filing: it keeps the financial entity responsible for handling and consequences after reporting under Article 19(1). Provision B requires the entity to inform its service recipients without delay, so the duties could be viewed as overlapping incident-response obligations with different addressees.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties. A assigns continuing responsibility for handling reported ICT incidents; B requires prompt information to service recipients about significant incidents affecting service provision. Nothing in A says that responsibility replaces recipient notification, and A identifies no recipient or deadline that could conflict with B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onverminderd de ontvangen feedback van toezichthouders blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant ICT-related incidents by a financial/essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same significant incident, but they require communications to different recipients: the competent authority under A and the entity’s service recipients under B. The duties therefore appear cumulative rather than substitutable, with different timing formulations and no text stating that the authority filing satisfies the customer-information duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with together: the entity submits the required updated notification to the competent authority and separately informs affected service recipients without delay. They regulate different communications and do not impose contradictory content, recipient, or action requirements.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity experiences a significant ICT-related incident that adversely affects its services and whose status materially changes after the initial notification. It must submit an updated notification to the relevant competent authority within the Article 20 deadlines and, independently, inform its service recipients without delay; filing the updated notification with the authority does not inform the service recipients or discharge the separate duty to them.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in:
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents and their notification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern communicating information about cyber incidents, so an incident could prompt activity under both regimes. However, provision A assigns CSIRTs a general warning and notification function, while provision B requires national competent authorities to notify the Commission of serious incidents; the texts do not make these duties mutually exclusive or impose incompatible content or deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily be performed cumulatively: a CSIRT can issue early warnings, notifications, or announcements to relevant entities and authorities, while the national competent authority separately informs the Commission immediately of each serious incident. They concern different actors and recipients, and nothing in either text says that one communication substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and their effects on natural persons' rights and freedoms
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern the same high-risk AI deployment, but they impose different obligations on different actors: the controller must conduct a data-protection impact assessment before processing, while notified bodies check conformity under the AI Act's conformity-assessment procedures. One might argue that the AI conformity assessment could be treated as addressing the relevant risks, leaving uncertainty about whether a separate DPIA is still required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are cumulative and directed at different actors and functions. A controller can perform the required DPIA before processing, while a notified body separately checks the AI system's conformity under Article 43; neither text says that one assessment substitutes for or overrides the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity that is both a provider subject to art. 11.3a and an essential or important entity under art. 29
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same personal-data incident may trigger an immediate notification to the affected person under provision A and a separate final report to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority under provision B. These are different recipients, different documents and different deadlines, so neither filing appears to discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can notify the affected person without delay and later submit the required detailed report within one month after the Article 27 notification. The texts do not impose incompatible content or deadlines, and the fact that both concern the same incident does not make them alternatives.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An entity is both a provider covered by art. 11.3a and an essential or important entity under art. 29. A personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect an identified person’s privacy and is also an incident requiring the Article 27 notification. The entity must notify the affected person immediately, while separately filing a final report with its CSIRT and competent authority no later than one month after the Article 27 notification; notifying the person does not satisfy either institutional filing.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related incident governance by financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern an entity’s response to ICT incidents, but they impose different actions: Provision A requires a post-incident evaluation after a serious ICT-related disruption, while Provision B requires specified information and contact details in an early warning for a significant incident. One might argue that the same incident triggers two overlapping compliance processes with potentially different incident thresholds and timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and concern different actions at different stages. A post-incident evaluation analyses causes, procedures and effectiveness after a serious disruption; an early warning supplies information about the suspected cause, cross-border effects and the responsible reporting officer. Nothing in either text says that performing one duty substitutes for or prevents the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Nationale cyberincidenten en crisisrespons
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen concern the public cyber-incident response framework: CSIRTs must respond to incidents and assist entities where applicable, while the Minister must establish a national plan for large-scale incidents and crisis response. One might argue that the plan could prescribe a different allocation or method of response, creating an apparent coordination issue.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties on different actors and at different levels. Article 11(1)(c) assigns an operational task to CSIRTs, whereas Article 20 requires the Minister to establish a strategic national plan; nothing in either text prohibits the other duty or makes compliance with one incompatible with compliance with the other.

However, Provision A concerns one Member State reimbursing another Member State for compensation paid for damage caused by its supervisory-authority personnel, while Provision B concerns a telecommunications provider refunding a consumer for certain calls.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors, beneficiaries, triggering events, and payments. A Member State's inter-state reimbursement duty under Provision A can coexist fully with a provider's consumer-refund duty under Provision B; neither requires or forbids conduct that would prevent compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Human oversight of a high-risk AI system and an individual's right to object to certain personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives the data subject an individual right to object and requires the controller to stop processing unless overriding compelling legitimate grounds exist. Provision B requires the operator to enable human overseers, where appropriate and proportionate, to address irregularities, failures and unexpected performance; one might argue that continued system operation or remediation under B could conflict with stopping processing for an objecting individual, especially where the AI system processes that person's data.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: A governs an individual's objection to processing under specified GDPR legal bases, while B concerns the design and capabilities of human oversight for high-risk AI systems. Human oversight under B can include stopping or overriding the system, and nothing in B requires continued processing or states that its system-level duty overrides the individual's objection right; the controller can comply with both by stopping the relevant processing unless the exception in A applies.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily coexist because they are triggered by different activities and addressed to different authorities. verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident response, so an incident could require the financial entity to evaluate the effectiveness of its internal incident escalation while an electronic-communications provider is ordered to resolve an incident within a specified period. verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and processing that may create high data-protection risks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same operator and project: the GDPR requires prior consultation where a DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while Article 16 requires the AI provider to supply information required under Article 20 on a reasoned request from a national competent authority. One might argue that the provider could face overlapping information demands or uncertainty about which authority's process governs.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties triggered by different facts and addressed to different authorities or processes. Article 36 requires the controller to consult the data-protection supervisory authority before processing; the selected Article 16(j) duty requires an AI provider to provide Article 20 information when requested by a national competent authority, so complying with one does not prevent compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and regulatory oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern high-risk AI systems and involve regulatory safeguards, but they impose different duties on different actors in different procedures. Provision A requires a controller to consult a supervisory authority before high-risk processing; Provision B requires a national authority to confirm that certified high-risk AI systems pose no risks to health, safety or fundamental rights in specified certification circumstances.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with together because they regulate different actors, triggers and processes: A concerns a data controller's prior consultation for processing presenting a high risk, while B concerns continuation of certificate validity after a notified body's designation changes. Nothing in B dispenses with or contradicts the consultation duty in A, and nothing in A prevents the authority from making the certification-related confirmation required by B.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk assessment/compliance obligations for regulated AI processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to a high-risk AI system, but they impose different compliance mechanisms: GDPR Article 36 requires prior consultation with the supervisory authority when the DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while Article 43(3) concerns using an exemption from third-party conformity assessment based on harmonised standards. One might argue that reliance on standards under Article 43 could be treated as sufficient risk mitigation, making prior consultation under Article 36 appear duplicative.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties on different matters and are triggered by different facts. Article 36 concerns a controller's proposed personal-data processing and requires consultation where the DPIA shows high residual risk without mitigation; the selected Article 43 paragraph merely conditions a manufacturer's optional use of a third-party-assessment exemption on applying standards or common specifications. Compliance with the latter neither substitutes for nor prevents the former.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related documentation and notification by entities processing personal data and subject to NIS2
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the controller to document every personal-data breach for the supervisory authority's compliance checks, while provision B may require the entity to notify its service recipients immediately of a significant incident adversely affecting service provision. If the same incident is both a personal-data breach and a significant incident, these are different acts directed to different purposes and potentially different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can maintain the documentation required by A and, where applicable, notify service recipients under B. Provision A does not prohibit notification, and provision B does not state that recipient notification replaces or conflicts with breach documentation.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident prevention and investigation by an entity operating network and information systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision B requires the entity to take measures to prevent incidents, while provision A restricts an investigation after a serious incident if it would modify the AI system in a way that could affect later evaluation of the incident’s causes without prior notice to the competent authorities. One might argue that preventive or corrective security work could require such system changes and therefore be delayed by the notice condition.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties that can both be satisfied: the entity may take appropriate preventive measures under B and, if a post-incident investigation would make a causally relevant system change, give the competent authorities prior notice under A. Provision A does not prohibit all changes or preventive measures; it only prohibits the specified investigation without prior notice.

Provision B assigns the CSIRT an information-sharing task concerning cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents, and does not regulate investment-screening deadlines, ministerial decisions, or disclosure of investment information. The provisions therefore impose no incompatible duties on the same actor or subject matter.
