verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and assessment of risks to natural persons’ rights and freedoms
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions address high-risk systems and fundamental-rights risks, but they impose different obligations: Article 35 GDPR requires the controller to conduct a data-protection impact assessment before processing where processing is likely to create a high risk, while Article 36(1)(a) AI Act requires a national authority to have confirmed that the relevant high-risk AI systems pose no risk to health, safety or fundamental rights for certificates to remain valid. One might argue that a positive GDPR assessment identifying residual risks could sit uneasily with the Article 36 confirmation of no risk.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors, triggers and functions. Article 35 requires a controller to perform a prior assessment of processing-related risks to individuals’ rights and freedoms; Article 36(1)(a) concerns a national competent authority’s confirmation, in the specific context of continued certificate validity after a notified body’s designation is withdrawn, that high-risk AI systems pose no risk to health, safety or fundamental rights. A controller can perform the GDPR assessment and the authority can separately make the Article 36 confirmation; neither text says that one assessment substitutes for or legally contradicts the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both NIS2 and the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an incident-reporting obligation, and a serious AI incident could also be a significant incident. The strongest tension case is that the AI Act report is due within 15 days of awareness, while the NIS2 final report is due within one month after the incident is handled, potentially creating two reporting duties on different clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish that the same incident necessarily falls within both regimes, and the quoted NIS2 norm concerns a final report following an earlier NIS2 incident notification, whereas the AI Act norm concerns the report referenced in Article 73(1). If both regimes apply, the texts can be complied with cumulatively; neither says that one report substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An operator is both a NIS2 ‘betrokken entiteit’ and an AI Act provider of a high-risk AI system. A serious AI-system incident is also a significant incident under NIS2, and the incident remains unresolved for more than one month. The operator must make the AI Act serious-incident report within 15 days of awareness and must later submit the NIS2 final report no later than one month after the incident is handled; making the first report does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate NIS2 final-report duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive issue is whether the same incident qualifies under both regimes and whether any unshown coordination or exemption rule treats one filing as satisfying the other. The provisions shown contain no such substitution rule.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use the verb “waarschuwingen geven,” which could superficially suggest that the same warning activity is governed by two different norms. verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an immediate communication duty triggered by a serious/significant ICT incident. verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are addressed to different recipients and concern different information: A is a regulatory progress report, whereas B is a client notification about the incident and mitigation measures. They can therefore be performed cumulatively without either duty preventing compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Enforcement powers concerning internet traffic and data-protection obligations

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same entity's cable-maintenance work on public land also constituted a significant incident, Provision A would require a prior notification to the municipal mayor (or authorised official), while Provision B would require an incident notification to both the CSIRT and competent authority. verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 7 verplicht iedere lidstaat een strategie vast te stellen die aan inhoudelijke eisen voldoet. Artikel 19 wijst de Nederlandse minister, in overeenstemming met de betrokken ministers, aan als degene die die strategie vaststelt; men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat een nationale verplichting en een nationale bevoegdheidsbepaling niet volledig samenvallen als artikel 19 geen afzonderlijke inhoudelijke uitvoeringsplicht bevat.

De minister kan een strategie vaststellen die alle in artikel 7 genoemde onderdelen bevat; artikel 7 legt de lidstaat de inhoudelijke resultaatsverplichting op, terwijl artikel 19 de nationale bevoegdheids- en besluitvormingsregeling bepaalt.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk classification and related documentation/consultation duties for AI or data-processing activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern a high-risk activity, but they use different triggers and address different duties: Article 36 GDPR is triggered by a DPIA finding that processing would pose a high risk without mitigation, while Article 6(3) AI Act concerns a provider’s assessment that an Annex III AI system is not high-risk and requires that assessment documentation on request. A provider could therefore face uncertainty about whether the activity’s classification under the AI Act has any bearing on the separate GDPR consultation trigger.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties on different actors and under different conditions, not incompatible commands. A provider can supply its AI Act assessment documentation when requested, while the controller separately consults the GDPR supervisory authority if the DPIA produces the Article 36 trigger; neither provision says that one assessment or duty substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider places an Annex III AI system on the market after documenting its view that the system is not high-risk and later supplies that documentation to a national competent authority on request. Separately, the customer/controller’s DPIA concludes that the proposed processing would pose a high risk without mitigation, requiring the controller to consult the GDPR supervisory authority before processing. The same system is therefore outside the provider’s claimed Article 6 high-risk classification but within the GDPR Article 36 consultation trigger.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity risk management, including identifying and handling ICT incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose duties concerning ICT and cybersecurity risk, but they apply through different legislative regimes and use somewhat different formulations: A requires risk-proportionate measures to manage risks and prevent or mitigate incidents, while B requires simplified-framework entities to identify and detect risks and anomalies as soon as possible and handle ICT incidents quickly. One might argue that the different proportionality and speed-oriented formulations create uncertainty about the applicable benchmark.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can readily be satisfied together: an entity can adopt risk-proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures under A while also maintaining documented ICT-risk controls that promptly detect anomalies and rapidly handle incidents under B. Neither provision says that compliance with one substitutes for, overrides, or conflicts with the other; moreover, B applies only to specified exempt or small financial entities, whereas A concerns essential and important entities.

verdict.shared_subject: Information duties concerning measures or cyber threats affecting network or service recipients/subscribers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information duties on an entity taking or responding to a security threat. If the same measure responds to a significant cyber threat, A requires notice to the affected subscriber as soon as possible when prior notice is impossible, while B requires the essential or important entity to inform potentially affected service recipients without delay about available measures and, if necessary, the threat itself; the texts do not expressly say that one notice satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the provider/entity can send one timely communication to the relevant subscriber or service recipients containing both the measure and the available response measures, and, where necessary, the significant threat. The texts do not establish different recipients, incompatible content, or incompatible deadlines; B's 'onverwijld' and A's 'zo snel mogelijk' can be met by the same prompt communication.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and early-warning content

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions guide authorities when responding to infringements and require attention to case-related factors. verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, compatible requirements rather than incompatible commands: an authority can consider relevant previous infringements while also ensuring that any GDPR fine is effective, proportionate and dissuasive. verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires, where applicable, notifying the entity’s service recipients without delay when a significant incident may adversely affect service provision. Provision B separately requires certain financial-sector entities to make the Article 19 notifications, including voluntary notifications, also to the sectoral CSIRT; these are different recipients and the texts do not say that notifying service recipients satisfies the CSIRT duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: an entity can notify its service recipients under A and report the relevant incident to the designated sectoral CSIRT under B. Moreover, A’s recipient-notification duty is conditional ('In voorkomend geval'), while B concerns a distinct statutory incident report, so neither duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank subject to both provisions experiences a significant ICT incident that adversely affects its customers’ services and is also an incident covered by the Article 19 notification obligation. The bank must notify its service recipients without delay under A and separately make the Article 19 notification to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors under B; notifying customers does not discharge the CSIRT filing, and B specifies no deadline that resolves how the two duties interact.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident enforcement and information-sharing by Dutch/EU authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern official responses to cybersecurity-related non-compliance or incidents. One might argue that the warning competence in provision A overlaps with the information-sharing duty in provision B, potentially raising questions about which authority should act or communicate.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A merely gives competent authorities power to issue warnings about infringements by important entities. Provision B imposes a separate duty on the central contact point to notify the relevant CSIRT and competent authority when information from another Member State indicates effects on services in the Netherlands. The provisions concern different actors, triggers, and actions, and nothing in either text makes a warning incompatible with that notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: a) waarschuwingen te geven over inbreuken op deze richtlijn door de betrokken entiteiten;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Als uit gegevens die het centrale contactpunt heeft ontvangen van een centraal contactpunt van een andere lidstaat van de Europese Unie blijkt dat een daar gemeld incident, bijna-incident of cyberdreiging gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van de diensten van een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit in Nederland, stelt het centrale contactpunt het betrokken CSIRT en de betrokken bevoegde autoriteit daarvan op de hoogte.

verdict.shared_subject: Communication or reporting of significant cyber threats and serious ICT-related incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires essential and important entities to notify recipients of their services of the significant cyber threat itself. B requires financial entities to submit an initial notification and subsequent reports about serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority. If a financial entity is also an essential or important entity and the same event is both a significant cyber threat to service recipients and a serious ICT-related incident, the duties concern different recipients and separate communications.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with: the entity can notify affected service recipients under A and separately report the incident to the competent authority under B. They do not impose incompatible content, timing, or recipient requirements, and B's reporting does not purport to replace A's communication.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity experiences a serious ICT-related incident that constitutes a significant cyber threat to its service recipients. It must communicate the threat itself to “die ontvangers” under A and submit the required initial notification and later reports to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” under B; filing with the authority does not notify the service recipients, and notifying the recipients does not satisfy the authority-reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in:

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident under Article 23 must be reported immediately to the entity’s CSIRT or competent authority. B requires financial entities to prepare and submit an initial notification and reports under Article 19(4), using DORA models, to the relevant competent authority; the regimes may therefore impose separate reporting content and procedures for the same incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: a financial entity can report the incident under DORA to its relevant competent authority while also making the NIS2 report to its CSIRT or competent authority. Article 19(6) expressly contemplates that DORA reports may additionally be provided to NIS2-designated competent authorities or CSIRTs, which supports coexistence rather than an inability to comply with both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity experiences an incident that is both a DORA “ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident” and a NIS2 “significant incident.” It must submit the DORA initial notification and subsequent reports to the relevant competent authority using the Article 20 models, while also immediately reporting the significant incident to its CSIRT or competent authority under NIS2; filing the DORA report alone does not clearly discharge the separate NIS2 duty, particularly where the NIS2 recipient is the CSIRT or where the required formats and reporting sequences differ.
verdict.decisive_exception: No exception is shown that makes one filing legally sufficient for the other. Article 19(6) permits Member States to require additional transmission of DORA reports to NIS2 authorities or CSIRTs, but it does not state that the DORA filing automatically replaces the Article 23 report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident or cyber-threat reporting by entities potentially subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an incident notification to the CSIRT or competent authority within 72 hours after knowledge of a significant incident. Provision B permits financial entities to make a voluntary significant-cyber-threat report to a relevant competent authority, which may forward it to other authorities; however, the shown B text does not establish a mandatory second filing, nor does it require reporting to the ECB for every event covered by A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be satisfied together because B is expressly voluntary: a financial entity may choose not to make the B notification and still comply with A. If it does make the voluntary notification, B concerns a significant cyber-threat judged relevant to specified interests, while A concerns a significant incident, so the texts do not establish that the same event necessarily triggers both duties or that two mandatory filings are required.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision B's voluntary character is decisive: it states that financial entities may report significant cyber-threats 'op vrijwillige basis'. The related DORA provision on mandatory reporting deadlines and recipients is not part of the norm being compared and cannot convert this shown voluntary norm into a mandatory second filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Termination or suspension of services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a third ICT provider to continue supplying critical or important ICT services during a mandatory transition period. Provision B permits an internet-access provider to suspend service for specified reasons, including non-payment or bankruptcy. If the same provider and service were subject to both, the continuation duty could appear to conflict with the suspension competence.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors and service contexts: A concerns contractual exit strategies for ICT services supporting critical or important functions, while B concerns an internet-access provider's statutory competence to suspend an end-user's internet access. Moreover, B's listed grounds are permissions, not duties, and A does not state that its continuation obligation overrides a statutory suspension ground; the provider can comply with both by continuing service unless a valid B ground is exercised.
verdict.decisive_exception: None established as necessary: the apparent overlap is avoided because Provision B is permissive and concerns a different service/actor context; the provisions can be cumulatively complied with.
verdict.evidence_span_a: waarin de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten de levering van de respectieve functies of ICT-diensten zal blijven voortzetten
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een aanbieder van een internettoegangsdienst aan een eindgebruiker kan de levering van deze dienst slechts geheel of gedeeltelijk beëindigen of opschorten

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a personal-data breach or serious incident by an operator subject to both GDPR Article 33 and AI Act Article 26
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without unreasonable delay after learning of a personal-data breach, while Article 26 requires a high-risk AI-system operator that detects a serious incident to notify first the provider and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities. If the same event is both a personal-data breach and a serious incident, the provisions point to different reporting recipients and sequences, and one notification does not expressly discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the processor informs the controller under Article 33 and the AI-system operator makes the Article 26 notifications. Article 33 does not prohibit additional notifications, and Article 26 does not state that its notifications replace the GDPR communication.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company operates a high-risk AI system and acts as a processor for a controller. A cyberattack causes a personal-data breach and is also detected as a serious incident involving the high-risk AI system. The company must inform the controller without unreasonable delay under Article 33, and must first notify the provider and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities under Article 26; notifying the controller does not notify those AI-Act recipients, and the texts do not establish which reporting sequence governs the combined event.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory notifications and their processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern notifications handled through regulatory or incident-reporting channels, so one might initially suspect competing notification workflows or priorities. However, Provision A requires a notifying authority to inform the Commission and other Member States of changes to a notified body's notification, while Provision B concerns the CSIRT's processing of voluntary incident-related reports and expressly permits prioritising mandatory reports.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors concerning different notifications: the notifying authority must transmit changes in a notified-body notification, whereas the CSIRT processes voluntary incident reports. Nothing in Provision B prevents the authority from making the notification required by Provision A, and Provision A does not regulate CSIRT processing or prioritisation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanmeldende autoriteit stelt de Commissie en de andere lidstaten via het in artikel 30, lid 2, bedoelde elektronische aanmeldingssysteem in kennis van alle relevante wijzigingen in de aanmelding van een aangemelde instantie.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verwerkt de vrijwillige meldingen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, overeenkomstig de in artikel 36 omschreven procedure.

verdict.shared_subject: Rapportage door gereguleerde entiteiten aan bevoegde autoriteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen informatieverplichtingen op aan mogelijk overlappende gereguleerde actoren, maar zij zien op verschillende informatie en richten zich tot verschillende autoriteiten: A vereist incidentmeldingen aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B bepaalde omstandigheden aan de aanmeldende autoriteit laat melden. Als één actor onder beide regimes valt en één gebeurtenis beide triggers activeert, kan één melding de andere niet zonder meer vervangen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen hebben verschillende adressaten en inhoudelijke triggers. A betreft geactualiseerde kennisgevingen over ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten na een eerste kennisgeving; B betreft omstandigheden die het toepassingsgebied of de voorwaarden voor aanmelding beïnvloeden. De teksten kunnen dus cumulatief worden nageleefd door afzonderlijke meldingen te doen, zonder dat zij elkaar verbieden of deadlines onverenigbaar maken.
verdict.evidence_span_a: in voorkomend geval gevolgd door geactualiseerde kennisgevingen telkens wanneer een relevante actualisering van de status beschikbaar is
verdict.evidence_span_b: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-response duties following reports of serious/significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern follow-up after an incident notification and impose prompt action. If the same incident is reported under both regimes, the market-surveillance authority must act within seven days, while the CSIRT must respond immediately and, where possible, within 24 hours; this could create coordination or timing pressure, especially because the duties concern different institutional responses.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors: provision A binds the market-surveillance authority, whereas provision B binds the CSIRT. They also require different actions for different recipients and do not require the same actor to choose between incompatible acts; each authority can perform its own duty, including the CSIRT's conditional provision of guidance on request.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verstrekt onverwijld en zo mogelijk binnen 24 uur na ontvangst van de vroegtijdige waarschuwing, bedoeld in artikel 26, een antwoord aan de meldende entiteit

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related obligations, but concerning different actors and events
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations connected with ICT or network security. In a very broad sense, a financial entity that is also an internet-access provider might have to conduct a post-incident evaluation while separately notifying a subscriber before taking a protective measure, creating additional compliance work.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different duties with different triggers and purposes. Provision A requires financial entities to perform post-incident evaluations after serious ICT incidents affecting core activities; provision B requires an internet-access provider to notify an affected subscriber before, or promptly after, a measure taken to protect network, service, or device integrity and security. Nothing in either text prevents performing both duties when their independent conditions are met.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose mandatory conduct, but they regulate different actors and subjects: GDPR art. 33 concerns a controller documenting personal-data breaches, while BWBR0009950 art. 5.4 concerns municipal executive authorities adopting a consent decision after a telecom works notification. No realistic fact pattern makes the same actor unable to perform both duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are fully compatible because they apply to different actors, concern different actions, and have different regulatory purposes. A controller can document all personal-data breaches while municipal authorities independently adopt a consent decision within the stated period.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.

verdict.shared_subject: Member States’ notifications to the Commission concerning national cybersecurity matters
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties on Member States within three months and both permit withholding information where necessary for national security. A possible concern is that the provisions cover overlapping national cybersecurity information and use slightly different formulations for the national-security withholding discretion.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different triggering events and information: Article 7 concerns notification of a national cybersecurity strategy, while Article 9 concerns notification of a cyber-crisis-management authority and information about national plans. Each duty can be performed within its own three-month period, and the national-security clauses can be applied cumulatively without making either duty impossible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lidstaten stellen de Commissie in kennis van hun nationale cyberbeveiligingsstrategieën binnen drie maanden na de vaststelling ervan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Binnen drie maanden na de aanwijzing of instelling van de in lid 1 bedoelde cybercrisisbeheerautoriteit stelt elke lidstaat de Commissie in kennis van de identiteit van zijn autoriteit en van alle latere wijzigingen ervan.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity governance and measures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose cybersecurity-related organisational action, but Provision A requires ENISA to establish appropriate information systems, policies and procedures for the European vulnerability database, while Provision B requires national competent authorities to take appropriate measures to ensure an adequate level of cybersecurity. One might argue that the different institutional duties use potentially different standards for what counts as appropriate or adequate.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions bind different actors and address different objects: ENISA's database-related systems and procedures versus national authorities' broader cybersecurity measures. They can be complied with cumulatively, and nothing in either text says that satisfying one duty substitutes for or prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Daartoe stelt Enisa de passende informatiesystemen, beleidsmaatregelen en procedures vast en onderhoudt deze
verdict.evidence_span_b: De nationale bevoegde autoriteiten nemen passende maatregelen om te zorgen voor een adequaat niveau van cyberbeveiliging.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory notifications by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties, and a single circumstance could potentially also constitute a significant incident. However, the provisions address different triggering facts and different actors: A concerns circumstances affecting a notified conformity-assessment body's notification scope or conditions, while B concerns a significant incident involving an essential or important entity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively if the same organisation happens to fall within both categories and both triggers occur. A notification to the notifying authority under A is not the same filing as a notification to the CSIRT and competent authority under B, so neither duty inherently discharges the other; absent a shared triggering event established by the texts, there is no concrete conflict.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant ICT-related/significant incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to submit updated notifications after an initial notification to the relevant competent authority, while Provision B separately requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29. If the same entity and incident fall within both regimes, the texts could impose separate reporting duties with potentially different procedures and recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: an entity can make the updates required by A and also report the incident under B. Provision B does not state that its report replaces A's notifications, and the text shown does not establish different recipients or incompatible deadlines; therefore, the evidence is insufficient for a dual-reporting tension.
verdict.missing_reference: Articles 26–29 of BWBR0052872, and the implementing deadlines/procedures under Article 20 of Regulation 2022/2554, would be needed to determine whether the duties require separate filings to different recipients or operate through the same report.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT-network and national CSIRT functions concerning cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations involving cyber-threat, vulnerability and incident information, monitoring, and analysis. One could argue that the EU-level CSIRT network’s information-exchange task and the national CSIRT’s monitoring-and-analysis task create overlapping operational responsibilities, with uncertainty about which body must perform the relevant activity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions assign complementary functions rather than incompatible duties: the CSIRT network exchanges relevant information among CSIRTs, while the national CSIRT monitors and analyses threats, vulnerabilities and incidents at national level. A national CSIRT can perform its national monitoring duty and also exchange the resulting information through the network; neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a measure or significant incident by an entity subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber of the measure, while Provision B requires the essential or important entity to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority. If the same measure is taken in response to the same significant incident, these are separate communications to different recipients, with A requiring notice as soon as possible and B requiring a report without delay or within 72 hours.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed: the provider can notify the subscriber under A and separately report the significant incident to the CSIRT and competent authority under B. The duties have different recipients and purposes, so neither filing purports to replace the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity takes a measure under Article 7.6a to remove a threat to the integrity or security of its network, service or terminal equipment, and the same event is also a significant incident known to the entity. It must notify the affected subscriber as soon as possible under A and separately submit a report to its CSIRT and competent authority without delay or within 72 hours under B; notifying the subscriber does not discharge the two authority reports.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related compliance and remediation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns an authority’s power to order an essential entity to remedy identified NIS2 deficiencies or infringements, while Provision B requires financial entities to establish and implement an ICT-incident process that includes reporting incidents. If the same entity is subject to both regimes, an enforcement order under A could require remediation of failures that include the reporting process required by B, creating overlapping compliance obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties on different actors and at different levels: A authorises competent authorities to issue remediation orders to essential entities, whereas B directly obliges financial entities to operate an incident-management process and report ICT incidents. Nothing in either text forbids compliance with the other, and an entity can both maintain the required process/report incidents and remedy any deficiencies identified by an authority.

verdict.shared_subject: Indiening van voortgangs-/tussentijdse verslagen door entiteiten bij ICT-incidenten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen na een ICT-incident een vervolgverslag verlangen. A ziet echter op een voortgangsverslag dat op een bepaald moment moet worden ingediend, terwijl B een tussentijds verslag en geactualiseerde kennisgevingen verlangt bij een ingrijpende statuswijziging of nieuwe informatie; als beide regimes op dezelfde financiële entiteit en hetzelfde incident van toepassing zijn, kan onduidelijk zijn of afzonderlijke stukken en termijnen gelden.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn cumulatief verenigbaar: A verlangt een voortgangsverslag aan het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B verslaglegging aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit verlangt volgens nog vast te stellen termijnen. Niets in de getoonde teksten verbiedt dubbele rapportage of bepaalt dat het ene verslag het andere vervangt; bovendien kan één verslag mogelijk beide informatiebehoeften vervullen, afhankelijk van de toepasselijke procedures en modellen.
verdict.missing_reference: De ontbrekende bepalingen over de toepasselijke termijnen en procedures in artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), van Verordening (EU) 2022/2554, alsmede de niet getoonde bepalingen die bepalen of een financiële entiteit onder Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555 als betrokken entiteit valt en of rapportage aan dezelfde bevoegde autoriteit het verslag onder beide regimes dekt.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the Commission to notify the European Parliament and the Council simultaneously after adopting a delegated act. Provision B requires a financial entity’s management body to establish internal reporting channels for information about ICT-service-provider arrangements and related changes; the duties concern different actors and actions, so no genuine collision is apparent.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The Commission’s notification duty and the financial entity’s internal-channel duty can both be performed independently. Neither provision restricts, delays, or makes impossible the conduct required by the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Zodra de Commissie een gedelegeerde handeling heeft vastgesteld, doet zij daarvan gelijktijdig kennisgeving aan het Europees Parlement en de Raad.
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over:

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingsplichten van een aanbieder in verband met een ernstig incident en een maatregel ter bescherming van netwerk- of dienstveiligheid.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij één feitelijke gebeurtenis kan een aanbieder zowel een ernstig AI-incident moeten melden als, voorafgaand aan of na een veiligheidsmaatregel, de betrokken abonnee moeten informeren. Dat zijn echter meldingen met verschillende aanleiding en ontvanger; naleving van de AI-melding aan de markttoezichtautoriteit vervangt de abonnee-informatie niet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen geen tegenstrijdige handelingen op: een aanbieder kan beide meldingen verrichten. Bovendien geldt artikel 73 alleen voor ernstige incidenten met de in de context genoemde AI-systemen, terwijl artikel 7.6a ziet op een maatregel ter bescherming van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat; zonder samenloop van die triggers zijn de plichten afzonderlijk.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een aanbieder van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem ontdekt een ernstig incident dat tevens de integriteit of veiligheid van het netwerk of randapparaat van een abonnee bedreigt. De aanbieder moet het incident uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat hij zich daarvan bewust wordt melden volgens artikel 73, en moet de betrokken abonnee vóór de veiligheidsmaatregel informeren of, als spoed dat onmogelijk maakt, zo snel mogelijk daarna; de melding aan de markttoezichtautoriteit vervangt de afzonderlijke melding aan de abonnee niet.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen. Wanneer dit wegens de vereiste spoed niet voorafgaand aan het nemen van de maatregel mogelijk is, doet de aanbieder zo snel mogelijk melding van de maatregel.

verdict.shared_subject: Het indienen van een tussentijds verslag na een significant/ernstig ICT-incident door een financiële entiteit die onder beide regelingen valt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen dezelfde financiële entiteit en hetzelfde ICT-incident betreffen, maar zij leggen tussentijdse rapportage op binnen verschillende rapportagestelsels: Richtlijn 2022/2555 verlangt een verslag op verzoek van het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl DORA een tussentijds verslag verlangt na de eerste kennisgeving bij een ingrijpende statuswijziging of gewijzigde behandeling, en ook op specifiek verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit. De teksten tonen niet aan dat één DORA-verslag automatisch het afzonderlijke NIS2-verslag aan het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit vervangt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: de entiteit kan één inhoudelijk afgestemd verslag opstellen en dit, waar de regimes dat toestaan, aan de relevante ontvangers verstrekken. Bovendien is de NIS2-verplichting in de getoonde norm slechts geactiveerd 'op verzoek', zodat zonder zo'n verzoek geen botsing ontstaat.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een financiële entiteit is tevens een betrokken entiteit onder Richtlijn 2022/2555. Na een ernstig ICT-incident dient zij haar eerste DORA-kennisgeving in bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit. De status van het incident wijzigt ingrijpend, zodat zij op grond van DORA een tussentijds verslag moet indienen; vervolgens verzoekt het NIS2-CSIRT afzonderlijk om een tussentijds verslag over relevante updates. De entiteit moet dan het DORA-verslag bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit indienen én het NIS2-verslag aan het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit verstrekken; de teksten bepalen niet dat de eerste indiening de tweede vervangt.
verdict.decisive_exception: De precieze termijnen en eventuele coördinatie- of vrijstellingsregels uit artikel 20, lid 1, punt a), ii), van Verordening 2022/2554 en de overige omzettings-/uitvoeringsregels van Richtlijn 2022/2555 zijn niet getoond. Zij kunnen bepalen of één gezamenlijk verslag of één ontvanger volstaat; op basis van de getoonde bepalingen is zo'n substitutieregel niet vastgesteld.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) op verzoek van het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit, een tussentijds verslag indienen over relevante updates van de situatie;
verdict.evidence_span_b: b) een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie, in voorkomend geval gevolgd door geactualiseerde kennisgevingen telkens wanneer een relevante actualisering van de status beschikbaar is, alsmede op specifiek verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit;

verdict.shared_subject: Use of personal data in a high-risk AI system by a public-service provider or other covered deployer
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives an individual an immediately exercisable right to object to certain processing and requires the controller to stop unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Article 27 requires a covered deployer to conduct a fundamental-rights impact assessment, including identifying affected persons, risks, human oversight, and complaint arrangements; one might argue that this system-level assessment could be treated as addressing the objection right, but the text does not say that it replaces or overrides individual objections.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative and independently satisfiable duties. A deployer can perform the Article 27 assessment and still stop particular processing when an individual objects under Article 21, unless it establishes the specified overriding grounds; Article 27(4) expressly describes the assessment as complementary to a GDPR data-protection impact assessment rather than as a substitute for individual rights.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke staakt de verwerking van de persoonsgegevens tenzij hij dwingende gerechtvaardigde gronden voor de verwerking aanvoert die zwaarder wegen dan de belangen, rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkene of die verband houden met de instelling, uitoefening of onderbouwing van een rechtsvordering.
verdict.evidence_span_b: de specifieke risico’s op schade die waarschijnlijk gevolgen zullen hebben voor de op grond van punt c) van dit lid geïdentificeerde categorieën natuurlijke personen of groepen personen

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related obligations concerning a provider/entity and personal-data incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply around the same significant incident, but they impose different content requirements rather than contradictory duties: A requires notifying the affected person, while B requires including specified information and the responsible official’s contact details in an early warning. The strongest possible tension case is that the same incident may require separate communications on different procedural tracks, but provision B does not identify its recipient, deadline, or whether it is the same communication as A’s notice.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily be performed cumulatively. The actor can notify the affected person without delay under A and, in the early warning under B, provide the responsible official’s contact details; neither provision forbids or makes compliance with the other impossible. B’s requirement is not shown to be an alternative or substitute for A’s notice.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding

v3_tightened_tensions::gpt-5.6-luna::non.needs_recheck_reason: evidence_span_b is not a verbatim substring of norm B's provision text

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT-taken inzake cyberincidenten en cyberdreigingen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen een CSIRT een operationele verplichting op, maar zij zien op verschillende handelingen: A vereist op verzoek bespreking en waar mogelijk uitvoering van een gecoördineerde respons op een incident, terwijl B het verstrekken en verspreiden van waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen voorschrijft indien mogelijk. Bij één incident kunnen beide taken tegelijk ontstaan, maar niets in de teksten maakt de handelingen of voorwaarden onverenigbaar.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Een CSIRT kan zonder probleem zowel een gecoördineerde respons bespreken/uitvoeren als waarschuwingen en meldingen verspreiden. De bepalingen hebben verschillende triggers en functies, en de voorwaarde “indien mogelijk” in B laat ruimte om de waarschuwingstaak naast de responsverplichting uit te voeren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: g) op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk, het bespreken en waar mogelijk uitvoeren van een gecoördineerde respons op een incident dat binnen de jurisdictie van die lidstaat is vastgesteld;
verdict.evidence_span_b: b. het verstrekken van vroegtijdige waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen en het verspreiden van informatie aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit, de bevoegde autoriteiten, Onze Minister van Economische Zaken, ten behoeve van de uitvoering van de taken, bedoeld in artikel 2, eerste lid, van de Wet bevordering digitale weerbaarheid bedrijven, en andere relevante partijen over cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten, indien mogelijk in bijna-realtime;

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risicobeheer en beveiligingsmaatregelen voor netwerk- en informatiesystemen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen een beveiligings- of ICT-risicobeheerplicht op, maar art. 16 verlangt dat bronnen van risico’s en anomalieën zo spoedig mogelijk worden geïdentificeerd en gedetecteerd, terwijl art. 21 proportionaliteit afstemt op onder meer blootstelling, omvang, incidentkans en gevolgen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat een kleine of weinig blootgestelde entiteit onder art. 21 minder vergaande detectiemaatregelen mag nemen dan de snelle detectieplicht van art. 16 suggereert.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: art. 16 bepaalt een concrete operationele doelstelling voor identificatie, detectie en incidentafhandeling, terwijl art. 21 voorschrijft dat de maatregelen proportioneel en risicogebaseerd worden gekozen. Art. 21 verbiedt niet dat een entiteit, rekening houdend met haar risico’s, maatregelen neemt die ook aan de specifieke detectieplicht van art. 16 voldoen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: ervoor zorgen dat bronnen van ICT-risico’s en anomalieën in de netwerk- en informatiesystemen zo spoedig mogelijk worden geïdentificeerd en gedetecteerd en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten snel kunnen worden afgehandeld
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten aanzien van de evenredigheid van de maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, houdt de entiteit naar behoren rekening met de mate waarin zij aan risico’s is blootgesteld, de omvang van de entiteit en de kans dat zich incidenten voordoen en de ernst ervan, met inbegrip van de maatschappelijke en economische gevolgen.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an entity subject to both GDPR Article 33 and NIS2 Article 23
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying personal-data breach must be reported to the GDPR supervisory authority, while a significant incident may require a separate notification to the entity’s service recipients. These are different recipients and distinct duties, so one notification does not necessarily discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers and can be complied with cumulatively: an entity can report the data breach to the supervisory authority and, where applicable, notify service recipients of the significant incident. Article 23’s recipient notification is conditional ('In voorkomend geval'), so it does not automatically apply to every incident covered by Article 33.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A cloud provider that is an essential or important entity suffers a cyberattack exposing customers’ personal data and significantly disrupting its services. The provider must, if the GDPR risk threshold is met, report the personal-data breach within 72 hours to 'de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit', and, where the significant incident may adversely affect service provision, notify 'de ontvangers van hun diensten' without delay. These are separate communications to different recipients; making the GDPR notification does not satisfy the customer notification duty, and vice versa.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 23 makes notification to service recipients conditional ('In voorkomend geval'), and the shown text does not specify when that condition is met. The dual-reporting conclusion applies where that condition is satisfied; it is not established that every Article 33 breach also triggers recipient notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident governance and reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern institutional responses to cybersecurity incidents, so one might initially suspect overlap between the competent authority’s incident-related feedback and the Minister’s national crisis-response plan. However, provision A concerns confirmation of receipt by the competent authority after a financial entity’s notification, while provision B concerns the Minister’s establishment of a national plan; neither requires or forbids the conduct specified by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and at different levels: the competent authority must confirm receipt of a notification, whereas the Minister establishes a national plan. The Minister’s plan can accommodate or coordinate such confirmations without preventing the competent authority from performing its duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: bevestigt de ontvangst ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister stelt een nationaal plan voor grootschalige cyberbeveiligingsincidenten en crisisrespons als bedoeld in artikel 9, vierde lid, van de NIS2-richtlijn vast.

v3_tightened_tensions::gpt-5.6-luna::non.needs_recheck_reason: evidence_span_a is not a verbatim substring of norm A's provision text

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of ICT-related incidents by certain financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the financial entity to submit updated notifications to the relevant competent authority after the initial notification. Provision B requires specified entities to make the Article 19 notification also to the sectoral CSIRT, so the same incident may require filings to two different recipients; filing with the competent authority would not, on the text shown, discharge the separate CSIRT duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can send the required notification to the relevant competent authority and also send it to the designated sectoral CSIRT. Provision B expressly uses “tevens” (also), indicating an additional recipient rather than an alternative or prohibition, and no incompatible deadline or content requirement is shown.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank has already submitted the initial serious ICT-incident notification to the relevant competent authority and then receives materially new information requiring an updated notification under Provision A. Under Provision A it must submit that update to the relevant competent authority; under Provision B it must also make the Article 19 notification to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors. These are separate filings to different recipients, and the text gives no rule stating that one filing discharges the other or clarifying how the update duty applies to the CSIRT filing.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting duplication. The decisive text is that Provision B requires the notification “tevens” to the designated CSIRT, while Provision A requires submission “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit.” The shown provisions do not establish whether the CSIRT filing must contain the same update, follow the same deadline, or be coordinated with the competent-authority filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie, in voorkomend geval gevolgd door geactualiseerde kennisgevingen telkens wanneer een relevante actualisering van de status beschikbaar is, alsmede op specifiek verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and serious ICT-related incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must promptly inform the controller of a personal-data breach, while B requires a financial entity to report serious ICT incidents to the relevant competent authority. A single incident could satisfy both triggers, requiring separate communications to different recipients, so one report would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the processor informs the controller without unreasonable delay, and the financial entity reports the serious ICT incident to the competent authority. They address different actors and recipients, and neither provision prevents the other communication.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also acting as a processor and suffers a serious ICT incident involving a personal-data breach. It must inform the controller without unreasonable delay under A and separately report the serious ICT incident to the relevant competent authority under B; informing the controller does not constitute reporting to that authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT security, integrity and governance
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose organisational or system-level ICT obligations, but they address different actors and objects: Enisa must secure and preserve the integrity of a European vulnerability database, while a financial entity’s governing body must establish governance and reporting channels. The overlap in ICT security terminology does not create an incompatible benchmark or duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations are cumulative and readily separable: Enisa’s database-security duty can be fulfilled through its own information systems, policies and measures, while the financial entity’s governing body establishes internal governance and information channels. Neither provision requires conduct that would prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de noodzakelijke technische en organisatorische maatregelen om de veiligheid en integriteit van de Europese kwetsbaarheidsdatabase te waarborgen
verdict.evidence_span_b: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over

verdict.shared_subject: Incident management and notification by financial entities that may also be high-risk AI-system users
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to establish integrated processes ensuring that ICT-incident root causes are detected, documented and removed, but it specifies no notification recipient or deadline. Provision B requires a high-risk AI-system user to notify specified external actors of a serious incident, creating an additional reporting duty that A neither addresses nor discharges.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties with different subject matter: A concerns internal ICT-incident management and root-cause remediation, while B concerns external notification of a serious AI incident. A financial entity can maintain the required internal processes and separately make B's notifications; nothing in either text forbids or substitutes for the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, teneinde ervoor te zorgen dat onderliggende oorzaken worden opgespoord, gedocumenteerd en weggenomen om dergelijke incidenten te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Compliance obligations concerning a high-risk AI system and its processing-related risks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply before a high-risk AI system is placed on the market: GDPR Article 36 requires prior consultation with the supervisory authority where a DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while the AI Act provision requires the importer to verify that the provider has appointed an authorised representative. One might argue that the importer’s verification obligation could require proceeding on the basis of provider documentation while the GDPR consultation could delay or affect the underlying processing, creating overlapping compliance steps.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different obligations on different actors and address different matters. Article 36 binds the controller of processing and requires prior consultation with the data-protection supervisory authority in a specified high-risk processing situation; Article 23(1)(d) binds an importer and requires checking whether the provider appointed an authorised representative before placing the AI system on the market. Nothing in either text forbids or substitutes for compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: de aanbieder een gemachtigde heeft aangewezen, in overeenstemming met artikel 22, lid 1

verdict.shared_subject: Processing and prioritisation of cyber-incident notifications by competent authorities and the CSIRT
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, where appropriate, to take all necessary measures to protect the immediate stability of the financial system after receiving and assessing information about a serious ICT-related incident. Provision B requires the CSIRT to process voluntary notifications, while allowing it to prioritise mandatory notifications; if the same incident information reaches both bodies, their operational priorities could diverge.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different actions: competent authorities take necessary stabilising measures, whereas the CSIRT processes voluntary notifications. Nothing in either text forbids the other duty, and the CSIRT's prioritisation rule does not prevent competent authorities from acting under Provision A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Op basis van die kennisgeving nemen de bevoegde autoriteiten, in voorkomend geval, alle nodige maatregelen om de onmiddellijke stabiliteit van het financiële systeem te beschermen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verwerkt de vrijwillige meldingen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, overeenkomstig de in artikel 36 omschreven procedure.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk processing or AI systems and their governance documentation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose advance or system-level governance obligations concerning potentially high-risk activities. However, Article 35 requires a data-protection impact assessment only when processing is likely to create a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms, while Article 17 requires a documented quality-management system for providers of high-risk AI systems; the texts do not specify whether one assessment can satisfy, replace, or be integrated into the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations have different content and can readily be performed cumulatively: the controller can conduct the GDPR impact assessment before processing and the AI provider can maintain the required quality-management system and documentation. Article 17 expressly requires a system covering many operational matters, whereas Article 35 requires an assessment of processing impacts and safeguards, so neither provision forbids compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van AI-systemen met een hoog risico voorzien in een systeem voor kwaliteitsbeheer dat de naleving van deze verordening waarborgt.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory language and concern institutional oversight, so one might initially suspect overlapping governance obligations. However, Provision A concerns governance of essential and important entities’ cybersecurity-risk measures, while Provision B concerns the Commission’s challenge and possible suspension or withdrawal of a notified body’s designation; they do not impose incompatible duties on the same actor or regulate the same underlying obligation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different actors, triggers, and subject matters. A requires Member States to ensure that governing bodies of essential and important entities approve and oversee cybersecurity measures; B empowers or requires action concerning a notified body that fails notification requirements, with suspension or withdrawal only where necessary or corrective action is not taken.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten de door deze entiteiten genomen maatregelen voor het beheer van cyberbeveiligingsrisico’s goedkeuren om te voldoen aan artikel 21, toezien op de uitvoering ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de lidstaat niet de nodige corrigerende actie onderneemt, kan de Commissie door middel van een uitvoeringshandeling de aanwijzing schorsen, beperken of intrekken.

verdict.shared_subject: Supervision of ICT or electronic-communications security incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the competent authority to acknowledge receipt of certain incident notifications and permits it to provide feedback to the financial entity. Provision B assigns designated officials of the Dutch Data Protection Authority supervisory responsibility for specified security or integrity breaches affecting personal data, so the authorities’ roles could overlap for an incident reported under A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different functions rather than incompatible commands: A concerns the competent authority’s receipt and possible feedback concerning DORA incident reports, while B allocates supervisory competence for particular breaches affecting personal data. Nothing in either text forbids the competent authority from acknowledging or giving feedback, or prevents the designated officials from exercising their separate supervisory role.

verdict.shared_subject: Voorafgaande risicobeoordeling en classificatie van systemen die persoonsgegevens verwerken

De twee beoordelingen kunnen dus tot verschillende toepassingsuitkomsten leiden, zonder dat de ene beoordeling de andere vervangt.

verdict.shared_subject: Informing service recipients/subscribers about a cyber threat or protective measure
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information duties that could arise around the same cybersecurity event, but they address different communications: A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber about a measure before or, if urgent, shortly after taking it, while B requires an essential or important entity to inform potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take and, if necessary, about the significant cyber threat. An enforcement order can require the entity to remedy a deficiency while the entity continues to apply the proportionality factors in B; nothing in A states that the order overrides or dispenses with those factors.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een bevel uit te vaardigen waarin de betrokken entiteiten worden verplicht de vastgestelde tekortkomingen of de inbreuken op deze richtlijn te verhelpen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ten aanzien van de evenredigheid van de maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, houdt de entiteit naar behoren rekening met de mate waarin zij aan risico’s is blootgesteld, de omvang van de entiteit en de kans dat zich incidenten voordoen en de ernst ervan, met inbegrip van de maatschappelijke en economische gevolgen.

verdict.shared_subject: Information and follow-up concerning incidents involving entities covered by both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related action and information flows, and a single serious incident involving a high-risk AI system operated by an essential entity that is also a critical entity could activate both regimes. However, provision A imposes a seven-day action duty on the market-surveillance authority, while provision B requires the CSIRT to provide information to the competent authority; the provisions do not impose incompatible duties on the same actor or establish conflicting deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are complementary and addressed to different institutional actors: the market-surveillance authority takes appropriate measures after receiving an AI serious-incident notification, while the CSIRT supplies incident information to the competent authority under the critical-entities regime. Each can be performed independently, and nothing in either text prevents both authorities from acting or the CSIRT from sharing the information.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen, en volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet.

verdict.shared_subject: A high-risk AI system involving personal-data processing before it is placed on the EU market
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose pre-deployment obligations concerning a high-risk activity: the controller must conduct a data-protection impact assessment where processing is likely to create a high risk, while the importer must verify that the required CE marking is affixed. One might argue that the importer’s conformity check could overlap with, or be treated as sufficient for, the GDPR risk assessment, but neither text says that it does.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and directed at different actors and objects: Article 35 requires the controller to assess the impact of intended personal-data processing, whereas Article 23 requires the importer to verify the product’s CE marking. Each can be performed independently, and nothing in either provision makes one duty substitute for or prevent compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Access to regulatory AI testing environments and access to domain-name registration data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory language concerning access, so one might superficially view them as overlapping access obligations. However, they impose duties on different actors, concern different objects, and are triggered by different conditions: priority access to AI regulatory sandboxes versus access to specific domain-registration data on a justified request.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The Member States' duty in provision A is to give qualifying SMEs priority access to AI regulatory test environments. Provision B requires domain-name registries or registration-service entities to provide specific registration data to a legitimate party making a lawful and duly motivated request. These duties can be fully performed simultaneously without contradiction.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations of regulated entities to public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification or reporting duties, and a real-world entity might be subject to both regimes. However, the duties concern different triggering matters: A concerns circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of a conformity-assessment notification, while B concerns an incident and requires a final report to specified cybersecurity recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations can be performed cumulatively without contradiction. A requires notification to the notifying authority, with no stated deadline, whereas B requires a final incident report within one month after the Article 27 notification to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority; neither provision says that one report substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity monitoring and enforcement involving essential entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern cybersecurity-related activity and use warning-related language. One might argue that the CSIRT’s monitoring role could overlap with the competent authority’s enforcement role, especially where monitoring reveals an infringement.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A merely gives competent authorities the power to issue warnings to entities for infringements of the Directive; it does not require or prohibit monitoring. Provision B assigns the CSIRT a national monitoring and analysis task, without regulating the competent authority’s warning power. The two functions can plainly coexist: the CSIRT can monitor and the authority can issue warnings based on identified infringements.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-incident management and reporting by entities subject to both instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to submit a progress report when the significant incident is still ongoing at the time the final report is due. Provision B separately requires financial entities to establish processes ensuring that underlying causes are identified, documented and remedied; one might argue that the reporting-related documentation and the remediation process impose overlapping incident-management burdens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties rather than incompatible ones. A is a conditional reporting duty concerning a specific significant incident and recipient, while B is an organisational process duty concerning registration, monitoring, follow-up and remediation; complying with B does not replace the progress report required by A, and nothing in either text forbids the other duty.
