verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents under the EU AI Act and Dutch cybersecurity legislation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same real-world incident and impose prompt reporting duties with different statutory triggers and deadlines. Provision B expressly requires a filing to both its CSIRT and competent authority, while provision A, read with the supplied context, requires a separate filing to market-surveillance authorities; one filing therefore does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different legal regimes and incident categories ('ernstige incidenten' versus 'significante incidenten'), so they may not overlap in every case. Even where they do overlap, both duties can be performed cumulatively; there is no textual impossibility in making both reports.

It must report the AI incident to the relevant market-surveillance authority immediately and no later than 15 days after awareness, while separately reporting the significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority immediately or, if that is not possible, within 72 hours; reporting to one set of recipients does not satisfy the other duty.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT functions concerning cybersecurity incidents and threats
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions assign cybersecurity functions to a CSIRT, and monitoring and analysing threats, vulnerabilities and incidents under Provision B could inform the coordinated incident response contemplated by Provision A. However, Provision A is a request-triggered cooperation duty, while Provision B is an unqualified monitoring-and-analysis duty; the texts do not make the duties incompatible or establish different benchmarks for the same duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and readily compatible: the CSIRT can continuously monitor and analyse threats, vulnerabilities and incidents under Provision B and, when a network member requests it, discuss and where possible carry out a coordinated response under Provision A. Nothing in either provision requires the CSIRT to stop monitoring, limits its analysis, or makes one duty substitute for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: g) op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk, het bespreken en waar mogelijk uitvoeren van een gecoördineerde respons op een incident dat binnen de jurisdictie van die lidstaat is vastgesteld;
verdict.evidence_span_b: a. het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau, en het op verzoek verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit met betrekking tot het realtime of bijna-realtime monitoren van haar netwerk- en informatiesysteem;

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and serious ICT-related incidents by a financial entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A single incident could qualify both as a personal-data breach and as a serious ICT-related incident. Article 33 requires a report to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours where applicable, while Article 19 requires a first notification to the relevant competent authority within separately determined Article 20 deadlines; the texts do not say that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can submit the GDPR breach notification and the DORA first notification, potentially using overlapping information. The authorities might in some cases be institutionally related, and the provisions do not expressly state that the reports must always be separate documents.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity suffers one cyberattack that causes a personal-data breach posing a likely risk to individuals and also qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. It must report the breach, if possible, within 72 hours of awareness “aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit” and separately submit the DORA first notification “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” within the Article 20 deadlines; filing one report with one authority does not, on the texts shown, discharge the other reporting duty.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a cybersecurity incident or threat by an actor potentially subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same financial entity is also an electronic-communications provider and the event qualifies both as a significant cyber threat and as a security breach adversely affecting personal-data protection, the provisions point to different recipients: the A-side reporting chain ultimately reaches the ECB, while B requires notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority. Both duties say the notification is made 'without delay', so one filing cannot discharge the other merely by being earlier.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: the entity can make the voluntary A-side notification through the relevant competent authority and separately notify the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens under B. There is no incompatible deadline or prohibition; both use an 'without delay' standard and can be performed in parallel.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst experiences one incident that is both a significant cyber threat relevant to the financial system and a security breach with adverse consequences for personal-data protection. It must make the A-side notification, which is forwarded to the ECB, and separately notify the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens 'onverwijld'; notifying one recipient does not notify the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De relevante bevoegde autoriteit kan dergelijke informatie aan de in lid 6 genoemde andere relevante autoriteiten verstrekken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and processing of personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a controller to conduct a data-protection impact assessment before processing where the processing is likely to create a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms. Provision B requires a high-risk AI provider to identify itself on the system or accompanying materials; these duties concern different actions and can be performed together without contradiction.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A provider can both conduct any required impact assessment before processing and display its name, registered name or trademark and contact address on the AI system or its documentation. Neither provision prohibits or excuses compliance with the other, and the provisions do not impose incompatible timing, content, or recipients.

If the same actor and event somehow fall within both triggers, the texts do not say that a report to the mayor satisfies the incident-reporting duty or identify the recipients and deadlines under Articles 26–29.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers and apparently different regulated actors: A concerns an operator carrying out cable-maintenance work on public land, whereas B concerns an essential or important entity experiencing a significant incident. A cable-maintenance activity is not necessarily a significant incident, and B's cross-referenced provisions may define its reporting recipient and timing. Each duty can therefore be performed independently, with no demonstrated incompatibility.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations triggered by different events under different regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a high-risk AI-system operator to notify specified parties of a serious incident, including the relevant market-surveillance authorities and, subsequently, the importer or distributor. verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different actors and triggers: A concerns a high-risk AI-system operator discovering a serious incident, while B concerns a provider taking a measure under Article 7.6a(1)(g) to address a network, service, or terminal-device integrity or security threat. verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity information exchange and oversight reports concerning ICT service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A facilitates voluntary information exchange among entities, potentially including information about cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and security procedures. Provision B empowers the lead overseer to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers concerning actions or corrective measures related to recommendations; one might argue that voluntary sharing could expose information that is later subject to oversight reporting, creating an additional burden or concern for the provider.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions establish different, cumulatively satisfiable arrangements. A requires Member States to enable voluntary cybersecurity information exchange, while B gives a supervisory authority a power to request specific reports from critical ICT third-party providers; neither provision prohibits the other, and A's exchange is optional rather than a mandatory duty that could collide with B.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related notifications by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity, where applicable, to notify its service recipients without delay, while provision B requires a financial entity to submit successive notifications and reports to the relevant competent authority within separately determined deadlines. A single significant/serious ICT incident could therefore trigger two distinct communications to different recipients, and the authority filing would not notify the entity’s service recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with: the entity can promptly inform affected service recipients under A and separately make the initial, intermediate, updated and final submissions required by B. Neither provision says that one notification substitutes for the other, and the different recipients make cumulative compliance possible rather than mutually incompatible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also an essential or important entity and suffers one ICT incident that significantly affects the provision of its services and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. It must notify its service recipients “onverwijld” under A and submit the initial notification, any required intermediate or updated notifications, and the final report “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” under B; filing with the authority does not discharge the separate notification duty to service recipients.

verdict.shared_subject: A significant incident affecting the provision of a trust service, reported by an essential or important entity that provides a trust service.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an incident-reporting duty on the same kind of trust-service provider for the same triggering event, but A requires an incident report within 72 hours while B requires a report within 24 hours. The strongest tension case is that A's EU wording identifies the recipient as the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority, whereas B expressly requires filing with both the entity's CSIRT and competent authority, potentially creating cumulative filings and different recipient obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: B appears to implement or specify the same underlying incident report for trust-service incidents: it requires the provider to report the incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours, which is earlier than A's 72-hour deadline. If the CSIRT and competent authority are the applicable recipients under A, one 24-hour filing to both could satisfy the substantive reporting obligation under both provisions; the texts do not expressly require two separate reports with different content or clocks.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing decisive reference is the provision establishing whether the report required by BWBR0052872 art. 27 must be a separate national filing from the incident report under 32022L2555 art. 23, or whether the national filing is the implementation of and satisfies the EU-law report. The shown provisions also do not establish whether, in the relevant case, the CSIRT and competent authority are the same or different recipients for purposes of A.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related notifications by authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related communications, and Provision A requires the competent authority to confirm receipt after receiving an initial notification and reports, while Provision B requires national competent authorities to notify the Commission immediately of every serious incident. If the same incident triggers both, the authority may face two communications with different recipients and potentially different timing requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct duties that can be performed cumulatively: confirming receipt to the notifying financial entity does not prevent, and may precede or accompany, notifying the Commission. Provision A concerns receipt of a financial entity's Article 19 notification, whereas Provision B concerns serious incidents under Article 20 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020; the texts do not establish that the same event necessarily triggers both duties or specify incompatible deadlines.

Als die verwijzingen verschillende procedures of bevoegdheden zouden aanwijzen, kan onduidelijkheid ontstaan over welk proces het CSIRT moet coördineren.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a cooperation duty, so an entity might need to provide assistance in connection with an investigation while also cooperating fully with competent or resolution authorities. verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of the interim report following a serious ICT-related incident by specified financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an interim report to be submitted to the relevant competent authority after the initial notification. Provision B requires specified entities to make the Article 19(1) notification to a sectoral CSIRT as well, so the same incident-reporting regime may require filings to two different recipients; a filing with the competent authority would not, on its face, discharge the separate CSIRT duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can submit the interim report to the relevant competent authority and also make the corresponding Article 19(1) notification to the designated sectoral CSIRT. Provision B does not expressly say that the interim report under A must also be sent to the CSIRT, and it supplies no separate deadline for that CSIRT filing.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank experiences a serious ICT-related incident, submits the initial notification to the relevant competent authority, and later faces a substantial change in the incident's status. It must submit the interim report to the relevant competent authority under A, while B separately requires the Article 19(1) incident notification to be made also to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors. The two recipients differ, and B does not state that filing with the competent authority satisfies the CSIRT obligation; the entity therefore must account for both filings and their potentially different timing or procedural requirements.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting duplication on the text shown. The unresolved procedural detail is the deadline and exact scope of the CSIRT filing, because B states no deadline and does not expressly specify whether the interim report itself must be sent to the CSIRT.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT-related and serious incidents by financial entities that are also high-risk AI-system deployers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires financial entities to establish and implement a process for detecting, managing and reporting ICT-related incidents. B separately requires a high-risk AI-system deployer that identifies a serious incident to notify the provider first and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities. If the same event is both an ICT-related incident and a serious AI incident, the provisions could impose cumulative reporting duties, with B identifying recipients that A does not specify.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the financial entity can use one incident-management process to make the notifications required by B, while also satisfying A's broader process duty. verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT incidents by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident under NIS2 must be reported immediately to the entity’s CSIRT or, where applicable, competent authority. B requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority under DORA; if the same event meets both definitions, the texts do not state that the DORA report discharges the NIS2 report, and the recipients and procedures are not necessarily identical.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions concern incident reporting and can be complied with cumulatively. In some cases the relevant competent authority may be the same authority, and NIS2 itself provides for forwarding a report received by the competent authority to the CSIRT, so the regimes could operate through coordinated reporting rather than inherently requiring two separate submissions.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also an essential or important entity under NIS2. One cyber incident causes a serious operational disruption and affects other persons, making it a NIS2 “significant incident,” while also qualifying as a DORA “serious ICT-related incident.” The entity must report under NIS2 “onverwijld” to “zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit” and under DORA to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46”; the provisions shown do not establish that one filing satisfies the other, particularly where the NIS2 route is the CSIRT and the DORA route is the relevant financial-sector authority.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive unresolved point is whether the applicable national implementation and designation of authorities, or another provision of either instrument, treats a DORA report to the relevant competent authority as also satisfying the NIS2 duty to report to the CSIRT or NIS2 competent authority. The text shown does not establish that equivalence.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related notifications by a financial entity/provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use an immediate-notification obligation, but they concern different recipients and different triggering events: A concerns voluntary reporting of significant cyber threats to an authority, while B concerns notifying the affected person of a personal-data breach likely to harm privacy. verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an ongoing significant/serious incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident reporting and could apply to the same ongoing event. Provision A requires an interim progress report while the incident is ongoing, whereas Provision B requires a serious-incident notification within its own deadline; if these are separate regimes and filings, the actor must make both, potentially to different authorities and on different procedural bases.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish that the two reports are the same filing, nor do the shown texts fully establish that the same actor, incident, and system fall within both regimes. Provision A's selected norm concerns an interim progress report, while Provision B concerns the notification referenced in Article 73(1), and the relevant triggering conditions and recipients are supplied only partly by context.

A significant cyber incident involving the AI system remains ongoing when the provider becomes aware of it. Under Provision A, it must submit an interim progress report because the incident is still ongoing at the time the final report would otherwise be submitted; under Provision B, it must separately notify the market-surveillance authority of the serious incident within 15 days of awareness. The NIS2 progress report and the AI Act notification are distinct filings under different regimes, so making one does not discharge the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: The conclusion depends on the Article 73(1) context establishing that the AI Act notification is made to market-surveillance authorities and on the assumption that the NIS2 interim progress report is a separate filing to the CSIRT or competent authority; the shown provisions do not expressly state that either filing substitutes for the other.

If so, an immediate notification to that authority satisfies A's 72-hour deadline as well as B's stricter timing, so the duties can be cumulatively complied with without conflict. verdict.missing_reference: The missing reference is the provision or authoritative rule establishing whether the Article 55 competent supervisory authority in A is the same recipient as the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens in B, and whether notification under one provision legally discharges the other or requires a separate filing.

verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT-related incidents under DORA and serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity that is also a provider or deployer of a high-risk AI system could face two reporting duties for the same incident: DORA requires updated notifications to the relevant competent authority, while the AI Act requires a notification within a maximum of 15 days. The texts identify different reporting regimes and do not state that one filing discharges the other.

If both apply, however, separate recipients and filings may still be required rather than one stricter report satisfying both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that provides a high-risk AI system experiences one serious incident after its initial DORA notification. verdict.shared_subject: Significante cyberdreigingen en ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen bij dezelfde cyberdreiging relevant zijn, maar zij leggen verschillende communicatieplichten op: A vereist geactualiseerde kennisgevingen aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B informatie aan de ontvangers van diensten vereist. Dat zijn inhoudelijk en qua ontvanger afzonderlijke handelingen, zodat naleving van de ene plicht de andere niet vervult.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn cumulatief goed uitvoerbaar: een entiteit kan de bevoegde autoriteit rapporteren volgens A en daarnaast de getroffen dienstontvangers informeren volgens B. Er is geen tegenstrijdige verplichting, en B ziet bovendien alleen op informatieverstrekking indien dat nodig is.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een financiële entiteit die tevens een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit is, ontdekt na haar eerste kennisgeving nieuwe informatie over een significante cyberdreiging die ontvangers van haar diensten kan treffen. Zij moet dan enerzijds een geactualiseerde kennisgeving bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit indienen en anderzijds de betrokken ontvangers onverwijld informeren over de te nemen maatregelen en, indien nodig, over de dreiging zelf; de twee afzonderlijke communicatieplichten hebben verschillende ontvangers.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct, independently satisfiable duties rather than incompatible commands: A requires a first notification to the relevant competent authority, while B requires information to potentially affected service recipients, where necessary. Thus, one incident may require both a client notification and an authority report, on different practical timelines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties apply to different actors and recipients: A concerns financial entities notifying clients, whereas B concerns providers or deployers of high-risk AI systems reporting to market-surveillance authorities. Each duty can therefore be performed independently, and the texts do not state that either notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also the provider or deployer of a high-risk AI system. The system causes a serious ICT-related incident affecting clients’ financial interests. The entity must notify those clients 'onverwijld' under A and separately make the Article 73(1) report to the market-surveillance authorities 'onmiddellijk' after establishing the causal link and no later than 15 days after awareness under B; notifying clients does not constitute the authority report.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and serious ICT-related incidents by a financial entity subject to both GDPR and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying incident may trigger two independently worded reporting duties: GDPR requires notification to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours where the breach is likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms, while DORA requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant Article 46 competent authority. The recipients are identified by different legal provisions and the texts do not say that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can submit the GDPR notification to the Article 55 supervisory authority and the DORA notification to the Article 46 authority, using the DORA forms and timing rules. The texts also do not establish that every personal-data breach is a serious ICT-related incident, or that the authorities must be different in a particular Member State.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity suffers one cyberattack that both constitutes a personal-data breach likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. It must notify the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours ('aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit', 'uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen') and separately report the serious ICT-related incident to the Article 46 authority ('aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46'). Filing the GDPR notification does not, on the text shown, satisfy the DORA reporting duty, and filing with the DORA authority does not satisfy the GDPR duty.
verdict.missing_reference: The exact DORA deadlines in Article 20 and the national designation of the Article 55 and Article 46 authorities could affect practical coordination, but they are not needed to establish that the provisions impose separate reporting duties to differently identified authorities.
verdict.decisive_exception: None. This is not a case where one deadline or filing is shown to discharge the other; the decisive feature is the separate recipient regimes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Transparency information for personal-data collection and human oversight of high-risk AI
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to an organisation using high-risk AI while collecting personal data: Article 13 requires informing the data subject about automated decision-making and its logic, significance, and expected consequences, while Article 14 requires enabling human overseers to understand, monitor, interpret, override, or stop the system. One might argue that the transparency information must be sufficiently detailed for data subjects while the oversight design may constrain what can be disclosed or how the system operates.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties on different aspects of operation: Article 13 concerns information supplied to the data subject at collection, whereas Article 14 concerns capabilities provided to human overseers of a high-risk AI system. Nothing in either text forbids the other duty, and providing explanations to data subjects can coexist with enabling human oversight.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities in the financial sector that may also be essential or important entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the covered financial-sector actors to make an incident notification to the designated financial-sector CSIRT. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report, or a progress report followed by a final report, on a different timetable; if the same incident triggers both regimes, the CSIRT notification does not obviously discharge the separate final/progress-report duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can notify the designated CSIRT under A and submit the progress/final report required by B. Provision A states no deadline or content that conflicts with B, and B does not say that its report replaces a notification to the CSIRT.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank that is also an essential entity suffers an incident that continues beyond the time when B's final report would otherwise be due. It must notify the designated CSIRT under A and submit a progress report instead of the final report under B, followed by a final report within one month after the incident is resolved; filing the CSIRT notification does not discharge the separate progress/final-report obligation.

Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT oversight and incident-related information
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers the lead overseer to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers about actions or corrective measures concerning recommendations. Provision B obliges an entity, in an early warning, to state whether a significant incident was probably caused by an unlawful or malicious act. One might argue that an incident-related report requested under A could overlap with the information required by B, creating uncertainty about whether the provider should report the same matter through the oversight mechanism or the early-warning mechanism.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of rules on different actors and concern different acts: A grants a supervisory competence to request post-oversight reports, while B requires an entity to include specified information in an early warning. Nothing in either text forbids complying with the other, substitutes one communication for the other, or establishes that the requested report under A is the same filing as the early warning under B.

verdict.shared_subject: Het indienen van een tussentijds verslag over een ICT-incident door een entiteit die zowel onder Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555 als onder Verordening (EU) 2022/2554 valt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide normen verplichten een tussentijds verslag, maar A verlangt dit op een specifiek moment wanneer het incident nog voortduurt, terwijl B het verslag na de eerste kennisgeving verlangt bij een ingrijpende statuswijziging of wijziging van de behandeling, met mogelijke verdere updates en een ander procedureel kader. Bovendien noemt A het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit als ontvanger, terwijl B de relevante bevoegde autoriteit noemt, zodat één verslag niet zonder meer beide verplichtingen lijkt te vervullen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: de entiteit kan hetzelfde inhoudelijke incident met afzonderlijke of gecoördineerde tussentijdse verslagen aan de toepasselijke ontvangers melden, op de momenten die elk regime voorschrijft. De teksten verbieden niet dat één verslag aan beide regimes voldoet wanneer ontvanger, timing en inhoud toevallig samenvallen; de enkele overlap in rapportage is daarom niet automatisch een conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een financiële entiteit die tevens een betrokken entiteit onder Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555 is, meldt een significant incident eerst aan het CSIRT. Het incident duurt voort wanneer het eindverslag onder A moet worden ingediend; daardoor moet zij op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen, terwijl zij onder B na haar eerste kennisgeving ook een tussentijds verslag aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit moet indienen omdat de status of behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd. Dit zijn potentieel twee cumulatieve meldingen aan verschillende in de normen genoemde ontvangers en volgens verschillende triggers; indien het CSIRT niet dezelfde ontvanger is als de relevante bevoegde autoriteit, ontslaat de ene melding haar niet van de andere.
verdict.decisive_exception: De teksten tonen niet aan dat een voortgangsverslag onder A automatisch geldt als het tussentijdse verslag onder B, of dat indiening bij het CSIRT automatisch indiening bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit vervangt. Ook zijn de concrete termijnen van artikel 20 van Verordening (EU) 2022/2554 niet weergegeven.
verdict.evidence_span_a: indien het incident nog aan de gang is op het moment dat het in punt d) bedoelde eindverslag wordt ingediend, zorgen de lidstaten ervoor dat de betrokken entiteiten op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions impose reporting or information duties on different actors for different subject matters: significant incidents must be reported by essential or important entities to a CSIRT or competent authority, while notified bodies must, on request, inform the notifying authority about their conformity-assessment activities. They therefore do not create two filings for the same actor and event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both duties can operate independently without contradiction. An entity could report a significant incident to its CSIRT or competent authority, while a notified body could separately provide requested information about its conformity-assessment activities to the notifying authority; neither duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and associated compliance procedures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same operator or provider in relation to a high-risk AI system, but they impose different compliance steps: prior consultation with the data-protection supervisory authority where a DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, and a conformity-assessment procedure for certain high-risk AI systems. One might argue that the conformity assessment could be treated as addressing the relevant risk and therefore make separate consultation unnecessary, or that the two procedures create overlapping timing and compliance burdens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers, actors, purposes and recipients. Article 36 concerns a controller's proposed processing of personal data and requires prior consultation only where the DPIA identifies a high risk absent mitigation; Article 43 concerns a provider's conformity assessment for high-risk AI systems covered by specified Union harmonisation legislation. Nothing in either text says that one procedure substitutes for or overrides the other, so both can be performed cumulatively where both apply.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: volgt de aanbieder de relevante conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure zoals vereist volgens die rechtshandelingen.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT mutual assistance obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a mutual-assistance duty on CSIRTs, but Provision A refers to assistance to other network members generally, while Provision B refers to assistance on the request of a network member. One might argue that the slightly different formulations create uncertainty about the precise trigger or scope of the duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose materially the same duty on the same type of actor, subject to the same capacity-and-authority limitation. Provision B's reference to a request from a network member is consistent with Provision A's reference to assistance to other members 'op hun verzoek'; the differences are drafting and implementation detail, not incompatible commands.
verdict.evidence_span_a: f) het deelnemen aan het CSIRT-netwerk en, in overeenstemming met hun capaciteiten en bevoegdheden, het verlenen van wederzijdse bijstand aan andere leden van het netwerk op hun verzoek;
verdict.evidence_span_b: f. het deelnemen aan het CSIRT-netwerk en, in overeenstemming met zijn capaciteiten en bevoegdheden, het verlenen van wederzijdse bijstand aan andere leden van het CSIRT-netwerk op verzoek van een lid van dat netwerk;

verdict.shared_subject: A duty to provide cooperation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require an institution or provider to cooperate, but they concern different investigations or actions and impose no expressly incompatible conduct. Nothing in either text says that complying with one cooperation duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires the relevant provider to cooperate with an investigation upon a request from the provider conducting that investigation. Provision B requires specified institutions to cooperate with a listed party in giving effect to a suspension under article 14a.7; the duties can be performed cumulatively because their triggers, counterparties and subject matters differ.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verleent medewerking aan het onderzoek
verdict.evidence_span_b: verleent medewerking aan een beursgenoteerde betrokken partij bij het gevolg geven aan de schorsing

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or ICT-related incident by an entity that is both a financial entity under DORA and an operator of a public electronic communications service.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious ICT-related incident may also be a security breach adversely affecting personal-data protection. In that case, A requires updated notifications to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit,” while B separately requires immediate notification to “de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens”; the recipients differ, so one filing does not obviously discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can apply to different actors and different incident categories, so many incidents trigger only one duty. Even when both apply, both notifications can be made cumulatively without incompatible content or deadlines; the texts do not prohibit dual reporting or make compliance with one duty impossible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that also provides a public electronic communications service suffers a serious ICT-related incident involving a security breach that adversely affects the protection of personal data. After its initial DORA notification, the incident status materially changes and the entity must submit an updated notification to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” under A, while B independently requires it to notify “de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens” “onverwijld.” Filing the updated notification with the relevant competent authority does not, on the text shown, notify the Dutch data-protection authority, so both filings are required on different regimes and potentially different clocks.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie, in voorkomend geval gevolgd door geactualiseerde kennisgevingen telkens wanneer een relevante actualisering van de status beschikbaar is, alsmede op specifiek verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit;
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens die zijn verwerkt in verband met de levering van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst in de Europese Unie.

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative decision-making and incident notification deadlines
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the municipal executive to adopt an approval decision within eight weeks, while Provision B requires an essential or important entity to issue an early warning immediately or within 24 hours after learning of a significant incident. One might argue that both impose time-sensitive obligations connected with regulated activities, creating different procedural clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors, events, recipients, and actions. A concerns the municipal executive’s decision on a written notification about planned cable works; B concerns an essential or important entity’s warning to its CSIRT and competent authority after a significant incident. Compliance with one does not prevent or interfere with compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Burgemeester en wethouders nemen het instemmingsbesluit binnen acht weken na ontvangst van de schriftelijke melding als bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel a.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_subject: Security incidents involving providers of public electronic communications networks or services and entities issuing an early warning
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern security incidents and impose obligations connected with incident handling. One could argue that the communications provider must implement measures aimed at limiting national-security or public-order consequences, while the other requires incident information and responsible-official contact details to be supplied in an early warning.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties: A concerns technical, operational and organisational risk-management measures by providers of public electronic communications networks or services, whereas B concerns the contents of an early warning by an entity. Nothing in either text makes compliance with one duty substitute for or prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun netwerken of diensten te beheersen
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose reporting duties concerning an incident that is still ongoing when a final report is due. Provision A requires an initial notification to the relevant competent authority, while provision B requires a progress report at that point instead of a final report, potentially creating uncertainty about whether both an A report and a B progress report must be filed.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different stages and types of reporting rather than incompatible commands. A's initial notification is due within the Article 20 deadlines, whereas B's progress report replaces only the final report when the incident remains ongoing; an entity can therefore submit the initial notification and later submit the required progress report, with no text requiring deletion or withholding of either report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in: a) een eerste kennisgeving;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Compliance obligations for high-risk AI systems and high-risk personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same project involving a high-risk AI system and high-risk personal-data processing. One requires prior consultation with the data-protection authority, while the other requires technical documentation before market placement or use; this could create parallel preparatory obligations, but neither text makes the duties incompatible or substitutes one for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations concern different acts and can readily be performed cumulatively: the controller can consult the supervisory authority before processing and separately prepare and update the AI technical documentation before placing the system on the market or putting it into service. Provision B's optional simplified-form duty applies only if an SME chooses simplified submission, and nothing in either provision prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident or works-related notification duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use prompt notification language and could conceivably be triggered by the same operational event. However, they address different triggering circumstances and different recipients: A concerns cable-maintenance works on public land and notification to the mayor, while B concerns significant incidents and notification to service recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative but independently satisfiable, not mutually inconsistent: an entity can notify the mayor under A and its service recipients under B, each within the applicable prompt timeframe. The different recipients mean that one notification cannot discharge the other, but that creates no conflict because neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT cyberbeveiligingstaken inzake incidenten en cyberdreigingen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen een CSIRT een verplichte taak op rond cyberincidenten en dreigingen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat A informatie-uitwisseling en bespreking op verzoek voorschrijft, terwijl B een bredere, eigen taak van dynamische analyse en situationeel bewustzijn voorschrijft, zodat onduidelijk zou zijn of dezelfde informatie-uitwisseling of analyse leidend is.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen cumulatieve en goed verenigbare taken op: A ziet op het uitwisselen en bespreken van informatie binnen het CSIRT-netwerk wanneer een mogelijk getroffen lid daarom verzoekt, terwijl B ziet op nationale dynamische risico- en incidentenanalyse en situationeel bewustzijn. Een CSIRT kan beide taken uitvoeren; geen van beide verbiedt of vervangt de andere.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk dat mogelijkerwijs gevolgen ondervindt van een incident, het uitwisselen en bespreken van informatie over dat incident en de daarmee samenhangende cyberdreigingen, risico’s en kwetsbaarheden
verdict.evidence_span_b: het zorgen voor dynamische risico- en incidentenanalyse en situationeel bewustzijn met betrekking tot cyberbeveiliging

verdict.shared_subject: ICT and electronic-communications activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to monitor user activities and ICT anomalies or incidents, while provision B requires a decision immediately after receiving a notification. If a financial entity is also the decision-maker receiving such a notification, the monitoring obligation could create an operational need to investigate before deciding immediately.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different apparent actors and concern different triggers: A requires financial entities to maintain monitoring capacity, whereas B requires an unspecified decision-maker to decide immediately after receiving a notification. Nothing in the texts makes monitoring a prerequisite to, or incompatible with, taking the decision immediately.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten zetten voldoende middelen en capaciteiten in om toezicht te houden op activiteiten van gebruikers en het optreden van ICT-anomalieën en ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, met name cyberaanvallen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and their assessment
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern high-risk technology or AI systems and require an assessment before or in connection with their operation. One might argue that the GDPR impact assessment and the AI Act's full conformity assessment overlap, creating uncertainty about whether one assessment suffices for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors, triggered in different circumstances and serving different regulatory purposes. Article 35 GDPR requires a controller to conduct a data-protection impact assessment before high-risk personal-data processing, while Article 36 requires a notified body taking over certificates to conduct a full conformity assessment of specified high-risk AI systems; neither text says that one assessment replaces or conflicts with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: Die laatste aangemelde instantie verricht vóór het einde van die periode van negen maanden een volledige beoordeling van de betrokken AI-systemen met een hoog risico

verdict.shared_subject: Nationale cyberbeveiligingsincidenten en crisisrespons
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen concern national cybersecurity governance, and the CSIRT duty includes dynamic risk and incident analysis while the Minister must establish a national plan for large-scale incidents and crisis response. One might argue that the operational CSIRT analysis duty and the Minister’s planning competence could create uncertainty about who is responsible for producing the relevant national assessment or plan.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A assigns CSIRTs an operational analytical task, while Provision B assigns the Minister competence to establish a national plan. The texts do not require the CSIRTs to establish the plan, prohibit the Minister from using CSIRT analysis, or impose incompatible duties, deadlines, recipients, or standards; the duties can plainly coexist.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het verzamelen en analyseren van forensische gegevens en het zorgen voor dynamische risico- en incidentenanalyse en situationeel bewustzijn met betrekking tot cyberbeveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister stelt een nationaal plan voor grootschalige cyberbeveiligingsincidenten en crisisrespons als bedoeld in artikel 9, vierde lid, van de NIS2-richtlijn vast.

verdict.shared_subject: Voorafgaande documentatie en risicobeoordeling van hoog-risico-AI-systemen waarbij persoonsgegevens worden verwerkt
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide verplichtingen kunnen vóór ingebruikname of verwerking documentatie vereisen, maar zij hebben verschillende inhoud en triggers: artikel 35 ziet op verwerking die waarschijnlijk een hoog risico voor natuurlijke personen oplevert, terwijl artikel 11 ziet op een AI-systeem dat als hoog risico geldt. Daardoor kan onduidelijk zijn of een systeem dat onder één risicobeoordeling valt ook onder de andere documentatieplicht valt. Dit is echter vooral een verschil in toepassingsbereik en cumulatieve verplichtingen, niet een onmogelijkheid om beide na te leven.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Een verwerkingsverantwoordelijke kan vóór de verwerking een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling uitvoeren en daarnaast vóór het in de handel brengen of ingebruikstellen technische documentatie opstellen en actualiseren. De verplichtingen hebben verschillende doelen en kunnen naast elkaar worden vervuld; geen van beide verbiedt of vervangt de andere.
verdict.evidence_span_a: voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: De technische documentatie van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico wordt opgesteld voordat dit systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld, en wordt geactualiseerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or providing information to public authorities by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a notified body, upon request, to inform the notifying authority about conformity-assessment and other activities. Provision B requires an essential or important entity, after a significant incident, to report to its CSIRT and competent authority within 72 hours. If the same actor is both a notified body and an essential or important entity, a significant incident could trigger B while a request separately triggers A, involving different recipients and distinct information duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers, actors, subject matter and recipients: A concerns a request for information about conformity-assessment activities, while B concerns a significant-incident notification. Nothing in either text forbids compliance with the other, and the texts do not establish that the same event triggers both duties or that the actor is subject to both regimes.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingen and subsequent decision-making
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a processor to inform the controller without unreasonable delay after learning of a personal-data breach. Provision B requires a decision to be made immediately after receipt of a notification, so if the same notification process is involved, the timing duties could appear to impose different obligations on different stages or actors.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors and different acts: A concerns a processor notifying a controller, while B concerns the timing of a decision after a notification is received. Nothing in the texts requires the processor to make the decision in B or makes the two deadlines incompatible; the duties can be performed cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related notifications by entities/providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity, where applicable, to notify its service recipients without delay about a significant incident adversely affecting service provision. Provision B requires a provider, when urgent action prevents prior notice, to notify the affected subscriber as soon as possible of the measure taken. A single incident could therefore lead to notifications to service recipients under A and to an affected subscriber under B, with different triggering conditions and potentially different content.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct, cumulatively satisfiable duties rather than incompatible ones. A concerns notification of a significant incident to service recipients, while B concerns notification of a specific measure to the affected subscriber when prior notice was impossible due to urgency; making one notification does not prevent making the other, and the texts do not establish that the same event necessarily triggers both.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer dit wegens de vereiste spoed niet voorafgaand aan het nemen van de maatregel mogelijk is, doet de aanbieder zo snel mogelijk melding van de maatregel.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents and institutional responses
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives competent authorities the power to issue warnings to important entities for infringements of the Directive. Provision B requires the CSIRT, where applicable, to respond to incidents and assist essential or important entities. One might argue that an authority warning and CSIRT assistance could pull the same entity toward enforcement and operational support, but the texts do not make those functions incompatible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different functions: A concerns the competent authority’s enforcement competence, while B concerns the CSIRT’s incident-response and assistance task. A warning by the authority does not prevent the CSIRT from responding to an incident, and CSIRT assistance does not remove the authority’s power to warn about an infringement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de bevoegdheid hebben om: a) waarschuwingen te geven over inbreuken op deze richtlijn door de betrokken entiteiten;
verdict.evidence_span_b: c. indien van toepassing, het reageren op incidenten en verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit;

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT-related incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a specific progress report to be submitted while a significant incident is ongoing, whereas provision B requires financial entities to establish and implement a process for reporting ICT-related incidents. If the same financial entity and incident fall within both regimes, the texts do not expressly say whether the process-based reporting duty in B is satisfied by A’s progress report or requires an additional report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B is a system-level organisational duty to create and implement an incident-management process, not a separate filing obligation for a particular incident. Provision A’s progress-report obligation can be incorporated into that process, so an entity can comply with both without making two reports merely because both provisions mention reporting.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden

verdict.shared_subject: Communicating a significant cyber threat or incident to affected recipients and reporting authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to inform service recipients who may be affected by a significant cyber threat, while provision B requires a trust-service provider to report a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. A single event may trigger both duties, but they concern different recipients and different communications, so the authority report cannot discharge the recipient notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can notify potentially affected service recipients under A and separately report the incident to the CSIRT and competent authority under B. Nothing in either text says that one communication substitutes for the other or prohibits making both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider that is an essential or important entity learns of a significant incident affecting its trust service and posing a significant cyber threat to some customers. It must notify those potentially affected service recipients under A, while also filing the incident report within 24 hours with both its CSIRT and competent authority under B; the recipient notification is not a filing with either authority and therefore does not discharge B, and the authority filing does not notify the customers as required by A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien van toepassing zorgen de lidstaten ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging worden getroffen, onverwijld meedelen welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging. Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
verdict.evidence_span_b: In afwijking van het eerste lid dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit als dat incident gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van haar vertrouwensdienst.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk management and ICT-incident governance for certain financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires certain exempt entities to maintain and operate an ICT-risk-management framework, including incorporating relevant operational conclusions from tests and post-incident analysis where appropriate. Provision B separately requires specified financial entities to report certain ICT incidents, including voluntary reports, to the sectoral CSIRT; an incident may therefore trigger both internal learning/documentation and an external notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties: A concerns internal ICT-risk-management processes and learning from tests or incidents, while B concerns reporting specified incidents to a CSIRT. Nothing in either text says that documenting conclusions substitutes for reporting, or that reporting prevents or limits the internal process.
verdict.evidence_span_a: h) in voorkomend geval de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk processing or AI systems and the operator’s pre-market/pre-processing compliance obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can impose obligations before an activity begins: GDPR Article 36 requires prior consultation where a DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while the AI Act provision requires technical documentation for a high-risk AI system before it is placed on the market or put into service. One might argue that the operator faces two overlapping pre-deployment compliance processes, potentially involving different authorities and information requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations are cumulative and independently satisfiable, not contradictory. Article 36 concerns prior consultation with the data-protection supervisory authority triggered by a specific DPIA finding about processing risk; Article 11 concerns the contents of technical documentation for a high-risk AI system and does not prohibit or replace consultation. Preparing the required documentation and, where applicable, consulting the supervisory authority can both be done.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De documentatie omvat ten minste de in bijlage IV uiteengezette elementen.

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingen over ICT-gerelateerde incidenten of maatregelen door respectievelijk financiële entiteiten en aanbieders
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen gebruiken een meldingsplicht en kunnen feitelijk op hetzelfde ICT- of veiligheidsincident betrekking hebben. Als een aanbieder tevens een financiële entiteit is, kan dezelfde gebeurtenis mogelijk zowel onder de algemene incidentmelding van A als onder de melding aan de abonnee van B vallen, met verschillende inhoud en een verschillend moment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen geen onverenigbare verplichtingen op. A vereist dat een financiële entiteit een proces heeft om ICT-incidenten te melden, zonder ontvanger of termijn te bepalen; B vereist een concrete melding aan de betrokken abonnee vóór of, bij spoed, zo snel mogelijk na een specifieke maatregel. Beide meldingen kunnen cumulatief worden gedaan, en B's melding van de maatregel vervangt A's incidentmeldingsplicht niet maar verhindert die ook niet.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Authority to impose an administrative enforcement order (last onder bestuursdwang)
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern competence to impose the same type of administrative enforcement order, and both name an authority that may exercise that competence. If they applied to the same obligations and violation, the texts alone would not identify which authority should act.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions assign competence over different statutory obligations and to different authorities: provision A refers to obligations under the provisions mentioned in article 15.1(2), while provision B enumerates a separate set of provisions and expressly excludes certain processing of personal data. Concurrent or divided enforcement competence is not itself a conflict, and neither provision forbids the other authority from acting.

verdict.shared_subject: EU-level institutional procedures involving the European Commission and regulatory bodies
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations involving EU-level oversight and coordination, so they may appear to create overlapping procedural activity around regulatory compliance. However, provision A concerns the EDPB’s guidance on reporting GDPR infringements, while provision B concerns the Commission’s safeguard review of national AI-market-surveillance measures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions govern different actors, subject matters, and triggers: A requires the EDPB to issue guidance on common procedures for individuals reporting GDPR infringements, whereas B requires the Commission to consult a Member State market-surveillance authority and operators after an objection or Commission concern about an AI-law measure. Nothing in either text prevents the other obligation from being performed.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uitvaardigen van richtsnoeren, aanbevelingen en beste praktijken in overeenstemming met punt e) van dit lid, ter vaststelling van gemeenschappelijke procedures waarmee natuurlijke personen inbreuken op deze verordening kunnen melden, als bedoeld in artikel 54, lid 2

verdict.shared_subject: Notification-related duties involving authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the competent authority to acknowledge receipt of certain notifications and reports, while provision B requires the market-surveillance authority to follow notification procedures after receiving a notification. If the authorities or procedures were different, one might face cumulative or potentially inconsistent handling duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different authorities and do not require the same actor to make two reports about one triggering event. Provision A concerns confirmation of receipt by the competent authority; provision B concerns measures and notification procedures followed by the market-surveillance authority after receipt. Nothing in the texts makes either duty impossible to perform alongside the other.

verdict.evidence_span_b: volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations on public or regulatory bodies, so one might initially suspect competing statutory duties. However, provision A concerns the ACM's contents of a number register, while provision B concerns the CSIRT's processing and prioritisation of voluntary incident reports; neither duty requires or prohibits conduct addressed by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The ACM can maintain a register containing the specified name, address and residence information while the CSIRT processes voluntary reports and prioritises mandatory reports. The provisions concern different actors, objects, and functions, with no incompatible command, deadline, permission, or reporting recipient.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het register bevat de vermelding van de naam, het adres en de vestigingsplaats, respectievelijk de woonplaats van degene aan wie nummers zijn toegekend.
