verdict.shared_subject: Uitwisseling van informatie over incidenten door het CSIRT-netwerk en informatieverstrekking tussen bevoegde autoriteiten.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen zien op informatie over incidenten, en bij een significant incident waarbij een essentiële entiteit tevens een kritieke entiteit is, kunnen informatie-uitwisselingsactiviteiten van het CSIRT-netwerk en de verplichte verstrekking tussen bevoegde autoriteiten naast elkaar plaatsvinden. Dat levert echter geen onverenigbare verplichtingen op: de bepalingen richten zich op verschillende actoren en handelingen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 15, onder f, verplicht het CSIRT-netwerk op verzoek van een mogelijk getroffen netwerklid informatie over een incident en de daarmee samenhangende dreigingen, risico’s en kwetsbaarheden uit te wisselen en te bespreken. Artikel 40 verplicht daarentegen de bevoegde autoriteit om informatie over een gemeld significant incident aan een andere bevoegde autoriteit te verstrekken; beide informatiebewegingen kunnen cumulatief worden uitgevoerd.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk dat mogelijkerwijs gevolgen ondervindt van een incident, het uitwisselen en bespreken van informatie over dat incident en de daarmee samenhangende cyberdreigingen, risico’s en kwetsbaarheden
verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related information duties in ICT services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives the lead overseer a power to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers about actions or corrective measures concerning recommendations. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to inform its service recipients without delay about significant incidents adversely affecting service provision. A single incident could therefore generate both an oversight-report request and customer notifications, potentially involving different content and recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and serve different functions: A concerns the lead overseer’s competence vis-à-vis critical ICT third-party providers, while B concerns an essential or important entity’s direct notification of its service recipients. Nothing in A forbids or substitutes for B, and A is only a power to request reports, not an unconditional reporting obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: na afloop van de oversightactiviteiten te verzoeken om verslagen met vermelding van de ondernomen acties of de corrigerende maatregelen die door de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten zijn genomen met betrekking tot de in punt d) bedoelde aanbevelingen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Melding van significante incidenten door essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij hetzelfde significante incident moet de entiteit onverwijld melden aan haar CSIRT of bevoegde autoriteit én, indien van toepassing, onverwijld haar dienstontvangers informeren. Dit zijn verschillende ontvangers en de tekst zegt niet dat één mededeling de andere vervangt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen zijn cumulatief maar goed verenigbaar: een entiteit kan beide meldingen onverwijld doen. Er is geen tegenstrijdige inhoud, deadline of verbod; de ene melding aan de autoriteit ontslaat de entiteit niet noodzakelijk van de afzonderlijke informatieplicht aan dienstontvangers.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een belangrijke entiteit ondervindt een incident dat een ernstige operationele verstoring veroorzaakt en daardoor een significant incident is. Zij moet dit onverwijld melden bij haar CSIRT of bevoegde autoriteit en moet daarnaast, omdat het incident de dienstverlening nadelig kan beïnvloeden, haar dienstontvangers onverwijld informeren; één melding aan de autoriteit voldoet niet aan de afzonderlijke informatieplicht aan de dienstontvangers.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security/ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority under Article 46, while B requires a provider of a public electronic communications service to notify the Dutch Data Protection Authority without delay of a security breach affecting personal-data protection. If the same entity and incident satisfy both triggers, the texts identify different recipients and do not say that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed by making the required notifications, and they apply only when their distinct actor and incident conditions overlap. Article 19 also contemplates additional reporting to other authorities or CSIRTs, so multiple reporting channels are not inherently inconsistent.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an operator of a public electronic communications service suffers one serious ICT-related security incident that adversely affects personal-data protection. It must report the serious ICT-related incident to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46” under A and, without delay, notify “de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens” under B; filing with one recipient does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate duty to the other recipient.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or providing information to authorities by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a notified conformity-assessment body to provide information, on request, to its notifying authority. Provision B requires an essential or important entity offering a trust service to report a significant incident, within 24 hours, to its CSIRT and competent authority. If the same entity and event fall within both provisions, the duties involve different recipients and separate communications, so reporting to the CSIRT and competent authority would not itself satisfy the request-based duty to the notifying authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can provide the requested conformity-assessment information to the notifying authority and separately report the significant incident to the CSIRT and competent authority. Moreover, A is conditional on a request and concerns activities within the scope of a notification, while B is triggered by a significant incident affecting provision of a trust service; the texts do not establish that both triggers will normally coincide.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A notified conformity-assessment body that offers a trust service learns of a significant incident affecting that service and is requested by its notifying authority to provide information about its conformity-assessment activities concerning the incident. It must send the incident report within 24 hours to its CSIRT and competent authority under B, and separately provide the requested activity information to the notifying authority under A; neither filing discharges the other because the recipients differ.

Article 36 requires a controller to consult the data-protection supervisory authority where a DPIA shows high residual risk absent mitigation, while Article 23 requires an importer, before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, to check that the provider completed the Article 43 conformity-assessment procedure; both can be satisfied cumulatively.

If both regimes apply, the entity might need to determine whether the A final report and the B final report are separate filings or whether one satisfies both.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can submit the reports required by A to the relevant competent authority and also submit the B progress/final report on its statutory timetable. Provision B does not prohibit or expressly replace the report required by A, and the texts shown do not establish a second recipient or an incompatible deadline. The different conditions may simply govern when each regime's report is due.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions needed to determine whether the reports are legally identical, whether the same authority receives them, and whether one filing is deemed to satisfy the other—particularly the detailed reporting and deadline rules referred to in Article 20 and the other provisions of BWBR0052872 art. 29—are not shown. On the text provided, however, this missing detail is not necessary to identify a present conflict: both duties can be performed.

verdict.shared_subject: Compliance of a high-risk AI system and its processing-related risks

The strongest tension case is that an importer might regard the AI Act conformity checks as sufficient while the controller still has a separate, broader data-protection impact-assessment duty, but the texts do not say that one substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties address different actors, triggers, and objects: Article 35 requires a controller to conduct a DPIA before high-risk processing, whereas Article 23 requires an importer to verify conformity documentation and procedures before placing a high-risk AI system on the market. They are cumulative and can readily both be performed; neither provision forbids or excuses compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Documenting personal-data breaches and voluntarily reporting significant cyber threats by financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern information about potentially overlapping cyber or data-security events, and provision B refers to forwarding a voluntary cyber-threat notification to another authority. If the same event were both a personal-data breach and a significant cyber threat, an entity might face questions about whether the information should be documented under A and reported under B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires the controller to document all personal-data breaches for supervisory-compliance purposes; it does not prohibit or regulate voluntary cyber-threat reporting. Provision B makes the financial entity's cyber-threat notification voluntary, and its forwarding duty arises only after that optional notification, so an entity can comply with A without making the B notification. The duties also concern different acts: internal documentation versus optional reporting/forwarding.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision B is expressly voluntary: “op vrijwillige basis melden”. An entity that does not make that optional notification incurs no forwarding duty; if it does make one, the forwarding obligation can be performed in addition to the documentation duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory oversight and information relevant to safe and reliable electronic services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires significant risks to health, safety and fundamental rights identified during an AI regulatory sandbox to be adequately mitigated. Provision B requires specified organisations and recognised entities to provide the Minister, on request or proactively, the data and information the Minister needs to prevent or end infringements of safe and reliable access to electronic services. One might argue that information about an AI sandbox risk could be needed by the Minister, creating overlapping duties concerning risk-related information and mitigation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: A concerns mitigating identified risks in AI regulatory test environments, while B concerns supplying information to the Minister for measures protecting access to electronic services. Nothing in A forbids disclosure or makes mitigation a substitute for providing information, and nothing in B prevents the required risk mitigation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Significante risico’s voor de gezondheid en veiligheid en de grondrechten die tijdens het ontwikkelen en testen van dergelijke AI-systemen worden vastgesteld, worden op adequate wijze beperkt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen.

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingen over incidenten of maatregelen door een aanbieder
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen verplichten een actor tot een melding, maar zij zien op verschillende gebeurtenissen en ontvangers: A betreft een voortgangsverslag over een nog lopend significant incident, terwijl B een abonnee vooraf of zo snel mogelijk over een maatregel informeert. Als dezelfde aanbieder beide gebeurtenissen meemaakt, kunnen beide meldingen cumulatief vereist zijn; de ene melding vervangt de andere niet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn goed naast elkaar uitvoerbaar omdat A een verslag aan het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit betreft en B een melding aan de betrokken abonnee. Bovendien verschillen de triggers: A vereist een nog lopend significant incident bij het eindverslag, terwijl B voorafgaand aan een maatregel ziet op het wegnemen van een bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid.
verdict.evidence_span_a: indien het incident nog aan de gang is op het moment dat het in punt d) bedoelde eindverslag wordt ingediend, zorgen de lidstaten ervoor dat de betrokken entiteiten op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident monitoring and related institutional duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the market-surveillance authority to follow notification procedures under Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 after receiving a serious-incident notification. Provision B requires the CSIRT to monitor and analyse cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents nationally; if the same incident is involved, the provisions assign related functions to different actors, but neither text makes those duties incompatible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct duties on distinct actors: the market-surveillance authority must follow notification procedures, while the CSIRT must monitor and analyse cyber incidents. Both can be performed for the same incident without either duty preventing compliance with the other, and the texts do not establish duplicate reporting by the same actor, conflicting deadlines, or an exclusive allocation of responsibility.
verdict.evidence_span_a: volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet
verdict.evidence_span_b: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau

verdict.shared_subject: Oversight, reporting, and monitoring involving ICT/AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers the lead overseer to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers about actions or corrective measures concerning its recommendations. Provision B obliges high-risk AI deployers to notify specified actors and authorities of serious incidents, so an incident involving both regimes might generate related reporting activity and potentially overlapping information demands.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of rules on different actors: A grants a supervisory authority a power to request reports from critical ICT providers, while B imposes an incident-notification duty on deployers of high-risk AI systems. Nothing in either text forbids the other action, makes the reports substitutes for the notifications, or establishes the same triggering event, recipients, or incompatible deadlines.
verdict.evidence_span_a: na afloop van de oversightactiviteiten te verzoeken om verslagen met vermelding van de ondernomen acties of de corrigerende maatregelen die door de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten zijn genomen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires municipal authorities to decide an approval within a specified period, while Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report when an incident continues. No fact pattern in the texts makes these duties collide: they concern different acts, actors, and subject matters.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The municipal decision deadline and the incident-reporting duty can be performed independently, even if the same organisation were involved in both contexts. Nothing in either provision prohibits or delays compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities in the financial/banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the relevant entities to make the Article 19 notification, including a voluntary notification, also to the sectoral CSIRT designated under the Cybersecurity Act. Provision B separately requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report to its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the Article 27 notification. If the same entity and incident fall under both regimes, the duties may involve different reporting events, recipients, and content, so the A filing would not obviously discharge B's final-report duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can make the Article 19 notification to the designated sectoral CSIRT and later submit the Article 29 final report to its CSIRT and competent authority. The texts do not establish that the Article 19 notification and the Article 27 notification concern the same triggering event, nor that the CSIRTs or reporting obligations are necessarily different.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions establishing the Article 19 notification and the Article 27 notification, including their triggering events, recipients, and relationship to the CSIRT designated under Article 16 of the Cybersecurity Act. Those provisions are needed to determine whether one incident triggers both duties and whether the CSIRT recipients are the same or distinct.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit waarin het volgende is opgenomen:

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting changes to public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require communication of changes, so an entity subject to both might initially appear to face overlapping reporting duties. However, provision A assigns the duty to each Member State and concerns rules established under Article 90(1), while provision B assigns the duty to a qualifying undertaking and concerns changes affecting the ACM's assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different actors, recipients, and subject matters: Member States report their adopted rules and amendments to the Commission, whereas a qualifying undertaking reports relevant changes to the ACM. Each duty can be performed independently, and nothing in either text prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat deelt de Commissie uiterlijk op 25 mei 2018 de regels mee die hij heeft vastgesteld overeenkomstig lid 1, alsmede onverwijld alle wijzigingen daarvan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een onderneming als bedoeld in het eerste lid informeert de Autoriteit Consument en Markt zo spoedig mogelijk over wijzigingen die van invloed zijn op het oordeel van de Autoriteit Consument en Markt, bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT-related incidents and submitting a final/progress report
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident reporting by regulated entities, and a single incident could potentially fall within both regimes. If Provision B required a report to a different recipient or on a separate clock, the entity might have to make two cumulative filings rather than one.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires financial entities to report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, with the detailed reporting sequence and deadlines supplied by Article 20 and Article 19(4). Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report and then a final report within one month after the incident is resolved, but it identifies no recipient and does not state that this report is separate from, or incompatible with, the Article 19 reporting sequence; the shown texts therefore do not establish two distinct filings.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions needed to determine whether Provision B's progress/final report is a separate filing from Provision A's Article 19(4) final report—especially the recipient, deadline, and reporting relationship under the provision containing the general incident-reporting duty and any implementing rules for Article 20 deadlines.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: AI-systemen met een hoog risico en de informatie- en toezichtsplichten rond verwerking van persoonsgegevens
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen raken aan geautomatiseerde besluitvorming: artikel 13 verplicht informatie over het bestaan en de gevolgen van zulke verwerking, terwijl artikel 14 vereist dat menselijke toezichthouders het systeem kunnen monitoren en de output kunnen negeren of terugdraaien. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat transparantie-informatie aan de betrokkene en operationele menselijke controle verschillende, mogelijk uiteenlopende eisen stellen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen echter verschillende, cumulatieve verplichtingen op aan verschillende aspecten van dezelfde activiteit. Artikel 13 vereist informatieverstrekking aan de betrokkene; artikel 14 vereist dat het AI-systeem aan toezichthoudende personen wordt verstrekt met bepaalde toezichtsmogelijkheden. Niets in de teksten bepaalt dat naleving van de ene verplichting de andere vervangt of ermee strijdig is.
verdict.evidence_span_a: f) het bestaan van geautomatiseerde besluitvorming, met inbegrip van de in artikel 22, leden 1 en 4, bedoelde profilering, en, ten minste in die gevallen, nuttige informatie over de onderliggende logica, alsmede het belang en de verwachte gevolgen van die verwerking voor de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: d) in alle specifieke situaties te kunnen besluiten om het AI-systeem met een hoog risico niet te gebruiken of de output van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico op andere wijze te negeren, door een andere beslissing te vervangen of terug te draaien;

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingsverplichtingen bij verschillende gebeurtenissen en ontvangers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen gebruiken een meldingsplicht, maar zij concern different triggers and recipients: A requires an incident final report by a covered entity to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B requires a provider to notify the affected subscriber before taking a protective measure. If one event involved both a significant incident and a measure under Article 7.6a(1)(g), the provider might have to make both communications. That is not, however, a conflict between the provisions, because neither filing substitutes for the other and the duties address different purposes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the provider can notify the subscriber as soon as required under B and separately submit the final incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority under A. They concern different recipients, triggers, and information, and A's one-month deadline does not purport to govern or discharge B's notification duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uiterlijk één maand na de indiening van het in punt b) bedoelde incidentmelding, een eindverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee

verdict.shared_subject: Timing of an authority’s decision and submission of a significant-incident final report
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the affected entity to submit a final report no later than one month after the incident notification, while provision B requires a decision immediately after receipt of a notification. If the decision under B is a prerequisite to, or must be incorporated into, A’s final report, the immediate-decision duty could create a timing or sequencing problem. However, neither text states that the decision must precede the final report or that the report depends on the decision.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different subjects and concern different acts: A requires a reporting entity to submit a final incident report within one month, whereas B requires an unspecified decision-maker to decide immediately after receiving a notification. The duties can readily be performed cumulatively, and B does not alter A’s reporting deadline or prohibit submission of the report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uiterlijk één maand na de indiening van het in punt b) bedoelde incidentmelding, een eindverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Communicating or reporting cyber incidents or threats
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires essential and important entities to inform recipients of their services about a significant cyber threat, while Provision B requires specified financial-sector entities to make an incident notification also to the designated sectoral CSIRT. For a financial-sector entity facing a significant cyber threat affecting service recipients, these appear to be separate communications to different recipients, with neither text stating that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can notify affected service recipients under A and separately report the relevant ICT incident to the sectoral CSIRT under B. Provision A concerns communicating protective measures and, if necessary, the threat itself to service recipients, whereas B concerns a notification to a CSIRT; the texts do not impose incompatible content or deadlines.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank that is an essential or important entity experiences a significant cyber threat that may affect its customers. It must inform those service recipients of the measures they can take and, if necessary, of the threat itself under A, while also making the Article 19 incident notification to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors under B. These are two filings or communications to different recipients—“de ontvangers” and the designated sectoral CSIRT—and neither provision says that notifying one recipient satisfies the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien van toepassing zorgen de lidstaten ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging worden getroffen, onverwijld meedelen welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging. Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying personal-data breach must be reported to the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours, while B requires a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system to be reported to the market-surveillance authorities, immediately and at the latest within 15 days. The same event could satisfy both triggers, requiring two reports to different authorities; reporting to one would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with because they regulate distinct reporting duties with different triggers and recipients. A report within 72 hours could be made promptly, while a separate AI serious-incident report could be made within its applicable deadline; neither text expressly prohibits or substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider's high-risk AI system causes a serious incident that also involves a personal-data breach posing a likely risk to individuals' rights and freedoms. The provider must report the breach, if possible, within 72 hours to the competent data-protection supervisory authority under A, and must report the serious incident immediately and no later than 15 days after awareness to the market-surveillance authorities under B. These are separate filings to different authorities, and filing with one does not satisfy the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap. The relevant issue is that A expressly names a data-protection supervisory authority, while the contextual text for B identifies market-surveillance authorities; the provisions do not state that one report substitutes for the other. B's additional exceptions or alternative deadlines in Article 73(3)-(4) could alter the applicable AI-reporting deadline for particular incidents, but they do not establish substitution of recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident notifications and follow-up by authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may be encountered around a security incident notification, but provision A governs measures by a market-surveillance authority after receiving an AI serious-incident notification, whereas provision B governs transitional treatment and forwarding of an existing Wbni notification by the Minister. No incompatible command, deadline, or recipient obligation is stated.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, sequentially compatible duties on different authorities: the Minister may treat or forward a qualifying legacy Wbni notification, while the market-surveillance authority takes appropriate measures within seven days after receiving the notification. Forwarding the notification does not prevent the receiving authority from taking those measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen, en volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien de melding ziet op een inbreuk op de beveiliging van netwerk- en informatiesystemen die aanzienlijke gevolgen kan hebben voor de continuïteit van de door de melder verleende dienst als bedoeld in artikel 10, eerste lid, onderdeel b, van de Wet beveiliging netwerk- en informatiesystemen, zendt Onze Minister de melding door aan de bevoegde autoriteit.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-incident and network/security management obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to register ICT-related incidents and establish processes ensuring that their underlying causes are identified, documented, and removed. Provision B requires a provider, before taking a specified measure, to notify the affected subscriber and, where urgency prevents prior notice, to notify them as soon as possible; an incident could conceivably lead to such a measure, creating additional notification work alongside A's internal incident-management duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors and concern different triggers. A is an internal incident-registration and root-cause-management obligation for financial entities, with no reporting recipient or deadline; B is a subscriber-notification duty for a provider taking a particular measure, and it does not require a filing to an authority. Even if one actor were subject to both, the duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten stellen passende procedures en processen vast voor een consistente en geïntegreerde monitoring, behandeling en follow-up van ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, teneinde ervoor te zorgen dat onderliggende oorzaken worden opgespoord, gedocumenteerd en weggenomen om dergelijke incidenten te voorkomen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen.

verdict.shared_subject: Verplichtingen rond hoog-risico-AI-systemen en gegevensverwerking
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen in de context van één hoog-risico-AI-systeem relevant zijn, maar artikel 36 verplicht de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke tot voorafgaande raadpleging wanneer een DPIA een niet-gemitigeerd hoog risico laat zien, terwijl de geselecteerde norm uit artikel 16 de aanbieder verplicht noodzakelijke corrigerende maatregelen te nemen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat corrigerende maatregelen eerst moeten worden genomen en dat daardoor de voorafgaande raadpleging niet meer nodig is, of omgekeerd dat raadpleging de corrigerende actie vertraagt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen verschillende, cumulatief uitvoerbare verplichtingen aan verschillende actoren en bij verschillende triggers op. De aanbieder kan noodzakelijke corrigerende maatregelen nemen, terwijl de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke — indien de DPIA-trigger van artikel 36 is vervuld — vooraf de toezichthoudende autoriteit raadpleegt; geen van beide teksten bepaalt dat de ene verplichting de andere vervangt of verhindert.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: nemen de noodzakelijke corrigerende maatregelen

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by a financial entity where the same event is both a personal-data breach and a serious ICT-related incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity may have to report the same incident to the GDPR supervisory authority and separately prepare and submit DORA incident notifications and reports to the relevant competent authority. Those are potentially cumulative filings to different recipients, and the shown provisions do not specify how the two reporting processes interact.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed independently: Article 33 requires a qualifying personal-data breach to be reported to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours, while Article 19 requires serious ICT-related incidents to be reported under its own procedure to the relevant competent authority. Nothing shown says that one filing substitutes for the other, but neither provision itself creates an impossible deadline or contradictory content requirement.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A Dutch bank discovers a cyberattack that both constitutes a personal-data breach likely to risk individuals’ rights and freedoms and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. The bank must report the personal-data breach to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours and separately prepare and submit the DORA initial notification and subsequent reports to the relevant competent authority using the Article 20 models; reporting to one authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the duty to report to the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident oversight and response involving a financial entity and a CSIRT
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the competent authority to acknowledge receipt of the financial entity’s notification, while Provision B requires the CSIRT to perform dynamic risk and incident analysis and maintain cybersecurity situational awareness. One might argue that both provisions concern the same incident-management process and could create coordination questions about which body should assess or follow up on the incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties on different actors: the competent authority acknowledges receipt, whereas the CSIRT performs cybersecurity analysis and situational-awareness tasks. Nothing in either text makes the CSIRT’s analysis replace the authority’s acknowledgement or prevents both from being carried out.
verdict.evidence_span_a: bevestigt de ontvangst ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: het zorgen voor dynamische risico- en incidentenanalyse en situationeel bewustzijn

verdict.shared_subject: Public notice of decisions versus subscriber notification about traffic-data use
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require a form of communication, so one might initially suspect overlapping publication or notification duties. However, Article 15.1 concerns publication of specified decisions in the Staatscourant, while Article 19.9 concerns an operator informing subscribers about particular traffic-data processing and consent.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different actors, recipients, triggers, and purposes: Article 15.1 requires publication of a decision in the Staatscourant, whereas Article 19.9(c) requires the provider to notify the relevant subscriber about specified traffic-data use. The same provider can comply with both without either duty preventing compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related obligations of regulated entities and network/service providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern responses to ICT-related problems and impose obligations on regulated actors. One might argue that post-incident improvement identification could require internal remedial action while the other requires notifying an affected subscriber before taking a measure, creating a procedural interaction.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts, triggers, and actors. Provision A requires financial entities to identify improvements after serious ICT incidents; Provision B requires a provider to notify an affected subscriber before a specified measure, or as soon as possible where urgency prevents prior notice. Identifying improvements does not prohibit or replace subscriber notification, and notification does not prevent the post-incident evaluation duty.

verdict.shared_subject: Compliance obligations concerning a high-risk AI system and its processing of personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to the same high-risk AI system: the GDPR requires a data-protection impact assessment before processing where processing is likely to create a high risk, while the AI Act requires the importer to verify that the provider has prepared technical documentation. One might argue that the importer’s verification duty and the controller’s impact-assessment duty create overlapping documentation/compliance burdens, with no clear indication that one document substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different actors, objects and functions. Article 35 requires the controller to assess the impact of intended personal-data processing on individuals’ data protection, whereas Article 23 requires the importer to check whether the provider prepared technical documentation under Article 11 and Annex IV; both can be performed independently and cumulatively.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT-related incidents under DORA and serious incidents under the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same financial entity or provider where a high-risk AI system causes a serious ICT-related incident. Provision A requires an interim report after the initial notification, while provision B requires a serious-incident notification within 15 days; the texts do not establish that the AI-Act notification satisfies DORA’s separate interim-report duty, and the recipients and reporting content are framed differently.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the actor can submit DORA’s initial and interim reports to the relevant competent authority and separately submit the AI-Act notification within its deadline. Nothing in the shown provisions expressly makes one filing substitute for the other, and the different statutory triggers and reporting regimes do not by themselves create a conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity operates a high-risk AI system and is subject to both instruments. The system causes a serious ICT-related incident; the entity first notifies DORA’s relevant competent authority, then must submit an interim report after that first notification, while also making the AI-Act serious-incident notification to the market-surveillance authority within 15 days of becoming aware of the incident. Filing the AI-Act notification does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate DORA interim-report obligation, so two reports to different regulatory regimes are required for the same event.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap. The relevant unresolved point is whether another provision outside the excerpts coordinates or treats one filing as satisfying the other; the shown texts do not provide such a substitution rule.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting involving personal-data breaches and serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same actor is both a processor under Article 33 GDPR and an AI provider or deployer covered by Article 73, the same event might trigger both an information duty concerning a personal-data breach and a serious-incident notification duty. The duties have different triggers and apparently different recipients or filing structures, so one communication might not necessarily discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish the same triggering event, the same actor, or two clearly separate filings: Article 33 requires the processor to inform the controller, while Article 73 concerns the notification referenced in Article 73(1), whose recipient and scope are supplied only by the contextual paragraph. The texts shown therefore support cumulative compliance where both regimes apply, but do not themselves establish a concrete dual-reporting conflict or incompatible deadlines; each duty can be performed independently.
verdict.missing_reference: Article 73(1) is needed to establish the recipient and full scope of the AI-incident notification; the shown context identifies market-surveillance authorities, but the extracted norm itself does not. A concrete determination that one event triggers both duties would also require the provisions defining a personal-data breach and a serious incident, and the applicable actor roles.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT handling and communication of incidents, near-incidents and cyber threats involving essential entities that are also critical entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern CSIRT incident-related activity. One might argue that provision A makes incident response conditional—“indien van toepassing”—while provision B imposes an unconditional duty to provide information about a reported incident, near-incident or cyber threat to the competent authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose compatible duties with different content: A requires the CSIRT to respond to incidents and assist entities where applicable, while B requires it to transmit specified information to a particular competent authority. Nothing in A prohibits or excuses the information-transfer duty in B, and the conditional wording in A concerns whether response or assistance is applicable, not whether reporting information must be provided.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/cybersecurity incident and deficiency management by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns an authority’s power to order an essential entity to remedy identified deficiencies or infringements of the NIS2 Directive. Provision B requires certain small or exempt financial entities to identify and detect ICT risks and anomalies as soon as possible and handle ICT incidents quickly. An entity could therefore be subject to an enforcement order under A concerning deficiencies in the incident-management duty described in B, but the texts do not prescribe incompatible conduct, deadlines, or recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different but cumulative norms: B is a substantive, ongoing ICT-risk and incident-management obligation for specified financial entities, while A is an enforcement power that permits authorities to order an essential entity to remedy NIS2 deficiencies or infringements. Compliance with B does not itself discharge any NIS2 obligation, and an enforcement order under A can be obeyed by taking the required remedial measures without conflicting with B.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident management and investigation/reporting obligations for ICT or AI incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity must include reporting ICT-related incidents in its incident-management process, while an AI provider investigating a serious incident must not modify the AI system in a way that could affect later causal evaluation without prior notice to competent authorities. If the same actor and incident fall under both regimes, the reporting duty and the prior-notice condition could create additional procedural steps, but the texts do not make them incompatible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: A requires a process for detecting, managing and reporting ICT-related incidents, while B regulates how an investigation may be conducted when system modifications could affect causal evaluation. Reporting an incident does not require modifying the system, and prior notice permits any otherwise restricted modification; neither provision forbids compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident documentation and reporting obligations concerning personal-data or significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the controller to document all personal-data breaches, while B requires a covered entity to submit an incident notification for a significant incident. If the same event qualifies under both provisions, the entity may have to maintain A's documentation and make B's notification, creating cumulative compliance work. However, A does not require a filing to a recipient or set a deadline, so the texts do not establish two separate reports or conflicting clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are readily cumulative: A is an internal documentation duty intended to enable supervisory review, whereas B is an external notification duty to the CSIRT or competent authority, with specified staged reports and deadlines. Documenting the breach can support the B notification, and nothing in either text says that one duty substitutes for or prevents compliance with the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require authorities to take account of or take action in response to incident-related circumstances. One could argue that A requires an authority to weigh the duration of an infringement in an enforcement decision, while B requires authorities, where appropriate, to take all necessary measures immediately to protect financial-system stability, potentially creating pressure to act before the duration-related assessment is complete.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT-taken concerning cybersecurity monitoring, analysis and information dissemination

verdict.shared_subject: Handling and consequences of ICT-related incidents by financial entities that may also be high-risk AI-system deployers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A keeps the financial entity fully responsible for handling and consequences of reported ICT incidents, while Provision B requires a deployer detecting a serious incident to notify specified recipients. One might argue that the continuing responsibility in A conflicts with B's incident-notification regime or that the financial entity must determine whether responsibility remains with it after notifying others.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, compatible duties: A preserves the financial entity's substantive responsibility for handling and consequences, whereas B requires notification of a serious incident to the provider and then the importer or distributor and market-surveillance authorities. A contains no prohibition on those notifications, and B does not transfer or remove the entity's responsibility under A.

Nothing in either text says that one set of criteria replaces, limits, or overrides the other; each authority can consider all criteria applicable under its own instrument.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or notification of an incident by an entity subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious ICT-related incident may also constitute a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect an individual's privacy. In that case, the same entity must make two distinct notifications: one to the competent authority under A and one to the affected person under B, with different recipients and potentially different timing requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are independently satisfiable and concern different recipients and purposes: regulatory incident reporting under A and individual privacy notification under B. Nothing in either provision says that one notification substitutes for the other, so there is no contradiction in making both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity suffers a serious ICT-related incident involving a database breach that is likely to have adverse consequences for the privacy of identified individuals. It must submit the initial notification “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” within the applicable Article 20 deadlines under A, and must also notify each affected person “onverwijld” under B; notifying the authority does not notify the individuals, and notifying the individuals does not satisfy the authority-reporting duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the cumulative reporting burden from the provisions shown. The separate exceptions or qualifications in the contextual material—such as encryption making individual notification unnecessary—could remove B in a particular case, but they do not make the two duties substitutes as a general matter.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity obligations of entities in the financial sector
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A imposes a broad, risk-based duty to adopt appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage cybersecurity risks and prevent or limit incidents. Provision B imposes an additional reporting duty for certain ICT incidents, including a voluntary report under the Regulation, to the sectoral CSIRT; one might argue that reporting is a separate operational burden not expressly addressed in A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: A concerns preventive and mitigating cybersecurity measures, while B concerns reporting specified ICT incidents to a designated CSIRT. Nothing in A forbids reporting or makes its security-measure duty a substitute for B's reporting obligation.

verdict.shared_subject: Digital operational resilience and conformity-assessment oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information-related obligations in regulated digital contexts, so an entity involved in both regimes might need to communicate post-incident changes and conformity-assessment matters. However, the duties concern different actors, triggers, recipients, and subject matter: financial entities perform post-incident evaluations, while notified bodies inform the notifying authority about notification-related circumstances and activities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations are independently satisfiable and do not prescribe incompatible conduct. Provision A requires financial entities to conduct post-incident evaluations after serious ICT incidents; provision B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about specified conformity-assessment matters, including circumstances affecting notification scope or conditions.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT-related incidents and personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires financial entities to report ICT-related incidents, while B requires an electronic-communications provider to notify the affected person without delay when a personal-data breach is likely to harm privacy. If one event falls within both descriptions, the duties concern different reporting actions and B expressly identifies the affected person as recipient, so reporting under A would not obviously satisfy B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: an incident-management process can include the required notification to the affected person. The texts do not establish that the same actor is subject to both provisions, that every personal-data breach is an ICT-related incident, or that A requires a separate filing to a different recipient or on a different deadline.
verdict.missing_reference: The recipient, deadline and procedural content of the reporting duty under 32022R2554 art. 17 (or its applicable implementing provisions), together with the scope of the actors subject to both provisions, are needed to determine whether A and B require two separate notifications or whether they can be satisfied through one communication.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: Transparency information about automated decision-making and human oversight of high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern automated decision-making and require information or capabilities relevant to detecting problems in automated systems. One could argue that Article 13(f)'s transparency duty and Article 14(a)'s oversight duty use different operational perspectives: the data subject must receive useful information about the underlying logic, while human overseers must understand the system's capabilities and limitations well enough to detect irregularities and unexpected performance.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative but distinct duties on different aspects of AI governance. Article 13 requires the controller to inform the data subject about automated decision-making and, at least in the specified cases, its logic, significance and expected consequences; Article 14 requires provision of a high-risk AI system enabling responsible natural persons to monitor it and detect irregularities. An operator can satisfy both duties independently, and neither text says that fulfilling one substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and their processing-related obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern a high-risk AI system and impose obligations on actors involved with it. However, Article 35 requires a data-protection impact assessment before high-risk processing, while Article 36 requires notification of specified certification circumstances; neither provision forbids or makes compliance with the other impossible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different objects, triggers, and addressees: the controller must conduct a prior assessment where processing likely creates a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms, whereas the competent authority or replacement notified body must immediately inform the Commission, Member States, and other notified bodies. They can be performed cumulatively without one discharging or obstructing the other.

verdict.shared_subject: The European Commission’s separate evaluation/assessment duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require the Commission to conduct an evaluative exercise, and both concern EU digital or cyber-related regulation. If the duties were directed to the same subject matter and timetable, their overlapping evaluation obligations could create duplication or uncertainty about whether one evaluation satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions require different evaluations for different purposes and under different legal instruments. Provision A requires an impact assessment before adopting delegated acts concerning mandatory use of European cybersecurity certification schemes, while Provision B requires, by 17 January 2026, an evaluation and report on whether strengthened digital-operational-resilience requirements should cover statutory auditors and audit firms; the Commission can perform both independently.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system by an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same serious incident and require reporting to different recipients. Article 26 requires notification first to the provider and then to the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities, while Article 29 separately requires a final report to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority within one month; one filing does not textually discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are individually satisfiable and concern different reporting stages, recipients, and content. Article 26 concerns immediate notification of a serious incident, whereas Article 29 concerns a later, detailed final report, so there is no requirement to choose between incompatible acts.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity operates a high-risk AI system and identifies a serious incident that is also an incident covered by Article 27. It must immediately notify the provider and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities under Article 26, and must separately submit a detailed final report to its CSIRT and competent authority no later than one month after the Article 27 notification under Article 29; the different recipients and reporting stages mean both filings are required.

They concern different authorities, procedures, triggers, and legal consequences; nothing in either text requires one authority to breach the other’s rule.

verdict.shared_subject: Human oversight of high-risk AI processing personal data and a data subject’s right to object
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 can require the controller to stop processing when a data subject objects, unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Article 14(e), as specified, requires the system to enable human overseers to decide in specific situations to ignore or override the AI output, which could appear to support continued human decision-making rather than cessation of the underlying processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: Article 21 governs the controller’s response to an objection to processing under GDPR Article 6(1)(e) or (f), while Article 14(e) concerns a high-risk AI system’s technical capability for human overseers to disregard its output. Enabling an override does not itself require continued processing after a valid objection, and the Article 21 exception permits processing where overriding legitimate grounds are established.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose reporting-related obligations that could arise around the same security incident or measure. However, Provision A requires notice to the affected subscriber, while Provision B requires an end report to the entity's CSIRT and competent authority; the recipients, content, and timing differ, so one filing does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the provider can promptly notify the subscriber under A and later submit the detailed end report to its CSIRT and competent authority under B. They concern different reports to different recipients and do not prescribe incompatible conduct or deadlines.

verdict.shared_subject: Onverwijlde kennisgeving van een incident aan personen die door de dienstverlening of persoonsgegevens worden geraakt
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij één incident kan een entiteit onder A haar dienstontvangers moeten informeren omdat het incident een nadelige invloed heeft op de dienstverlening, terwijl de aanbieder onder B de betrokken persoon moet informeren omdat de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen heeft voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer. Dit zijn afzonderlijke kennisgevingen aan verschillende ontvangers; de ene kennisgeving vervangt de andere niet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen kunnen zonder inhoudelijke botsing cumulatief worden nageleefd: dezelfde onverwijlde handelwijze kan beide kennisgevingsplichten uitvoeren, mits de relevante ontvangers en inhoud worden onderscheiden. Geen bepaling verbiedt of beperkt de andere kennisgeving.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit die tevens aanbieder is, krijgt te maken met één cyberincident dat zowel de dienstverlening nadelig beïnvloedt als waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen heeft voor de persoonlijke levenssfeer van een geïdentificeerde klant. De entiteit moet onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten informeren op grond van A én onverwijld de betrokken klant informeren op grond van B; een bericht aan de klant vervangt de kennisgeving aan alle dienstontvangers niet, en omgekeerd.
verdict.decisive_exception: Geen beslissende uitzondering is nodig voor de classificatie. Wel kunnen de in de context genoemde uitzonderingen bij B, zoals passende versleuteling, de concrete toepassing van B uitsluiten; die uitzondering is in het gegeven scenario niet aangenomen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

However, neither provision regulates the same decision, actor, deadline, or substantive outcome.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires a competent authority, when imposing specified enforcement measures against an essential entity, to take relevant previous infringements into account. Provision B establishes when a provisional measure concerning an AI system is deemed justified after a three-month or thirty-day objection period; it does not prohibit considering prior infringements or otherwise constrain the assessment required by A.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and investigation by entities subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A prohibits an AI provider from conducting a potentially causally relevant system-modifying investigation without prior notice to the competent authorities, while provision B requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident. If the same incident is both serious and significant, the reporting obligation in B might appear to require immediate reporting while A conditions a related investigative action on prior notice.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts: A restricts a particular form of investigation or system modification unless authorities are notified beforehand, whereas B requires reporting significant incidents under separate provisions. Reporting the incident under B can coexist with giving the prior notice required by A; neither text requires the prohibited investigation to occur without notice or makes the two duties mutually exclusive.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related communications by authorities and financial entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related information flows, and a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system used by a financial entity could lead to communications under both regimes. However, the duties are imposed on different actors and involve different actions: Provision A requires the competent authority to acknowledge a financial entity’s notification, while Provision B requires the market-surveillance authority to notify specified national authorities after receiving a serious-incident report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively without contradiction. The competent authority can acknowledge receipt under Provision A, while the market-surveillance authority separately informs the national authorities under Provision B; neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other action, and the texts do not establish that the same authority, recipient, or triggering report must be used.

verdict.shared_subject: Notifying recipients/subscribers about a significant cyber threat or network/service security threat
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to an internet-access provider facing a threat: Provision A requires notifying service recipients of the significant cyber threat itself, while Provision B requires notifying the affected subscriber before taking a protective measure, or as soon as possible afterward. The strongest tension case is that one event may trigger two notices to potentially overlapping but differently defined recipients, with no stated rule that one notice discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different triggers and purposes. A applies to essential or important entities and significant cyber threats affecting service recipients; B applies to an internet-access provider taking a measure under Article 7.6a(1)(g), and requires notice to the affected subscriber, including an opportunity to remedy the threat where possible. A provider can make both notifications, and neither provision forbids the other or establishes incompatible timing or content.

No text indicates that incident response would prevent maintaining the register or that the register would constrain CSIRT assistance.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The CSIRT duty applies to CSIRTs and concerns responding to incidents and providing assistance where applicable. The ACM provision requires the ACM to maintain a register containing specified information about number assignees; the duties can be performed independently and cumulatively without incompatible requirements.

verdict.shared_subject: Melding en daaropvolgende besluitvorming
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen gebruiken het begrip ‘melding’, zodat men oppervlakkig zou kunnen vermoeden dat zij dezelfde gebeurtenis en procedure regelen. Als artikel 5.6 op dezelfde melding ziet, schrijft het een onmiddellijke beslissing voor, terwijl artikel 33 een melding aan een toezichthoudende autoriteit binnen maximaal 72 uur regelt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 33 verplicht de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke een inbreukmelding aan een bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit te doen; artikel 5.6 verplicht kennelijk een andere besluitvormende actor om na ontvangst van een melding onverwijld een besluit te nemen. De bepalingen leggen dus geen tegenstrijdige verplichtingen aan dezelfde actor op en artikel 5.6 verbiedt of vertraagt de melding uit artikel 33 niet.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns a voluntary cyber-threat notification, with onward transmission by the competent authority to other authorities or, for significant credit institutions, to the ECB without delay. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report when an incident is still ongoing at the final-report deadline, so an incident could potentially involve both a voluntary threat notification and a mandatory progress report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not impose incompatible duties. A's notification is expressly voluntary and concerns a significant cyber threat, while B concerns a continuing incident and requires a progress report; an entity can refrain from making A's optional notification and still comply with B, or make both where their conditions are met. They also do not establish the same triggering event, recipient, or reporting clock sufficiently to show cumulative mandatory filings.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision A is voluntary ('op vrijwillige basis'), so an entity can avoid that reporting mechanism without violating A; the text also does not establish that A's voluntary notification and B's progress report are mandatory reports concerning the same event to different recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Handling and onward communication of significant ICT incidents or cyber threats
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related information flows and involve onward handling by public bodies. One could argue that the EU provision requires competent authorities to take all necessary measures after an assessment, while the Dutch provision gives a CSIRT competence to forward a voluntary report, potentially creating overlapping institutional handling.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors and different acts: Article 19 requires EBA, ESMA, Eiopa or the ECB, where appropriate, to take measures to protect financial-system stability after a notification assessment, whereas Article 33 merely permits a CSIRT to forward a voluntary report to another CSIRT. Nothing in either text forbids the other action, and the CSIRT forwarding competence does not prevent the financial authorities from taking necessary measures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Op basis van die kennisgeving nemen de bevoegde autoriteiten, in voorkomend geval, alle nodige maatregelen om de onmiddellijke stabiliteit van het financiële systeem te beschermen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT kan de vrijwillige melding ter behandeling doorsturen naar een ander CSIRT.

verdict.shared_subject: Transparency information for personal-data collection and effective human oversight of high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern automated processing and could apply to the same high-risk AI system. However, Article 13 requires the controller to inform the data subject about automated decision-making and its logic, importance, and expected consequences, while Article 14 requires the system to be designed so natural persons can effectively supervise it; one might argue that transparency information does not itself ensure effective oversight.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties that can readily be satisfied together: the controller provides the specified information to the data subject, and the high-risk AI provider designs the system and interfaces for effective human supervision. Nothing in Article 14 deems disclosure under Article 13 sufficient for oversight, and nothing in Article 13 forbids or limits the required human-supervision design.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions describe the same replacement filing, not two cumulative reports to different recipients: an ongoing incident means that the final report is replaced by a progress report, followed by a final report within one month after resolution. Provision B appears to implement or restate Provision A's rule for essential or important entities, and nothing shown requires an additional separate filing or identifies different recipients or incompatible deadlines.

verdict.shared_subject: Information/reporting duties concerning cyber threats and conformity-assessment activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information duties, but they concern different triggering events, recipients, and subject matter. If a notified body is also an essential or important entity and the same underlying activity involves a significant cyber threat affecting its service recipients, it could face a duty to inform those recipients and a separate duty to inform the notifying authority; one communication would not ordinarily discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are addressed to different recipients and regulate materially different information: provision A concerns notifying service recipients of a significant cyber threat, while provision B concerns a notified body's conformity-assessment activities, and only upon request. They can therefore be complied with cumulatively without contradiction, and provision B does not require reporting the cyber threat itself.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns how a competent authority weighs prior infringements when taking enforcement measures against an essential entity, while Provision B imposes a separate deadline for making a notification. The provisions regulate different actors, subject matters, and triggers, so no concrete incompatibility is apparent.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: An authority can consider prior infringements while the relevant person or entity makes the notification required by Provision B.
