verdict.shared_subject: Ministerial authority to prescribe arrangements when regulated parties cannot reach agreement
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions empower the Minister to intervene after parties fail to agree, so the same Minister could potentially receive requests concerning arrangements involving overlapping telecommunications infrastructure or frequency use. However, neither provision prohibits the other intervention or prescribes incompatible content, timing, or procedure.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 11a.3 concerns providers’ joint continuity plans for designated antenna sites, while Article 12.10 concerns users’ agreement on the joint use of assigned frequency space and operates on application by one or more users. These are distinct subject matters, actors, and statutory mechanisms; even if they overlap factually, both ministerial powers can be exercised cumulatively without contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien de in het vierde lid bedoelde aanbieders geen overeenstemming kunnen bereiken over het gezamenlijke continuïteitsplan, kan Onze Minister voorschriften geven inzake het tot stand brengen van het plan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien gebruikers als bedoeld in artikel 3.21 aan wie frequentieruimte is toegewezen als bedoeld in artikel 3.5, dan wel aan wie vergunning is verleend voor het gebruik van frequentieruimte, geen overeenstemming kunnen bereiken over de voorwaarden waaronder de aan hen toegewezen frequentieruimte gezamenlijk in gebruik zal worden genomen, kan Onze Minister op aanvraag van een of meer van hen, voorschriften geven inzake het tot stand brengen van een overeenkomst als bedoeld in artikel 3.21.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT incident response and cooperation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions assign incident-related functions to CSIRTs, and Provision A requires information exchange and discussion when a network member requests it after an incident, while Provision B requires the CSIRT, where applicable, to respond to incidents and assist an essential or important entity. In a complex incident, the CSIRT might need to allocate resources between responding to the entity and exchanging information with another network member.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and complementary, not incompatible: Provision A concerns exchanging and discussing incident information at the request of an affected CSIRT-network member, whereas Provision B concerns responding to incidents and assisting an essential or important entity where applicable. Nothing in either text prohibits performing both duties, and Provision B expressly includes participation in the CSIRT network and mutual assistance on request.
verdict.evidence_span_a: f) op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk dat mogelijkerwijs gevolgen ondervindt van een incident, het uitwisselen en bespreken van informatie over dat incident en de daarmee samenhangende cyberdreigingen, risico’s en kwetsbaarheden;
verdict.evidence_span_b: c. indien van toepassing, het reageren op incidenten en verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit;

verdict.shared_subject: Verplichtingen rond transparantie over persoonsgegevens en menselijk toezicht op hoog-risico-AI
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen op dezelfde hoog-risico-AI-toepassing betrekking hebben, maar regelen verschillende verplichtingen: AVG art. 14 verlangt individuele informatie aan de betrokkene, terwijl AI Act art. 14 proportionele toezichtmaatregelen verlangt. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat toezichtmaatregelen en informatie over geautomatiseerde besluitvorming verschillende, mogelijk overlappende waarborgen zijn, zodat onduidelijkheid ontstaat of het ene het andere kan vervangen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen cumulatieve maar goed verenigbare verplichtingen op aan verschillende aspecten van dezelfde verwerking. De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke kan de betrokkene informeren over geautomatiseerde besluitvorming en de onderliggende logica, terwijl de aanbieder of gebruiksverantwoordelijke daarnaast proportionele menselijke toezichtmaatregelen toepast; geen van beide teksten bepaalt dat naleving van de andere verplichting volstaat of haar uitsluit.
verdict.evidence_span_a: g) het bestaan van geautomatiseerde besluitvorming, met inbegrip van de in artikel 22, leden 1 en 4, bedoelde profilering, en, ten minste in die gevallen, nuttige informatie over de onderliggende logica, alsmede het belang en de verwachte gevolgen van die verwerking voor de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De toezichtmaatregelen staan in verhouding met de risico’s, de mate van autonomie en de gebruikscontext van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant/serious incident by an entity or AI-system provider subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an incident-reporting obligation with different deadlines: A requires an incident notification within 72 hours, while B requires a notification immediately and no later than 15 days. If the same incident falls within both regimes, the texts could be read as requiring separate reports under each instrument, potentially to different authorities and on different procedural bases.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not themselves establish that two separate filings are required for the same incident. A's extracted recipient is unspecified, and B's recipient appears only in the contextual paragraph, not in the compared paragraph. The shorter 72-hour deadline can be met while also satisfying B's 15-day deadline, so absent proof of distinct recipients or separate filings, the duties are cumulatively satisfiable rather than conflicting.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions establishing whether the A incident notification to the CSIRT or competent authority and the B serious-incident notification to the market-surveillance authority are separate mandatory filings when the same event qualifies under both regimes. The shown B paragraph alone does not identify its recipient, while the recipient appears in art. 73(1), which is supplied only as context.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk processing or AI systems and the associated compliance obligations

One might argue that the operator faces two overlapping pre-deployment procedures and that the AI Act documentation could be viewed as addressing the same risk-assessment function as the GDPR consultation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations have different triggers, actors’ actions, and purposes. Article 36 requires consultation with the supervisory authority when the DPIA shows high residual risk absent mitigation; Article 11 requires technical documentation demonstrating conformity with the AI Act and supplying information to competent authorities and notified bodies. The operator can prepare the documentation and, where Article 36 is triggered, separately consult the data-protection authority; neither provision says that one substitutes for or prevents the other.

The recipients and triggering matters differ, so one filing would not ordinarily discharge the other.

verdict.shared_subject: EU digital-law oversight and warning documentation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations concerning information and oversight in the digital-regulation sphere. One requires the Committee to issue guidance about when a personal-data breach is likely to create a high risk, while the other requires qualified system-risk warnings to contain a description of relevant facts and reasons; their subject matter and addressees differ, however, and nothing in either text makes the duties incompatible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The GDPR provision binds the Committee to issue guidance concerning circumstances in which a personal-data breach likely creates a high risk, whereas the AI Act provision binds qualified warnings to state the relevant facts and reasons. These are different duties performed by different institutional actors, and both can be fully satisfied without affecting the other.

De meldingen zouden echter verschillende doelen en ontvangers hebben: A betreft een vrijwillige melding van een significante cyberdreiging door een financiële entiteit aan een bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B een aanbieder verplicht een betrokken abonnee te informeren vóór of zo snel mogelijk na een maatregel.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/security incidents involving financial entities that are also providers of public electronic communications services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to establish processes ensuring that underlying causes of ICT-related incidents are detected, documented, and removed. Provision B separately requires a provider of a public electronic communications service to notify the Dutch data-protection authority immediately of a qualifying security breach; the same incident could therefore trigger both an internal root-cause-remediation duty and an external notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties on different aspects of incident handling: A concerns registration, monitoring, investigation, documentation, and remediation, while B concerns immediate notification to a specified authority. A contains no reporting duty or recipient, so B's notification cannot conflict with or be discharged by A's processes; nor does B prevent the investigation and remediation required by A.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant or serious incidents involving an AI system or essential/important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: For an incident that is both a serious incident under Provision A and a significant incident under Provision B, the same entity may have to make separate notifications: A requires notification to the provider and then the importer or distributor and market-surveillance authorities, while B requires prompt notification to the recipients of its services. The recipients differ, and notifying one group does not notify the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be satisfied cumulatively: the entity can notify all recipients required by A and separately notify its service recipients under B. Nothing in either text says that one notification substitutes for the other, and the duties concern different recipients rather than incompatible acts.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity operates a high-risk AI system and suffers one incident that qualifies both as a serious incident under Article 26 and as a significant incident adversely affecting service provision under Article 30. It must first notify the AI provider and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities under A, while also notifying its service recipients without delay under B; notifying the authorities and supply-chain actors does not discharge the separate notification to service recipients.

The reporting power in B can be exercised to oversee or document cybersecurity measures and does not prohibit or make compliance with A impossible.

verdict.shared_subject: Personal-data/security breaches involving providers of public electronic communications services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions address breach-related compliance, and a qualifying security breach under provision B may also be a personal-data breach that must be documented under provision A. However, provision A requires documentation for supervisory control, while provision B requires immediate notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens; the texts do not expressly say that notification substitutes for the separate documentation duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are different and cumulatively satisfiable: provision A requires maintaining documentation, whereas provision B requires notifying the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens without delay. Notification under B does not prevent the provider from also documenting the breach under A, and A does not impose a separate filing deadline or recipient that would create a second reporting obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke documenteert alle inbreuken in verband met persoonsgegevens, met inbegrip van de feiten omtrent de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de gevolgen daarvan en de genomen corrigerende maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens die zijn verwerkt in verband met de levering van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst in de Europese Unie.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related measures and reporting by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber of the measure as soon as possible when urgency prevents prior notice. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report during an ongoing incident and a final report within one month after resolution; if the same actor and event fall under both, these are different communications with different apparent recipients and purposes, so one filing would not obviously discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the provider can promptly notify the affected subscriber under A and separately submit the progress and final reports required by B. The texts do not impose incompatible content, deadlines, or prohibitions; A's extracted recipient is unspecified, and B's reporting recipient is also not stated here, so the text shown does not establish the distinct-recipient condition required for dual-reporting tension.
verdict.decisive_exception: None. Although the provisions may require separate communications in practice, the shown text does not establish that they are reports to different recipients or otherwise make one filing incapable of satisfying the other; in any event, both duties can be performed cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer dit wegens de vereiste spoed niet voorafgaand aan het nemen van de maatregel mogelijk is, doet de aanbieder zo snel mogelijk melding van de maatregel.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk processing/AI systems and the obligations applicable before or during deployment
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to a high-risk AI system involving personal-data processing. Article 36 requires prior consultation where the DPIA identifies high residual risk, while Article 9 requires testing during development and before market placement or use; these are different, cumulative obligations rather than incompatible commands.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations have different triggers, objects, and timing: Article 36 concerns consultation with the supervisory authority when a DPIA shows high risk absent mitigation, whereas Article 9 concerns testing against predefined metrics and thresholds for a high-risk AI system. An operator can perform the required testing and also consult the authority, so neither provision prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het testen van AI-systemen met een hoog risico vindt, zoals passend, in de loop van het ontwikkelingsproces plaats en in ieder geval voordat het systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident under Provision A must be reported immediately to the entity’s CSIRT or competent authority, while Provision B requires a financial entity to submit an initial notification and subsequent interim and final reports to the relevant competent authority. If the same financial entity and incident fall under both regimes, the provisions point to different reporting structures and potentially different clocks, with DORA’s continuing reports not discharged by the NIS2 notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can notify the NIS2 CSIRT or competent authority immediately and separately submit DORA’s initial, interim, and final reports to the relevant competent authority. The texts do not expressly make one filing substitute for the other; indeed, they identify distinct reporting obligations and recipients, although the NIS2 context allows national arrangements involving DORA authorities or CSIRTs.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also an essential or important entity under NIS2 and suffers one cyber incident that both significantly affects its services and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident under DORA. It must report the incident “onverwijld” to its NIS2 CSIRT or competent authority under Provision A, and must submit DORA’s initial notification, then an interim report after a material change and a final report with the completed root-cause analysis and actual impact figures to the “relevante bevoegde autoriteit” under Provision B. Filing the immediate NIS2 report does not itself provide the DORA interim and final reports, and the provisions do not establish a single harmonised recipient or clock for the two regimes.
verdict.decisive_exception: The result could differ if applicable national implementation or DORA/NIS2 coordination rules expressly deem one filing to satisfy the other or establish a single coordinated reporting channel. The text shown does not establish such a substitution; DORA’s context instead says that Member States may additionally require reporting to NIS2 authorities or CSIRTs.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in: a) een eerste kennisgeving; b) een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie, in voorkomend geval gevolgd door geactualiseerde kennisgevingen telkens wanneer een relevante actualisering van de status beschikbaar is, alsmede op specifiek verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit; c) een eindverslag, wanneer de analyse van de onderliggende oorzaken is voltooid, ongeacht of er reeds beperkende maatregelen zijn uitgevoerd, en wanneer de werkelijke impactcijfers beschikbaar zijn in plaats van ramingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations of regulated entities to public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties, and a single organisation might conceivably be both an aangemelde instantie and an aanbieder of a public electronic communications service. In that case, the duties concern different events and recipients: A covers requested conformity-assessment activities, while B covers a qualifying personal-data security breach and requires immediate notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are independently satisfiable because their triggers, subject matter, and recipients differ. A is a request-based disclosure to the notifying authority about conformity-assessment activities; B is an immediate breach notification to the data-protection authority, so neither filing discharges the other and there is no incompatible command.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same serious incident could trigger A's continuing reports to the relevant competent authority and B's immediate notification first to the provider and then to the importer or distributor and market-surveillance authorities. Those are separate duties with different recipients and timing, so one notification does not obviously discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can submit A's initial, interim and final reports within the Article 20 deadlines while separately making B's immediate notifications. Nothing in either provision says that compliance with one reporting regime substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank operating a high-risk AI system discovers one serious ICT-related incident that is also a serious incident involving that AI system. It must submit A's initial and subsequent reports “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” within the Article 20 deadlines, while under B it must immediately notify the provider first and then “de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten”; filing the A report does not make those separate B notifications.

verdict.shared_subject: Analyses, technical investigation, and ICT-incident response
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern responding to ICT-related threats or incidents. One could argue that setting detection thresholds and response criteria might channel the response process, while the other requires the Minister or another authority to conduct analyses and technical research, potentially creating overlapping operational expectations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties on different functions: Provision A requires detection mechanisms to set thresholds and criteria for activating incident-response processes, while Provision B requires an authority to perform analyses and technical research for assisting other entities. Nothing in either text forbids the other activity, and detection criteria can trigger or inform the assistance and research without replacing it.

verdict.shared_subject: Member States’ designation or establishment of competent authorities for cybersecurity-related functions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require each Member State to designate or establish one or more competent authorities, and Article 8 assigns cybersecurity and Chapter VII supervisory responsibilities while Article 9 assigns large-scale cyber-incident and crisis-management responsibilities. A tension might be alleged if the provisions were read as requiring separate authorities for each function, potentially creating overlapping institutional requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose compatible organisational duties: a Member State may designate or establish authorities that perform different, overlapping, or combined functions. Neither provision requires the authorities to be distinct, nor does either prohibit an Article 8 authority from also serving as a cyber-crisis-management authority; the additional Article 9 requirements concerning resources and coordination can be satisfied cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat gaat over tot het aanwijzen of instellen van een of meer bevoegde autoriteiten, verantwoordelijk voor cyberbeveiliging en voor de in hoofdstuk VII van deze richtlijn bedoelde toezichthoudende taken (bevoegde autoriteiten).
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat gaat over tot het aanwijzen of instellen van een of meer bevoegde autoriteiten die verantwoordelijk zijn voor het beheer van grootschalige cyberbeveiligingsincidenten en crises (cybercrisisbeheerautoriteiten).

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations concerning regulated activities or incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns onward dissemination by a competent authority after receiving serious ICT-incident notifications, while Provision B requires a separate notification by the person or entity concerned before implementing a specified intention. If the same actor and event happened to fall within both regimes, the actor might face two reporting-related obligations with different triggers and timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts, triggers, and apparent actors: A requires a competent authority to provide incident details to listed recipients after receiving reports, whereas B requires a notification concerning an intention, generally eight weeks before implementation or, for a public bid, no later than its announcement. Nothing in the texts makes compliance with one notification impossible or substitutes one for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related duties of a provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern a provider responding to an incident, and both involve communication with an authority. One might argue that an incident under Article 73 could also be a personal-data security breach requiring immediate notification under Article 11.3a, creating overlapping response obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Article 73 regulates how an AI provider investigates a serious incident and prohibits modifying the AI system during that investigation without prior notice to the competent authorities. Article 11.3a separately requires a provider of a public electronic communications service to notify the Dutch data-protection authority of a qualifying personal-data security breach; the provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties and do not prohibit either notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verricht geen onderzoek waarbij het AI-systeem wordt gewijzigd op een wijze die van invloed kan zijn op de latere evaluatie van de oorzaken van het incident, zonder de bevoegde autoriteiten daarvan vooraf in kennis te stellen

verdict.shared_subject: A provider of a high-risk AI system experiencing a serious incident that is also a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect an individual's privacy.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same underlying breach may trigger two distinct notifications: A requires a serious-incident notification by the statutory deadline, while B requires immediate notice to the affected person. These duties are directed to different recipients and are not interchangeable, so one notification cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the provider can notify the market-surveillance authority under A and the affected person under B, with B being made immediately and A no later than 15 days after awareness. Nothing in either shown provision forbids or substitutes for the other notification.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider of a high-risk AI system becomes aware of a serious incident that has caused a personal-data breach likely to have adverse effects on a named individual's privacy. The provider must make the serious-incident notification required by A, ultimately within 15 days, and must also notify the affected individual immediately under B; notifying the individual does not notify the market-surveillance authority, and notifying that authority does not notify the individual.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: The CSIRT duty to proactively scan an essential or important entity’s network and information system for vulnerabilities with potentially significant consequences.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A refers to scanning the entity’s “network- en informatiesystemen” (plural), while Provision B refers to scanning the entity’s “netwerk- en informatiesysteem” (singular). One might argue that B is narrower and does not require scanning multiple information systems, whereas A does.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions impose the same substantive task on a CSIRT: on request, proactively scan the relevant network and information system(s) of an essential or important entity to detect vulnerabilities with potentially significant consequences. The singular/plural wording does not establish incompatible duties, deadlines, permissions, or scopes; a CSIRT can comply with both by scanning the relevant systems as required.
verdict.decisive_exception: The apparent singular/plural difference is ordinary drafting or scope wording, not an express limitation making compliance with one provision violate the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek van een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit: het proactief scannen van de netwerk- en informatiesystemen van de betrokken entiteit om kwetsbaarheden met mogelijk significante gevolgen op te sporen
verdict.evidence_span_b: het op verzoek van een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit proactief scannen van het netwerk- en informatiesysteem van de betrokken entiteit om kwetsbaarheden met mogelijk significante gevolgen op te sporen

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use notification-related language, so one might superficially suggest overlapping reporting activity. If the same actor and event were involved, the GDPR authority’s notice and the Dutch-law notification could appear to create parallel duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A gives a supervisory authority the competence to notify a controller or processor of an alleged GDPR infringement; it does not impose a notification duty on the actor governed by provision B. Provision B requires a separate notification, at least eight weeks before the intended implementation date (or at the public-offer announcement), concerning a contemplated transaction. The actors, triggers, recipients, and legal functions are distinct.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke of de verwerker in kennis te stellen van een beweerde inbreuk op deze verordening
verdict.evidence_span_b: De melding in het eerste lid wordt gedaan uiterlijk acht weken voor de beoogde datum van uitvoering van dit voornemen.

verdict.shared_subject: Handling and onward communication of serious ICT-related incidents and voluntary incident reports
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern the handling of incident-related information and allow or require onward involvement of another CSIRT or competent authority. In a case where a voluntary report is forwarded by the CSIRT while the financial-sector authorities are also required to assess and notify other Member State authorities, the texts do not specify how the two channels interact or which authority controls the onward handling.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A imposes an assessment and notification duty on EBA, ESMA, Eiopa or the ECB after receiving information under Article 19(6), whereas Provision B merely gives the CSIRT competence to forward a voluntary report to another CSIRT. These are different actors, triggers and functions; forwarding a report does not prevent the financial authorities from performing their separate assessment and notification duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Na ontvangst van informatie overeenkomstig lid 6 beoordelen de EBA, de ESMA of de Eiopa en de ECB, in overleg met Enisa en in samenwerking met de relevante bevoegde autoriteit, of het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident relevant is voor andere bevoegde autoriteiten van andere lidstaten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT kan de vrijwillige melding ter behandeling doorsturen naar een ander CSIRT.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns outsourcing incident-reporting duties by financial entities and preserves their responsibility. Provision B concerns requesting an ACM decision about the applicability, location, timing, and manner of works after failed negotiations; it imposes no incident-reporting duty or prohibition that conflicts with A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different subjects, actors, triggers, and authorities: A concerns financial-entity ICT-incident reporting and outsourcing responsibility, while B concerns a telecom/infrastructure-style dispute and a request for an ACM decision within a specified period. An entity could comply with both if both happened to apply, because neither provision restricts the conduct required by the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten mogen de rapportageverplichtingen uit hoofde van dit artikel aan een derde aanbieder van diensten uitbesteden overeenkomstig Unie- en nationaal sectoraal recht.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien binnen 2 maanden na de datum van verzending van de schriftelijke kennisgeving geen overeenstemming is bereikt, kan de aanbieder alsmede de rechthebbende of de beheerder, bedoeld in artikel 5.2, binnen 2 weken de Autoriteit Consument en Markt verzoeken een beschikking te geven over de toepasselijkheid van de gedoogplicht of de plaats, het tijdstip en de wijze van de uit te voeren werkzaamheden.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and associated compliance assessments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply around the deployment of a high-risk AI system, but they impose different obligations on different actors and address different assessments. A market-surveillance authority may temporarily allow placing the system on the market while conformity procedures are completed, whereas a controller must conduct a data-protection impact assessment before processing where processing is likely to create a high risk to individuals’ rights and freedoms; the authorization does not textually waive or replace that DPIA.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are readily cumulative: the authority can grant a temporary derogation from the conformity-assessment procedure, while the controller separately performs any required DPIA before personal-data processing. They concern different actors, triggers, and procedures, and neither provision says that the Article 46 authorization exempts the controller from Article 35.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit

verdict.shared_subject: ICT governance, security and information about vulnerabilities or ICT risks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose organisational or technical arrangements concerning ICT security and information flows. One could argue that Enisa’s database and the financial entity’s governance and reporting channels create overlapping expectations about how ICT vulnerabilities and risks are managed.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different functions: Enisa must develop and maintain a European vulnerability database, while a financial entity’s management body must establish governance arrangements and internal information channels. The duties can be performed cumulatively without either requiring conduct prohibited by the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related reporting by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns voluntary reporting of significant cyber threats, with the relevant authority forwarding the notification to the ECB without delay. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report during an ongoing incident and a final report within one month after resolution; if the same event qualifies under both regimes, the reports have different content, recipients or procedural bases and one does not expressly discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: an entity may voluntarily notify the relevant authority under A and separately submit the progress or final report required by B. Moreover, A is expressly voluntary, so an entity can avoid that reporting duty by not making the optional notification; the texts do not establish an unavoidable conflict or incompatible deadlines.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision A is voluntary ('op vrijwillige basis'), so it is an avoidable duty rather than an obligation that necessarily collides with B. The provisions also do not establish that A's notification and B's progress/final report are filings for the same recipient or that one must substitute for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zij dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld.

verdict.shared_subject: Maatregelen en handhaving rond aanbieders van ICT- of elektronische communicatiediensten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers the lead overseer to impose a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider after non-compliance with oversight measures. Provision B requires an electronic-communications provider to notify the affected subscriber before taking a measure, or as soon as possible where urgency prevents prior notice; a measure could potentially be both an oversight-enforced measure and a subscriber-affecting measure.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different norms on different actors and concern different legal acts: A concerns the lead overseer's competence to impose a fine, while B concerns the provider's notification duty toward a subscriber. Nothing in A forbids notification, and nothing in B forbids or limits the lead overseer's competence to impose a fine; both can therefore be complied with cumulatively where their scopes overlap.
verdict.evidence_span_a: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingsplichten rond ICT- of netwerkveiligheidsincidenten/maatregelen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen in een feitelijk samenhangende cybersecuritysituatie een melding verlangen, maar zij richten zich op verschillende ontvangers en gebeurtenissen: A aan de bevoegde autoriteit bij een ernstig ICT-incident, B aan de betrokken abonnee vóór of zo snel mogelijk na een maatregel. Als één incident zowel onder A valt als aanleiding geeft tot de maatregel van B, is de melding aan de ene ontvanger niet de melding aan de andere.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen geen onverenigbare verplichtingen op. A vereist een toezichthoudersmelding door een financiële entiteit; B vereist een abonnee-melding door een aanbieder in verband met een specifieke maatregel, zodat beide meldingen cumulatief kunnen worden gedaan. Bovendien is bij A geen concrete termijn in de getoonde norm opgenomen, terwijl B alleen de timing van de abonnee-melding regelt.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een financiële entiteit die tevens aanbieder van een netwerk- of dienst is, krijgt een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident dat ook een bedreiging vormt voor de integriteit of veiligheid van het netwerk of de dienst. Zij moet het incident melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit op grond van A én, voordat zij de bedoelde maatregel neemt, de betrokken abonnee melden en gelegenheid geven de bedreiging weg te nemen; als spoed voorafgaande melding onmogelijk maakt, moet zij de abonnee zo snel mogelijk na de maatregel informeren. De twee meldingen hebben verschillende ontvangers en functies, zodat de ene filing de andere niet vervangt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system to make or support a decision involving a data subject, where GDPR Article 21 gives that person an objection right.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 can require the controller to stop processing after an objection unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Article 14(d), by contrast, requires the high-risk AI system to be supplied so that human overseers can decide, where appropriate and proportionate, to disregard or reverse the system’s output and replace it with another decision. One might argue that the AI Act’s human-override design duty presupposes continued system use, while the GDPR right may require cessation of the relevant processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative and compatible duties: the AI system must enable human intervention or reversal, while the controller must separately respect an objection and stop processing unless an overriding ground applies. Human oversight and reversal do not themselves authorise continued processing or displace the GDPR’s exception; the controller can comply with both by stopping the processing when Article 21 requires it and ensuring the system also supports appropriate human intervention in other cases.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 21 itself supplies the decisive condition: processing may continue only if the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds overriding the data subject’s interests, rights and freedoms, or grounds relating to legal claims. Article 14(d) does not state that the ability to reverse an AI output overrides that right or substitutes for stopping processing.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts and apparently different actors or procedures: A concerns post-incident evaluation and identifying ICT or continuity-policy improvements by financial entities; B concerns taking a decision immediately after receiving a notification. Nothing in the texts makes A's improvement-identification duty the decision referred to in B, nor does B impose a deadline on A's evaluation.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory language and concern notification or documentation-related conduct. However, Provision A applies to financial entities and ICT-related incidents, while Provision B applies to cable-maintenance work on public land and requires notice to a municipal mayor or authorised official; no common actor, event, recipient, or reporting duty is established.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate entirely different activities and actors. Provision A requires financial entities to register ICT incidents and ensure their underlying causes are identified, documented, and remedied; Provision B requires a cable-work provider to notify the competent municipal authority before work and, where applicable, requires the authorised official to inform the mayor as soon as possible. They can both be complied with whenever their separate scopes happen to overlap.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and associated data-protection compliance
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to an organisation involved with a high-risk AI system, but they impose different duties: GDPR Article 36 requires prior consultation only where a DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while Article 16 requires the provider to draw up an EU declaration of conformity. One might argue that the AI Act conformity declaration could be treated as sufficient assurance that no prior data-protection consultation is needed, creating uncertainty about whether both procedures must be performed.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct, cumulative duties with different triggers, actors, and purposes. Article 36 concerns a data controller's prior consultation with the supervisory authority when the DPIA shows a high risk absent mitigation; the selected norm in Article 16 concerns an AI provider's obligation to prepare an EU declaration of conformity. Nothing in either text states that the declaration substitutes for, overrides, or discharges the GDPR consultation duty.

verdict.shared_subject: A duty to provide cooperation, involving different categories of actors and different recipients or purposes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use a mandatory cooperation duty, so an entity that falls within both descriptions might have to cooperate with the military authority under Article 14.5 and with a listed telecommunications party under Article 14a.5. If the requested actions were incompatible, the entity would face competing mandatory instructions, but neither text states such incompatibility.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different actors, triggers, and purposes: Article 14.5 concerns providers of public telecommunications networks or services and frequency users when Article 31 of the War Act is applied, while Article 14a.5 concerns specified connected financial-market institutions cooperating with a listed telecommunications party in an investigation. Both duties can ordinarily be performed cumulatively, and no provision forbids compliance with the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory language concerning information and regulatory oversight, so one might initially suspect overlapping reporting or accountability burdens. However, Article 22 concerns financial entities’ responsibility for ICT-related incidents, while Article 45 concerns notified conformity-assessment bodies reporting their activities to the notifying authority; the texts do not impose incompatible duties on the same actor or regulate the same event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different actors, triggers, and subject matters. A financial entity remains responsible for reported ICT incidents under Article 22, whereas a notified body must, upon request, inform the notifying authority about conformity-assessment and related activities under Article 45; both duties can be performed independently without one preventing compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity governance and incident-related compliance
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers competent authorities to order a person or entity to stop and not repeat conduct that infringes Regulation 2022/2554. Provision B obliges the CSIRT to ensure dynamic risk and incident analysis and cybersecurity situational awareness; an authority’s corrective order could theoretically affect conduct relevant to that function, but the texts do not say that the order may lawfully require the CSIRT to stop this statutory task.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of rules on different actors: A grants competent authorities enforcement powers, while B assigns a task to the CSIRT. Nothing in A requires an authority to prohibit the CSIRT’s statutory cybersecurity analysis, and nothing in B prevents enforcement against infringing conduct; both can therefore operate cumulatively.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related/significant incident management and reporting by regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an incident notification within 72 hours after knowledge of a significant incident, while provision B requires financial entities to establish integrated processes ensuring that underlying causes are identified, documented and remedied. For a financial entity covered by both, the reporting obligation and the root-cause-management duty concern the same incident but impose different actions, so one does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative and independently satisfiable requirements: the entity can submit the incident notification required by A and also register, investigate, document and remedy underlying causes under B. Provision B contains no separate reporting recipient or deadline, and provision A does not prohibit or replace the internal incident-management processes required by B.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an incident that may qualify both as a serious ICT-related incident and as a personal-data security breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity that is also an operator of a public electronic communications service could face one incident triggering both duties. The filings go to different recipients—the relevant competent authority under A and the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens under B—and use different timing rules, so reporting to one does not, on the text shown, discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative rather than contradictory: the entity can submit an interim report to the relevant competent authority after the initial notification while also notifying the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens without delay. Nothing in either provision forbids the second filing or states that one report substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company qualifying as both a financial entity and an operator of a public electronic communications service suffers a security breach that is both a serious ICT-related incident and has adverse consequences for personal-data protection. It must submit the interim report to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” after the initial notification under A, within the Article 20 deadlines, and separately notify “de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens” “onverwijld” under B; the two recipients and clocks differ, and neither filing is stated to satisfy the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a notified body to provide information to the notifying authority on request about its conformity-assessment activities. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report when an incident is still ongoing at the time the final report is due. If one organisation happened to be subject to both regimes, the duties could involve separate reporting obligations, but the texts do not show that they concern the same event, recipient, or report.

Nothing in either text makes one report substitute for the other or creates incompatible deadlines or contents.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without unreasonable delay under Provision A, while a financial entity must submit an initial notification and subsequent reports to the relevant competent authority under Provision B. A single serious ICT incident involving a personal-data breach could therefore trigger communications to different recipients under separate regimes, with no indication that the DORA reports to the competent authority discharge the GDPR processor-to-controller notification.

Nothing in either text prohibits the other communication or states that one filing substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Bijstand bij cyberbeveiligingsmonitoring
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen gebruiken een verplichting tot het verlenen van bijstand, zodat een oppervlakkige lezing kan suggereren dat dezelfde actor voor dezelfde monitoringstaak onder twee regimes valt. De bepalingen formuleren die bijstand echter voor verschillende institutionele rollen en met verschillende voorwaarden.

Artikel 16, onder a, betreft daarentegen de taak van het CSIRT om op verzoek een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit bij te staan bij realtime- of bijna-realtime-monitoring; beide verplichtingen kunnen naast elkaar worden uitgevoerd en geen van beide verbiedt de andere.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the financial entity to notify affected clients, while B requires an essential or important entity offering a trust service to report the significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority. If the same entity and incident fall within both provisions, these are cumulative communications to different recipients, with B also imposing a 24-hour outer deadline; notifying clients does not notify either authority, and reporting to the authorities does not notify clients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed because they address different recipients and purposes: client notification under A and regulatory/CSIRT reporting under B. There is no incompatible command or deadline; the entity can make both notifications promptly.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that offers a trust service discovers a significant ICT-related incident that affects the financial interests of its clients and the provision of its trust service. It must notify the affected clients under A and separately report the incident to its CSIRT and competent authority under B, within 24 hours if immediate reporting is not possible; neither filing discharges the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Bevoegdheden van overheidsinstanties en bevoegde autoriteiten om maatregelen te verlangen rond gereguleerde entiteiten of AI-systemen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen concern intervention by an authority, but they confer different powers: provision A allows a fundamental-rights authority to request testing of a high-risk AI system, while provision B allows the competent authority to issue a binding direction to an essential entity. If the same authority and entity are involved, the provisions could raise questions about which authority controls the intervention and whether a binding direction can constrain the requested testing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily operate cumulatively because they have different actors, triggers, objects and legal regimes. Provision A concerns a reasoned request by a fundamental-rights authority to the market-surveillance authority for technical testing when documentation is insufficient; provision B concerns a competent authority's binding direction to an essential entity for compliance with the NIS2 framework. Neither provision forbids the other's action or makes one power exclusive.

Als zij op exact dezelfde aanvraag en hetzelfde bevoegde orgaan zouden zien, zou moeten worden vastgesteld welke termijn geldt.

Een beslistermijn van twee maanden voor de ACM botst niet met een termijn van drie maanden voor de ministeriële procedure; ieder orgaan kan zijn eigen termijn naleven.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity-related reporting and follow-up
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A CSIRT must guarantee the anonymity of a person or entity reporting a vulnerability, while B requires a competent authority to acknowledge receipt of incident notifications. If the same communication channel or records were used, an acknowledgement process could potentially create administrative traces that expose a reporter's identity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different reports, recipients and actors: A concerns a coordinator CSIRT protecting the identity of a vulnerability reporter; B concerns a competent authority acknowledging a financial entity's DORA incident notification. B neither requires disclosure of a vulnerability reporter's identity nor displaces the CSIRT's anonymity obligation.
