verdict.shared_subject: Security and incident-risk management by an entity that is also a provider of a general-purpose AI model with systemic risk
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose security- and risk-related obligations, but they use different formulations: Provision A requires an appropriate cybersecurity level for the AI model and its physical infrastructure, while Provision B requires measures proportionate to the entity’s exposure, size, incident likelihood and severity, including social and economic consequences. The strongest tension case is that an operator might regard a risk-proportionate level under B as sufficient even though A requires an independently appropriate level for the model and infrastructure.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the operator can apply Provision B’s risk-based proportionality factors while also ensuring the appropriate cybersecurity protection required by Provision A. Nothing in either text says that compliance with one benchmark substitutes for or overrides the other; the provisions also concern different regulatory duties and potentially different scopes.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity may outsource its reporting duties under Article 19 but remains fully responsible. verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related notification by an internet-access or network service provider

If the provisions were applied to the same delegated act, one might question whether their scopes or legal bases produce different extension rules.

They can be performed cumulatively, and neither text says that the interim report substitutes for informing recipients or vice versa.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity experiences a significant cyberthreat after making the initial notification required by provision A. It must submit an interim report to “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” after the initial notification, while also informing potentially affected service recipients without delay and, if necessary, notifying them of the threat; filing the interim report with the authority does not inform those recipients or discharge the separate duty to them.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations of an organisation that is both a GDPR controller and a notified conformity-assessment body
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A personal-data breach may require the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours, while the same underlying event could also be an circumstance affecting the scope or conditions of the body's notification and therefore require notification to the notifying authority. Those are potentially separate filings to different authorities, and provision B supplies no deadline or rule that one notification discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers and recipients: provision A concerns a personal-data breach posing a risk to individuals, whereas provision B concerns circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of a conformity-assessment body's notification. A breach will not necessarily affect that scope or those conditions, so in the ordinary case each duty operates independently without conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A notified conformity-assessment body that is also a GDPR controller suffers a cyberattack exposing personal data and, as a result, loses a condition or capability relevant to its notification. It must notify the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach and separately notify the notifying authority of the circumstance affecting the scope or conditions of its notification; filing with one authority does not notify the other, and provision B states no deadline resolving how the two reports interact.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or notification duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a financial entity to submit an initial notification to the relevant competent authority concerning a serious ICT-related incident. Provision B requires advance notification to the municipal mayor or authorised official when cable-maintenance work is carried out on public land; if the same actor and event somehow fall within both regimes, the duties concern different authorities and different triggers, so one filing would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to materially different activities and triggers: A concerns financial entities reporting serious ICT-related incidents, while B concerns providers notifying municipal authorities before cable-maintenance work on public land. Nothing in either text forbids or makes compliance with the other impossible; each can be performed independently when its own conditions are met.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in: a) een eerste kennisgeving;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious/significant ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority, while B requires a qualifying trust-service entity to report a significant incident to both its CSIRT and its competent authority within 24 hours. If the same incident falls under both provisions, the entity appears to owe a report to the CSIRT in addition to the report required under A, and the texts do not say that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions require incident reporting to a competent authority, and B's 24-hour deadline could be met alongside A's duty without any incompatible content or deadline. Moreover, A permits Member States to require reporting to CSIRTs, which could indicate coordination between the regimes, although the provision shown does not establish that the B filing is the same filing or that it satisfies A.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity providing a trust service becomes aware of an incident that is both a serious ICT-related incident under A and a significant incident affecting provision of its trust service under B. It must report under A to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46” and under B “bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” within 24 hours; reporting to the competent authority under A does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate CSIRT filing required by B.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive unresolved point is whether the competent authority under A and the competent authority under B are the same recipient and, more importantly, whether a single filing can legally satisfy both duties. The text shown does not establish that the A report may be submitted to the CSIRT or that the B filing discharges A's reporting obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: In afwijking van het eerste lid dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit als dat incident gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van haar vertrouwensdienst.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions both use the concept of a notification or reported event, so a superficial comparison might suggest overlapping reporting obligations. However, provision A concerns a proposed acquisition of control in a telecommunications party, while provision B concerns information-sharing about significant incidents involving an essential entity that is also a critical entity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors, concerning different triggers, recipients, and subject matter. A requires the person intending to acquire control to make a notification by a specified time; B requires a competent authority to provide information about a reported significant incident. Nothing in either text prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De melding in het eerste lid wordt gedaan uiterlijk acht weken voor de beoogde datum van uitvoering van dit voornemen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting by a financial entity/provider concerning a cyber or serious AI incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same entity and event fall under both regimes, provision A requires a voluntary significant-cyber-threat notification to be forwarded onward, while provision B requires a serious-incident notification to market-surveillance authorities. The duties appear to concern different reports and recipients, so one filing would not necessarily discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A is expressly voluntary: a financial entity may report only when it considers the threat relevant. It therefore can avoid triggering A, and the shown text does not establish that the same event must be reported under both provisions or that the A forwarding duty and B incident notification are separate mandatory filings for the same actor.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions establishing whether the entity is an AI-system provider subject to Article 73(1), whether the event is a serious incident under that provision, and whether the voluntary Article 19 notification is actually made and must be forwarded to a recipient distinct from the Article 73 market-surveillance authority.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 19's voluntary nature is decisive: the entity can comply with Article 73 without making the optional Article 19 notification. The shown text also does not establish that Article 19's forwarding duty is mandatory once a voluntary notification is made in the relevant circumstances.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious/significant ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an incident report within 72 hours to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. Provision B separately requires financial entities to report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, with no deadline stated in the shown norm; therefore, a qualifying financial entity may face two reporting duties, potentially involving different recipients and procedures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: the entity can submit A's incident report within 72 hours and B's report to the relevant competent authority. Moreover, A itself permits reporting to a competent authority, and B's shown text does not establish a different deadline or expressly require a separate filing for the same incident.
verdict.missing_reference: The classification depends on whether the same incident is both a 'significant incident' under Directive (EU) 2022/2555 and a 'serious ICT-related incident' under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, and on the Article 20 deadlines, models and procedures referenced by Article 19(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. The shown provisions do not establish whether the two reports are separate filings, whether they go to the same recipient in practice, or whether one filing can satisfy both duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Toezicht en opvolging rond ICT-dienstverleners en ernstige incidenten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen een bevoegde autoriteit een verplichting op in een toezichtcontext. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat dezelfde autoriteit bij één incident zowel risico’s van een kritieke ICT-dienstverlener moet meewegen als de kennisgevingsprocedures moet volgen, zonder dat de verhouding tussen die taken wordt uitgewerkt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen regelen echter verschillende handelingen: A schrijft een inhoudelijk beoordelingscriterium voor bij een besluit over een kritieke derde ICT-dienstverlener, terwijl B de markttoezichtautoriteit verplicht passende maatregelen te nemen en kennisgevingsprocedures te volgen binnen zeven dagen. Geen van beide verplichtingen verbiedt of vervangt de andere; zij kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de ernst van de niet-naleving
verdict.evidence_span_b: volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet

verdict.shared_subject: Informatie over significante incidenten en handhaving bij essentiële entiteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen raken aan significante incidenten bij essentiële entiteiten. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat het doorgeven van incidentinformatie aan een andere bevoegde autoriteit de handhavingsbeoordeling beïnvloedt, terwijl artikel 32 vereist dat de autoriteit de ernst en het belang van de geschonden bepalingen meeweegt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 32 legt een beoordelingsplicht op aan bevoegde autoriteiten bij handhavingsmaatregelen; artikel 40 legt een informatieverstrekking op aan een bevoegde autoriteit over een gemeld incident. De bepalingen schrijven geen tegenstrijdige handelingen voor: informatieverstrekking kan juist naast en ten behoeve van de beoordeling van de ernst van een inbreuk plaatsvinden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de ernst van de inbreuk en het belang van de geschonden bepalingen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident

verdict.shared_subject: Information about reported ICT vulnerabilities and electronic-service security
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the coordinating CSIRT to guarantee the reporter’s anonymity. Provision B requires certain public bodies and organisations to provide the Minister with data and information needed to prevent or end breaches of secure and reliable electronic access; if that information includes the reporter’s identity, disclosure could undermine A’s anonymity guarantee.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different functions: A concerns the coordinating CSIRT’s handling of vulnerability reports, while B concerns specified bodies and organisations supplying information to the Minister. Provision B does not expressly require disclosure of a vulnerability reporter’s identity, and the texts do not establish that the same actor must disclose information that A requires to remain anonymous.
verdict.evidence_span_a: waarborgt de anonimiteit van de natuurlijke of rechtspersoon die de kwetsbaarheid meldt
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents and the institutional response to them
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, when taking enforcement measures, to consider the seriousness and importance of the breached provisions. Provision B requires the CSIRT, where applicable, to respond to incidents and provide assistance; one might argue that an incident response focused on assistance could sit uneasily with an authority’s enforcement assessment, particularly where the incident reflects a serious breach.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and serve different functions: A governs how competent authorities assess enforcement measures, while B assigns operational incident-response and assistance tasks to the CSIRT. Nothing in B forbids enforcement or requires the CSIRT to disregard the seriousness of a breach, and nothing in A prevents incident response or assistance.

verdict.evidence_span_b: indien van toepassing, het reageren op incidenten en verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit;

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of ICT incidents or cyber threats by entities subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern reporting-related actions, and a financial entity could potentially be involved in an ongoing significant incident while also voluntarily reporting a significant cyber threat under DORA. The strongest tension case is that the NIS2 progress report and the DORA voluntary notification may involve different reporting channels and separate communications, so one might not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The compared NIS2 norm requires a progress report only when the significant incident is still ongoing, whereas the compared DORA norm concerns a voluntary report of a significant cyber threat, not a mandatory report of the same incident. The DORA provision therefore does not require the entity to make the voluntary report, and the texts do not establish that the two reports concern the same triggering event or that both filings are mandatory.
verdict.decisive_exception: The voluntary nature of the DORA reporting mechanism: “op vrijwillige basis”. An entity can comply with both provisions by submitting the mandatory NIS2 progress report and choosing not to make the optional DORA cyber-threat notification; the shown text also does not establish that a DORA voluntary notification is a separate mandatory filing triggered by the NIS2 incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: indien het incident nog aan de gang is op het moment dat het in punt d) bedoelde eindverslag wordt ingediend, zorgen de lidstaten ervoor dat de betrokken entiteiten op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.

verdict.shared_subject: The entity’s reporting of a significant incident, specifically the final report and the early-warning information.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions regulate information supplied in connection with a significant incident, and Article 23(a) requires an early warning containing information that Article 26 also requires. If Article 26 were read as imposing a separate early-warning filing, the entity might face two reporting duties concerning overlapping information.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A, as expressly limited, requires submission of a final report, due no later than one month after the incident report (and, in the stated continuing-incident case, after handling the incident). Provision B requires contact details to be supplied in the early warning; it does not require a separate filing or impose a conflicting deadline, and the two duties can readily be performed cumulatively.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed: the provisions concern different reporting stages and do not establish two separate filings triggered by the same event with different recipients or incompatible clocks.

verdict.shared_subject: Verplichte medewerking door partijen of aanbieders van openbare telecommunicatiediensten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen verplichten tot medewerking, zodat men oppervlakkig zou kunnen denken dat dezelfde aanbieder mogelijk twee verschillende bevelen of verzoeken moet uitvoeren. De teksten bevatten echter geen tegenstrijdige inhoud, termijn of verbod: medewerking aan een geschilbeoordeling kan naast medewerking aan een rechtmatige tap- of opnamebevelgeving bestaan.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 12.11 ziet op partijen bij een geschil en medewerking die de minister redelijkerwijs kan vorderen binnen een redelijke termijn. Artikel 13.2 ziet specifiek op aanbieders van openbare telecommunicatiediensten en op uitvoering van strafvorderlijke, psychiatrische of inlichtingenrechtelijke bevelen of toestemmingen; naleving van de ene verplichting verhindert naleving van de andere niet.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bij het geschil betrokken partijen zijn verplicht onverwijld, maar in elk geval binnen de door Onze Minister gestelde redelijke termijn, alle medewerking te verlenen die deze redelijkerwijs kan vorderen ten behoeve van de beoordeling van het geschil.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van openbare telecommunicatiediensten zijn verplicht medewerking te verlenen aan de uitvoering van een bevel op grond van het Wetboek van Strafvordering of artikel 13:3a, eerste lid, onderdeel b, van de Wet verplichte geestelijke gezondheidszorg dan wel een toestemming op grond van de Wet op de inlichtingen- en veiligheidsdiensten 2017 tot het aftappen of opnemen van door hen verzorgde telecommunicatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities potentially subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a final incident report after the incident is handled, while provision B concerns voluntary reporting of significant cyber threats and, for certain significant credit institutions, forwarding that notification to the ECB. If the same financial entity and event fall within both regimes, the texts point to different reporting processes and potentially different recipients, so one filing may not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B is expressly voluntary: a financial entity may report a significant cyber threat only when it chooses to do so. It therefore does not impose a mandatory filing that conflicts with A, and the shown text does not establish that the same event must be reported under both provisions or that B's voluntary notification is the same subject matter as A's mandatory final incident report.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision B's voluntary character is decisive: an entity can comply with A without making the optional B notification. The text also does not establish that A's final report must be forwarded to the ECB or that B's voluntary cyber-threat notification substitutes for A's final incident report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uiterlijk één maand na de indiening van het in punt b) bedoelde incidentmelding, een eindverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Incident or breach reporting by a financial entity/provider where the same event is both a serious ICT-related incident and a personal-data breach.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the financial entity to prepare incident notifications and reports, while provision B requires notifying the affected data subject without delay. For one event, these are separate communications to different recipients, so reporting to the competent authority does not itself notify the affected person.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can both be performed: the entity can prepare the reports required by A and separately notify the affected person under B. Nothing in either shown provision says that one notification substitutes for the other or makes compliance with one impossible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an incident involving an AI system and a network/information system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same event is both a ernstig incident under Provision A and an incident continuing until the deadline for the final report under Provision B, the same entity may have to make A's immediate notifications to the provider, importer/distributor and market-surveillance authorities, while also submitting B's progress report. These are different reporting acts, with different content and no text stating that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: the entity can immediately notify the recipients required by A and separately submit the progress report required by B. They concern different reporting duties and the texts shown do not impose incompatible deadlines or prohibit making both reports.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial or other entity using a high-risk AI system experiences a continuing cyber incident that both qualifies as a “ernstig incident” under A and remains unresolved when B's final-report deadline arrives. The entity must first notify the provider and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities under A, while also submitting a progress report under B “op dat moment”; submitting the progress report does not notify A's recipients, and notifying A's recipients does not submit B's report.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the cumulative reporting burden on the texts shown; the key issue is that the provisions require distinct filings. The exact recipient and content requirements under B's first paragraph are not shown, but B expressly requires a progress report and A expressly requires notifications to specified recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities providing public electronic communications services that are also essential or important entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same security incident could trigger both duties: Provision A requires immediate notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, while Provision B requires a final report to both the entity's CSIRT and competent authority within one month. These are separate reports to different recipients, with different content and timing, so compliance with one does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed: the actor can notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately and later submit the required detailed final report to its CSIRT and competent authority. Nothing in either text prohibits the other filing or makes the deadlines mutually exclusive.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An entity that provides a public electronic communications service and is also an essential or important entity suffers one security breach affecting the protection of personal data. It must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens 'onverwijld' under Provision A and separately submit, no later than one month after the Article 27 notification, a final report 'bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit' containing the incident description, cause and mitigation measures under Provision B; the first filing does not reach the two recipients or satisfy the specified content of the second.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk processing or AI systems and the associated compliance assessments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same AI-related processing, but they impose different assessments on different actors for different purposes: the GDPR requires the controller to conduct a data-protection impact assessment before processing where the processing is likely to create a high risk, while the AI Act provision requires the provider to follow an Annex VII conformity-assessment procedure in specified standardisation circumstances. The strongest tension case is therefore that an organisation may need to perform two substantial assessments, with no indication in the shown texts that one substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are cumulative and readily satisfiable: a controller can conduct the GDPR impact assessment before processing and the provider can separately follow the applicable AI Act conformity-assessment procedure. They concern different legal duties, actors, triggers and subject matter, and neither text says that compliance with one discharges or conflicts with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: de aanbieder de conformiteitsbeoordelingsprocedure van bijlage VII

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting information about significant ICT-related incidents or cyber threats
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns forwarding a voluntary cyber-threat notification to another authority, while provision B requires an entity to include three specific items in an early warning. If the same communication is both a voluntary A notification and a B early warning, A does not expressly say that the forwarded notification must contain B’s fields, and B does not identify a recipient or state that its early warning satisfies A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not impose incompatible content or deadlines. An entity can include the information required by B in an A notification and forward it as required by A; moreover, A’s forwarding duty is triggered only when the entity voluntarily makes the relevant notification, so it can avoid that optional duty altogether.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De relevante bevoegde autoriteit kan dergelijke informatie aan de in lid 6 genoemde andere relevante autoriteiten verstrekken.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt de entiteit de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding.

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative enforcement orders (last onder dwangsom) for regulatory violations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions empower an authority to impose an enforcement order on an entity following a violation. If the same domain-name registrar also falls within the financial-supervision obligations referenced in provision A, it could face orders from two authorities concerning overlapping conduct, potentially with different terms or deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different authorities, legal bases, and regulated obligations: provision A addresses violations of obligations under article 3.17(7) of the Financial Supervision Act, while provision B addresses domain-name registration services and specified articles 42, 44, 47, 49 and 50. Each order can be complied with independently, and neither provision forbids or discharges the other authority’s enforcement power.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteit kan een entiteit die domeinnaamregistratiediensten verleent een last onder dwangsom opleggen in geval van overtreding van het bepaalde bij of krachtens de artikelen 42, 44, 47, 49 en 50.

verdict.shared_subject: AI systems involving personal-data processing and high-risk compliance
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to a high-risk AI system, but they impose different obligations: Article 35 requires the controller to conduct a prior data-protection impact assessment, while Article 25 requires an original provider to provide technical access and assistance needed for AI Act compliance. One might argue that the provider-assistance duty could require access to information or systems implicated in the DPIA, creating an additional coordination burden.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties on different actors and for different purposes. Article 35 requires a controller to assess risks to natural persons' rights and freedoms before processing, whereas Article 25 requires an original provider, in the specified value-chain circumstances, to assist a new provider with AI Act obligations, particularly high-risk conformity assessment; neither provision forbids compliance with the other or makes one duty substitute for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: A duty to provide cooperation, but imposed on different actors for different administrative purposes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory cooperation language, so a superficial reading might suggest overlapping obligations to provide assistance. If the same entity somehow fell within both actor categories, it would have to cooperate with both sets of authorities or administrative bodies.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and in different contexts. Provision A binds providers of public telecommunications networks or services and frequency users to assist authorities designated under Article 14 of the Exceptional Powers Civil Authority Act, whereas Provision B binds the other involved administrative bodies to provide cooperation needed for substantive coordination of permit applications; neither text requires or forbids conduct that prevents compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Significante cyberincidenten of cyberdreigingen affecting an essential or important entity and its service recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same serious cyber event, but they require communications to different audiences: A requires an incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 72 hours, while B requires prompt information to potentially affected service recipients. These are separate communications, so the authority report cannot discharge the recipient-information duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different purposes and recipients and can readily be performed cumulatively: the entity can report the incident to the CSIRT or competent authority while separately informing affected service recipients about protective measures and, where necessary, the threat. Nothing in either provision prohibits or substitutes for the other communication.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity discovers a significant cyberincident that both compromises its network and creates a significant cyberthreat for its customers. It must submit the incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 72 hours under A, while also promptly informing the potentially affected service recipients about measures they can take and, if necessary, the threat under B. Filing with the CSIRT or competent authority does not inform the recipients, and informing the recipients does not satisfy the authority-reporting duty; both communications are required, with B providing no fixed deadline.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting cyber/data-security incidents by financial entities that may also involve personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A personal-data breach must be reported to the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours where applicable, while DORA art. 19 permits voluntary reporting of significant cyber threats and, for certain significant credit institutions, provides for forwarding the voluntary notification to the ECB. If the same event qualifies under both provisions, the recipients differ and the GDPR filing does not discharge the separate DORA-related notification or forwarding route.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision B concerns a voluntary notification of a significant cyber threat, so a financial entity can avoid that mechanism and still comply with the mandatory GDPR breach notification duty. Moreover, B does not itself impose a mandatory ECB filing on every entity or every incident; its voluntary and conditional wording means there is no unavoidable conflict with A.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive point is that B's reporting is expressly voluntary ('op vrijwillige basis') and applies only where the entity considers the threat relevant to the specified interests; the extracted ECB forwarding route is likewise conditional on the voluntary notification and the provision's classification conditions. Thus an entity can comply with A without making the optional B notification. If the question instead concerned mandatory serious-incident reporting under art. 19(4), that separate provision would be needed, but it is expressly excluded here.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related incident management and an immediately issued decision after receipt of a notification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions mention incident-related processes or notifications, so one might initially suspect that the incident-management process under Provision A must accommodate the immediate decision required by Provision B. However, Provision A imposes a general process-design duty on financial entities, while Provision B requires an unspecified decision by an unspecified actor immediately after receiving a notification; the texts do not establish that they regulate the same actor, decision, trigger, or operational duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with together: a financial entity can establish and implement an ICT-incident management process while any applicable decision-maker takes a decision immediately after receiving a notification. Nothing in Provision A requires delaying a decision, and nothing in Provision B prohibits or displaces an incident-management process.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity enforcement and information-sharing concerning essential/critical entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern competent authorities and cybersecurity incidents involving regulated entities. One could argue that authority A permits warnings for infringements, while provision B requires an authority to transmit information about a reported significant incident, potentially creating overlapping handling duties for the same matter.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of rules on different actors: provision A grants competent authorities enforcement competence to issue warnings for infringements of the Directive, whereas provision B requires a competent authority to provide information to the authority designated under Article 8 of the Critical Entities Resilience Act. A warning is not prohibited by the information-sharing duty, and the information-sharing duty does not prevent or replace enforcement action.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity governance and enforcement
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, when taking enforcement measures, to consider the seriousness of infringements and the importance of the provisions breached. Provision B requires the Minister to establish a national plan for large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crisis response; one might argue that a centrally planned crisis-response framework could constrain case-specific enforcement priorities, but no such constraint is stated.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and operate at different levels: A governs how competent authorities assess enforcement measures in individual cases, while B assigns the Minister competence to establish a national plan. The national plan can coexist with case-specific consideration of infringement seriousness and does not direct authorities to disregard those factors.

These are different reporting stages and, on the text shown, A's final report is not the same filing as B's initial notification, so both could be required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity submits B's notification within 72 hours and later submits A's final report within one month after handling the incident. Neither provision forbids the other filing, and the different deadlines do not make simultaneous compliance impossible.

verdict.shared_subject: Assistance provided by a processor versus mutual assistance between CSIRTs
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory language concerning assistance, so one might initially suspect overlapping duties. However, Article 28 concerns a processor assisting its controller with GDPR compliance, while Article 11 concerns CSIRTs assisting other CSIRT-network members, and the actors, triggers, and subject matter differ.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A processor can provide the controller the assistance required by Article 28(e) while a CSIRT separately provides mutual assistance to another CSIRT under Article 11(f). Nothing in either provision prohibits or makes compliance with the other impossible; Article 11(f) is also expressly limited by the CSIRT’s capacities and powers.

verdict.shared_subject: Significant cyber incidents or threats affecting an essential or important entity and its service recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be engaged by the same cyber event, but they require communications with different audiences and serve different purposes: A requires a progress report concerning an ongoing significant incident, while B requires informing potentially affected service recipients about measures and, if necessary, the significant cyberthreat. Thus, one communication would not necessarily discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative rather than contradictory. A progress report is made under the incident-reporting process, whereas B is a separate protective communication to affected service recipients; the entity can make both without violating either provision.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-management and conformity-assessment notification duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose organisational information or process duties, so one might argue that an incident-management process could generate circumstances relevant to an entity’s notification scope or conditions. However, provision A concerns financial entities’ ICT-incident processes, while provision B concerns notified conformity-assessment bodies informing a notifying authority about specified accreditation circumstances; the texts do not make the duties incompatible or establish a common triggering event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties apply to different actors and require different actions: financial entities must establish and implement an ICT-incident management process, whereas notified bodies must inform the notifying authority about circumstances affecting their notification scope or conditions. Each can be fully performed without preventing performance of the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Notifying individuals of personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern the competent authority’s power to require or order notification of a personal-data breach to the affected person. A possible tension is that Provision A describes the supervisory authority as able to order notification, while Provision B says the Dutch authority may require it only where the provider failed to make the required notification and likely adverse privacy effects exist.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively and consistently: Provision B specifies a national-law power concerning a public electronic communications provider after non-notification and a likelihood-of-harm assessment, while Provision A gives the GDPR supervisory authority a corrective power to order notification. The texts do not state that one power excludes, overrides, or substitutes for the other; different conditions and formulations alone do not establish conflict.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant/serious incident involving a high-risk AI system and a network or information system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an incident notification within 72 hours to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. B separately requires the AI-system user, after first notifying the provider, to notify the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities of a serious incident; these are different recipients and the texts do not say that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with: the operator can submit A’s incident notification within 72 hours and make B’s sequential notifications immediately. They concern different regimes and triggers, so overlapping duties alone would not create a conflict if the incidents and recipients are distinct.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company operates a high-risk AI system whose malfunction both qualifies as a significant incident under the NIS2 regime and causes a serious, irreversible disruption of critical infrastructure, making it a serious incident under the AI Act. verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen gebruiken een verplichting tot het verlenen van bijstand, maar zij richten die verplichting tot verschillende actoren en in verschillende juridische relaties: de verwerker ondersteunt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke bij AVG-verplichtingen, terwijl een CSIRT bijstand verleent aan essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten bij realtime of bijna-realtime monitoring. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat bijstand bij monitoring onder beide regimes verschillende verwachtingen of verantwoordelijkheden kan oproepen.

verdict.shared_subject: A duty to provide full cooperation to authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a cooperation duty, but they operate in different regulatory contexts and concern different categories of actors and authorities. One might argue that an actor could face uncertainty if authorities under the two regimes issue incompatible cooperation requests, but neither text creates incompatible commands, deadlines, or limits on cooperation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the relevant ICT provider must cooperate with the financial entity’s competent and resolution authorities under A, while the telecommunications providers or spectrum users must cooperate with authorities designated under the emergency-powers provision under B. The provisions do not prohibit cooperation with the other authority or prescribe conflicting content, timing, or scope.

verdict.shared_subject: Information and oversight concerning secure electronic services and possible GDPR infringements
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A assigns competence to a supervisory authority for a complaint or infringement of the GDPR, while Provision B requires specified bodies and organisations to provide information to the Minister to prevent or end infringements concerning secure and reliable access to electronic services. For an incident involving such a service and personal-data processing, the same organisation might have to cooperate with both authorities, potentially raising coordination questions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of rules on different institutional relationships: A allocates GDPR enforcement competence among supervisory authorities, whereas B creates an information-supply duty to the Minister for specified entities. Nothing in A forbids supplying information to the Minister, and nothing in B reallocates or limits the GDPR supervisory authority's competence; both duties can therefore be performed cumulatively.

This could create parallel pre-action obligations, but neither text makes consultation a substitute for conformity checks or makes conformity checks a substitute for consultation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are imposed on different actors and concern different actions and triggers. A controller can consult the data-protection supervisory authority, while an importer separately checks conformity with the AI Act; both obligations can readily be performed cumulatively, with no incompatible deadline, recipient, or substantive requirement.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting and regulatory response to serious incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions respond to a serious incident, but they impose duties on different actors and through different mechanisms. A serious ICT-related incident may trigger measures by financial-sector competent authorities under A, while a serious incident during real-world testing must be reported by the provider or potential provider to the national market-surveillance authority under B; the texts do not state that one duty replaces the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily operate cumulatively because A concerns competent authorities taking necessary measures, whereas B concerns the provider or potential provider reporting an incident and taking immediate risk-mitigation measures or stopping testing. Their actors, triggers, and duties are distinct, so compliance with both is possible without contradiction.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory treatment of breaches and administrative measures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern consequences of unlawful conduct or personal-data breaches, so one might initially suspect that the information required in a breach notification could affect the authority’s later assessment of responsibility or sanctions. However, provision A governs how competent authorities determine an administrative penalty or corrective measure, while provision B governs the minimum contents of a notification; neither requires or forbids conduct required by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different subjects and at different stages: authorities must consider listed circumstances when setting a measure, whereas the provider’s notification must contain specified breach information. A provider can make the required notification, and the authority can independently consider the listed factors when deciding a measure, without any incompatibility.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT contribution to deploying secure information-sharing tools under Article 10(3) of the NIS2 Directive
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an obligation on a CSIRT to contribute to the rollout of secure information-sharing tools. A possible difference is that provision A expressly conditions the task on Article 10(3), while provision B states the task without an explicit condition, which could appear to make B broader.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions describe the same underlying task and point to the same legal basis: provision A says “op grond van artikel 10, lid 3” and provision B says “bedoeld in artikel 10, derde lid, van de NIS2-richtlijn.” The wording difference is explanatory drafting, not an incompatible duty; a CSIRT can comply with both by contributing to the Article 10(3) rollout.

verdict.shared_subject: Gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling (DPIA) voor verwerking door een hoog-risico-AI-systeem
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Artikel 35 GDPR maakt de DPIA-plicht afhankelijk van een waarschijnlijk hoog risico voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen, terwijl artikel 26 AI Act de gebruiksverantwoordelijke van een hoog-risico-AI-systeem opdraagt de informatie uit artikel 13 te gebruiken om aan diezelfde DPIA-verplichting te voldoen. Dat kan op het eerste gezicht verschillende toepassingsdrempels en informatievereisten opleveren.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 26 verbiedt of beperkt artikel 35 niet, maar verwijst er juist naar en ondersteunt de naleving ervan door het gebruik van artikel-13-informatie voor de DPIA. De verplichtingen kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd: de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voert de op grond van artikel 35 vereiste beoordeling uit en gebruikt daarbij de relevante informatie uit artikel 13; artikel 35 kan bovendien één beoordeling voor vergelijkbare verwerkingen toestaan.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit

verdict.shared_subject: Transparency information about personal-data processing and human oversight of high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to a high-risk AI operator processing personal data: Article 13 requires information to the data subject about automated decision-making and its underlying logic, while Article 26 requires human oversight by qualified persons. One might argue that operationalising meaningful human oversight could require access to information or processes that are not fully disclosed to the data subject. However, neither text forbids the other duty or makes compliance with one substitute for compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties on different aspects of operation. Article 13 requires the controller to provide specified transparency information to the data subject; Article 26 requires the deployer of a high-risk AI system to assign human oversight to suitably qualified persons. The operator can provide the required information and separately arrange the required human oversight.
verdict.evidence_span_a: f) het bestaan van geautomatiseerde besluitvorming, met inbegrip van de in artikel 22, leden 1 en 4, bedoelde profilering, en, ten minste in die gevallen, nuttige informatie over de onderliggende logica, alsmede het belang en de verwachte gevolgen van die verwerking voor de betrokkene.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Gebruiksverantwoordelijken dragen het menselijk toezicht op aan natuurlijke personen die over de nodige bekwaamheid, opleiding en autoriteit beschikken en de nodige ondersteuning krijgen.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI or data-processing activities and the duties imposed on their operators/controllers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same activity, but they impose different obligations: Article 35 requires a prior data-protection impact assessment where processing is likely to create a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms, while Article 16 requires providers of high-risk AI systems to ensure compliance with the AI Act’s Section 2 requirements. The strongest tension argument is that the two regimes use different high-risk triggers and therefore may not identify the same systems or activities as requiring the respective safeguards.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can readily be performed together: a provider can ensure AI-system compliance under Article 16 while the controller separately conducts a DPIA before high-risk personal-data processing. Neither provision says that AI Act compliance substitutes for a DPIA, nor that conducting a DPIA satisfies the Article 16 obligations.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider places an AI system on the market that is classified as high-risk under the AI Act and must therefore comply with Article 16, but the customer’s intended personal-data processing is not, on the facts shown, processing that is likely to result in a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms under Article 35. Conversely, a non-high-risk AI system could be used for processing that independently meets Article 35’s high-risk threshold. The same real-world deployment can therefore fall within one regime’s trigger but not the other’s.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A obliges certain entities to report significant incidents to a CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B gives an operator and other specified parties an optional power to request an ACM decision about the applicability or implementation of a tolerated-duty obligation; the provisions do not impose incompatible acts or deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different subject matters, actors, triggers and authorities: A concerns mandatory cybersecurity-incident reporting, while B concerns a possible request concerning a gedoogplicht and works. An entity can comply with A and, if it chooses and is eligible, separately exercise B without either rule preventing compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien binnen 2 maanden na de datum van verzending van de schriftelijke kennisgeving geen overeenstemming is bereikt, kan de aanbieder alsmede de rechthebbende of de beheerder, bedoeld in artikel 5.2, binnen 2 weken de Autoriteit Consument en Markt verzoeken een beschikking te geven over de toepasselijkheid van de gedoogplicht of de plaats, het tijdstip en de wijze van de uit te voeren werkzaamheden.

verdict.shared_subject: Providing copies of documents in distinct legal proceedings
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require transmission or submission of a copy, so an institution handling related enforcement material might face two document-handling duties. However, they concern different actors, proceedings, recipients, and triggering documents, and neither duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires the lead overseer to send a copy of an information-disclosure decision to specified financial authorities and the JON. Provision B requires a copy of an interested party’s enforcement request to be submitted with a court application; these are cumulative, independently satisfiable obligations concerning different documents and procedures.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De lead overseer zendt onverwijld een afschrift van het besluit inzake informatieverstrekking aan de bevoegde autoriteiten van de financiële entiteiten die gebruikmaken van de diensten van de betrokken kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten en aan het JON.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Bij het verzoekschrift wordt een afschrift overgelegd van het verzoek van de belanghebbende om handhaving van bij of krachtens wet bepaalde regels inzake de bescherming van persoonsgegevens

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions impose obligations in different regulatory domains: provision A requires municipal authorities to decide a consent application within a specified period, while provision B requires an entity to include specified information in an early warning. No fact pattern in the texts makes performance of one obligation prevent performance of the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily be performed cumulatively: the municipality can issue its consent decision within the statutory period, while the relevant entity separately provides the required incident information and contact details in an early warning. They concern different actors, triggers, recipients, and subject matter, with no incompatible deadline, prohibition, or reporting overlap.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Burgemeester en wethouders nemen het instemmingsbesluit binnen acht weken na ontvangst van de schriftelijke melding als bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel a.
verdict.evidence_span_b: geeft de entiteit aan of het significante incident grensoverschrijdende gevolgen kan hebben

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations for different events and activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose prompt notification duties and could, at a very broad level, involve the same operator communicating with public authorities. If a cable-maintenance provider is also an essential or important entity experiencing a significant incident, it might have reporting obligations under both regimes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different triggers, subject matter, and recipients: provision A concerns significant incidents affecting service provision and requires reporting to a CSIRT or competent authority, while provision B concerns planned cable-maintenance work on public land and requires prior notice to the municipal mayor or authorised official. They can readily be performed cumulatively, and neither filing discharges the other; ordinarily they simply regulate different events.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar.

verdict.shared_subject: Information sharing about assessment or audit results
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require disclosure of information about compliance-related results, so an entity involved in both regimes might need to disclose overlapping results to different institutional actors. However, provision A concerns results of targeted cybersecurity audits made available to the competent authority, while provision B concerns a notified body sharing negative, and requested positive, AI conformity-assessment results with other notified bodies; the texts do not establish that these are the same results, trigger, actor, or recipient.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are addressed to different actors and concern different processes and recipients: A requires targeted cybersecurity-audit results to be made available to the competent authority, whereas B requires a notified body to share AI conformity-assessment results with other notified bodies, with positive results shared only on request. Both duties can be performed cumulatively without either prohibiting or discharging the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De resultaten van een gerichte beveiligingsaudit worden ter beschikking gesteld van de bevoegde autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke aangemelde instantie verstrekt de andere aangemelde instanties die soortgelijke conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten voor dezelfde soorten AI-systemen verrichten, relevante informatie over negatieve conformiteitsbeoordelingsresultaten, en op verzoek ook over positieve conformiteitsbeoordelingsresultaten.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting certain incidents by financial-sector entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying personal-data breach must be reported to the competent data-protection supervisory authority, while B requires the listed financial-sector entities to make the relevant ICT-incident notification also to the sectoral CSIRT. The recipients are different, and nothing in the shown provisions says that reporting to one recipient discharges the other; thus one incident may require two filings.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can report the same incident to the supervisory authority within 72 hours and also notify the designated CSIRT. B has no stated deadline, so there is no incompatible timing requirement, and B's reference to a voluntary notification may mean that not every incident triggers that particular limb.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank discovers an ICT security incident that constitutes a personal-data breach likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms and also falls within the ICT-incident notification referred to in B. The bank must report it to the Article 55 competent supervisory authority within 72 hours and separately make the Article 19 notification to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors; filing with the first recipient does not, on the text shown, notify the second.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the Article 19 notification in B is mandatory for this particular incident, including whether the referenced 'vrijwillige melding' is being invoked, depends on the referenced Article 19 provisions and potentially the Cybersecurity Act. If that notification is not triggered, there is no dual-reporting burden for that incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative orders (last onder bestuursdwang/last) imposed for regulatory non-compliance
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern imposing an administrative order on an offender, so a single operator might face enforcement under both regimes. However, neither provision forbids compliance with the other, and they assign competence to different authorities for different underlying obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A authorises the Minister to impose a bestuursdwang order to enforce obligations under the provisions referred to in article 15.1(1), while Provision B authorises the Dutch Data Protection Authority to impose an order concerning obligations under article 3.17(7) of the Financial Supervision Act. These are cumulative, separately scoped enforcement competences, and the texts do not establish incompatible orders, deadlines, recipients, or subject-matter requirements.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister is bevoegd tot: a. oplegging van een last onder bestuursdwang ter handhaving van de verplichtingen, gesteld bij of krachtens de in artikel 15.1, eerste lid, bedoelde bepalingen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: De Autoriteit persoonsgegevens kan in geval van overtreding van de krachtens artikel 3.17, zevende lid, van de Wet op het financieel toezicht gestelde verplichtingen aan de overtreder een last opleggen om waar passend, op een nader bepaalde manier en binnen een nader bepaalde termijn, verwerkingen in overeenstemming te brengen met het daar bepaalde.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related duties concerning regulated systems and services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A high-risk AI-system user must notify specified parties when it identifies a serious incident, while B requires public electronic communications providers to take measures to limit the consequences of security incidents for national security or public order. If the same actor and incident fall within both regimes, the measures required under B could affect how the AI incident is handled, but the texts do not prescribe incompatible actions or benchmarks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties: A is an incident-notification duty for a user of a high-risk AI system, whereas B is a preventive or organisational security-measures duty for providers of public electronic communications networks or services. An actor can take the required security measures and also notify the parties listed in A; nothing in either text says that compliance with one substitutes for or prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Aanbieders van openbare elektronische communicatienetwerken of openbare elektronische communicatiediensten nemen bij of krachtens algemene maatregel van bestuur vastgestelde technische, operationele en organisatorische maatregelen om de risico’s voor de beveiliging van hun netwerken of diensten te beheersen, teneinde de gevolgen van beveiligingsincidenten op de nationale veiligheid of openbare orde te beperken.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The provisions both use mandatory language, but they regulate different acts: provision A concerns a CSIRT’s requested discussion and possible execution of a coordinated incident response, while provision B concerns making a notification about an intended acquisition of controlling influence in a telecommunications party. No fact pattern makes the same actor legally unable to perform both duties.

A is triggered only “op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk” and concerns an incident response; B requires a specified acquisition notification, generally eight weeks before implementation or, for a listed telecommunications party, simultaneously with a public-offer announcement. They can readily be performed cumulatively without either rule excusing or contradicting the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Cyber-incident information exchange and foreign-investment screening deadlines
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A obliges the CSIRT network to exchange relevant information about incidents, near-incidents, cyber threats, risks and vulnerabilities. Provision B permits the Minister to extend a foreign-investment screening decision period by up to three months after a qualifying notification, but it does not prohibit information exchange or impose a conflicting deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors, mechanisms and subject matters: A concerns operational cooperation among national CSIRTs, while B concerns the Minister’s procedural deadline in foreign-investment screening. Nothing in B restricts CSIRT information exchange, and nothing in A governs the Minister’s screening period.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen zien op informatie over incidenten, bijna-incidenten en cyberdreigingen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat artikel 15 een algemene uitwisselingstaak binnen het CSIRT-netwerk oplegt, terwijl artikel 40 een specifieke verstrekking aan een bevoegde autoriteit voorschrijft, zodat onduidelijkheid kan ontstaan over de juiste ontvanger of reikwijdte.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen cumulatieve, goed verenigbare taken op: artikel 15 betreft informatie-uitwisseling binnen het CSIRT-netwerk, terwijl artikel 40 een afzonderlijke verstrekking door het CSIRT aan de bevoegde autoriteit vereist voor gemelde gebeurtenissen van een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is. Niets in artikel 40 verbiedt de uitwisseling uit artikel 15 of bepaalt dat die uitwisseling de specifieke verstrekking vervangt.

verdict.shared_subject: Retention of copies of AI-system documentation that may contain personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a processor, after the processing services end, to delete existing copies of personal data unless Union or Member State law requires storage. Provision B requires an importer to retain certain AI documentation for ten years, so if the importer is also a processor and the documents contain personal data, the retention duty could appear to require keeping copies that A otherwise requires deleted.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different roles and concern different objects: A concerns a processor’s copies of personal data after processing services end, while B concerns an importer’s copies of specified AI documentation. B does not expressly require retaining personal data, and A itself permits retention where Union or Member State law requires it; the texts therefore do not establish that the same copy must both be deleted and retained.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed for compatibility on the texts shown: the provisions do not establish that the documentation copy required by B is a copy of personal data subject to A’s deletion duty, nor that the same actor is subject to both duties in the relevant capacities.
