verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and associated personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to the same organisation and high-risk AI deployment, but they impose different obligations: Article 36 requires prior consultation only where a DPIA identifies a high risk that would remain without mitigation, while Article 16(a) requires the provider to ensure compliance with the AI Act’s Section 2 requirements. The strongest possible tension argument is that an operator might regard AI Act compliance as sufficient risk control and therefore not consult under Article 36, although the texts do not say that AI Act compliance substitutes for GDPR consultation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different triggers, addressees and subject matter, and can readily be performed cumulatively. A provider that is also the GDPR controller can ensure AI-system compliance under Article 16(a) and, independently, consult the supervisory authority before processing whenever the Article 36 condition is met; neither provision exempts the actor from the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer uit een gegevensbeschermingseffectbeoordeling krachtens artikel 35 blijkt dat de verwerking een hoog risico zou opleveren indien de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke geen maatregelen neemt om het risico te beperken, raadpleegt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke voorafgaand aan de verwerking de toezichthoudende autoriteit.
verdict.evidence_span_b: zorgen ervoor dat hun AI-systemen met een hoog risico in overeenstemming zijn met de eisen van afdeling 2;

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents that may simultaneously constitute a personal-data breach and a significant incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying event can trigger two mandatory reports by the same entity: GDPR Article 33 requires reporting to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours where the breach is likely to risk individuals’ rights and freedoms, while NIS2 Article 23 requires reporting a significant incident immediately to the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority. The recipients and reporting regimes are not established as identical, and the stricter NIS2 timing does not itself discharge the separate GDPR filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can apply cumulatively without contradiction: an entity can report the same event to both bodies, and reporting immediately under Article 23 does not prevent reporting under Article 33 within 72 hours. In some national arrangements the competent authorities or reporting channels might overlap, but the texts shown do not establish that overlap or that one report legally substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A cloud-service provider that is an essential or important entity suffers a security incident causing loss of personal data and a serious operational disruption to its services. The event is both a personal-data breach likely to risk individuals’ rights and freedoms and a significant incident under Article 23(3). The provider must report it without undue delay to its CSIRT or applicable competent authority under Article 23 and separately, no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of it, to the Article 55 competent supervisory authority under Article 33; filing with the first recipient does not, on the text shown, discharge the second duty.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the CSIRT or NIS2 competent authority is legally the same body as the GDPR Article 55 supervisory authority, and whether national implementation provides a single filing channel that legally satisfies both duties, is not established by the provisions shown. The texts also contain different triggering conditions, so not every incident triggers both reports.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident or personal-data breach reporting by an entity/provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires an incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 72 hours, while B requires notifying the affected data subject without delay. For a significant incident that is also a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy, the same actor must make two distinct communications to different recipients; satisfying one does not notify the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed without contradiction: the actor can report to the CSIRT or competent authority under A and separately notify the affected person under B. Neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other communication.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A provider becomes aware of a significant cyber incident that compromises personal data and is likely to have adverse effects on the privacy of identified individuals. It must submit the incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 72 hours under A and, separately, notify each affected data subject without delay under B; notifying the data subjects does not discharge the report to the authority, and reporting to the authority does not discharge the individual notifications.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: Government handling of a notified proposed acquisition and CSIRT incident-response duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives the Minister competence to decide whether to impose a prohibition after a notification concerning proposed control of a telecommunications party. Provision B requires the CSIRT, where applicable, to respond to incidents and provide assistance; both may arise in a telecommunications context, but they regulate different actors, subject matters, and triggers.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The Minister's decision-making deadline and competence under Provision A do not require or prohibit any CSIRT incident response. Conversely, the CSIRT's incident-response task does not constrain the Minister's eight-week decision period or six-month extension. Each provision can therefore be complied with independently.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onze Minister beslist binnen acht weken na ontvangst van de melding of een verbod op grond van artikel 14a.4, eerste lid, wordt opgelegd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: indien van toepassing, het reageren op incidenten en verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit;

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system to process personal data under GDPR Article 6(1)(e) or (f)
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives the data subject an objection right that can require the controller to stop processing, while Article 14 requires appropriate and proportionate human oversight, including awareness of automation bias. In a case where the controller must continue operating the AI system to provide the relevant service but must also stop the objected-to processing, the provisions could appear to pull in different directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative and independently satisfiable duties, not incompatible commands. The controller can provide human oversight and ensure that responsible persons remain alert to automation bias while also honoring an objection by stopping the relevant processing, unless overriding legitimate grounds apply under Article 21.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke staakt de verwerking van de persoonsgegevens tenzij hij dwingende gerechtvaardigde gronden voor de verwerking aanvoert die zwaarder wegen dan de belangen, rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkene of die verband houden met de instelling, uitoefening of onderbouwing van een rechtsvordering.
verdict.evidence_span_b: zich bewust te blijven van de mogelijke neiging om automatisch of te veel te vertrouwen op de output van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system to process personal data under GDPR Article 6(1)(e) or (f)
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives the data subject a right to object and requires the controller to stop processing unless overriding legitimate grounds or legal-claim grounds apply. Article 14(d)-(e) requires the high-risk AI system to be supplied so that human overseers can decide not to use or override its output and can intervene or stop it; in a case where stopping the system would be necessary to honor an objection, the AI Act duty could appear to require continued operational availability while GDPR requires cessation of the relevant processing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: Article 21 governs the controller's response to an individual objection, while Article 14 requires the system's design to enable human intervention or shutdown where appropriate and proportionate. The operator can provide those capabilities and then stop or refrain from using the system for the objector's data, unless an Article 21 exception applies; Article 14 does not require processing to continue.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke staakt de verwerking van de persoonsgegevens tenzij hij dwingende gerechtvaardigde gronden voor de verwerking aanvoert die zwaarder wegen dan de belangen, rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkene of die verband houden met de instelling, uitoefening of onderbouwing van een rechtsvordering.
verdict.evidence_span_b: in alle specifieke situaties te kunnen besluiten om het AI-systeem met een hoog risico niet te gebruiken of de output van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico op andere wijze te negeren, door een andere beslissing te vervangen of terug te draaien

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant cyber/ICT incidents or threats by entities potentially covered by both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns a voluntary report of a significant cyber threat, while Provision B requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident. If the same event is both a voluntarily reportable cyber threat under A and a significant incident under B, the regimes could involve different reporting channels and obligations, potentially requiring separate action.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A does not impose a mandatory reporting duty for the relevant cyber threat: it expressly says financial entities may report on a voluntary basis. Provision B imposes a mandatory duty only for a significant incident and does not specify a recipient or deadline in the text shown. An entity can therefore comply with B without making the optional report under A; choosing not to invoke A avoids any conflict, and the texts do not establish two mandatory filings for the same event.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions shown do not establish whether a particular cyber threat is also a 'significant incident' under B, nor do they specify B's recipient or deadline. Those details would be needed to assess any cumulative reporting burden, but the voluntary character of A is already sufficient to reject a direct or dual-reporting conflict.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision A is voluntary ('op vrijwillige basis'). A financial entity can comply with the mandatory duty in B while declining to make the optional report under A; the actor is not forced to trigger the potentially overlapping mechanism.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.

verdict.shared_subject: De bevoegdheid van bevoegde autoriteiten om administratieve geldboeten op te leggen aan entiteiten onder Richtlijn (EU) 2022/2555.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen regelen dezelfde soort handhavingsbevoegdheid en gebruiken vrijwel dezelfde formulering, maar voor verschillende categorieën entiteiten. Als een entiteit of activiteit op grond van de richtlijn niet duidelijk als essentieel of belangrijk is ingedeeld, kan worden betwijfeld welke bepaling de bevoegdheidsgrondslag vormt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen verlenen parallelle bevoegdheden voor verschillende adressatencategorieën: artikel 32 ziet op essentiële entiteiten en artikel 33 op belangrijke entiteiten. Voor een entiteit die correct onder één categorie valt, kan de bevoegde autoriteit de relevante bevoegdheid uitoefenen; de bepalingen verbieden elkaar niet en leggen geen onverenigbare verplichtingen op.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op grond van artikel 34 een administratieve geldboete op te leggen
verdict.evidence_span_b: op grond van artikel 34 een administratieve geldboete op te leggen

verdict.shared_subject: Melding van incidenten waarbij persoonsgegevens mogelijk zijn geschonden
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij één ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident kan een financiële entiteit onder A aan een bevoegde autoriteit moeten rapporteren en onder B dezelfde inbreuk onverwijld aan de betrokken persoon moeten melden. Dat zijn afzonderlijke kennisgevingen aan verschillende ontvangers; de ene melding vervangt de andere niet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen zijn inhoudelijk en procedureel naast elkaar uitvoerbaar: A ziet op rapportage door financiële entiteiten aan een bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B ziet op kennisgeving door een aanbieder aan de betrokkene. Bovendien is niet uit de getoonde teksten zeker dat iedere financiële entiteit ook een ‘aanbieder’ in de zin van B is, of dat ieder ernstig ICT-incident een persoonsgegevensinbreuk met waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen vormt.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een financiële entiteit die tevens aanbieder is, krijgt een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident waarbij persoonsgegevens van een klant zijn gelekt en waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer ontstaan. Zij moet dan onder A een eerste kennisgeving indienen ‘bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit’ binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20 vast te stellen termijnen, en onder B de betrokken klant ‘onverwijld’ informeren; indien de termijnen samenvallen of overlappen, blijven dit twee afzonderlijke meldingen aan verschillende ontvangers.
verdict.decisive_exception: De kwalificatie veronderstelt dat de financiële entiteit tevens ‘de aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid’ is en dat het incident onder B als een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens valt. De getoonde bepalingen stellen die personele en materiële overlap niet volledig vast, maar bij die overlap zijn de meldingen cumulatief.
verdict.evidence_span_a: bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents and enforcement-related monitoring
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities to consider the duration of an infringement when taking enforcement measures. Provision B requires the CSIRT to monitor and analyse cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents nationally; monitoring incidents could generate information relevant to determining infringement duration, potentially creating an overlap in institutional activity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different functions: A governs how competent authorities assess enforcement measures, while B defines the CSIRT's operational monitoring and analysis tasks. Nothing in either text makes CSIRT monitoring substitute for, constrain, or conflict with the authority's duty to consider infringement duration.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) de duur van de inbreuk;
verdict.evidence_span_b: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory powers and the ACM’s number register
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers competent authorities to order cessation of conduct that infringes Regulation 2022/2554, while Provision B requires the ACM to maintain a register containing identifying and allocation data. One might argue that an order to cease conduct could affect the register’s operation or data, creating a possible conflict if the ACM were both enforcing A and maintaining the register.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of rules on different subjects and concern different conduct. Provision A grants competent authorities an enforcement power concerning infringements of Regulation 2022/2554; Provision B requires the ACM to maintain a number register with specified information. Nothing in A orders the ACM to stop maintaining that register, and nothing in B prevents an authority from ordering cessation of an infringement.
verdict.evidence_span_a: natuurlijke of rechtspersoon bij officieel besluit gelasten de gedraging die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening, te staken en deze gedraging niet te herhalen
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt door de Autoriteit Consument en Markt een nummerregister bijgehouden dat een overzicht bevat van toekenningen

verdict.shared_subject: Bevoegde autoriteiten en hun beoordeling/beperking van risico’s bij toezicht en handhaving
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen sturen het optreden van bevoegde autoriteiten, maar zij doen dat op verschillende manieren: A verlangt dat bij handhaving rekening wordt gehouden met de duur van de inbreuk, terwijl B verlangt dat significante gezondheids-, veiligheids- en grondrechtenrisico’s adequaat worden beperkt. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat een langdurige inbreuk of een beperking die innovatie belemmert tot verschillende prioriteiten leidt, maar geen tekst verplicht de autoriteit tot onverenigbare uitkomsten.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De normen zijn cumulatief en zien op verschillende aspecten van overheidshandelen. A is een beoordelingsfactor bij handhavingsmaatregelen tegen essentiële entiteiten; B betreft risicobeperking tijdens AI-testomgevingen en laat toezichts- en corrigerende bevoegdheden uitdrukkelijk onverlet. Een autoriteit kan beide naleven door zowel de duur van de inbreuk mee te wegen als significante risico’s adequaat te beperken.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de duur van de inbreuk
verdict.evidence_span_b: Significante risico’s voor de gezondheid en veiligheid en de grondrechten die tijdens het ontwikkelen en testen van dergelijke AI-systemen worden vastgesteld, worden op adequate wijze beperkt.

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingen aan bevoegde autoriteiten over verschillende events
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns a voluntary cyber-threat notification by a financial entity, with onward transmission by the competent authority to other authorities or, where applicable, by the entity to CSIRTs. Provision B concerns advance notification of cable-maintenance works on public land, with an authorised municipal official informing the mayor; the recipients, triggers, and subject matter are different, so no single event creates two cumulative filings.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with because they regulate distinct activities and actors: voluntary reporting of significant cyber threats by financial entities versus advance notification of cable works by a provider. Even where an entity might fall within both categories, a cyber-threat notification does not replace a municipal works notification, and neither provision forbids the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT-related incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to report each significant incident immediately to its CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B requires a financial entity to establish and implement a process to report ICT-related incidents, but the shown text does not identify a separate recipient, deadline, or filing distinct from the reporting required by A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be satisfied cumulatively: a financial entity can include the immediate reporting of significant incidents to the CSIRT or competent authority within its ICT-incident-management process. Nothing in B requires a different recipient, clock, or filing, so the texts do not establish two separate reports or an incompatibility.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity oversight and incident-related assessment
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities to take relevant prior infringements by the entity into account when imposing enforcement measures. Provision B requires the CSIRT to conduct dynamic risk and incident analysis, which could produce information about an entity’s past incidents or deficiencies; one might therefore argue that the CSIRT’s operational analysis and the authority’s enforcement assessment overlap.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different functions: A governs how competent authorities assess enforcement measures, while B assigns the CSIRT a cybersecurity analysis task. Nothing in B requires the CSIRT to disregard prior infringements, and nothing in A restricts dynamic risk or incident analysis; both duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: elke relevante eerdere inbreuk door de betrokken entiteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: het zorgen voor dynamische risico- en incidentenanalyse en situationeel bewustzijn met betrekking tot cyberbeveiliging

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system involving personal-data processing and human oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives the data subject a right to object to certain processing and requires the controller to stop unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Article 14 separately requires proportionate human-oversight measures for high-risk AI, so an oversight measure could involve continuing or reviewing processing that the data subject has opposed; however, Article 14 does not expressly require processing to continue or override the objection right.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: Article 21 governs whether particular personal-data processing must cease after an objection, subject to its exception, while Article 14 requires proportionate human-oversight measures for a high-risk AI system. The operator can design and apply oversight measures consistently with Article 21, including by stopping the relevant processing where no overriding grounds exist.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke staakt de verwerking van de persoonsgegevens tenzij hij dwingende gerechtvaardigde gronden voor de verwerking aanvoert die zwaarder wegen dan de belangen, rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkene of die verband houden met de instelling, uitoefening of onderbouwing van een rechtsvordering.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system to process personal data concerning an individual
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives the data subject an objection right that requires the controller to stop processing unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Article 14 requires the deployer to ensure that human overseers can intervene in or stop the high-risk AI system where appropriate and proportionate; in a case where the system's processing must stop under Article 21, continued operation could appear to conflict with that intervention duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties: Article 21 governs the controller's response to an individual's objection, while Article 14 requires the deployer to provide human-supervision capabilities. Article 14 does not require continued processing or prohibit stopping the system; its intervention capability can be used to comply with Article 21, subject to the separate conditions and allocation of responsibilities.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke staakt de verwerking van de persoonsgegevens tenzij hij dwingende gerechtvaardigde gronden voor de verwerking aanvoert die zwaarder wegen dan de belangen, rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkene of die verband houden met de instelling, uitoefening of onderbouwing van een rechtsvordering.
verdict.evidence_span_b: in te grijpen in de werking van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico of het systeem te onderbreken door middel van een stopknop of een vergelijkbare procedure waarmee het systeem op veilige wijze kan worden stopgezet.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident involving a public electronic communications service provider that is also an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same security incident could both adversely affect personal-data protection and still be ongoing when the final report under Provision B is due. Provision A then requires immediate notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, while Provision B requires a progress report at that time; if Provision B's report is a separate filing, the actor faces two reporting duties concerning one incident, potentially to different recipients and on different procedural requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: the actor can notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately under A and submit the progress report under B when the final report would otherwise be due. Provision B does not state that its progress report replaces, discharges, or prohibits the notification required by A; nor does the text shown identify B's recipient, so it does not establish a genuine dual-recipient reporting conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity providing a public electronic communications service suffers an ongoing security incident that adversely affects the protection of personal data. It must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens immediately under A and, when the final report would otherwise be due while the incident continues, submit the progress report required by B. Whether these are separate filings cannot be determined from the text shown because B's recipient and relationship to the notification under A are unspecified.
verdict.missing_reference: Provision B's reporting provisions identifying the recipient, content and procedural relationship of the progress report, and any rule stating whether that report also constitutes or replaces the notification required by Provision A.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive missing link is whether Provision B's progress report is a separate report to another authority or is submitted to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens / otherwise legally discharges A's immediate notification duty.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in

verdict.shared_subject: Significante incidenten affecting an essential or important entity’s services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same significant incident, but they require communications to different recipients: A requires an incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 72 hours, while B requires prompt information to the entity’s service recipients. The duties are therefore cumulative rather than one filing satisfying the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations address different audiences and purposes, so the entity can comply with both by reporting to the CSIRT or competent authority and separately informing affected service recipients. There is no incompatible command, and the different deadlines do not prevent simultaneous compliance.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An important entity suffers a significant incident that adversely affects the provision of its online service. It must submit the incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority within 72 hours under A and, for the same incident, inform its service recipients without delay under B; notifying one recipient group does not notify the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: onverwijld en in elk geval binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis hebben gekregen van het significante incident, een incidentmelding indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT-related incidents by a financial entity that is also a high-risk AI-system user
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same serious incident could trigger both regimes for the same financial entity, with DORA requiring a report to the relevant competent authority and the AI Act requiring immediate notification first to the provider and then to the importer or distributor and market-surveillance authorities. These are cumulative reporting duties to different recipients, and the provisions shown do not establish that one notification discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can report the incident to the DORA competent authority and separately notify the AI provider, importer or distributor, and market-surveillance authorities. The provisions do not require mutually incompatible content or prohibit making the additional notifications.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank subject to DORA uses a high-risk AI system, and the system suffers an incident that qualifies both as a serious ICT-related incident and as a serious incident under the AI Act. The bank must report the ICT incident to the relevant competent authority under DORA, while also immediately notifying the AI provider first and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities under the AI Act; the two regimes therefore require separate reports to different recipients, with no shown rule making one filing sufficient for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Information duties concerning different events and recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information duties, so a notified conformity-assessment body could conceivably also be an essential or important entity and face overlapping communication obligations. However, the duties concern different triggers and recipients: provision A concerns circumstances affecting notification, while provision B concerns informing service recipients about measures responding to a significant cyberthreat.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations can readily be performed cumulatively without contradiction. Provision A requires informing the notifying authority about circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of notification; provision B requires informing potentially affected service recipients about measures and, if necessary, the threat itself. Neither duty forbids or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding
verdict.evidence_span_b: deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging

verdict.shared_subject: Transparency about automated decision-making and human oversight of high-risk AI
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the controller to inform the data subject about automated decision-making, including useful information about the underlying logic, significance, and expected consequences. Provision B requires the high-risk AI system to be supplied so that responsible natural persons can understand its capabilities and limitations and monitor and address irregularities, failures, and unexpected performance; these are different transparency and oversight duties, but neither text makes compliance with one substitute for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties on different immediate recipients and for different purposes: A is an individual information duty owed to the data subject, while B is a system-design and human-oversight duty enabling responsible persons to monitor and intervene. A controller can provide the required individual information and separately ensure that the system enables the oversight described in B; no incompatible command, prohibition, deadline, or benchmark is stated.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory oversight and mitigation of risks in regulated digital activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the competent authority to acknowledge receipt of specified notifications, while provision B requires risks identified during AI testing to be adequately mitigated. If the same authority must promptly acknowledge a notification while mitigation is still unresolved, one might argue that the receipt-confirmation duty and the risk-mitigation duty create competing regulatory priorities. This is weak, however, because neither provision makes acknowledgement conditional on, or a substitute for, mitigation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties on different subjects and concerning different actions. A competent authority can confirm receipt of a financial entity’s notification under A, while national competent authorities or test-environment participants ensure adequate mitigation of identified AI risks under B; nothing in either text prohibits the other duty or treats one as satisfying the other.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT-taken inzake cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen een CSIRT een monitoring- en analysetaak op. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat de Nederlandse bepaling, door haar eigen formulering en definities, een mogelijk andere reikwijdte of benchmark voor die taak hanteert dan artikel 11 van de NIS2-richtlijn.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen schrijven in wezen dezelfde taak voor: monitoring en analyse op nationaal niveau van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten. Verschillen in redactie en de nadere Nederlandse definities maken de verplichtingen niet onverenigbaar; een CSIRT kan beide cumulatief naleven door de ruimste toepasselijke reikwijdte te hanteren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau
verdict.evidence_span_b: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau

verdict.shared_subject: Incident or security breach affecting an electronic communications service and potentially constituting a significant incident for an essential or important entity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying security breach must be reported immediately to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens, while a qualifying significant incident must be reported immediately to the entity’s service recipients. These are different recipients, so one notification does not discharge the other; the same event may therefore require two separate notifications.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed without contradiction: the provider can notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens and, where the incident is significant and the entity is essential or important, also notify its service recipients. Both deadlines are 'onverwijld', so there is no incompatible timing requirement.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity providing a public electronic communications service suffers a security breach that adversely affects the protection of personal data and also significantly impairs the provision of its services. It must notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens 'onverwijld' under provision A and separately notify the recipients of its services 'onverwijld' under provision B; notifying one recipient does not notify the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten

verdict.shared_subject: Nationale cyberincidenten en cybercrisisrespons
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen raken aan de nationale aanpak van cyberincidenten: de CSIRT’s moeten vroegtijdige waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen verstrekken, terwijl de minister een nationaal plan voor grootschalige incidenten en crisisrespons moet vaststellen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat een waarschuwingstaak en een nationaal crisisplan elkaar raken bij hetzelfde grootschalige incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen echter verschillende soorten normen op aan verschillende actoren. Artikel 11 verplicht CSIRT’s tot het verstrekken van waarschuwingen en meldingen; artikel 20 verleent de minister de bevoegdheid om een nationaal plan vast te stellen. Niets in de teksten verbiedt waarschuwingen, stelt een onverenigbare termijn vast of bepaalt dat het plan de CSIRT-taak vervangt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) het verstrekken van vroegtijdige waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen en het verspreiden van informatie onder betrokken essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten en aan de bevoegde autoriteiten en andere relevante belanghebbenden over cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten, in bijna-realtime indien mogelijk;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister stelt een nationaal plan voor grootschalige cyberbeveiligingsincidenten en crisisrespons als bedoeld in artikel 9, vierde lid, van de NIS2-richtlijn vast.

verdict.shared_subject: Telecommunications/cybersecurity-related activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory language and concern actions involving telecommunications-related matters. One requires the CSIRT network to exchange information about incidents, near-incidents, threats, risks and vulnerabilities, while the other requires a notification to be made by a specified deadline; in a very broad thematic sense, both impose administrative obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different subjects for different triggers and purposes. Provision A concerns information exchange by the CSIRT network, whereas Provision B concerns a notification by a person intending to acquire controlling influence in a telecommunications party; nothing in either text makes compliance with one duty prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) het uitwisselen van relevante informatie over incidenten, bijna-incidenten, cyberdreigingen, risico’s en kwetsbaarheden;
verdict.evidence_span_b: De melding in het eerste lid wordt gedaan uiterlijk acht weken voor de beoogde datum van uitvoering van dit voornemen.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT assistance with real-time or near-real-time monitoring for essential and important entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose the same assistance duty on a CSIRT, but Provision A refers to monitoring the entity’s plural “network and information systems,” while Provision B refers to its singular “network and information system.” If those formulations were legally intended to cover different scopes, a CSIRT might face uncertainty about whether assistance must cover multiple systems or only one system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are substantively parallel implementations of the same CSIRT task, with no incompatible command, prohibition, deadline, recipient, or benchmark. The singular/plural wording is not enough to establish a real conflict, particularly because Provision B’s definition expressly covers a network, a device or group of devices, and the digital data processed through them; the duties can therefore be performed cumulatively without contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek, het verlenen van bijstand aan betrokken essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten met betrekking tot het realtime of bijna-realtime monitoren van hun netwerk en informatiesystemen
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit met betrekking tot het realtime of bijna-realtime monitoren van haar netwerk- en informatiesysteem

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations involving regulatory authorities and documentation. One requires central securities depositories to provide ICT-continuity-test results, while the other requires an authorised representative of a general-purpose AI-model provider to provide a copy of its mandate to the AI Office on request; however, they concern different actors, documents, and regulatory regimes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations are independently satisfiable and do not regulate the same actor, event, document, or deadline. Provision A concerns central securities depositories and ICT-continuity-test results; provision B concerns authorised representatives of general-purpose AI-model providers and a mandate copy requested by the AI Office.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT verstrekking van waarschuwingen, meldingen en informatie over cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen het CSIRT een informatieverstrekkende taak op. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat art. 40 een specifieke, beperkte doorgifte betreft na een melding door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is, terwijl art. 11, onder b, een bredere en bijna-realtime verspreiding voorschrijft, zodat onduidelijkheid kan ontstaan over de vereiste ontvangers, timing en reikwijdte.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn cumulatief en vullen elkaar aan: art. 11, onder b, noemt algemene waarschuwingen, meldingen en informatieverstrekking aan entiteiten en autoriteiten, terwijl art. 40 een concrete doorgifte aan de bevoegde autoriteit uit de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten voorschrijft. Niets in de teksten verbiedt de bredere informatieverstrekking of bepaalt dat naleving van de ene taak de andere vervangt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) het verstrekken van vroegtijdige waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen en het verspreiden van informatie onder betrokken essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten en aan de bevoegde autoriteiten en andere relevante belanghebbenden over cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten, in bijna-realtime indien mogelijk;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een incident, bijna-incident of cyberdreiging dat overeenkomstig artikel 33, eerste lid, onderdeel a, is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.

verdict.shared_subject: Submission of regulatory drafts to EU-level and national authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose submission duties, so one might initially see overlapping obligations concerning regulatory or decision drafts. However, they concern different actors, different documents, and different regulatory procedures, with no incompatible timing, recipient, or content requirement shown.

Provision B requires a notifying authority to inform the Commission and other Member States of relevant changes to a notified body's notification. They address different actors, duties, and subject matter, with no incompatible command.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can plainly coexist: an enforcement authority may consider relevant previous infringements, while a notifying authority separately reports relevant changes through the specified electronic system. Neither provision restricts or alters the other's action, deadline, recipient, or legal assessment.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents by a financial entity that experiences both a personal-data breach and a serious ICT-related incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying event may trigger two mandatory reporting regimes: Article 33 requires notification of a personal-data breach to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours, while Article 19 requires a financial entity to submit an initial notification and later reports concerning a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority on separately determined deadlines. The texts identify potentially different authorities and expressly require multiple Article 19 reports, so one filing may not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can notify the Article 55 supervisory authority under Article 33 and separately submit the Article 19 notifications and reports to the relevant competent authority. Nothing in either provision forbids the other filing or states that one report substitutes for the other; the apparent overlap is therefore an additional reporting burden rather than an inability to obey both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity suffers one cyberattack that both causes unauthorised access to personal data, creating a GDPR personal-data breach with a risk to individuals, and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. The entity must notify the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours and also submit the Article 19 initial notification, subsequent interim updates and final report to the relevant competent authority under the Article 20 deadlines; filing the first report with one authority does not itself make the separate filing to the other authority.
verdict.decisive_exception: The texts do not establish that the two authorities are always the same or that an Article 19 filing is legally sufficient to satisfy Article 33. Article 33 also contains a risk-based exception ('tenzij het niet waarschijnlijk is ...'), but the concrete scenario assumes that exception does not apply.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity oversight and crisis response
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern cybersecurity governance, but provision A requires competent authorities to assess risks and non-compliance concerning a critical ICT third-party provider, while provision B assigns the Minister responsibility for establishing a national plan for large-scale cyber incidents and crisis response. One might argue that the national plan could prescribe a different institutional approach to risks addressed by the authorities under A, but no such inconsistency is stated.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable functions: A governs how competent authorities take specified risks and non-compliance into account when making a decision, whereas B gives the Minister competence to establish a national plan. A national crisis-response plan can coexist with the authorities’ case-specific assessment duty.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related reporting by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns a voluntary onward transmission by a relevant national competent authority to the ECB, while Provision B requires the entity itself to submit a final report to both its CSIRT and competent authority. If the same incident triggers both mechanisms, the reports have different senders, recipients, contents and timing, so one filing would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: the entity may submit the required final report under Provision B, while the competent authority separately forwards a voluntary cyber-threat notification under Provision A. Provision A is expressly voluntary, however, so an entity can avoid any overlap by not making or triggering that optional notification.
verdict.decisive_exception: Provision A is voluntary: the financial entity controls whether it makes the significant-cyber-threat notification, and the text does not require it to invoke that mechanism. The extracted A recipient/deadline (ECB, immediately) also concerns the authority's onward transmission, not an additional mandatory filing by the entity under the shown norm.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT/security incidents by entities potentially covered by both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires financial entities to report ICT-related incidents as part of their incident-management process, while B separately requires a provider of a public electronic communications service to notify the Dutch data-protection authority immediately of certain security breaches. If the same actor and incident fall within both scopes, A could entail a report under the DORA process while B requires a distinct immediate notification to a named authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not specify a recipient, deadline, format, or separate filing; it may simply require the actor to include reporting in its incident-management process. Provision B supplies a concrete notification duty, and nothing in the shown text says that A requires a second filing to a different recipient or on a different clock.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions governing the content, recipient, deadline, and procedure for the reporting duty in 32022R2554 art. 17 (including any applicable provisions of that Regulation specifying to whom and when ICT-related incidents must be reported).
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether A and B require genuinely separate notifications cannot be determined from the shown text: A states only that incidents must be reported, whereas B identifies the recipient and deadline.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems and related regulatory oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern a high-risk AI system, but Article 36 GDPR requires the controller to consult a supervisory authority before processing where a DPIA identifies an unmitigated high risk, while Article 31 AI Act regulates the independence and permitted use of notified bodies. One might argue that the notified body's use of the assessed system for conformity-assessment activities could involve processing that triggers prior consultation, creating an additional regulatory step.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors and address different matters: Article 36 governs a controller's prior consultation concerning high-risk personal-data processing, whereas Article 31 governs the independence of notified bodies and permits their use of assessed high-risk AI systems for conformity-assessment or personal purposes. Nothing in Article 31 forbids or displaces GDPR consultation, and both duties can be complied with cumulatively where their respective triggers apply.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident notifications and their processing by public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident notifications and impose action on an authority or incident-response body. A possible tension is that A requires the market-surveillance authority to act within seven days after receiving a serious-incident notification, while B requires the CSIRT to process voluntary notifications under its own procedure and permits prioritisation of mandatory notifications, potentially creating different handling priorities for related incidents.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions bind different actors and regulate different functions: A requires the market-surveillance authority to take appropriate measures after receiving a serious-incident notification, whereas B governs how the CSIRT processes voluntary notifications. Nothing in either text requires one body to refrain from acting, makes the CSIRT's processing substitute for the market-surveillance authority's measures, or establishes that the same notification must be handled by both bodies under incompatible deadlines.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen, en volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verwerkt de vrijwillige meldingen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, overeenkomstig de in artikel 36 omschreven procedure. Het CSIRT kan daarbij voorrang geven aan de verwerking van verplichte meldingen als bedoeld in artikel 25 boven vrijwillige meldingen als bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal-data breaches and significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a processor to inform the controller, while B requires a covered entity to submit an incident notification to the CSIRT or competent authority. If the same event qualifies under both regimes, these are separate communications to different recipients, with different content and potentially different timing; notifying one recipient does not notify the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with: the processor can promptly inform the controller under A and the relevant entity can separately report the significant incident under B. They impose cumulative duties rather than mutually incompatible commands, and A's 'without undue delay' requirement does not prevent the B filing within 72 hours.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A processor discovers that a cyberattack has caused unauthorised access to personal data and also seriously compromised a network service, making the event both a personal-data breach and a significant incident. It must inform the controller under A and, separately, the covered entity must submit the incident notification to the CSIRT or competent authority under B; the two communications have different recipients and both must be made.

verdict.shared_subject: Information and human oversight concerning high-risk AI and automated decision-making
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the controller to inform the data subject about automated decision-making and provide useful information about its underlying logic, significance, and expected consequences. Provision B requires the high-risk AI system to enable human overseers to understand and monitor the system and, where appropriate and proportionate, replace its output with another decision; these duties could create uncertainty about whether information to the data subject must also explain the human-overseer intervention mechanism or whether the AI Act's oversight arrangements suffice.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties on different aspects of governance: A is an information duty owed by a GDPR controller to the data subject, while B is a system-design and human-oversight duty concerning users of high-risk AI. Nothing in B removes or substitutes for A's individual information rights, and both duties can be satisfied independently.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incident reports by entities subject to both DORA art. 19 and BWBR0052872 art. 29
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require reporting after an incident, and A requires an interim report after the initial notification while B requires a progress report instead of a final report if the incident is still ongoing. If the same ongoing incident falls under both regimes, the texts could be read as requiring two differently characterised reports on potentially different schedules, with no express rule that one satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not clearly impose two separate filings to different recipients. A expressly requires submission to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit,” whereas B’s quoted paragraph does not specify a recipient and may regulate the content and timing of the report required under that regime. An entity could therefore submit a report satisfying both duties, provided it contains the required information and is filed within both applicable deadlines.

verdict.shared_subject: Rapportage van hetzelfde ernstige/significante ICT-incident door een financiële entiteit die ook een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit is
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij een overlappend incident kan dezelfde entiteit onder beide bepalingen rapporteren, maar aan verschillende primaire ontvangers: A aan het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit, en B aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit. A vereist bovendien onverwijlde melding, terwijl B een eerste kennisgeving en latere verslagen volgens andere termijnen en inhoudelijke fasen verlangt; één melding aan de ene ontvanger vervult daarom niet noodzakelijk de andere verplichting.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen kunnen in de praktijk naast elkaar worden nageleefd: de entiteit kan onverwijld aan de A-ontvanger melden en daarnaast de eerste kennisgeving en vervolgverslagen aan de B-autoriteit indienen. Bovendien kan de bevoegde autoriteit onder A de melding aan het CSIRT doorsturen, en laat B onder de aangehaalde context toe dat informatie aan NIS2-autoriteiten of CSIRT’s wordt verstrekt, zodat coördinatie mogelijk is.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een financiële entiteit die tevens een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit is, ondervindt één cyberincident dat zowel een ‘significant incident’ onder A als een ‘ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident’ onder B is. Zij moet het incident onverwijld melden ‘bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit’ en daarnaast bij ‘de relevante bevoegde autoriteit’ een eerste kennisgeving indienen binnen de op grond van artikel 20 vast te stellen termijn, gevolgd door de in B genoemde tussen- en eindverslagen. Een melding aan het CSIRT onder A is niet de melding aan de relevante financiële bevoegde autoriteit onder B; beide rapportageketens moeten dus worden bediend.
verdict.decisive_exception: Geen tekst in de getoonde bepalingen bepaalt dat één melding aan het CSIRT of een NIS2-bevoegde autoriteit automatisch geldt als de eerste kennisgeving en vervolgverslagen aan de relevante financiële bevoegde autoriteit. De mogelijke doorgeleiding door autoriteiten is geen vrijstelling van de eigen meldplicht van de entiteit.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in: a) een eerste kennisgeving;

verdict.shared_subject: Impact assessments for certain processing or high-risk AI use
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can require an impact assessment before or at the start of use, but they use different triggers and address different assessment objects: GDPR Article 35 concerns processing likely to create a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms, while Article 27 concerns specified users of high-risk AI systems. An operator might therefore need to determine whether one assessment can satisfy both, particularly because Article 27 permits reliance on earlier fundamental-rights assessments while Article 35 requires an assessment of intended processing activities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can be satisfied together: where both apply, the controller or deployer can conduct a GDPR data-protection impact assessment and an Article 27 fundamental-rights impact assessment, ensuring that each contains the information required by its own instrument. Neither provision says that one assessment substitutes for, overrides, or is deemed to satisfy the other; Article 27’s permission to reuse earlier assessments does not remove any applicable GDPR duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De verplichting als neergelegd in lid 1 is van toepassing op het eerste gebruik van een AI-systeem met een hoog risico.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious ICT-related incident that also constitutes a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident can trigger both duties: A requires notification to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours, while B requires the financial entity to notify affected clients without delay. These are different recipients and different communications, so notifying the authority does not notify the clients or discharge B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the entity can notify the supervisory authority under A and its clients under B. Neither provision forbids the other notification, and B's client notice may be unnecessary if the incident does not affect clients' financial interests.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity discovers a serious ICT-related incident involving unauthorised access to clients' personal data, and the incident has consequences for clients' financial interests. The entity must report the personal-data breach to the competent supervisory authority, if possible within 72 hours, and separately notify its clients without delay of the serious incident and mitigation measures; one filing cannot satisfy both duties because the recipients and required information differ.

verdict.shared_subject: Bevoegdheden om ICT- of cyberbeveiligingstekortkomingen door aanbieders of entiteiten te laten verhelpen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen voorzien in bevoegdheden om van een gereguleerde actor corrigerende maatregelen of verslaggeving te verlangen. In een grensoverschrijdende situatie kan een actor met verschillende toezichthouders en regimes worden geconfronteerd, maar de getoonde teksten maken niet duidelijk dat de ene bevoegdheid de andere uitsluit of dat naleving van de ene opdracht de andere vervangt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen richten zich op verschillende actoren en regimes: A betreft essentiële entiteiten onder NIS2, terwijl B de lead overseer bevoegd maakt ten aanzien van kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten onder DORA. Bovendien geeft B slechts een bevoegdheid om verslagen over genomen acties of corrigerende maatregelen te verzoeken, terwijl A een handhavingsbevoegdheid van nationale autoriteiten beschrijft; beide kunnen naast elkaar bestaan zonder tegenstrijdige verplichtingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system involving personal-data processing and affected natural persons
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same deployment and require information or assessment concerning affected natural persons and the system’s use. A possible concern is that GDPR transparency information is individual-facing, while the AI Act assessment is an organisational, system-use assessment, so the latter does not itself provide all information required to each data subject.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different objects and can readily be performed cumulatively: the controller gives each data subject the GDPR information at collection, while the deployer performs the fundamental-rights impact assessment before first use. Provision B expressly treats its assessment as complementary to a GDPR data-protection impact assessment, confirming that the regimes are intended to operate together rather than substitute for one another.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or notification duties of regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information-reporting duties, and a real-world organisation might conceivably fall within both regulatory regimes. If the same event or information also concerned the scope or conditions of an accreditation, the organisation could face two notification channels and potentially different reporting content.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors, subjects and recipients: Provision A requires financial entities to prepare serious ICT-incident notifications and reports for the relevant competent authority, while Provision B requires notified conformity-assessment bodies to inform the notifying authority about circumstances affecting their notification scope or conditions. Nothing in the shown text makes one duty prohibit, replace or alter the other, and the provisions do not establish that the same actor or event is involved.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident response and information-sharing involving CSIRTs and essential entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incidents involving essential entities and CSIRT-related action. One could argue that a CSIRT’s duty to respond and assist under provision A might overlap with provision B’s mandatory transfer of incident information between competent authorities, creating uncertainty about whether the CSIRT should act directly or route information through the authorities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different actions: provision A requires CSIRTs, where applicable, to respond to incidents and assist entities, while provision B requires a competent authority to provide information to another competent authority about a reported significant incident. Nothing in either text prohibits the other action, and responding to an incident can occur alongside inter-authority information sharing.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations involving administrative action and deadlines, so a single telecommunications operator could theoretically be involved in circumstances triggering both regimes. However, provision A concerns reporting a personal-data breach to a data-protection supervisory authority, while provision B concerns municipal approval of cable works; the required acts, triggers, and recipients are distinct.

Neither provision prohibits or delays compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk AI systems processing personal data and the information provided to data subjects
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the controller to inform the data subject about storage, rights, consent withdrawal, complaints, data provision, and automated decision-making. Provision B requires high-risk AI systems to be designed so that natural persons can effectively supervise them; one might argue that this system-level human-supervision duty does not itself ensure that each data subject receives the individual information required by A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties on different aspects of compliance: A concerns transparency information given to the data subject when personal data are collected, while B concerns the design of high-risk AI systems for effective human oversight during use. An operator can design effective human oversight and separately provide all information required by A; neither provision deems one duty to substitute for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT/AI incidents by a financial entity that is also a high-risk AI-system deployer
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same serious incident could trigger both provisions for the same financial entity: A requires preparation of an initial notification and reports for the competent authority, while B requires notification of the incident to the provider and then to the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities. These are distinct reporting channels, and neither provision says that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can prepare and submit A's reports to its relevant competent authority while separately notifying B's recipients. A also expressly contemplates additional reporting to other authorities, so the texts do not make simultaneous reporting legally impossible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity uses a high-risk AI system, and that system causes a serious incident. The entity must prepare and submit A's initial notification and reports to the relevant competent authority, while under B it must first notify the provider and then the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities. Filing the A report with the competent authority does not, on the text shown, notify B's separate recipients; therefore both reporting duties must be performed, with no rule shown resolving which authority or reporting sequence governs the overall incident response.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the cumulative reporting burden on the text shown; the key issue is that the recipients differ and no substitution rule is provided.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related notifications by entities subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same significant incident, but they require communications to different recipients: the competent authority under A and the entity’s service recipients under B. They also use different timing rules—Article 19 requires the interim report within the Article 20 deadlines, while Article 30 requires informing service recipients without delay—so one communication cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are individually satisfiable and concern different audiences, so an entity can prepare the interim regulatory report while promptly informing affected service recipients. Nothing in either text prohibits making both notifications or makes one notification legally exclusive.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity suffers a significant ICT-related incident that adversely affects its services. It must submit the interim report to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” within the applicable Article 20 deadline and, separately, inform “de ontvangers van haar diensten” immediately; notifying the authority does not notify the service recipients, and informing the recipients does not submit the regulatory report.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Supervisory or competent authorities addressing an entity’s regulatory infringement

verdict.shared_subject: Incident involving personal data and a trust service offered by an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident could both be a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect an individual's privacy and a significant incident affecting the provision of a trust service. In that case, the operator must make separate notifications: promptly to the affected person and promptly, or within 24 hours if that is impossible, to its CSIRT and competent authority; notifying one set of recipients does not discharge the other duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the operator can notify the affected person and separately report the incident to the CSIRT and competent authority. They concern different recipients and different reporting functions, so there is no requirement that makes compliance with one impossible or legally substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A trust-service provider that is an essential or important entity suffers a cyberattack exposing customers' personal data. The breach is likely to have adverse consequences for those customers' privacy and also has consequences for the provision of the trust service. The provider must notify each affected person without delay and separately report the significant incident without delay, or within 24 hours if immediate reporting is impossible, to both its CSIRT and competent authority; the three recipient groups and clocks are not merged by either provision.

verdict.shared_subject: Use of a high-risk AI system to process personal data under GDPR Article 6(1)(e) or (f)
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives the data subject a right to object and requires the controller to stop processing unless overriding legitimate grounds or legal-claim grounds exist. Article 14 requires the high-risk AI system to be supplied so that human overseers can decide, where appropriate and proportionate, not to use or to disregard its output; exercising that oversight could result in stopping or changing the processing, but Article 14 does not itself conflict with Article 21 or remove its exceptions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties on different aspects of the activity: Article 21 governs the controller’s response to an individual objection, while Article 14 requires human-oversight capabilities for a high-risk AI system. A controller can provide the required override and stop capabilities and separately stop processing after an objection, unless it establishes the Article 21 grounds for continuing.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident or measure reporting by a provider/operator in the financial-sector context
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same event is both a measure under Provision A and an ICT incident covered by Provision B, the actor may have to notify the affected subscriber under A and separately report to the designated sectoral CSIRT under B. These are different recipients and Provision A's 'zo snel mogelijk' timing does not discharge Provision B's separate reporting duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the actor can notify the involved subscriber and also make the required CSIRT report. Provision A concerns notice to the affected subscriber about a measure, whereas Provision B concerns an incident report to a designated CSIRT; neither text says that one notice substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank takes an urgent measure to address a threat to the integrity or security of its network after an ICT incident. Because prior notice to the subscriber was impossible due to urgency, it must notify that subscriber 'zo snel mogelijk' under A, while it must also make the Article 19 incident report to the designated CSIRT under B. Sending the subscriber notice does not report the incident to the CSIRT, and sending the CSIRT report does not notify the subscriber, so both filings are required.
