verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related responses by different authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern an incident notification and impose prompt action after receipt. If the same event and notification triggered both regimes, the market-surveillance authority would have to act within seven days while the CSIRT would have to respond immediately and, where possible, within 24 hours, creating parallel obligations and possible coordination issues.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different actions: the market-surveillance authority takes appropriate measures under Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, while the CSIRT sends a response and initial feedback to the reporting entity. Each can perform its own duty, and the texts do not require incompatible conduct or establish that the same actor must make both responses.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verstrekt onverwijld en zo mogelijk binnen 24 uur na ontvangst van de vroegtijdige waarschuwing, bedoeld in artikel 26, een antwoord aan de meldende entiteit

verdict.shared_subject: Incident involving personal data and network/information systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same incident, but they impose different communications: A requires prompt notice to the affected person, while B requires a final or progress report by the regulated entity. If B's report is a separate filing, the same incident could generate two obligations on different content and timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different recipients and functions: A is an individual privacy notification, whereas B is an incident report whose recipient is not specified in the excerpt. They can therefore be performed cumulatively, and nothing in either text says that the report under B substitutes for the notice under A.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity suffers an incident compromising personal data, with likely adverse effects on an affected person's privacy, and the incident continues past the deadline for the final report. The entity must notify the affected person immediately under A and submit a progress report instead of the final report, followed by a final report within one month after resolution, under B; notifying the person does not constitute submission of B's report, and B's recipient is not identified in the text shown.
verdict.missing_reference: The recipient and procedural requirements for the report under BWBR0052872 art. 29 are not stated in the excerpt. If another provision establishes that the report is sent to the same affected person and that the report itself satisfies the notice required by A, the classification could change; that substitution rule is not shown here.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the art. 29 progress/final report is a separate filing to an authority or other recipient, rather than a communication that can also satisfy A's individual notice duty, is not established by the text shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: dient een eindverslag in binnen één maand nadat het incident is afgehandeld

verdict.shared_subject: Toezicht en maatregelen rond netwerk-, informatie- en AI-systemen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen raken aan toezicht op digitale systemen en incidenten, maar artikel 11 verplicht CSIRT’s tot monitoring en analyse, terwijl artikel 79 een procedurele termijn regelt voor bezwaren tegen voorlopige markttoezichtmaatregelen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat een CSIRT-analyse en een markttoezichtprocedure verschillende beoordelingen van hetzelfde systeem kunnen opleveren, zonder dat de bepalingen aangeven hoe die zich tot elkaar verhouden.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen verplichtingen op aan verschillende actoren en regelen verschillende onderwerpen: artikel 11 betreft de operationele cyberbeveiligingstaken van CSIRT’s, terwijl artikel 79 lid 6 een termijn vaststelt waarbinnen markttoezichtautoriteiten of de Commissie bezwaar kunnen maken tegen een voorlopige maatregel. Niets in artikel 79 verbiedt monitoring of analyse door CSIRT’s, en niets in artikel 11 verhindert markttoezichtmaatregelen of bepaalt de bezwaarprocedure.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien er binnen drie maanden na ontvangst van de in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving door een markttoezichtautoriteit van een lidstaat of door de Commissie geen bezwaar tegen een voorlopige maatregel van een markttoezichtautoriteit van een andere lidstaat is ingediend, wordt die maatregel geacht gerechtvaardigd te zijn.

verdict.shared_subject: Information exchange and reporting by entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A authorises or requires ACM and AP to exchange necessary data with each other, while provision B requires covered entities to notify a central contact point of changes to specified registration data. If the same information is involved, one might argue that A creates an inter-authority information channel that could overlap with B’s reporting route.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and serve different functions: A concerns cooperation between ACM and AP, whereas B requires covered entities to notify the central contact point. Nothing in A relieves entities of B’s reporting duty, and nothing in B prohibits or regulates inter-authority data sharing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn bevoegd uit eigen beweging en desgevraagd verplicht aan elkaar de gegevens te verstrekken die noodzakelijk zijn voor de uitvoering van deze wet
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen het centrale contactpunt onverwijld of in elk geval binnen drie maanden na de datum waarop de wijziging van kracht is geworden, in kennis van wijzigingen van de gegevens

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity-related incidents or threats involving an AI-system provider or service entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can involve communications following a harmful event: A requires an incident notification, while B may require informing affected service recipients about a significant cyberthreat. If the same event qualifies under both, the actor might face an incident notification to the market-surveillance authority and a separate communication to recipients, with different content and no common deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different recipients and are independently satisfiable. A concerns the notification referenced in Article 73(1), while B concerns informing potentially affected service recipients about measures and, if necessary, the threat; neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging. Indien nodig stelt de entiteit die ontvangers ook in kennis van de desbetreffende significante cyberdreiging.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incidents involving personal data and significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose reporting-related obligations that could apply to the same incident. However, provision B only specifies information that must be supplied in an early warning and, in the text shown, does not identify a recipient, deadline, or an independent filing obligation; it may therefore be part of the same warning/report rather than a separate filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: where the same incident qualifies under both regimes, the entity can include B's required information—whether the incident was unlawful or malicious, possible cross-border effects, and the responsible officer's contact details—in the GDPR notification required by A, while sending it to A's supervisory authority within 72 hours. Nothing in B shown here requires a different recipient or clock, and the extracted fields identify no separate B recipient or deadline.
verdict.missing_reference: The provision referred to in B as the basis for the 'vroegtijdige waarschuwing' (the first paragraph of Article 26), including any rule identifying its recipient, deadline, or whether it must be a separate filing, would be needed to establish a dual-reporting tension.
verdict.decisive_exception: If the omitted first paragraph or another applicable provision requires the early warning to be filed separately with a different recipient or on a different clock, that could establish dual_reporting_tension; Article 26 alone does not show this.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt de entiteit de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents and oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, when imposing enforcement measures, to take account of the duration of an infringement. Provision B requires the CSIRT to ensure dynamic risk and incident analysis and cybersecurity situational awareness; one might argue that ongoing analysis could generate or prolong an enforcement-relevant incident record, creating pressure between operational monitoring and enforcement assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different functions: A governs how competent authorities assess enforcement measures, while B assigns analytical and situational-awareness tasks to the CSIRT. The CSIRT can perform its duty, and the authority can independently consider infringement duration; neither provision requires conduct that prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: b) de duur van de inbreuk;
verdict.evidence_span_b: het zorgen voor dynamische risico- en incidentenanalyse en situationeel bewustzijn met betrekking tot cyberbeveiliging

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and CSIRT processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the central contact point to forward received significant-incident reports to the central contact points of other affected Member States when requested by the CSIRT or competent authority. Provision B requires the CSIRT to process voluntary reports, while allowing it to prioritise mandatory reports; one might argue that forwarding or processing obligations could compete for CSIRT attention, especially where mandatory reports are prioritised.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable functions on different institutional actors and concern different categories of reports. A concerns forwarding reports between central contact points upon request, whereas B concerns the CSIRT's processing and prioritisation of voluntary reports; nothing in B forbids forwarding, and prioritisation is expressly permitted rather than a prohibition on other duties.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Op verzoek van het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit stuurt het centrale contactpunt de op grond van lid 1 ontvangen meldingen door naar de centrale contactpunten van de andere betrokken lidstaten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verwerkt de vrijwillige meldingen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, overeenkomstig de in artikel 36 omschreven procedure.

verdict.shared_subject: The content of an early warning concerning a significant incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an entity to submit a progress report only if the incident is still ongoing when the final report is submitted. Provision B requires information to be supplied in the early warning, but does not itself require a separate filing or impose a conflicting timing or recipient rule; therefore the strongest tension case is only that the provisions concern different reporting stages and could be mistakenly treated as overlapping filings.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties. A concerns submitting a progress report at the final-report stage, whereas B concerns supplying specified information in the early warning; an entity can perform both, and nothing in either text makes one filing substitute for or conflict with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: indien het incident nog aan de gang is op het moment dat het in punt d) bedoelde eindverslag wordt ingediend, zorgen de lidstaten ervoor dat de betrokken entiteiten op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt de entiteit de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative fines imposed on entities participating in an AI regulatory sandbox
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires administrative fines to be imposed in addition to specified NIS2 measures. Provision B, under its stated condition, prohibits authorities from imposing administrative fines for violations of other EU or national law while the relevant authorities were actively involved in supervision and issued compliance guidance. If the same entity and violation fall within both provisions, A appears to require a fine while B prohibits it.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns fines imposed on essential and important entities for measures under specified NIS2 provisions, whereas provision B concerns participants in an AI regulatory sandbox and fines for violations of the AI Act or other law under a specific supervisory-involvement condition. The texts do not establish that the same violation, entity, authority, and legal basis are covered, nor that B overrides the NIS2 fine obligation.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity participating in an AI regulatory sandbox commits a violation covered by the measures listed in NIS2 Article 34, while other competent authorities responsible for the relevant EU or national law actively supervised the AI system in the sandbox and provided compliance guidance. Article 34 requires an administrative fine to be imposed, while Article 57 states that no administrative fine is imposed with respect to that other law; the texts shown do not establish whether the sandbox protection also applies to the NIS2 fine obligation.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether Article 57's no-fine rule applies to administrative fines imposed under NIS2 Article 34, or whether the phrase 'met betrekking tot dat recht' limits the prohibition to fines under the other EU or national law for which the other authorities were responsible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Administratieve geldboeten worden opgelegd bovenop een of meer van de in artikel 32, lid 4, punten a) tot en met h), artikel 32, lid 5, en artikel 33, lid 4, punten a) tot en met g), bedoelde maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer andere bevoegde autoriteiten die verantwoordelijk zijn voor ander Unierecht en nationaal recht actief betrokken waren bij het toezicht op het AI-systeem in de testomgeving en richtsnoeren voor naleving hebben verstrekt, worden met betrekking tot dat recht geen administratieve geldboetes opgelegd.

verdict.shared_subject: Meldingsplichten bij ICT-/netwerkveiligheidsincidenten of bedreigingen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen bij één veiligheidsgebeurtenis een meldingsplicht opleggen, maar aan verschillende ontvangers: A vereist onverwijlde kennisgeving aan cliënten, terwijl B voorafgaande of zo spoedig mogelijke melding aan de betrokken abonnee vereist. Als een financiële entiteit tevens aanbieder is en dezelfde persoon zowel cliënt als abonnee is, lijkt één melding mogelijk beide belangen te kunnen dienen, maar de teksten bepalen niet dat een melding aan cliënten tevens de melding aan de betrokken abonnee is, noch dat de ontvangers juridisch samenvallen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn afzonderlijk uitvoerbaar: A ziet op een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident met gevolgen voor financiële belangen van cliënten en verlangt melding aan cliënten; B ziet op een maatregel ter bescherming van netwerk-, dienst- of randapparaatintegriteit en verlangt melding aan de betrokken abonnee. Een actor kan beide meldingen doen, en de teksten bevatten geen tegenstrijdige inhoud, termijn of verbod.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern regulatory consequences following non-compliance, but they regulate different duties, actors, and mechanisms: GDPR Article 34 concerns communicating a personal-data breach to the data subject, while DORA Article 35 concerns imposing a coercive fine on a critical ICT third-party provider. No text requires one action to be withheld because of the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively without contradiction. A provider or controller may make the required breach communication to the data subject while the lead overseer separately imposes a coercive fine for non-compliance with oversight measures after the stated period.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde mededeling aan de betrokkene bevat een omschrijving, in duidelijke en eenvoudige taal, van de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.evidence_span_b: neemt de lead overseer een besluit aan waarmee een dwangsom wordt opgelegd om de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten tot nakoming van die maatregelen te dwingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security/ICT incident by an entity that is both a financial entity and a provider of a public electronic communications service.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity must submit an initial notification to the relevant competent authority, while the communications-service provider must notify the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens without delay. If the same incident qualifies under both provisions, the texts identify different recipients and do not say that one notification substitutes for the other, suggesting two cumulative filings on potentially different clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed by sending the required notifications to each authority. Nothing in either text forbids parallel reporting or states that the DORA notification discharges the separate personal-data-breach notification; the duties therefore do not impose incompatible conduct.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company is both a financial entity and an aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst. One security incident is simultaneously a serious ICT-related incident and a security breach adversely affecting the protection of personal data. The company must submit an initial notification “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” within the Article 20 deadlines and separately notify “de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens” “onverwijld”; filing with one authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the other filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in: a) een eerste kennisgeving;
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens die zijn verwerkt in verband met de levering van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst in de Europese Unie.

verdict.shared_subject: Communicating a cyber or network-security threat or measure to an affected subscriber/service recipient
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to inform service recipients of the significant cyber threat itself, while Provision B requires a provider to notify the involved subscriber of a measure taken to address a threat, potentially as soon as possible when prior notice is impossible. For a single urgent threat-response measure, the texts could be read as imposing two communications with different content and potentially different triggering conditions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different communications: A concerns informing service recipients about the significant cyber threat, whereas B concerns notifying the involved subscriber about the measure taken and, ordinarily, giving that subscriber an opportunity to remove the threat. The same recipient may receive both communications, but neither text says that one communication substitutes for the other; both duties can be performed cumulatively, and B does not establish a separate recipient or reporting regime that would make this a dual-reporting conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer dit wegens de vereiste spoed niet voorafgaand aan het nemen van de maatregel mogelijk is, doet de aanbieder zo snel mogelijk melding van de maatregel.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities to establish and implement a process to report ICT-related incidents, while provision B requires a qualifying trust-service provider to make a specific incident notification within 24 hours to its CSIRT and competent authority. If A's reporting process entails a separate reporting duty to a different recipient or on a different timetable, the same incident could trigger two cumulative reporting obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A does not specify a recipient, deadline, or separate filing; it requires a management process that includes reporting incidents. Provision B supplies a concrete notification duty, and an entity can implement its A process so that the B notification is the required reporting step, with no textual indication that A requires an additional filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten omschrijven een beheerproces voor ICT-gerelateerde incidenten, stellen dit vast en leggen dit ten uitvoer, om ICT-gerelateerde incidenten te detecteren, te beheren en te melden.
verdict.evidence_span_b: In afwijking van het eerste lid dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit als dat incident gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van haar vertrouwensdienst.

verdict.shared_subject: Information provision concerning electronic-service security and incident notifications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern supplying information connected with cybersecurity. A requires specified bodies and recognised entities to provide information to the Minister when requested or on their own initiative, while B requires a central contact point to forward received incident-related reports to contact points in other EU Member States on request of the CSIRT or competent authority. If the same organisation and event fall within both regimes, the actor may face separate information flows and authorities, with no coordination rule shown.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors and are triggered by different circumstances. A concerns information needed by the Dutch Minister to prevent or end infringements of secure and reliable access to electronic services; B concerns forwarding reports already received under Articles 25 and 33 to other Member States' central contact points. Both duties can be performed cumulatively, and the texts do not establish incompatible recipients, deadlines, or content.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties, op grond van artikel 9, tweede of derde lid, toegelaten houders van een erkenning en op grond van artikel 11 erkende middelenuitgevers en diensten verstrekken aan Onze Minister desgevraagd en uit eigen beweging de gegevens en inlichtingen die hij nodig heeft om maatregelen te kunnen nemen om inbreuk op de veilige en betrouwbare toegang tot elektronische dienstverlening te voorkomen of beëindigen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Op verzoek van het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit stuurt het centrale contactpunt de op grond van de artikelen 25 en 33 ontvangen meldingen door naar de centrale contactpunten van de andere betrokken lidstaten van de Europese Unie.

verdict.shared_subject: High-risk processing or AI systems and the associated risk-management obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose advance risk-related obligations on an operator, but they require different activities: a GDPR data-protection impact assessment before processing where processing is likely to create a high risk to natural persons’ rights and freedoms, and testing of a high-risk AI system during development and before market placement or use. An operator might therefore face uncertainty about whether the GDPR assessment and the AI testing obligation overlap or whether completion of one is sufficient for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations are cumulative and address different objects and triggers: Article 35 requires a data-protection impact assessment concerning intended personal-data processing, while Article 9 requires testing the AI system against predefined metrics and probabilistic thresholds. Nothing in either text says that one assessment substitutes for, overrides, or is deemed to satisfy the other; a diligent operator can perform both.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een soort verwerking, in het bijzonder een verwerking waarbij nieuwe technologieën worden gebruikt, gelet op de aard, de omvang, de context en de doeleinden daarvan waarschijnlijk een hoog risico inhoudt voor de rechten en vrijheden van natuurlijke personen voert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke vóór de verwerking een beoordeling uit van het effect van de beoogde verwerkingsactiviteiten op de bescherming van persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het testen van AI-systemen met een hoog risico vindt, zoals passend, in de loop van het ontwikkelingsproces plaats en in ieder geval voordat het systeem in de handel wordt gebracht of in gebruik wordt gesteld.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or information duties concerning regulated entities and authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose communication duties to authorities, and a real entity could conceivably be subject to both regimes. If the same underlying event also constituted an activity or circumstance covered by Provision B, the entity might need to communicate related information to two different authorities, with neither text stating that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different actors, triggers, and subject matter: Provision A concerns financial entities reporting serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, while Provision B concerns notified bodies informing the notifying authority, on request, about conformity-assessment and other activities. Nothing shown requires the same actor to make both filings for the same triggering event; the duties can therefore be complied with independently.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose mandatory action, so one might superficially see competing statutory obligations. However, they regulate different actors, subject matters, triggers, and legal processes: financial entities must classify ICT incidents, while municipal executive authorities must decide a consent application within a specified period.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations can be fully satisfied simultaneously because they do not prescribe incompatible conduct, deadlines, recipients, or standards. Compliance with the incident-classification duty has no bearing on the municipal consent decision, and the municipal deadline does not constrain incident classification.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity oversight and incident-related functions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern cybersecurity-related monitoring or oversight. One could argue that the competent authority’s power to issue warnings about infringements overlaps with the CSIRT’s mandatory task of providing early warnings and notifications about cyber threats, vulnerabilities, and incidents.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of norms on different actors: provision A gives Member States’ competent authorities a power to issue warnings to essential entities about their infringements, while provision B requires the CSIRT to perform dynamic risk and incident analysis. The CSIRT’s analysis duty does not prohibit or displace the authority’s warning competence, and the texts do not require incompatible actions.

verdict.shared_subject: The submission of an auditor’s statement to the Minister concerning compliance with designated standards or information-security rules.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an obligation to submit an auditor’s statement to the Minister, but Article 3 concerns a statement showing whether an appointed standard is applied, while Article 4 concerns a statement showing compliance with the rules referred to in Article 4(1). If those are distinct statements or scopes, an organ might face two submission duties, but the text shown does not establish incompatible content, timing, or that one submission cannot satisfy the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied cumulatively: Article 3 permits rules requiring organs to submit an auditor’s statement about application of an appointed standard, and Article 4 requires administrative bodies and designated organisations to submit an auditor’s statement about compliance with Article 4(1) rules. Nothing shown forbids submitting both, and the provisions may concern the same or overlapping statement without creating an irreconcilable duty.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related reporting by entities potentially covered by both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose incident-related submissions with different triggers and clocks. A requires an immediate serious-incident notification, in any event within 15 days after awareness, while B requires a final report within one month after the incident is resolved, or a progress report instead if the incident is still ongoing when the final report is due; this could indicate two cumulative filings rather than one replacing the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts shown do not establish that the same actor, incident, and reporting obligation fall under both provisions, nor do they identify B's recipient or expressly require a separate report from A's notification. B may be a later progress/final reporting regime for a different statutory incident framework, and A's notification could potentially be the only relevant filing for its incidents.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions establishing B's scope and reporting recipient, including whether an AI provider or deployer subject to Article 73 is also an 'essential entity' or 'important entity' under BWBR0052872, and whether B's progress/final report is a separate filing from the Article 73 serious-incident notification. The shown text also does not establish that the same incident qualifies under both regimes.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents involving essential entities and the roles of competent authorities and the CSIRT
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, when imposing enforcement measures, to take account of the offender’s intent or negligence. Provision B requires the CSIRT, where applicable, to respond to incidents and provide assistance. One might argue that CSIRT assistance could affect the assessment of the entity’s negligence, creating a possible interaction between incident response and enforcement assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different functions: competent authorities must consider intent or negligence when taking enforcement measures, while the CSIRT responds to incidents and provides assistance. Nothing in either text requires the CSIRT to establish, disregard, or determine negligence, and neither provision prevents the authority from considering it.

verdict.shared_subject: Disclosure of investigation results by public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the Minister to provide geographic-research results to the European Commission, BEREC, and specified administrative bodies. Provision B allows the competent authority to require an essential entity to provide audit results to that competent authority; if the same authority or entity is involved, the provisions could create overlapping disclosure obligations concerning investigation results.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different investigations, actors, and recipients: A concerns the Minister's geographic research and disclosure to listed public bodies, while B concerns an essential entity's independent audit and disclosure to the competent authority. Nothing in either text forbids the other disclosure, makes the results identical, or creates incompatible deadlines or recipients.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity oversight and incident-related information duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities to take the duration of an infringement into account when imposing enforcement measures. Provision B requires the CSIRT, where possible, to issue and disseminate early warnings, notifications and announcements, potentially concerning the same incident or vulnerability; one might argue that rapid dissemination could expose or prolong an infringement-related situation, complicating the authority’s duration assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties on different actors and address different actions. A concerns how competent authorities assess infringements during enforcement, while B concerns the CSIRT’s operational dissemination of cybersecurity information; nothing in either text requires the CSIRT to conceal information or prevents an authority from considering the infringement’s duration.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT-taken bij cyberdreigingen en incidenten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen CSIRT’s taken op rond cyberincidenten en waarschuwingen. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat de Nederlandse bepaling een extra ontvanger toevoegt — Onze Minister van Economische Zaken — en dat daardoor onduidelijk is of een CSIRT naast de in de NIS2-richtlijn genoemde partijen ook aan die minister moet informeren.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn inhoudelijk grotendeels parallel en kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd. Provision B concretiseert nationaal de ontvangers en voegt taken toe, maar verbiedt niet dat waarschuwingen ook aan de in Provision A genoemde bevoegde autoriteiten en andere belanghebbenden worden verstrekt; bovendien wordt hier alleen de afzonderlijke norm over reageren en bijstand uit B vergeleken met de afzonderlijke norm over vroegtijdige waarschuwingen uit A.

verdict.evidence_span_b: indien van toepassing, het reageren op incidenten en verlenen van bijstand aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit

verdict.shared_subject: Information and compliance obligations, but concerning different actors and regulatory processes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an obligation to provide information or evidence to a public authority. One could argue that a critical ICT third-party provider may need to provide a reasoned statement to the lead overseer while an organisation subject to the Dutch rule must provide an auditor’s statement to the Minister, creating overlapping administrative burdens if the same entity falls within both regimes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions require different things from different actors and serve different procedures: Provision A concerns a critical ICT third-party provider responding to recommendations within 60 calendar days, whereas Provision B concerns administrative bodies and designated organisations submitting an auditor’s statement about compliance with information-security rules. Nothing in either text makes one submission substitute for, prohibit, or conflict with the other.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Bestuursorganen en aangewezen organisaties overleggen aan Onze Minister een verklaring van een auditor waaruit blijkt of zij voldoen aan de in het eerste lid bedoelde regels.

verdict.shared_subject: Onverwijlde kennisgeving van een significant incident door een essentiële of belangrijke entiteit
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij hetzelfde significante incident verplicht A melding aan het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit, terwijl B kennisgeving aan de ontvangers van de diensten verplicht. Dit zijn verschillende ontvangers en de tekst bepaalt niet dat één kennisgeving de andere vervangt; beide verplichtingen kunnen dus cumulatief gelden.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen zijn inhoudelijk goed naast elkaar uitvoerbaar: de entiteit kan onverwijld zowel de bevoegde instantie als haar dienstontvangers informeren. A en B regelen verschillende communicatiedoelen en bevatten geen tegenstrijdige inhoud, deadline of verbod.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een belangrijke entiteit ondervindt een incident dat een ernstige operationele verstoring veroorzaakt en daardoor een significant incident is. Zij moet dit onverwijld melden bij haar CSIRT of bevoegde autoriteit op grond van A én de getroffen ontvangers van haar diensten onverwijld informeren op grond van B. Een melding aan het CSIRT voldoet niet aan de afzonderlijke kennisgeving aan de dienstontvangers, en omgekeerd; de twee meldingen lopen bovendien naar verschillende ontvangers.
verdict.decisive_exception: Geen beslissende uitzondering is zichtbaar in de getoonde teksten. De bepalingen leggen afzonderlijke verplichtingen aan verschillende ontvangers op; er is geen bepaling dat de ene melding de andere vervangt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat zorgt ervoor dat essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten elk incident dat aanzienlijke gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van hun diensten als bedoeld in lid 3 (significant incident) onverwijld meldt bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit overeenkomstig lid 4.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Use and oversight of a high-risk AI system involving personal-data processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 21 gives the data subject an individual right to object to processing based on Article 6(1)(e) or (f), requiring the controller to stop unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Article 14 requires human overseers of a high-risk AI system to be able to monitor its operation and detect and address irregularities, but it does not expressly require them to stop processing in response to an individual objection; this could create a practical gap if the system continues processing despite the objection.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative duties rather than incompatible ones. A controller can provide the Article 14 oversight capabilities, detect the objection or its consequences, and separately comply with Article 21 by stopping the relevant processing unless an overriding ground applies; Article 14 does not authorise continued processing or deem system oversight sufficient to satisfy the individual right.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 21 itself contains the applicable exception: processing may continue only if the controller demonstrates compelling legitimate grounds overriding the data subject’s interests, rights and freedoms, or grounds relating to legal claims. Article 14 neither conflicts with nor substitutes for that rule.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and information sharing involving public-sector or designated organisations and entities that are both essential and critical
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can concern the same underlying cybersecurity incident, but they impose different duties on different actors: Provision A requires the affected bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify the Minister immediately, while Provision B requires a competent authority to provide information to another competent authority about a significant incident reported by a dual-status essential/critical entity. If the same organisation and incident fall within both regimes, the provisions could create overlapping reporting and onward-information flows, with potentially different recipients and triggers.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are cumulative and directed at different actors rather than contradictory: A requires the affected organisation to notify the Minister, whereas B requires a competent authority to share information with the authority under article 8 after a significant incident has been reported under article 25. Nothing in either text says that one notification substitutes for, prohibits, or delays the other; the organisation can notify the Minister and the competent authority can separately share the required information.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by a financial entity/provider where an ICT incident also constitutes a personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity must report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority, while B requires the provider to notify the affected data subject without delay when a personal-data breach is likely to adversely affect that person’s privacy. If the same event satisfies both triggers, the actor must make two communications to different recipients; notifying one does not notify the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are independently satisfiable and concern different recipients and purposes: regulatory incident reporting to the competent authority versus individual privacy notification. There is no contradiction in making both reports, and A does not prohibit or replace the notification required by B.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity suffers a serious ICT incident involving a breach of identifiable customers’ personal data that is likely to adversely affect their privacy. It must report the serious ICT-related incident to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46” under A and, “onverwijld,” notify each affected data subject under B; filing with the authority does not notify the data subjects, and notifying the data subjects does not satisfy the authority-reporting duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations to authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information-reporting duties, but they concern different actors, subject matter, recipients, and triggers. A financial entity must submit updated notifications about a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority, whereas a notified body must, on request, inform the notifying authority about conformity-assessment and other activities; the texts do not establish one filing as satisfying the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with cumulatively because they apply to different actors and events. Provision A concerns financial entities and serious ICT-related incidents, while provision B concerns notified bodies and requested information about activities within their notification scope; neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other duty.

verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming.

verdict.shared_subject: Cyber-threat and ICT-incident communications by entities potentially subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to notify its service recipients of the significant cyber-threat itself, while provision B requires a financial entity to submit incident notifications and reports to the relevant competent authority. If the same financial entity is also an essential or important entity and the event is both a significant cyber-threat affecting recipients and a serious ICT-related incident, the duties concern different communications and recipients, so one filing cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can notify affected service recipients under A and separately report the serious ICT-related incident to the competent authority under B. They impose no incompatible content, deadline, or prohibition, and B's reporting duty does not replace A's recipient communication.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial cloud-service entity that is also an essential or important entity detects a significant cyber-threat that may affect its customers and qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident. It must notify the potentially affected service recipients of the threat under A and submit the initial notification, interim updates, and final report to the relevant competent authority under B; notifying the customers does not constitute the required filing with the authority, and filing with the authority does not notify the customers.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident enforcement and CSIRT assistance
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern conduct following a significant incident, and an essential entity could be involved in an enforcement process while also requesting operational guidance from the CSIRT. However, provision A governs how authorities assess enforcement measures, whereas provision B requires the CSIRT to respond to a requesting reporting entity; neither requires or forbids the conduct required by the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are imposed on different actors and concern different actions: competent authorities must consider the duration of an infringement, while the CSIRT must provide guidance or operational advice upon request within the stated timeframe. The entity's optional request does not create a conflict, and the two duties can be performed cumulatively without either discharging or obstructing the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Uitwisseling/verstrekking van informatie over incidenten door CSIRT’s en bevoegde autoriteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen betrekking hebben op informatie over hetzelfde incident. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat artikel 15 uitwisseling binnen het CSIRT-netwerk op verzoek verlangt, terwijl artikel 40 informatieverstrekking aan de bevoegde autoriteit verlangt, zodat onduidelijkheid ontstaat over welke instantie de informatie moet ontvangen of welke procedure voorrang heeft.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen verplichtingen op aan verschillende institutionele actoren en hebben verschillende functies: artikel 15 regelt operationele informatie-uitwisseling binnen het CSIRT-netwerk op verzoek, terwijl artikel 40 een bevoegde autoriteit verplicht informatie aan een andere bevoegde autoriteit te verstrekken over een gemeld significant incident. Geen van beide verbiedt de andere handeling, en cumulatieve naleving is mogelijk.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk dat mogelijkerwijs gevolgen ondervindt van een incident, het uitwisselen en bespreken van informatie over dat incident en de daarmee samenhangende cyberdreigingen, risico’s en kwetsbaarheden
verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld door een essentiële entiteit die tevens een kritieke entiteit is als bedoeld in de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security/ICT incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity that is also an operator of a public electronic communications service could face one incident that is both a serious ICT-related incident and a security breach adversely affecting personal-data protection. Provision A requires reporting to the relevant competent authority, while Provision B requires immediate notification to the Dutch Data Protection Authority; the texts identify different recipients and do not say that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can report the incident to the relevant competent authority under A and notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens under B. Provision A contains no deadline in the norm shown, so B's 'onverwijld' deadline does not itself create incompatible clocks or make either duty impossible.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank that is also an operator of a public electronic communications service suffers a ransomware incident exposing customer personal data. The incident qualifies as a serious ICT-related incident under A and as a security breach adversely affecting personal-data protection under B. The bank must report under A 'aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46' and separately notify B 'de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld'; notifying one authority does not, on the text shown, satisfy the duty to notify the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens die zijn verwerkt in verband met de levering van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst in de Europese Unie.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related information and reporting involving ICT service providers and service recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives the lead overseer a power to request reports from critical ICT third-party providers about actions or corrective measures concerning recommendations. Provision B separately requires an essential or important entity, where applicable, to inform its service recipients without delay about significant incidents adversely affecting service provision; a single incident could therefore generate information flows involving overlapping ICT-service activity, with uncertainty about whether the requested report must also address the recipient notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable rules on different actors and for different triggers. A concerns the lead overseer’s optional competence to request a post-oversight report from a critical ICT third-party provider concerning recommendations, whereas B concerns an essential or important entity’s mandatory notification to its service recipients about significant incidents; neither provision forbids or substitutes for compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: na afloop van de oversightactiviteiten te verzoeken om verslagen met vermelding van de ondernomen acties of de corrigerende maatregelen die door de kritieke derde aanbieders van ICT-diensten zijn genomen met betrekking tot de in punt d) bedoelde aanbevelingen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident- or security-related notifications by a service provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use a notification duty, and a provider subject to both might have to notify an affected subscriber under A while also reporting a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority under B. However, the duties have different recipients and triggers, so they are not substitutes for one another; the main apparent overlap is cumulative reporting rather than an inability to obey both.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly be complied with together: the provider can notify the subscriber before taking the security measure, or as soon as possible in an urgent case, and separately report a qualifying significant incident to the CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. A concerns a measure under Article 7.6a(1)(g) and a subscriber-facing warning, whereas B concerns a significant incident affecting a trust service and institutional reporting.

If the protective measure follows a significant incident, the provider might have to make both communications, to different recipients and for different purposes.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct, cumulatively satisfiable duties: A concerns a final incident report to the CSIRT or competent authority, whereas B concerns notice to the affected subscriber before or after a network or service measure. Niets in de teksten bepaalt dat het bewaren van artikel 18-documentatie de DPIA vervangt, haar verhindert of daarmee onverenigbaar is; beide verplichtingen kunnen afzonderlijk worden nageleefd.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities in the financial/banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the relevant entities to make the Article 19 notification, including a voluntary notification, also to the sectoral CSIRT designated under the Cybersecurity Act. Provision B separately requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report to its CSIRT and competent authority within one month after the Article 27 notification. If the same incident triggers both regimes, the reports have different statutory bases, potentially different recipients, and different content, so the A filing would not obviously discharge B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions concern incident communications to a CSIRT, and the CSIRT named in A might be the same CSIRT referred to in B. The texts do not expressly state that the reports are incompatible or that the same incident cannot be reported through a single coordinated submission; moreover, B's final report is a later, more detailed report and could supplement an earlier notification rather than conflict with it.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank that is also an essential or important entity suffers one incident that triggers the Article 19 notification and the Article 27 notification. It must notify the designated sectoral CSIRT under A and, within one month after the Article 27 notification, submit the detailed final report under B to both “haar CSIRT” and “haar bevoegde autoriteit”; filing the A notification does not itself make the required final report to the competent authority, and the texts do not establish that one filing substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of ICT/security incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a financial entity to report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, while provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a final report within one month after the incident is resolved. If the same incident falls within both regimes, the texts could require separate reports under different statutory schemes, and A's recipient is expressly identified while B's recipient and any coordination rule are not shown.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish that the reports are separate filings to different recipients or that their contents and deadlines are incompatible. Provision A's referenced reporting framework expressly includes a final report, and provision B may simply impose an additional incident-reporting requirement that can be satisfied cumulatively; the absence of a recipient in the excerpt prevents treating this as a demonstrated dual-reporting conflict.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns the municipal approval decision for cable works, including an eight-week decision period and possible extension. Provision B concerns incident reporting by an essential or important entity, with a progress report replacing a final report during a continuing incident; these duties can readily be performed independently and do not prescribe incompatible conduct.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Burgemeester en wethouders nemen het instemmingsbesluit binnen acht weken na ontvangst van de schriftelijke melding als bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel a.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting changes relevant to regulatory rules or assessments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require information about changes to be communicated, but they address different recipients and apparently different underlying regulatory matters: provision A requires a Member State to notify the European Commission, while provision B requires a qualifying undertaking to notify the ACM. If the same change affected both regimes, the actor-specific duties would still be separately applicable rather than mutually incompatible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and to different authorities: provision A concerns each Member State's communication to the Commission, whereas provision B concerns a qualifying undertaking's communication to the ACM. Each can be performed independently, and neither prohibits or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke lidstaat deelt de Commissie uiterlijk op 25 mei 2018 de regels mee die hij heeft vastgesteld overeenkomstig lid 1, alsmede onverwijld alle wijzigingen daarvan.

verdict.shared_subject: Oversight and incident-related information concerning ICT/AI operations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The lead overseer may request reports from critical ICT third-party providers concerning actions or corrective measures related to its recommendations, while an AI-system deployer must notify specified AI actors and market-surveillance authorities immediately when it detects a serious incident. If the requested report concerned the same incident, one might argue that the reporting and oversight channels overlap and could create uncertainty about which communication is required.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A is merely a competence granted to a lead overseer vis-à-vis critical ICT third-party providers; it permits requesting reports after oversight activities. Provision B imposes an incident-notification duty on AI-system deployers, directed first to the provider and then to importers/distributors and market-surveillance authorities. They concern different actors, different actions, and different recipients, and nothing in either text makes compliance with one substitute for or prevent compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident-related duties of the market-surveillance authority and CSIRT
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related information flows under EU/Dutch cybersecurity regulation, and the CSIRT’s monitoring and analysis could generate information relevant to procedures followed after a serious-incident notification. verdict.shared_subject: Cyberdreigingen en incidentmeldingen door entiteiten in de financiële sector
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Bij een significante cyberdreiging kan norm A de entiteit verplichten de getroffen ontvangers van haar diensten rechtstreeks over de dreiging te informeren, terwijl norm B voor bepaalde financiële entiteiten een melding bij een aangewezen sectoraal CSIRT verlangt. Dat zijn verschillende handelingen voor verschillende ontvangers; een CSIRT-melding vervangt de kennisgeving aan de dienstontvangers niet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen kunnen zonder tegenstrijdigheid cumulatief worden nageleefd: de entiteit informeert haar mogelijk getroffen dienstontvangers over de dreiging en doet daarnaast de vereiste melding bij het aangewezen CSIRT. Geen van beide bepalingen verbiedt of vervangt de andere handeling.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een centrale tegenpartij wordt getroffen door een significante cyberdreiging die haar klanten kan raken. Zij moet de mogelijk getroffen klanten onverwijld informeren over de dreiging op grond van A én dezelfde gebeurtenis melden bij het aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en financiëlemarktinfrastructuur op grond van B; de twee meldingen gaan naar verschillende ontvangers en geen van beide ontslaat haar van de andere.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by an AI-system provider where the same event is both a personal-data breach and a serious incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same incident can trigger both duties: GDPR requires notification to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours, while the AI Act requires the Article 73(1) notification to market-surveillance authorities, immediately and no later than 15 days. These are different regimes and recipients, so making the GDPR notification does not itself make the AI-Act notification, and the provider may need to submit two reports on different clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be satisfied cumulatively without contradictory content: the provider can notify the data-protection supervisory authority within 72 hours and separately notify the relevant market-surveillance authority immediately or within 15 days. The shorter GDPR deadline does not discharge the distinct AI-Act filing, but neither duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An AI provider's high-risk system suffers a security incident that unlawfully exposes users' personal data and is also a serious incident causally linked to the AI system. The provider must notify the competent data-protection supervisory authority within 72 hours under Article 33 and separately make the Article 73(1) serious-incident notification to the market-surveillance authorities immediately after establishing the causal link and no later than 15 days after awareness; filing with the first authority does not constitute filing with the second.

One might argue that both provisions concern the same reported incident and could create overlapping institutional handling duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties on different actors: A concerns the competent authority’s receipt confirmation, whereas B concerns the CSIRT’s analytical and situational-awareness tasks. Nothing in either text makes the CSIRT’s analysis replace the authority’s confirmation, or makes the authority’s confirmation discharge the CSIRT’s duties.

However, provision A concerns publication of a decision in the Staatscourant, while provision B concerns an operator informing subscribers about specified traffic-data information; the texts identify different acts, recipients, and triggers.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are readily cumulative and apply to different subject matter: A requires publication of a qualifying decision in the Staatscourant, whereas B requires the provider to notify the subscriber within six months concerning traffic data covered by onderdeel b. Performing one notification does not purport to replace or prevent the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern follow-up to incident notifications in network or information systems. One might argue that the market-surveillance authority must act within seven days, while the other requires the Minister to forward a qualifying notification to the competent authority, potentially creating uncertainty about which authority should handle the notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different authorities and do not prescribe incompatible actions, deadlines, recipients, or outcomes. The market-surveillance authority can take appropriate measures within seven days while the Minister separately forwards a qualifying notification; nothing in either text makes one action substitute for or prohibit the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT-related incidents under DORA and serious incidents involving high-risk AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A financial entity that is also an AI provider could face both duties for the same incident: DORA requires an interim report after the initial notification to the relevant competent authority, while the AI Act requires a serious-incident notification to the market-surveillance authority within the stated deadline. These are distinct reporting duties to different authorities, so making one filing does not, on the text shown, discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed cumulatively: the actor can submit the DORA interim report to the relevant competent authority and separately submit the AI-Act notification to the market-surveillance authority. Nothing in either excerpt prohibits the second filing or states that one report substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank that is also the provider of a high-risk AI system experiences one serious incident involving that system. After making the initial DORA notification, it must submit an interim report to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit,” while it must also make the AI-Act serious-incident notification to the market-surveillance authority under Article 73(1), no later than 15 days after becoming aware of the incident. verdict.shared_subject: ICT incident response and organisational measures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires financial entities, after a serious ICT-related incident, to identify improvements to ICT activities or business-continuity policy. Provision B requires a provider, before taking a specified measure, to notify the affected subscriber and allow the threat to be removed, or to notify as soon as possible where urgency prevents prior notice. A possible overlap in incident-related activity does not make these duties incompatible: identifying improvements and notifying a subscriber can both be done.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties with different triggers and likely different actors. A financial entity can conduct the required post-incident evaluation and identify improvements while an affected subscriber is notified before, or promptly after, a measure is taken; neither text requires withholding the other action.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten verrichten ICT-gerelateerde post-incidentevaluaties na verstoringen van hun kernactiviteiten ten gevolge van een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident, analyseren daarbij de oorzaken van de verstoring en identificeren de verbeteringen die moeten worden aangebracht in de ICT-activiteiten of in het kader van het ICT-bedrijfscontinuïteitsbeleid als bedoeld in artikel 11.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen.
