verdict.shared_subject: Melding van informatie of incidenten en de daaropvolgende procedures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen raken aan kennisgevingen en daaropvolgende overheidsprocedures. Bij een gebeurtenis die zowel als vrijwillig gemelde informatie onder artikel 30 als als kennisgeving van een ernstig incident onder artikel 73 wordt behandeld, kan onduidelijkheid ontstaan over welke procedure en termijn leidend zijn.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 30 verplicht de lidstaten/autoriteiten slechts tot het verstrekken van ontvangen informatie met vertrouwelijkheid en passende bescherming; artikel 73 verplicht de markttoezichtautoriteit maatregelen te nemen binnen zeven dagen en de toepasselijke kennisgevingsprocedures te volgen. De bepalingen leggen geen tegenstrijdige handelingen, termijnen of ontvangers aan dezelfde actor op, en artikel 30 bepaalt bovendien dat vrijwillige melding geen nieuwe verplichtingen voor de meldende entiteit mag creëren.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de bevoegde autoriteiten, de centrale contactpunten de informatie over de meldingen die op grond van dit artikel zijn ontvangen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen

verdict.shared_subject: AI systems processing personal data and subject to human oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives a data subject a right to object to processing based on Article 6(1)(e) or (f), requiring the controller to stop unless overriding legitimate grounds exist. Provision B requires the high-risk AI system to be supplied so that human overseers can monitor its operation, which could entail continuing to process personal data after an objection in order to perform that monitoring.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose cumulative, independently satisfiable requirements rather than incompatible commands. A controller can provide the required monitoring capability while respecting an objection by stopping the relevant processing, unless it establishes the overriding grounds expressly preserved by Provision A; moreover, Provision B applies only to high-risk AI systems and does not itself require processing of the objector’s personal data.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerkingsverantwoordelijke staakt de verwerking van de persoonsgegevens tenzij hij dwingende gerechtvaardigde gronden voor de verwerking aanvoert die zwaarder wegen dan de belangen, rechten en vrijheden van de betrokkene of die verband houden met de instelling, uitoefening of onderbouwing van een rechtsvordering.
verdict.evidence_span_b: de relevante capaciteiten en beperkingen van het AI-systeem met een hoog risico goed te begrijpen en de werking ervan naar behoren te kunnen monitoren

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or notification duties of regulated entities/assessment bodies
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information-related obligations, and a single ongoing incident might conceivably affect the scope or conditions of an assessment body's notification. If so, the actor could face an incident-related progress report under Provision A and a separate notification to the notifying authority under Provision B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different actors, triggers, recipients, and subject matter. Provision A concerns a significant incident and requires a progress report to the CSIRT or competent authority, while Provision B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority about circumstances affecting their notification scope or conditions; neither duty prevents or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/cyber-risk assessment versus the timing of a decision after receipt of a notification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use mandatory language and could arise in an operational setting involving an ICT-related notification or risk. One might argue that an immediate decision leaves no time for the required cyber-threat and vulnerability assessment.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires financial entities to assess relevant cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities; provision B requires that a decision be made immediately after receipt of a notification. They regulate different duties, triggers, and apparently different actors, and nothing in either text says that the assessment must precede or delay the decision. The assessment can therefore be performed alongside or independently of the decision duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: beoordelen de cyberdreigingen en ICT-kwetsbaarheden die relevant zijn voor hun door ICT ondersteunde bedrijfsfuncties en informatie- en ICT-activa
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity governance and protection for entities or AI models
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose cybersecurity-related obligations, but they regulate different duties and potentially different actors: Provision A concerns governance bodies approving and overseeing an entity’s cybersecurity-risk measures, while Provision B requires providers of systemic-risk general-purpose AI models to ensure an appropriate cybersecurity-protection level for the model and its physical infrastructure. The strongest tension case is that the same provider or organisation may have to satisfy both a governance/oversight regime and a model-specific protection requirement, with no indication that one benchmark discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: a governance body can approve and oversee cybersecurity-risk measures under Provision A, while the AI-model provider separately performs the model-specific evaluation, risk mitigation, incident documentation/reporting, and cybersecurity protection required by Provision B. They do not prescribe incompatible conduct, different deadlines for the same report, or competing cybersecurity benchmarks that leave the governing standard unclear.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten de door deze entiteiten genomen maatregelen voor het beheer van cyberbeveiligingsrisico’s goedkeuren om te voldoen aan artikel 21, toezien op de uitvoering ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: zorgen voor een passend niveau van cyberbeveiligingsbescherming voor het AI-model voor algemene doeleinden met een systeemrisico en de fysieke infrastructuur van het model

verdict.shared_subject: Melding van incidenten of cyberdreigingen door actoren die onder beide regelingen vallen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen zien op informatieverstrekking na een beveiligings- of cyberincident. Bij een financiële entiteit die tevens verwerker is, kan dezelfde gebeurtenis aanleiding geven tot een melding door de verwerker aan de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke en tot een vrijwillige melding van een significante cyberdreiging aan de bevoegde autoriteit; die meldingen hebben verschillende geadresseerden en de tweede is bovendien optioneel.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 19 verplicht financiële entiteiten in het getoonde onderdeel niet om een cyberdreiging te melden: zij kunnen dat vrijwillig doen en alleen wanneer zij zelf oordelen dat de dreiging relevant is. De actor kan dus volledig aan beide bepalingen voldoen door geen vrijwillige melding onder artikel 19 te doen; bovendien verplicht artikel 33 de verwerker slechts tot informeren van de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, niet tot een melding aan dezelfde autoriteit.
verdict.decisive_exception: Geen uitzondering is nodig voor de compatibiliteitsbeoordeling: de vermeende botsing berust op het vrijwillig activeren van artikel 19. De tekst toont geen verplichting om die optionele melding te doen, en de in artikel 19 genoemde doorzendplicht ontstaat alleen nadat de financiële entiteit vrijwillig heeft gemeld.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.

verdict.shared_subject: Information and reporting content concerning ICT/AI risks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information-related obligations, so an organisation might need to structure its internal reporting channels while information about an AI-model system risk is being formally recorded. However, Provision A concerns a financial entity’s internal corporate channels and Provision B concerns the required contents of qualified warnings issued by the scientific panel; neither prescribes incompatible content, recipient, timing, or action.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The financial entity’s duty is to establish business-level channels enabling it to obtain information about ICT-service-provider arrangements, changes, effects, and serious ICT incidents. The scientific panel’s duty is to ensure that qualified warnings contain a description of relevant facts and reasons, plus specified information. These duties can be performed cumulatively without either preventing compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: het opzetten van meldingskanalen op bedrijfsniveau die het in staat stellen informatie in te winnen over:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Gekwalificeerde waarschuwingen moeten terdege worden gemotiveerd en ten minste het volgende vermelden of bevatten:

verdict.shared_subject: Informing persons or service recipients about threats or incidents affecting them
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require prompt information to people affected by a harmful event. A single cyber incident could simultaneously be a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect data subjects and a significant cyber threat affecting the entity’s service recipients, creating potentially overlapping notices with different content and recipient categories.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are addressed to different actors and concern different triggering events and information. Provision A requires the provider to notify the person whose personal data are concerned about a qualifying personal-data breach, while provision B requires an essential or important entity to inform potentially affected service recipients about measures and, if necessary, the significant cyber threat; both notices can be made cumulatively, and neither text says one notice substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien nodig stelt de entiteit die ontvangers ook in kennis van de desbetreffende significante cyberdreiging.

verdict.shared_subject: Cooperation with designated public authorities or persons in the execution of statutory objectives
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose cooperation duties, but they address different recipients and operational contexts: provision A requires specified market actors to assist the Minister, while provision B requires the involved party and related persons to assist the designated person. One might argue that an actor could face competing instructions or uncertainty about which cooperation duty takes priority, but neither text makes the duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the actors listed in A can cooperate with the Minister, while the involved party and its personnel cooperate with the designated person under B. Nothing in either provision prohibits compliance with the other, and B expressly requires cooperation with its own designated person rather than displacing A's duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: verleent medewerking aan de Minister bij de tenuitvoerlegging van het eerste lid
verdict.evidence_span_b: verleent de aangewezen persoon alle medewerking

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of significant cyber/ICT incidents or threats by entities potentially subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns a voluntary report of a significant cyber threat, with the relevant authority potentially forwarding it to other authorities, while provision B requires the entity itself to report a significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority. If the same event is both a significant cyber threat and a significant incident, the provisions point to different reporting structures and potentially different triggers, but A is optional and does not itself require a filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: An entity can comply with both provisions because A expressly permits voluntary reporting, whereas B imposes a mandatory incident-reporting duty only when its own conditions are met. The actor can simply refrain from the optional A report; moreover, the shown text of A does not establish a mandatory separate filing to the ECB—the ECB forwarding rule appears only in the contextual, excluded paragraph.
verdict.decisive_exception: None. The apparent ECB-reporting difference comes from contextual material that the instructions exclude from provision A, and A's operative rule is voluntary. The extracted ECB recipient/deadline is inconsistent with the operative text selected for A and cannot create a dual-reporting duty here.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit wanneer zij van oordeel zijn dat de dreiging relevant is voor het financiële stelsel, de gebruikers van diensten of de cliënten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting an incident that is both a GDPR personal-data breach and a significant incident for an essential or important entity.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: The same event can trigger both reporting duties, but A requires notification to the GDPR supervisory authority while B requires a notification to the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority. These are distinct recipients and filings; reporting to one set does not, on the text shown, discharge reporting to the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both duties generally use a 72-hour outer deadline, so there is no incompatible timing requirement. An entity could comply with both by making the GDPR notification and the NIS2 notifications within 72 hours, with the additional information required by B.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity suffers one cyberattack that both compromises personal data, creating a GDPR personal-data breach, and qualifies as a significant incident. The entity must notify the GDPR supervisory authority within 72 hours under A and separately notify its CSIRT and competent authority within 72 hours under B; one notification does not name or reach all of the recipients required by the other provision.
verdict.decisive_exception: The texts do not establish that the GDPR supervisory authority is the same body as the CSIRT or the competent authority, nor that one filing legally satisfies the other. A’s risk-based exception could remove the GDPR duty if it is unlikely that the breach risks individuals’ rights and freedoms, but the scenario assumes that exception does not apply.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Notification-related obligations
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a notified body to inform the notifying authority about circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of its notification. Provision B requires a decision immediately after receipt of a notification, so a notification under A could potentially trigger B's decision duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different legal mechanisms: A concerns a notified body's reporting to a notifying authority, while B concerns taking a decision after receipt of a notification. Nothing in the texts establishes that A's report is the notification received under B, that the same actor is bound by both, or that the duties have incompatible content or timing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a serious ICT/AI incident by a financial-sector AI operator
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious incident involving a high-risk AI system requires notification under provision A to the provider first and then to the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities. Provision B separately requires certain financial-sector entities to make the Article 19 incident notification also to the designated sectoral CSIRT, so the same incident may require an additional filing to a different recipient; neither text says that one notification discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the operator can notify the recipients listed in provision A and also send the required Article 19 notification to the designated CSIRT. Provision B may concern a different underlying ICT-incident reporting regime, and the texts shown do not expressly establish that every serious AI incident under A is also an Article 19 incident under B.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank uses a high-risk AI system and discovers an incident that qualifies as a serious incident under Article 26 and also as an Article 19 ICT incident. The bank must first notify the AI provider and then notify the importer or distributor and the relevant market-surveillance authorities under A, while also making the Article 19 notification to the designated CSIRT for the banking and financial-market-infrastructure sectors under B. These are separate filings to different recipients, and B supplies no deadline in the text shown, leaving unresolved how the two reporting duties and their timing interact.
verdict.decisive_exception: The decisive uncertainty is whether the incident qualifies under the separate Article 19 reporting regime and whether that regime contains an exception or coordination rule providing that notification under Article 26 satisfies the CSIRT duty. No such rule is shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.shared_subject: A duty to provide cooperation in an administrative or ministerial process
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use a cooperation duty, so one might initially suspect overlapping obligations concerning assistance to a public authority. However, they impose those duties on different actors and in different procedures: Provision A concerns specified market or institutional parties assisting the Minister, while Provision B concerns other administrative bodies assisting the municipal authorities in coordinating an applicant’s requests.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can plainly be complied with simultaneously because they regulate different obligated parties, authorities, and contexts. Nothing in either text requires an actor to refuse or limit the cooperation required by the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een beursgenoteerde betrokken partij, een aangesloten instelling, centraal instituut, intermediair, instelling in het buitenland of buitenlandse instelling met een functie vergelijkbaar met die van het centraal instituut verleent medewerking aan de Minister bij de tenuitvoerlegging van het eerste lid.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De overige betrokken bestuursorganen verlenen de daarvoor benodigde medewerking.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT information-sharing and warning functions concerning cyber incidents and threats
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information-related obligations on CSIRTs, and a warning or notification under Provision B could concern the same cyber threat, vulnerability, or incident as the information exchange required by Provision A. However, the texts do not make the duties mutually exclusive or prescribe incompatible content, recipients, or deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires the CSIRT network to exchange relevant information among its CSIRTs, while Provision B requires the national CSIRT to provide and disseminate early warnings, notifications, and announcements to listed entities, authorities, the Minister, and other relevant parties where possible in near-real time. These are cumulative functions with different operational forms and recipients; a CSIRT can perform both.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) het uitwisselen van relevante informatie over incidenten, bijna-incidenten, cyberdreigingen, risico’s en kwetsbaarheden;
verdict.evidence_span_b: b. het verstrekken van vroegtijdige waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen en het verspreiden van informatie aan de betrokken essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit, de bevoegde autoriteiten, Onze Minister van Economische Zaken, ten behoeve van de uitvoering van de taken, bedoeld in artikel 2, eerste lid, van de Wet bevordering digitale weerbaarheid bedrijven, en andere relevante partijen over cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten, indien mogelijk in bijna-realtime;

verdict.shared_subject: Informing relevant recipients about a cyber or AI-system incident/threat
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can require the same entity to communicate about the same underlying event: an AI-system incident may also constitute a significant cyber threat affecting service recipients. Article 26 requires notification to market-surveillance authorities and the importer or distributor, while Article 30 requires informing affected service recipients, so one communication does not discharge the other because the recipients differ.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different communications and recipients, and both duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction. Article 30 applies only when the entity is essential or important and notification is needed, whereas Article 26 concerns a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system; their different scopes do not themselves create a conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An important entity operates a high-risk AI system. The system suffers a serious incident that also creates a significant cyber threat likely to affect recipients of the entity’s services. The entity must first notify the provider and then notify “de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten” and “de importeur of distributeur” under Article 26, while also informing the affected service recipients under Article 30; notifying the authorities, provider, importer or distributor does not notify the service recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien nodig stelt de entiteit die ontvangers ook in kennis van de desbetreffende significante cyberdreiging.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant/security incidents by an electronic-communications service provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the entity, where appropriate, to notify its service recipients of significant incidents adversely affecting service provision, while B requires the provider to notify the Dutch data-protection authority of a security breach adversely affecting personal-data protection. For an incident satisfying both triggers, these are separate notifications to different recipients, and neither text says that notifying one recipient discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the provider can promptly notify both its service recipients and the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens. They concern different recipients and partly different triggering interests, so there is no impossibility or contradiction in obeying both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A public electronic-communications provider suffers one security incident that is a significant incident adversely affecting service provision and also has adverse consequences for the protection of personal data processed in providing the service. The provider must notify its service recipients under A and, separately, notify the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens under B, both onverwijld; notifying one recipient does not notify the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst stelt de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging, bedoeld in artikel 11.3, die nadelige gevolgen heeft voor de bescherming van persoonsgegevens

verdict.shared_subject: Incident management and risk control by an organisation using a high-risk AI system
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A high-risk-AI user must immediately notify specified parties when it identifies a serious incident, while an essential or important entity must take proportionate measures to limit incident consequences. In a serious incident involving both regimes, the notification duty and the mitigation duty may operate simultaneously, but neither text says that performing one discharges the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties: provision A requires notification of a defined serious AI incident, whereas provision B requires technical, operational and organisational measures to control security risks and limit consequences. An actor can comply with both by notifying the required recipients and taking appropriate mitigation measures; the texts do not require incompatible conduct.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer de gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ook neemt zij deze maatregelen om incidenten te voorkomen of de gevolgen van incidenten voor de afnemers van haar diensten en voor andere diensten te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related communications and reports by an operator/provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber before taking a network or service measure, or as soon as possible afterward in an urgent case. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report when an incident continues past the final-report deadline; these could arise from the same underlying incident, creating multiple communications with different content and potentially different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct duties serving different purposes and addressed to different recipients: A is a notice to the involved subscriber about a protective measure, while B is a progress report under the incident-reporting regime. Nothing in either text says that one filing substitutes for the other, and the texts do not establish that the same actor, event, and trigger necessarily coincide.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien het incident nog voortduurt op het moment dat het eindverslag had moeten worden ingediend, dient de essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit op dat moment in plaats van een eindverslag een voortgangsverslag in waarin wordt ingegaan op de aspecten, genoemd in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Member States notifying the European Commission of later legislative amendments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require Member States to notify the Commission of later amendments, but they concern different underlying legislative provisions and addressees. The texts do not create incompatible deadlines, contents, or recipients; the same amendment could be reported in both notifications.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and independently satisfiable: Article 83 requires notification of later changes to the provisions adopted under that GDPR paragraph, while Article 53 requires notification of later changes to the provisions implementing that DORA chapter. Both expressly include the Commission, and neither forbids or substitutes for the other notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: alsmede onverwijld alle latere wijzigingen daarvan en alle daarop van invloed zijnde wijzigingswetgeving
verdict.evidence_span_b: De lidstaten stellen de Commissie, de ESMA, de EBA en de Eiopa onverwijld in kennis van latere wijzigingen van deze bepalingen.

verdict.shared_subject: Verplichte medewerking door telecomaanbieders of financiële instellingen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen gebruiken een verplichte medewerkingsplicht, zodat men oppervlakkig zou kunnen vermoeden dat een instelling moet meewerken aan concurrerende of conflicterende opdrachten. De teksten regelen echter verschillende actoren en verschillende soorten handelingen: aftappen of opnemen van telecommunicatie enerzijds en gevolg geven aan een beursgerelateerde schorsing anderzijds.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Artikel 13.2 verplicht openbare telecomaanbieders uitsluitend mee te werken aan een strafvorderlijk, psychiatrisch of inlichtingenrechtelijk bevel of toestemming tot aftappen of opnemen. Artikel 14a.8 richt zich op andere, specifiek opgesomde financiële instellingen en verplicht hen mee te werken aan een beursgenoteerde betrokken partij bij een schorsing; geen van beide bepalingen verbiedt naleving van de andere.

verdict.shared_subject: CSIRT-taken concerning assistance
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose CSIRT assistance duties, but the selected norms concern different assistance: A requires assistance to essential or important entities for real-time or near-real-time monitoring, whereas B requires mutual assistance to other CSIRT-network members on request. The duties could theoretically compete for limited CSIRT capacity, but neither text makes one duty exclusive or sets incompatible priorities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address distinct recipients, triggers and functions. A concerns assistance to entities upon their request and in connection with monitoring their networks and information systems; B concerns mutual assistance to other CSIRT-network members upon a member's request, subject to the CSIRT's capacities and powers. Both can be performed cumulatively, and B's capacity condition does not prohibit compliance with A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek, het verlenen van bijstand aan betrokken essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten met betrekking tot het realtime of bijna-realtime monitoren van hun netwerk en informatiesystemen
verdict.evidence_span_b: het deelnemen aan het CSIRT-netwerk en, in overeenstemming met zijn capaciteiten en bevoegdheden, het verlenen van wederzijdse bijstand aan andere leden van het CSIRT-netwerk op verzoek van een lid van dat netwerk

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT or personal-data incidents by a financial entity that is also a processor
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A processor must inform the controller without unreasonable delay, while B requires a financial entity to submit an initial notification and later reports to the relevant competent authority within separately determined deadlines. A single serious ICT incident involving a personal-data breach could therefore trigger two distinct communications to different recipients, with no indication that notifying one recipient satisfies the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the entity can promptly inform the controller under A and separately file the required initial notification and subsequent reports with the competent authority under B. The provisions do not impose incompatible content, deadlines, or prohibitions; the apparent burden is simply two independently applicable reporting regimes.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity acting as a processor suffers a serious ICT incident that is also a personal-data breach. It must inform the controller without unreasonable delay under A and separately submit B's first notification to the relevant competent authority within the Article 20 deadline, followed by any required interim and final reports; notifying the controller does not constitute filing with the competent authority.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory notifications and information-sharing by authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern regulatory communications, and a notified body could potentially be connected to a financial entity experiencing a serious ICT-related incident. In that situation, information might need to move through both the DORA authority channels and the AI Act notification system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors, concerning different events and communications. Provision A requires a competent authority, after receiving a financial entity’s serious ICT-incident notification, to provide details to specified financial, cybersecurity, resolution and other public authorities; Provision B requires a notifying authority to inform the Commission and other Member States of changes concerning a notified conformity-assessment body. Neither duty prevents compliance with the other, and no single triggering event or common reporting obligation is established.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanmeldende autoriteit stelt de Commissie en de andere lidstaten via het in artikel 30, lid 2, bedoelde elektronische aanmeldingssysteem in kennis van alle relevante wijzigingen in de aanmelding van een aangemelde instantie.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents or threats affecting financial-sector entities and their service recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires specified financial-sector entities to make an incident notification also to the designated sectoral CSIRT. Provision B separately requires an essential or important entity, where necessary, to inform potentially affected service recipients about the significant cyber threat; thus one event could trigger communications to both a CSIRT and service recipients, creating cumulative notification duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different recipients and different information functions: A concerns reporting an ICT incident to a sectoral CSIRT, while B concerns warning service recipients about a significant cyber threat and possible response measures. Each duty can be performed independently, and nothing in either text suggests that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien nodig stelt de entiteit die ontvangers ook in kennis van de desbetreffende significante cyberdreiging.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident- or activity-related information duties of different entities under separate instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information duties that could be triggered by the same underlying event or activity, but they require communication to different recipients: the notifying authority under A and the entity’s service recipients under B. If a notified body is also an essential or important entity and a significant incident affects service provision, notifying one recipient would not discharge the other duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different actors, triggers, and information: A concerns a notified body’s requested reporting of conformity-assessment and other activities within its notification scope, while B concerns an essential or important entity informing service recipients of significant incidents. Each duty can be performed independently, and the texts do not expressly establish that the same event triggers both.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A notified body that is also an essential or important entity experiences a significant incident affecting the provision of its services, and the incident concerns conformity-assessment activities within the scope of its notification. It must, on request, inform “de aanmeldende autoriteit” about those activities under A and, “onverwijld”, inform “de ontvangers van haar diensten” about the significant incident under B; communicating to either recipient does not communicate to the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten

verdict.shared_subject: Incident- or work-related notifications by potentially overlapping entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an entity to notify its service recipients without delay when a significant incident adversely affects service provision. Provision B requires a cable-maintenance provider to notify the municipal mayor before public-ground works, so a provider could face two notifications concerning the same operational event, to different recipients and on different temporal triggers.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate materially different events and recipients: A concerns significant cybersecurity incidents and service recipients, while B concerns planned cable-maintenance works on public land and the mayor. Even if the same provider is subject to both, the duties are independently satisfiable and neither filing substitutes for the other; ordinarily they are simply cumulative obligations triggered by different facts.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden

verdict.shared_subject: The Minister’s granting of a transition permit for reassigned frequency space
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Article 3.8a requires the Minister to grant a transition permit ex officio to specified permit holders and the person acquiring the new permit. Article 3.18 allows the Minister to refuse a permit where, for example, competition would be significantly restricted or harmful interference is reasonably feared, so one might argue that the mandatory grant leaves no room to refuse a transition permit on those grounds.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can operate cumulatively: Article 3.8a establishes a specific transition-permit mechanism for reassignment, while Article 3.18 states grounds on which a permit may be refused. The text shown does not establish that Article 3.18 applies to, or overrides, the specific ex officio grant under Article 3.8a; moreover, the general grant/refusal relationship within the same instrument is ordinary legislative structure rather than a demonstrated conflict.
verdict.missing_reference: A provision stating whether the refusal grounds in Article 3.18 apply to or override the ex officio transition permits required by Article 3.8a would be needed to establish a conflict.
verdict.decisive_exception: None established; the shown text does not say that Article 3.18 refusal grounds displace the Article 3.8a duty to grant.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister verleent ambtshalve een transitievergunning:

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or submitting reports under EU digital-law instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose reporting-related obligations, and one might argue that a report arising from a peer review could overlap with the annual oversight report. If the same underlying material were used for both, the actor might face different procedural requirements or reporting contexts.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and concern different reports, triggers, recipients, and timing. Provision A concerns peer-review experts submitting peer-review reports to the Cooperation Group and CSIRT network when relevant; Provision B concerns the ESAs submitting an annual report on the application of a section to the European Parliament, Council, and Commission. Each duty can be performed independently, and neither text says that one report substitutes for or conflicts with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verslagen worden voorgelegd aan de samenwerkingsgroep en het CSIRT-netwerk wanneer dat relevant is.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De ETA’s dienen, via het Gemengd Comité en op basis van de voorbereidende werkzaamheden van het oversightforum jaarlijks een verslag in bij het Europees Parlement, de Raad en de Commissie over de toepassing van deze afdeling.

verdict.shared_subject: Melding van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen regelen kennisgeving na dezelfde soort persoonsgegevensinbreuk, maar aan verschillende ontvangers: de verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke, terwijl de aanbieder de betrokken persoon informeert. Bij één incident kunnen dus twee afzonderlijke kennisgevingen met verschillende ontvangers vereist zijn; de ene kennisgeving vervangt de andere niet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen verplichtingen op aan verschillende actoren en richten zich op verschillende ontvangers, zodat iedere actor zijn eigen kennisgeving kan doen zonder de andere verplichting onmogelijk te maken. Er is geen inhoudelijke tegenstelling of onverenigbare termijn: beide kunnen cumulatief worden nageleefd.
verdict.concrete_scenario: Een verwerker ontdekt onverwijld een datalek bij een aanbieder van een openbare elektronische communicatiedienst, waarbij persoonsgegevens waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen hebben voor de persoonlijke levenssfeer van een betrokkene. De verwerker moet de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging informeren, terwijl de aanbieder de betrokkene onverwijld moet informeren; dit zijn twee afzonderlijke kennisgevingen aan verschillende ontvangers, zodat de eerste melding de tweede niet vervangt.
verdict.decisive_exception: Geen beslissende uitzondering is nodig voor de kwalificatie op basis van de getoonde hoofdregels. Wel kan de in de context genoemde uitzondering van art. 11.3a lid 5 de kennisgeving aan de betrokkene uitsluiten wanneer passende technische beschermingsmaatregelen zijn genomen; die uitzondering ziet alleen op de verplichting van de aanbieder en heft de verplichting van de verwerker jegens de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke niet op.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De aanbieder, bedoeld in het eerste lid, stelt degene wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens indien de inbreuk waarschijnlijk ongunstige gevolgen zal hebben voor diens persoonlijke levenssfeer.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both DORA and the Dutch cybersecurity legislation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require reporting after an incident, but they require an interim report under Provision A and a final report under Provision B. The duties also run to different recipient sets: A requires filing with the relevant competent authority, while B requires filing with both the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, so one filing does not clearly discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different report stages and can be performed cumulatively: an entity can submit the DORA interim report after its initial notification and later submit the statutory final report within one month after the Article 27 notification. Provision A’s deadline is to be set under Article 20, while Provision B’s one-month deadline does not expressly prohibit earlier or additional reporting.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also an essential or important entity and suffers one incident covered by both regimes. After its initial notification, it must submit an interim report to the relevant competent authority under Provision A, while it must separately submit the final report required by Provision B to both its CSIRT and competent authority no later than one month after the Article 27 notification. Filing the interim report with the competent authority does not, on the text shown, constitute the required final report to the CSIRT; the entity therefore faces two reporting duties, with different report stages, recipients and potentially overlapping timing.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the cumulative reporting structure on the text shown; the decisive point is that Provision B expressly adds the CSIRT as a recipient and requires a final report, whereas Provision A requires an interim report to the relevant competent authority. The exact DORA deadline remains dependent on Article 20, which is not reproduced.
verdict.evidence_span_a: een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a)
verdict.evidence_span_b: dient uiterlijk één maand na de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een eindverslag in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: ICT- en cyberbeveiligingsrisicobeheer door bepaalde financiële entiteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen raken aan cyberbeveiliging en kunnen voor dezelfde financiële entiteit relevant zijn. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat informatie-uitwisseling onder A gevoelige operationele informatie of dreigingsinformatie kan blootleggen, terwijl B een gedocumenteerd en voortdurend bewaakt ICT-risicobeheerkader verlangt, maar B verbiedt of beperkt die uitwisseling niet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A verplicht de lidstaten slechts om vrijwillige informatie-uitwisseling mogelijk te maken; de betrokken entiteit hoeft dus niet deel te nemen. B verplicht bepaalde entiteiten daarentegen tot het opnemen van relevante operationele conclusies uit tests en incidentanalyses in hun risicobeoordelingsproces, en beide kunnen zonder tegenstrijdigheid worden nageleefd.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op vrijwillige basis onderling relevante informatie over cyberbeveiliging kunnen uitwisselen
verdict.evidence_span_b: in voorkomend geval de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns discussing and, where possible, carrying out a coordinated response to an incident at the request of a CSIRT-network member. Provision B requires a notification by a deadline in a contemplated public offer involving a listed telecommunications party. No actor, action, trigger, recipient, or deadline is shared closely enough to create a concrete collision.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate entirely different matters: A assigns an operational-cooperation task to the CSIRT network, triggered by a member's request concerning an incident; B imposes a notification deadline for a contemplated public offer. Even if an incident happened during such a transaction, performing the coordinated response would not prevent making the separate notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek van een lid van het CSIRT-netwerk, het bespreken en waar mogelijk uitvoeren van een gecoördineerde respons op een incident dat binnen de jurisdictie van die lidstaat is vastgesteld
verdict.evidence_span_b: De melding in het eerste lid wordt gedaan uiterlijk acht weken voor de beoogde datum van uitvoering van dit voornemen. Indien het voornemen betrekking heeft op een openbaar bod op een beursgenoteerde telecommunicatiepartij wordt de melding gedaan uiterlijk gelijktijdig met de aankondiging van een openbaar bod

verdict.shared_subject: Incident response by CSIRTs and administrative or corrective enforcement powers of competent authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A CSIRT must be responsible for incident handling, which includes responding to and recovering from incidents. An authority empowered under Provision B could order the conduct constituting a DORA infringement to cease and not be repeated; if that conduct were incident-handling activity, the order might appear to restrict the CSIRT’s mandated response.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A assigns CSIRTs an incident-handling responsibility, while Provision B grants competent authorities enforcement powers concerning infringements of Regulation 2022/2554. The enforcement power does not itself prohibit incident handling, and the texts do not establish that lawful CSIRT activity constitutes an infringement or that an order under B would target the CSIRT’s statutory responsibility.
verdict.evidence_span_a: zijn verantwoordelijk voor incidentenbehandeling volgens een welbepaald proces
verdict.evidence_span_b: natuurlijke of rechtspersoon bij officieel besluit gelasten de gedraging die inbreuk maakt op deze verordening, te staken en deze gedraging niet te herhalen

verdict.shared_subject: Risk-proportionate security measures for networks and information systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a security-level duty tied to risk, but A requires a level proportionate to the relevant risk while accounting for technology and implementation costs, whereas B requires alignment with the risks and adds a more detailed proportionality assessment including entity size, incident likelihood, severity, and social and economic consequences. One might therefore argue that the applicable security benchmark or proportionality assessment is not identical.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and materially compatible: both require risk-based, proportionate security measures and both expressly require consideration of the state of technology and costs. B supplies additional factors for assessing proportionality; it does not permit a lower level than A or state that compliance with B substitutes for A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De maatregelen garanderen, rekening houdend met de stand van de techniek en de kosten van de tenuitvoerlegging, een passend beveiligingsniveau dat in verhouding staat tot het desbetreffende risico.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De maatregelen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, zorgen voor een beveiligingsniveau van de netwerk- en informatiesystemen dat is afgestemd op de risico’s, bedoeld in het eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: An AI-system provider’s investigation duty after a serious incident and the obligation to take a decision immediately after receiving a notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A serious AI incident may require the provider to conduct an investigation immediately, while the other provision requires a decision immediately after receipt of a notification. If the decision must be made before the investigation can be completed, the provider could face pressure to decide without the information the investigation is meant to establish. However, the texts do not show that the decision-maker and the investigating provider are the same actor, nor that the decision must await or depend on the investigation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different apparent actors and functions: provision A requires an AI provider to investigate a serious incident, whereas provision B requires that a decision be taken immediately after receipt of a notification. Both can be performed concurrently, and nothing in the shown text makes the investigation a prerequisite for, or legally incompatible with, the decision.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Na de melding van een ernstig incident op grond van lid 1 verricht de aanbieder onverwijld het nodige onderzoek in verband met het ernstige incident en het betrokken AI-systeem.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Potentially the same entity involved in high-risk AI testing and subject to NIS2 enforcement
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern consequences surrounding incidents, so one might argue that an entity must account for prior incidents when authorities enforce NIS2 while also immediately reporting serious incidents during real-world AI testing. However, provision A governs how competent authorities assess enforcement measures, whereas provision B imposes an incident-reporting duty on the provider or potential provider; they prescribe different actions and do not conflict.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The entity can comply with both: it can report each serious incident to the national market-surveillance authority and, separately, competent authorities can consider any relevant previous infringements when taking enforcement measures. Nothing in either provision makes reporting a serious incident incompatible with considering prior infringements.
verdict.evidence_span_a: elke relevante eerdere inbreuk door de betrokken entiteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Elk ernstig incident dat tijdens het testen onder reële omstandigheden wordt vastgesteld, wordt gemeld bij de nationale markttoezichtautoriteit overeenkomstig artikel 73.

verdict.shared_subject: Significant incidents affecting the provision of an essential or important entity’s services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: For the same significant incident, provision A requires the entity, where applicable, to notify its service recipients, while provision B requires a report to both the CSIRT and competent authority. These are distinct communications to different recipients, so one filing cannot discharge the other; the entity must make both without delay, with B additionally allowing a 72-hour outer limit where immediate reporting is impossible.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions can be obeyed cumulatively: the entity can promptly notify affected service recipients and separately report to the CSIRT and competent authority. They address different recipients and complementary information flows, rather than imposing incompatible duties or deadlines.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential entity suffers a significant incident that adversely affects service delivery. It must notify its service recipients without delay under A and separately file a report with its CSIRT and competent authority without delay (or within 72 hours if immediate reporting is impossible) under B; reporting to the authorities does not notify the service recipients, and notifying the recipients does not satisfy the authority/CSIRT filing.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 72 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting serious ICT-related incidents by an entity covered by both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same financial entity is also an AI-system provider subject to Article 73, Article 19 requires it to prepare and submit an initial notification and reports to the relevant competent authority, while Article 73 requires a notification to market-surveillance authorities. These are potentially separate filings to different authorities, with Article 73 expressly setting a deadline but the Article 19 deadline being incorporated by reference and not shown here.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with: the entity can prepare the Article 19 notification and reports for its relevant competent authority and separately make the Article 73 notification to the market-surveillance authority. Nothing in the shown text says that one filing substitutes for the other, and the Article 19 provision even contemplates additional reporting to other authorities or CSIRTs.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an AI-system provider experiences one serious incident affecting a high-risk AI system. It must prepare and submit the Article 19 initial notification and reports to the relevant competent authority, while also making the Article 73 notification to the market-surveillance authorities; filing with the relevant competent authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate market-surveillance notification due immediately and no later than 15 days after awareness.
verdict.missing_reference: The exact Article 19 deadlines in Article 20 and the full Article 73 provisions could affect the timing analysis, but they are not needed to establish that the shown duties concern separate recipients and filings.
verdict.decisive_exception: No substitution or single-filing rule is shown. The decisive issue is whether the Article 19 competent authority is the same recipient as the Article 73 market-surveillance authority and whether either regime expressly treats one notification as satisfying the other; the text shown does not establish that.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De in lid 1 bedoelde melding wordt gedaan onmiddellijk nadat de aanbieder een oorzakelijk verband tussen het AI-systeem en het ernstige incident of de redelijke waarschijnlijkheid van een dergelijk verband heeft vastgesteld en in ieder geval uiterlijk 15 dagen nadat de aanbieder of, in voorkomend geval, de gebruiksverantwoordelijke zich bewust wordt van het ernstige incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident/vulnerability information handled by designated CSIRT or contact-point authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern follow-up or information handling relating to cyber vulnerabilities or incidents, so the same cross-border event might involve a vulnerability report under A and an incident notification under B. However, A imposes a careful-follow-up duty on the coordinating CSIRT, while B requires the central contact point to inform the CSIRT and competent authority; the provisions do not require incompatible conduct or establish different mandatory reports by the same actor.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties apply to different actors and are triggered by different facts: A concerns the coordinating CSIRT’s follow-up to a reported vulnerability, whereas B concerns information received from another Member State’s central contact point showing effects on services of an essential or important entity in the Netherlands. The coordinating CSIRT can provide careful follow-up while the central contact point separately informs the relevant CSIRT and authority.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het als coördinator aangewezen CSIRT ziet erop toe dat zorgvuldige follow-up wordt gegeven aan de gemelde kwetsbaarheid
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt het centrale contactpunt het betrokken CSIRT en de betrokken bevoegde autoriteit daarvan op de hoogte

verdict.shared_subject: Informatieverplichtingen van verschillende entiteiten aan verschillende ontvangers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen leggen informatieverplichtingen op, maar aan verschillende actoren en over verschillende onderwerpen: aangemelde instanties melden omstandigheden aan de aanmeldende autoriteit, terwijl essentiële of belangrijke entiteiten ontvangers van hun diensten informeren over significante cyberdreigingen. In een uitzonderlijk feitencomplex kan dezelfde gebeurtenis beide verplichtingen activeren, maar de teksten maken die gebeurtenis, actorencombinatie of rapportage-overlap niet concreet.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De verplichtingen zijn cumulatief noch concurrerend: zij gelden voor verschillende actoren, hebben verschillende triggers en zijn gericht aan verschillende ontvangers. Een melding aan de aanmeldende autoriteit vervangt geen informatie aan dienstontvangers, maar er is ook geen concrete situatie in de getoonde teksten waarin één actor beide afzonderlijke plichten moet vervullen.
verdict.evidence_span_a: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien nodig stelt de entiteit die ontvangers ook in kennis van de desbetreffende significante cyberdreiging.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern authorities taking action after regulatory information or notification, so one might initially suspect overlapping institutional procedures. However, provision A concerns financial-sector authorities responding to serious ICT incidents, while provision B concerns the legal effect of a market-surveillance authority’s provisional AI measure and its objection period; neither prescribes an incompatible action, deadline, or recipient for the same actor.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different functions on different authorities in different procedures. A requires, where appropriate, competent authorities to take necessary measures to protect immediate financial-system stability; B provides that a provisional AI measure is deemed justified after three months, or thirty days for certain prohibited AI practices, absent an objection, while preserving the operator’s procedural rights. Both can operate simultaneously without either discharging or preventing the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Op basis van die kennisgeving nemen de bevoegde autoriteiten, in voorkomend geval, alle nodige maatregelen om de onmiddellijke stabiliteit van het financiële systeem te beschermen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien er binnen drie maanden na ontvangst van de in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving door een markttoezichtautoriteit van een lidstaat of door de Commissie geen bezwaar tegen een voorlopige maatregel van een markttoezichtautoriteit van een andere lidstaat is ingediend, wordt die maatregel geacht gerechtvaardigd te zijn.

verdict.shared_subject: The duty to provide cooperation under two separate provisions of BWBR0009950.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a cooperation duty on potentially overlapping telecommunications actors or institutions. If one actor falls within both categories and receives simultaneous instructions, the provisions could appear to require cooperation in two contexts, potentially creating practical prioritisation issues.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different triggers and recipients: provision A applies when Article 31 of the War Act for the Netherlands is applied and requires cooperation with the military authority, while provision B concerns giving effect to a suspension under Article 14a.7 and cooperation with a listed involved party. The texts do not make the duties mutually exclusive; an actor can comply with both, and merely having separate cooperation obligations is not a conflict.

verdict.evidence_span_b: verleent medewerking aan een beursgenoteerde betrokken partij bij het gevolg geven aan de schorsing, bedoeld in artikel 14a.7, eerste lid.

verdict.shared_subject: Documentatie- en verantwoordingsverplichtingen rond verwerking door hoog-risico-AI-systemen

Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat de DPIA en de AI-logbewaarplicht overlappende documentatie- of verantwoordingslasten veroorzaken, zonder dat uit de getoonde tekst blijkt of één document of registratie de andere vervangt.

Beide kunnen volledig en cumulatief worden nageleefd; geen van beide verbiedt of vervangt de andere.

verdict.shared_subject: Significante cyberdreigingen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to notify potentially affected service recipients of the significant cyberthreat itself. Provision B concerns a financial entity voluntarily reporting such a threat to a competent authority, with possible onward transmission to other authorities; the recipients and legal triggers therefore differ, so one communication would not ordinarily discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can readily be complied with cumulatively: an entity can notify affected service recipients under A and, if it voluntarily chooses to report under B, separately notify the competent authority. Provision B is expressly voluntary, so an entity that does not opt into that reporting faces no conflict with A.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Financiële entiteiten kunnen significante cyberdreigingen op vrijwillige basis melden aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a significant incident affecting the provision of a trust service
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a final report no later than one month after the incident report, while provision B requires an incident notification within 24 hours to both the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority. For an affected trust-service provider, these appear to be different filings with different content and timing, so the 24-hour notification would not itself discharge A’s later final-report duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can both be performed: the entity can submit B’s 24-hour notification and later submit A’s final report within one month after the incident report. B’s earlier deadline does not prohibit or replace A’s later report, and the texts do not expressly state that the filings are mutually exclusive.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification duties triggered by different events and addressed to different recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use prompt-notification language and could, in a broad factual setting, involve the same operator. However, Provision A concerns a personal-data breach and requires the processor to inform the controller, while Provision B concerns cable-maintenance work on public land and requires notification to the municipal mayor or authorised official; they are not two reports of the same triggering event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can readily be complied with cumulatively because their triggers, recipients, and subject matter differ. A processor can notify the controller of a personal-data breach without that satisfying or replacing the separate prior notification concerning cable-maintenance work on public land, and vice versa; there is no conflict or unresolved dual-reporting burden for one event.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or notifying authorities about events relevant to regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an essential or important entity to report each significant incident immediately to its CSIRT or, where applicable, its competent authority. Provision B separately requires a notified body to inform its notifying authority about circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of its notification; if the same event qualifies both as a significant incident and as such a circumstance, the duties concern different recipients and are not discharged by one filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions apply to different regulated actors and triggers: A concerns essential or important entities and significant incidents, while B concerns notified conformity-assessment bodies and circumstances affecting notification. On the texts shown, there is no established fact pattern in which the same actor and event satisfy both triggers, so the provisions may simply operate independently.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A notified body that is also an essential or important entity suffers a cyber incident that significantly affects its services and also changes the scope or conditions of its notification. It must report the significant incident “bij zijn CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, zijn bevoegde autoriteit” “onverwijld” under A, and separately notify “de aanmeldende autoriteit” under B; filing with one recipient does not discharge the other duty.

verdict.shared_subject: A high-risk AI system involving personal-data processing and its provider/controller
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions may apply to the same project, but they impose different obligations on potentially different actors and concern different compliance steps: prior consultation with a data-protection supervisory authority under GDPR versus affixing a CE marking under the AI Act. Nothing in either text makes CE marking a substitute for consultation or makes consultation incompatible with CE marking.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations are cumulative and readily satisfiable: the relevant controller can consult the supervisory authority before processing, while the provider can affix the CE marking after the applicable conformity requirements are met. The provisions address different duties, triggers, and institutional functions, with no prohibition or incompatible timing stated.

verdict.evidence_span_b: brengen de CE-markering aan op het AI-systeem met een hoog risico

verdict.shared_subject: Deadlines and procedures following a notification
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern action after a notification, but they impose duties on different authorities and address different decisions: the market-surveillance authority must follow Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 procedures, while the Minister decides whether to impose a prohibition within eight weeks, subject to extensions and suspensions. Nothing shown requires the same actor to perform incompatible acts or establishes competing deadlines for one filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are readily cumulative: the market-surveillance authority can take measures and follow its notification procedures, while the Minister separately decides on a telecommunications-sector prohibition within the applicable statutory period. They concern different authorities, decisions, and regulatory regimes, so compliance with one does not prevent compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De markttoezichtautoriteit neemt passende maatregelen, zoals bedoeld in artikel 19 van Verordening (EU) 2019/1020, binnen zeven dagen na de datum waarop zij de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving heeft ontvangen, en volgt de kennisgevingsprocedures waarin die verordening voorziet.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister beslist binnen acht weken na ontvangst van de melding of een verbod op grond van artikel 14a.4, eerste lid, wordt opgelegd.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity and ICT-risk management duties of regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require governance or operational measures addressing security risks and incidents, but they apply to different regulatory populations and impose different kinds of duties. Provision A concerns approval, oversight and accountability by governing bodies of essential and important entities, whereas Provision B concerns the simplified ICT-risk-management framework of specified financial entities.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can readily be satisfied together: a governing body can approve and oversee cybersecurity-risk measures under Provision A while the relevant financial entity separately identifies ICT risks, detects anomalies and handles incidents quickly under Provision B. Neither provision requires conduct that the other prohibits, and the different actors and scopes do not themselves create tension.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/cybersecurity incident management involving an entity potentially subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A allows a competent authority to order an essential entity to remedy identified shortcomings or infringements of the NIS2 Directive. Provision B requires a financial entity to analyse the frequency, types, scale and evolution of ICT-related incidents and cyberattacks. One might argue that an enforcement order could require remedial action that affects how the entity allocates resources to the incident-analysis duty, creating competing operational demands.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable norms: B requires the financial entity to perform incident analysis, while A concerns the enforcement powers that Member States must give competent authorities against essential entities. Nothing in A prohibits the analysis required by B, and nothing in B prevents compliance with an enforcement order. The provisions also have different actors and regulatory functions, without any stated incompatible deadline, content, or priority rule.

verdict.shared_subject: Voortgangsverslag en eindverslag bij een voortduring van hetzelfde incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen zien op een incident dat nog voortduurt wanneer een eindverslag aan de orde is, maar A verplicht op dat moment een voortgangsverslag in en B formuleert daarnaast een verplichting om binnen één maand na afhandeling een eindverslag in te dienen. Als dit als twee zelfstandige rapportageplichten wordt gelezen, moet dezelfde entiteit beide stukken indienen; de teksten tonen echter geen verschillende ontvangers of andere zelfstandige rapportageklokken die een dual-reportingconflict opleveren.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen zijn juist complementair: het voortgangsverslag wordt tijdens het nog lopende incident ingediend, waarna het eindverslag binnen één maand na afhandeling volgt. B bevestigt daarmee de vervolgstap die A eveneens voorschrijft, zodat naleving van beide cumulatieve verplichtingen mogelijk is en geen plicht de andere uitsluit.

verdict.shared_subject: Technical and organisational measures for GDPR-compliant processing and security of processing
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose risk-based technical and organisational measures on a controller, and Article 32 additionally specifies security capabilities and testing. One might argue that the controller faces two potentially different benchmarks for the same measures: overall compliance under Article 24 versus a risk-appropriate security level under Article 32.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are cumulative and expressly compatible: Article 24 concerns measures ensuring and demonstrating compliance with the Regulation generally, while Article 32 concerns the narrower objective of security of processing and lists measures that may be appropriate. A controller can satisfy both by implementing measures that address overall compliance and the specified security requirements; neither provision says that compliance with one substitutes for the other.
