verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations potentially applying to the same organisation or provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a provider of a general-purpose AI model meeting the specified condition to notify the Commission within two weeks. Provision B separately requires an essential or important entity to report every significant incident, so a single organisation could potentially be subject to both duties and need to make two reports concerning the same event or model-related incident.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers and regulated actors: A concerns a provider and a condition relating to a general-purpose AI model, while B concerns an essential or important entity and a significant incident. The texts shown do not establish that the same event triggers both duties, that the same actor falls within both categories, or that B's incident report is addressed to a different recipient; therefore the provisions can be complied with independently and no concrete dual-reporting conflict is established.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions needed to determine whether the duties overlap are not shown: Article 51(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, which defines the condition triggering A; Articles 26–29 of BWBR0052872, which define the significant-incident reporting procedure, including the recipient and deadline; and the provisions identifying essential or important entities and the competent recipient under B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit meldt overeenkomstig de artikelen 26 tot en met 29 ieder significant incident.

verdict.shared_subject: A third-party ICT service provider that is also an essential or important entity and experiences a significant incident while designated as critical
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the entity to notify its service recipients without delay of a significant incident adversely affecting service provision. Provision B requires the critical ICT provider to notify its financial-entity customers of its critical designation and the start date of oversight; if those financial entities are also the relevant service recipients, the same customers receive two legally distinct notifications, but the provisions do not specify whether one notice can satisfy both or how their content and timing interact.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different triggering events and different information: A is triggered by a significant incident and requires notice to service recipients, whereas B is triggered by designation as critical and requires notice of that designation and the oversight start date to financial entities. They can readily be made cumulatively, with the provider sending an incident notice under A and a designation/oversight notice under B; neither provision forbids the other or makes one notice legally sufficient for both.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten
verdict.evidence_span_b: De derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten stelt de financiële entiteiten waaraan hij diensten verleent in kennis van zijn aanwijzing als cruciaal.

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative sanctions and corrective measures in relation to voluntary notifications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A protects an entity that makes a voluntary notification from being subjected to additional obligations merely because it notified. Provision B requires Member States to establish effective, proportionate and deterrent administrative sanctions and corrective measures for infringements of the Regulation; if a voluntary notifier is sanctioned or subjected to a corrective measure solely because of the notification, that could appear to impose an additional measure contrary to A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different things: A prohibits additional obligations caused by the voluntary notification itself, while B requires sanctions and corrective measures for infringements of the Regulation. A sanction based on an underlying infringement, rather than on the decision to notify, can satisfy B without violating A; moreover, A expressly preserves criminal-law prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution.
verdict.decisive_exception: Any apparent conflict would depend on whether a measure is imposed because the entity voluntarily notified or instead because it committed an infringement. The text of B does not require sanctions for voluntary notification itself, and A's criminal-law reservation is also relevant.
verdict.evidence_span_a: mag vrijwillige melding er niet toe leiden dat de meldende entiteit bijkomende verplichtingen worden opgelegd waaraan zij niet onderworpen zou zijn geweest indien zij de melding niet had ingediend
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen de lidstaten regels vast voor de invoering van passende administratieve strafmaatregelen en corrigerende maatregelen voor inbreuken op deze verordening, en waarborgen zij de daadwerkelijke uitvoering van deze maatregelen

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident oversight and response involving essential entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, when taking enforcement measures, to consider the circumstances of each individual case and the seriousness of the infringement. Provision B requires the CSIRT, where applicable, to respond to incidents and provide assistance, so one might argue that incident response and enforcement assessment could pull institutional attention in different directions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulatively satisfiable duties on different actors and at different stages. Provision A governs how competent authorities assess and enforce infringements, while Provision B assigns the CSIRT an incident-response and assistance function; nothing in either text makes CSIRT assistance incompatible with case-specific enforcement assessment.

Provision A applies expressly to banks, trading venues, central securities depositories and central counterparties and concerns notifications under a specified regulation, including a voluntary notification. Provision B applies to an essential or important entity in the manufacturing sector and concerns an interim report requested in connection with a notification under article 27. The shown texts therefore support separate, potentially non-overlapping regimes, not an established dual-reporting conflict.

verdict.shared_subject: An aanbieder that is both subject to the AI Act notification duty and the personal-data-breach notification duty
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require prompt notification by an aanbieder, but they concern different triggering events and recipients: A requires notification to the Commission concerning an AI model satisfying the Article 51 condition, while B requires notification to the affected person concerning a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect that person's privacy. If one event satisfies both triggers, the notifications are separate and notification to one recipient cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be cumulatively satisfied because they have different triggers, recipients, and subject matter. A requires notification to the Commission within two weeks and supporting information about the AI-model condition; B requires immediate notification to the affected data subject about a qualifying personal-data breach, so neither duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An aanbieder places a general-purpose AI model on the market, thereby satisfying the Article 51 condition, and the model simultaneously causes a personal-data breach likely to have adverse effects on an identifiable person's privacy. The aanbieder must notify the Commission under A within two weeks and notify the affected person immediately under B; notifying one recipient does not satisfy the separate duty owed to the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting overlap. The relevant issue is that the duties are owed to different recipients; any exception to B in the related provisions (such as appropriate encryption) could remove B for a particular case, but no such exception is established for the concrete scenario.

verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity discovers a significant ICT-related incident that has major adverse effects on systems supporting critical or important functions and affects clients' financial interests. verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify Onze Minister immediately of a security or integrity breach or misuse involving its own electronic service. Provision B separately requires an essentiële or belangrijke entiteit, in the context of the Article 27 notification, to submit an interim report on relevant updates when requested by its CSIRT or competent authority; the recipients and the nature of the filing differ, so one communication may not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be obeyed: the entity can make the immediate notification required by A and, if requested, submit the interim update required by B. Provision B is conditional on a request and concerns updates in an Article 27 reporting process, while A concerns immediate notification of specified incidents; nothing in either text forbids or substitutes for compliance with the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A aangewezen organisatie that is also an essentiële entiteit suffers a security breach in its own electronic service. It must notify Onze Minister “onverwijld” under A, and, in the Article 27 reporting process, must separately submit an interim report on relevant updates if its CSIRT or competent authority requests one under B. The two duties concern different communications and potentially different recipients—Onze Minister versus the entity’s CSIRT or bevoegde autoriteit—so filing the first does not, on the texts shown, discharge the second.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient in het kader van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, op verzoek van haar CSIRT of haar bevoegde autoriteit een tussentijds verslag in over relevante updates van de situatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related duties of an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated periodically and when serious ICT-related incidents occur, while Provision B requires immediate notification of service recipients about significant incidents adversely affecting service provision. A serious incident could therefore trigger both an internal/framework evaluation and an external notification, creating different incident-related burdens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties rather than conflicting commands: A concerns documenting and evaluating the risk-management framework, with an evaluation report submitted to the competent authority only on request; B concerns promptly informing service recipients of qualifying significant incidents. Nothing in A forbids or substitutes for the notification required by B, and A does not require a separate filing on every incident.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

If the same actor and event somehow fell within both regimes, the reports would be to different authorities and would not obviously substitute for one another.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different actors, activities, triggers, and recipients. Provision A applies to a notified conformity-assessment body reporting, on request, activities within its notification scope; provision B applies to a provider carrying out cable-maintenance work on public land, reporting before the work. Nothing in either text forbids or discharges the other duty, and the texts do not establish a shared triggering event.

If the same provider is subject to both duties, the filings have different subject matter, recipients, and triggers, so one filing would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate distinct events: A concerns a significant incident and requires an incident report or interim report only on request, whereas B concerns notification that a general-purpose AI model satisfies a specified condition. Nothing in the texts makes the AI-model notification an incident report or makes the incident-reporting duty applicable to the model notification.

The financial entity can comply with its internal-channel duty while ENISA independently maintains its database; neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggering events, subjects, recipients, and information: A concerns planned cable-maintenance work on public land and notification to the municipal mayor or authorised official; B concerns an ongoing incident and a progress report, followed by a final report, with no recipient specified in the text. Nothing in either provision says that one report substitutes for the other, but neither provision establishes a single triggering event requiring both filings.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident final reporting by entities under the NIS2-related regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require a final report after an incident, but Provision A’s selected norm is triggered only when the CSIRT or competent authority requests an interim report, whereas Provision B requires a final report one month after the Article 27 notification. If the same entity and incident fall under both regimes, the provisions could appear to impose different reporting sequences and reference points.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The selected norm in Provision A does not itself impose a final-report duty: it requires an interim report only upon request. Provision B separately requires a final report to both the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority, so the duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction; the extracted absence of an A recipient and deadline confirms that A does not establish a second final filing or competing clock.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving electronic services or entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same incident, but they impose different reporting duties with different content and timing. Provision A requires immediate notification to Onze Minister, while provision B requires a progress report during a continuing incident and a final report within one month after it is resolved; the texts do not say that either report substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: an entity can immediately notify Onze Minister under A and later submit the progress or final report required by B. There is no direct contradiction, and B's report is not necessarily a substitute for A's notification because the provisions concern different reporting functions and A expressly requires all necessary information.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation subject to both instruments suffers a security breach that remains ongoing when the final report under B would otherwise be due. It must notify Onze Minister immediately under A, providing all necessary information, and must also submit a progress report at that time under B and a final report within one month after the incident is resolved; filing the immediate notification with Onze Minister does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate progress/final-report duty.

Het bestuursorgaan of de aangewezen organisatie verstrekt daarbij alle benodigde informatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related ICT/security governance and reporting by an organisation subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same serious security or integrity incident. Provision A requires the ICT-risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated and, on request, its evaluation report to be submitted to the competent authority, while Provision B requires immediate notification with all necessary information to the Minister; the texts identify different recipients and do not say that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are substantively different and can be performed cumulatively: A concerns documenting and evaluating the risk-management framework, with a report submitted only if requested, whereas B concerns immediate incident notification. Nothing in either text forbids the other filing or makes the duties mutually exclusive.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation suffers a serious breach of the security of its own electronic service. It must immediately notify the Minister of the breach and provide all necessary information under B, while it must document and evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework under A and, if the competent authority requests the evaluation report, submit that report to the competent authority. The Minister and the competent authority are distinct recipients, and the immediate notification does not itself constitute submission of the requested evaluation report.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or notification duties under DORA and the AI Act
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information duties, and a third-party ICT service provider could conceivably also perform notified conformity-assessment activities, creating potentially overlapping communications. However, the texts identify different actors, recipients, and triggering subject matter: Provision A concerns the designation of a critical ICT third-party provider and notification through the Joint Committee, while Provision B concerns notified conformity-assessment bodies reporting activities to the notifying authority on request.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively without contradiction. Provision A requires the ESAs to notify the critical ICT third-party provider via the Joint Committee, whereas Provision B requires notified bodies to inform the notifying authority, upon request, about conformity-assessment activities; neither duty forbids or substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risk-management documentation/evaluation and incident-related reporting by an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can involve the same serious ICT-related incident and require information to be supplied to an authority. A could require submission of an evaluation report to the competent authority, while B could separately require an interim report on relevant updates to the CSIRT or competent authority, potentially creating different documents or requests.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties with different triggers and objects: A concerns documenting, evaluating and continuously improving the ICT-risk-management framework, with an evaluation report submitted on request; B concerns an interim report on relevant situation updates within the reporting process under Article 27(1), submitted on request of the CSIRT or competent authority. Nothing in the texts says that one report substitutes for the other, but neither text establishes that the same event necessarily triggers both duties or that two separate filings must be made.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents affecting electronic services or network-and-information systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify Onze Minister immediately of a security or integrity breach, misuse, or improper use. Provision B separately requires an essentiële or belangrijke entiteit to report every significant incident under Articles 26–29; if the same actor and event fall under both regimes, the texts do not state that the Article 25 report is made to Onze Minister or that it discharges the immediate notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: an actor can notify Onze Minister immediately under A and make the report required by B under Articles 26–29. Provision B specifies neither recipient nor deadline in the text shown, so the extracts do not establish that the duties require different filings, recipients, or incompatible clocks.
verdict.missing_reference: BWBR0052872 Articles 26–29, which determine the recipient, timing, and reporting procedure for the Article 25 significant-incident report; the definitions or scope provisions establishing whether the same actor is both a bestuursorgaan/aangewezen organisatie and an essentiële/belangrijke entiteit would also be relevant.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the Article 25 report under Articles 26–29 is the same filing as, or legally discharges, the immediate notification to Onze Minister under Article 18.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident response and cooperation
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern cooperation or assistance in relation to cyber incidents. One could argue that the CSIRT's duty to respond to incidents and provide assistance might overlap with the authorities', ETAs' and ECB's duty to coordinate supervision and exchange information, potentially raising questions about which body leads or how responsibilities are divided.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and serve complementary functions: Article 49 requires competent authorities, the ETAs and the ECB to cooperate, exchange information and coordinate supervision, while Article 16 assigns the CSIRT operational monitoring, incident response and assistance tasks. Nothing in either text requires incompatible conduct, and the CSIRT's incident-response duty can be performed alongside institutional cooperation and information exchange.

Neither provision requires or forbids conduct that would prevent compliance with the other, and Provision A does not itself impose a reporting duty on ENISA or regulate vulnerability disclosure.

The texts shown do not establish that the same event triggers both duties, nor do they identify incompatible deadlines or recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are independently satisfiable and address different subjects. Those duties concern different regulatory triggers and recipients, and neither text says that one notification substitutes for the other.

Provision A concerns serious ICT-related incidents of financial entities, while provision B concerns an AI model for general purposes meeting the condition in Article 51(1)(a). They can therefore be complied with cumulatively if both triggers occur, and no incompatible deadline or content is shown.

Nothing in B requires the ACM to identify vulnerability reporters or to disclose their identities, and nothing in A prohibits the ACM from maintaining its separate register.

Provision B merely empowers the competent authority to provide feedback or discuss corrective measures with the financial entity; it does not prohibit, condition, or replace the forwarding duty.

The authority can provide feedback while the central contact point separately performs any requested forwarding, so both can be complied with cumulatively.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory cooperation and national market-surveillance procedures concerning AI or financial-sector oversight
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, the ESAs and the ECB to cooperate, exchange information and closely coordinate supervision. Provision B establishes a three-month, or in certain cases thirty-day, period in which another market-surveillance authority or the Commission may object to a provisional measure; coordination under A could create practical questions about how authorities exchange information or coordinate during that period.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties on different regulatory actors and address different procedures. A requires inter-authority cooperation in carrying out tasks under Articles 47–54, while B determines when a provisional market-surveillance measure is deemed justified if no objection is filed; nothing in B prohibits the cooperation or information exchange required by A, and nothing in A changes B’s objection deadlines.

verdict.shared_subject: Voluntary reporting by an entity that is also a financial entity subject to DORA reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If a financial entity voluntarily reports information under Article 30 of Directive (EU) 2022/2555, Article 30 prohibits that voluntary report from causing additional obligations that would not otherwise apply. Article 19 of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 allows Member States to require financial entities to provide the same Article 19 incident reports also to NIS2 authorities or CSIRTs, which could appear to turn the voluntary NIS2 submission into an additional reporting obligation.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be satisfied together because Article 19 concerns reports that financial entities must already prepare and submit under DORA for serious ICT-related incidents; the possible additional transmission to NIS2 authorities or CSIRTs is a Member-State competence, not necessarily an obligation triggered by the voluntary NIS2 report. Moreover, Article 30 expressly protects against additional obligations caused by voluntary reporting, so the DORA reporting duty can remain independently applicable without being imposed because of the voluntary submission.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 30 itself contains an exception for the prevention, investigation, detection and prosecution of criminal offences, but no criminal-law facts are presented. More importantly, the text does not establish that the Article 19 transmission is imposed because the entity made the voluntary NIS2 report rather than because it is a financial entity subject to the DORA regime.

verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts identify different triggers, recipients, and objects: A concerns periodic and incident-related documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, with a report submitted to the competent authority only upon request; B concerns notification to the Commission when a general-purpose AI model meets a specified condition, including information proving that condition. Nothing states that the B notification replaces A's requested evaluation report, but the duties can be performed cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een evaluatieverslag van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt op verzoek bij de bevoegde autoriteit ingediend.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Information duties concerning ICT-service providers or entities and their service recipients
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require communications by an entity connected with ICT or digital services, and a critical ICT third-party provider may also have financial entities as its service recipients. If the same real-world event involved both a critical designation/oversight start and a significant cyberthreat, the communications could concern overlapping recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different actors, triggered by different facts and addressed to different recipients. Provision A requires the ESAs, via the Joint Committee, to notify the critical ICT third-party provider of its designation and oversight start date; Provision B requires an essential or important entity to notify its service recipients about measures and, where necessary, the significant cyberthreat. Neither communication discharges the other, but there is no conflict or dual-reporting event shown.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nadat een derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten als cruciaal is aangewezen, stellen de ETA’s de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten via het Gemengd Comité in kennis van die aanwijzing alsook van de aanvangsdatum vanaf wanneer zij daadwerkelijk aan oversightactiviteiten zullen worden onderworpen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging. Indien nodig stelt de entiteit die ontvangers ook in kennis van de desbetreffende significante cyberdreiging.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory enforcement involving entities/operators of AI or cybersecurity systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A gives a competent authority power to order an entity to stop conduct violating the NIS2 Directive and refrain from repeating it. Provision B establishes a three-month, or in a specified case thirty-day, period during which another authority or the Commission may object to a provisional measure; one might argue that this procedural period could delay or constrain immediate enforcement action concerning the same operator or system.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different acts by different authorities: A concerns the substantive enforcement competence of authorities toward important entities, while B concerns when a provisional market-surveillance measure is deemed justified after notification and objection. Nothing in B prohibits, delays, or otherwise limits an authority from exercising A's power, and the texts do not establish that the same measure, authority, trigger, or recipient is involved.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de betrokken entiteiten te gelasten een einde te maken aan gedragingen die inbreuk maken op deze richtlijn en af te zien van herhaling van die gedragingen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien er binnen drie maanden na ontvangst van de in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving door een markttoezichtautoriteit van een lidstaat of door de Commissie geen bezwaar tegen een voorlopige maatregel van een markttoezichtautoriteit van een andere lidstaat is ingediend, wordt die maatregel geacht gerechtvaardigd te zijn.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations of potentially overlapping actors
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a mandatory notification duty, and a financial entity that is also a cable provider could face a serious ICT incident during cable-maintenance work on public land. It would then have to make an initial notification to the relevant competent authority within the Article 20 deadlines and a separate prior-work notification to the municipal mayor or authorised official; neither filing appears to discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different triggering events and different subject matters: Article 19 concerns serious ICT-related incidents, while Article 5.6 concerns cable-maintenance work on public land. Even if the same actor is subject to both, the obligations can be cumulatively satisfied because they require different information, recipients and timing rather than incompatible conduct.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that also provides cable-maintenance services schedules maintenance on public land and, before the work, experiences a serious ICT-related incident. It must separately notify the mayor or authorised municipal official “voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden” and submit the Article 19 initial notification “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” within the Article 20 deadline; notifying one recipient does not satisfy the other duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a:
Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in:

a) een eerste kennisgeving;
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting by regulated entities or bodies to authorities under separate digital-law regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose information or reporting duties that could concern the same underlying compliance or security situation. If a notified conformity-assessment body under Provision A were also an essential or important entity under Provision B, the recipients differ: A requires notice to the notifying authority, while B requires an interim report to its CSIRT or competent authority, so one filing would not obviously discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different actors and different triggers: A concerns a notified conformity-assessment body's circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of its notification, whereas B concerns an essential or important entity's interim report on relevant updates, submitted only on request in the context of an Article 27 notification. Nothing in the texts establishes that the same actor or event must satisfy both duties, or that an A-type circumstance is a B-type relevant update.
verdict.evidence_span_a: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient in het kader van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, op verzoek van haar CSIRT of haar bevoegde autoriteit een tussentijds verslag in over relevante updates van de situatie.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires documentation, evaluation, continuous improvement, and submission of an evaluation report to the competent authority on request. Provision B requires a decision immediately after receipt of a notification, but it does not state that the decision concerns the ICT-risk-management framework, that it is a report, or that it is sent to the competent authority; therefore no concrete overlap or conflicting obligation is established.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different apparent subject matters: A concerns an ICT-risk-management framework and, when requested, an evaluation report to the competent authority, while B concerns taking a decision immediately after receiving a notification. Even if the same actor is involved, both duties can be performed independently, and B's immediate decision does not discharge A's separately required report.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een evaluatieverslag van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt op verzoek bij de bevoegde autoriteit ingediend.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting/documentation duties following different events involving AI systems and personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a processor to inform the controller without undue delay after learning of a personal-data breach, while Provision B requires a deployer to notify the market-surveillance authority of the results of a fundamental-rights impact assessment and submit a completed template. If the same organisation is both processor and deployer, the duties concern different triggering events, recipients and information, so one filing would not obviously satisfy the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish one common triggering event: A is triggered by knowledge of a personal-data breach, whereas B is triggered once a specified fundamental-rights impact assessment has been carried out. They also impose duties on different roles and require different communications; each can be performed independently, and the texts do not create incompatible deadlines or content requirements.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting significant or serious ICT-related incidents by entities subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a financial entity to report a serious ICT-related incident to the relevant competent authority, while Provision B requires an essential or important entity to give an early warning about a significant incident to both its CSIRT and its competent authority within 24 hours. If the same entity and incident fall within both provisions, the CSIRT filing under B is an additional recipient and is not discharged by reporting to A's relevant competent authority; the texts also do not establish that the reports are the same filing or that A's timing satisfies B's 24-hour deadline.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can report to A's relevant competent authority and separately send B's early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Provision A does not prohibit or make unnecessary the additional B notification, and Provision B does not state that its early warning replaces A's report.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity that is also an essential or important entity discovers an incident that qualifies both as a serious ICT-related incident under Provision A and as a significant incident under Provision B. It must report under A to the relevant competent authority and, under B, give an early warning within 24 hours to both its CSIRT and its competent authority; reporting to the competent authority under A does not itself make the separate CSIRT notification required by B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of an incident and the subsequent decision
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A obliges a financial entity to report serious ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority, while provision B requires that “the decision” be taken immediately after receipt of a notification. If provision B applied to the receiving authority’s handling of A’s report, the authority would face an immediate decision duty in addition to the entity’s reporting duty, but B does not identify the recipient, the decision, or any connection to serious ICT incidents.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different apparent subjects and concern different acts: A concerns a financial entity’s reporting to a competent authority, whereas B concerns taking a decision after receiving a notification. Nothing in the texts establishes that B concerns the same notification, the same actor, or a separate filing obligation, and B does not require a second report.
verdict.missing_reference: A provision identifying the actor, decision, and notification covered by BWBR0009950 art. 5.6, and linking it to serious ICT-incident reports under 32022R2554 art. 19, would be needed to establish any interaction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Institutional handling and cooperation concerning cybersecurity information and incident reports
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the competent authorities, the ETAs and the ECB to cooperate and exchange information closely in carrying out their supervisory tasks. Provision B requires the CSIRT to process voluntary reports, while allowing it to prioritise mandatory reports; one might argue that this prioritisation could delay information exchange or cooperation expected under A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different institutional actors and address different functions: A governs inter-authority cooperation and supervisory coordination, whereas B governs the CSIRT’s processing and prioritisation of voluntary reports. Nothing in B forbids cooperation or information exchange, and nothing in A requires the authorities to process voluntary CSIRT reports on a particular timetable or in a particular manner.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteiten, de ETA’s en de ECB werken onderling nauw samen en wisselen informatie uit om hun taken overeenkomstig de artikelen 47 tot en met 54 te verrichten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verwerkt de vrijwillige meldingen, bedoeld in het eerste lid, overeenkomstig de in artikel 36 omschreven procedure.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations by an entity/provider in connection with cable-maintenance work and significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use reporting-related language and could, in a broad factual setting, apply to the same organisation. If cable-maintenance work itself constituted a significant incident, the organisation might have to make the municipal advance notification under A while also making the early warning described in B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggering events and different content. A requires an advance notification to the mayor or authorised municipal official before cable-maintenance work on public land; B requires an entity's early warning to include specified incident information and the responsible reporting officer's contact details. Nothing in either text makes one filing substitute for the other, and B does not itself impose a separate recipient or deadline in the excerpt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar.
verdict.evidence_span_b: verstrekt de entiteit de contactgegevens van de functionaris die verantwoordelijk is voor de melding.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident involving both personal data and network or information systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident may also be a personal-data breach, requiring the entity to provide the data subject with a clear description and specified information while, on request, submitting an interim report to the CSIRT or competent authority. The reports may concern overlapping incident facts, but the provisions do not prescribe incompatible content, deadlines, or recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and directed to different recipients: Article 34 requires communication to the affected data subject, whereas the selected Article 23 norm requires an interim report to the CSIRT or competent authority only upon request. An entity can provide both communications, tailoring each to its recipient; neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde mededeling aan de betrokkene bevat een omschrijving, in duidelijke en eenvoudige taal, van de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens en ten minste de in artikel 33, lid 3, onder b), c) en d), bedoelde gegevens en maatregelen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: c) op verzoek van het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit, een tussentijds verslag indienen over relevante updates van de situatie;

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related ICT governance and reporting by an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the ICT risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated periodically and when serious ICT-related incidents occur, while Provision B requires an early warning about a significant incident to be given to both the entity’s CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. A serious/significant incident could therefore trigger both an internal/framework evaluation duty and an external early-warning duty, creating additional compliance work.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, independently satisfiable duties: A concerns documenting and evaluating an ICT risk-management framework, with no reporting recipient or deadline extracted, whereas B concerns an early-warning communication to two specified recipients within 24 hours. Nothing in A forbids or substitutes for B, and the absence of a reporting duty in A means there are not two filings for the same event.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Obligations concerning ICT/network security measures and incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern security-related events and impose documentation or notification duties. In a broad factual scenario, an ICT-related incident could require evaluation under A while a provider's security measure could require notice to an affected subscriber under B, creating additional compliance work and potentially overlapping timing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different subjects and are triggered by different events. A requires periodic and incident-related documentation and evaluation of an ICT-risk-management framework, with submission to the competent authority only on request; B requires a provider to notify the affected subscriber before, or urgently after, taking a specified measure. They are not two reports about the same event to different recipients, and neither duty prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory documentation/evaluation and notification duties concerning ICT or AI-related systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose compliance-related duties on potentially overlapping digital-system actors, and A requires documentation and evaluation after serious ICT-related incidents while B requires a prompt notification to the Commission when a condition concerning a general-purpose AI model is met. If the same event both constitutes a serious ICT-related incident and causes the Article 51 condition to be met, the actor might face concurrent documentation/evaluation and notification obligations.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different objects and triggers: A concerns periodically and incident-triggered documentation, evaluation, and continuous improvement of an ICT-risk-management framework, whereas B concerns notifying the Commission that a general-purpose AI model satisfies a specified condition and supplying proof. They are not two reports to different recipients arising from the same reporting event; A's evaluation report is submitted only on request to the competent authority, while B's notification is made to the Commission, so both duties can be performed cumulatively without one discharging or conflicting with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden voldoet aan de in artikel 51, lid 1, punt a), bedoelde voorwaarde, stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incident enforcement and CSIRT warnings
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern incident-related cybersecurity information. One might argue that the enforcement authority’s case-specific assessment could require attention to circumstances that differ from, or complicate, the CSIRT’s near-real-time dissemination of warnings and notifications.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different functions: Article 32 requires competent authorities to consider individual-case circumstances when taking enforcement measures, while Article 16 requires the CSIRT, where possible, to issue warnings and disseminate information. Nothing in Article 32 prohibits or limits CSIRT communications, and nothing in Article 16 prevents case-specific enforcement assessment.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Bij het nemen van de in lid 4 of 5 bedoelde handhavingsmaatregelen eerbiedigen de bevoegde autoriteiten de rechten van de verdediging en houden zij rekening met de omstandigheden van elk afzonderlijk geval
verdict.evidence_span_b: het verstrekken van vroegtijdige waarschuwingen, meldingen en aankondigingen en het verspreiden van informatie ... over cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten, indien mogelijk in bijna-realtime

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or personal-data breach
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A qualifying personal-data breach affecting an electronic public service can trigger both duties for the same organisation. The GDPR duty requires notification to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours where possible, while Article 18 requires immediate notification to the Minister of the Interior; these are different recipients and the texts do not say that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can be performed cumulatively: the organisation can notify both recipients, immediately notify the Minister, and notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours. There is no contradiction in the required content or timing, although the separate reporting burden remains.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation operating an electronic public service suffers a cyberattack that causes unauthorised access to stored personal data and therefore constitutes a personal-data breach, while also being a breach of the security or integrity of its own electronic service. The organisation must notify the Minister of the Interior immediately ('onverwijld') and separately notify the competent supervisory authority under Article 55 within 72 hours of becoming aware, if possible; notifying one recipient does not notify the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: Article 33 contains an exception where it is unlikely that the breach poses a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. On the stated facts the breach is a qualifying personal-data breach with unauthorised access, so that exception is not established; nor does Article 18 provide an exception eliminating its separate notification duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-related entities and providers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations involving ICT-related actors and communications, so a broad topical relationship exists. One might argue that an incident-related progress report and a designation/oversight notification create overlapping administrative reporting burdens.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The selected norm in A requires the affected entity to submit an interim report to the CSIRT or competent authority when a significant incident is still ongoing. B requires the ESAs, via the Joint Committee, to notify a third-party ICT service provider of its critical designation and oversight start date; it is not a report by that provider and is not triggered by an incident. The duties therefore concern different actors, triggers, recipients, and subject matter, and neither filing discharges or obstructs the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen de ETA’s de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten via het Gemengd Comité in kennis van die aanwijzing alsook van de aanvangsdatum vanaf wanneer zij daadwerkelijk aan oversightactiviteiten zullen worden onderworpen

verdict.shared_subject: Bevoegde autoriteiten en toezicht op entiteiten/ICT-dienstverleners
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen raken aan handhavings- of toezichtbesluiten waarbij autoriteiten rekening houden met tekortkomingen of risico’s. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat A een bevoegdheid geeft om inbreukmakend gedrag te beëindigen, terwijl B een verplichte beoordelingsstap voorschrijft voordat een besluit over een kritieke ICT-dienstverlener wordt genomen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen geen onverenigbare handelingsplichten op. A verleent autoriteiten een bevoegdheid jegens belangrijke entiteiten om inbreukmakend gedrag te doen beëindigen; B verplicht bevoegde autoriteiten in een specifiek DORA-proces om bepaalde risico’s en de ernst van niet-naleving mee te wegen. Een autoriteit kan beide regels naleven: zij kan de voorgeschreven factoren beoordelen en vervolgens, indien bevoegd en passend, een beëindigingsbevel geven.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) de betrokken entiteiten te gelasten een einde te maken aan gedragingen die inbreuk maken op deze richtlijn en af te zien van herhaling van die gedragingen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteiten nemen na het ontvangen van de in artikel 35, lid 1, punt c), bedoelde meldingen bij het nemen van het in lid 6 van dit artikel bedoelde besluit het soort en de omvang van het risico dat of de risico’s die de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten niet heeft verholpen, in aanmerking, alsook de ernst van de niet-naleving

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations that may apply to the same entity or provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If a cable-maintenance provider is also an essential or important entity and the same incident significantly affects its services, it may have to notify its service recipients under Provision A and separately notify the municipal mayor or authorised official before public-ground cable-maintenance works under Provision B. These duties have different recipients, triggers, and timing, so compliance with one filing would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose independently satisfiable duties concerning different events and recipients: Provision A concerns significant incidents affecting service provision, while Provision B concerns planned cable-maintenance work on public grounds. Even if both apply to the same provider, the provider can make both notifications; neither provision forbids or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related obligations concerning personal-data breaches and ICT risk-management frameworks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A personal-data breach may also be a serious ICT-related incident, so the same controller could have to notify the GDPR supervisory authority while separately documenting and evaluating its ICT risk-management framework under DORA. However, Provision B does not require an incident report to a different recipient or impose a second reporting deadline; it requires documentation and evaluation, not a separate filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and concern different actions: A requires notification to the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours where the breach is likely to risk individuals' rights and freedoms, while B requires periodic and serious-incident documentation and evaluation in accordance with supervisory instructions. The texts provide no incompatible deadline, recipient, or content requirement, and compliance with one does not purport to substitute for the other.

An entity or authority can comply with both without either rule preventing compliance with the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity governance and enforcement under the NIS2 framework
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, when taking specified enforcement measures, to assess the circumstances of each individual case and at least properly consider factors such as the seriousness and duration of the infringement. Provision B requires the Minister to establish a national plan for large-scale cybersecurity incidents and crisis response; one might argue that a centrally standardised crisis plan could constrain case-specific enforcement discretion, but no such constraint is stated.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, compatible functions on different actors: A governs how competent authorities must exercise enforcement powers against essential entities, while B assigns the Minister the competence to establish a national crisis-response plan. Nothing in B removes the authorities' obligation under A to consider each enforcement case individually, and nothing in A prevents adoption of a national plan.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting ICT/security incidents by an organisation subject to both provisions
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same incident, but they require notification to different recipients: Provision A requires immediate notice to Onze Minister, while Provision B requires the relevant report also to be made to the sectoral CSIRT. The text does not say that notifying the CSIRT satisfies the duty to notify Onze Minister, so the actor may face two cumulative filings.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are individually compatible because an actor can promptly notify both recipients, and Provision B expressly uses the word “tevens” (also), which supports an additional notification rather than a prohibition or substitution. There is no incompatible deadline: Provision A specifies “onverwijld,” while Provision B states no separate deadline in the text shown.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bank that is also an aangewezen organisatie suffers a security breach affecting its own electronic service. It must notify Onze Minister “onverwijld” under Provision A and must also make the Article 19 incident report to the designated financial-sector CSIRT under Provision B; notifying the CSIRT does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate duty to notify Onze Minister.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting burden. The decisive point is that the recipients differ and Provision B says the report must be made “tevens” to the CSIRT. The text shown does not establish any rule making one notification substitute for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related duties of an essential or important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by a serious or significant ICT incident. Provision A requires documentation and evaluation of the ICT risk-management framework, while Provision B requires prompt notification of service recipients; these are different actions, and A does not state that documenting or evaluating the framework informs recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct, cumulatively satisfiable duties rather than conflicting ones. A requires internal or supervisory documentation and evaluation, whereas B requires informing service recipients without delay; neither duty prohibits or substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit stelt in voorkomend geval onverwijld de ontvangers van haar diensten in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.

verdict.shared_subject: Cooperation and information exchange concerning regulatory tasks and personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires competent authorities, the ESAs and the ECB to cooperate and exchange information for supervisory tasks. Provision B requires a notification to the Dutch data-protection authority and the affected person containing specified breach information; if the authorities’ cooperation required sharing information that B limits or if the notification duties conflicted with confidentiality rules, an issue might arise, but neither text establishes such a restriction or incompatibility.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors and address different functions: A governs inter-authority cooperation and supervisory coordination, while B governs the content of a provider’s breach notification to the Autoriteit persoonsgegevens and the affected person. The texts can be fully complied with cumulatively; A does not prohibit or alter the notification required by B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteiten, de ETA’s en de ECB werken onderling nauw samen en wisselen informatie uit om hun taken overeenkomstig de artikelen 47 tot en met 54 te verrichten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De kennisgeving aan de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens en de persoon wiens persoonsgegevens het betreft, omvat in ieder geval de aard van de inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, de instanties waar meer informatie over de inbreuk kan worden verkregen en de aanbevolen maatregelen om de negatieve gevolgen van de inbreuk te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification duties concerning threats or incidents affecting network, service, or clients/subscribers
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require an undertaking to notify an affected person, and a single event could potentially be both a serious ICT-related incident affecting clients and a threat requiring a provider to take a measure. However, the provisions address different actors, triggers, and notification content, and neither text requires two notifications to different recipients or establishes incompatible deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: A financial entity must notify its clients about a serious ICT-related incident and mitigation measures, while a provider must notify the involved subscriber before, or urgently after, taking a measure to remove a threat to network, service, or equipment integrity. Where both duties apply, the actor can make both notifications; the texts do not state that one notification substitutes for the other or that their requirements conflict.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

There is no same triggering event, same report, or conflicting deadline, so the strongest tension case is only that an actor might have to perform both obligations in parallel.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are independently satisfiable and have different triggers, purposes, and apparent recipients. A concerns documenting and evaluating an ICT-risk-management framework in accordance with supervisory instructions, whereas B concerns notifying the Commission about satisfaction of a specified condition for a general-purpose AI model; neither duty prohibits or substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Different statutory duties involving an ACM number register and a CSIRT response to an early warning.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern regulatory information handling and communications, so one might initially suspect overlapping administrative obligations. However, provision A requires the ACM to maintain a register containing allocation and identifying details, while provision B requires a CSIRT to respond to a reporting entity within a specified period; neither duty prescribes conduct that prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different actors, concerning different actions and triggers. The ACM can maintain the required number register, and a CSIRT can separately answer a reporting entity after receiving an early warning; compliance with one does not obstruct or substitute for compliance with the other.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations involving communications or submissions and contain timing language. However, provision A concerns the ETAs notifying a critical ICT third-party provider of its designation and oversight start date, while provision B concerns an essential or important entity submitting a progress report instead of a final incident report.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different actors, triggers, recipients and subject matter. A requires the ETAs to notify a critical ICT service provider after designation; B requires the affected essential or important entity to submit an incident progress report and later a final report. Compliance with one does not purport to replace or discharge the other, but there is no overlapping filing duty.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting a security or data incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a controller to notify the competent supervisory authority under Article 55 within 72 hours for a personal-data breach posing a likely risk. B separately requires an essential or important entity to give an early warning about a significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours; the recipients differ, so the 24-hour warning does not discharge A's supervisory-authority notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can both be performed by the same actor, with the earlier B notification followed by the A notification where the incident also qualifies as a risky personal-data breach. There is no contradiction in the required content or timing; the apparent burden is cumulative reporting to different recipients.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company is both a GDPR controller and an essential or important entity. A cyberattack causes a personal-data breach that is also a significant incident and likely risks individuals' rights and freedoms. The company must warn its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours under B, and separately notify the Article 55 competent supervisory authority within 72 hours under A; notifying the CSIRT and sectoral competent authority does not itself constitute the GDPR notification to the supervisory authority.
verdict.decisive_exception: The provisions do not establish that the CSIRT or B's competent authority is the same recipient as the Article 55 competent supervisory authority, nor that one filing legally substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident-related reporting and information duties
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same incident, but they require communications to different recipients: the affected person under A and the CSIRT or competent authority under B. A notification to the affected person cannot satisfy B's requested interim report, and B's report cannot satisfy A's duty to notify the affected person.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are independently performable and concern different communications rather than incompatible commands. Nothing in either text prevents the entity from notifying the affected person and, if requested, submitting the interim report to the CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A medical-device manufacturer classified as an essential or important entity suffers a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect an individual's privacy. It must notify the affected person 'onverwijld' under A and, in connection with the Article 27 notification, submit an interim update report when requested by its CSIRT or competent authority under B; sending the individual notice does not constitute the requested report to the CSIRT or competent authority.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification duties involving different actors and authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification-related obligations, and one might argue that a critical ICT third-party provider could also perform cable-maintenance work on public land, creating multiple notifications concerning that provider's activities. However, the duties concern different triggering events, recipients, and responsible actors, so this is not a genuine dual-reporting conflict.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires the ETAs, via the Joint Committee, to notify a critical ICT third-party provider of its designation and oversight start date. Provision B requires an authorised municipal official to notify the mayor when a cable-work provider has made the required prior notification. These are separate duties concerning different events and actors, and both can be performed without contradiction.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nadat een derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten als cruciaal is aangewezen, stellen de ETA’s de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten via het Gemengd Comité in kennis van die aanwijzing alsook van de aanvangsdatum vanaf wanneer zij daadwerkelijk aan oversightactiviteiten zullen worden onderworpen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of serious/significant ICT incidents by an entity subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires updated notifications after an initial notification to the relevant competent authority, while B requires an early warning to both the entity’s CSIRT and its competent authority within 24 hours. If the same incident triggers both regimes, the texts appear to require separate communications to different recipients, and A’s deadline is not specified here.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can send B’s early warning within 24 hours and separately submit A’s updated notification after the initial notification when a relevant status update becomes available. Nothing shown says that either filing substitutes for the other, so the apparent overlap is an additional reporting burden rather than an impossibility of compliance.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also an essential or important entity and suffers one incident that qualifies both as a serious ICT-related incident under A and a significant incident under B. It must submit A’s updated notification to “de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” after its initial notification, while also giving B’s early warning “aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” within 24 hours; sending the A notification to the competent authority does not, on the text shown, discharge the separate CSIRT notification required by B.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations for cable-maintenance work and significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: An operator carrying out cable-maintenance work on public land could also be an essential or important entity experiencing a significant incident. Provision A then requires advance notice to the mayor or authorised official, while provision B requires reporting the significant incident under Articles 26–29; if the incident-reporting regime requires a different recipient, timing, or content, both duties could be cumulative.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish incompatible duties. A concerns advance notification of planned cable-maintenance work to a municipal recipient, whereas B concerns reporting a significant incident under cross-referenced provisions, and B itself specifies neither a conflicting deadline nor a different recipient in the text shown. The same event is not necessarily involved: planned maintenance and an incident affecting network or information systems are distinct triggers, and both notices can be made if they overlap.
verdict.missing_reference: Articles 26–29, and potentially Article 25(2), are needed to determine B’s recipient, deadline, content, and the precise definition of a significant incident. Without those provisions, a dual-reporting burden cannot be established from the texts shown.

verdict.shared_subject: Institutional cooperation and information-sharing arrangements concerning incidents or eIDAS-related notifications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A obliges the CSIRT network, upon request from an affected member, to exchange and discuss information about an incident and related cyber threats, risks and vulnerabilities. Provision B separately obliges Dutch ministers and the Personal Data Authority to make arrangements concerning the handling of matters of mutual interest for effective and efficient eIDAS notifications; one might argue that these overlapping coordination duties could prescribe different institutional handling arrangements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose duties on different institutional subjects and address different functions: A concerns operational incident-information exchange within the CSIRT network, while B concerns inter-authority arrangements for eIDAS notifications. Nothing in either text forbids, limits, or makes compliance with the other duty impossible; the arrangements under B can coexist with the information exchange required by A.
