verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be satisfied cumulatively: the actor can make the GDPR breach notification and separately document/evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework, submitting the evaluation report if requested. Article 16 does not expressly require an immediate incident report, and the texts do not establish that every personal-data breach is a serious ICT-related incident or that the authorities are different.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity subject to both instruments suffers one serious cyberattack that causes a personal-data breach. It must, if possible, notify the Article 55 competent supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of the breach, and it must document and evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework in connection with the serious ICT-related incident; if the competent authority requests the evaluation report, it must submit that report as well. The GDPR notification and the DORA evaluation-report duty are separate filings to potentially different competent authorities, and neither text says that one substitutes for the other.
verdict.decisive_exception: The conclusion depends on the incident satisfying both provisions' triggers and, for the second filing, on a request by the competent authority. The texts do not identify whether the GDPR supervisory authority and the DORA competent authority are the same, nor do they specify a deadline for the requested evaluation report; if they are the same authority and the evaluation report is not requested, the obligations may be compatible rather than a dual-reporting burden.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens heeft plaatsgevonden, meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd. ... Een evaluatieverslag van het kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt op verzoek bij de bevoegde autoriteit ingediend.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of incident updates by an entity potentially subject to both NIS2 and DORA
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require incident-related follow-up reporting, and a financial entity could face an NIS2 request for an interim report while also having to submit DORA interim or updated notifications. The strongest tension case is that the instruments may require separate submissions under different procedural regimes, with no text here stating that a DORA filing discharges an NIS2 request.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions are compatible because A is conditional: an interim report is required only 'op verzoek' of the CSIRT or competent authority, whereas B establishes the financial entity's DORA reporting sequence to the relevant competent authority. The texts do not show that the same triggering event necessarily requires two separate filings, nor do they establish different recipients or incompatible deadlines; both duties can therefore be performed cumulatively.
verdict.evidence_span_a: c) op verzoek van het CSIRT of, indien van toepassing, de bevoegde autoriteit, een tussentijds verslag indienen over relevante updates van de situatie;
verdict.evidence_span_b: b) een tussentijds verslag na de eerste kennisgeving als bedoeld in punt a), zodra de status van het oorspronkelijke incident ingrijpend is gewijzigd of de behandeling van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident is gewijzigd op basis van beschikbare nieuwe informatie, in voorkomend geval gevolgd door geactualiseerde kennisgevingen telkens wanneer een relevante actualisering van de status beschikbaar is, alsmede op specifiek verzoek van de bevoegde autoriteit;

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity incidents or threats affecting electronic services and their users
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie to notify Onze Minister immediately about a security or integrity breach, misuse, or improper use involving its own electronic service. B separately requires an essential or important entity to inform potentially affected service recipients immediately about measures responding to a significant cyberthreat and, if necessary, about that threat itself; for an entity falling within both provisions, the same event could trigger two communications to different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can be complied with cumulatively: the entity can notify the Minister under A and inform affected service recipients under B. They concern different recipients and different information purposes, so neither communication necessarily substitutes for the other; moreover, B applies only where the threat is significant and informing about the threat is necessary.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important entity that is also an aangewezen organisatie suffers a significant cyberthreat causing a security breach in its own electronic service, potentially affecting service recipients. It must notify Onze Minister immediately under A and separately inform the potentially affected recipients immediately about protective measures—and, if necessary, the threat itself—under B; notifying the Minister does not inform the recipients, and informing the recipients does not notify the Minister.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst of van misbruik of oneigenlijk gebruik van de toegang tot de eigen elektronische dienstverlening.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit deelt de ontvangers van haar diensten, die mogelijkerwijs door een significante cyberdreiging in relatie tot het ontvangen van die diensten worden getroffen, onverwijld mee welke maatregelen die ontvangers kunnen nemen in reactie op die dreiging.

verdict.shared_subject: The timing of a progress report under NIS2 and the timing of a decision under BWBR0009950 art. 5.6
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the relevant entity to submit a progress report when the incident is still ongoing at the time the final report is due. Provision B requires that a decision be taken immediately after receipt of a notification; if the progress report is itself a notification within B's scope, the actor might face an immediate-decision requirement alongside A's reporting duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different duties on different apparent actors and concern different acts: A concerns an entity submitting a progress report, while B concerns taking a decision after receiving a notification. Nothing in the texts establishes that A's progress report is the notification triggering B, that the same actor must perform both acts, or that the duties impose incompatible timing or content requirements.
verdict.evidence_span_a: indienen en binnen één maand nadat zij het incident hebben afgehandeld, een eindverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Essentiële entiteiten die tevens kritieke entiteiten zijn en de bevoegde autoriteiten die daarop toezicht houden
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A concerns the competent authority’s power to order an essential entity to stop conduct violating the NIS2 Directive and refrain from repeating it. Provision B imposes an information-transfer duty on a competent authority concerning a reported significant incident. One might argue that an authority’s enforcement intervention could affect how the entity handles or reports an incident, while another authority must receive information about it.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different norms on different actors and address different actions: A grants an enforcement competence to a competent authority, whereas B requires an authority to transmit information about a reported significant incident to the authority under the Critical Entities Resilience Act. Nothing in B forbids, limits, or makes conditional the enforcement power in A, and nothing in A excuses or obstructs the information-transfer duty in B.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de betrokken entiteiten te gelasten een einde te maken aan gedragingen die inbreuk maken op deze richtlijn en af te zien van herhaling van die gedragingen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteit verstrekt de bevoegde autoriteit, bedoeld in artikel 8 van de Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten, informatie over een significant incident dat overeenkomstig artikel 25 is gemeld

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations potentially applicable to the same entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a financial entity to prepare and submit serious ICT-incident notifications and reports to the relevant competent authority, while Provision B requires an AI-model provider to notify the Commission within two weeks when the specified condition is met. If the same organisation is both a financial entity subject to A and an AI-model provider subject to B, one incident or development might appear to trigger two separate notifications to different recipients. However, the texts do not establish that the event triggering B is the same event as the serious ICT-related incident triggering A.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern different triggers, actors and subject matter: A concerns serious ICT-related incidents of financial entities and reporting to the relevant competent authority; B concerns an AI model for general purposes satisfying a condition under Article 51(1)(a) and notification to the Commission. Even where one entity falls within both personal scopes, the duties can be performed cumulatively, and neither provision says that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten melden overeenkomstig lid 4 van dit artikel ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten aan de relevante bevoegde autoriteit als bedoeld in artikel 46.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden voldoet aan de in artikel 51, lid 1, punt a), bedoelde voorwaarde, stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification of cyber/security threats or incidents by entities providing electronic services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by the same serious security event affecting an entity’s electronic service. Provision A requires notifying potentially affected service recipients about the significant cyber threat, while Provision B requires notifying the Minister immediately about a security or integrity breach; these are separate recipients and separate communications, so notifying one does not appear to satisfy the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different audiences and purposes and can readily be performed cumulatively: the entity can promptly warn affected recipients and separately inform the Minister with the required information. Nothing in either text says that one notification substitutes for or prohibits the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A designated organisation providing an electronic public service suffers a serious security breach that constitutes a significant cyber threat to its service users. It must notify potentially affected recipients of the threat under Provision A and, separately and without delay, notify the Minister of the breach and provide all necessary information under Provision B; sending the recipient warning does not discharge the ministerial notification, and sending the ministerial notification does not warn the recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Indien nodig stellen de entiteiten die ontvangers ook in kennis van de significante cyberdreiging zelf.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst

verdict.shared_subject: Obligations to submit notifications or reports to public authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose an obligation involving a notification, so an operator subject to both might initially appear to face overlapping reporting duties. However, Provision A concerns the results and template of a fundamental-rights impact assessment for certain high-risk AI systems, while Provision B concerns advance notice of cable-maintenance work on public land; they do not regulate the same event or filing.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties can plainly be performed together because they have different triggers, subject matter, recipients, and timing. Provision A requires the completed template as part of a notification to the market-surveillance authority, whereas Provision B requires the cable provider to notify the municipal mayor or authorised official before the works; neither filing discharges or prevents the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon
verdict.evidence_span_b: wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente binnen wiens grondgebied de werkzaamheden zullen plaatsvinden, of bij een daartoe door hem gemachtigd ambtenaar

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations triggered by different events, involving different actors and recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose prompt notification duties, and a single organisation might conceivably be involved in both a personal-data breach and the qualifying condition for a general-purpose AI model. In that situation, however, the duties concern different triggers and require notifications to different legally identified recipients, so they would be cumulative rather than one discharging the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The GDPR provision requires a processor to inform the controller of a personal-data breach, while the AI Act provision requires the relevant provider to inform the Commission when the Article 51(1)(a) condition is met. They apply to different actors, triggers, subject matter and recipients; compliance with one does not purport to replace the other, and there is no conflict in making both notifications where both triggers occur.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden voldoet aan de in artikel 51, lid 1, punt a), bedoelde voorwaarde, stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations, but they concern different conduct, actors, triggers, and recipients. No realistic fact pattern makes approving and overseeing cybersecurity-risk measures conflict with notifying a municipal mayor about cable-maintenance work on public land.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The governance obligation applies to member states and the governing bodies of essential or important entities, requiring approval and oversight of cybersecurity-risk measures. The notification obligation applies to a provider carrying out cable-maintenance work on public land and requires advance notice to the mayor or authorised official; the duties can readily be performed cumulatively where both happen to apply.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de bestuursorganen van essentiële en belangrijke entiteiten de door deze entiteiten genomen maatregelen voor het beheer van cyberbeveiligingsrisico’s goedkeuren om te voldoen aan artikel 21, toezien op de uitvoering ervan
verdict.evidence_span_b: Ingeval de werkzaamheden in verband met de instandhouding van kabels worden verricht in of op openbare gronden, wordt hiervan door de aanbieder tevens voorafgaand aan de uit te voeren werkzaamheden melding gedaan bij de burgemeester van de gemeente

verdict.shared_subject: Monitoring, evaluation, and incident-related obligations for ICT/AI systems
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose ongoing oversight-related obligations on an operator, and provision B requires immediate notification of a serious incident while provision A requires documentation and evaluation at serious ICT-related incidents. One might argue that the same incident creates overlapping compliance work and that the relationship between the evaluation record and the AI Act notifications is not specified.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are different and cumulative: A requires periodic and incident-triggered documentation and evaluation of the ICT risk-management framework, whereas B requires notification of a serious AI incident to specified recipients. A has no extracted recipient or deadline, so B's notifications cannot discharge A's separate documentation and evaluation duty, and A does not impose a competing reporting obligation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer gebruiksverantwoordelijke een ernstig incident vaststellen, stellen zij ook onmiddellijk eerst de aanbieder hiervan in kennis, en vervolgens de importeur of distributeur en de betreffende markttoezichtautoriteiten van dat incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Supervisory authorities’ enforcement and follow-up concerning ICT/cybersecurity risks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers authorities to order an essential entity to stop conduct that infringes the NIS2 Directive. Provision B obliges authorities, after specified notifications and when taking a DORA decision, to consider risks not remedied by a critical ICT third-party provider and the seriousness of non-compliance; if the same authority and entity are involved, the provisions could appear to require different enforcement considerations or actions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions regulate different enforcement frameworks, actors, and triggers: A concerns a Member State authority’s competence toward an essential entity for conduct infringing NIS2, while B concerns authorities’ decision-making after particular DORA notifications regarding a critical ICT third-party provider and a financial entity. Nothing in either text requires an authority to continue conduct that the other requires it to stop, nor does B displace A’s enforcement competence.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de betrokken entiteiten te gelasten een einde te maken aan gedragingen die inbreuk maken op deze richtlijn en af te zien van herhaling van die gedragingen
verdict.evidence_span_b: De bevoegde autoriteiten nemen na het ontvangen van de in artikel 35, lid 1, punt c), bedoelde meldingen bij het nemen van het in lid 6 van dit artikel bedoelde besluit het soort en de omvang van het risico dat of de risico’s die de kritieke derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten niet heeft verholpen, in aanmerking

verdict.shared_subject: Toezicht en persoonsgegevens binnen gereguleerde nummer- of medische-hulpmiddelenactiviteiten
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen noemen een toezichthoudende autoriteit en persoonsgegevens, maar zij leggen verschillende institutionele taken op. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat het bijhouden van een register met naam- en adresgegevens en het melden van een potentiële persoonsgegevensinbreuk verschillende gegevensstromen en verantwoordelijkheden creëren die bij één incident kunnen overlappen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A verplicht de Autoriteit Consument en Markt een nummerregister bij te houden met gegevens over nummer-toekenningen. Provision B verplicht een bevoegde autoriteit in een specifieke NIS2/GDPR-context de Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens te informeren over een potentiële inbreuk; geen van beide verbiedt de andere handeling of bepaalt dat het register niet mag worden bijgehouden of dat een melding achterwege moet blijven.
verdict.evidence_span_a: wordt door de Autoriteit Consument en Markt een nummerregister bijgehouden dat een overzicht bevat van toekenningen. Het register bevat de vermelding van de naam, het adres en de vestigingsplaats, respectievelijk de woonplaats van degene aan wie nummers zijn toegekend.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer de op grond van de Algemene verordening gegevensbescherming bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit in een andere lidstaat van de Europese Unie is gevestigd, stelt de bevoegde autoriteit de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens in kennis van de potentiële inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens, bedoeld in het tweede lid.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT incidents and the duties of entities subject to both instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires, where applicable, immediate notification of significant incidents to the entities’ service recipients. Provision B requires the ICT risk-management framework to be documented and evaluated at regular intervals and when serious ICT-related incidents occur; an incident may therefore trigger both an external notification and incident-related framework documentation, creating additional compliance work.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties have different objects and recipients: A concerns notifying service recipients about significant incidents adversely affecting service provision, while B concerns documenting and evaluating an ICT risk-management framework. They can readily be performed cumulatively, and B does not state that documentation substitutes for A’s notification or that the two duties use incompatible deadlines or content.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het in lid 1, tweede alinea, punt a), bedoelde kader voor ICT-risicobeheer wordt overeenkomstig de toezichtinstructies op gezette tijden en bij ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incidenten gedocumenteerd en geëvalueerd.

verdict.shared_subject: Submitting an interim report on relevant updates during a significant incident
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern reporting by an entity during an incident, and provision B expressly requires an interim report on request. Provision A, however, is the norm extracted here as requiring a final report, not an interim report, so the texts do not establish two separate filings for the same event or conflicting clocks.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires submission of a final report no later than one month after the incident report, while provision B requires an interim report only if requested by the entity’s CSIRT or competent authority. An entity can submit any requested interim report and later submit the final report; neither provision says that one substitutes for the other or makes compliance with both impossible.
verdict.evidence_span_a: uiterlijk één maand na de indiening van het in punt b) bedoelde incidentmelding, een eindverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: op verzoek van haar CSIRT of haar bevoegde autoriteit een tussentijds verslag in over relevante updates van de situatie

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity oversight of essential entities and their networks
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers competent authorities to order an essential entity to stop conduct violating the directive, while provision B obliges the CSIRT to monitor and analyse cyber threats, vulnerabilities and incidents. One might argue that an enforcement order could restrict monitoring activity or require cessation of conduct that the CSIRT’s monitoring duty entails.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns the competent authority’s enforcement competence over an essential entity; provision B concerns the CSIRT’s institutional monitoring task. The texts do not require the authority to prohibit CSIRT monitoring, nor do they make the CSIRT subject to the entity-directed order, and both can operate simultaneously.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de betrokken entiteiten te gelasten een einde te maken aan gedragingen die inbreuk maken op deze richtlijn en af te zien van herhaling van die gedragingen;
verdict.evidence_span_b: het monitoren en analyseren van cyberdreigingen, kwetsbaarheden en incidenten op nationaal niveau

verdict.shared_subject: Handling and reporting ICT-related incidents by a financial or essential/important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision B requires an essential or important entity to send an early warning to both its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Provision A makes a financial entity remain fully responsible for handling and consequences of incidents reported under Article 19(1), but does not itself impose a separate reporting recipient or deadline; therefore, it does not create a second filing that could conflict with B.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose complementary duties. B specifies an early-warning communication to two recipients and a 24-hour clock, while A preserves the financial entity’s substantive responsibility despite supervisory feedback; making the warning does not transfer or eliminate that responsibility, and both duties can plainly be performed together.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Onverminderd de ontvangen feedback van toezichthouders blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd.
verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Provider notification duties under different legal regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a notification duty on an actor called an “aanbieder,” so a provider might initially appear to face two overlapping reporting obligations. However, the duties concern different triggering events, recipients, and subject matter: A concerns notifying the Commission about a qualifying general-purpose AI model, while B concerns notifying the affected subscriber before or promptly after taking a network-service measure.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations can readily be performed cumulatively because they are not alternative reports about the same event. A requires notification to the Commission within two weeks of the relevant AI-model condition becoming satisfied or known; B requires notification to the affected subscriber in connection with a measure protecting network or service integrity and security. Compliance with one does not purport to discharge the other, but there is no single triggering event requiring two reports under both provisions.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee

verdict.shared_subject: Administrative enforcement and inter-authority coordination
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern public authorities and institutional handling of regulatory matters, so one might argue that coordinated treatment under the eIDAS framework could affect how enforcement matters are handled. However, neither provision regulates the same decision, duty, sanction, deadline, or substantive outcome.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires supervisory authorities to ensure that GDPR administrative fines are effective, proportionate, and dissuasive. Provision B requires specified Dutch authorities to make arrangements for handling matters of mutual interest concerning eIDAS notifications; making such arrangements does not prevent or alter the required characteristics of GDPR fines.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Elke toezichthoudende autoriteit zorgt ervoor dat de administratieve geldboeten die uit hoofde van dit artikel worden opgelegd voor de in de leden 4, 5 en 6 vermelde inbreuken op deze verordening in elke zaak doeltreffend, evenredig en afschrikkend zijn.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Onze Minister, Onze Minister van Veiligheid en Justitie en de Autoriteit persoonsgegevens maken in het belang van effectieve en efficiënte meldingen als bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, van de eidas-verordening, afspraken over de wijze van behandeling van aangelegenheden van wederzijds belang.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory handling and follow-up of reported ICT/AI incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern official action after an incident notification, and both involve communication with regulated entities or public authorities. One might argue that supervisory feedback under Provision A could overlap with the mandatory notification chain in Provision B, creating uncertainty about which authority should communicate and for what purpose.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A gives the competent authority a discretionary power to provide high-level feedback or discuss corrective measures with a financial entity, while Provision B requires the market-surveillance authority to notify specified national public authorities after receiving a serious-incident report. These are different actions, actors, recipients, and triggers; the discretionary feedback does not replace or obstruct the mandatory notification.
verdict.evidence_span_a: kan zij, waar mogelijk, tijdig relevante en evenredige feedback of richtsnoeren op hoog niveau aan de financiële entiteit verstrekken
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de betrokken markttoezichtautoriteit de in artikel 77, lid 1, bedoelde nationale overheidsinstanties of -organen in kennis

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal data and serious ICT-related incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires the controller to notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware of a qualifying personal-data breach. B separately requires a financial entity to notify its clients without delay when a serious ICT-related incident affecting clients’ financial interests is detected; the recipients and required information differ, so one notification does not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can both be complied with because they impose complementary notifications to different recipients: the supervisory authority under A and clients under B. A single incident may trigger both duties, but there is no contradiction between notifying both, and B’s client-notification duty does not replace A’s regulatory notification.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity, acting as controller, discovers a security incident that both constitutes a personal-data breach likely to risk individuals’ rights and freedoms and is a serious ICT-related incident affecting clients’ financial interests. It must notify the competent supervisory authority within 72 hours under A and notify affected clients without delay under B; notifying the authority does not notify the clients, and notifying the clients does not satisfy the authority filing.
verdict.decisive_exception: The duties are subject to different triggers and recipients, and no text shown provides that client notification under B substitutes for notification to the supervisory authority under A. A’s exception applies only where the breach is not likely to risk individuals’ rights and freedoms; B’s client-notification rule may still apply independently if its trigger is met.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze zonder onredelijke vertraging en, indien mogelijk, uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit
verdict.evidence_span_b: stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification duties arising from different events involving an AI system and personal data
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties on an operator/provider, and a single AI-related personal-data incident could potentially trigger both a notification to the market-surveillance authority and an immediate notification to the affected person. The duties differ in recipient and trigger, so notifying one recipient would not, on the face of these texts, satisfy the other duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions concern distinct triggering events and recipients: provision A requires submission of a completed fundamental-rights-impact-assessment template as part of a notification to the market-surveillance authority, whereas provision B requires notifying the affected data subject of a personal-data breach likely to adversely affect privacy. They can therefore be performed cumulatively, and neither text forbids or substitutes for the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting and decision-making concerning electronic communications works
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires notified bodies, upon request, to inform the notifying authority about conformity-assessment and related activities. Provision B requires that a decision be taken without delay after receipt of a notification; if the notification in B were the same event or filing as A's requested information, the duties could involve different actions, actors, and timing, potentially creating an unresolved procedural relationship.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish the same actor, recipient, triggering event, or filing. A concerns a notified body's information duty to the notifying authority, triggered by a request, while B concerns taking a decision promptly after receipt of a notification and identifies no recipient; both can therefore be complied with independently, and B's deadline cannot discharge A's separate requested-information duty.
verdict.evidence_span_a: op verzoek, de binnen het toepassingsgebied van hun aanmelding verrichte conformiteitsbeoordelingsactiviteiten en andere activiteiten, waaronder grensoverschrijdende activiteiten en onderaanneming.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het besluit wordt onverwijld na het tijdstip van ontvangst van de melding genomen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations triggered by different events for potentially different regulated entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires an AI-model provider to notify the Commission within two weeks after the relevant condition is met or is known to be met. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit a progress report at the time an incident’s final report is due if the incident is still ongoing. If the same actor and facts happen to satisfy both triggers, the duties concern different reports and potentially different regulatory regimes, so one filing would not obviously discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not establish the same triggering event, the same actor, or even an identified recipient for provision B. A concerns notification of an AI model meeting a condition under Article 51(1)(a), whereas B concerns an ongoing incident and substitution of a progress report for a final report; each can be performed independently without making compliance with the other impossible.

Die kennisgeving bevat de informatie die nodig is om aan te tonen dat aan de desbetreffende eis is voldaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification duties concerning regulated ICT/AI providers or models
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose notification duties, and a single undertaking might conceivably be both a critical third-party ICT-service provider and an AI-model provider. However, the duties concern different triggering events and recipients: Provision A concerns notification of a critical designation and oversight start date, while Provision B concerns notification to the Commission that a general-purpose AI model meets a specified condition.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can readily both be performed: Provision A requires the ETAs, through the Joint Committee, to notify the ICT provider of its designation and oversight start date, whereas Provision B requires the relevant provider to notify the Commission within two weeks of satisfying or expecting to satisfy the Article 51 condition. Neither provision says that one notification substitutes for the other, and the actors, triggers, and subject matter differ.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stellen de ETA’s de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten via het Gemengd Comité in kennis van die aanwijzing alsook van de aanvangsdatum vanaf wanneer zij daadwerkelijk aan oversightactiviteiten zullen worden onderworpen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-risicobeheer, incidenten en opvolging door gereguleerde entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen raken aan de opvolging van ICT-incidenten: A verlangt dat relevante conclusies uit tests en incidentanalyses in het risicobeoordelingsproces worden opgenomen, terwijl B een tussentijds verslag over relevante updates verlangt. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat dezelfde incidentinformatie zowel intern moet worden verwerkt als extern moet worden gerapporteerd, met mogelijk verschillende inhoudelijke verwachtingen.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen verschillende, cumulatief uitvoerbare verplichtingen op. A betreft een intern ICT-risicobeoordelings- en leerproces, en geldt bovendien alleen 'in voorkomend geval'; B betreft een tussentijds verslag aan het CSIRT of de bevoegde autoriteit, uitsluitend wanneer daarom wordt verzocht in het kader van een melding. Geen van beide verplichtingen verbiedt naleving van de andere of bepaalt dat de ene handeling de andere vervangt.
verdict.evidence_span_a: de in punt f) bedoelde plannen en maatregelen, alsmede de doeltreffendheid van de overeenkomstig de punten a) en c) uitgevoerde controles regelmatig testen; h) in voorkomend geval de relevante operationele conclusies die voortvloeien uit de in punt g) bedoelde tests en uit de analyse na een incident opnemen in het ICT-risicobeoordelingsproces

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting events relevant to regulated entities and authorities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires a notified conformity-assessment body to inform the notifying authority about circumstances affecting the scope or conditions of its notification, without a deadline. Provision B requires an essential or important entity to give an early warning about a significant incident to both its CSIRT and competent authority, immediately or within 24 hours; if the same actor and event fall under both provisions, the recipients and reporting duties differ, so one report would not necessarily discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions address different actors and triggers: A concerns a notified body and circumstances affecting its notification, while B concerns an essential or important entity and a significant incident. Even where one event satisfies both triggers, both duties can be performed cumulatively, and A's lack of deadline does not conflict with B's 24-hour deadline.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A notified conformity-assessment body that is also an essential or important entity discovers a significant cybersecurity incident that affects the scope or conditions of its notification. It must notify the notifying authority under A and separately give the early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority under B, immediately or within 24 hours; notifying one recipient does not satisfy the duties owed to the other recipients.
verdict.evidence_span_a: omstandigheden die van invloed zijn op het toepassingsgebied van of de voorwaarden voor de aanmelding
verdict.evidence_span_b: geeft ten behoeve van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, een vroegtijdige waarschuwing over het significante incident aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit. Dit doet zij onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident.

verdict.shared_subject: Entities involved in ICT or trust services and regulatory oversight/reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern regulatory communications involving ICT-service activity, and an entity could conceivably be affected by both an oversight-designation communication and an incident-reporting duty. However, provision A concerns notification by the ESAs to a critical third-party ICT service provider about its designation and oversight start date, while provision B concerns an entity's own incident report to its CSIRT and competent authority; the acts, actors, triggers, recipients, and subject matter differ.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose distinct duties that can plainly be performed together: the ESAs notify a provider of a designation, while the affected entity reports a significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority within 24 hours. Neither provision says that one communication substitutes for, prevents, or discharges the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nadat een derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten als cruciaal is aangewezen, stellen de ETA’s de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten via het Gemengd Comité in kennis van die aanwijzing alsook van de aanvangsdatum vanaf wanneer zij daadwerkelijk aan oversightactiviteiten zullen worden onderworpen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: In afwijking van het eerste lid dient een essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit die een vertrouwensdienst aanbiedt onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur nadat zij kennis heeft gekregen van het significante incident een melding van het significante incident in bij haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit als dat incident gevolgen heeft voor de verlening van haar vertrouwensdienst.

verdict.shared_subject: Notification duties involving ICT service providers and personal-data breaches
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions use notification language and could, at a high level, involve the same ICT service provider. If a critical ICT provider also processes personal data and a breach occurs, one might initially suspect overlapping communications duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires a processor to inform the controller, without undue delay, of a personal-data breach. Provision B requires the lead overseer/ESAs to notify the ICT provider of its designation and oversight start date; it is a regulatory designation notice, not a breach report. The duties have different triggers, actors, recipients and subject matter, so neither filing discharges the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De verwerker informeert de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke zonder onredelijke vertraging zodra hij kennis heeft genomen van een inbreuk in verband met persoonsgegevens.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Nadat een derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten als cruciaal is aangewezen, stellen de ETA’s de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten via het Gemengd Comité in kennis van die aanwijzing alsook van de aanvangsdatum vanaf wanneer zij daadwerkelijk aan oversightactiviteiten zullen worden onderworpen.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting duties imposed on an aanbieder
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions require an aanbieder to make a notification, and a single provider might conceivably be involved in both an AI-model notification and a network or service security measure. The notifications have different apparent triggers, recipients and timing: A concerns notifying the Commissie within two weeks, while B concerns notifying the betrokken abonnee before or, if urgent, as soon as possible after a measure.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different events and recipients: A is triggered by an AI model satisfying a specified condition and requires information proving that condition, whereas B is triggered by a measure addressing a threat to network, service or device integrity and security and requires notice to the affected subscriber. Even if the same aanbieder is subject to both, each filing can be made independently; neither text says that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan. Die kennisgeving bevat de informatie die nodig is om aan te tonen dat aan de desbetreffende eis is voldaan.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Voorafgaand aan het nemen van een maatregel, bedoeld in het eerste lid, onderdeel g, doet de aanbieder melding aan de betrokken abonnee, en geeft de abonnee daarbij de gelegenheid de in dit onderdeel bedoelde bedreiging van de integriteit en veiligheid van netwerk, dienst of randapparaat weg te nemen.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting and follow-up reporting
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern reporting after an incident, and a single organisation could potentially be subject to both regimes. However, provision A requires an AI serious-incident notification, while provision B requires an interim update report only when requested by a CSIRT or competent authority, so the texts do not establish incompatible duties or deadlines.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are cumulative and can readily both be performed: the AI provider makes the serious-incident notification within the applicable deadline, and the essential or important entity submits an interim report if requested. They concern different actors, triggers and reporting content, and neither provision says that one report substitutes for the other.

verdict.evidence_span_b: De essentiële entiteit of belangrijke entiteit dient in het kader van de melding, bedoeld in artikel 27, eerste lid, op verzoek van haar CSIRT of haar bevoegde autoriteit een tussentijds verslag in over relevante updates van de situatie.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations potentially applicable to the same financial entity that is also an AI-model provider
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same undertaking is both a financial entity reporting a serious ICT-related incident and an AI provider whose general-purpose AI model meets the Article 51(1)(a) condition, it must make two distinct notifications: one to the relevant competent authority under Article 19 and one to the Commission under Article 52. The filings concern different triggering facts and recipients, and neither text says that one notification substitutes for the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The obligations can be performed cumulatively without contradiction: the undertaking can notify the relevant competent authority within the Article 20 deadlines and notify the Commission within two weeks. Article 19 concerns serious ICT-related incidents, whereas Article 52 concerns satisfaction of a condition for a general-purpose AI model, so the provisions do not impose incompatible content, timing, or prohibitions.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien een AI-model voor algemene doeleinden voldoet aan de in artikel 51, lid 1, punt a), bedoelde voorwaarde, stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting incidents involving personal-data breaches and significant incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A controller must report a qualifying personal-data breach to the Article 55 supervisory authority within 72 hours where possible. B requires a covered entity to submit an incident notification, and potentially other reports, to the CSIRT or competent authority, creating a possible second reporting stream for the same event with different content and potentially a different recipient.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions can apply cumulatively: a single event may be both a personal-data breach and a significant incident, in which case the controller can make the GDPR notification to the Article 55 supervisory authority and the NIS2 reports to the CSIRT or competent authority. Neither text says that one filing substitutes for the other, and the extracted material does not establish B's recipient or deadline sufficiently to prove a dual-reporting conflict.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A security incident at a covered entity compromises personal data and also qualifies as a significant incident. The entity may have to notify the Article 55 supervisory authority under A and submit the NIS2 incident notification under B, but the shown text does not establish whether the relevant NIS2 competent authority is the same recipient or how the reporting duties interact.
verdict.missing_reference: The missing part of 32022L2555 art. 23 identifying the applicable recipient and the complete triggering and reporting rules for the relevant entity, especially the provisions defining the significant-incident scope and competent authority; those are needed to determine whether B requires a separate filing from A.
verdict.decisive_exception: Whether the CSIRT or competent authority under B is the same recipient as the Article 55 supervisory authority under A, and whether B's reporting duty is triggered by the same event and independently requires a separate filing. The text shown does not establish this.
verdict.evidence_span_a: meldt de verwerkingsverantwoordelijke deze ... uiterlijk 72 uur nadat hij er kennis van heeft genomen, aan de overeenkomstig artikel 55 bevoegde toezichthoudende autoriteit

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions involve institutional handling of information or records, but they regulate different actors, objects, and functions. No text requires the financial authorities' stability measures to affect ACM's number register, nor does ACM's register duty constrain those measures.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns competent financial authorities taking necessary measures, where appropriate, to protect immediate financial-system stability after notification of a serious ICT incident. Provision B concerns ACM maintaining a register of number allocations and acting as controller for that register; the duties can plainly coexist without either preventing compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Op basis van die kennisgeving nemen de bevoegde autoriteiten, in voorkomend geval, alle nodige maatregelen om de onmiddellijke stabiliteit van het financiële systeem te beschermen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: door de Autoriteit Consument en Markt een nummerregister bijgehouden dat een overzicht bevat van toekenningen.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory obligations concerning entities or providers involved in regulated digital activities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose obligations in the broader digital-regulation context, and a financial entity could theoretically also be an AI-model provider. However, provision A concerns continuing responsibility for reported ICT-related incidents, while provision B concerns a specific notification to the Commission when an AI model meets a statutory condition; the texts do not impose incompatible duties or require two reports about the same event.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are independently satisfiable and concern different triggers, objects, and addressees. A requires financial entities to remain responsible for handling and consequences of reported ICT incidents, whereas B requires the relevant AI provider to notify the Commission within two weeks of a specified condition; neither duty excuses or prevents compliance with the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: blijven financiële entiteiten volledig verantwoordelijk voor de behandeling en de gevolgen van de ICT-gerelateerde incidenten die op grond van artikel 19, lid 1, zijn gerapporteerd
verdict.evidence_span_b: stelt de betrokken aanbieder de Commissie daarvan onverwijld in kennis, doch in ieder geval binnen twee weken nadat aan die eis is voldaan of nadat bekend is geworden dat aan die eis zal worden voldaan

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting or notification duties of regulated entities under separate EU digital-law instruments
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose a notification-related obligation, and a qualifying financial entity could also be a deployer of a high-risk AI system. Article 19 requires filings to the relevant competent authority within Article 20 deadlines, while Article 27 requires notification of a fundamental-rights-impact assessment to the market-surveillance authority and submission of a completed template; if the same facts trigger both, the recipients and contents differ.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties concern different triggering events and substantive objects: serious ICT incidents under Article 19 versus completion of a fundamental-rights-impact assessment for a high-risk AI system under Article 27. Even if one entity is subject to both regimes, each filing can be made independently; neither provision forbids or purports to replace the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Financiële entiteiten dienen, binnen de overeenkomstig artikel 20, eerste alinea, punt a), ii), vast te stellen termijnen, bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit het volgende in:
verdict.evidence_span_b: Zodra de in lid 1 van dit artikel bedoelde beoordeling is uitgevoerd, stelt de gebruiksverantwoordelijke de markttoezichtautoriteit in kennis van de resultaten ervan, en dient hij als onderdeel van de kennisgeving het in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde ingevulde sjabloon in.

verdict.shared_subject: The effect of a voluntary NIS2 notification and DORA administrative or corrective measures
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A protects a reporting entity from receiving additional obligations merely because it made a voluntary notification. Provision B requires Member States to empower authorities to impose administrative sanctions or corrective measures on responsible persons when its stated conditions apply; one might argue that a measure imposed after a voluntary notification is an additional consequence triggered by that notification.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A concerns additional obligations imposed on the reporting entity as a consequence of making a voluntary notification, whereas Provision B concerns sanctions or corrective measures against members of a financial entity’s management body or other persons responsible under national law for an infringement. Provision B is triggered by the DORA infringement and its conditions, not by the voluntary notification, and A expressly preserves measures connected with preventing, investigating, detecting or prosecuting criminal offences.
verdict.decisive_exception: No unresolved exception is needed: on the texts shown, Provision B’s measures are based on an infringement and are directed at responsible persons, not additional obligations imposed on the reporting entity because it voluntarily reported.
verdict.evidence_span_a: mag vrijwillige melding er niet toe leiden dat de meldende entiteit bijkomende verplichtingen worden opgelegd waaraan zij niet onderworpen zou zijn geweest indien zij de melding niet had ingediend
verdict.evidence_span_b: verlenen de lidstaten de bevoegde autoriteiten de bevoegdheid om administratieve strafmaatregelen of corrigerende maatregelen te nemen ten aanzien van leden van het leidinggevend orgaan van de financiële entiteit en andere personen die krachtens nationaal recht verantwoordelijk zijn voor de inbreuk

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security or integrity incidents involving electronic services
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same security incident, but they require notifications to different recipients: A requires a progress report to the CSIRT or competent authority, while B requires immediate notification to Onze Minister. The actor would therefore have to make both reports; notifying the Minister would not, on the text shown, discharge the separate report to the CSIRT or competent authority.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are individually satisfiable and could potentially be coordinated in practice, especially because A's progress report is required only if the incident is still ongoing when the final report is due. One might also argue that the authorities could share information, but neither provision states that such sharing substitutes for the actor's separate reporting duties.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A bestuursorgaan suffers a significant security incident affecting its own electronic public service and the incident is still ongoing when the final report under A is due. It must submit A's voortgangsverslag to the CSIRT or competent authority ('op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen') and separately notify Onze Minister immediately under B ('stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis'). These are different recipients and separate filings; the text provides no rule that one filing discharges the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: indien het incident nog aan de gang is op het moment dat het in punt d) bedoelde eindverslag wordt ingediend, zorgen de lidstaten ervoor dat de betrokken entiteiten op dat moment een voortgangsverslag indienen
verdict.evidence_span_b: Een bestuursorgaan of een aangewezen organisatie stelt Onze Minister onverwijld in kennis van een inbreuk op de beveiliging of de integriteit van een eigen elektronische dienst

verdict.shared_subject: Notifying service recipients or clients about significant ICT incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same financial entity and the same incident, requiring prompt notification to affected users. Provision A refers to recipients of the entity’s services, while provision B refers to its clients and additionally requires information about mitigation measures; if those groups or required content differ, one notice may not discharge both duties.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose compatible, cumulative customer-notification duties rather than contradictory ones: both require notification without delay, and a single sufficiently comprehensive notice to the relevant recipients could satisfy both where the recipients overlap. The texts do not expressly require separate filings, different recipients in every case, or incompatible deadlines.
verdict.evidence_span_a: In voorkomend geval stellen de betrokken entiteiten de ontvangers van hun diensten onverwijld in kennis van significante incidenten die een nadelige invloed kunnen hebben op de verlening van die diensten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Wanneer een ernstig ICT-gerelateerd incident optreedt en gevolgen heeft voor de financiële belangen van cliënten, stellen financiële entiteiten, zodra zij het incident hebben opgemerkt, hun cliënten onverwijld in kennis van het ernstige ICT-gerelateerde incident en van de maatregelen die zijn genomen om de negatieve gevolgen van een dergelijk incident te beperken.

verdict.shared_subject: Institutional cooperation and incident-response communications
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions concern cooperation and information exchange in response to incidents. One might argue that the broad coordination duty in Provision A could overlap with Provision B's specific obligation to provide a response within 24 hours, creating uncertainty about how the cooperation should be organised.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A requires competent authorities, the ESAs and the ECB to cooperate and exchange information in carrying out their supervisory tasks. Provision B separately requires the CSIRT to respond to the reporting entity after an early warning, within a specified timeframe; the provisions address different actors, functions and recipients, and nothing in either text makes one response substitute for the other.
verdict.evidence_span_a: De bevoegde autoriteiten, de ETA’s en de ECB werken onderling nauw samen en wisselen informatie uit om hun taken overeenkomstig de artikelen 47 tot en met 54 te verrichten.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Het CSIRT verstrekt onverwijld en zo mogelijk binnen 24 uur na ontvangst van de vroegtijdige waarschuwing, bedoeld in artikel 26, een antwoord aan de meldende entiteit

verdict.shared_subject: ICT-sector entities and communications under DORA and Dutch cybersecurity law
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A requires the lead overseer/ETAs to notify a critical ICT third-party provider about its designation and oversight start date. Provision B requires specified financial entities to report ICT incidents, including voluntary reports, to the sectoral CSIRT; these are different communications, with different actors, recipients, and triggers, so they do not substitute for one another.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions concern ICT-related communications in the financial sector, and a critical ICT provider could serve financial entities subject to the reporting duty. However, the texts do not impose the same action on the same actor in response to the same event, so there is no genuine overlap requiring reconciliation.
verdict.evidence_span_a: Nadat een derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten als cruciaal is aangewezen, stellen de ETA’s de derde aanbieder van ICT-diensten via het Gemengd Comité in kennis van die aanwijzing alsook van de aanvangsdatum vanaf wanneer zij daadwerkelijk aan oversightactiviteiten zullen worden onderworpen.
verdict.evidence_span_b: Banken, handelsplatformen, centrale effectenbewaarinstellingen en centrale tegenpartijen doen de melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, eerste lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, en de vrijwillige melding, bedoeld in artikel 19, tweede lid, eerste paragraaf, van de verordening, tevens bij het bij of krachtens artikel 16, eerste lid, van de Cyberbeveiligingswet aangewezen CSIRT voor de sectoren bankwezen en infrastructuur voor de financiële markt.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose documentation or notification-related obligations, but they concern different activities, triggers, and recipients. Provision A concerns documenting and evaluating an ICT-risk-management framework; Provision B concerns an infrastructure provider's advance notice of cable-maintenance work on public land.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: An actor subject to both could comply with each independently: it can periodically and incident-triggeredly document and evaluate its ICT-risk-management framework while separately notifying the relevant mayor or authorised official before cable-maintenance work. Provision A has no reporting recipient or deadline that overlaps with Provision B's advance municipal notification, so there is no dual-reporting conflict.

verdict.shared_subject: Handhaving tegen entiteiten/operators wegens niet-naleving van EU-verplichtingen
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Beide bepalingen kunnen in een handhavingssituatie rond hetzelfde AI-systeem of dezelfde onderneming worden toegepast. Men zou kunnen aanvoeren dat een NIS2-autoriteit een einde moet laten maken aan een gedraging, terwijl een markttoezichtautoriteit onder de AI-verordening een voorlopige maatregel laat voortbestaan wanneer daartegen binnen de toepasselijke termijn geen bezwaar is gemaakt.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: De bepalingen leggen geen inhoudelijk onverenigbare gedragsvoorschriften aan dezelfde actor op. A geeft bevoegde autoriteiten slechts een handhavingsbevoegdheid ten aanzien van essentiële entiteiten en NIS2-inbreuken; B regelt uitsluitend de procedurele werking van een voorlopige markttoezichtmaatregel en de termijn waarbinnen daartegen bezwaar kan worden gemaakt. Beide kunnen naast elkaar worden nageleefd.

verdict.evidence_span_b: Indien er binnen drie maanden na ontvangst van de in lid 5 van dit artikel bedoelde kennisgeving door een markttoezichtautoriteit van een lidstaat of door de Commissie geen bezwaar tegen een voorlopige maatregel van een markttoezichtautoriteit van een andere lidstaat is ingediend, wordt die maatregel geacht gerechtvaardigd te zijn.

verdict.shared_subject: ICT/security incidents involving an electronic service operated by a bestuursorgaan or aangewezen organisatie
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can be triggered by a serious security or integrity incident. Provision A requires periodic and incident-related documentation and evaluation of the ICT-risk-management framework, while Provision B requires immediate notification to Onze Minister; if the documentation under A were treated as the relevant response, its timing and recipient are not specified and it would not obviously satisfy B's separate notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different, cumulative duties rather than incompatible ones: A concerns documenting and evaluating an ICT-risk-management framework, whereas B concerns notifying Onze Minister and supplying necessary information about a specific breach or misuse. An organisation can document and evaluate under A and separately notify the Minister immediately under B; A does not purport to replace or discharge B.

verdict.shared_subject: Incident reporting by entities subject to both DORA and the Dutch NIS2 implementing rules
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can require reporting about the same incident and both contemplate an interim report. Provision A requires a financial entity to submit an initial notification to the relevant competent authority within Article 20 deadlines, while provision B requires an essential or important entity to submit an interim report, on request, to its CSIRT or competent authority; if the regimes require separate filings to different recipients, one filing would not discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The texts do not establish that the two duties require separate filings: B is expressly submitted 'in het kader van de melding' under Article 27, and its recipient may be the entity's competent authority, while A also requires submission to 'de relevante bevoegde autoriteit.' B is conditional on a request and concerns an interim report, whereas A's shown norm concerns an initial notification, so both could be satisfied cumulatively without contradiction; the text shown does not establish different mandatory recipients or incompatible deadlines.
verdict.missing_reference: The provisions needed to determine whether the DORA relevant competent authority and the NIS2 competent authority/CSIRT are the same or different for a particular entity, and whether Article 27's reporting duty requires a separate filing rather than submission through or as part of the same incident-reporting process.
verdict.decisive_exception: If the applicable provisions outside the excerpts expressly require separate submissions of the same interim information to different recipients, the relationship could instead be a dual-reporting tension. That is not established here.

verdict.shared_subject: Cybersecurity enforcement and information-sharing duties involving essential/critical entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers a competent authority to order an entity to stop conduct that infringes the NIS2 Directive and refrain from repeating it. Provision B requires a competent authority to provide another competent authority with information about a reported significant incident; if the information concerns conduct that A has ordered stopped, the authorities may need to coordinate enforcement and information-sharing, but the texts do not establish any incompatibility between those functions.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose different kinds of norms on different institutional actors: A concerns an authority’s enforcement competence toward important entities, while B requires an authority to transmit information about a reported significant incident to the authority designated under the Critical Entities Resilience Act. An enforcement order to stop infringing conduct can coexist with inter-authority information-sharing, and neither provision forbids or displaces the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting obligations triggered by different events involving potentially overlapping digital-service/AI actors
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A significant incident may require the entity to notify its service recipients immediately, while an AI provider may separately have to notify the Commission within two weeks when the model meets the Article 51(1)(a) condition. If the same organisation is both an affected NIS2 entity and the relevant GPAI provider, these are separate notifications to different recipients and arise from different triggers, so one filing cannot discharge the other.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions impose independently satisfiable duties with different triggers and recipients: Article 23 concerns a significant incident adversely affecting service provision, whereas Article 52 concerns an AI model satisfying a condition in Article 51(1)(a). Compliance with both is possible, and neither text makes one notification substitute for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A company operates a covered digital service and also places a general-purpose AI model on the market. A significant cyber incident adversely affects the service and must be notified immediately to the company's service recipients under Article 23, while the company's GPAI model has also just met the Article 51(1)(a) condition, requiring a separate notification to the Commission within two weeks. The recipient notification does not satisfy the Commission notification, and the Commission notification does not satisfy the recipient notification.

verdict.shared_subject: Regulatory compliance and enforcement of entities
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Provision A empowers competent authorities to order an essential entity to stop conduct violating the NIS2 Directive and refrain from repeating it. Provision B separately obliges the relevant actor to submit a notification by a specified deadline, but nothing in the shown text indicates that an enforcement order under A could lawfully prevent or alter that notification duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Provision A is a competence granted to authorities, not a direct prohibition on the entity’s notification. Provision B imposes a notification deadline for a distinct contemplated transaction; an entity can comply with that deadline while also ceasing any conduct that violates the Directive, and the provisions do not prescribe incompatible conduct, recipients, or deadlines.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting events involving network or cable infrastructure
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions impose prompt notification duties, and a single real-world event might conceivably involve both cable-maintenance work and a significant incident. If so, Provision A concerns notifying the mayor (through an authorised official), while Provision B requires an early warning to both the CSIRT and competent authority, creating potentially cumulative notifications to different recipients.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions have different triggers and actors: A applies when cable-maintenance work is carried out on public land and the authorised official must inform the mayor, whereas B applies to an essential or important entity after it learns of a significant incident. Even if both apply, the texts require notifications to different recipients and do not make one notification substitute for the other; each can be performed independently.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An essential or important telecommunications entity carries out cable-maintenance work on public land, and the work causes a significant incident affecting the availability of a network service. The authorised municipal official must inform the mayor as soon as possible under A, while the entity must give an early warning to its CSIRT and competent authority without delay or within 24 hours under B; notifying one set of recipients does not notify the other.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting and follow-up duties concerning an incident or situation involving an AI system or essential/important entity
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: If the same event is both a serious incident under Article 26 and a situation covered by the Article 27 notification framework, Article 26 requires immediate notification to the provider and then the importer/distributor and market-surveillance authorities, while Article 28 may require an interim report to the entity’s CSIRT or competent authority. These are potentially separate communications to different recipients, and Article 26 does not say that an Article 28 interim report satisfies its notification duty or vice versa.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The provisions do not clearly establish the same triggering event or require two filings on the same facts: Article 26 concerns a serious incident involving a high-risk AI system, whereas Article 28 concerns an interim report requested in connection with a notification under Article 27. If both regimes apply, the duties can be performed cumulatively, with no textual contradiction.

verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: Both provisions can apply to the same underlying security event. Provision A requires the provider to notify the affected subscriber, while Provision B requires the essential or important entity to give an early warning to both its CSIRT and competent authority, creating multiple recipient-specific communications and potentially different timing requirements.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: The duties are addressed to different actors or may have different statutory triggers: A concerns a provider taking a measure under Article 7.6a(1)(g), whereas B concerns an essential or important entity reporting a significant incident. Even if one actor is subject to both, the texts impose complementary notifications to different recipients rather than mutually incompatible conduct; both can be performed.
verdict.concrete_scenario: An entity that is both the provider taking the Article 7.6a(1)(g) measure and an essential or important entity experiences a significant incident threatening network integrity. Before taking the measure, it must notify the affected subscriber and give that subscriber an opportunity to remove the threat; independently, it must give an early warning about the significant incident to its CSIRT and competent authority, without delay or within 24 hours after learning of it. A notification to the subscriber does not notify the CSIRT or competent authority, so both communications must be made.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting of serious/significant ICT incidents by an entity subject to both regimes
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a financial entity to submit an initial notification and later reports to the relevant competent authority, while B requires an essential or important entity to give an early warning to both its CSIRT and its competent authority within 24 hours. For an entity and incident covered by both provisions, the texts identify different reporting packages and an additional CSIRT recipient under B, so the A filing does not on its face discharge B's separate early-warning duty.
verdict.strongest_case_for_compatibility: Both provisions can be obeyed cumulatively: the entity can send B's early warning within 24 hours and submit A's initial notification and subsequent reports within the Article 20 deadlines. The fact that both involve a competent authority does not make them incompatible, and the texts do not state that one filing substitutes for the other.
verdict.concrete_scenario: A financial entity is also an essential or important entity under the Dutch regime, and one incident qualifies both as a serious ICT-related incident under A and a significant incident under B. The entity must submit A's initial notification “bij de relevante bevoegde autoriteit” within the Article 20 deadlines, while separately giving B's early warning “aan haar CSIRT en haar bevoegde autoriteit” “onverwijld of, indien dat niet mogelijk is, binnen 24 uur”; sending the A notification to the relevant competent authority does not, on the text shown, make the separate CSIRT filing required by B or establish that the two filings are the same.
verdict.decisive_exception: None is needed to establish the reporting burden on the text shown; the decisive point is that B expressly names a CSIRT as an additional recipient and imposes a distinct early-warning duty. The provisions shown do not contain a substitution rule making A's notification satisfy B.

verdict.shared_subject: Reporting security or ICT-related incidents
verdict.strongest_case_for_tension: A requires a financial entity to notify affected clients without delay when a serious ICT-related incident affects clients’ financial interests. B requires a public body or designated organisation to notify the Minister without delay of a security or integrity breach or misuse involving its own electronic service. If one actor falls within both regimes and one event satisfies both triggers, the duties run to different recipients and require separate notifications.
